Diagnostic Performance of Urinary Clusterin for Early Detection of Diabetic 
Kidney Disease in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Case-Control Analysis.

Hasan MAT(1), Fahmey SS(1), Ewas HK(1).

Author information:
(1)Department Pediatrics, Faculty of Medicine, Beni-Suef University, Beni-Suef, 
Egypt.

BACKGROUND: Urinary Clusterin, a glycoprotein linked to oxidative stress and 
tubular injury, is being evaluated as a more sensitive biomarker for diabetic 
kidney disease (DKD). This study aims to assess the role of Clusterin in the 
early detection and prognostication of diabetic kidney disease in children with 
Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM), addressing a critical gap in pediatric clinical 
data.
METHODS: This case-control study at Beni-Suef University compared 50 children 
with T1DM (duration ≥5 years) to 40 healthy controls. Assessments included Body 
Mass Index (BMI), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and lipid profiles. Urinary 
Clusterin was measured using Enzyme Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA). A 
Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was employed to determine 
the diagnostic performance of urinary Clusterin in detecting diabetic 
nephropathy.
RESULTS: Diabetic cases exhibited significantly higher levels of AST, 
cholesterol, triglycerides, and serum creatinine compared to the control group. 
The urinary profile revealed significantly elevated urinary creatinine, albumin, 
and albumin-to-creatinine ratios in cases, with urinary clusterin levels being 
significantly higher in children with diabetes (49.7 vs. 32.3 pg/mL, p<0.001) 
than in healthy controls. Within the case group, urinary clusterin significantly 
correlated with ALT, serum creatinine, and triglycerides, although no 
significant associations were found with age, BMI, or HbA1c. At a cutoff value 
of 37.6 pg/mL, urinary clusterin is a highly effective marker for early 
detection of diabetic nephropathy with an 80% sensitivity, and 90% specificity.
CONCLUSION: Urinary clusterin is a potential non-invasive biomarker for early 
diabetic nephropathy in children with T1DM, outperforming traditional measures 
and offering a promising tool for earlier screening and improved clinical 
management.

Translation, Cultural Adaptation, and Validation of the Turkish Version of the 
St George's Respiratory Questionnaire for Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis 
(SGRQ-I).

Pehlivan E(1), Özcan ZB(2), Koçak C(3), Karaahmetoğlu FS(2), Zeren M(4), Eren 
R(5), Demirkol B(6), İlhan U(5), Çınarka H(5), Çetinkaya E(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation, Hamidiye Faculty of Health 
Sciences, University of Health Sciences, İstanbul, Türkiye.
(2)Department of Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation, Hamidiye Institute of Health 
Sciences, University of Health Sciences, İstanbul, Türkiye.
(3)Department of Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation, İstanbul Esenyurt University 
Faculty of Health Sciences, İstanbul, Türkiye.
(4)Department of Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation, İzmir Bakırçay University 
Faculty of Health Sciences, İzmir, Türkiye.
(5)Clinic of Chest Diseases, University of Health Sciences Türkiye, Yedikule 
Chest Diseases and Thoracic Surgery Training and Research Hospital, İstanbul, 
Türkiye.
(6)Department of Pulmonary Diseases, University of Health Sciences Türkiye, 
Başakşehir Çam and Sakura City Hospital, İstanbul, Türkiye.

OBJECTIVE: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) substantially impairs 
health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The IPF-specific St George's Respiratory 
Questionnaire (SGRQ-I) is not available in Turkish. This study aimed to 
translate, culturally adapt, and validate the SGRQ-I for Turkish-speaking 
patients with IPF.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Following international guidelines, the SGRQ-I underwent 
forward translation, reconciliation, back translation, developer review, and 
cognitive debriefing. Adult patients with IPF were consecutively recruited. 
Validity was assessed against the Turkish SGRQ and by examining associations 
with forced vital capacity (FVC), diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO), 
the six-minute walk test (6MWT), gender-age-physiology (GAP) stage, modified 
Medical Research Council (mMRC) grade, and long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) 
status. Test-retest reliability was assessed over seven days in clinically 
stable patients.
RESULTS: One hundred eighty patients were included (mean age 66.3±10.0 years; 
36% male). Agreement with the SGRQ was excellent for the activities, impact, and 
total scores [intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) >0.90] and moderate for 
the symptoms score. The SGRQ-I total score was significantly correlated with 
FVC% (r = -0.476), DLCO% (r = -0.406), and 6MWT distance (r = -0.462, all P < 
0.001). SGRQ-I scores differed significantly across groups stratified by DLCO%, 
GAP stage, mMRC grade, and LTOT status (P < 0.01). Test-retest reliability was 
good to excellent, with ICCs ranging from 0.891 to 0.962.
CONCLUSION: The Turkish SGRQ-I is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing 
HRQoL in IPF, supporting its use in clinical practice and multinational 
research.

Eucalyptus camaldulensis essential oil inhibits biofilm formation and disrupts 
pre-formed biofilms in clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa: an in vitro 
study.

Khanem A(1), Younas F(1), Ullah I(1), Islam-Ud-Din(2).

Author information:
(1)SA-Center for Interdisciplinary Research in Basic Sciences (CIRBS), 
International Islamic University, Islamabad, Pakistan.
(2)Department of Environmental Science, International Islamic University, 
Islamabad, Pakistan.

AIM: P. aeruginosa biofilms enable persistent colonization. This study evaluated 
Eucalyptus camaldulensis essential oil (EUEO) against twenty four clinical 
Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.
METHODOLOGY: EUEO was obtained by hydro-distillation and characterized by FT-IR 
and GC-MS. Antibacterial activity was assessed by agar well diffusion, MIC and 
MBC. Biofilm inhibition (oil added at the start of incubation) and disruption 
(oil added to 18-h pre-formed biofilms) were quantified. Membrane damage was 
inferred from the leakage of cytoplasmic content after 4, 8, and 12 h of 
exposure at 1×MIC.
RESULTS: EUEO was rich in Eucalyptol, comprising 90%. 79.16% isolates formed 
strong biofilms with OD >0.240, 12.5% showed no biofilm formation (OD <0.120) 
and 8.3% had moderate biofilms (OD 0.120-0.240). MICs ranged from 3.125 to 
25 µg/mL and MBCs from 25 to 50 µg/mL. At 1×MIC, EUEO reduced biofilm formation 
by 40-85.71% and reduced the biomass of pre-formed biofilms by 46-90%. 
Time-dependent increase in release of cytoplasmic content, post EUEO exposure 
was consistent with loss of membrane integrity.
CONCLUSION: These in vitro findings suggest that EUEO may be a candidate natural 
agent against P. aeruginosa biofilms, although viability-based and in vivo 
studies are needed to confirm this.

Study protocol of a prospective, non-interventional cohort study evaluating the 
benefits of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in patients with 
hepatocellular carcinoma receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab 
(NISTIPS TRITICC-4, IKF092).

Angendohr C(1)(2), Weigel C(1)(2), Kunstein A(1)(2), Joerdens M(1)(2), Goetze 
T(3)(4), Al-Batran SE(3)(4), Zäpf B(4), Gonzalez-Carmona M(5), Sahin C(6)(7),

(17)Department of Gastroenterology, Infectious Diseases and Rheumatology, 
Charité-University Medicine, Berlin, Germany.
(18)TUM School of Medicine and Health, Department for Internal Medicine II, 
Technical University of Munich, TUM University Hospital, Munich, Germany.

BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related 
mortality, with most patients diagnosed at an advanced stage. Atezolizumab plus 
bevacizumab is a current standard first-line therapy; however, outcomes are 
strongly influenced by underlying cirrhosis and clinically significant portal 
hypertension (CSPH). Complications such as ascites and variceal bleeding may 
limit treatment continuation, particularly as bevacizumab increases bleeding 
risk. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) reduces portal 
pressure and may improve outcomes, but its role in patients receiving 
immunoncology-based systemic therapy remains unclear.
METHODS: NISTIPS TRITICC-4 is a prospective, multicentre, non-interventional 
cohort study conducted at up to 25 centers in Germany. A total of 350 adult 
patients with cirrhosis and unresectable or metastatic HCC receiving first-line 
atezolizumab plus bevacizumab will be enrolled. Patients are allocated to two 
cohorts: TIPS in situ plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab or atezolizumab plus 
bevacizumab alone, according to routine clinical practice.The primary endpoint 
is time to deterioration of liver function (TTDL), defined as persistent 
worsening of liver parameters for >4 weeks. Secondary endpoints include overall 
survival, time on treatment, overall response rate, time to new extrahepatic 
lesions or death, and safety with focus on bleeding and TIPS-related 
complications.Time-to-event endpoints will be analyzed using Kaplan-Meier 
methods and Cox models. Propensity score matching will be applied to adjust for 
confounding. Analyses are exploratory.
DISCUSSION: This study will provide real-world evidence on the impact of TIPS in 
HCC patients receiving atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and may support more 
individualized management strategies in this high-risk population.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT07365930.

Plain Language Summary: Hepatocellular carcinoma is the most common form of 
primary liver cancer and often develops in people with liver cirrhosis. In many 
patients, the cancer cannot be treated with surgery or local procedures and 
systemic drug treatment is required. A commonly used first-line treatment 
combines atezolizumab and bevacizumab. However, patients with cirrhosis may also 
suffer from increased pressure in the portal vein, which can lead to 
complications such as bleeding from enlarged veins in the esophagus or stomach, 
fluid accumulation in the abdomen, and worsening liver function. Bevacizumab can 
increase the risk of bleeding, which may make treatment more difficult in some 
patients.A transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is a procedure 
that reduces pressure in the portal vein by creating a new connection between 
blood vessels inside the liver. The NISTIPS TRITICC-4 study investigates whether 
patients with liver cancer who have a TIPS and receive atezolizumab plus 
bevacizumab have different clinical outcomes compared with patients receiving 
the same drug treatment without TIPS.The study will include 350 patients at up 
to 25 centers in Germany. It will assess changes in liver function, survival, 
duration of treatment, tumor response, bleeding events, treatment-related 
complications, and quality of life. The study aims to provide real-world 
evidence on the potential benefits and risks of TIPS in patients with liver 
cancer receiving modern systemic treatment.

Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral 
arterio-venous graft; a case series.

Shi Y(1), Bao X(1), Fu X(1), Mi L(1), Liu S(1), Wu C(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Vascular Surgery, LongHua Hospital of Shanghai University of 
Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China.

OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and 
clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous 
stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was 
conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts 
(AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein 
stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical 
details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded.
RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean 
age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in 
nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case 
demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all 
other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 
9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had 
a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. 
Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. 
All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The 
technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all 
cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 
10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence 
interval [CI] = 0.74,1).
CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein 
stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

Flexible Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Substrates for on-Site Detection in 
Real Application Scenarios: Development, Advantages, Classification, and 
Application Perspectives.

Guo F(1), Chen C(1), Zhang Y(1), Wang X(1), Ge Y(1), Jiang M(2), Xu Z(1), Wang 
X(1).

Author information:
(1)Key Laboratory of Food Processing Technology and Quality Control in Shandong 
Province, College of Food Science and Engineering, Shandong Agricultural 
University, Tai'an, People's Republic of China.
(2)Department of Chemistry, University of Massachusetts Amherst, Amherst, 
Massachusetts, USA.

Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) technology is widely used in various 
fields due to its extremely high detection sensitivity, yet its performance is 
highly dependent on the substrate material. Traditional rigid SERS substrates 
exhibit notable limitations for in situ detection on complex surfaces and rapid 
on-site analysis. This review provides a comprehensive review of emerging 
flexible SERS substrates. First, the evolution of SERS substrates from colloidal 
solutions and rigid solids to flexible platforms is traced, highlighting the 
need for this flexible design shift. Next, the key advantages of flexible SERS 
substrates over rigid ones are systematically outlined. On this basis, the main 
material systems used for flexible SERS substrates are elaborated in detail, and 
the important manufacturing strategies are summarized. Furthermore, the broad 
application prospects of flexible SERS substrates in cutting-edge areas are 
explored, including food safety, environmental monitoring and health monitoring. 
Finally, current challenges in interfacial stability, signal uniformity, and 
quantitative analysis of complex samples are summarized, and future directions 
are outlined. Through the deep integration of materials science and 
nanotechnology, flexible SERS substrates have successfully transformed SERS from 
a laboratory-confined precision instrument into a portable detection tool 
suitable for complex real-world scenarios, demonstrating significant application 
potential and societal value.

Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in 
dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in 
hemodialysis patients.

Zhang H(1), Liu H(1), Zou Z(1), Chen S(1), Shi L(1), Li Y(1), Dou S(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Medical Imaging, Henan Provincial People's Hospital, Zhengzhou, 
China.

OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of 
arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study 
aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical 
findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in 
patients with dysfunctional AVFs.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive 
hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral 
CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, 
procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous 
lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging 
modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based 
angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively.
RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean 
procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events 
included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic 
reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The 
mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central 
venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis 
in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). 
Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed 
agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was 
interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy.
CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical 
feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous 
abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further 
prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and 
clinical impact.
ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment 
of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a 
practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

Oral Versus Injectable Incretin-Based Anti-Obesity Therapies: An Integrated 
Computational and Evidence-Based Comparison of Orforglipron, Semaglutide, and 
Tirzepatide.

Sahu L(1), Nayak L(2), Tripathy A(3), Ramachandiran S(4), Gunasekaran B(4), 
Lokaiah T(4).

Author information:
(1)IMS & SUM Hospital-II Phulnakhara, Siksha O Anusandhan (Deemed to be 
University), Bhubaneswar, India.
(2)Department of Pharmacology, DRIEMS Institute of Health Sciences and Hospital, 
Tangi, India.
(3)Department of Pharmacology, Dharanidhar Medical College and Hospital, 
Keonjhar, India.
(4)Drithe Diagnostics Centre, Mogappair, Chennai, India.

Incretin-based agents are transforming obesity pharmacotherapy, and 
orforglipron, the first oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist to complete 
phase 3 testing, invites direct comparison with the injectable agents 
semaglutide and tirzepatide. We integrated clinical trial evidence, including 
the direct head-to-head SURMOUNT-5 trial, independently verified molecular 
descriptors, a fully specified drug-target-disease network with 
permutation-tested hub significance, hypergeometric pathway enrichment, and 
multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) across four weighting schemes with 
formal sensitivity analysis. Tirzepatide produced significantly greater weight 
loss than semaglutide under randomized, head-to-head conditions (20.2% vs. 13.7% 
at week 72) and ranked highest under balanced, efficacy-, and safety-dominant 
MCDA models once a composite ADMET score misapplied to two large peptides was 
removed. Orforglipron's lipophilicity exceeds the Lipinski ceiling, showing that 
its oral absorption reflects deliberate chemistry rather than default 
small-molecule developability; it nonetheless ranked highest under an 
accessibility-dominant model driven by oral feasibility and manufacturing 
scalability. These rankings were stable under Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis 
for three of four weighting schemes, with the balanced model comparatively 
fragile. Tirzepatide's cardiovascular evidence has also advanced, with 
SURPASS-CVOT reporting non-inferiority to dulaglutide. No single agent dominates 
every criterion; treatment selection should match the clinical priority the 
individual patient weights most heavily.

"A Minefield for the Novice": Australian Women's Experiences Seeking Health 
Information Online About Perimenopause.

During perimenopause, many women experience psychological and physiological 
symptoms that can seriously impact quality of life and future health. However, 
they report challenges accessing appropriate information and medical support, 
likely exacerbated by clinician knowledge gaps, stigma, and a persistent lack of 
research, consistent with a documented pattern of structural sexism in health 
systems. Consequently, women increasingly turn to alternative sources, 
particularly online, for support. Although scholarship exists on online 
health-information seeking and women's digital health engagement, limited 
research examines how women navigate online health information under clinical 
and structural invalidation. This study gathered responses from 58 
perimenopausal women through an online qualitative survey and constructed three 
themes using reflexive thematic analysis: (a) the search for validation; (b) 
trust erosion and the support gap; and (c) self-efficacy, agency and kinship. 
Interpreted through an epistemic injustice lens, the findings indicated that 
participants used digital literacy strategies to reassert epistemic standing and 
compensate for structural lack of support, yet were left to navigate 
variable-quality health information. Therefore, health information providers and 
policymakers should acknowledge perimenopausal complexity, model 
knowledge-appraisal strategies rather than present information as resolved, and 
mandate training to address the support gap. Health professionals should also 
validate women's epistemic standing before clinically interpreting symptoms.

Clinical Hypnosis as a Supportive Nonpharmacological Intervention for Distress

Makhmudah S(1), Yuniarti KW(1).

Author information:
(1)Faculty of Psychology, Gadjah Mada University, Yogyakarta, Indonesia.

OBJECTIVES: This scoping review mapped the available evidence on clinical 
hypnosis as an adjunctive intervention for older adults in hospital and 
geriatric care, focusing on anxiety, distress, depression, pain, and 
intervention delivery.
METHODS: This scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR. PubMed and Scopus were 
searched without date restrictions. Eligible studies included adults aged 60 
years or older receiving clinical hypnosis or hypnosis-based interventions in 
hospital or geriatric settings.

fidelity reporting, restricted interpretation.

pain but does not establish comparative effectiveness. Depression, longer-term 
function, medication use, rehabilitation, and intervention fidelity remain 
insufficiently examined.
CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Clinical hypnosis may be considered alongside usual care 
for older adults facing stressful procedures, provided they can follow verbal 
instructions and treatment is delivered safely.

The Schematic Brain: The Neurophysiology of Behavioral Schemas.

Maor I(1), Zong W(1), Gostolupce D(1), Schoenbaum G(1).

Author information:
(1)Intramural Research Program of the National Institute on Drug Abuse, 
Baltimore, MD, USA.

How does prior experience shape the way we interpret new situations, learn 
faster, and adapt when the world changes? These capacities depend on schemas: 
structured representations of relational knowledge that the brain builds through 
experience and reuses flexibly across contexts. Although schemas have long been 
central to theories of memory and cognition, their neural implementation is only 
now becoming accessible through advances in large-scale neural recordings, 
population-level analysis methods, and precise causal circuit tools. Here we 
review the emerging systems neuroscience of schemas, focusing on animal models 
where mechanistic dissection is feasible. We argue that schema formation, use, 
and updating are not discrete processes but reflect a continuous adaptive 
interplay between the strength of prior knowledge and the degree to which new 
information aligns with it. At the neural level, schemas appear to be encoded as 
structured low-dimensional population geometries distributed across 
hippocampal-prefrontal circuits, with distinct but interacting contributions 
from orbitofrontal cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, 
and hippocampus. These representations actively shape perception, guide 
behavior, and reorganize when the environment demands it.

(1)Departments of Neurology and Rehabilitation Medicine, Georgetown University

(2)Department of Ophthalmology, University of Pittsburgh, PA, USA.

Among the most devastating effects stroke can have on the lives of survivors and 
those around them are language production and comprehension impairments. The 
most notable of them - often given the joint diagnostic label of "aphasia" 
despite their heterogeneity and dissociability - are associated with damage to 
the brain's left hemisphere, which, in large part for this reason, is considered 
the "language-dominant" hemisphere. However, the right hemisphere's contribution

the possibilities and limitations of neuroplasticity for supporting language 
recovery after stroke. Thus, in this review, we focus on the role of the right 
hemisphere in supporting human language function, in the neurologically healthy 
brain and after stroke. We discuss the remarkable capability of the right 
hemisphere to support normal language abilities after a large left-hemisphere 
stroke early in life, the more limited capacity for right-hemisphere language 
support after left-hemisphere stroke in adulthood, and potential interactions 
between typically left-hemisphere dominant "core" language functions with 
language functions typically thought to be right-hemisphere dominant, such as 
emotional prosody. We conclude by highlighting gaps in current knowledge and 
suggesting areas for future research.

Analytical Detection and Sample Preparation Techniques for Selected New 
Psychoactive Substances: Advances, Critical Limitations, and Future 
Perspectives.

Saleh ARQ(1), El-Tahlawy AS(1), Abuhejail RM(2), Alahmad W(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chemistry, Faculty of Science, Chulalongkorn University, 
Bangkok, Thailand.
(2)Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry, College of Pharmacy, King Saud 
University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

New psychoactive substances (NPS) present a rapidly evolving challenge for 
forensic and clinical toxicology because newly introduced compounds may remain 
undetected by conventional analytical panels or become difficult to identify 
after metabolism, degradation, or matrix-related interference. This review 
critically evaluates 41 original research studies issued between 2020 and 2026 
on sample-preparation and analytical detection strategies for selected NPS, 
particularly synthetic opioids, synthetic cathinones, synthetic cannabinoids, 
and designer benzodiazepines, with emphasis on the factors governing the 
reliability, adaptability, and interpretive value of toxicological workflows. To 
the best of our knowledge, this is the first review to comprehensively integrate 
and critically assess both sample-preparation procedures and instrumental 
detection methods across the major classes of NPS. The reviewed evidence 
indicates that analytical sensitivity alone is insufficient to ensure reliable 
identification. Method performance depends on the interaction between extraction 
selectivity, matrix compatibility, analyte stability, metabolite selection, 
chromatographic resolution, and the scope of instrumental screening. Targeted 
methods remain highly effective for the confirmation and quantification of known 
compounds, whereas high-resolution and complementary screening approaches 
provide greater flexibility for detecting newly emerging substances and 
retrospectively examining previously acquired data. Nevertheless, broad 
detection capability must be supported by robust validation and sufficient 
structural evidence to avoid uncertain or incomplete identification. Future 
analytical strategies should therefore integrate targeted and non-targeted 
approaches, strengthen metabolite-informed detection, improve reference and 
spectral resources, and prioritize matrix-specific validation using authentic 
specimens. Such coordinated workflows are essential for producing timely, 
adaptable, and scientifically defensible results in emerging-drug toxicology.

The Event-Level Association Between Alcohol Use and Intimate Partner Violence 
Perpetration: A Systematic Narrative Review of the Literature.

Gulati NK(1), Hammett JF(2), George WH(1), Chen W(2), Stappenbeck CA(3).

Author information:
(1)University of Washington, Seattle, USA.
(2)Arizona State University, Phoenix, USA.
(3)Georgia State University, Atlanta, USA.

Intimate partner violence (IPV) perpetration is a significant public health 
concern, with up to 90% of individuals in intimate relationships experiencing 
some form of physical, psychological, or sexual IPV from their partner 
throughout their lifetime. Over 30 years of research have concluded that alcohol 
use results in greater risk for IPV perpetration. Despite this known 
association, only recently has alcohol use been examined as a proximal predictor 
of IPV perpetration in daily diary-type studies. The present study aimed to 
provide a systematic narrative review of current research on the event-level 
association between alcohol use and psychological, physical, and sexual IPV 
perpetration. Relevant studies were obtained by searching PsycInfo, PubMed, and 
CINAHL. Full-text peer-reviewed studies published in English that quantitatively 
assessed the event-level association between alcohol use and physical, 
psychological, and/or sexual IPV perpetration (N = 24) were retained. Results 
provide support for the event-level association between alcohol use and IPV 
perpetration across college student, couple, community, clinical, and 
adjudicated samples. Future research is needed to distinguish whether certain 
patterns of alcohol use, quantity, or level of intoxication are associated with 
greater IPV risk. Similarly, future studies should aim to examine psychological, 
physical, and sexual IPV perpetration separately, and to identify how other 
known risk factors may interact with alcohol use to predict event-level IPV 
perpetration. These findings highlight the usefulness of clinical intervention 
efforts that provide skills to target urges to drink or to aggress in the moment 
when they are needed, with the ultimate goal of reducing alcohol-related IPV 
perpetration.

Jung KH(1), Choi MH(2), Choi JY(3), Kang SW(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Orthopedic Surgery, Yeson Hospital, Bucheon, Korea.
(2)Department of Preventive, Occupational and Environmental Medicine, Office of

(4)Department of Orthopedic Surgery, Research Institute for Convergence of

BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the long-term clinical and radiological 
outcomes in patients undergoing semi-constrained total elbow arthroplasty (TEA). 
Postoperative complications and implant survival rates were also investigated.
METHODS: Of 68 patients who underwent primary semi-constrained TEA, data from 62 
with a minimum follow-up of 5 years were analyzed. The mean follow-up duration 
was 117.1 months (range, 60-246 months). Forty-one patients had posttraumatic

outcomes were assessed using the Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS) and Oxford 
Elbow Score (OES), whereas radiological outcomes were analyzed using radiolucent

BACKGROUND: Superior capsule reconstruction (SCR) using the long head of the

Scam-Based Human Trafficking Through a Trauma-Informed and Intersectional Lens: 
An Integrative Narrative Review.

Yeh HC(1), Liu S(1), Rodney T(1).

Author information:
(1)Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA.

Scam-based human trafficking is an emerging form of digitally mediated 
exploitation in which individuals may be financially victimized, coerced into 
online fraud operations, or both. This integrative narrative review synthesizes 
academic and gray literature on scam-based trafficking, including pig-butchering 
scams, romance fraud, scam compounds, forced criminality, and cyber-enabled 
financial exploitation, through a trauma-informed and intersectional lens. 
Structured searches were conducted in Google Scholar and PubMed, supplemented by 
citation tracking, coauthor-identified references, and targeted review of policy 
and agency reports. Sources were eligible if they addressed scam-based 
trafficking, online fraud, forced criminality, trauma vulnerability, 
psychological consequences, revictimization, help-seeking barriers, linguistic 
or technological mechanisms of deception, digital literacy, platform design, or 
trauma-informed intervention. After screening and eligibility assessment, 88 
sources were included in the final synthesis. Findings are organized across five 
domains: trauma as a vulnerability factor, linguistic and technological 
mechanisms of deception, intersecting sociocultural and structural 
vulnerabilities, trauma outcomes and revictimization cycles, and trauma-informed 
interventions. The review suggests that trauma may function both as a 
preexisting vulnerability and as an outcome of exploitation. Scam-based 
trafficking should therefore be understood not only as financial fraud or 
cybercrime, but also as a trauma-related and intersectionally structured form of 
exploitation. Effective responses should combine trauma-informed clinical care, 
emotional scam literacy, culturally responsive services, digital safety 
education, platform accountability, and coordinated systems of support.

OBJECTIVES: To determine the diagnostic accuracy of the Radiographic Assessment 
of Lung Edema (RALE) score for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and 
its interobserver reliability.
DESIGN: Post hoc analysis of a prospective observational cohort study.
SETTING: ICUs at Vanderbilt University Medical Center participating in the 
Validating Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers for Diagnosis study.
PATIENTS: Adult patients receiving invasive ventilation for at least two 
consecutive days, with chest radiographs available on the first 2 ICU days.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Chest radiographs from the first 2 ICU days were 
scored independently by at least two experienced raters; scores were averaged 
per radiograph, and the highest averaged score from ICU day 1 or 2 was selected

intraclass correlation coefficients ranging from 0.81 to 0.87.

score demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy for ARDS at a cutoff of 20, 
together with high interobserver reliability, supporting its potential role as a 
standardized radiographic tool in the diagnosis of ARDS.

Author information:

(4)School of Medicine, University of Surrey and Intensive Care Unit, Royal

OBJECTIVES: Heterogeneity of treatment effect is thought to drive conflicting 
results for the benefits of corticosteroids in sepsis. Proenkephalin A (PENK) is 
a biomarker of renal function. Given the kidney's role in sepsis pathophysiology 
and corticosteroid metabolism, we hypothesized that baseline renal function, 
assessed using PENK, would be associated with hydrocortisone efficacy.
DESIGN: A post hoc analysis of a double-blind, randomized clinical trial in 
septic shock (Effect of Early Vasopressin vs. Norepinephrine on Kidney Failure 
in Patients with Septic Shock [VANISH]).
SETTING: ICUs across the United Kingdom.
PATIENTS: One hundred seventy-three patients admitted to ICU with septic shock.
INTERVENTIONS: Norepinephrine vs. vasopressin and hydrocortisone vs. placebo.

failure-free days. Although we found no significant interaction for 28-day 
mortality (p = 0.14), the patients with high PENK who received hydrocortisone 
had the highest mortality (high PENK hydrocortisone 50%, placebo 32% and low 
PENK hydrocortisone 14%, placebo 24%).

baseline PENK and hydrocortisone treatment on kidney failure-free days. These 
findings require validation in independent and prospective studies.

From Genes to Neural Circuits: Genetic and Systems Mechanisms of Ethanol 
Sensitivity and Tolerance in Drosophila melanogaster.

Subedi A, Lee Y(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Integrative Biotechnology, Kookmin University, Seoul, 02707, 
Republic of Korea.

Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a complex neuropsychiatric disease shaped by 
genetic, environmental, and physiological factors. Over four decades, Drosophila 
melanogaster has emerged as a powerful model for dissecting the molecular and 
neural mechanisms underlying ethanol sensitivity, tolerance, preference, and 
consumption. Its conserved signaling pathways, sophisticated genetic toolkit, 
and robust behavioral assays have enabled discovery of genes and neural circuits 
governing alcohol responses across biological levels. This review summarizes 
major advances in the genetics and neurobiology of ethanol-related behaviors in 
Drosophila. Forward genetic screens identified conserved regulators of ethanol 
sensitivity and tolerance, including cAMP/PKA signaling components, ion 
channels, neurotransmitter receptors, cytoskeletal regulators, and neuropeptide 
pathways. Subsequent studies revealed distinct roles for the ellipsoid body, 
mushroom bodies, circadian neurons, and barrier glia in intoxication, tolerance, 
and reward. Epigenetic studies further established chromatin remodeling and 
transcriptional regulation as mechanisms of long-term behavioral plasticity, 
while systems genetics and genome-wide association studies highlighted the 
polygenic basis of natural variation in alcohol-related traits. Together, these 
findings advance an integrated view of ethanol action and provide a framework 
for understanding human AUD. Emerging approaches include single-cell and 
connectomics analyses, functional testing of human variants, and integration of 
systems genetics with circuit neuroscience.

Author information:
(1)Division of Cardiology, Department of Internal Medicine, Severance

Doxorubicin (DOX) is a widely used anthracycline chemotherapeutic agent; 
however, its clinical efficacy is hampered by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, 
which can lead to irreversible heart failure. Despite extensive research, 
effective strategies for preventing or mitigating DOX-induced cardiac injury 
remain lacking. The Hippo signaling effectors, Yes-associated protein (YAP) and

Words That Heal: A Systematic Review of Healthcare Providers-Patient

Pietrabissa G(1), Rapelli G(1), Marchesi G(1), Castelnuovo G(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Psychology, Catholic University of Milan.
(2)Clinical Psychology Research Laboratory, IRCCS Istituto Auxologico Italiano.

Chronic diseases represent a major global health burden, and suboptimal 
treatment adherence remains a key obstacle to long-term management. Healthcare 
provider (HCP)-patient communication is a modifiable determinant of adherence 
and psychological functioning, yet evidence remains fragmented across conditions 
and communication domains. This review builds on patient-centered communication 
scholarship and established models of communication functions and pathways 
linking clinician-patient communication to health outcomes. This systematic 
review synthesizes empirical evidence on HCP-patient communication strategies 
associated with treatment adherence and psychological outcomes among adults with 
chronic diseases, including diabetes, cancer, cardiovascular, and respiratory 
conditions. Following PRISMA guidelines and PROSPERO registration 
(CRD42020171690), five databases (Scopus, PubMed, PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, 
Google Scholar) were searched. Results: Twenty-seven studies met the inclusion 
criteria. Communication strategies clustered into four macro-domains: (1) trust 
and interpersonal relationship; (2) information exchange and decision processes; 
(3) active involvement, empowerment, and autonomy; and (4) change processes, 
emotional regulation, and management of difficulties. Domains were defined a 
priori from patient-centered communication, self-management, and behavior-change 
literature and refined during data extraction. Across conditions, integrated 
communication patterns addressing multiple domains were generally associated 
with favorable adherence, self-management, clinical, quality-of-life, and 
healthcare-utilization outcomes, although evidence strength varied by study 
design, disease context, and methodological quality. Findings support a 
provisional, evidence-informed framework in which HCP-patient communication 
strategies, organized within relational, informational, participatory, and 
change-regulatory macro-domains, may engage proximal regulatory processes that, 
in turn, may be associated with adherence and other chronic-care outcomes. 
Prospective studies are needed to test these pathways.

Zheng CC(1), Chen YL(1), Wang Z(2), Dai L(3), Zhang XH(4), Tan ZJ(4).

Author information:
(1)School of Physics and Technology, College of Life Sciences, Renmin Hospital

Cellular environments generally contain abundant organic cosolvents, yet how 
in-cell cosolvents modulate the mechanics of RNA-DNA hybrid (RDH) duplex remains 
unclear. Here, we combined high-precision magnetic tweezer experiments with 
all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the structural elasticity 
of RDH duplexes using PEG200, PEG1000, and ethanol as model cosolvents. We found 
that high-concentration cosolvents sharply soften RDH duplexes in bending and 
induce an apparent RNA-like positive twist-stretch coupling. Specifically, for 
RDH duplex, the bending persistence length P decreases from ∼54 nm to ∼27-35 nm 
(∼35-50% decrease) by 40% cosolvents. Meanwhile, the twist-stretch coupling 
parameter dL/dN shifts from ∼0 to -0.56--0.45 nm/turn, approaching that of RNA

mainly arises from local hydrogen-bond disruption associated with structural 
mismatch between RNA and DNA strands and enhanced strand fluctuation driven by 
increased ion neutralization. Moreover, the RNA-like twist-stretch coupling 
originates from cosolvent-induced shifts of structure and deformation pathway of 
RDH duplex toward RNA-like ones from comprehensive analyses at the helix, 
base-pair, and strand levels. Our findings revealed that cosolvents can 
substantially reshape the structure and mechanics of RDH duplexes, potentially 
providing a physical basis for understanding their behavior in cells.

Parallel-stranded G-quadruplexes (G4s) exhibit remarkable kinetic stability.

intrinsically high activation energy Ea or a constrained transition pathway.

magnetic tweezers to quantify the unfolding dynamics of c-MYC promoter G4s

measurement of G4 energy landscapes.

Sugar signaling governs carbon allocation between source and sink organs in 
plants, and excess sugar is known to repress transcripts of photosynthesis and 
sugar-metabolism genes. How this regulation operates post-transcriptionally 
remains unclear. Here we study RGGA, a RGG-repeat RNA-binding protein, and its 
interaction with the 5'-3' exoribonuclease XRN4 to understand how selective mRNA

XRN4-mediated selective mRNA degradation, shaping post-transcriptional gene 
expression and plant growth in response to sugar availability. Prolonged 
stability of specific mRNAs promotes sugar-dependent growth, revealing a 
mechanism by which plants modulate carbon allocation via mRNA turnover.

Trust, Traits, and Turning Points: Decoding Operator Responses to Real-World 
ADAS Malfunctions.

Garakani G(1), Guo H(2), Chen B(1), Pulver E(3), Bao S(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering Department, University of 
Michigan-Dearborn, Dearborn, MI, USA.
(2)University of Michigan Transportation Research Institute, Ann Arbor, MI, USA.
(3)State Farm Technology Research and Innovation Laboratory, Bloomington, IL, 
USA.

OCCUPATIONAL APPLICATIONThis study found that high emotional trust in Advanced 
Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) showed a non-significant tendency toward slower 
manual intervention during malfunctions, and that an operator's personality was 
related to specific information needs. For practitioners, this indicates a 
critical safety gap where affective comfort, feeling "too safe" reduces 
readiness. To mitigate these risks, organizations should prioritize hands-on, 
simulated malfunction training. By exposing operators to controlled scenarios 
such as "phantom braking" events, practitioners can help them experience system 
limitations firsthand, rebuilding the protective skepticism and preparedness 
that sustained automation use tends to erode. Because occupational driving spans 
a range of operational models, safety protocols should be tailored accordingly. 
In managed fleets, organizations have an opportunity to implement 
personality-aligned Human-Machine Interface (HMI) configurations that address 
the specific cognitive and informational needs of individual drivers. For "Bring 
Your Own Device" (BYOD) gig platforms, where organizations cannot modify the 
vehicle's native systems, broader software-based interventions are more 
practical, for example, in-app geofenced warnings that alert drivers as they 
approach known ADAS limitation zones. Together, these targeted, 
context-sensitive interventions help recalibrate trust and prevent overreliance, 
supporting rapid recovery and sustained situational awareness across the diverse 
occupational contexts in which ADAS is now used.

Plain Language Summary: Background: As vehicles adopt increasingly sophisticated 
Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS), the driver’s role is being redefined 
from active controller to supervisory systems manager within a “mobile 
workplace.” In occupational driving contexts, safety depends on how effectively 
an operator can recognize and respond when automation reaches its functional 
limits. Real-world ADAS malfunctions, such as phantom braking or sensor-related 
errors, represent occupational safety hazards that can disrupt workflow, erode 
trust, and compromise performance.Purposes: Despite widespread reliance on these 
systems, the human baseline for responding to such malfunctions remains 
inadequately understood. This study addresses that gap by examining ADAS 
malfunctions from the operator’s perspective, developing a taxonomy of 
malfunction types and behavioral responses across varied driving 
contexts.Methods: Using a mixed-methods design, we evaluated 30 drivers who 
experienced real-world ADAS malfunctions. Participants first completed 
survey-based assessments measuring Big Five personality traits and 
multidimensional automation trust. We then conducted semi-structured interviews 
to capture detailed malfunction narratives (N = 56 eligible cases). Qualitative 
thematic analysis was paired with exploratory correlation and binary logistic 
regression analyses.Results: Exploratory analyses indicated distinct association 
patterns between personality profiles and trust dimensions: Neuroticism 
correlated with lower perceived transparency, Openness with greater adoption 
intent, and Conscientiousness with lower emotional trust but higher perceived 
transparency. Age-stratified patterns suggested that younger drivers higher in 
Neuroticism perceived systems as less transparent, whereas older drivers drew on 
Conscientiousness for a more deliberate calibration of trust. Qualitatively, six 
recurring malfunction categories were identified, frequently triggered by

with an increased likelihood of proactive manual braking, higher Emotional Trust 
exhibited a negative, non-significant tendency with braking 
intervention.Conclusions: These findings show that driver responses during ADAS 
malfunctions are related to multidimensional trust, while personality shapes how 
drivers calibrate that trust. Enhancing occupational driving safety requires 
superior system transparency and targeted training frameworks that foster 
calibrated trust and timely manual intervention across a diverse workforce.

"It's like saving for a rainy day": perceptions of voice banking for people

Krikheli L(1)(2), Jackson N(2), Gomizel K(2), Jackson N(3).

This exploratory qualitative study examined how people living with Motor Neurone 
Disease (PlwMND) and their partners perceived voice banking and related voice 
preservation counseling within a specialist Australian service. Semi-structured 
interviews were conducted in 2022 with five PlwMND and two partners.

technological capability. The study highlights the importance of proactive, 
accurate, and staged informational counseling that reflects evolving voice 
preservation technologies and local service pathways.

Association between IRAK1 gene rs1059703 polymorphism and rheumatoid arthritis

Wang Z(1), Li J(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Organization and Personnel, Changzhou Center for Disease 
Control and Prevention, Changzhou, People's Republic of China.
(2)Department of Physical and Chemical Laboratory, Changzhou Center for Disease 
Control and Prevention, Changzhou, People's Republic of China.

OBJECTIVES: This meta-analysis aimed to investigate the relationship between 
interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase (IRAK1) gene rs1059703 and rheumatoid 
arthritis (RA) risk.
METHODS: The pooled odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (95% CI) were 
calculated. Funnel plot with trim-and-fill analysis was used for publication 
bias investigation.
RESULTS: IRAK1 gene rs1059703 was not significantly associated with RA risk 
under dominant genetic model (OR = 1.47, 95%CI = 0.96-2.24, p = 0.071), 
recessive genetic model (OR = 1.14, 95%CI = 0.92-1.40, p = 0.2258), allele 
genetic model (OR = 1.29, 95%CI = 0.95-1.75, p = 0.0878), and codominant genetic 
model (OR = 1.33, 95%CI = 0.82-2.15, p = 0.2125). Subgroup analysis also 
suggested that IRAK1 gene rs1059703 polymorphism was correlated with RA risk 
under dominant genetic model (I2 = 80.9%, PQ < 0.0001, OR = 1.77, 
95%CI = 1.12-2.79, p = 0.014) and allele model (I2 = 79.6%, PQ = 0.0002, 
OR = 1.45, 95%CI = 1.05-2.00, p = 0.026) in Caucasian. Sensitivity analysis 
indicated that there was no significant change in the combined OR. No 
publication bias was observed.
CONCLUSION: A statistically significant association between IRAK1 rs1059703 and 
RA risk was observed in Caucasian populations, but not in Asian populations with 
the available power under the current sample size. The apparent Caucasian 
association observed in the full dataset was not sustained after restricting 
analyses to HWE-compliant studies, where only a single Caucasian study remained.

Aspiration Thrombectomy for High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism With Life-Threatening 
Anemia and Active Uterine Bleeding: A Case Report.

Saoudi O(1), Wang B(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, First Affiliated 
Hospital of Hebei North University, Zhangjiakou, Hebei, China.
(2)Hebei Key Laboratory of Pathogenic Mechanisms and Diagnosis & Treatment 
Technologies for Lung Microbiome, First Affiliated Hospital of Hebei North 
University, Zhangjiakou, Hebei, China.

BACKGROUND High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) carries significant mortality, and 
management becomes complex when it coexists with severe anemia and active 
bleeding, as thrombolysis is then contraindicated. We report the case of a 
patient with high-risk PE complicated by severe anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L) and 
active uterine bleeding from adenomyosis. CASE REPORT A 48-year-old woman 
presented with haemodynamic instability (blood pressure 74/47 mm Hg), critical 
anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L), and a 3-year history of irregular vaginal bleeding 
from adenomyosis. Computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography confirmed 
bilateral PE with right pulmonary artery main-trunk occlusion; echocardiography 
showed severe pulmonary hypertension, and duplex ultrasound showed extensive 
left lower-limb deep vein thrombosis. Thrombolysis was contraindicated. 
Emergency percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy was performed using large-bore 
catheters (22F, 20F, 16F) with concurrent inferior vena cava filter placement, 
reducing pulmonary artery pressure from 51/23 to 34/12 mm Hg; the estimated 
blood loss, quantified from filtered aspirate, was approximately 100 mL. 
Adjuncts included transfusion of 13 units of packed red cells, dilatation and 
curettage, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist therapy, and titrated 
anticoagulation. At discharge after a 24-day hospitalization she was 
hemodynamically stable, and free of dyspnea, with resolved edema and hemoglobin 
72 g/L, on oral rivaroxaban. CONCLUSIONS In this thrombolysis-contraindicated 
patient, aspiration thrombectomy with inferior vena cava filter placement was a 
feasible rescue strategy that achieved rapid hemodynamic and angiographic 
improvement without thrombolysis, with palliative rather than curative intent. 
As a single case, it cannot establish comparative safety or efficacy, and 
broader conclusions regarding efficacy cannot be drawn. It illustrates a 
potentially useful approach in similarly complex scenarios where coordinated 
multidisciplinary care is essential.

Progress in research on the bidirectional relationship between circadian rhythm 
and depression: A bibliometric analysis.

He K(1), Cheng K(1), Li W(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)School of Basic Medical Sciences, Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese 
Medicine, Chengdu, Sichuan, China.
(2)School of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Sichuan College of Traditional 
Chinese Medicine, Mianyang, China.

This study used VOSviewer and CiteSpace to conduct a bibliometric analysis of 
444 publications on the relationship between circadian rhythms and depression, 
retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (January 2015 to April 2025). 
Publication numbers remained low until 2017 but increased markedly after 2018, 
with the United States contributing the largest share. Ian B. Hickie and Joanne 
S. Carpenter were the most prolific authors; the University of Pittsburgh and 
Chronobiology International were the most productive institution and journal, 
respectively. McClung, Dubocovich, and Logan were the top co-cited authors, 
while frequent keywords included "expression," "sleep," "circadian rhythms," and 
"melatonin." These findings underscore the growing importance of circadian 
rhythms in depression pathophysiology and therapy, with future research likely 
to focus on diagnosis, biomarker identification, individualized treatment, 
prognosis, and health management.

Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury in Oncology Patients During Active 
Chemotherapy: A Saudi Arabian Retrospective Study.

Alzahrani A(1), Alsayed M(1), Shihata S(1), Mohamed W(1), Alqarni MS(2), 
Almoallim R(1), Khiyami A(1), Felemban A(3), Ashour M(1), Zia Z(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Radiology, King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Centre, 
Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
(2)Department of Internal Medicine, King Abdulaziz Medical City, Ministry of 
National Guard, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
(3)Department of Radiology, King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Centre, 
Madinah, Saudi Arabia.

BACKGROUND Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a recognized 
complication in oncology patients undergoing contrast-enhanced computed 
tomography (CECT) during chemotherapy. Limited data exist on CA-AKI incidence in 
patients with preserved baseline renal function, particularly in Middle Eastern 
populations. MATERIAL AND METHODS We conducted a retrospective analysis of 146 
adult oncology patients with baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate 
(eGFR) greater than 50 mL/min/1.73 m² who underwent CECT within 45 days of 
chemotherapy at a tertiary cancer center in Saudi Arabia (January 2017-December 
2018). CA-AKI was defined as an absolute serum creatinine increase of 0.3 mg/dL 
or more, or as a relative increase of more than 50% within 48 to 72 hours of 
contrast administration. Given the small number of events (n=2), descriptive 
statistics and exploratory univariate analyses were performed. RESULTS CA-AKI 
occurred in 2 of 146 patients (1.4%; 95% CI: 0.2%-5.0%). Mean age was 51.5±16.2 
years; 58% were women. Cancer types included solid tumors (81.5%) and 
hematological malignancies (17.8%). The chemotherapy-to-CECT interval was 
shorter in patients with CA-AKI (mean: 2 days) than in patients without CA-AKI 
(mean: 23.3±12.8 days; P=0.02). This association is exploratory and 
hypothesis-generating given the extremely limited number of events. CONCLUSIONS 
CA-AKI incidence was relatively low (1.4%) in oncology patients with preserved 
baseline renal function undergoing CECT during active chemotherapy. The observed 
association between shorter chemotherapy-to-imaging intervals and CA-AKI 
requires prospective validation and should not be interpreted as a definitive 
causal relationship. These findings provide preliminary regional data from Saudi 
Arabia and underscore the need for larger, well-designed prospective studies to 
better characterize CA-AKI risk in this population.

Scientific Remix: Epistemic Idioms and the Spread of Data Science.

Tanweer A(1).

Author information:
(1)University of Washington, USA.

Scholarship on science has long contained a tension between accounts emphasizing 
convergent forces and those highlighting divergent practices. This article 
addresses that tension through an ethnographic study of data science. It 
advances the concept of epistemic idiom-a recognizable and portable pattern of 
practices that evolve alongside knowledge-making tools, analogous to musical 
idioms arising from the interaction of material affordances and learned 
techniques. Through analysis of a project attempting to sequence chromosomal 
centromeres, I show participants enacting the nomad idiom of data science: a 
data-led approach involving tools for iteration and exploration, 
cross-disciplinary borrowing, bricolage construction of bespoke assemblages, and 
the motivation to scale. Though the project failed to sequence centromeres, it 
generated unexpected discoveries, challenged established theories, and yielded 
lasting changes to scientific practice. The case reveals how epistemic trends 
can spread without being totalizing-the nomad idiom enabled both convergence 
(shared technical toolkit) and divergence (local adaptations, surprise outcomes) 
simultaneously. The epistemic idiom concept complements existing STS frameworks 
by explaining how practices can migrate across epistemic communities, while 
those communities retain distinct cultures. It speaks to concerns over 
computational universalism and epistemic monocultures, demonstrating that 
alternatives exist-ways for scientific trends to be borrowed rather than 
imposed, becoming remixes instead of replacements.

Outcome following lag screw fixation of non-C3 carpal slab fractures in horses.

Chevalier JM(1), Brown KA(1), Smith A(1), Richardson DW(1), Ortved KF(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Clinical Studies, School of Veterinary Medicine, University of 
Pennsylvania, Kennett Square, Pennsylvania, USA.

OBJECTIVE: To describe clinical features and short- and long-term outcomes of 
horses treated with lag screw fixation of slab fractures of the radial carpal 
(Cr), intermediate carpal (Ci), ulnar carpal (Cu), second (C2) or fourth (C4) 
carpal bones.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective case study.
ANIMALS: Horses (n = 19) treated with lag screw fixation for slab fractures of 
Cr, Ci, Cu, C2 or C4.
METHODS: Medical records of patients with carpal slab fractures were reviewed, 
and those undergoing internal fixation of slab fractures involving Cr, Ci, Cu, 
C2, or C4 carpal bones from January 2008 to January 2026 were included. 
Long-term outcomes were obtained by a standardized questionnaire. Descriptive 
data are presented.
RESULTS: Predominant breeds included Thoroughbreds (7/19) and Warmbloods (7/19). 
A total of 10 of 19 fractures were caused by traumatic falls, including six 
during recovery from general anesthesia. Five of 19 surgeries were performed 
with arthroscopic guidance, and 14/19 surgeries were performed with computed 
tomography (CT) guidance. Survival beyond 1 year was 88%, with 53% returning to 
previous athletic function and 71% owner satisfaction.
CONCLUSION: Prognosis for return to the previous level of work was good and 
comparable to that previously reported for internal fixation of C3 slab 
fractures.
CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Lag screw fixation provides good outcomes in survival, 
return to work, and owner satisfaction for slab fractures of Cr, Ci, Cu, C2, or

Additive Effects of Time Awake and Number of Flights on Fatigue in Short-Haul 
Pilots: Implications for Duty Time Regulation.

Steven D(1), Tritschler K(2), Basner M(3), Elmenhorst EM(1), Aeschbach D(1)(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Sleep Und Human Factors Research, Institute of Aerospace 
Medicine, German Aerospace Center, Cologne, Germany.
(2)Germanwings GmbH, Cologne, Germany.
(3)Unit for Experimental Psychiatry, Division of Sleep and Chronobiology, 
Department of Psychiatry, University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of 
Medicine, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA.
(4)Institute of Experimental Epileptology and Cognition Research, University of 
Bonn Medical Center, Bonn, Germany.

Time awake affects airline pilots' fatigue but it is less clear how workload 
during that time awake impacts fatigue. Although current flight time limitations 
take the number of flights within a duty period as a measure of workload into 
account, quantitative evidence for its fatiguing effect is scarce. Here, we 
analysed fatigue, subjective workload and flight-associated hassles at the end 
of 553 short-haul flights from 37 airline pilots. Two linear mixed-models with 
fatigue or subjective workload as the dependent variable were generated, 
adjusted for time awake, number of completed flights, number of hassles, prior 
sleep and pilot's responsibility (flying/monitoring). Results showed that 
fatigue was influenced by time awake, number of flights and pilot's 
responsibility, whereas no effect was found for number of hassles. The critical 
fatigue threshold (flying not recommended) was exceeded 2.4 h earlier when 
operating four flights compared with one flight. Fatigue was lower but 
subjective workload was higher when the pilot was flying instead of monitoring. 
Subjective workload increased with number of hassles, but not with number of 
flights or time awake. European duty time limitations are justified to include a 
penalty for additional flights but may underestimate the fatiguing effect.

Sleep, inflammation, and pain in musculoskeletal rehabilitation: a structured 
integrative review of neurobiological mechanisms and non-pharmacological pain 
management strategies.

de Freitas EM(1), Silva A(2), Esteves AM(3).

Author information:
(1)Faculty of Physical Education, Universidade Estadual de Campinas - UNICAMP, 
Campinas, São Paulo, Brazil.
(2)Department of Sports Science, Federal University of Minas Gerais - UFMG, Belo 
Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil.
(3)Faculty of Applied Sciences, Universidade Estadual de Campinas - UNICAMP, 
Limeira, São Paulo, Brazil.

BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbance, inflammation, and persistent pain may reinforce 
one another, compromising musculoskeletal rehabilitation.
PURPOSE: To synthesize evidence on mechanisms linking sleep, inflammation, and 
pain and identify relevant non-pharmacological interventions.
METHODS: This structured integrative review examined peer-reviewed studies 
published from January 2010 to December 2025, identified through PubMed, Scopus, 
PEDro, and SciELO. Reporting and synthesis were guided by SANRA and EQUATOR 
recommendations.
RESULTS: Fifty-seven studies were included: 24 experimental or observational 
studies, 17 systematic reviews or meta-analyses, and 16 narrative or integrative 
reviews. Sleep restriction was associated with changes in interleukin-6, tumor 
necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein, with responses varying across 
populations and protocols. Prostaglandins and bradykinin may promote nociceptive 
sensitization, while disrupted sleep may impair descending pain inhibition. 
Exercise, manual therapy, neuromuscular electrical stimulation, low-level laser 
therapy, and sleep-focused behavioral interventions showed mechanistic 
plausibility, although confirmatory trials remain limited.
CONCLUSION: Sleep assessment and sleep-focused interventions should be 
considered within multimodal musculoskeletal pain management, while further 
controlled research clarifies clinical effectiveness.

Plain Language Summary: Why was this study done? Sleep problems, inflammation, 
and pain are closely linked. When people do not sleep well, the body may make 
more molecules that cause inflammation, which can lower the ability to cope with 
pain and make recovery harder. This can turn into a cycle that keeps pain going. 
We looked at recent research to understand how these three things affect each 
other and what health professionals including pain doctors and physiotherapists 
can do about it.What did we find? Poor sleep is linked with body changes that 
may make pain feel worse. Treatments that do not rely on medicines such as 
aerobic exercise, strength training, hands-on (manual) therapy, and sleep 
education may help lower pain by improving inflammation, calming the nervous 
system, building confidence in movement, and improving sleep. Stronger proof 
from high-quality trials is still needed.What does this mean for patients? 
Health professionals should ask patients about their sleep as a routine part of 
care. Adding sleep-focused strategies to musculoskeletal pain care may help some 
patients, but this still needs to be confirmed by high-quality clinical trials.

Characterizing geographic diversity of acetolactate synthase resistance in US 
johnsongrass (Sorghum halepense) biotypes.

Purvis C(1), Patterson EL(1), Burns EE(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Plant, Soil and Microbial Sciences, Michigan State University, 
East Lansing, MI, USA.

BACKGROUND: Acetolactate synthase (ALS)-inhibiting herbicides are widely used 
for Sorghum halepense weed control across agroecosystems. However, little is 
known about variation in resistance phenotypes and mechanisms among 
geographically diverse biotypes. This study surveyed S. halepense biotypes 
collected across the USA to quantify resistance to ALS inhibitors, identify 
target and non-target site mechanisms, and evaluate alternative herbicide 
options.
RESULTS: Dose response assays identified nicosulfuron resistance in 24% of 
evaluated biotypes, with resistant biotypes ED50 ranging from 66 to 
>4160 g ha-1. Among nicosulfuron resistant biotypes, 56% and 44% were also 
resistant to imazethapyr and thiencarbazone, respectively, demonstrating 
variability in resistance patterns among ALS herbicides of different chemical 
families. A novel primer set enabled simultaneous screening of all reported ALS 
resistance mutations across both ALS homeologs. Molecular screening identified 
the Trp574 substitution as the sole target-site resistance mechanism in 64% of 
resistant biotypes. Further, Trp574 mutation frequency varied among resistant 
biotypes, ranging from 21% to 91%, and was positively correlated with 
nicosulfuron resistance level. Resistant biotypes lacking target-site mutations 
exhibited over eightfold reductions in nicosulfuron ED50 following malathion 
pretreatment, suggesting involvement of cytochrome P450 non-target site 
resistance mechanisms. Despite the identification of these mechanisms, 
glyphosate and clethodim remained effective for S. halepense control in all but 
one biotype.
CONCLUSION: Overall, we demonstrated that ALS resistance in S. halepense varies 
across geographically diverse biotypes from the USA. Together, these findings 
provide important insight for resistance evolution and support development of 
management strategies for ALS resistant S. halepense biotypes. © 2026 The

A One-Stone-Two-Birds Strategy to Develop P-Por COF/PDES Composite Gels for 
Photothermal/Photodynamic Antibacterial Activity and Wearable Strain Sensing.

Ma Z(#)(1), Wang L(#)(1), Fan Z(2), Yang W(1), Xuan S(3), Lu H(1), Yang W(1)(4).

Author information:
(1)School of Energy, Materials and Chemical Engineering, Hefei University, 
Hefei, Anhui, P. R. China.
(2)School of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering, Hefei University, Hefei, Anhui, 
P. R. China.
(3)Department of Modern Mechanics, University of Science and Technology of 
China, Hefei, P. R. China.
(4)Anhui Provincial Key Laboratory of Urban Rail Transit Safety and Emergency 
Management, Hefei University, Hefei, Anhui, P. R. China.
(#)Contributed equally

Flexible wearable electronics face growing bacterial infection risks from 
prolonged skin contact, creating an urgent demand for flexible materials 
integrating efficient sensing and antibacterial functions. Herein, a novel 
phosphorus-containing porphyrin covalent organic framework (P-Por COF) was 
synthesized via a solvothermal Schiff-base reaction, and incorporated into a 
polymerizable deep eutectic solvent to fabricate P-Por COF/PDES composite gels 
through in-situ UV polymerization. The resulting gel exhibited enhanced 
photothermal performance, improved mechanical properties, and excellent 
near-infrared (NIR) triggered antibacterial activity. Under 730 nm NIR light 
irradiation, the P-Por COF/PDES composite gel could reach 76 °C with 4 min, 
while showing excellent stability of photothermal cycle. Based on the 
synergistic effect of photodynamic production of singlet oxygen and photothermal 
effect, the P-Por COF/PDES composite gel resulted in a high bactericidal rate of 
nearly 100% against both Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and Escherichia coli 
(E. coli). The P-Por COF/PDES composite gel delivered a fracture strain up to 
2435.82% and 2.6-fold higher toughness than pure PDES, along with stable, 
sensitive and self-healable strain sensing for human motion monitoring. Overall, 
this work provides a simple and effective strategy for developing antibacterial 
materials and multifunctional gels with integrated therapeutic and sensing 
capabilities.

BACKGROUND: In 2015 the World Health Assembly (WHO), based on recommendations by 
the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery, passed resolution (68:15) on 
strengthening emergency and essential surgical care and anesthesia as a 
component of universal health coverage. However, children's surgery was not 
adequately represented and in response, the Global Initiative for Children's 
Surgery (GICS) published the Optimal Resources for Children's Surgical Care 
(OReCS) in 2019 providing insight into procedures which should be performed at 
different facility types. OReCS 2 addresses a gap in both policy and published 
literature to further define surgical conditions and procedural capabilities by 
hospital level.
METHODS: We performed a review of the literature to identify procedures 
routinely performed in a variety of settings. We then used an iterative Delphi 
like approach to identify specialty-specific procedures and nursing skills by 
hospital level. Participation was open to all members of GICS with 
representation from 21 working groups and more than 50 low-middle income 
countries (LMICs) and high-income countries (HICs). Data on essential procedures 
were collected for twelve specialty groups. Modifications of the recommendations 
provided by the working groups were made by the executive board based on 
firsthand knowledge of capabilities at lower-level facilities where 
subspecialists have less experience. Final recommendations were made based on 
greater than 75% agreement by respondents and review of the executive board of 
GICS.
RESULTS: Procedures performed at health centers were limited to those not 
requiring anesthesia or sedation and were largely identified to help triage and 
stabilize patients for transfer to higher level care. Similarly, first level 
hospital procedures focused on stabilization and transfer to referral level 
hospitals for most specialties. Alternatively, specialties such as ophthalmology 
and dental surgery have identified definitive procedures for lower-level 
facilities. Procedures performed at the National Children's Hospital level 
include those requiring specialty providers and equipment such as 
transplantation, repair of congenital heart disease, and reconstructive surgery 
for complex trauma, congenital anomalies, and burns.
CONCLUSIONS: This updated version of OReCS provides specific examples of 
procedural capabilities for twelve subspecialties at the health center, first, 
second, third, and referral level hospitals in LMICs. Whereas the list is not 
meant to be all inclusive, it provides a framework within which to define the 
minimum essential material resources, equipment, and personnel by hospital 
level.

The architectural and functional landscape of transposon-derived chimeric RNAs.

Xiang Y(1)(2), Liang H(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Medical Genetics and Development, Key Laboratory of Reproductive 
Genetics (Ministry of Education) and Department of Reproductive Endocrinology, 
Women's Hospital, School of Medicine, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China.
(2)Zhejiang Provincial Birth Defect Control and Prevention Research Center, and 
Zhejiang International Science and Technology Cooperation Base of Reproductive

This review systematically examines the architectural and functional landscape 
of transposable element (TE)-derived chimeric RNAs, classifying them into three 
major categories: TE-coding gene chimeras, TE-lncRNA chimeras and TE-TE 
chimeras. We delineate four potential molecular mechanisms contributing to their 
biogenesis: transcriptional read-through coupled with cis-splicing, promoter 
hijacking by TE-derived regulatory elements, trans-splicing of independent 
transcripts and epigenetic regulation of TE genomic loci. Functionally, TE and 
their chimeric RNAs can coordinately participate in genomic regulation at 
different levels: they remodel native gene expression patterns via alternative 
promoters, introduce novel functional domains into proteins and lncRNAs, and 
form integrated transcriptional regulatory networks. These chimeric transcripts 
exert critical roles in early embryonic development, stem cell potency, 
differentiation or pathogenic condition. Looking forward, long-read sequencing 
and genomic targeting technologies hold great promise to unravel the 
functionality and therapeutic application of TE-derived chimeric RNAs. 
Collectively, this review establishes TE-derived chimeric RNAs as fundamental 
drivers of transcriptomic innovation, evolutionary adaptation and disease 
aetiology, bridging basic genome biology with physiology and clinical 
translation.

Assessing health related quality of life of patients on maintenance hemodialysis

Mourchid R(1), Yassine A(2), Cherrah Y(1), Serragui S(1).

Author information:

BACKGROUND: This study evaluated health-related quality of life (HRQoL) 
differences between public (N = 61) and private (N = 61) sector hemodialysis 
patients in Morocco using Moroccan and French EQ-5D-5 L value sets.
METHODS: EQ-5D-5 L dimensions, utility index, and Visual Analog Scale (EQ-VAS) 
scores were compared between sectors through a bivariate analysis HRQoL 
determinants were identified via Generalized Linear Model (GLM) multivariable 
regression, adjusting for socio-demographic and clinical covariates.
RESULTS: Private sector patients reported higher 'no problem' rates in mobility 
(45.9% vs. 19.7%), self-care (34.4% vs. 18.0%), usual activities (34.4% vs. 
6.6%), and pain/discomfort (31.1% vs. 11.5%). Median Moroccan utility scores 
were significantly higher in private vs. public sectors (0.79 vs. 0.48, 
p = 0.003), mirrored by French scores (0.85 vs. 0.63, p > 0.001) and EQ-VAS 
(median: 72 vs. 70, p > 0.001). In multivariable GLM regression, the treatment 
sector was not an independent predictor (beta = -0.128, p = 0.345). Instead, 
employment status (beta = 0.302, p = 0.035) exhibited significantly higher 
health-related quality of life, whereas lower weekly dialysis frequency 
(beta = -0.362, p = 0.003) independently predicted lower HRQoL.
CONCLUSION: HRQoL contrasts among Moroccan hemodialysis patients highlight 
urgent needs to manage fatigue and encourage structured physical and social 
participation.
