MagGami: An Electromagnetic Origami Actuator With High Stiffness-Switching 
Density for Lightweight Joint-Space Wearable Haptics.

Jin T(#)(1)(2), Niu Z(#)(1)(2), Tang Q(1)(2), Wang Z(1)(2), Qiao Y(1)(2), Yao 
G(3), Zhou Y(4), Shan B(1)(2), Zhang Y(1)(2), Wang D(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)State Key Laboratory of Virtual Reality Technology and Systems, Beihang 
University, Beijing, China.
(2)School of Mechanical Engineering and Automation, Beihang University, Beijing, 
China.
(3)Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, Beijing, China.
(4)Linkerbot Beijing Technology Co., Ltd, Beijing, China.
(#)Contributed equally

Kinesthetic feedback gloves play a central role in immersive virtual and 
augmented reality (VR/AR) by enabling the perception of object shape, stiffness, 
and spatial constraints. However, key challenges remain: 1) achieving a large 
stiffness contrast between free-space and constrained-space states, 2) enabling 
independent actuation on finger joints, and 3) maintaining lightweight, 
low-power wearable operation. Here, we introduce MagGami, a miniaturized 
origami-based variable-stiffness actuator weighing 1.2 g for distributed 
joint-space integration. By combining origami geometric interlocking with an 
electromagnetic bistable mechanism, it can be triggered by transient current 
pulses at the flattened 0° configuration of the origami mechanism. MagGami 
switches from a freely compliant state to a self-locked high-resistance state 
with a mean locking response time of 102.8 ms, while requiring no coil power to 
hold the locked state. The mean device-level locked-to-free effective 
rotational-stiffness ratio is 795.46, corresponding to a module-level 
stiffness-switching density of 6.63 × 105 kg- 1, and the specified switching 
cycle consumes 444 mJ. MagGami uses distributed joint-space actuation to deliver 
lightweight, independently addressable binary constraint cues at individual 
finger joints, thereby enhancing the perception of virtual spatial constraints 
and high-resistance contact in VR/AR interactions. This work demonstrates a 
compact and energy-efficient strategy for next-generation wearable haptic 
interfaces.

Chiral-Nematic Lattice Instability in Charge Density Wave of 1T-TiSe(2).

Alghifari AA(1)(2), Do E(1), Park JW(1), Yeom HW(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Center for Artificial Low Dimensional Electronic Systems, Institute for Basic 
Science (IBS), Pohang, Republic of Korea.
(2)Department of Physics, Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH), 
Pohang, Republic of Korea.

Chiral charge-density waves (CDWs) are a rare form of electronic order with 
handedness, enabling novel couplings among light, lattice, and topology in 
quantum materials. Yet the microscopic origin of chirality has remained elusive, 
even in the prototypical chiral CDW system 1T-TiSe2. Using ab initio 
calculations, we investigate the structural stability and electronic structure 
of competing CDW models in 1T-TiSe2. We show that a chiral monoclinic ( C2 ) 
structure is stabilized by the cooperative condensation of multiple phonon modes 
and reproduces the chiral topography and energy gap observed experimentally. We 
further find an exceptionally soft potential landscape around this 
energy-minimized structure, along the direction that removes the remaining 
rotational symmetry, allowing the lattice to fluctuate through fully asymmetric 
configurations while its average structure remains chiral. This dynamical chiral 
CDW naturally reconciles the chiral domains seen by time-averaged topographic 
probes with the complete loss of symmetry detected by bulk spectroscopy, and 
clarifies how chiral CDWs emerge from the interplay of lattice instability and 
fluctuation.

Polat Dünya C(1), Tuncer M(2), Özkan İ(3), Yalçın GY(4), Gündüz T(5), Kürtüncü

effects on sexual function and quality of life. Eighty-six women aged 
18-45 years were randomized to counseling (n = 43) or control (n = 43). 
Sixty-three participants completed all follow-up assessments and were included 
in the complete-case analysis (counseling, n = 31; control, n = 32). The 
intervention comprised four counseling sessions over four weeks. Outcomes were

Gao J(#)(1), Guo S(#)(1), Ji Z(1), Cao M(1), Lu W(1), Ding L(1), Chen J(1), Qu

Although ion gels are promising for flexible sensing, simultaneously achieving 
high mechanical strength, stretchability, ionic conductivity, and interfacial 
adhesion remains challenging. Here, we report the preparation of ion gels with 
tunable mechanical properties using two ionic liquids (ILs) with different 
compatibilities with poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) via a one-pot ultraviolet

and enable repeatable monitoring of human joint motions and daily activities.

engineering high-performance ion gels for wearable sensing.

Preoperative apical margin risk estimation from T2-weighted MRI radiomics in 
prostate cancer with MRI-visible apical tumors: toward multidisciplinary 
decision support.

Liu Y(1), Zhao YZ(2), Liu S(3), Gao XS(2), Ma MW(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Radiology, Peking University First Hospital, Beijing 100034, 
China.
(2)Department of Radiation Oncology, Peking University First Hospital, Beijing 
100034, China.
(3)Department of Radiology, Aerospace Center Hospital, Beijing 100049, China.

This retrospective study developed and validated a T2-weighted imaging 
(T2WI)-based radiomics model for preoperative prediction of apical positive 
surgical margins (PSMs) in patients undergoing radical prostatectomy for 
prostate cancer. Overall, 235 patients (74 with apical PSMs and 161 without 
apical PSMs) were randomly divided into a training set (n = 164; 69.8%) and an 
independent test set (n = 71; 30.2%). Eligible patients had preoperative 
multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging within 6 weeks before surgery, an 
index lesion involving or abutting the prostatic apex, definitive apical margin 
status, and standard radical prostatectomy without nerve-sparing. Patients with 
inadequate imaging for apical assessment or region-of-interest delineation, 
prior transurethral resection of the prostate, or neoadjuvant 
androgen-deprivation therapy were excluded. A total of 1409 radiomic features 
were extracted from T2WI. After normalization and removal of highly correlated 
features (|r| > 0.99), six optimal features were selected by recursive feature 
elimination. A gradient boosting machine model was constructed, and performance 
was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 
(AUC), Brier score, and decision curve analysis. The apical PSM rate was 31.5%. 
In the test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.874, Brier score of 0.120, 
accuracy of 87.3%, sensitivity of 81.8%, and specificity of 89.8%. Skewness was 
the most important feature, contributing 34.8% to the model. Apical PSMs were 
significantly associated with extraprostatic extension (P = 0.001), and the 
tumor-margin model provided the greatest net clinical benefit. T2WI-based 
radiomics may support individualized preoperative risk assessment and surgical 
planning for prostate cancer.

Minimal-Burden Prosthodontics: Simple Care and Comprehensive Risk Assessment in 
Older Adults.

Molinero-Mourelle P(1)(2)(3)(4), Schimmel M(1), Mosaddad SA(2)(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Reconstructive Dentistry and Gerodontology, School of Dental 
Medicine, University of Bern, Bern, Switzerland.
(2)Department of Conservative Dentistry and Prosthodontics, Faculty of 
Dentistry, Complutense University of Madrid, Madrid, Spain.
(3)Ramon y Cajal Research Institute (IRYCIS), Madrid, Spain.
(4)Restorative Dental Sciences, Faculty of Dentistry, The University of Hong 
Kong, Hong Kong, China.
(5)Department of Research Analytics, Saveetha Dental College and Hospitals, 
Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, Saveetha University, 
Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India.

BACKGROUND: Older adults represent a growing population in whom oral health 
impairment may affect comfort, nutrition, dignity, social participation, and 
quality of life. Conventional prosthodontic approaches, often guided by 
comprehensive rehabilitation, technical refinement, and long-term restorative 
ideals, require assessment of present and foreseeable functional, cognitive, and 
maintenance needs.
OBJECTIVE: This commentary discusses minimal-burden prosthodontics as an 
application of established gerodontology principles to independent and 
semi-dependent community-dwelling older adults.
DISCUSSION: The concept does not imply that prosthodontic care can be 
burden-free. All prostheses carry biological, functional, temporal, 
psychological, and maintenance-related costs, and no prosthesis is permanent. 
These burdens should be explicitly identified, minimized, and justified by 
meaningful benefit. Building on rational dental care, geriatric dental 
assessment, the Seattle Care Pathway, minimal intervention dentistry, and 
patient-priorities-aligned care, comprehensive risk assessment should precede 
rehabilitation and establish a feasible maintenance plan. Proportional care 
serves as the ethical principle, prosthodontic sufficiency as the clinical 
objective, and contingency planning as a practical requirement if later frailty, 
cognitive decline, or loss of support makes treatment unmaintainable. Homebound 
patients require explicit arrangements for access and follow-up.
CONCLUSION: When the patient's main wish is to eat comfortably and enjoy daily 
life, the goal should be the simplest suitable care that achieves that wish.

Pseudo-Haptic Feedback: Multi-Modal Approaches to Stiffness Perception and User 
Experience.

Cansev ME(1), Sun X(2), Salvietti G(3), Prattichizzo D(3), Beckerle P(1)(4).

Author information:
(1)Chair of Autonomous Systems and Mechatronics, Department of Electrical 
Engineering, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, Erlangen, 
Germany.
(2)Department of Electrical Engineering, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität 
Erlangen-Nürnberg, Erlangen, Germany.
(3)Department of Information Engineering and Mathematics, University of Siena, 
Siena, Italy.
(4)Department of Artificial Intelligence in Biomedical Engineering, 
Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, Erlangen, Germany.

Pseudo-haptics is a technique that creates the illusion of haptic sensations in 
virtual environments by leveraging visual feedback and the interplay between 
visual and haptic perception. Pseudo-haptic feedback can enhance virtual reality 
interactions by providing perceptual cues that substitute for or complement 
physical haptic feedback. This work extends a 3D deformation rendering approach 
to generate visual deformation cues for stiffness perception in virtual reality 
and evaluates their impact on user experience through a user study measuring 
presence and workload. Results from a user study ( n = 20 ) indicate that 
deformation cues support stiffness perception at levels comparable to physical 
haptic feedback in both objective and subjective measures. Combining 
pseudo-haptic and force feedback further enhances stiffness perception accuracy 
and presence without increasing workload. These findings demonstrate that 
well-designed pseudo-haptic feedback mechanisms can effectively complement or 
substitute for force feedback in virtual reality interactions.

(4)Department of Future Energy Engineering (DFEE), Sungkyunkwan University 
(SKKU), Suwon, Republic of Korea.

Photoelectrochemical (PEC) solar energy conversion offers a promising route for 
transforming sunlight into chemical fuels and value-added products through 
light-driven redox reactions at semiconductor-electrolyte interfaces. Among 
semiconductor photoabsorbers, black silicon (b-Si) is particularly attractive 
because its micro-/nanostructured surface enables ultralow reflectance, 
broadband light absorption, a large electrode-electrolyte interfacial area, and 
versatile integration of catalysts and protective layers. These characteristics 
allow b-Si to combine effective photon management with interfacial reaction 
engineering, making it relevant to a broad range of PEC processes. This review 
first introduces the fundamental characteristics of b-Si and summarizes 
representative fabrication methods, with emphasis on the relationships among 
processing, morphology, and physicochemical properties. It then examines how 
these properties affect PEC water splitting, nitrate reduction, nitrogen 
reduction, and carbon dioxide reduction. Particular attention is given to the 
roles of surface morphology, junction design, passivation, catalyst integration, 
charge separation and transport, and the local reaction environment in governing 
activity, selectivity, and stability. Finally, the major limitations of 
b-Si-based PEC systems-including charge-carrier recombination, photocorrosion, 
parasitic reactions, and mass-transport constraints-are critically assessed. On 
this basis, future research directions are proposed for developing 
reaction-adaptive b-Si photoelectrodes capable of efficient, selective, durable, 
and practically relevant solar-fuel and chemical production.

Bipolar Disorder and the Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases: A Systematic Review 
and Meta-Analysis of Observational Studies.

Motta FDS(1)(2), Ruffini ML(1)(3), Ritter AC(1)(4), Ferrão SM(1)(3), Silva 
RS(1)(2), Mastella NDS(1)(3), Montezano BB(1)(2)(5), Ajub E Neto(6), Kapczinski

(1)Laboratory of Molecular Psychiatry, Centro de Pesquisa Experimental (CPE) and

(2)Department of Psychiatry, Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul, School

(3)Hospital de Clínicas de Porto Alegre, Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do

INTRODUCTION: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a chronic psychiatric illness 
characterized by recurrent manic and depressive episodes, affecting 2% of the 
global population. It is associated with premature mortality, including 
cardiovascular disease (CVD)-related mortality. Although clinically important, 
the absolute burden and incidence of cardiovascular outcomes in BD remain 
incompletely characterized. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized 
observational evidence on CVD prevalence and incidence in adults with BD.
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines and prospectively registered in PROSPERO 
(CRD42023484712), we searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and 
PsycInfo, screening 11,909 records. Thirty-two observational studies in adults 
with BD were included after Newcastle-Ottawa Scale assessment. Data were 
extracted on overall CVD, coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular disease, 
peripheral arterial disease, comorbidities, and psychotropic exposure. Pooled 
prevalence and incidence rate ratios were calculated using random-effects models 
when data were comparable.
RESULTS: The pooled CVD prevalence in BD was 7.70% (95% CI: 5.07-11.52), with 
coronary artery disease at 6.89% (95% CI: 4.05-11.47), cerebrovascular disease 
at 4.45% (95% CI: 2.13-9.05), and peripheral arterial disease at 3.30% (95% CI: 
1.66-6.45). However, prevalence estimates showed extreme heterogeneity and 
should be interpreted as broad indicators of absolute burden rather than precise 
estimates for a single BD population. In controlled incidence studies, BD was 
associated with increased CVD incidence (IRR 1.66, 95% CI: 1.32-2.08), with 
elevated coronary and cerebrovascular estimates. Clinical variable analyses 
involving medication use, lifestyle factors, and cardiometabolic comorbidities 
were not feasible because reporting was insufficient and noncomparable.
CONCLUSION: Adults with BD show substantial cardiovascular burden and increased 
incidence. However, extreme heterogeneity, limited incidence data, observational 
designs, and insufficient moderator reporting limit the precision and 
generalizability of pooled estimates. These findings support integrated 
cardiovascular screening in BD populations and future prospective studies.

Development of the Readiness to Change Diet Questionnaire (RCdQ) for Assessing 
Willingness to Adopt Anti-Inflammatory Diet Among Coronary Artery Disease 
Patients.

Chauhan S(1), Singh A(1), Kaur S(1), Bhushan S(1), Ghosh-Jerath S(2), Roy A(1).

Author information:
(1)All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, India.

This study aimed to develop and validate a questionnaire to assess readiness to 
change for adopting an anti-inflammatory diet among patients with coronary 
artery disease. The Readiness to Change Questionnaire-Treatment Version (RCQ-TV) 
was adapted for dietary behavior, translated into Hindi, and evaluated using an 
e-Delphi approach for face validation. The study was conducted in the National 
Capital Region, India. Domain experts (n = 6) assessed the clarity, content, and 
structure of the adapted questionnaire across iterative rounds, and 
consensus-driven revisions were made. The validated tool was subsequently pilot 
tested among 25 participants. Scores for each stage of change were calculated 
using an established scoring template, with the highest scale score indicating 
stage of readiness. Open-ended expert feedback from each iteration was 
summarized to inform revisions, and internal consistency was assessed using 
Cronbach's alpha. Modifications included simplification of terminology, revision 
of instructions and specific items, addition of definitions, and simplification

pre-contemplation stage, 10 in contemplation, and 13 in the action stage. The 
questionnaire demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .73).

items, and response options understandable, relevant, and appropriate, although 
10 participants required assistance to complete it. Overall, the adapted 
questionnaire demonstrated satisfactory face validity, internal consistency, and 
usability in both English and Hindi, suggesting wide applicability for assessing 
readiness to change dietary behavior in populations.

The abscopal effect, a systemic phenomenon induced by localized irradiation and 
associated with inflammatory factor activation, has attracted significant 
interest in the context of radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy. While 
recognized as potentially beneficial in oncology, this effect can have 
detrimental off-target consequences. The underlying mechanisms for abscopal

Deng W(1)(2)(3), Yang Y(1)(2)(3), Wang T(1)(2)(3), Chu C(1)(2)(3), Cai

BACKGROUND: Chinese cabbage is one of the most widely consumed vegetables in 
China. However, malodorous compounds generated from the decomposition of 
discarded leaves during harvest and distribution have become a significant 
environmental concern. This study aimed to identify the key odor compounds 
produced during Chinese cabbage decompostion and to characterize their 
associations with microbial community dynamics.
RESULTS: Physicochemical monitoring showed declining total solids and sugars, 
rising soluble protein, and fluctuating total nitrogen. Gas

disulfide and dimethyl trisulfide as early dominant odorants. The content of

principal odor compounds during Chinese cabbage decomposition, with indole 
dominating the later stages. Microbial succession drives the temporal shift in 
odor profiles. Rhodotorula mucilaginosa and Yarrowia lipolytica were validated 
as highly effective indole-degrading agents, highlighting their potential for 
biological odor mitigation during cabbage decomposition, although their capacity 
for sulfur-compound removal remains limited. © 2026 Society of Chemical

Alati NA(1), Arya PH(1), Tian Y(1), Reddy A(1), Ritzer DB(1)(2), Abdollahi

Photovoltaics and solar thermal collectors each face limitations in efficiently 
harnessing solar energy. This study presents a hybrid semi-transparent 
perovskite-photovoltaic and concentrating solar thermal (SPV-CST) collector 
designed to maximize solar energy utilization through spectral splitting. The 
perovskite solar cell captures both diffuse and direct solar irradiance, 
converting shorter-wavelength sunlight into electricity while transmitting the 
near-infrared spectrum. The SPV-CST collector achieves effective thermal 
decoupling between the photovoltaic and thermal components. Specifically, the

producing heat at temperatures ranging from 88.0°C to 154.9°C. Meanwhile, the 
operating temperature of the perovskite solar cell is limited to 38.5°C to 
reduce thermal stability issues and preserve its electrical efficiency at 13.8%.

the SPV-CST collector is projected to improve its electrical efficiency from 
13.8% to 21.3%, with only a slight reduction in thermal efficiency from 20.7% to 
19.2% at 100°C output temperature. This work provides insights into the design, 
modeling, and operational optimization of hybrid solar collectors, paving the 
way for sustainable solar energy applications across diverse conditions and 
climates.

Hypothalamic POMC Neurons Gate the Fear-Feeding Trade-Off.

Miralpeix C(#)(1), Eraso-Pichot A(#)(1), Simon V(1), Jouque V(1), Sadallah M(1), 
Clark S(1), Zizzari P(1), Skupio U(1), Covelo A(1), Dupuy N(1), Nicolas JC(1),

To survive, animals must constantly balance the need to obtain food with the 
need to avoid danger. Feeding is essential, yet perceived danger shifts priority 
toward safety and transiently suppresses food intake, even when organisms are 
hungry. Hypothalamic pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons align metabolic outputs 
with energy demands and control feeding. However, the role of POMC neurons in 
determining the trade-off between feeding and threat responses remains unclear.

integrators of metabolic and stress signals that bias decision making between

Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Dentistry: A Scoping Review.

Rokhshad R(1), Tichy A(2)(3), Chen JW(1), Taheri S(4), Motamedi S(5), 
Schwendicke F(2).

Author information:
(1)Pediatric Dentistry Department, Loma Linda University School of Dentistry, 
Loma Linda, California, USA.
(2)Clinic for Conservative Dentistry, Periodontology and Digital Dentistry, LMU 
University Hospital, Munich, Germany.
(3)Institute of Dental Medicine, First Faculty of Medicine, Charles University, 
Prague, Czech Republic.
(4)Loma Linda School of Dentistry, Loma Linda, California, USA.
(5)Endodontics Department, Loma Linda School of Dentistry, Loma Linda, 
California, USA.

This review scoped artificial intelligence (AI) in paediatric dentistry to 
summarize current applications and limitations. A comprehensive literature 
search was completed across PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, Embase, IEEE Xplore, 
and medRxiv/aArXiv. The preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and 
Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) checklist was used for 
reporting the present study. Studies concerning paediatric dentistry and 
utilizing AI, machine learning (ML) or large language models (LLMs) were 
included. Two independent reviewers screened and three extracted data on AI 
methodologies, performance metrics, and clinical applications. Fifty-nine 
studies were included. Computer vision studies (n = 32) most often used 
panoramic radiographs (n = 14), mainly for tooth detection, numbering and 
segmentation (n = 10) and caries detection (n = 9). Non-imaging ML studies 
(n = 18) primarily used clinical variables and questionnaire data (n = 8) or 
salivary/biological samples (n = 10). Accuracy ranged from 50% to 100%, with 
sensitivity reaching 100% in biomarker-based studies. LLM accuracy varied widely 
(33%-96%). Computer vision and non-imaging ML show promise for paediatric 
dentistry, particularly in the detection of dental structures and diseases, as 
well as risk stratification. Variable LLM performance underscores the need for 
standardized evaluation before clinical integration. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: 
AI-based tools may support paediatric dentists by improving tooth detection, 
dental structure assessment, caries detection, disease prediction and risk 
stratification. Computer vision and non-imaging machine learning approaches 
appear to have potential, but their clinical value depends on robust external 
validation, transparent reporting and integration into paediatric dental 
workflows. Given their variable performance, AI tools should be used only as 
adjunctive tools or a second reviewer.

(1)Department of Clinical Nutrition, NewYork-Presbyterian Weill Cornell, New

BACKGROUND: Feeding guidelines (FGs) reduce the incidence of necrotizing 
enterocolitis (NEC) and improve growth and enteral nutrition (EN) practices in 
very low birth weight (VLBW) infants. Our unit's baseline data revealed delayed 
initiation of EN, prolonged time to full EN, prolonged days on parenteral 
nutrition (PN), and frequent use of peripherally inserted central catheters 
(PICC). After introduction of this FG, our specific, measurable, attainable, 
realistic, and time-bound (SMART) aims were to reduce PICC placements in infants 
1000-1500 g by 30% and to reduce the time to achieve full EN in VLBW infants by 
20% without adversely impacting NEC rate, growth, and mom's own milk (MOM)

t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and chi-square tests were used to analyze 
demographic data, numerical variables, and categorical variables, respectively. 
Statistical process control charts and established rules for special cause 
variation were applied.
RESULTS: Our results demonstrate a 54% reduction in PICC placements and a 38% 
reduction in time to achieving full EN. We saw no increase in NEC rate but 
observed a decrease in growth and MOM provision.
CONCLUSION: The use of a standardized FG resulted in fewer PICC placements and 
decreased time to full EN without increasing the NEC rate. Future initiatives 
will focus on improving growth and MOM provision in VLBW infants.

Validity and agreement of bioelectrical impedance equations against dual energy 
X-ray absorptiometry for muscle mass assessment in patients on hemodialysis: A 
cross-sectional study.

Borges S(1), Martins TF(2), Machado FVC(3)(4), Júnior GC(1), Cipriano GFB(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Health Sciences and Technologies Graduate Program, University of Brasília 
(UnB), Brasília, Brazil.
(2)Rehabilitation Sciences Program, University of Brasília (UnB), Brasília, 
Brazil.
(3)Rehabilitation Research Center (REVAL), Faculty of Rehabilitation Sciences, 
Hasselt University, Diepenbeek, Belgium.
(4)Biomedical Research Institute (BIOMED), Faculty of Medicine and Life 
Sciences, Hasselt University, Diepenbeek, Belgium.

BACKGROUND: Low muscle mass is common in patients on hemodialysis (HD), and 
bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) predictive equations have been proposed 
as an alternative for estimating muscle mass. This study aimed to analyze the 
validity and agreement of different BIA-based prediction equations against dual 
energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) for estimating skeletal muscle mass (SMM) and 
appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASMM) in patients on HD.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study enrolled patients on HD. Clinical and 
laboratory data and body composition by BIA and DXA were collected. The accuracy 
of six prediction equations (Janssen, Barbosa-Silva, Kyle, Lin, Macdonald, and 
Sergi) for estimating SMM and ASMM was tested against DXA as the reference 
standard. Agreement was assessed using Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient 
(CCC), Bland-Altman analysis, Kappa statistics, Receiver Operating 
Characteristic (ROC) curves, and Passing-Bablok regression.
RESULTS: The sample consisted of 57 participants, age 52 ± 13 years, 32 (56%) 
male, median dialysis vintage 14 (4-40) months, 17 (30%) with diabetes, and 48 
(84%) with hypertension. The best agreement with DXA was observed for the Lin 
(CCC = 0.911), Sergi (CCC = 0.902) and Kyle (CCC = 0.902) equations. For low 
muscle mass diagnosis, Kappa values ranged from moderate to substantial, with 
the Lin equation showing the highest agreement (κ = 0.734). Additionally, the 
Lin equation demonstrated good accuracy (AUC = 0.794, 95% CI 0.68-0.91), with 
68,4% sensitivity and 89.5% specificity.
CONCLUSION: The Lin equation provided the most accurate and reproducible 
estimates of muscle mass compared with DXA and showed good diagnostic 
performance for low muscle mass in patients on HD.

Tropical leaf phenology as a thermoregulation trait: how changes in crown 
structure modulate thermal dynamics for two dominant Hawaiian trees.

Bayliss SLJ(1), Broadbent EN(2), Almeyda Zambrano AM(3), Pau S(1)(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Environmental Science, Policy and Management, University of 
California, Berkeley, Berkeley, CA, 94704, USA.
(2)School of Forest, Fisheries & Geomatics Sciences, University of Florida, 
Gainesville, FL, 32608, USA.
(3)Center for Latin American Studies, University of Florida, Gainesville, FL, 
32608, USA.
(4)Department of Geography, University of California, Berkeley, Berkeley, CA, 
94704, USA.

Canopy and leaf temperatures often diverge from air temperature, influencing 
photosynthesis, water loss, and heat stress. While leaf traits are known to 
affect heat exchange, how changes in crown structure interact with environmental 
drivers to regulate canopy thermal dynamics is poorly understood, particularly 
in tropical forests. In a Hawaiian wet tropical montane forest, we used repeated 
UAV-based (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) thermal and LiDAR (light detection and 
ranging) measurements of sunlit leaves within and across 397 tree crowns of 
Acacia koa and Metrosideros polymorpha to investigate (1) seasonal and 
species-specific variation in crown traits; (2) how crown traits and 
environmental drivers interact to determine canopy-air temperature differences 
(Tdiff), within-crown thermal variability (TcanSD), and maximum leaf 
temperatures (TcanMAX); and (3) whether crowns with greater seasonal structural 
change exhibit enhanced thermoregulation. All crown traits showed 
species-specific seasonal dynamics, with trait-trait and trait-environment 
interactions shaping thermal metrics differently across species. In M. 
polymorpha, crowns with greater seasonal structural change exhibited lower 
relative Tdiff, whereas A. koa did not show this buffering effect. These results 
indicate that canopy thermoregulation emerges from interacting crown traits 
dynamically reshaped across phenological and seasonal cycles. Seasonal crown 
dynamics provide partial thermal buffering in some species, highlighting 
species-specific pathways of thermal acclimation or vulnerability under climate 
change.

Who Do We Trust to Correct Health Misinformation? Credibility of AI-Generated 
Fact-Checking Messages.

Moon WK(1), Lim HS(2).

Author information:
(1)College of Journalism and Communications, University of Florida.
(2)School of Journalism and Communication, University of Oregon.

As artificial intelligence (AI)-generated messages are increasingly used to 
correct health misinformation, it remains unclear when such messages are 
perceived as credible and how credibility shapes subsequent information 
behaviors. This study examines how source labeling (AI vs. human scientists) 
influences the perceived credibility of health-related fact-checking messages 
and whether these effects depend on perceived AI objectivity and trust in 
science. Using a 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment with U.S. adults (N = 231), 
we assessed credibility perceptions and three information responses: 
accuracy-oriented information seeking, fact-checking message sharing, and 
issue-relevant information avoidance. Source labeling alone did not affect 
perceived credibility. Instead, credibility judgments were conditional. 
Perceived credibility was positively associated with message sharing and 
negatively associated with information avoidance but was not robustly related to 
accuracy-oriented information seeking. Independent of credibility, AI-labeled 
fact-checking messages elicited greater intentions to seek additional 
information. These findings highlight the conditional nature of AI credibility 
in health communication and underscore the importance of aligning AI-based 
fact-checking with audience trust orientations.

Combined Host-Derived and Microbiological Biomarkers for the Detection of 
Peri-Implant Bone Loss: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study.

Arce M(1)(2), Lima C(2), Virto L(2), Gamonal JD(2), Banaco D(2), Romandini M(3), 
Sanz M(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Conservative Dentistry, School of Dentistry, University of 
Chile, Santiago, Chile.
(2)ETEP Research Group, School of Dentistry, Complutense University of Madrid, 
Madrid, Spain.
(3)Department of Implant Dentistry, Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital, Shanghai 
Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Shanghai, China.

AIM: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of host-derived and microbiological 
biomarkers, alone and in combination with clinical parameters, for the detection 
of peri-implant bone loss (BL).
METHODS: A university-based cohort of subjects with dental implants was examined 
at baseline and after a mean follow-up of 3.9 years. Peri-implant BL served as 
the reference standard, defined as > 1 mm between baseline and follow-up 
radiographs; implants with < 0.5 mm BL served as controls. At follow-up, 
peri-implant crevicular fluid and submarginal-microbiological samples were 
collected. Bone metabolism and inflammatory biomarkers were quantified using 
Luminex technology. Bacterial loads were quantified by qPCR. Associations of 
biomarkers with BL were evaluated using multilevel logistic regression models. 
Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using ROC curves, with AUC, sensitivity, 
specificity, and predictive values reported.
RESULTS: Seventy-one subjects with 273 implants were included. Twenty-eight 
exhibited peri-implant-BL > 1.0 mm over the follow-up period. Increased levels 
of IL-1β, T. denticola, Fusobacterium spp., and T. forsythia were associated 
with BL in unadjusted analyses. However, these associations were no longer 
statistically significant after adjustment for clinical parameters. Individual 
biomarkers demonstrated limited diagnostic accuracy (maximum AUC = 0.68). In 
contrast, biomarker combinations with clinical parameters exhibited excellent 
discriminative performance (AUC > 0.95). The combination of IL-1β and BoP-or-PPD 
achieved the highest accuracy (AUC = 0.97).
CONCLUSIONS: While individual biomarkers showed limited diagnostic utility, 
combining multiple predictors significantly improved the ability to detect 
peri-implant BL. Combining IL-1β with either BoP or PPD significantly 
outperformed individual clinical measures but did not outperform the combination 
of clinical parameters, highlighting the potential of integrated biomarker and 
clinical parameter approaches as screening tools for detecting BL.

Ball AE(1), Lannin NA(2)(3), Glinsky JV(4)(5), Dean CM(1), McCredie L(3), 
Christie LJ(6)(7)(8), Scrivener K(1)(2)(3).

Author information:

(2)Department of Neuroscience, School of Translational Medicine, Monash

(5)John Walsh Centre for Rehabilitation Research, Northern Sydney Local Health

BACKGROUND: High-dose motor training is rarely implemented later after stroke. 
This study explored intervention therapists' beliefs and experiences delivering 
a high-dose walking booster program (HiWalk) within a Phase II trial.
OBJECTIVE: The objectives of this study were to (i) describe the beliefs 
intervention therapists held about a high-dose walking booster program prior to 
delivery, (ii) report facilitators and barriers to delivery, and (iii) to 
describe the strategies intervention therapists used to maintain training 
intensity during the program.
METHODS: A multimethod design examined intervention therapists' perspectives of 
delivering a high-dose walking booster program to stroke survivors who were more

RESULTS: All therapists who delivered the HiWalk program (n = 6) participated.

Resources).
CONCLUSIONS: Intervention therapists can deliver a high-dose walking booster

AIM: This study aimed to describe the pharmacokinetics (PK) of levetiracetam 
(LEV) in term neonates treated for neonatal seizures secondary to 
hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE).
METHODS: Fifteen neonates were included and received a loading dose ranging from 
30 to 60 mg/kg followed by eight maintenance doses corresponding to one-fourth 
of the loading dose every 8 h. Five blood PK samples were drawn for each 
neonate: three after the loading dose and two after the last maintenance dose. 
Data were analysed by a population approach using NONMEM software. The possible 
relationship between LEV Cmax and AUC from time 0 to 4 h after the loading dose 
(AUC4h) and the relative seizure difference (RSD) that defined the LEV efficacy 
was investigated by linear regression.

(CLcr) and natremia were found to be significant covariates for LEV clearance 
(CL), CL increasing with CLcr and natremia. No relationship was found between 
LEV Cmax or AUC4h and RSD.
CONCLUSION: A population PK model of LEV in term neonates with HIE was 
developed. The influence of natremia was highlighted for the first time and 
could reflect the relationship between the encephalopathy severity and LEV PK in 
this population.

Fostering Psychological Safety From Unsafe Ground: Professional Identity and the 
Leadership Paradox in NHS Nursing and Midwifery.

Leader C(1), Sanders T(1), Potthoff S(1).

Author information:
(1)Northumbria University, Newcastle upon Tyne, UK.

AIM: To explore how nursing and midwifery (N&M) leaders draw on professional 
identity to navigate their role in relation to workforce wellbeing and 
psychological safety, and the consequences of this work when conducted within 
hostile organisational cultures.
DESIGN: Constructivist Grounded Theory.
METHODS: Eighteen participants holding current or recent formal leadership and 
management responsibilities within United Kingdom NHS settings were recruited 
via purposive sampling. Intensive semi-structured interviews were conducted and 
analysed using initial and focused coding, constant comparative analysis and 
memo writing.
RESULTS: Three interconnected themes were generated: (1) professional identity 
as the foundation for psychological safety work, with participants drawing on 
values of care, integrity and advocacy to build trust-based team cultures; (2) 
professional credibility as the currency of trust, with leaders' demonstrable 
connection to frontline practice acting as the primary mechanism translating 
professional identity into team trust; and (3) the paradox: professional 
identity under threat, whereby the same professional values driving 
participants' commitment to psychological safety placed them at risk within 
their own organisational contexts, generating cumulative moral distress. This is 
conceptualised as the leadership and wellbeing paradox: fostering psychological 
safety from unsafe ground.
CONCLUSION: N&M leaders cannot sustainably foster psychological safety when they 
are operating on unsafe ground.
IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Healthcare organisations 
must actively protect the psychological safety of N&M leaders for safe, 
compassionate care cultures. Failure to address the leadership and wellbeing 
paradox will continue to drive moral distress and attrition across the 
professions.
IMPACT: Professional identity was found to motivate and endanger leaders' 
psychological safety work, generating a paradox in which cumulative moral 
distress damages wellbeing and threatens retention. The findings have direct 
relevance for N&M leaders, healthcare organisations and policymakers addressing 
workforce attrition and culture change.
NO PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This study did not involve patient or public 
contribution. The research focused exclusively on the professional experiences 
and perceptions of nursing and midwifery leaders as study participants. Given 
the study's focus on leadership practice and workforce wellbeing from the 
perspective of professionals in leadership roles, patient, service user or 
public involvement in the design, conduct or analysis of the research was not 
applicable.

OBJECTIVES: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a 
debilitating condition associated with antiresorptive agents (ARAs) and can 
occur around well-osseointegrated dental implants. Although implant 
presence-triggered osteonecrosis (IPTO) has been primarily linked to

Konuma T(1), Monna-Oiwa M(1), Nagai E(2), Kato S(1), Andoh S(1), Kuroda J(1),

BACKGROUND: Newly positive hepatitis B virus (HBV) serologic results after 
allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) may reflect passive antibody 
transfer from blood-derived products rather than HBV infection. We investigated 
the incidence and temporal patterns of hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) 
and antibody to hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) acquisition after 
allogeneic HCT.

allogeneic HCT for hematologic diseases between May 2012 and March 2025 at a 
single institution in Japan. Anti-HBs, anti-HBc, and hepatitis B surface antigen

Yu C(1), Lado JL(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Applied Physics, Aalto University, Espoo, Finland.

Altermagnets feature unconventional magnetism due to their momentum-dependent 
spin splitting purely driven by magnetic order, for which a variety of 
transition-metal-based d -wave altermagnets have been proposed. However, 
carbon-based altermagnets remain largely unexplored, even though magnetism of 
graphene nanostructures has been widely demonstrated. Here, through a 
comprehensive symmetry analysis, we establish a symmetry-guided design principle 
for realizing higher-order i -wave altermagnetism in graphene antidot 
superlattices and demonstrate its emergence in both monolayer and bilayer

interaction-induced i -wave altermagnetic splitting, originating from the 
intrinsic magnetic instability of 2D graphene antidot superlattices. Our work 
establishes a strategy to engineer i -wave altermagnetism in a graphene 
platform, extending the materials landscape beyond conventional d -wave 
altermagnets and putting forward a carbon-based platform for higher-order 
altermagnetic spintronics.

Cytological Findings and Diagnostic Pitfalls of a Rare Tumor Arising From a Rare

Bohara S(1), Brij S(1), Gangwar S(1), Shukla P(1), Srivastava D(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pathology, Hind Institute of Medical Sciences, Safedabad,

(2)Department of Orthopedics, Hind Institute of Medical Sciences, Safedabad,

Chondromyxoid fibroma (CMF) is a rare, benign cartilaginous tumor composed of 
myxoid and fibrous components, accounting for approximately 1% of all bone 
tumors. It typically arises in the metaphysis of long bones, with epiphyseal 
involvement of the short tubular bones of the hand and foot being uncommon. We

hypercellular smears comprising pleomorphic oval to spindle-shaped cells along 
with dense, pink osteochondroid material; the cytological diagnosis was rendered

examination showed a well-circumscribed tumor with a lobular architecture 
composed of alternating hypocellular and hypercellular areas of myxomatous

fibroma. Although a low-grade tumor, CMF may show nuclear atypia histologically 
and can mimic chondrosarcoma; distinguishing between the two is of paramount 
importance to avoid over-diagnosis and unnecessarily aggressive treatment of 
this benign entity. Complete surgical resection with long-term follow-up remains 
the mainstay of management, given the relatively high rate of recurrence.

Recurrence Risk After Resection of Typical and Atypical Pulmonary Carcinoids: A 
Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

Guevara-Tirado A(1), Barra GG(1), Espinoza MFXB(1).

Author information:
(1)Universidad Científica del Sur, Lima, Peru.

BACKGROUND: Pulmonary carcinoids generally have favorable outcomes after 
surgery, but postoperative recurrence differs substantially by histological 
subtype. Existing guidance recognizes atypical histology and nodal involvement 
as adverse features, yet a focused quantitative synthesis of the magnitude and 
consistency of this association remains limited.
METHODS: MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception to July 
12, 2026 for surgical cohorts reporting postoperative recurrence. Two reviewers 
independently screened titles and abstracts and assessed full-text eligibility, 
with disagreements resolved by consensus. The primary meta-analysis emphasized 
the risk ratio (RR) of observed recurrence in atypical versus typical carcinoids 
using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood and modified 
Hartung-Knapp intervals; odds ratios (ORs) and risk differences were 
complementary measures. Time-defined recurrence, adjusted prognostic factors, 
and anatomical patterns were synthesized separately because of incompatible 
outcome definitions and effect measures.
RESULTS: Eighteen reports were included in the review, 11 contributed structured 
quantitative evidence, and 7 independent comparative cohorts entered the primary 
meta-analysis. Among 1074 resected tumors, recurrence occurred in 24 of 816 
typical carcinoids and 51 of 258 atypical carcinoids. The pooled RR of observed 
recurrence was 6.57 (95% CI, 3.65-11.84), with a complementary OR of 8.08 (95% 
CI, 4.20-15.53). No statistical heterogeneity was detected (I2 = 0%), but this 
result was interpreted cautiously because only seven studies were available and 
clinically important differences in follow-up, staging, pathological review, and 
surveillance remained. Leave-one-out RR estimates ranged from 5.77 to 7.48. 
Time-defined evidence suggested recurrence of approximately 18%-25% by 5 years 
and 29%-32% by 10 years in atypical tumors, whereas node-negative typical tumors 
generally remained below 5% at 10 years, although late events occurred. Nodal 
involvement, advanced pT category, and larger tumor size were adverse prognostic 
features.
CONCLUSION: Observed recurrence after resection was substantially more frequent 
in atypical than in typical pulmonary carcinoids. Histology and nodal status 
provide a clinically useful basis for postoperative risk stratification, but the 
available evidence does not establish the optimal surveillance modality, 
interval, or duration.

OBJECTIVE: To assess and compare the prevalence and pattern of dental and 
craniofacial injuries sustained by conventional two-wheeler riders versus

accidents and orofacial injuries compared with conventional riders. After

Describe or Direct? Artificial Intelligence Explanation Type, Trust and User

O'Callahan K(1), Sitters S(1), O'Callahan M(1), Senior-Partridge A(1), Kirtley 
M(1).

Author information:
(1)Unitec, Auckland, New Zealand.

INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into 
healthcare, with most healthcare AI applications concentrated in radiology. 
While explainable AI (XAI) has been proposed as a means of improving 
transparency and trust, the relationship between explanation features, trust and 
user behaviour remains underexplored, particularly in healthcare contexts. This 
study examined how final-year medical imaging students interacted with 
descriptive and prescriptive AI explanations during a simulated rostering task, 
with a focus on trust and user behaviour.
METHODS: A human-grounded evaluation using an explanatory mixed methods design 
was undertaken. Final year medical imaging students completed simulated 
rostering tasks using an XAI system that generated either descriptive or

explanations, alongside critical engagement with inaccuracies and regeneration 
patterns.

explanations within a simulated medical imaging rostering task and were 
associated with higher trust and reduced explanation regeneration. Participants

human interaction with XAI systems in healthcare workflow settings.

EXPRESS: Synaptic density PET mediates the relationship between Alzheimer's 
disease pathology and cognitive performance.

McLachlan MJ(1), Bettcher B(1), Langhough R(1), DiFilippo A(2), Betthauser T(1), 
McVea A(3), LeMerise L(1), Zammit M(1), Grover E(1), Jonaitis EM(4), Ennis G(1), 
Chin N(1), Asthana S(1), Johnson SC(1), Bendlin BB(4), Christian BT(1).

Author information:
(1)University of Wisconsin-Madison, Madison, WI, USA.
(2)Yale School of Medicine, New Haven, CT, USA.
(3)University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA.
(4)University of Wisconsin-Madison, Madison, WI, USA.

INTRODUCTION: Synaptic loss is one of the strongest post-mortem predictors of 
Alzheimer's disease (AD) severity and may impact how pathology affects 
cognition. This study compared regional [11C]UCB-J synaptic density across the 
AD continuum and evaluated the extent to which synaptic density mediates 
relationships between AD biomarkers.
METHODS: Seventy-two participants completed PET scans, MRIs, and cognitive 
testing. Participants were categorized into subgroups representing typical AD 
progression. Regional synaptic density was compared across subgroups and 
pathological variables. Standard mediation and moderated mediation analyses were 
performed using amyloid and tau as predictors/moderators and MoCA score as 
outcome.
RESULTS: The amyloid+/tau+/impaired subgroup showed lower synaptic density than 
controls, particularly for transverse temporal, inferior parietal, and 
hippocampal regions (Cohen's d=1.60, 1.57, 1.50). Hippocampal synaptic density 
had the strongest associations with tau (β=-0.473); transverse temporal synaptic 
density had the strongest association with amyloid (β=-0.543) and age 
(β=-0.614). Eight of twelve assessed brain regions demonstrated significant 
indirect effects across mediation frameworks. The inferior parietal lobe showed 
the largest mediation for amyloid (45.3%) and tau (28.9%).
DISCUSSION: These findings support the hypothesis that synaptic loss is a 
primary mechanism contributing to clinical AD and suggest that synaptic density 
imaging can provide complementary information to the existing AD framework.

Association With Glymphatic‑Related Cognitive Impairment.

Zhan C(1), Wang W(1)(2), Lu X(1)(3), Xie X(1), Li Y(4), Huang CC(5)(6).

Author information:
(1)Department of Neurology, WuHu Hospital, East China Normal University ( The 
Second People' s Hospital, WuHu), Anhui, 241000, China.
(2)Graduate School of Bengbu Medical university, Bengbu, Anhui, 233030, China.
(3)Graduate School of Wannan Medical university, Wuhu, Anhui, 241002, China.
(4)Shanghai Key Laboratory of Brain Functional Genomics (Ministry of Education),

(5)Shanghai Key Laboratory of Brain Functional Genomics (Ministry of Education),

Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a leading cause of vascular cognitive 
impairment. The glymphatic system, a brain-wide waste clearance pathway, may be 
impaired in CSVD, but its upstream drivers and role linking systemic factors to 
cognitive impairment remain unclear. This study explored whether glymphatic 
dysfunction statistically mediates the association between left-heart 
dysfunction and cognitive impairment in CSVD. We enrolled 80 CSVD-VCI, 80 
CSVD-NCI, and 80 normal controls aged 50-80 years. All participants underwent 
neuropsychological assessment, cardiac ultrasound (measuring left ventricular 
ejection fraction [LVEF], left ventricular end-diastolic diameter [LVEDD], and 
left atrial diameter [LAD]), and brain MRI to measure the DTI-ALPS index of 
glymphatic activity. The DTI-ALPS index was progressively reduced: NC > CSVD-NCI 
> CSVD-VCI. It correlated positively with LVEF and negatively with LAD, and was 
associated with multiple cognitive domains. Mediation analysis suggests that 
DTI-ALPS statistically significantly mediated the effects of LVEF and LAD on 
cognitive performance. These cross-sectional findings suggest that glymphatic 
dysfunction is a key feature of CSVD and may represent a potential correlative 
link connecting left-heart dysfunction to cognitive impairment, consistent with 
a potential cardio-glymphatic pathway in CSVD pathophysiology.

for Nimodipine's Neuroprotection in Traumatic Brain Injury.

Feng X(1), Cao W(2), Shen X(2), Yu H(2), Shen G(2), Qian Q(2), Xu Y(1), Fang 
J(2), Xu D(2), Xu Y(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Neurosurgery, The First Hospital of Jiaxing, Affiliated 
Hospital of Jiaxing University, Jiaxing, China.
(2)Department of Emergency, The First Hospital of Jiaxing, Affiliated Hospital

OBJECTIVE: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) induces severe secondary injury where 
molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigates the involvement of 
the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) 
signaling pathway in this process and evaluates the neuroprotective effect of 
the L-type calcium channel blocker nimodipine, focusing on calcium homeostasis, 
mitochondrial function, and inflammatory signaling.
METHODS: Using primary neuronal and mouse TBI models, we assessed outcomes via 
fluorescent calcium imaging, JC-1 staining, Western blot, quantitative PCR 
(qPCR)/reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction, 
enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and behavioral tests. Nimodipine was applied 
to inhibit L-type channels, specifically testing its role in reducing 
mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release, blocking cGAS-STING activation, and 
suppressing neuroinflammation.

pro-inflammatory factors and apoptosis. In the cellular oxygen-glucose 
deprivation model, calcium overload was directly observed by Fluo-4 AM staining 
and was associated with subsequent mitochondrial permeability transition pore 
opening and mtDNA release, identifying this process as a key upstream event for 
cGAS-STING activation. Nimodipine inhibited intracellular calcium overload, 
reduced mitochondrial injury and mtDNA release, and consequently suppressed 
cGAS-STING pathway activation. Both in vivo and in vitro experiments showed 
dose-dependent decreases in pro-inflammatory factors, along with improved 
neurological function and attenuated brain tissue pathology.

apoptosis after TBI by inhibiting calcium influx, decreasing mtDNA release, and 
suppressing cGAS-STING signaling. These results suggest that the 
Ca2+-mtDNA-cGAS-STING axis contributes to TBI pathology and that nimodipine may 
serve as a potential multitarget therapy. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 00, 000-000.

EXPRESS: Reperfusion-sensitive induction of endothelial NDRG1 identifies a 
dynamic vascular stress response to thrombolysis in ischemic stroke.

Furon J(1), Etuze T(1), Fosset L(1), Goulet R(1), Lemarchand E(1), Repesse 
Y(1)(2), Vivien D(1)(3), Dubois F(1)(4).

Author information:
(1)Normandie University, UNICAEN, INSERM UMR-S U1237, Physiopathology and 
Imaging of Neurological Disorders (PhIND), GIP Cyceron, Institut Brain, Blood 
and Memory @ Caen-Normandie (BBM@C), 14000, Caen, France.
(2)Haemophilia Treatment Centre CRC-MHC, Caen-Normandie University Hospital,

Ischemic stroke (IS) outcome critically depends on the neurovascular unit's 
capacity to respond to ischemia-reperfusion stress within the salvageable 
penumbra. Here, we characterize the spatiotemporal regulation of N-myc 
downstream-regulated gene 1 (NDRG1) and identify it as an early, 
reperfusion-sensitive marker of endothelial stress. Under physiological 
conditions, NDRG1 is primarily expressed in neurons and oligodendrocytes, with 
minimal endothelial expression. Following middle cerebral artery occlusion, 
NDRG1 undergoes marked spatial and cellular redistribution, becoming strongly 
induced in endothelial cells across the cerebrovascular tree.Endothelial NDRG1 
induction was detectable as early as 6 hours after ischemia and evolved from a 
vesicular pattern to diffuse vascular labeling by 24 hours. Importantly, 
recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator (rtPA) selectively enhanced 
endothelial NDRG1 expression in peri-lesional vessels in the rtPA-sensitive 
thrombin model, but not in the rtPA-resistant FeCl3 model, indicating that NDRG1 
induction is linked to effective reperfusion. In vitro, oxygen-glucose 
deprivation (OGD) recapitulated endothelial NDRG1 induction, further enhanced by 
rtPA through a pathway involving the LDL receptor family.Collectively, these 
findings identify endothelial NDRG1 as a dynamic molecular readout of 
reperfusion-sensitive vascular stress. NDRG1 may serve as a biomarker of 
endothelial responsiveness to thrombolytic therapy, providing new insight into 
cerebrovascular adaptations associated with successful reperfusion.

Skyrmion Bubbles by Design in a Centrosymmetric Kagome Magnet.

El Gazzah M(1)(2), Yasin FS(3)(4), Jamaluddin S(1)(2), Bhandari H(1)(2)(5), 
Regmi RB(1)(2), Yu X(4)(6), Ghimire NJ(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of Notre Dame, Notre Dame, 
Indiana, USA.
(2)Stavropoulos Center For Complex Quantum Matter, University of Notre Dame, 
Notre Dame, Indiana, USA.
(3)Center for Nanophase Materials Sciences, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak 
Ridge, Tennessee, USA.
(4)RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science, Wako, Japan.
(5)Department of Physics and Astronomy, Rice University, Houston, Texas, USA.
(6)Institute of Science Tokyo, Tokyo, Japan.

Topologically protected nanoscale spin textures, such as magnetic skyrmions, 
have attracted significant interest for spintronics applications. While 
skyrmions in noncentrosymmetric materials are known to be stabilized by the 
Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), their deliberate design in 
centrosymmetric materials remains a challenge. This difficulty largely stems 
from the complexity of controlling magnetocrystalline anisotropy-a critical 
factor in the absence of DMI. Here, we demonstrate the chemical tuning of 
magnetocrystalline anisotropy in the centrosymmetric Kagome magnet TmMn6Sn6 . 
The resulting compound exhibits a spin reorientation transition accompanied by 
an emergent skyrmion bubble lattice, confirmed by cryogenic Lorentz transmission 
electron microscopy and cryogenic Lorentz differential phase contrast scanning 
transmission electron microscopy. Our findings overcome a key materials design 
challenge and open possibilities for deliberate design of skyrmionic textures in 
centrosymmetric systems.

EXPRESS: Letter to the Editor Regarding "Much ado about eating: Intermittent 
fasting and post-stroke neuroprotection".

Carneiro GB(1), Pace CM(2), Figueiredo EG(3).

Author information:
(1)Division of Medicine, University of São Paulo, Av. Dr. Arnaldo, 455, 
Cerqueira César, São Paulo, SP 01246-903, Brazil.
(2)Division of Medicine, Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, Av. Carlos Chagas 
Filho, 373, Cidade Universitária, Rio de Janeiro, RJ 21941-902, Brazil.
(3)Division of Neurosurgery, University of São Paulo, Av. Dr. Enéas de Carvalho

Vemuganti and colleagues highlight intermittent fasting (IF)'s neuroprotective 
potential post-stroke via autophagy and mitochondrial biogenesis. However, 
clinical translation faces hurdles in metabolically vulnerable patients. This 
letter critiques IF's bedside applicability, emphasizing post-stroke catabolic 
stress, dysphagia (~50% cases), sarcopenia risk, and cardiovascular concerns. 
Recent evidence links short eating windows to higher mortality, countering IF 
benefits. The obesity paradox suggests nutritional reserves aid survival. 
Strategies: protein-prioritized planning, dysphagia screening, dietitian 
monitoring, and supplements. Until RCTs confirm safety/efficacy, prioritize 
nutritional adequacy. Preclinical insights warrant study.Keywords: dysphagia, 
intermittent fasting, neuroprotection, obesity paradox, sarcopenia.

Coordination Chemistry of Single-Atom Catalysts in Expediating Kinetics for 
Advanced Lithium-Sulfur Batteries.

Chen P(1)(2), Zhao J(3), Zhang J(4), Miao Y(5), Li W(6), Li H(7)(8), Wang 
J(7)(8), Zhang Y(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Textile and Clothing, Nantong University, Nantong, China.
(2)Institute for Innovative Materials and Energy, Faculty of Chemistry and 
Chemical Engineering, Yangzhou University, Yangzhou, China.
(3)School of pharmacy, Nantong University, Nantong, China.
(4)School of Materials Science and Engineering, Xi'an University of Technology, 
Xi'an, China.
(5)School of Material and Chemical Engineering, Xuzhou University of Technology, 
Xuzhou, China.
(6)School of Chemistry, University of Glasgow, Glasgow, UK.
(7)Helmholtz Institute Ulm (HIU), Ulm, Germany.
(8)Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT), Karlsruhe, Germany.

The shuttling effect and sluggish conversion kinetics of lithium polysulfides 
(LiPSs) hinder the further advancement of lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries, 
exhibiting high barriers. Among catalysts, single-atom catalysts (SACs) can 
accelerate LiPSs redox kinetics by leveraging M-S coordination, interfacial 
charge transfer, and anchoring effect of coordinating heteroatoms. Numerous 
researches have reported improved catalytic activity via screening central metal 
and coordinating atoms as well as optimizing coordination configurations. 
However, systematic summary concerning the principles in screening and design of 
asymmetric coordination structures, the evolution mechanisms of orbital 
hybridization and spatial geometry, and the corresponding structure-activity 
relationships governing LiPSs conversion kinetics remain unknown. In this 
review, we systematically summarize the modifications brought by asymmetric 
coordination chemistry and dual-atom coordination structures in terms of 
geometric configuration engineering, molecular orbital hybridization, and 
interfacial charge rearrangement, together with the underlying mechanisms for 
boosting LiPSs conversion kinetics. Centered on theoretical calculations 
supplemented by experimental validations, we elaborate the critical significance 
of asymmetric coordination chemistry of SACs in elevating the catalytic 
efficiency. Finally, the future developments of SACs in Li─S batteries are 
outlooked and prospected.

The Vertical Tarsotomy Technique: Serial Tarsotomies Enable Direct Closure of 
Moderate-to-Large Full-Thickness Eyelid Defects.

Kaur S(1), Malhotra R.

Author information:
(1)Corneoplastic Unit, Queen Victoria Hospital, East Grinstead, United Kingdom.

BACKGROUND: Direct closure of eyelid defects is traditionally limited to small 
defects of less than a third of the horizontal eyelid length due to concern 
regarding distortion of the palpebral aperture and risk of eyelid malposition. 
We describe a simple, reproducible technique using serial vertical 
full-thickness tarsotomy incisions to lengthen the residual eyelid. This 
facilitates direct closure of larger defects, avoiding the need for Tenzel, 
Macgregor, and in selected cases, even Hughes flaps.
METHODS: Single-center retrospective case series of patients undergoing eyelid 
reconstruction following periocular tumor excision. Serial vertical 
full-thickness tarsotomies were performed in the residual tarsus to increase 
eyelid length and facilitate direct closure. Patient demographics, tumor 
characteristics, defect size, reconstructive techniques, and complications were 
recorded.
RESULTS: Ten patients were included with a mean age of 78.5 years (range 65-93). 
Six (60%) patients were female, and basal cell carcinoma accounted for 90% of 
tumors. The lower eyelid was involved in 80% of cases. Defects ranged from 
one-third to two-thirds of the horizontal eyelid length, with the majority (70%) 
involving more than half of the eyelid. Additionally, internal lateral 
cantholysis was performed in 8 cases, and direct closure was achieved in all 
cases. Mean follow-up was 8.1 (range 5-17) months. Postoperative complications 
occurred in 3 patients, including corneal irritation requiring temporary bandage 
contact lens wear (n = 1) and mild ectropion (n = 2). There were no cases of 
wound dehiscence or sight-threatening complications.
CONCLUSION: Serial vertical tarsotomies represent a unique technique to increase 
eyelid length and facilitate direct closure of moderate-to-large eyelid margin 
defects. This approach offers favorable functional and aesthetic outcomes and 
may represent a new reconstructive option in the management of full-thickness 
eyelid defects.

Decoding Perovskite Interfaces: Machine Learning Uncovers Geometry-Matched 
Dual-Site Hydrogen Bonding.

Cheng C(#)(1)(2), Gu X(#)(3), Sun K(4), Wang R(2), Yang Z(1), Xu Y(1), Yang 
P(2), Wang Z(4), Wu J(1)(2), Chen H(3), Wu L(1).

Author information:
(1)State Key Laboratory of Chemistry for NBC Hazards Protection, College of 
Chemistry, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou, P. R. China.
(2)College of Physics and Information Engineering, Institute of Micro-Nano 
Devices and Solar Cells, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou, P. R. China.
(3)Center of Future Photovoltaics Research, Global Institute of Future 
Technology (GIFT), Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, P. R. China.
(4)Institute for Advanced Materials & Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of

Molecular passivation is central to efficient and stable perovskite 
photovoltaics, yet interfacial molecules are still largely selected through 
chemical intuition and iterative experimentation. Here, an interpretable 
machine-learning framework is developed that extracts chemically meaningful 
structure-performance relationships from literature data and uses them to guide 
molecular screening. Using approximately 100 data points, the model 
quantitatively relates six molecular and material features to photovoltaic 
performance, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis ranks their 
relative contributions and identifies hydrogen-bonding capacity and adsorption 
strength as the two most influential factors. Guided by these data-derived 
relationships, nine previously unexplored molecules were screened, with 
2-amino-thiazole-4-carboxamide (ATC) and 1-(2-aminoethyl)-1H-pyrrole-2,5-dione 
(MPD) emerging as leading candidates. Theoretical and experimental 
investigations show that MPD exhibits stronger Pb2 + coordination, whereas ATC 
forms stronger geometry-matched multisite N─H···I interactions, increasing the 
calculated iodide-migration barrier from 0.39 to 0.67 eV and suppressing 
interfacial iodide redistribution. ATC-modified cells achieve a PCE of 27.13% 
and a certified stabilized efficiency of 26.59%, while retaining 90% of their 
initial efficiency after 1460 h of unencapsulated operation. The strategy 
further delivers efficiencies of 24.01% and 21.14% in 20.98 cm2 rigid and 21.0 
cm2 flexible modules, respectively, providing a data-to-mechanism route for 
rational and scalable perovskite interface engineering.

Unidirectional Hydrogen Migration Through Interfacial Engineering for Promoted 
Brønsted Acid Catalysis.

Xing S(1)(2), Liang S(1)(3), Zhang S(1)(3), Jiang Q(1)(3), Ti J(1)(3), Ma J(4), 
Qin Y(5), Shi J(6), Gao Z(7).

Author information:
(1)State Key Laboratory of Coal Conversion, Institute of Coal Chemistry, Chinese 
Academy of Sciences, Taiyuan, China.
(2)School of Basic Medical Sciences, Hebei University, Baoding, China.
(3)Center of Materials Science and Optoelectronics Engineering, University of 
Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China.
(4)Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility, Shanghai Advanced Research 
Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai, China.
(5)College of Materials Science and Engineering, Qingdao University of Science 
and Technology, Qingdao, China.
(6)State Key Laboratory of High Performance Ceramics and Superfine 
Microstructure, Shanghai Institute of Ceramics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, 
Shanghai, China.
(7)School of Materials Science and Engineering, Tianjin University, Tianjin,

Though playing a critical role, the controllable and directional migration of 
reactive species in chemical reactions is still hard to achieve. Here, we 
propose an interfacial engineering strategy for constructing a hydrogen 
spillover nanodiode that channels hydrogen unidirectionally. Such a nanodiode 
design is materialized in a composite WOx/TiO2/Pt catalyst with spatially 
separated structure, where WOx and Pt particles are dispersed on the outer and 
inner surfaces of porous TiO2 nanotubes, respectively. This nanodevice permits 
forward H migration (Pt→TiO2→WOx) while suppresses the reverse path (WOx→TiO2), 
as directly evidenced by in situ x-ray absorption fine structure 
characterization under hydrogenation and H2 generation reactions. This 
rectification behavior originates from the diode characteristics of the TiO2-WOx 
heterojunction, which hinders both proton and electron transfer from WOx to 
TiO2. Consequently, WOx/TiO2/Pt accumulates highly concentrated Brønsted acid 
sites in H2 atmosphere and thus exhibits superior catalytic performance compared 
to the closely contacted WOx-Pt/TiO2 catalyst. Up to 5.3 times higher liquid 
alkane yield has been achieved over WOx/TiO2/Pt relative to WOx-Pt/TiO2 in the 
polyethylene hydrocracking reaction. This nanodiode design strategy is general 
and can be extended to other catalysts/species, offering mechanistic insight and 
boosting catalytic performance in diverse reactions.

EXPRESS: Quantification of arterial hemodynamics in steno-occlusive disease 
using time-resolved MRI-based angiography.

Deckers Q(1), Uniken-Venema SM(2), Braun KP(3), van der Zwan A(3), van Doormaal 
TPC(3), Deckers PT(2), Siero JC(1)(4), Bhogal A(1).

Author information:
(1)Translational Neuroimaging group, Center for Image Sciences, UMC Utrecht, 
Netherlands.
(2)Department of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine, UMC Utrecht, Netherlands.
(3)Brain Center, Department of Neurology and Neurosurgery, UMC Utrecht, 
Netherlands.
(4)Precision Imaging Group, Center for Image Sciences, UMC Utrecht, Netherlands.

BackgroundIntracranial steno-occlusive disease (SOD) assessment benefits from 
hemodynamic imaging, but comprehensive evaluation often relies on contrast- or 
radiation-based techniques. Arterial spin labeling (ASL) provides a non-invasive 
alternative for quantifying tissue-level perfusion and cerebrovascular 
reactivity, yet does not capture upstream arterial flow dynamics. As a result, 
non-invasive assessment of macrovascular hemodynamics for SOD remains limited. 
This study evaluates whether quantitative 4D-MRA provides complementary arterial 
information beyond established ASL-derived metrics.MethodsTwelve SOD patients (7 
women; age 42.3±25.8 years) underwent multi-delay ASL and 4D-MRA before and 
after acetazolamide. Cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR), arterial transit time 
(ATT), macrovascular ATT (mATT), and labeled blood volume (LBV) were quantified. 
Associations and vasodilatory responses were assessed using linear mixed-effects 
models.ResultsAt baseline, mATT correlated with ATT (β=0.66±0.08, p<0.001). Both 
decreased following acetazolamide (mATT: 1.07±0.03s to 1.01±0.03s, p=0.029; ATT: 
1.63±0.07s to 1.40±0.07s, p<0.001). However, changes in mATT and ATT were not 
associated with CVR. In contrast, CVR was positively associated with ΔLBV 
(β=8.84, SE=2.43, p=0.01). Case analyses further demonstrated artery-level 
delayed inflow and vascular steal.ConclusionQuantitative 4D-MRA provides 
complementary macrovascular information to ASL in SOD. ΔLBV more consistently

Gregerson CH(1), Nickerson KG(2), Kazim M(1).

Author information:
(1)Edward S. Harkness Eye Institute, Columbia University Medical Center, New

(2)Department of Rheumatology and Clinical Immunology, Columbia University

PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of tocilizumab as a primary 
treatment and with bridge corticosteroid treatment for early active-phase 
thyroid eye disease (TED).
METHODS: A single-center observational study was conducted among adult patients 
with treatment-naïve TED who initiated tocilizumab infusions (8 mg/kg 
administered monthly) within 9 months of developing the signs or symptoms of the

Anion-Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal

Zhang T(1), Xiao Y(1), Han Y(1), Wang X(1), Yang Y(1), Wang H(1), Xie Z(2), Chen 
S(1).

Author information:
(1)State Key Laboratory of Chemical Resource Engineering, Beijing Key Laboratory 
of Electrochemical Process and Technology of Materials, National Engineering 
Research Center for Fuel Cell and Hydrogen Source Technology, Beijing University 
of Chemical Technology, Beijing, P. R. China.
(2)College of Chemistry, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou, Henan, China.

Anion-dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been 
intensively pursued for low-temperature sodium-metal batteries (SMBs), yet they 
face constraints from temperature-sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial 
control. Here we propose anion-cation-targeted regulation via Sn(OTf)2 that 
simultaneously constructs a solvent-reinforced solvation structure and 
electrochemically induces an alloy-based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)

longstanding trade-off between low-temperature kinetics and stability in SMBs,

Parasitic Infections of the Lacrimal System: A Major Review of Etiology, 
Clinical Presentation, and Management.

Salari Y(1), Juniat V(1), Ali MJ(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Ophthalmology, Sussex Eye Hospital, Brighton, United Kingdom.
(2)Govindram Seksaria Institute of Dacryology, L.V. Prasad Eye Institute, 
Hyderabad, India.

PURPOSE: Parasitic infections of the lacrimal system are rare and often 
under-recognized causes of lacrimal pathology. Their clinical presentation 
frequently mimics more common conditions such as chronic dacryocystitis, leading 
to diagnostic challenges and delays in appropriate management. This study aims 
to systematically review the literature on parasitic infections of the lacrimal 
system and to characterize their etiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic 
approaches, management strategies, and outcomes.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted across MEDLINE, Embase, Emcare, and 
PubMed from inception to March 2026. Studies reporting parasitic infections 
involving the lacrimal apparatus were included. Data on demographics, clinical 
presentation, anatomical involvement, causative organisms, diagnostic methods, 
treatment, and outcomes were extracted. Due to heterogeneity and predominance of 
case reports and small series, a qualitative descriptive analysis was performed.
RESULTS: A total of 44 studies comprising 172 cases were included. 
Rhinosporidium seeberi was the most frequently reported pathogen, accounting for 
147 cases (85.5%), followed by Leishmania (8 cases, 4.7%) and Ascaris 
lumbricoides (7 cases, 4.1%). The lacrimal sac was the most commonly involved 
site. Clinical presentation was nonspecific, with epiphora and medial canthal 
swelling predominating. Diagnosis was most often established by histopathology 
following surgical intervention. Management varied by etiology, with surgical 
excision commonly used for rhinosporidiosis and mechanical extraction for 
helminthic infections. Outcomes were generally favorable, although recurrence 
was reported, particularly in R. seeberi infections.
CONCLUSIONS: Parasitic infections of the lacrimal system are rare but clinically 
important, with diverse presentations and management approaches. Increased 
awareness is essential for early diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Further 
studies with standardized reporting are needed to optimize management 
strategies.

AIM: To examine factors associated with advance directive (AD) completion among

Supramolecular Enforcement of Planar Tetracoordinate Halides.

Zhang J(1), Maiti A(1), Greb L(1).

Author information:
(1)Anorganisch-Chemisches Institut, Ruprecht-Karls-Universität Heidelberg, 
Heidelberg, Germany.

Planar tetracoordinate halides have been widely explored by quantum 
computational approaches but remain rare as deliberately targeted experimental 
motifs. Here we show that these geometries can be accessed by supramolecular 
enforcement, and challenge its connection to the VSEPR model. Bowl-shaped 
calix[4]pyrrolato indium units preorganize four lithium ions into a confined Li4 
pocket that traps Cl-, Br-, and I- in strongly flattened to ideal planar 
tetracoordinate environments. Computational analysis of the parent tetrahedral 
[Li4X]3 + units reveals small planarization energies that can be overcome by a 
charge-attenuating host of appropriate shape. The experimental series shows that 
halide planarity is highly sensitive to subtle supramolecular effects, such as 
calix[4]pyrrolato doming and crystal packing, experimentally confirming the 
generally low angular deformation energies. The results establish supramolecular 
enforcement as a rational design principle for planar tetracoordinate heavier 
halides and show that such motifs are accessible outcomes of engineered 
electrostatic cavities.

Dual-Targeting Nanomicelles Co-Loading Sorafenib and Artesunate Combats 
Hepatocellular Carcinoma via the Synergistically Enhanced Ferroptosis Strategy.

Lu W(#)(1), Yang J(#)(1), Mi J(1), Luo F(1)(2), Guo Y(1), Zhang Y(1), Zhang 
X(1)(3), Xie Y(1).

Author information:
(1)Research Center for Health and Nutrition, School of Public Health, Shanghai 
University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China.
(2)Institute of Chinese Materia Medica, Shanghai University of Traditional

(3)Pharmacy Department, Shanghai Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western

(#)Contributed equally

Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a formidable malignancy with limited 
response to conventional monotherapies, largely due to its complicated 
pathogenesis and useful cellular defense systems. In this study, we constructed 
a dual-targeting polymeric micelle (S&A@TPD/HG PMs), co-delivering sorafenib 
(SOR), and artesunate (ART) to achieve synergistic ferroptosis-based therapy 
against HCC. The micelle features a hyaluronic acid (HA) shell functionalized 
with glycyrrhetinic acid (GA) for active dual targeting to CD44 and GA receptors 
overexpressed on HCC cells; while its triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-decorated inner 
core facilitates mitochondrial anchoring and co-conveys the drugs, enabling 
stepwise subcellular targeting. Compared with free drugs or single-drug-loaded 
micelles, S&A@TPD/HG PMs effectively induced mitochondrial damage by depleting 
glutathione (GSH), and downregulating GSH peroxidase 4 (GPX4) expression to 
disrupt the mitochondrial antioxidant defense system, elevating intracellular 
Fe2+ to increase reactive oxygen species (ROS) and lipid peroxidation (LPO)
