Alcohol-positive polytrauma patients: injury patterns, ICU resource use and 
mortality at a German Level I trauma center.

Thiedemann C(1)(2), Gorovoi S(3), Huber L(4), Popp D(4), Galler M(3), Schmitz 
P(3), Alt V(4), Ernstberger A(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Trauma Surgery, University Hospital Regensburg, 
Franz-Josef-Strauss-Allee 11, 93053, Regensburg, Germany. 
claudius.thiedemann@ukr.de.
(2)Department of Trauma Surgery, Caritas Hospital St. Josef Regensburg, 
Regensburg, Germany. claudius.thiedemann@ukr.de.
(3)Department of Trauma Surgery, Caritas Hospital St. Josef Regensburg, 
Regensburg, Germany.
(4)Department of Trauma Surgery, University Hospital Regensburg, 
Franz-Josef-Strauss-Allee 11, 93053, Regensburg, Germany.

BACKGROUND: In most countries, alcohol consumption is so culturally ingrained 
that even small amounts are permitted while driving. Even at a blood alcohol 
concentration of 0.5 g/L, ethanol impairs mental and cognitive performance. 
Studies from the US and Europe estimate that elevated blood alcohol levels may 
be detected in 10%-40% of all emergency department patients. Against this 
background, we investigated the impact of alcohol consumption on injury 
severity, injury patterns, as well as primary and secondary outcomes in 
polytrauma patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 
patients admitted to a Level I trauma center via the trauma room and documented 
in the TraumaRegister DGU® between 2015 and 2023. Serum ethanol was determined 
routinely in all adolescent and adult trauma room patients. Patients without 
serum ethanol measurement or younger than 13 years were excluded. Patients with 
detectable serum ethanol (> 1 mg/dL, detection limit of the laboratory; ALC) 
were compared with patients without (noALC) using the χ² and Mann-Whitney U 
tests. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were adjusted for 
age, sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) and 
pre-injury ASA classification. A dose-response analysis was performed using 
serum ethanol categories.
RESULTS: A total of 1,524 patients were analyzed: 431 (28.3%) were 
alcohol-positive (ALC) and 1,093 (71.7%) were not (noALC). ALC patients were 
younger, more often male and had a lower prehospital Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 
score (p < 0.001), whereas the ISS did not differ (p = 0.396). They were more 
frequently victims of violent crime and were overrepresented among pedestrians 
and falls from < 3 m, whereas motorcyclists were more often sober. 
Alcohol-positive patients were more often treated in the ICU (90.0% vs. 86.3%; 
p = 0.048), but this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment 
(adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40; 95% CI 0.96-2.03). Length of ICU stay and 
duration of mechanical ventilation did not differ, and alcohol was not 
independently associated with mortality (aOR 0.91; 95% CI 0.56-1.47). Severe TBI 
was more frequent in alcohol-positive patients (38.5% vs. 29.5%), increased with 
serum ethanol concentration, and was the strongest predictor of ICU treatment 
and mortality.
CONCLUSION: Nearly one in three severely injured patients had detectable serum 
ethanol. After adjustment for confounders, alcohol was not independently 
associated with mortality or intensive care resource use, and no dose-response 
relationship was found for these outcomes. The more frequent ICU treatment of 
alcohol-positive patients appears to be explained by their distinct injury 
pattern, particularly the concentration-dependent increase in severe TBI.

Cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes: insights from 
myocardial strain and renal Doppler assessment.

Atef A(1), Fayed A(2)(3), El-Haddad H(1), Fathy M(4), El Deeb H(5).

Author information:
(1)Endocrinology Unit, Internal Medicine Department, Kasr Alainy School of 
Medicine, Cairo University, Cairo, Egypt.
(2)Nephrology Unit, Internal Medicine Department, Kasr Alainy School of 
Medicine, Cairo University, Cairo , Egypt. drfayed@kasralainy.edu.eg.
(3)Cairo University Hospitals, Al-Saray St., El-Maniel, Cairo, 11562, Egypt. 
drfayed@kasralainy.edu.eg.
(4)Nephrology Unit, Internal Medicine Department, Kasr Alainy School of

(5)Cardiology Department, Kasr Alainy School of Medicine, Cairo University,

BACKGROUND: Prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) may be 
accompanied by subclinical cardiac and renal injury before overt disease 
appears. This study evaluated early cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and 
early T2DM using myocardial strain imaging and renal Doppler assessment.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 180 participants: 60 with 
prediabetes, 60 with newly diagnosed T2DM (≤ 2 years), and 60 age- and 
sex-matched healthy controls. Conventional echocardiography and two-dimensional 
speckle-tracking echocardiography were used to assess left ventricular (LV) 
function and left atrial (LA) mechanics. Renal vascular resistance was assessed 
using the Doppler-derived renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility index 
(PI). Glycemic status and albuminuria were evaluated using fasting glucose, oral 
glucose tolerance testing, HbA1c, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, participants with prediabetes and T2DM showed 
early alterations in LV relaxation/filling indices and reduced LA strain. LV 
ejection fraction was modestly lower, while GLS became progressively less 
negative across the dysglycemic groups (p < 0.001), consistent with reduced 
longitudinal myocardial deformation. Renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility 
index (PI) were significantly increased in the dysglycemic groups. RRI 
correlated positively with E/e', linking higher renal vascular resistance with 
higher estimated LV filling pressure (r = 0.440, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Prediabetes and early T2DM were associated with subclinical 
abnormalities in myocardial mechanics and renal vascular indices despite 
preserved conventional cardiac and renal function. Myocardial strain and renal 
Doppler measures may provide complementary phenotypic information, but 
prospective validation is required before routine clinical application.

Comparison of Labeled Dosages Between Japan and the United States for Drugs 
Approved in Japan from 2020 to 2025.

Funatogawa T(1), Yoshida A(2).

Author information:
(1)Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., 1-1 Nihonbashi-Muromachi 2-Chome, Chuo-ku, 
Tokyo, 103-8324, Japan. funatogawatks@chugai-pharm.co.jp.
(2)Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., 1-1 Nihonbashi-Muromachi 2-Chome, Chuo-ku, 
Tokyo, 103-8324, Japan.

INTRODUCTION: Although approved doses in Japan have generally been lower than in 
Western countries, these differences have been diminished with global drug 
development. Studies evaluating dose differences between Japan and the United 
States (US) using post-2010 data are limited, and none have focused on the 
2020s.
METHODS: This study characterized labeled dosage differences between Japan and 
the US for new molecular entities approved during 2020-2025. Major differences 
were defined as a ≥2-fold difference in the maintenance or maximum dose; all 
others were classified as minor differences.
RESULTS: Of 187 comparable drugs, 38 (20.3%) had dosage differences between 
Japan and the US: seven drugs (3.7%) showed major differences (three with higher 
doses in Japan and four with higher doses in the US), and 31 drugs (16.6%) 
showed minor differences. Common minor differences included initial-dose 
differences and body weight-based subgroup differences. Nervous system drugs 
showed the highest proportion of dosage differences (50.0%), followed by 
alimentary tract and metabolism (31.3%) and cardiovascular system drugs (22.2%). 
In contrast, dermatological (11.1%), antineoplastic (10.7%), and systemic 
anti-infective drugs (8.3%) showed lower proportions. No large differences were 
observed across assessed factors such as dosing types (fixed dose, per body 
weight) and administration routes.
CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 20% of drugs approved in Japan during 2020-2025 had 
dosage differences from those in the US. The proportion of drugs with dosage 
differences varied across therapeutic areas. Only 3.7% had major differences. 
These findings may reflect progress in the international harmonization of 
labeled drug dosages between Japan and the US.

The Inflation Reduction Act's Modeled Impacts upon Late-Stage R&D.

Bowen HP(1), O'Loughlin G(2), Schleicher C(2), Schulthess DG(3).

Author information:
(1)McColl School of Business, Queens University of Charlotte, Charlotte, USA.
(2)Vital Transformation LLC, 1100 15TH ST NW, Suite 400, Washington, DC, 20005, 
USA.
(3)Vital Transformation LLC, 1100 15TH ST NW, Suite 400, Washington, DC, 20005, 
USA. duane.schulthess@vitaltransformation.com.

BACKGROUND: The impact of the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) upon late-stage 
developments has assumed to be limited. The Congressional Budget Office's IRA 
analysis excluded post-approval innovation, potentially overlooking substantial 
economic risks to drug developers and declines in the availability of treatments 
in areas of high unmet medical need such as oncology.
METHODS: A total of 1148 secondary trials from 364 FDA-approved medicines, 
published from 2018 to 2025, were obtained from Biomedtracker and 
clinicaltrials.gov. We use fractional logit regression to model the number of 
studies and use fractional multinomial logit regression to model the share 
distribution of secondary indication studies across 19 disease groups to 
identify any change in the share distribution post-IRA .
RESULTS: We find that, after the IRA's introduction, small molecule follow-on 
studies in oncology exhibited a statistically significant 37% decline (p < 
0.05), lead indication small molecule oncology approvals exhibited a 
statistically significant 27% decline (p < 0.05), and the share of orphan 
oncology studies exhibited a statistically significant 14% decline (p < 0.05).
RESEARCH CONCLUSIONS: This study's results call into question claims that the 
IRA would have minimal negative effects upon late-stage biopharmaceutical R&D, 
as the introduction of the IRA is associated with a decline in small molecule 
oncology studies. We hope this study reinvigorates debate about the law's 
possible unintended consequences and encourages thoughtful policy solutions, as 
the IRA appears to negatively impact patients seeking needed new medicines, 
particularly those addressing metastatic late-stage cancers with a small 
molecule modality.

Evidence for Embedding Smoking and Vaping Cessation Support in Primary Care: A 
Scoping Review.

Wang S(1), Rojas I(1), Dean E(2), Hoek AC(1), Pettigrew S(3).

Author information:
(1)The George Institute for Global Health, UNSW Sydney, Sydney, New South Wales, 
Australia.
(2)Quit, Cancer Council Victoria, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.
(3)The George Institute for Global Health, UNSW Sydney, Sydney, New South Wales, 
Australia. SPettigrew@georgeinstitute.org.

BACKGROUND: Smoking is a leading preventable cause of disease, with vaping 
creating new public health concerns. This review synthesised evidence on 
interventions and strategies to integrate cessation care into primary 
healthcare.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic scoping review of PubMed and EMBASE for 
studies published between 19 September 2020 and 19 September 2024. Eligible 
studies evaluated smoking and/or vaping cessation interventions or 
implementation strategies in primary care settings in high-income countries 
(Australia, Canada, EU, UK, USA). Two reviewers independently extracted data on 
study characteristics, intervention types, outcomes, and abstinence 
verification.
RESULTS: Of 2166 records screened, 30 empirical studies were included. Most 
focused on smoking cessation, with only two addressing e-cigarette users. The 
strongest evidence supported multi-component interventions combining behavioural 
counselling and pharmacological treatments. Implementation strategies included 
electronic health record prompts, cost-free pharmacotherapy, financial 
incentives, and integration of cessation support into low-dose computed 
tomography screening or post-spirometry feedback. Evidence for the effectiveness 
of provider education was inconclusive.
CONCLUSIONS: The evidence supports several interventions and implementation 
strategies for integrating smoking cessation into primary care, though data on 
vaping cessation are limited. These findings will inform the development of 
targeted approaches to enhance cessation support in primary healthcare.

Relationships, Resilience, and Relative Value Units: A Qualitative Study of the 
Promotion and Erosion of Humanistic Practice.

Volpe RL(1)(2), Haidet P(3), Thompson BM(3), Dalke KB(4).

Author information:
(1)Penn State College of Medicine, Hershey, PA, USA. 
rvolpe@pennstatehealth.psu.edu.
(2)Department of Humanities, Penn State College of Medicine, Hershey, USA. 
rvolpe@pennstatehealth.psu.edu.
(3)Penn State College of Medicine, Hershey, PA, USA.
(4)Department of Psychiatry, Penn Medicine, Philadelphia, PA, USA.

BACKGROUND: Formal medical curricula increasingly emphasize humanism, yet 
humanistic practice (HP) is often described subjectively and little is known 
about how practicing clinicians experience and develop HP within contemporary 
healthcare environments.
OBJECTIVE: To explore how practicing physicians conceptualize, develop, and 
experience HP, and to identify implications for undergraduate medical education.
DESIGN: Qualitative study using semi-structured focus groups.
PARTICIPANTS: Twenty-six physicians across multiple specialties and 15 U.S. 
states participated, recruited through professional listservs, investigator 
networks, and snowball sampling. Years in practice ranged from 0 to 53 
(mean ~ 18).
APPROACH: Four 90-min virtual focus groups (six to seven participants each) were 
conducted in January-February 2023. Open-ended questions explored clinicians' 
understandings of HP and factors facilitating or impeding it. Transcripts were 
iteratively analyzed using thematic coding and reflexive discussion.
KEY RESULTS: Five themes emerged. Clinicians described HP as relational and 
inseparable from competent care. HP was primarily cultivated through 
relationships with patients, mentors, and role models, and those humanistic 
relationships also supported clinician resilience. Participants noted 
ambiguities in defining HP and experienced substantial tensions between HP and 
healthcare system priorities focused on efficiency, standardization, and 
commercialization. The culture and pedagogies of medical training were also seen 
as undermining HP development, with clinicians describing their training as 
"damaging" to their native humanism.
CONCLUSIONS: Clinicians deeply value HP but face systemic and cultural forces 
that challenge its practice, making it essential to address both education and 
healthcare systems in sustaining humanistic care. Preparing future physicians to 
understand, resist, and creatively work within the constraints of an 
industrialized system is essential to ensuring that medicine remains a 
profoundly human endeavor.

Photosynthetic performance of photobionts under intense visible and UV-A 
radiation in lichens with light-absorbing or light-reflecting fungal pigments.

Osyczka P(1), Kamińska N(1), Myśliwa-Kurdziel B(2).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Botany, Faculty of Biology, Jagiellonian University, 
Gronostajowa 3, Kraków, 30-387, Poland.
(2)Department of Plant Physiology and Biochemistry, Faculty of Biochemistry, 
Biophysics and Biotechnology, Jagiellonian University, Gronostajowa 7, Kraków, 
30- 387, Poland. b.mysliwa-kurdziel@uj.edu.pl.

This study investigated the effect of exposure to direct sunlight and its main 
components, i.e. visible (VIS) radiation and long-wavelength UV-A (UV-A1; 
350-400 nm) radiation, on the photosynthetic performance of two mat-forming 
epigeic lichens Cetraria aculeata (melanic species with light-absorbing cortex) 
and Cladonia uncialis (usnic species with light-reflecting cortex). A short-term 
(one-hour) irradiation stress was applied to metabolically active thalli and 
parameters related to photosynthesis at various recovery periods after treatment 
was examined through complementary in vivo chlorophyll fluorescence techniques 
(OJIP transients and quenching analysis), 77 K fluorescence emission spectra and 
assimilation pigment measurements. In both species, considerable but reversible 
photoinhibition of photosystem II was observed following sunlight and VIS 
radiation exposure, as evidenced by a significant decrease in FV/FM and 
increased K and J steps of the OJIP curves; albeit photodamage resulting from 
sunlight was more pronounced. Although UV-A1 had negligible inhibitory effect, 
it stimulated pigment synthesis in C. aculeata and enhanced photochemical energy 
utilization in C. uncialis. The two species revealed different strategies to 
cope with excess light energy; namely, C. aculeata relied on enhanced 
non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) and redistribution of excitation energy toward 
PSI, whereas C. uncialis preserved a more efficient donor site of PSII (higher 
FV/F0). Overall, VIS radiation was identified as the primary factor impairing 
PSII, posing a substantially greater threat than UV-A1. These findings might be 
relevant for understanding lichen performance under variable and atypical 
weather events, such as sunshowers or scattered showers with sunny spells.

Single-step GWAS reveals candidate genes associated with longevity traits in 
Iranian Holstein cattle.

Maddahi N(1), Sadeghi M(2), Sarghale AJ(3), Siar MKD(4), Kholghi M(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Animal Science, College of Agriculture and Natural Resources, 
University of Tehran, Karaj, Iran. nargesmaddahi@ut.ac.ir.
(2)Department of Animal Science, College of Agriculture and Natural Resources,

(4)Department of Animal Sciences, Faculty of Agriculture, Bu-Ali Sina

Longevity is a complex, polygenic trait of economic and welfare importance in 
dairy production. This study aimed to identify genomic regions and candidate 
genes associated with longevity traits-herd life (HL), productive life (PL), 
milking life (ML), and age at first insemination (AFI) in Iranian Holstein 
cattle using a single-step genome-wide association study (ssGWAS) based on

regulation, oxidative stress response, and energy metabolism. These findings 
provide exploratory insights into the genetic architecture of longevity in 
Iranian Holsteins, although validation in larger independent cohorts is required 
before marker integration into genomic selection.

Otorhinolaryngological manifestations of systemic autoimmune and 
autoinflammatory diseases: a comprehensive review.

Bayar Muluk N(1), Cingi C(2)(3).

Author information:
(1)Faculty of Medicine, Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Kirikkale University, 
Kirikkale, Turkey. nuray.bayar@yahoo.com.
(2)Faculty of Medicine, Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Eskisehir Osmangazi 
University, Eskisehir, Turkey.
(3)Faculty of Medicine, Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Istanbul Atlas 
University, Istanbul, Turkey.

In many autoimmune and autoinflammatory diseases, the head and neck are the 
first sites of symptom manifestation. Recognizing these early signs is crucial 
to prevent diagnostic delays and fatal consequences. This review addresses: (1) 
specific otorhinolaryngological (ENT) manifestations indicating systemic 
diseases (2), evidence for differentiating these from isolated ENT disorders, 
and (3) the multidisciplinary role in patient management. A comprehensive 
narrative literature review was conducted utilizing established scientific 
databases, including PubMed/Medline, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase, 
covering articles published from 1983 up to 2026. A structured search strategy 
applied keywords like "systemic disorders," "ENT symptoms," "granulomatosis with 
polyangiitis," and "Sjögren syndrome." Peer-reviewed clinical trials, 
mechanistic studies, and authoritative guidelines were included to synthesize 
current evidence regarding the clinical detection and management of systemic 
diseases through ENT manifestations. ENT symptoms typically manifest locally 
before systemic organ involvement. Sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) frequently 
accompanies autoinflammatory diseases. Auricular chondritis strongly indicates 
relapsing polychondritis (RP). Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (GPA) and RP 
classically present with refractory rhinosinusitis, nasal crusting, and 
saddle-nose deformities. Orally, Sjögren syndrome causes severe sicca syndrome, 
while Behçet's disease leads to mucosal ulcerations. Furthermore, GPA 
(developing in 2-20% of cases) and RP are common causes of potentially fatal 
laryngeal involvement, including progressive subglottic stenosis. ENT 
manifestations frequently herald severe systemic diseases. Early detection by 
otolaryngologists is vital. Implementing a multidisciplinary strategy that 
integrates rheumatology and internal medicine ensures timely diagnosis, 
facilitates appropriate systemic immunosuppression, and significantly improves 
patient survival and overall quality of life.

Anjali(1), Kumar A(2), Pande M(3), Sarma L(2), Samad HA(2), Chouhan VS(2),

Author information:
(1)Division of Cattle Physiology and Reproduction, ICAR-Central Institute for

antioxidant responses in Tharparkar and Sahiwal under heat stress conditions.

acclimatization period, a 21-day heat exposure period for the control (25 °C),

was significantly (p < 0.05) higher in Tharparkar than in Sahiwal animals.

defence and better thermo-adaptability than in Sahiwal.

Do Carmo M(1), Genro TCM(2), Scarlato S(3), Soca P(3).

Author information:
(1)Departamento de Sistemas Agrarios y Paisajes Culturales, Centro Universitario

(3)Departamento de Producción Animal y Pasturas, Facultad de Agronomía, Ruta 3

We study the effect of herbage allowance (HA, High HA vs. Low HA, 5 vs. 3 kg 
DM/kg BW respectively) on temporal foraging strategy during lactation (40±12 d 
after calving) in two years using 34 cows equipped with automatic behavior 
recorders during herbage intake assessment. Herbage mass (HM), and its chemical 
composition were assessed, while daily grazing (GT, min/d) and ruminating time 
(RT min/d) were monitored and expressed relative to herbage intake (DMI) in 
kg/cow/day. The number of feeding stations (FeSt) per minute and bites/FeSt were 
recorded by direct observation for 30 min/d in two to four cows per plot for two 
or three consecutive days. Data analysis using MIXED model with HA as fixed and 
block as random effect was performed using the plot as the experimental unit.

respectively and the greater DMI could be partially explained by access to 
greater HM in both years and by grazing behavior at FeSt. Cows in the High HA 
group showed a tendency toward more selective foraging behavior, with an 
increase in FeSt/min (P = 0.09) and a decrease in bites/FeSt (9 vs. 13 ± 2; 
P = 0.08), suggesting enhanced selectivity despite marginal statistical 
significance but when integrated over 11 h of GT it significantly affects DMI. 
In the second year, RT/kg DMI tended to increase in the Low HA group, competing 
directly with GT. This suggests that lower DMI could trigger a behavioral 
adaptation to increase digesta retention time diminishing particle size through 
rumination trying to extract more nutrients of the herbage ingested and making 
space for new herbage intake.

Suicide among children and adolescents in India as a public mental health 
priority.

Ramakrishnan T(1), Deac AA(2), Vivekanandhan S(1), Salisbury TT(3), Ramasamy 
DP(1), Cherian AV(1), Madegowda RK(4), Kannuri NK(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Psychiatric Social Work, National Institute of Mental Health 
and Neurosciences, Bengaluru, Karnataka, 560029, India.
(2)Institute for Connected Communities, University of East London, London, UK. 
a.deac@uel.ac.uk.
(3)Centre for Global Mental Health, King's College London, London, UK.
(4)Department of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, National Institute of Mental 
Health and Neuro Sciences, Bangalore, Karnataka, 560029, India.
(5)Department of Anthropology, University of Hyderabad, Hyderabad, Telangana, 
500046, India.

BACKGROUND: Suicide among children and adolescents (≤ 18 years old) is a growing 
public health concern in India, contributing to an alarming 6% of total suicides 
reported in 2022. Despite policy efforts, systemic gaps in prevention, 
reporting, and mental health infrastructure persist.
METHODS/APPROACH: This paper uses secondary data from the Accidental Deaths and 
Suicides in India (ADSI) reports (2014-2023) published by the National Crime 
Records Bureau (NCRB) to map the key trends and key drivers of suicide among 
youth in India. Descriptive report estimates on suicide data among individuals 
aged 0-18 years were categorised by gender, cause, and year. To interpret the 
underlying drivers of suicide, we applied the Socio-Ecological Model (SEM), 
which organises risk factors across four levels: individual, interpersonal, 
community, and societal.
RESULTS: Between 2014 and 2023, a total of 100,787 children died by suicide in 
India, with female children consistently outnumbering males. The most frequently 
reported causes were family-related problems (25,049), followed by academic 
failure (12,988), love affairs (12,988), and mental illness (6143). Nearly 29% 
of suicides were attributed to unknown or "other" causes, indicating gaps in 
documentation.
CONCLUSION: Suicide among Indian children and adolescents is driven by 
multifaceted structural and psychosocial factors. A Bronfenbrenner's 
socio-ecological approach reveals multiple points of intervention, including 
school-based mental health services, family support programs, anti-stigma 
initiatives, and community-level capacity building. A coordinated public health 
response tailored to each SEM level is essential to reverse current trends and 
safeguard child mental health.

Prediction error (PE) signals support feedback evaluation and adaptive updating, 
and are closely linked to medial frontal theta dynamics, particularly within 
dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC)-centered networks. However, evidence 
linking these oscillatory mechanisms to the modulation of PE encoding remains 
limited. Here, we tested whether theta-band modulation of a dACC-centered medial 
frontal network altered trial-level PE encoding during food-reward processing. 
In a single-blind, sham-controlled pre-post design, individuals with elevated 
food addiction symptoms performed a food incentive-delay task while undergoing 
electroencephalographic recordings combined with theta-band temporal 
interference stimulation. Single-trial analyses revealed that feedback-related 
negativity (FRN) amplitudes varied as a function of both behavioral and 
model-derived prediction errors. Critically, theta-band modulation altered 
FRN-PE coupling, with the effect most pronounced for unfavorable outcomes, 
whereas anticipatory activity remained unchanged. These findings support the 
hypothesis that theta-band modulation can alter feedback-related PE encoding 
within this population and task context.

Retrospective serological evidence of exposure to selected equine viruses in 
horses from Indigenous communities of Costa Rica, 2011.

Sánchez Bermúdez JF(1), Bonilla MC(1), Dolz G(2).

Author information:
(1)Laboratorio de Zoonosis y Entomología, Programa Integrado de Medicina 
Poblacional (MEDPOB), Escuela de Medicina Veterinaria, Universidad Nacional, 
Campus Pbro. Benjamín Nuñez, Lagunilla, Heredia, 3000, Costa Rica.
(2)Laboratorio de Zoonosis y Entomología, Programa Integrado de Medicina 
Poblacional (MEDPOB), Escuela de Medicina Veterinaria, Universidad Nacional,

gaby.dolz.wiedner@una.ac.cr.

Horses are essential for transportation and livelihoods in Indigenous 
communities of Costa Rica. However, information on their exposure to viral 
pathogens remains scarce. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional 
serosurvey using samples collected from horses from four Indigenous communities 
(Alto Pacuare, Amubre, Paso Marcos, and Vereh) sampled between March and October 
2011 (n = 278). Sera were tested in 2014 using commercial immunodiffusion or 
ELISA assays for antibodies against West Nile virus (WNV), equine herpesviruses 
1 and 4 (EHV-1 and EHV-4), influenza A virus, equine arteritis virus (EAV), and 
equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV). Seroprevalence estimates and Wilson 95% 
confidence intervals were calculated, and differences among communities were 
assessed using Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, as appropriate. The 
number of tested sera differed across assays due to sample availability. 
Serological evidence compatible with WNV exposure was detected in 58.9% 
(139/236) of horses, with the highest proportion in Amubre (83.3%). EHV-4 showed 
consistently high seropositivity (91.2%, 125/137), whereas EHV-1 seroprevalence 
was low (6.6%, 9/137). Antibodies to influenza A virus and EAV were detected at 
low frequencies (5.1%, 12/237, and 3.0%, 7/236, respectively). EIAV 
seroprevalence reached 16.6% (35/211), with the highest proportion in Paso 
Marcos (23.8%). Significant differences among communities were observed for WNV, 
influenza A virus, and EHV-4 seropositivity. These findings represent historical 
serological evidence of exposure in 2011 and should not be interpreted as 
reflecting current viral circulation. Nevertheless, they provide a retrospective 
baseline for comparison with future surveillance and highlight the value of 
including underserved Indigenous equine populations in disease-monitoring and 
prevention programs.

Adiposity and the risk of aortic dissection incidence and mortality: results 
from the UK Biobank, the J-SHC study and a meta-analysis of cohort studies.

Dillman A(1), Otaki Y(2), Sanchez-Perez M(1), Irfan Khan MY(1), Hibino M(3), 
Konta T(2), Yamagata K(4), Fujimoto S(4), Tsuruya K(4), Narita I(4), Kasahara 
M(4), Shibagaki Y(4), Iseki K(4), Moriyama T(4), Kondo M(4), Asahi K(4), 
Watanabe T(4), Watanabe T(2), Watanabe M(2), Aune D(5)(6)(7).

Author information:
(1)Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, School of Public Health, 
Imperial College London, White City Campus, 90 Wood Lane, London, W12 0BZ, UK.
(2)Department of Cardiology, Pulmonology, and Nephrology, Yamagata University 
School of Medicine, Yamagata, Japan.
(3)Department of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery, Thoracic Institute, 
Cleveland Clinic, Heart, Vascular, Cleveland, OH, USA.
(4)Steering Committee of Research on Design of the Comprehensive Health Care 
System for Chronic Kidney Disease Based on the Individual Risk Assessment by 
Specific Health Check, Fukushima, Japan.
(5)Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, School of Public Health, 
Imperial College London, White City Campus, 90 Wood Lane, London, W12 0BZ, UK. 
d.aune@imperial.ac.uk.
(6)Department of Nutrition, Oslo New University College, Oslo, Norway. 
d.aune@imperial.ac.uk.
(7)Department of Research, Cancer Registry of Norway, Norwegian Institute of 
Public Health, Oslo, Norway. d.aune@imperial.ac.uk.

Few studies have investigated the association between adiposity and risk of 
aortic dissection and data is lacking on adiposity measures other than body mass 
index (BMI). We analyzed the association between adiposity and risk of aortic 
dissection in the UK Biobank, and the Japan Specific Health Checkups (J-SHC) 
Study, and conducted a meta-analysis of cohort studies to clarify the 
associations between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. The analytical 
cohorts included 496,255 participants in the UK Biobank and 630,841 participants 
in the J-SHC Study. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models 
were used to analyze associations between adiposity and risk of aortic 
dissection. PubMed and Embase were searched for relevant studies up to February 
27, 2026. Random effects models were used to calculate summary relative risks 
(RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between adiposity 
and risk of aortic dissection. In the UK Biobank and J-SHC, there were 371 and 
105 aortic dissections during 12.3 and 4 years follow-up, respectively. In the 
UK Biobank, positive associations (HRs, 95% CIs) were observed between high BMI 
(1.54, 1.01-2.37, ptrend=0.01), waist circumference (1.82, 1.27-2.60, 
ptrend=0.001), hip circumference (1.77, 1.25-2.50, ptrend<0.001), 
waist-to-height ratio (1.88, 1.30-2.70, ptrend=0.10), and fat mass (1.36, 
0.97-1.91, ptrend=0.02) and aortic dissection risk, but no clear association was 
observed for waist-to-hip ratio (1.28, 0.90-1.81, ptrend=0.08) and body fat 
percentage (1.09, 0.77-1.54, ptrend=0.53). In the J-SHC Study, higher BMI (2.36, 
0.98-4.84, ptrend=0.018), waist circumference (2.26, 1.18-4.60, ptrend=0.003), 
and waist-to-height ratio (2.61, 1.27-5.92, ptrend=0.009) were positively 
associated with aortic dissection mortality. Five cohort studies were included 
in the meta-analysis on BMI and aortic dissection (2007 cases and 4,962,288 
participants). The summary RR per 5 kg/m2 increment in BMI was 1.09 (1.00-1.20, 
I2 = 43%), per 10 cm increment in waist circumference was 1.21 (1.05-1.40, 
I2 = 50%, n = 2), and per 0.1 unit increment in waist-to-height ratio was 1.32 
(1.08-1.61, I2 = 39%, n = 2). These findings provide evidence for a positive 
association between both general and abdominal adiposity and the risk of aortic 
dissection, with the strongest associations observed for high waist-to-height 
ratio. Although further large-scale studies are warranted for confirmation, 
these findings suggest avoiding excess weight may be an important strategy for 
the prevention of aortic dissection.

Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of vision loss. 
Leukocyte subtypes have been implicated in the pathogenesis, but causality 
remains uncertain. We investigated whether leukocyte counts are causally 
associated with clinically diagnosed AMD using observational and genetic 
analyses in three prospective cohorts. We included 117,714 individuals from the 
Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS), 388,758 from the UK Biobank (UKB), 
and 285,612 from the Million Veteran Program (MVP), all of European ancestry and 
without clinically diagnosed AMD at baseline. In total, 27,130 incident AMD 
cases were identified. Baseline leukocyte counts were log2-transformed and 
standardized. Observational associations with incident AMD were estimated using 
Cox regression in CGPS and UKB, and then meta-analysed. Genetic instruments 
derived from genome-wide association studies were used for one-sample mendelian 
randomization (MR) and multivariable MR (MVMR) analyses in UKB and MVP, and 
estimates then meta-analysed. Observationally, a 1-standard deviation (SD) 
increase in leukocyte (Hazard ratio (HR) [95% confidence interval (CI)], 1.07 
[1.05-1.09]), neutrophil (1.07 [1.05-1.09]), monocyte (1.05 [1.03-1.07]), 
basophil (1.06 [1.04-1.08]), and eosinophil (1.05 [1.03-1.06]) counts was 
associated with increased risk of clinically diagnosed AMD (all p < 0.0001). In 
the genetic analyses, a 1-SD increase in genetically determined eosinophil 
counts was causally associated with increased risk of clinically diagnosed AMD 
in the MR (OR [95% CI], 1.07 [1.00-1.15]; p = 0.038) and MVMR (OR [95% CI], 1.12 
[1.03-1.21]; p = 0.006) analyses. This large-scale study provides observational 
and genetic evidence that elevated eosinophil counts are causally linked to risk 
of clinically diagnosed AMD. These findings highlight systemic eosinophil-driven 
immune pathways as potential contributors to AMD pathogenesis.

Interacting climatic, environmental, biologic and socio-economic drivers of the 
global dengue expansion.

Semenza JC(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Epidemiology and Global Health, Umeå University, Umeå, Sweden.
(2)Heidelberg Institute of Global Health, University of Heidelberg, Heidelberg, 
Germany.

Dengue is the most rapidly expanding mosquito-borne viral disease worldwide. The 
worst year on record was 2024, with over 100 countries reporting 14.4 million 
cases and over 11,000 deaths. Since then, and up to August 2026, another 7.4 
million cases and over 5000 deaths have been reported. The region of the 
Americas was impacted the most, followed by South-East Asia and the Western 
Pacific. Both the spread of dengue viruses (DENV) and their primary vectors, 
Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, are driven by several factors. Globalization 
has accelerated vector dispersal, particularly through international trade and 
transportation networks. The movement of desiccation-resistant eggs in 
used-vehicle tyres and the inadvertent transport of adult mosquitoes via trucks 
and passenger vehicles have enabled the establishment of vector populations in 
previously uncolonized regions. Human mobility and unplanned urbanization 
further contribute to dengue emergence by introducing DENV into susceptible 
populations where competent vectors circulate. Climate change has enhanced 
dengue transmission potential by altering temperature and rainfall patterns that 
influence mosquito survival, reproduction, biting behaviour and viral 
replication. Containing or even reversing this global dengue expansion will 
require a complementary set of interventions that rely on proven and novel 
control strategies, including sterile insect techniques, Wolbachia-infected 
mosquitoes, virus-resistant mosquito strains through CRISPR-Cas9 gene drive, 
vaccines, antiviral drug prophylaxis and urban interventions that eliminate 
Aedes habitats. Building climate-resilient urban environments through 
sustainable development to minimize the urban heat island effect and advancing 
climate-informed early warning systems are long-term strategies for effective 
dengue control.

Non-contrast CT radiomics for identifying nonfunctioning kidneys: a multicenter 
development and external validation study.

Jiang Y(#)(1), Zheng Y(#)(1), Feng Z(2), Bao L(3), Wei Q(4)(5).

Author information:
(1)The First School of Clinical Medicine, Southern Medical University, 
Guangzhou, Guangdong, 510515, China.
(2)Department of Urology, Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital (Guangdong 
Academy of Medical Sciences), Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, 510080, 
China.
(3)Department of Urology, Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital (Guangdong 
Academy of Medical Sciences), Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, 510080, 
China. 13728954468@163.com.
(4)Department of Urology, Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital (Guangdong 
Academy of Medical Sciences), Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, 510080, 
China. qwei@smu.edu.cn.
(5)Department of Urology, Ganzhou Hospital-Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical 
University (Ganzhou People's Hospital), Ganzhou, 341000, China. qwei@smu.edu.cn.

PURPOSE: In urological practice, the decision to resect or preserve a kidney 
with obstruction, tumor or atrophy is based on split renal function, although 
SPECT renal dynamic scintigraphy as the reference standard is 
resource-intensive. We developed and externally validated a non-contrast CT 
radiomics model to identify nonfunctioning kidneys and support urological 
decision-making in this setting.
METHODS: In this three-center retrospective study (TRIPOD+AI), adults underwent 
non-contrast CT and SPECT renal dynamic scintigraphy within 72 h. IBSI-compliant 
radiomics features were extracted with PyRadiomics, and between-kidney asymmetry 
features were constructed. After three-stage selection (Spearman, recursive 
feature elimination, and LASSO), 12 machine learning models were developed and 
externally validated in 2 independent cohorts. A Rad-score and clinical nomogram 
were also derived.
RESULTS: Among 1029 patients, the internal cohort included 418 patients. 
Twenty-three of features were retained. The random forest model yielded an 
internal test AUC of 0.9426, sensitivity of 85.5%, specificity of 88.3%, and 
negative predictive value of 95.6%. Its external AUCs were 0.875 and 0.913. The 
nomogram attained external AUCs of 0.920 and 0.881. At the thresholds fixed in 
the training data, the random forest achieved external sensitivity of 66.0 and 
76.4% with negative predictive values of 94.8 and 93.3%, and the nomogram 92.5 
and 93.7% with 98.3 and 97.2%. Both radiomics models outperformed 
logistic-regression baselines built from clinical variables and simple CT size 
and asymmetry measurements, although the margin over the combined baseline was 
not statistically significant in one external cohort. The Rad-score was 
correlated with single-kidney GFR (ρ = -0.738, P < 0.001) and facilitated risk 
stratification.
CONCLUSION: Non-contrast CT radiomics identified nonfunctioning kidneys without 
contrast agents or radiotracers. Because non-contrast CT is already part of 
routine urological workup, this externally validated rule-out tool may reduce 
unnecessary SPECT examinations and support decisions between nephrectomy and 
nephron-sparing management.

Contrast-Enhanced NeuroPOCUS in Neurocritical Care: Overcoming Technical 
Barriers to Bedside Transcranial Ultrasound.

Bianchini A(1), Malferrari G(2), Zanoni A(3), Volpe G(3), Felicani C(4), Modolon 
C(5), Zangheri E(3).

Author information:
(1)Anesthesiology and General Intensive Care Unit, IRCCS Azienda 
Ospedaliero-Universitaria di Bologna, Via Albertoni 15, 40138, Bologna, Italy. 
amedeo.bianchini@aosp.bo.it.
(2)Neurology and Neurosonology, Centro di Neuroscienze Anemos, Reggio Emilia, 
Italy.
(3)Anesthesiology and General Intensive Care Unit, IRCCS Azienda 
Ospedaliero-Universitaria di Bologna, Via Albertoni 15, 40138, Bologna, Italy.
(4)UOC Medicina ad Indirizzo Metabolico Nutrizionale, Policlinico di Modena, 
Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria di Modena, Via del Pozzo 71, 41125, Modena, 
Italy.
(5)Pediatric and Adult Cardio Thoracic and Vascular, Oncohematologic, and 
Emergency Radiology Unit, IRCCS Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria di Bologna, 
Via Albertoni 15, 40138, Bologna, Italy.

Neuro-point-of-care ultrasound (NeuroPOCUS) is an emerging bedside modality that 
extends the neurological examination through real-time assessment of cerebral 
structure and hemodynamics in neurocritical care. Despite increasing integration 
into clinical pathways and endorsement of transcranial ultrasound-based 
neuromonitoring by international guidelines, implementation is often hampered by 
inadequate acoustic windows and poor image and Doppler signal quality, 
frequently leading to nondiagnostic examinations. Ultrasound contrast agents 
(UCAs), traditionally used in specialist neurosonology, may overcome these 
barriers and recover diagnostic information in patients with limited acoustic 
windows. This clinically oriented narrative review synthesizes the available 
evidence on contrast-enhanced transcranial ultrasound and examines its potential 
translation into NeuroPOCUS as a bedside tool for frontline clinicians across 
vasospasm monitoring, intracranial pressure assessment, evaluation of 
steno-occlusive cerebrovascular disease, assessment of cerebral circulatory 
arrest, and other neurocritical care applications. A literature search of 
PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), 
Embase, and Scopus was conducted through June 2026, and relevant studies, 
reviews, and guideline documents were descriptively synthesized according to 
clinical application. Available evidence indicates that UCAs improve Doppler 
signal quality, enhance visualization of intracranial vessels, and increase the 
proportion of diagnostic examinations in patients with limited acoustic windows, 
thereby improving the interpretability of bedside hemodynamic assessments. 
However, implementation remains constrained by operator dependence, 
heterogeneous acquisition and interpretation protocols, limited standardization, 
and the need for structured training and validated, application-specific 
velocity cutoffs. Looking ahead, contrast enhancement may expand the scope of 
bedside neurovascular assessment, including in emergency and acute-care settings 
where dedicated probes and presets are not readily available. Its favorable 
safety profile and enhanced bedside feasibility may help bridge the gap between 
guideline recommendations and clinical practice, although further technical and 
clinical validation is needed to define its role in frontline NeuroPOCUS.

PURPOSE: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) is an established technique to measure 
the mechanical properties of cells and tissues. Measurements are based on force 
interactions between cantilever and sample. These measurements can be influenced 
by the underlying substrate. Published literature has utilized this phenomenon 
to measure the turgor pressure of eukaryotic cells through the cell membrane. 
The purpose of the current study was to determine how to increase measurement 
sensitivity of pressure in larger-scale biological tissues, specifically 
intraocular pressure.
METHODS: AFM was used to measure pressurized artificial corneas. Tipless and 
tipped cantilevers were used to acquire measurements of Young's modulus of 
elasticity and apparent stiffness over the pressure range: 15, 25, and 35 mmHg 
to represent normal, elevated, and uncontrolled IOP.
RESULTS: In this study, fourteen tipless cantilevers and eight modified 
cantilevers were tested to determine which cantilever parameters best measured 
the pressure beneath the tissue. The parameters evaluated were spring constant, 
indenter tip radius, and effective working length. Spring constant had a more 
pronounced effect on apparent stiffness than any other parameter examined for 
both unmodified and modified cantilevers. For modified cantilevers, the ratio of 
working length to indenter radius enhances the bottom-substrate effect, with 
lower ratios being more advantageous.
CONCLUSION: The results of this study suggest that AFM could be used to quantify 
pressure beneath biological tissues, but care must be taken to select a 
cantilever with appropriate specifications.

Opportunities and challenges of artificial intelligence and digital pathology in 
adult CNS tumors.

Lechpammer M(1), Norrell JT(2), Parnas JN(2), Vojnic M(2), Sherman JH(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Pharmacology, New York University

PURPOSE: For over a century, the pathologist's interpretation at the microscope 
was the final word on a brain tumor's identity. The 2021 World Health 
Organization (WHO) classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors, 5th 
edition, changed that hierarchy by introducing a layered, integrated diagnosis 
in which molecular findings take precedence over histology when the two 
conflict. Artificial intelligence (AI) applied to digitized slides adds a 
computational layer to this framework and marks a fundamental change in 
diagnostic workflow. This review examines the role of AI and digital pathology 
in adult CNS tumors and discusses the opportunities and challenges in clinical, 
neuro-oncology implementation.
METHODS: We conducted a narrative review of relevant literature indexed in 
PubMed before and after the 2021 WHO classification, covering digital pathology, 
whole-slide imaging (WSI), and AI applications in adult neuro-oncology. We 
synthesized evidence on diagnostic performance, molecular prediction, prognostic 
modeling, workflow integration, and ethical considerations.
RESULTS: AI and digital pathology show potential to improve diagnostic 
consistency, shorten turnaround time, and integrate histopathological, 
molecular, and radiological information. AI models may support glioma grading, 
prediction of molecular alterations from routine histology, survival 
stratification, prediction of brain metastasis, and intraoperative decisions. 
Barriers to clinical adoption include limited generalizability, lack of 
transparency, data privacy, and evolving regulatory oversight.
CONCLUSION: AI and digital pathology are transforming adult CNS tumor 
diagnostics and could improve precision, efficiency, and multidisciplinary 
decision-making. Successful implementation will require rigorous 
multi-institutional clinical validation, transparent governance, equitable 
access, and collaboration among patients and health care professionals.

Couture S(1)(2), Paquette MM(3)(4), Guyon R(5)(4), Hébert M(6)(4), Fernet

Author information:
(1)Department of Psychiatry and Neuroscience, Université Laval, 1050, Avenue de

Large language model chatbots, such as ChatGPT, have garnered increasing 
attention in the field of education, due to its versatility, processing speed, 
and widespread accessibility. However, its application to sexual education 
remains understudied, highlighting the need for more research into its potential 
to support informed decision-making among youth. The current study aimed to 
document ChatGPT-3.5 responses to adolescents' questions about romantic 
relationships and sexuality, using a more-than-human netnography approach. To 
obtain these responses, 393 anonymized emails written in French and English from 
adolescents aged 14 to 16 were collected from a recognized youth support 
organization. Data were obtained through ChatGPT-3.5 from January 14 to 31, 
2024. The analyses focused on identifying content violations and describing the 
response formats, followed by a conventional content analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 
recommendations. Overall, 17.8% of the emails were flagged as potentially 
violating ChatGPT-3.5's content policy. Responses were provided in two formats: 
(1) structured text or (2) continuous text that both included an introduction 
clarifying the question, normalizing the experience, and/or validating emotions; 
a list of recommendations; and a conclusion promoting support seeking, and/or a 
positive outlook. The recommendations aimed to encourage adolescents to embrace 
authenticity and personal agency, practice self-care and build self-confidence, 
engage in open communication, develop meaningful relationships, and seek support 
when needed. The findings highlight ChatGPT's potential to contribute to 
comprehensive sex education for adolescents seeking information.

Organ Wet Mount (Squash) Preparations in Fish Pathology: An Underused, Rapid and 
Low-Cost Tool for Tissue-Level Diagnosis During Necropsy.

Sahatrakul K(1)(2), Payne IL(3), Denk D(1).

Author information:
(1)SeaWorld Yas Island Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi, UAE.
(2)Singapore Oceanarium, Resorts World Sentosa, Singapore.
(3)Independent Author, UK.

Rapid, practical diagnostic approaches are essential for effective fish health 
management, yet cytological wet mount assessment of internal organs remains 
underused and inconsistently described in peer-reviewed aquatic veterinary 
literature. Organ wet mount (squash preparation) cytology offers a simple, 
low-cost method for immediate evaluation of fresh tissues. Unlike impression 
smears and aspirates, in which cells are assessed largely in isolation, squash 
preparations retain structural relationships within the tissue, providing 
tissue-level information at the point of examination that would otherwise await 
histopathology. The technique is widely applicable and requires minimal 
equipment, but guidance on its application beyond gill, skin, and fin samples is 
limited. A survey of fish health professionals confirmed that internal organ 
preparations are used less than external wet mounts. This review outlines the 
use of organ squash preparations during fish necropsy, emphasising technique, 
interpretation, and recognition of common findings rather than a comprehensive 
overview of disease. Key limitations, such as post-mortem changes, are 
discussed, as is the role of targeted special stains and follow-up diagnostics. 
Greater awareness and more consistent use of organ squash cytology have the 
potential to improve early detection of disease and support more targeted 
diagnostic decision-making in fish health investigations.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the overall safety of stent placement for malignant 
superior or inferior vena cava (SVC/IVC) syndrome by assessing adverse events in 
a nationwide multicenter population.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Japanese Diagnosis 
Procedure Combination nationwide inpatient database. Patients who underwent 
stent placement for malignant superior or inferior vena cava (SVC/IVC) syndrome 
between April 2019 and March 2023 were included. The primary endpoint was the 
overall incidence of adverse events, which were identified using International 
Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision codes. Secondary evaluations included 
patient characteristics, underlying malignancies, therapeutic interventions, 
7-day mortality after stent placement, 30-day in-hospital mortality after 
admission, and comparisons between the SVC and IVC groups.
RESULTS: This nationwide study included 301 patients from 137 hospitals, of whom 
187 underwent SVC stenting, and 114 underwent IVC stenting. Overall, 34 adverse 
events occurred in 32 patients (10.6%). Red blood cell transfusion was required 
in 10 patients (3.3%), but no invasive treatment, including embolization, was 
required. Seven-day mortality after stenting was 5.0%, and 30-day in-hospital 
mortality after admission was 11.6%. In comparisons between the SVC and IVC 
groups, respiratory failure was more common after SVC stenting, whereas other 
adverse events and mortality were comparable between groups. Lung tumors 
predominated in SVC cases and liver tumors in IVC cases; multiple stents were 
used more frequently in IVC cases.
CONCLUSION: Stent placement for malignant vena cava obstruction demonstrated an 
overall complication rate of 10.6% with no serious adverse events requiring 
invasive intervention.

Analysis of serological markers and synovial fluid cytology in aseptic revision 
total knee arthroplasty.

Khury F(1)(2)(3), Zhong J(4), Ruff G(4), Sarfraz A(4), Bahlouli L(4), Aggarwal 
VK(4), Schwarzkopf R(5).

Author information:
(1)The Ruth and Bruce Rappaport Faculty of Medicine, Technion - Israel Institute 
of Technology, Haifa, Israel. farouk.khury@technion.ac.il.
(2)Department of Orthopedic Surgery, New York University Langone Medical Center,

(3)Division of Orthopedic Surgery, Rambam Health Care Campus, Haifa, Israel. 
farouk.khury@technion.ac.il.
(4)Department of Orthopedic Surgery, New York University Langone Medical Center,

(5)Department of Orthopedic Surgery, New York University Langone Medical Center,

BACKGROUND AND AIM: Recent studies examining synovial fluid analysis to 
differentiate causes for aseptic revision total knee arthroplasty (rTKA) were 
limited to aseptic loosening and instability. This study aims to establish 
specific serological and synovial profiles for various rTKA etiologies.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent aseptic rTKA at a 
single academic institution between 2012 and 2023. Inclusion required complete 
serum inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive 
protein (CRP)) and synovial fluid differentials within three months 
pre-operatively. Periprosthetic joint infections were strictly excluded 
utilizing the 2018 International Consensus Meeting criteria. In total, 156 
patients were included and stratified into five aseptic etiologies: aseptic 
loosening (50.6%), instability (28.2%), arthrofibrosis (16.7%), liner wear 
(2.6%), and component malposition (1.9%). Serological markers were evaluated 
utilizing a multivariate general linear model adjusting for patient 
demographics, while synovial markers were assessed via Welch's Analysis of 
Variance (ANOVA) and Games-Howell post-hoc testing.
RESULTS: Multivariate analysis demonstrated that the underlying rTKA indication 
was not a significant independent predictor of elevated ESR (P = 0.661) or CRP 
(P = 0.947). Welch's ANOVA revealed significant differences in the percentage of 
synovial monocytes (P < 0.001) and lymphocytes (P = 0.010), alongside the 
polymorphonuclear cells/monocyte (P = 0.030) and lymphocyte/monocyte (P = 0.005) 
ratios. Games-Howell post-hoc testing demonstrated the tibial liner wear group 
exhibited significantly higher monocyte percentages, paired with lower 
lymphocyte percentages and cellular ratios, compared to other aseptic 
etiologies.
CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed that routine systemic inflammatory markers and 
standard synovial fluid cell counts do not significantly vary among the common 
etiologies of aseptic rTKA. Nonetheless, tibial polyethylene liner wear appears 
to elicit an exploratory, monocyte-predominant and lymphocyte-depleted local 
macrophage response that is absent in other mechanisms of aseptic failure. 
Further research with larger cohorts is warranted to validate this association 
and explore its potential as a diagnostic tool.

Abomasal ulcer (AU) is a common condition in dairy cows that significantly 
affects productivity and longevity. This study evaluated the diagnostic value of 
serum biomarkers and the fecal occult blood test (FOBT), and tested a Light 
Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model to predict ulcer occurrence. 
Postmortem analyses were performed on 304 culled dairy cows, from which blood 
and fecal samples were collected. Animals were classified according to the 
presence (n = 249) or absence (n = 55) of abomasal ulcers. No individual

indicate that current serum biomarkers and routine blood variables are 
insufficient for accurate individual diagnosis of AU, underscoring the need for 
more specific diagnostic tools.

Utility of ultrasonography for articular cartilage assessment in knee 
osteoarthritis: a comparative study with clinical scores and magnetic resonance 
imaging.

Tandon A(1), Ahmad M(2), Jain S(2), Mehrotra G(2), Chakraborti KL(3), Aggarwal 
AN(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Radio-Diagnosis, University College of Medical Sciences and

(4)Department of Orthopedics, University College of Medical Sciences and Guru

OBJECTIVE: To assess the utility of ultrasonography in evaluating femoral 
articular cartilage in knee osteoarthritis and to determine the relationship 
between sonographic cartilage abnormalities and clinical pain scores.
METHODS: A prospective study was conducted on 63 clinically diagnosed knee 
osteoarthritis patients (126 knees) and 30 age-matched controls (60 knees). All 
participants underwent clinical evaluation and ultrasonography by two reviewers. 
Cartilage thickness and morphological abnormalities were assessed using a 
semi-quantitative sonographic grading system. Pain severity was evaluated using 
the visual analogue scale (VAS), and the relationship between sonographic 
cartilage grade and clinical pain was statistically analysed. A subgroup of 18 
knees also underwent MRI for exploratory comparison of cartilage grading.
RESULTS: Cartilage abnormalities were detected by USG in 97% of OA knees 
compared to 50% of controls (p < 0.001). Medial condyle cartilage was 
significantly thinner in osteoarthritis knees (1.48[95% CI 1.37-1.60] mm) than 
controls (1.74[95% CI 1.59-1.88] mm, p = 0.027). Interrater agreement was almost 
perfect (Quadratic weighted Cohen Kappa was 0.89[95% CI 0.93-0.97). Higher 
cartilage grades (≥ 2B) on USG had significantly higher VAS scores compared to 
low cartilage grade (< 2B) (p < 0.001). USG showed fair agreement (Quadratic 
weighted Kappa = 0.40[95% CI 0.9-0.72] in detection of all cartilage 
abnormalities with MRI, however it underestimated severity compared to MRI 
(≥ Grade 2B in 67% vs. 95%).
CONCLUSION: Ultrasound is a reliable, accessible tool for detecting femoral 
cartilage changes in knee osteoarthritis, showing significant correlation with 
clinical symptoms. Its affordability, safety, and dynamic capabilities make it a 
valuable adjunct for initial assessment and monitoring in routine clinical 
practice.

visual performance reflect a general visual ability or a set of largely 
task-specific processes. Previous studies have often reported weak associations 
across heterogeneous perceptual tasks, challenging the idea of a common visual 
factor. Here, we asked whether shared variance becomes more evident when visual 
tasks are conceptually and procedurally similar. One hundred fifty-eight adults 
completed eight low-level acuity and hyperacuity paradigms implemented in 
FrACT10: single letter, Landolt C, tumbling E, row of optotypes, flanking rings, 
frame ring, Vernier two-line, and Vernier three-line tasks. After outlier 
exclusion, analyses were conducted on 132 participants. Within-session 
test-retest reliability was moderate for most tasks. Pairwise correlations 
revealed a broad positive manifold: all correlations were positive, 27 of 28 
survived false-discovery-rate correction, and Bayesian analyses provided strong 
evidence for nonzero associations in most task pairs. However, association 
strength depended strongly on task similarity, with robust correlations among 
optotype-based tasks and weaker links between optotype and Vernier paradigms. 
Exploratory factor analyses indicated substantial shared covariance but failed 
to support a stable latent structure: A one-factor model fit poorly, whereas 
two-factor and three-factor solutions produced improper estimates. These 
findings support an intermediate account of visual individual differences. 
Visual performance is neither fully independent across tasks nor reducible to a 
strong general visual factor; instead, commonality appears partial, 
task-dependent, and shaped by the composition of the task battery. OPEN

the Method section and are based on FrACT10. This study was not preregistered.

Effects of topical vildagliptin versus triamcinolone acetonide on experimentally

Nasser ZA(1), Jaafar FR(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pharmacology, College of Medicine, Al-Nahrain University,

The present study aimed to evaluate the effects of topical vildagliptin on 
experimentally induced hypertrophic scars (HTSs) in a rabbit model. A total of 
40 healthy male albino rabbits were randomly assigned to five groups (n = 8): 
healthy control (CTRL), untreated induced HTS model (HTS model), 
vehicle-received (VEH), 0.1% triamcinolone acetonide-treated (TAC), and 3%

for the treatment of HTSs.

Analysis of the Safety and Efficacy of Cryoablation in Patients with Locally 
Advanced Pancreatic Cancer.

Shao S(#)(1), Wang L(#)(1), Tan F(#)(2), Hou S(1), Xue K(1), Huang X(1), Cao 
D(3), Xiong J(4), Tian B(5).

Author information:
(1)Division of Pancreatic Surgery, Department of General Surgery, West China 
Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, People's Republic of China.
(2)Department of Hepatopancreatobiliary Surgery, The People's Hospital of 
Zizhong County, Neijiang City, Sichuan Province, China.
(3)Division of Pancreatic Surgery, Department of General Surgery, West China 
Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, People's Republic of China. 
caodan@scu.edu.cn.
(4)Division of Pancreatic Surgery, Department of General Surgery, West China 
Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, People's Republic of China. 
junjiex2011@126.com.
(5)Division of Pancreatic Surgery, Department of General Surgery, West China

BACKGROUND: Cryoablation is emerging as a potential treatment option for locally 
advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC). The aim of this study was to retrospectively 
evaluate the safety and efficacy of cryoablation in patients with LAPC. The 
study has been prospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry 
(ID: ChiCTR2300068376).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Adult patients with LAPC were stratified based on the 
treatment modality (cryoablation versus systemic therapy). The cryoablation was 
performed using a single cryoprobe under ultrasound guidance. The Kaplan-Meier 
method was utilized to evaluate and compare overall survival (OS) among the 
groups. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was employed to identify 
independent predictors of overall survival.
RESULTS: Of 186 enrolled patients with LAPC between August 2022 and December 
2024, 142 were in the cryoablation group and 44 in the systemic therapy alone 
group. The median OS was 17.8 months with systemic therapy alone and 18.7 months 
with cryoablation alone. Combined cryoablation and systemic therapy yielded a 
median OS of 22.1 months. Among patients receiving cryoablation combined with 
chemotherapy median OS was 19.8 months, and for combination systemic therapy 
group (chemotherapy + immunotherapy ± targeted therapy), it was 25.4 months. 
Multivariate analysis identified age, tumor location, treatment type, and 
jaundice as independent OS predictors. Additionally, nearly all patients 
experienced marked pain relief after cryoablation treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: When combined with systemic therapy, cryoablation has a more 
significant survival advantage than systemic therapy alone. However, due to the 
heterogeneity of the cohort and potential immortal time bias, these survival 
outcomes should be interpreted with caution. Additionally, cryoablation offers 
effective benefits for relieving cancer pain and preserving functional quality 
of life in patients with LAPC.

Effects of Paid Family Leave Policies on Intimate Partner Violence in New York 
City from 2012 to 2022.

Klika JB(1), Thibodeau EL(2), Murphy CA(2), Merrick MT(2), Marçal KE(3), 
Showalter K(4), Park Y(5), Chang OD(5), Maguire-Jack K(5).

Author information:
(1)Prevent Child Abuse America, Chicago, IL, USA. bklika@preventchildabuse.org.

(4)College of Social Work, University of Kentucky, Lexington, KY, USA.

INTRODUCTION: Experiencing intimate partner violence (IPV) during the prenatal 
period can result in maternal mental health challenges, adverse birth outcomes 
(e.g., pre-term birth and low birth rates), and children's mental, cognitive, 
and physical health issues (Donovan et al., 2016; Hahn et al., 2018). Access to 
economic support policies, like state-sponsored paid family leave (PFL), during 
the perinatal period may be a strategy to reduce financial stress and prevent 
IPV (Niolon et al., 2017). This paper explores whether living in a state with 
PFL (i.e., New York) reduces IPV for working mothers during pregnancy.
METHODS: Data for this study are drawn from the Pregnancy Risk and Monitoring 
System (PRAMS). We used difference-in-differences (DiD) accounting for multiple 
time periods and multiple groups to estimate the average treatment effect (ATE) 
of paid family leave enactment in New York State using data from New York City.
RESULTS: We found nearly a 30% reduction in IPV during pregnancy for working 
mothers in NYC compared to those living in states without a state-sponsored PFL 
policy.
DISCUSSION: These findings suggest economic support policies may have an 
anticipatory effect on expectant caregivers. Additional research is needed to 
further understand this association.

OBJECTIVES: To examine the prevalence and predictors of self-harm ideation 
during the perinatal period among mothers (N = 9638) enrolled in a home visiting 
program.
METHODS: Subjects were all mothers enrolled in a home visiting program in the 
United States between 2006 and 2023 who completed the Edinburgh Postnatal 
Depression Scale (EPDS; Cox et al., 1987) prenatally and/or at up to 6 months

compared with older mothers. Given the dangers of unrecognized and untreated

position to support and link mothers to mental health services.

Spatial transition of radon control mechanisms in groundwater: evidence from a 
tropical aquifer in Vietnam.

Tran HD(1)(2), Nguyen TH(3), Doan HM(3), Truong VM(1), Lam XAD(4)(5), Nguyen 
VT(4)(5), Le CH(6)(7).

Author information:
(1)Faculty of Natural Science, Dong Nai University, Dong Nai City, Viet Nam.
(2)Department of Nuclear Physics, Faculty of Physics and Engineering Physics, 
University of Science, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
(3)Dong Nai Department of Science and Technology, Science and Technology Center, 
Dong Nai City, Viet Nam.
(4)Nuclear Technique Laboratory, University of Science, Ho Chi Minh City, 
Vietnam.
(5)Vietnam National University, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
(6)Nuclear Technique Laboratory, University of Science, Ho Chi Minh City, 
Vietnam. lchao@hcmus.edu.vn.
(7)Vietnam National University, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. lchao@hcmus.edu.vn.

Radon (222Rn) in groundwater represents a natural radiological hazard and a 
potential tracer of subsurface processes. This study investigates the spatial 
variability and controlling mechanisms of radon in 66 domestic groundwater 
samples collected from Bien Hoa City, Vietnam, a rapidly urbanizing tropical 
region. Measured radon concentrations ranged from 0.18 ± 0.12 to 
1.36 ± 0.45 Bq/L, with a mean value of 0.44 ± 0.27 Bq/L, well below the 
guideline limits recommended by the USEPA (11.1 Bq/L), UNSCEAR (40 Bq/L), and 
WHO (100 Bq/L), significantly below international guideline limits, indicating 
negligible radiological risk. Multivariate statistical analysis reveals a weak 
but statistically significant negative correlation between radon concentration 
and pH (r =  - 0.36, p < 0.01), while no meaningful relationships are observed 
with total dissolved solids (TDS) or electrical conductivity (EC). These results 
suggest that the measured hydrochemical parameters alone are insufficient to 
fully explain the observed spatial variability of radon; instead, the observed 
radon distribution is more consistent with the influence of geological 
heterogeneity within the study area. Importantly, spatial analysis suggests a 
transition in the factors controlling radon variability: in near-river 
environments, radon variability is likely influenced primarily by hydrodynamic 
processes and salinity-induced degassing, whereas in inland areas, geochemical 
conditions, particularly pH, appear to play a more important role. This spatial 
shift suggests the coupled influence of physical and geochemical processes on 
radon behavior in tropical aquifers. The findings provide baseline data on 
groundwater radon distribution in Bien Hoa City, support the use of radon as a 
hydrogeological indicator, and contribute to groundwater quality assessment in 
rapidly developing regions.

Intravenous ibuprofen versus ketorolac for acute low back pain in the emergency 
department: a triple-blind randomized clinical trial.

Jafarkhani M(1)(2), Bahreini M(3)(4), Rasooli F(2)(5).

Author information:
(1)Sina Trauma and Surgery Research Center, Tehran University of Medical 
Sciences, Tehran, Iran.
(2)McGill University, Montreal, Qc, Canada.
(3)Dalhousie University, Cape Breton Medical Campus, Sydney, NS, Canada. 
bahreinimaryam@gmail.com.
(4)McGill University, Montreal, Qc, Canada. bahreinimaryam@gmail.com.
(5)Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran.

Considering the frequency of recurrence in low back pain (LBP), there is no 
single medication group with promising efficacy in acute settings. Non-steroidal 
anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) provide better pain relief with rather low 
complications. Since ketorolac has been relatively effective, we compared its 
safety and efficacy with ibuprofen as an alternative for pain relief in acute 
LBP. In this multi-centric triple-blind randomized clinical trial, we compared 
intravenous (IV) ibuprofen and ketorolac in patients with acute LBP presenting 
to the EDs of three university hospitals. Group 1 received IV ibuprofen 
(800 mg), and group 2 received IV ketorolac (30 mg), based on a computerized 
random sequence. Trained head nurses prepared analgesics in blocks of four. 
Neither patients nor the researcher or the statistician knew about the 
medication. We applied Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for patients to score their 
pain at baseline and 10 and 30 min after pain medications. Of 73 enrolled 
patients, 39 were in the ketorolac group and 34 participants in the ibuprofen 
group. Pain scores were significantly lower in the ibuprofen group at both 
10 min (49.6 vs 57.4; p =0.013) and 30 min (32.2 vs 40.7; p =0.038). Based on 
the pain intensity after 30 min, the majority of patients in the ibuprofen group 
(70.6%) rated their pain as mild, while only 35.9% of the ketorolac group 
reported pain relief to a mild level (p <0.001). The mean ED length of stay was 
significantly lower in the ibuprofen group, whereas rescue analgesia and adverse 
events were comparable between the groups. Pain intensity was significantly 
lower in the ibuprofen group than in the ketorolac group after 10 and 30 min, 
without a significant difference in side effects. Intravenous ibuprofen can 
serve as an acceptable alternative and might be more effective than ketorolac in 
acute LBP in the ED.

Projected changes in high-temperature extremes across Indian urban 
agglomerations under different global warming levels: a bivariate approach.

Maurya HK(1)(2), Gupta R(3), Joshi N(3), Suryavanshi S(4), Kumar V(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Hydrology, Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee, Roorkee, 
Uttarakhand, India. hardeep.maurya@iitjammu.ac.in.
(2)Department of Civil Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Jammu, Jammu,

(3)Department of Civil Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Jammu, Jammu,

(4)National Institute of Hydrology, Roorkee, Uttarakhand, India.
(5)Planning and Development Department, Patna, Bihar, India.

Climate extremes have risen in recent decades, and anthropogenic interventions 
are projected to continue driving climate change. This study assessed the annual 
maximum intensity of high-temperature extremes of 2, 5, and 10 consecutive days 
for 54 urban agglomerations under 1.5 °C, 2 °C, and 3 °C global warming levels 
(GWLs) using the Coupled Model Intercomparison Phase 6 (CMIP6) framework. We 
also assessed this relationship between duration and intensity of 
high-temperature extreme events by using bivariate copula functions. The average 
intensity of urban agglomerations increased by 3-8% across the different GWLs 
for 2-day duration. This trend continues for 5 and 10 days, highlighting the 
increasing risk of high-temperature extremes. The study found that urban 
high-temperature extremes rose significantly for 2, 5, and 10 days under various 
GWLs. Urban areas like Amritsar, Jalandhar, Delhi, Shimla, and Kanpur showed a 
higher increase in intensity of 20-26%, 22-28%, and 26-33% under 1.5 °C, 2 °C, 
and 3 °C GWLs, respectively. The return values (10, 20, 50, and 100 years) for a 
2-day duration are projected to increase by 3.5-9% across most urban 
agglomerations under different GWLs. Amritsar, Jalandhar, Delhi, and Shimla 
experienced a significant increase in return values (10, 20, 50, and 100 years) 
for durations of 2, 5, and 10 days under different GWLs. By using 
temperature-intensity-duration-frequency (TIDF) curves, this study also 
highlights the interaction between duration and intensity for the selected eight 
urban agglomerations under various GWLs. This study highlights the urgent need 
for immediate climate change mitigation aligned with the national (Smart Cities 
Mission and AMRUT 2.0) and international (IPCC agreement and SGD11) goals that 
support urban planners, policymakers, and communities in managing the challenges 
posed by extreme temperatures.

To explore the influence mechanism of liquid nitrogen treatment on the methane 
adsorption characteristics and swelling deformation behavior of coal, this study 
adopts coal samples with different degrees of metamorphism as research objects 
and conducts isothermal methane adsorption experiments and swelling deformation 
tests before and after liquid nitrogen cold soaking (LN2-CS). Combining Fourier

decrease. The decline rates are 28.82%, 10.68%, and 11.60%, respectively. The 
swelling deformation caused by methane adsorption in coals with different 
metamorphic degrees after liquid nitrogen treatment is all smaller than that of 
the raw coal. The volume strain of lignite changes the most before and after 
liquid nitrogen treatment, with the maximum decrease reaching 13.66%. Through 
peak-fitting calculations of the Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy of each 
coal sample, it is found that liquid nitrogen-treated does not change the types 
of functional groups on the coal surface, but the contents of hydroxyl and 
carboxyl groups increase significantly. Hydroxyl and carboxyl groups weaken the 
coal's methane adsorption process by reducing the coupling energy between coal 
and methane. Combining the results of BET and NMR experiments, the liquid 
nitrogen-treated promotes the transformation of coal pore sizes towards larger 
pores; it enhances pore connectivity but reduces the effective adsorption space. 
Pearson correlation analysis further reveals that for coals of different 
metamorphic grades, the adsorption pore specific surface area and BET specific 
surface area exhibit a strong positive correlation with saturated adsorption 
capacity (Pearson correlation coefficient > 0.71), whereas BJH total pore volume 
and average pore diameter show a strong negative correlation with saturated 
adsorption capacity (Pearson correlation coefficient > 0.73). The enhanced 
connectivity accelerates initial gas migration, but the reduced adsorption space 
slows the subsequent deformation rate during methane uptake. These findings 
reveal the microscopic influence law of LN2-CS on coal methane adsorption 
deformation and supply fundamental microscopic data for related coal reservoir 
research.

Embedded Autism Evaluations in Pediatric Primary Care Clinics: Perspectives on

The Autism in Primary Care Program (APC) was developed to train embedded 
psychologists in urban community primary care settings to provide autism 
diagnostic evaluations and to engage care coordinators in supporting families 
navigating autism services. The objective of this study was to understand 
provider and caregiver experiences and clarify implementation and sustainment

sustainment of the program, many of which aligned with qualitative findings from 
caregivers and PCPs. Identifying multiple perspectives on APC can inform our 
field on a promising model which can improve earlier diagnosis and treatment
