priorities, and purchasing behaviors. A total of 302 participants completed the 
questionnaire. A Principal Component Analysis identified three principal 
components that explained 49.5% of the total variance: ostrich welfare

Yan BJ(1), Belke D(2), Chen YX(2), Zheng XL(3).

Author information:

Platycodin D (PD), a triterpenoid saponin from Platycodon grandiflorus, has been 
reported to have cardiovascular activity, but its actions in vascular smooth 
muscle cells (VSMCs) and atherosclerosis remain unclear. We integrated network

OBJECTIVES: Methacrylic acid ester-based resins for denture fabrication release 
residual monomers and leachable substances that may interact with oral tissues. 
With increasing adoption of CAD/CAM technologies, a systematic comparison of 
leachable substance profiles and surface characteristics across polymerization 
methods is needed.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study compared the chemical composition and profiles 
of leachable substances of four denture materials - autopolymerized, thermal 
polymerized, milled, and 3D-printed - using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry 
(GC-MS). Surface roughness was evaluated by confocal microscopy.
RESULTS: GC-MS screening detected 24 distinct compounds in the solid specimens. 
Among the MMA/PMMA-based materials, methyl methacrylate content was highest in 
the thermally polymerized resin, followed by the autopolymerized and milled 
materials, and absent from the 3D-printed resin, consistent with its MMA-free 
formulation. MMA levels in the extracts did not exceed those of the negative 
control in any group. Surface roughness was comparable on the polished face (Ra 
≈ 0.21-0.25 μm), consistent with SEM findings but material-dependent on the 
unpolished, tissue-contacting face (Ra 0.37-1.03 μm).
CONCLUSIONS: Both fabrication method and material formulation influence the 
volatile and semi-volatile extractables of denture resins. As the present GC-MS 
screening may not reliably capture high-molecular-weight dimethacrylates such as 
Bis-EMA and UDMA, novel CAD/CAM materials require additional, complementary 
toxicological evaluation.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The leachable substance profiles of CAD/CAM denture resins, 
particularly the distinct compounds detected in the 3D-printed material, 
underscore the need for material-specific biocompatibility data to support 
informed clinical material selection and patient safety.

Mycobacterium abscessus (Mab) is a rapidly growing non-tuberculous mycobacterium 
that causes opportunistic infections and exhibits extensive intrinsic antibiotic 
resistance. The proline-glutamate (PE) and proline-proline-glutamate (PPE) 
protein families are mycobacteria-specific virulence factors implicated in 
immune modulation, antigenic variation, and persistence. While Mycobacterium 
tuberculosis (Mtb) harbors approximately 170 PE/PPE members, the repertoire of 
PE/PPE genes in Mab remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we performed a 
genome-wide survey of PE/PPE genes in Mab ATCC 19,977 and identified 18 
candidate family members, representing a relatively small fraction of the genome 
compared with slow-growing mycobacteria. Most predicted proteins harbor 
canonical PE or PPE domains and display acidic physicochemical properties. 
Phylogenetic analysis resolved the proteins into three subfamilies: PE, PPE, and 
PE-PPE, revealing moderate structural diversity but limited family expansion. 
Motif and gene structure analyses supported the evolutionary conservation. 
Notably, no PE_polymorphic GC-rich repetitive sequence (PE_PGRS) or PPE_major 
polymorphic tandem repeat (PPE_MPTR) members were detected, suggesting 
lineage-specific genomic reduction relative to other pathogenic mycobacteria. 
AlphaFold predictions revealed conserved N-terminal folds and variable 
C-terminal regions, which may contribute to functional diversification. 
Subcellular localization predictions indicated that most proteins are 
extracellular. Synteny analysis revealed no detectable collinearity among these 
genes. Transcriptomic analyses revealed condition-dependent expression of PE/PPE 
genes during amoeba and macrophage infection and under artificial sputum medium 
and metal ion stress, suggesting roles in environmental adaptation and host 
interaction. This study provides the first systematic overview of PE/PPE gene 
repertoire in Mab and lays the groundwork for elucidating their roles in 
intracellular survival, host interaction, and antimicrobial resistance.

Chronic and poorly healing wounds require dressings that do more than provide 
coverage, but actively regulate infection, oxidative stress, and tissue repair. 
In this study, hydrogels formulated from fish-scale-derived low-molecular-weight 
chitosan and chitooligosaccharide (COS) were evaluated using integrated 
antimicrobial, antioxidant, and in vivo wound-healing analyses to assess their 
comparative therapeutic performance. Antimicrobial testing against Gram-positive 
bacteria (Bacillus subtilis and Micrococcus luteus) and Gram-negative bacteria 
(Aeromonas hydrophila and Klebsiella pneumoniae) showed that COS displayed 
stronger activity overall, with minimum inhibitory concentrations ranging from 
0.156 to 1.25 mg/mL, compared with 0.313 to 1.25 mg/mL for chitosan. COS also 
showed a clearer bactericidal effect, particularly against the Gram-positive 
strains, whereas chitosan was predominantly bacteriostatic under the conditions 
tested. In antioxidant assays, COS demonstrated stronger hydroxyl radical and 
ABTS radical scavenging activity than chitosan, indicating a more favourable 
redox-modulating profile. Physicochemical analyses revealed differences in the 
swelling and degradation profiles of the two hydrogel formulations. In vivo, 
both hydrogels promoted wound contraction relative to untreated wounds, with COS 
exhibiting the more rapid response. The COS-treated group achieved complete mean 
wound contraction by day 14, accompanied by greater collagen-associated staining 
during subsequent histological assessment. By day 21, the collagen-associated 
percentages reached 95.71% in COS-treated wounds and 84.81% in chitosan-treated 
wounds. Immunohistochemical analysis further demonstrated temporal changes in 
TGF-β1 expression, with increased staining during the proliferative stage of 
wound repair. Collectively, these findings indicate favourable wound-healing 
performance of fish scale-derived COS hydrogel relative to chitosan hydrogel 
under the experimental conditions examined. The results support further 
investigation of fish scale-derived biopolymers as potential materials for wound 
dressing development.

PURPOSE: This study defined thresholds for clinical importance (TCIs) for the 
European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Communication 
Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-COMU26). TCIs support the clinical evaluation of 
individual patients' communication with professionals.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, an international sample of cancer 
patients with mixed diagnoses and treatments completed the EORTC QLQ-COMU26, 
which comprises six scales and four individual items. Item 26, which evaluates 
patients' satisfaction with communication with professionals, served as the 
anchor for detecting a negative event (unsatisfactory communication). Diagnostic 
accuracy for each domain was determined using ROC analysis, and the sensitivity 
of the TCIs was evaluated. Sensitivity analyses using multivariate binary 
logistic regression explored potential variability in TCIs across patient 
groups.
RESULTS: A total of 988 patients from 13 countries participated (mean age, 60.7; 
50.0% female). TCIs ranged from 80.3 to 92.5 on the 0-100 metric of the 
QLQ-COMU26 scales. All TCIs demonstrated sensitivity of at least 0.75, and ROC 
AUC values ranged from 0.80 to 0.90. Separate TCIs were identified for 
communication with nurses and doctors, with thresholds > 4 points higher for 
nurses in five QLQ-COMU26 domains. No evidence supported separate thresholds by 
age, gender, or treatment intention.
CONCLUSION: This study established TCIs with high diagnostic accuracy for the 
EORTC QLQ-COMU26, supporting its use in clinical practice and research. The 
findings suggest that the questionnaire can identify patients who report low 
communication for specific domains and help improve communication in clinical 
settings.

Two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectric semiconductors offer unique opportunities for 
ultrathin non-volatile memory and neuromorphic devices, yet the role of stacking 
order in intrinsic ferroelectric systems remains largely unexplored. Here we 
report the stacking-controlled growth of large-area 2D β'- and α-In2Se3 with 
distinct 2H and 3R configurations through chemical vapour deposition by 
regulating selenium kinetics and strain relaxation. By combining 
atomic-resolution microscopy, non-linear optical characterization and 
first-principles calculations, we uncover a strong correlation between stacking 
order and ferroelectric behaviour: β'-In2Se3 undergoes an 
antiferroelectric-to-paraelectric transition when switching from 2H to 3R 
stacking, whereas in α-In2Se3, in-plane ferroelectric polarization vanishes 
during the 3R-to-2H transition. We further achieve the controlled synthesis of 
2H/3R ferroelectric homojunctions and directly visualize polarization-dependent 
interfacial potential barriers using differential phase-contrast scanning 
transmission electron microscopy. The engineered homojunctions exhibit 
switchable band alignment and tunable carrier transport, yielding memristors 
with significantly reduced switching voltages and an on/off ratio of ∼2.6 × 104, 
approximately one order of magnitude higher than devices based on 
single-stacking α-In2Se3. These findings establish stacking order as a powerful 
structural parameter for tailoring ferroelectricity in 2D materials and 
introduce stacking-engineered polymorphic heterogeneity as a versatile platform 
for high-performance ferroelectric electronics and memory technologies.

Chemical ligation of polymer segments is an essential approach to extend the 
length of synthetic polymers. Ligating individual polymer chains at the 
molecular level remains a formidable challenge owing to the entropically 
disfavoured collision probability between reactive end groups, and the need to 
overcome the activation barrier. Here we report a pathway to chemical ligation 
of synthetic polymers via folding-driven supramolecular polymerization followed 
by dynamic covalent polycondensation. Our strategy, which does not require 
thermal activation, uses hydrogen bonds that induce conformational folding to 
rigidify the polymer backbone while providing sticky ends for supramolecular 
pre-organization. This promotes base-catalysed covalent exchange between 
terminal groups (in our case, thiolate-disulfide groups). We obtain mechanistic 
insight in the ligation process by engineering side-chain units that determine 
conformational foldability and intermolecular H-bonding pre-organization. The 
resulting extended helical polymers fold into hierarchical globular 
architectures in solution and exhibit thermo-responsive macromolecular 
entanglements in bulk films. The combination of noncovalent assembly and dynamic 
covalent polymerization offers a supramolecular pathway for non-thermal and 
controllable polycondensation of dynamic polymers with secondary structures.

BACKGROUND: Evidence of treatment strategies in frail patients (i.e. not fit for 
combination therapies) with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is 
limited to dose-reduced doublet regimens or oral fluoropyrimidines (FP) with 
bevacizumab. We conducted a systematic review analyzing evidence for oral FPs 
with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-directed monoclonal antibodies for 
patients with RAS wild-type (WT) mCRC across treatment lines.
METHODS: We searched PubMed and Cochrane Library for phase II and phase III 
studies evaluating oral FPs (capecitabine, S-1 or trifluridine/tipiracil 
(FTD/TPI)) plus EGFR-directed monoclonal antibody (panitumumab or cetuximab) in 
mCRC. Outcomes included efficacy and safety.
RESULTS: Seven publications met inclusion criteria (n = 262 patients). 
First-line data was limited to elderly cohorts receiving capecitabine plus 
cetuximab or panitumumab with a median progression-free survival (PFS)/median 
overall survival (OS) of 7.2/17.1 months (cetuximab) and 7.5/23.7 months 
(panitumumab), respectively. In third-line and beyond, median PFS for the 
combination of FTD/TPI plus cetuximab or panitumumab ranged from 2.4 (cetuximab) 
to 5.8 months (panitumumab), and OS from 9.8 (cetuximab) to 14.2 months 
(panitumumab). S-1 plus cetuximab was associated with a median PFS of 5.5 months 
and OS of 13.6 months.
CONCLUSION: While capecitabine should not be used together with anti-EGFR 
antibodies, FTD/TPI in combination with an EGFR-directed antibody appears 
feasible, shows promising activity and manageable toxicity profile in RAS WT 
mCRC potentially offering an alternative for frail patients; prospective trials 
are needed.

Patient-specific management in high-risk revision total hip arthroplasty: 
mid-term outcomes of a next-generation constrained acetabular liner.

Khury F(1)(2)(3), Luebbering B(4), Ruff G(4), Bahlouli L(4), Sarfraz A(4), 
Schwarzkopf R(4), Aggarwal VK(5).

BACKGROUND: Managing recurrent instability in revision total hip arthroplasty 
(rTHA) requires a personalized approach, as traditional constrained liners often 
yield suboptimal results due to locking-mechanism failure and limited 
impingement-free range of motion. This study aimed to evaluate the mid-term 
clinical outcomes of a novel constrained acetabular liner (CAL) when utilized as 
a patient-specific solution for a high-risk cohort undergoing complex rTHA. By 
tailoring the constraint to individual biomechanical deficits, this 
next-generation device seeks to mitigate historic failure modes.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 32 patients who underwent 37 rTHA 
procedures with a next-generation CAL at a single urban academic center between 
March 2017 and October 2023. Average follow-up was 4.7 years (range, 0.3 to 9.7 
years). The most common indication for rTHA was instability (70.3%), followed by 
infection (16.2%), aseptic loosening (10.8%), and polyethylene wear (2.7%). Just 
over one third of patients (37.5%) had undergone a prior revision. Preoperative 
constructs included fixed-bearing (37.8%), dual-mobility (32.4%), CAL (24.3%), 
static spacer (2.7%), and hemiarthroplasty (2.7%).
RESULTS: In most procedures (70.3%), the CAL was implanted into a pre-existing 
acetabular cup, whereas 29.7% involved both cup and liner revision. Following 
rTHA, no cases of implant wear, breakage, acetabular cup aseptic loosening, or 
periprosthetic fracture were observed. Six patients (18.8%) underwent a total of 
sixteen subsequent reoperations after CAL implantation-10 for instability and 6 
for infection. Among instability-related reoperations, 4 involved revision to a 
new next-generation CAL. Survivorship free from all-cause reoperation was 83.8% 
at one year and 72.6% at latest follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates favorable mid-term clinical outcomes and 
reoperation-free survivorship following complex revision THA using a novel 
constrained acetabular liner system. For patient cohorts suffering from severe 
recurrent dislocation, this next-generation CAL provides an effective, tailored 
tool in the surgical armamentarium by adapting to unique patient anatomy and 
soft-tissue compromises. Further research with larger sample sizes and extended 
follow-up is needed to assess long-term durability.

BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a severe condition characterized by a 
sudden decline of kidney function with a high mortality rate and healthcare 
costs. While extreme heat is a recognized risk factor for AKI, the effects of 
both heat and cold exposure across different demographics remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between ambient temperatures and AKI 
emergency hospitalizations, with a focus on age and sex differences.
METHODS: Using a nationwide database, we identified 119,027 AKI emergency 
hospitalizations from 2011 to 2019. A space-time-stratified case-crossover study 
with conditional quasi-Poisson regression analysis was applied to estimate 
region-specific relative risk (RR) of AKI emergency hospitalization over lag 
days 0-13. Pooled RRs were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis. 
Analyses were stratified by age (younger, 15-49; middle-age, 50-64; and older, 
65+ years old) and sex.
RESULTS: Both extreme cold (first percentile) and heat (99th percentile) were 
associated with an increased risk of AKI emergency hospitalizations, with 
cumulative RRs of 1.24 (95% CI 1.09-1.40) and 2.21 (95% CI 2.00-2.43), 
respectively. Heat-related susceptibility was highest in younger (RR 4.24, 95% 
CI 2.93-6.15) and middle-aged men (RR 4.20, 95% CI 3.46-5.10), while in women it 
occurred in the older group (RR 1.87, 95% CI 1.64-2.14). Cold-related 
susceptibility was highest among older males (RR 1.28, 95% CI 1.06-1.53) and 
females (RR 1.29, 95% CI 1.04-1.58).
SIGNIFICANCE: Extreme temperatures elevate AKI risk, with distinct age- and 
sex-specific vulnerability patterns. These findings highlight the need for 
targeted prevention strategies during temperature extremes, particularly 
protecting younger and middle-aged men from heat and older adults from cold 
exposure. Understanding the biological and social mechanisms underlying these 
demographic differences is essential for developing effective public health 
interventions in a changing climate IMPACT STATEMENT: This nationwide study 
reveals that both extreme heat and cold significantly increase acute kidney 
injury (AKI) emergency hospitalizations in Japan, with distinct age- and 
sex-specific vulnerability patterns. Younger and middle-aged men face a fourfold 
higher risk during heat exposure, while older adults of both sexes are most 
vulnerable to cold. These findings expand beyond heat-focused research and 
demonstrate the need for demographically targeted prevention strategies. As 
climate change intensifies temperature variability, these demographic-specific 
patterns highlight the need for tailored public health interventions to protect 
kidney health and reduce preventable AKI hospitalizations.

Organogenesis marks one of the most dynamic periods of early human embryonic 
development. Although the morphological features of this period have been 
described, the underlying transcriptional and metabolic landscapes remain poorly 
understood owing to the lack of an integrated spatial strategy. We present 
spatial transcriptomic and metabolomic maps of a Carnegie stage 12 (CS12) human 
embryo, co-registered with embryonic anatomy to generate a unified spatial 
multi-omic framework. Unsupervised clustering of the spatial transcriptomic data 
identified 17 cell populations covering the major organ primordia. Notably, we 
observed spatially separable hepatocyte- and cholangiocyte-lineage primed 
transcriptional programmes within the liver primordium, and detected cardiac 
outflow tract and sinoatrial node progenitors at CS12. Furthermore, integration 
of gene and metabolite abundance highlighted regional associations between 
transcription factors and metabolic pathways underpinning lineage specification. 
Our work presents a spatially resolved multi-omic atlas of a human embryo at the 
onset of organogenesis.

Lineage plasticity-driven immunometabolic state transitions in advanced prostate 
cancer: biomarkers and therapeutic stratification.

Wu H(#)(1), Zhang W(#)(1), Yan X(#)(1), Ma K(#)(1), Colucci M(2), Dong Q(3), 
Song P(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Urology, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, 
Sichuan, China.
(2)Institute of Oncology Research (IOR), CH6500 Bellinzona, Switzerland, 
Università Della Svizzera Italiana, CH6900, Lugano, Switzerland.
(3)Department of Urology, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, 
Sichuan, China. dongqiang@scu.edu.cn.
(4)Department of Urology, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu,

Advanced prostate cancer is commonly described as immunologically cold, yet that 
label obscures a disease continually remodelled by treatment. Androgen-receptor 
(AR) pathway inhibition, chemotherapy, DNA-damage-directed therapy and 
radioligand treatment select resistant clones while altering lineage identity, 
metabolic dependence, antigen presentation and metastatic niches. AR-high, 
AR-low, double-negative, amphicrine and treatment-emergent neuroendocrine 
phenotypes are therefore better viewed as evolving immunometabolic states than 
as fixed histologies. Here, we develop a lineage-metabolism-immunity framework 
that integrates metastatic biopsies, longitudinal sampling, single-cell and 
spatial analyses, functional imaging and mechanistic prostate cancer models. 
Lineage determines which metabolic programmes remain available; tumour, stromal 
and immune cells then compete for nutrients and exchange metabolites that shape 
antigen presentation, myeloid suppression and lymphocyte function. We focus on 
glucose and lactate, lipids, amino acids, hypoxia-adenosine signalling and 
epigenetically active metabolites, while separating patient evidence from causal 
prostate cancer models and pan-cancer inference. The framework reframes three 
clinical tasks: identifying the state driving progression, recognising 
transitions under therapy and selecting combinations that relieve the dominant 
immune bottleneck without disabling effector cells. Translation will require 
longitudinal, lesion-aware measurements that connect lineage markers to 
functional evidence of metabolic dependence and immune context. The goal is not 
a universal metabolic target, but a tractable intervention matched to the tumour 
state, metastatic site and therapeutic window.

MAKR6 integrates TMK and CAMEL/CANAR signalling for auxin canalization in 
Arabidopsis.

Ge Z(1), Koczka L(2)(3), Mazur E(4), Molnar G(1), Vladimirtsev D(1), Kassem 
N(1), Ikene SA(1), Fiedler L(1), Friml J(5).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Science and Technology Austria, Klosterneuburg, Austria.
(2)Mendel Centre for Plant Genomics and Proteomics, Central European Institute 
of Technology, Masaryk University, Kamenice, Czech Republic.
(3)National Centre for Biomolecular Research, Faculty of Science, Masaryk

(4)Institute of Biology, Biotechnology and Environmental Protection, Faculty of

Adaptive plant development is orchestrated, among other means, by directional, 
intercellular transport of the phytohormone auxin. Self-organizing phenomena 
such as flexible vasculature formation depend on auxin canalization, which 
manifests as the gradual formation of auxin-transporting channels through 
feedback between auxin signalling and transport. Here we identify MAKR6 as a 
component of this feedback. MAKR6 transcripts accumulate in vascular cells and 
are tightly regulated by auxin via the Aux/IAA-ARF-WRKY23 transcriptional 
cascade. MAKR6 is required for auxin canalization-dependent processes, including 
leaf venation, vascular regeneration and de novo channel formation from local 
auxin sources. Mechanistically, MAKR6 interacts with the PIN1 auxin transporter 
and modulates its trafficking and polarization. MAKR6 also associates with and 
integrates TMK1/4 and CAMEL-CANAR, two key receptor-like kinase complexes 
involved in canalization. Together, our study establishes MAKR6 as a 
multifaceted regulator that couples transcriptional auxin signalling to PIN1 
repolarization and coordinates multiple RLK-mediated pathways into a concerted 
process. This provides mechanistic insight into auxin canalization and 
exemplifies a framework for exploring similar regulatory nodes in other 
developmental contexts.

Clinical outcomes of surgical laser interventions and adjunctive 
photobiomodulation in osseous crown lengthening: A systematic review.

Fereidouni K(1), Mosleh-Shirazi O(2), Nikdast P(3), Kiany F(4).

Author information:
(1)School of Dentistry, Shiraz University of Medical Sciences, Shiraz, Islamic 
Republic of Iran. kiarashfereidouni@gmail.com.
(2)School of Dentistry, Shiraz University of Medical Sciences, Shiraz, Islamic 
Republic of Iran.
(3)Department of Periodontics, School of Dentistry, Shiraz University of Medical 
Sciences, Shiraz, Islamic Republic of Iran.
(4)Oral and Dental Disease Research Center, Department of Periodontics, School 
of Dentistry, Shiraz University of Medical Sciences, Shiraz, Islamic Republic of 
Iran. kianif@sums.ac.ir.

To synthesize the available clinical evidence on laser-based interventions in 
osseous crown-lengthening procedures, considering surgical laser techniques and 
adjunctive photobiomodulation separately. A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, 
Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science was conducted from database inception 
to June 2025. We included clinical studies involving adults undergoing osseous 
crown lengthening with laser-assisted surgery or postoperative 
photobiomodulation. Three reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts, 
assessed potentially eligible full-text articles, and extracted data. Risk of 
bias was assessed at the outcome level using RoB 2 for randomized studies and 
ROBINS-I for the nonrandomized comparative study. Because of substantial 
clinical and methodological heterogeneity, we evaluated findings using a 
structured narrative synthesis rather than meta-analysis. We included five 
clinical studies published between 2021 and 2024. Three evaluated lasers used 
during the surgical procedure, while two evaluated adjunctive photobiomodulation 
following conventional surgery. Some studies reported reduced intraoperative 
bleeding and improved surgical visibility with surgical laser techniques, 
although they did not consistently assess these outcomes using standardized 
quantitative measures. Periodontal and gingival-margin outcomes were generally 
comparable with conventional procedures. Findings regarding postoperative pain 
were inconsistent, with benefits reported in some but not all studies. Across 
two small studies using different irradiation protocols, adjunctive 
photobiomodulation was associated with reduced early postoperative pain at 
selected assessment times; only one study reported lower analgesic consumption. 
Among the four randomized studies, one assessed result was judged to have a high 
overall risk of bias and three raised some concerns; none was judged to have a 
low overall risk of bias. The nonrandomized comparative study was judged to have 
a serious risk of bias. Some studies descriptively reported potential 
intraoperative advantages with surgical laser techniques, while adjunctive 
photobiomodulation may reduce early postoperative pain at selected assessment 
times. Given the small and heterogeneous evidence base and its methodological 
limitations, current evidence remains insufficient to establish superiority over 
conventional osseous crown-lengthening surgery or to identify an optimal laser 
protocol.Clinical trial number: not applicable.

Cooling water to near freezing breaks the activity-stability trade-off of water 
oxidation electrocatalysis.

Wardhana AC(1), Ooka H(1)(2), Lim T(1), Li A(1)(3), Adachi K(4), Chen C(1), 
Hashizume D(4), Nakamura R(5)(6).

Author information:
(1)Biofunctional Catalyst Research Team, RIKEN Center for Sustainable Resource 
Science (CSRS), Wako, Japan.
(2)Mathematical Catalysis Research Team, NIMS Research Center for Energy and 
Environmental Materials, Tsukuba, Japan.
(3)State Key Laboratory of Precision and Intelligent Chemistry, University of 
Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China.
(4)Materials Characterization Support Team, RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter 
Science (CEMS), Wako, Japan.
(5)Biofunctional Catalyst Research Team, RIKEN Center for Sustainable Resource 
Science (CSRS), Wako, Japan. ryuhei.nakamura@riken.jp.
(6)Earth-Life Science Institute (ELSI), Institute of Science Tokyo, Tokyo, 
Japan. ryuhei.nakamura@riken.jp.

Temperature is a fundamental parameter in reaction kinetics, typically 
accelerating rates according to the Arrhenius law. In catalytic systems, 
however, competing pathways often respond differently to temperature, allowing 
the selective promotion of desired reactions while suppressing undesired ones 
through temperature modulation. Here we show that regulating the temperature 
near the freezing point of water can resolve the activity-stability trade-off in 
the oxygen evolution reaction on manganese dioxide. Although lowering the 
temperature decreases water oxidation rates, catalyst degradation through 
permanganate formation is suppressed more effectively, extending catalyst 
lifetime. Counterintuitively, further cooling below 0 °C accelerates 
permanganate formation, yielding an optimum temperature near 0 °C that balances 
activity and stability. This anti-Arrhenius behaviour, arising from electrolyte 
supercooling, is a rare example of anomalous temperature-dependent 
electrocatalysis under subzero conditions. Our findings highlight temperature 
regulation as a viable strategy for enhancing catalytic lifetime, with 
implications for electrochemical systems operating in wintertime and in polar 
and extraterrestrial environments.

Artificial intelligence decision support for breast ultrasound: potential to 
reduce benign biopsies.

Fishman MDC(1), Lamb LR(1), Haver HL(2), Giess CS(2), DiPiro PJ(2), Chesebro 
AL(2), Chung SH(2), Gombos EC(2), Karimova EJ(2), Portnow LH(2), Saksena MA(1), 
Salah FA(2), Wang GX(1), Bahl M(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Radiology, Massachusetts General Hospital, 55 Fruit Street, WAC 
240, Boston, MA, 02114, USA.
(2)Department of Radiology, Brigham and Women's Hospital, 75 Francis Street, 
Boston, MA, 02115, USA.
(3)Department of Radiology, Massachusetts General Hospital, 55 Fruit Street, WAC 
240, Boston, MA, 02114, USA. mbahl1@mgh.harvard.edu.

PURPOSE: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the potential impact of a Food 
and Drug Administration (FDA)-cleared artificial intelligence (AI)-based 
decision support tool for breast ultrasound in reducing benign biopsies.
METHODS: This study was conducted at two academic medical centers from March to 
May 2025 following the clinical implementation of an FDA-cleared AI-based 
decision support tool for breast ultrasound interpretation (Koios DS; New York, 
NY). Fourteen breast imaging radiologists documented BI-RADS 4 (suspicious) 
cases, along with the corresponding AI output. AI assessments were compared with 
biopsy pathology results to characterize AI classification within this selected 
cohort.
RESULTS: Overall, 271 lesions in 253 women (mean age, 54 years; range, 
24-92 years) were categorized as BI-RADS 4 and were biopsied, aspirated, and/or 
surgically excised. Of these, 23.2% (63/271) yielded malignant pathology, while 
76.8% (208/271) were benign. The AI tool classified 90.5% (57/63) of malignant 
lesions as BI-RADS 4 and 9.5% (6/63) as BI-RADS 2 or 3. Among benign cases, the 
AI tool assigned 41.8% (87/208) as BI-RADS 2 (benign), 18.8% (39/208) as BI-RADS 
3 (probably benign), and 39.4% (82/208) as BI-RADS 4 (suspicious). Retrospective 
application of the AI output to biopsy triage decisions suggests the potential 
for reduction in benign biopsy recommendations, with 60.6% (126/208) of benign 
lesions classified by the AI tool as BI-RADS 2 or 3.
CONCLUSION: AI may help reduce benign biopsy recommendations among lesions 
assessed as BI-RADS 4 by radiologists; however, careful integration with 
radiologist judgment and clinical history is essential to ensure timely cancer 
diagnosis.

BACKGROUND: Watchful waiting (WW) for inguinal hernia has been established as a 
safe strategy for selected patients. However, this approach relies on regular 
long-term follow-up and adherence rates to WW are poorly characterized.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed including patients with 
inguinal hernia enrolled in a WW surveillance protocol between May 2013 and May 
2026. Follow-up visits were scheduled every 6 months during the first year and 
annually thereafter. Demographic, clinical, and long-term adherence to 
surveillance protocols were analyzed Patients who were lost to follow-up were 
contacted via a structured questionnaire to update their clinical status and 
identify causes for discontinuing protocol.
RESULTS: A total of 400 patients were included in the WW protocol. Overall 
follow-up adherence was low, with 240 patients (60.0%) failing to maintain 
scheduled surveillance at the end of this study. Kaplan-Meier analysis 
demonstrated a progressive drop out of the protocol over time. Younger age was 
an independent factor associated with follow-up discontinuation. Patients 
younger than 30 years demonstrated the highest rate of surveillance 
discontinuation (92.9%), compared with 63.6% among patients aged 30-50 years and 
56.4% among patients older than 50 years (p = 0.015). Seventy-seven (32%) 
responded to the survey; the most frequent causes for discontinuation were the 
absence of symptoms and the lack of awareness of recommended follow-up intervals 
(36% and 27%, respectively). Eleven patients (14.1%) had an elective hernia 
repair at another institution. No emergency surgery was identified among 
patients who remained under institutional follow-up or among those successfully 
contacted after surveillance discontinuation.
CONCLUSIONS: Watchful waiting appears to remain an acceptable management 
strategy for selected patients with asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic inguinal 
hernia. However, long-term adherence to surveillance beyond 2 years is low, 
posing a significant limitation to sustained WW management.

BACKGROUND: Intraoperative indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence cholangiography 
has been linked to fewer conversions to open surgery in emergency 
cholecystectomy, but it adds cost, and evidence for its effect on conversion and 
operative time is graded moderate to low even by the consensus statement 
recommending routine use. We asked whether preoperative C-reactive protein 
(CRP), a marker of surgical difficulty and conversion risk, identifies patients 
in whom ICG's benefit is greatest.
METHODS: Prospective cohort of 221 patients undergoing emergency laparoscopic 
cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis, stratified by ICG use (85 ICG vs 136 
conventional). We tested the interaction between CRP and ICG use on conversion 
using Firth penalized logistic regression, and on operative time, length of 
stay, and complications using linear/logistic regression with a log-CRP 
sensitivity analysis. We compared conversion rates across CRP tertiles and 
calculated a CRP-stratified estimated absolute risk reduction (ARR) and number 
needed to treat (NNT).
RESULTS: Conversion occurred only in the conventional arm (12/136, 8.8%; 0/85 
ICG), rising from 0 to 15.4% across CRP tertiles. The formal CRP×ICG interaction 
for conversion was not significant (Firth model, p = 0.878), reflecting the 
absence of ICG-arm events; the ARR associated with ICG use rose from not 
estimable to 9.8 points (95% CI 3.9-22.5; NNT≈10) in the middle tertile and 15.4 
points (95% CI 8.0-27.5; NNT 6.5) in the highest. The interaction was 
significant for operative time (p = 0.045), strengthening under a log-CRP 
sensitivity model (p = 0.001), with CRP-related lengthening of surgery markedly 
smaller in the ICG arm.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, ICG's clinical benefit was not uniform across the 
CRP range. The CRP×ICG interaction reached significance for operative time; for 
conversion, the pattern was consistent and clinically plausible but not 
statistically significant, and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. A 
CRP-informed strategy for prioritising ICG may be worth testing prospectively.

BACKGROUND: Lower rectal gastrointestinal stromal tumors (rGISTs) pose a 
surgical challenge, as complete resection must be balanced against anorectal 
function preservation. Transanal local excision (taLE) may offer a less invasive 
alternative to transabdominal laparoscopic radical resection (tlRR), but 
comparative evidence, particularly for larger tumors, is limited.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of patients with 
primary lower rGIST (lower tumor margin ≤ 5 cm from the anal verge; tumor size 
≥ 2 cm and < 7 cm) undergoing taLE or tlRR (April 2015-April 2023). Inverse 
probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) balanced baseline characteristics, and 
doubly robust models adjusted residual imbalance. Perioperative outcomes, 
recurrence-free survival (RFS), and a prespecified ≥ 5 cm subgroup analysis were 
evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 101 patients (taLE, n = 74; tlRR, n = 27; median follow-up, 
40 months), IPTW-adjusted analyses showed significantly reduced surgical burden 
with taLE: shorter operative time (- 118.4 min, P < 0.001), lower postoperative 
pain (- 2.5, P < 0.001), earlier drain removal (- 5.1 days, P = 0.008), no 
permanent stoma (0/74 vs. 5/27), and lower odds of temporary stoma (OR 0.05, 
P < 0.001) and reoperation (OR 0.02, P = 0.009). These advantages remained 
largely consistent in the ≥ 5 cm subgroup. Only four recurrences occurred, with 
no significant RFS difference (log-rank P = 0.43); power was limited.
CONCLUSIONS: taLE was associated with substantially reduced surgical burden in 
selected patients with lower rGIST, and no significant difference in 
recurrence-free survival was observed during available follow-up. However, with 
only four events, the study was underpowered to establish oncologic equivalence. 
The taLE-based organ-preserving pathway may represent a promising option pending 
confirmation in larger cohorts.

BACKGROUND: Lateral pancreaticojejunostomy (LPJ) is the treatment of choice in 
patients with symptomatic wide-duct chronic pancreatitis and a normal-size 
pancreatic head. Adequate pain control in the first days after LPJ via 
laparotomy is often challenging in these patients due to opioid tolerance 
resulting from chronic opioid use. Although a robotic approach may improve 
short-term outcome, comparative multicenter data on robotic versus open LPJ are 
lacking.
METHODS: This nationwide multicenter retrospective cohort study included 
consecutive adults who underwent robotic or open LPJ for symptomatic wide-duct 
chronic pancreatitis in the Netherlands (2010-2025). Primary outcomes were 
hospital stay and major complications (Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher).
RESULTS: Overall, 133 patients undergoing LPJ were included, of whom 36 (27%) 
robotic and 97 (73%) open LPJ. The robotic LPJ conversion rate was 0% (0/36). In 
the overall cohort, 90-day mortality was 0% (0/133) and median hospital stay was 
2 days shorter after robotic LPJ (5 [IQR, 4-7] vs 7 [6-10] days; P < 0.001) 
compared with open LPJ, while the rate of major complications did not differ 
significantly between groups (36.1% [13/36] vs 26.8% [26/97]; P = 0.405). Blood 
loss was less with robotic LPJ (100 [IQR, 50-100] vs 300 [125-500] mL; 
P < 0.001), whereas operative time was comparable (275 [IQR 180-330] vs 232 
[188-276] minutes; P = 0.210), and the rate of postoperative pancreatic fistula 
(POPF) grade B/C was higher (22.2% [8/36] vs 7.2% [7/97]; P = 0.034). The main 
findings of the overall cohort remained broadly consistent after propensity 
score matching.
CONCLUSIONS: In this early nationwide experience, robotic LPJ was associated 
with shorter hospital stay compared with open LPJ. Although operative time and 
major complications did not differ significantly between groups, POPF occurred 
more frequently after robotic LPJ. The potential benefits of robotic LPJ and the 
possible learning curve effect should be further assessed in randomized trials 
in experienced centers.

BACKGROUND: Older adults present unique challenges in emergency general surgery 
(EGS) due to increased comorbidities and frailty. While minimally invasive 
surgery (MIS), including laparoscopic (lap) and robotic techniques, reduces 
perioperative morbidity, the role of minimally invasive EGS in geriatric 
patients remains unclear. This study compares outcomes for geriatric EGS 
patients following robotic, lap, and open procedures. We hypothesize that MIS 
approaches would improve perioperative outcomes in geriatric patients.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the ACS-NSQIP database 
(2022-2023) including patients ≥65 years undergoing emergent or urgent 
intra-abdominal surgery. Operative approach was categorized as robotic, lap, or 
open. The primary outcome was severe complication, and secondary outcomes 
included length of stay (LOS), discharge disposition, and readmission.
RESULTS: 58,940 patients were included: 1832 robotic, 30,137 lap, and 26,971 
open. With robotic vs lap and open, operative time was shortest (82.5 vs 110 vs 
96 min, p < 0.001), conversion to open was less frequent (6.2 vs 12.9%, 
p < 0.001), and LOS was shorter (4 vs 4 vs 8 days, p < 0.001). Readmission and 
reoperation were lowest following MIS (9.2 vs 7.9 vs 9.8%, and 3.7 vs 3.3% vs 
7.6%, both p < 0.001). After propensity matching, robotic patients had higher 
ASA scores and more transfusions but lower rates of sepsis (2.6 vs 6.5%) and 
mortality (2.3 vs 2.7%) compared to the lap group (p < 0.001). Multivariable 
regression demonstrated decreased risk of severe complications for patients who 
underwent robotic surgery (p = 0.025) with no difference in operative time or 
LOS, and patients were more likely to be discharged home.
CONCLUSIONS: Robotic EGS in geriatric patients is associated with fewer severe 
complications, lower conversion rates, shorter LOS, and favorable discharge 
disposition.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of bilateral R2 
sympathetic surgery for CFH, to characterize the 10-year longitudinal trajectory 
of postoperative CH and recurrence, and to identify clinically accessible 
predictors of CH and postoperative satisfaction that may assist in preoperative 
risk communication. Preliminary nomograms were developed and internally 
validated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration plots, sensitivity, 
and specificity.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 127 patients who underwent bilateral R2 
sympathetic surgery for CFH between April 2013 and April 2023 were 
retrospectively analyzed. Baseline characteristics, operative details, and 
follow-up outcomes were extracted from medical records and structured telephone 
interviews. Predictive features were selected using least absolute shrinkage and 
selection operator (LASSO) regression. Cox proportional hazards and multivariate 
logistic regression models were subsequently applied to identify independent 
predictors of CH and satisfaction, respectively. Nomograms were developed and 
internally validated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic 
curve (AUC), calibration plots, sensitivity, and specificity.
RESULTS: All patients achieved immediate resolution of craniofacial sweating, 
accompanied by a significant postoperative heart rate reduction (84.8 ± 11.68 → 
72.17 ± 7.54 bpm, P < 0.001). Severe CH (grade IV) developed in 70.1% of 
patients, predominantly involving the thoracoabdominal (84.3%) and thigh (54.3%) 
regions. Cox regression identified preoperative heart rate > 79.5 bpm (HR = 
2.46, 95% CI 1.61-3.75, P = 0.0002) and sympathetic clamping (HR = 5.69, 95% CI 
3.03-10.67, P = 0.001) as independent risk factors for severe CH. Logistic 
regression showed that lower preoperative thoracoabdominal sweating was 
associated with higher postoperative satisfaction (OR = 0.05, 95% CI 0.01-0.23, 
P = 0.001). The nomograms demonstrated adequate discrimination and calibration.
CONCLUSION: Bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery achieves rapid and durable relief 
of craniofacial hyperhidrosis with sustained high satisfaction over 10 years. 
Beyond confirming efficacy, the extended follow-up uniquely demonstrates that CH 
severity stabilizes within the first postoperative year and does not worsen over 
time-a critical finding for patient reassurance. Preoperative resting heart rate 
> 79.5 bpm and the use of sympathetic clamping independently predict severe CH, 
whereas lower baseline thoracoabdominal sweating predicts superior satisfaction. 
Although the proposed nomograms require external validation before routine 
adoption, they offer a practical, individualized reference for preoperative risk 
communication and, combined with the intraoperative choice of electrocautery, 
support a dual-phase strategy for optimizing surgical outcomes in CFH patients.

BACKGROUND: Diverse representation in clinical research is essential for 
equitable healthcare. Despite mandates from organizations like the NIH and 
ICMJE, race and gender remain underreported in surgical research, raising 
concerns about the generalizability of findings. This study examines demographic 
reporting trends in minimally invasive surgery (MIS) and advanced endoscopy 
publications before and after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.
METHODS: A systematic review of Surgical Endoscopy, Journal of Robotic Surgery, 
and Surgical Innovation was conducted, analyzing articles published between 
January 1, 2018, and December 31, 2023. 472 studies were included. For each 
study, study type, journal, date, geographic origin, and reported demographic 
data were recorded. Reporting rates across time periods (pre- vs. post-March 
2020), region of origin, study design, and journal were analyzed via Chi-square, 
Fisher's exact tests, and Cochran-Armitage trend tests.
RESULTS: Of the 472 studies, 61.2% were randomized controlled trials, with 
geographic representation from Asia (37.7%), Europe (34.8%), and North America 
(22.3%). Only 21 North American studies (20 U.S., 1 Canada) reported race; no 
studies from Asia or Europe did so. Among U.S. studies, race reporting did not 
differ significantly pre- vs. post-COVID (22.2% vs. 21.8%; p = 0.25), nor did 
gender reporting (p = 0.07). Regional differences in U.S. race reporting were 
significant (p = 0.003), with the Midwest having the lowest rate. Post-2020, 
gender reporting was significantly higher in Asia (94.9%) compared to Europe 
(84.7%) and North America (80.9%) (p = 0.005).
CONCLUSIONS: Demographics remain underreported in MIS and advanced endoscopy 
research, particularly outside North America. Despite increased attention to 
health equity during the COVID-19 pandemic, reporting practices have not 
significantly improved. Broader adoption of standardized demographic reporting 
is needed to ensure evidence-based surgical care for all populations.

A multi-omics study integrating single-cell transcriptomics, spatial

m5C, an important RNA modification, is closely associated with breast cancer; 
however, their causal relationship is unknown. We examined the relationship 
between m5C regulation and breast cancer. Genome-wide association study breast 
cancer data and expression quantitative trait loci of m5C regulatory factor 
genes in blood were collected. We explored the causal relationship among m5C 
regulatory genes, breast cancer susceptibility, and prognosis through Mendelian 
randomization. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from peripheral blood mononuclear 
cells of patients with breast cancer and healthy controls were used to determine 
the differential expression of key genes among different cellular 
subpopulations. The effects of these genes on specific cellular subpopulations 
were further explored in single-cell RNAseq data from primary breast cancer 
using cellular communication, metabolic and cellular function analyses and 
validated the findings using flow cytometry. We validated the prognostic value 
of specific cellular subpopulations expressing key genes and assessed the impact 
of antitumor immunity using spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomics, and 
immunofluorescence analysis of tissue microarray (120 patients). Mendelian 
randomization analysis indicated that the expression of the m5C writer tRNA 
aspartate methyltransferase 1 (TRDMT1) in blood was associated with breast 
cancer prognosis. TRDMT1 expression in T cells was decreased in patients with 
breast cancer. TRDMT1 was closely related to T-cell function. Moreover, it may 
modulate the antitumor immune effects of CD8+ T cells by influencing cellular 
communication and metabolism, impacting the prognosis and immunotherapeutic 
response of patients with breast cancer. We confirmed the immunotherapy predict 
value and prognostic value of measuring TRDMT1 levels in CD8+ T cells, provided 
insights into enhancing CD8+ T-cell function, and identified potential targets 
to improve breast cancer prognosis and immunotherapy. Our research may help 
guide breast cancer treatment decisions and provide a prognostic evaluation 
option for future breast cancer treatment.

Intramuscular self-amplifying RNA and adenoviral RSV vaccines program distinct 
systemic and respiratory mucosal immune architectures.

Zhang Y(#)(1), Qin Y(#)(1), Qi Z(1), Yang Q(1), Zhang X(1), Hu S(1), Li Y(1), 
Xiao B(1), Hu J(1), Cheng P(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biotherapy, Cancer Center and State Key Laboratory of 
Biotherapy, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, 17 People's South Road, 
Chengdu, 610041, PR China.
(2)Department of Biotherapy, Cancer Center and State Key Laboratory of 
Biotherapy, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, 17 People's South Road, 
Chengdu, 610041, PR China. chengping@scu.edu.cn.
(#)Contributed equally

Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a major cause of severe lower 
respiratory tract disease in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised 
individuals, underscoring the need for vaccine strategies that balance systemic 
protection with frontline respiratory immunity. Although adenoviral and 
RNA-based RSV are both promising platforms, how the platform itself shapes 
systemic versus respiratory mucosal immunity under the same antigenic context 
remains insufficiently defined. We conducted a head-to-head comparison of an 
LNP-delivered saRNA vaccine (LNP-RSV-preF saRNA) and a recombinant Ad5-vectored 
vaccine (Ad5-RSV-preF) in mice using intramuscular prime-boost immunization. The 
two platforms drove distinct immune architectures rather than just differences 
in response magnitude. LNP-RSV-preF saRNA preferentially promoted respiratory 
mucosal immunity, including elevated BALF IgG, pulmonary antibody-secreting 
cells, CD69+ T cells, and lung-resident memory T (TRM) cells, as well as cycling 
and memory-associated CD8+ T-cell states and durable lung IgA memory. In 
contrast, Ad5-RSV-preF induced stronger systemic immunity, featured by higher 
early serum IgG, splenic polyfunctional effector T cells, enhanced germinal 
center/TFH responses, and effector-polarized CD8 + T cells, with sustained 
systemic humoral memory. Ad5-vectored and LNP-saRNA vaccine platforms induce 
distinct compartmentalized immune responses to the same RSV preF antigen. This 
study establishes a framework for rational platform selection in RSV vaccine 
design, enabling tailored strategies to balance systemic immunity and 
respiratory mucosal memory.

INTRODUCTION: Podany et al. examined associations between Area Deprivation Index 
(ADI) and tumor genomics, PI3K inhibitor use, and survival in 1,127 patients 
with metastatic breast cancer. While their multi-institutional, genomically 
annotated dataset is a valuable contribution, several methodological issues 
warrant scrutiny.

multiple-comparison handling, potential confounding from ctDNA shedding

BACKGROUND: In nipple-areola complex (NAC) reconstruction, maintaining the 
projection and volume of the reconstructed nipple is so important.
METHODS: This study evaluates the effectiveness of plasma-treated human 
acellular dermal matrix (hADM) in maintaining nipple projection and volume after 
nipple reconstruction using the modified C-V flap technique. We conducted a 
retrospective analysis of 42 patients who received either plasma-treated (n=20) 
or plasma-untreated (n=22) hADM grafts from October 2022 to January 2025. Nipple 
volumes were measured immediately after surgery and at intervals of 1, 4, 8, and 
24 weeks using Antera 3D® imaging.
RESULTS: The percentage of initial nipple volume maintained in the 
plasma-treated group was significantly greater than in the plasma-untreated 
group at 4 weeks (93.3% vs. 87.7%, p < 0.05), 8 weeks (87.3% vs. 78.6%, p < 
0.01), and 24 weeks (85.9% vs. 74.9%, p < 0.005). At 1 week, volumes were 
similar (99.4% vs. 98.6%, p > 0.05). A reduction in revision rates was noted, 
though this was not statistically significant. The incidence of complications 
was comparable between the two groups.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that plasma treatment of hADM improves 
volume maintenance in nipple reconstruction.

Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Reconstruction Planning of Cheek Soft Tissue 
Defects: A Comparative Study Against Surgical Expert Consensus.

Shafi R(1)(2), Radulesco T(3), Penicaud M(4), Michel J(3), Ebode D(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, AP-HM, La Conception 
University Hospital, marseille, France. Rahaf.shafii@gmail.com.
(2)University of Lorraine, Nancy, France. Rahaf.shafii@gmail.com.
(3)Aix Marseille University, CNRS, IUSTI, Marseille, France.
(4)Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, AP-HM, La Conception

BACKGROUND: Reconstructive planning for cheek soft tissue defects requires 
expert assessment of defect size and location to preserve aesthetic harmony. 
Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), has 
emerged as a potential decision-support tool in plastic and reconstructive 
surgery. This study evaluates the accuracy and reliability of ChatGPT-4o in 
proposing reconstructive approaches for post-excisional cheek defects.
METHODS: A comparative observational image-based study was performed using 46 
standardized oblique facial photographs of healthy volunteers, on which cheek 
soft tissue defects were manually delineated to simulate post-excisional tissue 
loss. Each annotated photograph was submitted to ChatGPT-4o alongside a 
standardized prompt incorporating patient-specific clinical data. Two experts 
independently rated AI-generated responses across five domains using a 
five-point Likert scale (1-5). Inter-rater agreement was assessed using Cohen's 
kappa and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC).
RESULTS: ChatGPT-4o achieved high ratings across all domains: clinical accuracy 
4.88/5, safety 4.59/5, aesthetic result 3.96/5, first reconstruction selection 
4.05/5, and relevance of alternatives 3.65/5, with an average of 4.22/5. Strong 
inter-rater agreement was observed between evaluators (ICC = 0.75, 95% CI 
0.57-0.86, p < 0.001), with high consistency for safety (κ = 0.82) and first 
reconstruction selection (κ = 0.76). However, ChatGPT-4o failed to generate 
illustrative depictions of the proposed reconstructive approaches.
CONCLUSION: ChatGPT-4o demonstrated strong concordance with expert evaluators 
and shows promise as a decision-support adjunct in cheek reconstructive 
planning. However, its inability to generate visual depictions of proposed flaps 
remains a notable limitation. Expert supervision remains indispensable, and 
prospective clinical validation is warranted before routine implementation.

Diagnostic accuracy of standard practice wrist MRI for scapholunate ligament 
injuries: a retrospective arthroscopic correlation study.

Spodzieja S(1), Boever J(2), Rau J(1)(3), Bruckner T(4), Müller H(1), Wulf J(2),

INTRODUCTION: The scapholunate ligament is the most injured intercarpal 
ligament. Untreated tears can lead to carpal instability and subsequent 
radiocarpal and midcarpal osteoarthritis. While wrist arthroscopy remains the 
gold standard, the diagnostic performance of standard practice preoperative MRI 
in clinical practice warrants further investigation.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed patients who underwent preoperative wrist 
MRI followed by wrist arthroscopy between 2013 and 2021. MRI findings regarding 
scapholunate ligament integrity were compared with arthroscopic findings serving 
as reference standard. Sensitivity and specificity were calculated for detection 
of any scapholunate ligament lesion (partial or complete tear).
RESULTS: A total of 889 patients were included. Complete paired data were 
available for 864 patients with a mean age of 42.4 ± 15.4 years (range 10-83 
years). 51.3% were male. MRI classified the ligament as intact in 83.9%, 
partially ruptured in 9.1%, and completely ruptured in 6.9%. Arthroscopy 
identified intact ligaments in 78.2%, partial tears in 12.9%, and complete tears 
in 8.9%. In this cohort, MRI demonstrated high specificity (91.1%, 95% CI 
89.0-93.3) but limited sensitivity (42.0%, 95% CI 35.0-49.1) for scapholunate 
ligament lesions.
CONCLUSION: In standard clinical practice, preoperative wrist MRI shows high 
specificity but insufficient sensitivity for detecting scapholunate ligament 
injuries. In this cohort, MRI detected intact ligaments reliably, but a relevant 
proportion of partial and complete tears remained unrecognized.

The landscape of gene loss and missense variation across the mammalian tree

Patterns of gene and sequence preservation across species provide insight into 
gene essentiality under natural selection. Here we developed two interspecies 
constraint metrics across 462 mammalian species: Gene Identity Score of 
Mammalian Orthologs (GISMO), which quantifies gene loss weighted by evolutionary 
distance to humans, and GISMO-mis, which measures missense constraint using the 
ratio of missense to synonymous variation across mammals. Both metrics are 
strongly correlated with human loss of function, missense and dosage constraint 
derived from large-scale sequencing studies, yet are largely independent of 
coding sequence length. GISMO and GISMO-mis identify essential genes missed by 
existing human-only metrics, particularly short genes. Genes in the most 
constrained deciles are enriched for rare variant associations in disorders 
linked to reduced fecundity, including schizophrenia, autism and 
neurodevelopmental disorders, and show strong enrichment for common variant 
heritability. These deciles also exhibit reduced copy number variation, 
consistent with dosage sensitivity. In addition, GISMO improves prioritization 
of recessive disease genes and captures signatures of homozygous selection 
across the mammalian tree. Taken together, GISMO and GISMO-mis leverage deep 
mammalian evolution to provide complementary, length-robust measures of gene 
essentiality that strengthen disease-gene prioritization and illuminate the 
selective forces shaping human biology.

A systems perspective on monoallelic inborn errors of immunity.

Werner M(1)(2)(3), Spaan AN(4), Mogensen TH(5)(6)(7).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biomedicine, Aarhus University, Aarhus, Denmark.
(2)Center for Immunology of Viral Infections, Aarhus University, Aarhus,

The genetic architecture of inborn errors of immunity continues to grow in 
complexity, exposing the limitations of variant-centric concepts that have long 
shaped the field. While complete loss-of-function genotypes have been 
instrumental in defining essential gene functions in human immunity and 
inflammation, they have also entrenched binary interpretations of causality that 
fail to account for pleiotropy, variable expressivity and incomplete 
penetrance-especially in monoallelic disease. Monoallelic variants often perturb 
signaling rather than abolishing it. The integration of these perturbations into 
molecular and cellular systems, and eventually immune circuits, governs 
phenotypic expression. Here, we revisit and extend classic concepts of genetic 
dominance and genetic pleiotropy and suggest that these are not sole properties 
of alleles but emerge from the complex and dynamic behavior of molecular, 
cellular and immune systems to buffer genetic variance.

Conditional and joint (COJO) analysis of genome-wide association study (GWAS) 
data is a standard post-GWAS analysis for identifying statistically independent 
associations. Although GWAS meta-analyses are increasingly conducted across 
multiple ancestry groups, the optimal strategy for multiancestry COJO analysis 
remains unclear. Here we introduce Manc-COJO, a method for multiancestry COJO 
analysis. Simulations and real-data analyses show that Manc-COJO improves 
detection of independent association signals while reducing false positives 
compared with single-ancestry COJO implemented in genome-wide complex trait 
analysis (GCTA) and its ad-hoc multiancestry adaptations. We also introduce 
Manc-COJO:FIX, a follow-up algorithm to identify ancestry-specific independent 
associations. The C++ implementation of Manc-COJO is over 120-fold faster than 
GCTA-COJO and supports linkage disequilibrium references derived from either 
individual-level genotype data or pre-computed matrices, facilitating analyses 
when data sharing is limited.

Cyto-genotoxic potential and in silico analysis of emerging contaminants of the 
Ganges River water.

Akhtar S(1), Malik A(2).

The Ganges River, vital for drinking water, agriculture, fisheries, and 
socio-religious practices, is increasingly threatened by contaminants, 
compromising its ecological and biological integrity. Present study was 
undertaken to identify contaminants in the river water using chemical profiling 
integrated with bacterial and plant bioassays, complemented by in silico 
analysis. GC-MS analysis of hexane and chloroform extracts revealed the presence

to 20.62%, along with increased chromosomal abnormalities from 2.33% to 26.17%.

by root tip damage and reduced root cell viability as detected by confocal 
microscopy. Computational docking analysis and 100-ns molecular dynamics 
simulations revealed stable binding of selected contaminants to molecular 
targets involved in nucleotide biosynthesis, DNA replication, topological 
regulation, and cell division. These findings suggested that the bioactive 
compounds may induce genetic and cellular damage, contributing to the biological 
effects associated with contaminant mixtures in river water.

A simple single-reagent colorimetric method for arsenic speciation analysis:

Ganveer S(1), Pruseth KL(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Geology and Geophysics, Indian Institute of Technology

In this study, a simple colorimetric method was developed using cupric acetate 
monohydrate to detect and differentiate arsenic species in groundwater in the 
Dongargarh-Kotri region, Chhattisgarh, Central India. The method produced 
precipitate that was distinctly green for As(III) and blue for As(V). The method 
achieved a detection limit of 5.5  μ g L - 1 in collected groundwater samples

method also offers a semi-quantitative estimation of the relative proportions of 
As(III) and As(V). The successful application of this method to contaminated 
groundwater samples demonstrates its potential as a rapid, low-cost, and 
field-deployable screening tool for arsenic speciation and monitoring in 
resource-limited regions.

Although brain cholesterol dysregulation is implicated in Parkinson's disease 
(PD), targeting cholesterol synthesis has shown limited efficacy. Here we 
identify ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) as a critical regulator of 
cholesterol homeostasis in PD. We show that ABCA1 expression is elevated in the 
substantia nigra of postmortem PD brains and in a PD mouse model, with regional 
analyses revealing preferential alterations in nigral and striatal circuits. 
Mechanistically, astrocytic ABCA1 drives excessive cholesterol efflux in mice, 
promoting neuronal cholesterol overload. In neurons, ABCA1 localizes to 
lysosomes, where it facilitates cholesterol import, leading to cholesterol 
accumulation, autophagy impairment and α-synuclein pathology. Genetic silencing 
of Abca1 in either astrocytes or dopaminergic neurons attenuates 
neurodegeneration and behavioral deficits in vivo. Furthermore, we identify 
magnesium citrate as an ABCA1 inhibitor and show that it reduces dopaminergic 
neuronal loss in a PD mouse model. Our findings identify an ABCA1-dependent 
cholesterol pathway underlying PD pathogenesis and support ABCA1 inhibition as a 
potential disease-modifying strategy.

The thalamus integrates sensory, motor and associative functions through 
distinct nuclei, yet the developmental principles driving their specification 
remain unclear. Here we generate a spatiotemporal single-cell multiomic and 
spatial transcriptomic atlas of the embryonic mouse thalamus, combined with 
barcoding-based lineage tracing. We identify two major glutamatergic lineages, 
sensory-related and motor-associative, each governed by different gene 
regulatory programs and temporal dynamics. These lineages arise from spatially

fate. Together, our findings define the molecular architecture and developmental 
trajectories that underpin thalamic modality specification, providing a 
framework to understand how functional circuits emerge in the mammalian brain.

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is rising globally, yet factors shaping its 
genomic evolution remain poorly understood. We investigated how socioeconomic, 
climate, and health factors are associated with AMR spread in multi-drug 
resistant (MDR) Salmonella enterica across China's food chain, mapped hotspots 
and forecasted genomic trait prevalence to 2050. We analysed 2,536 MDR genomes 
from 15 provinces over 16 years, covering patients, food and non-food workers, 
meat, livestock, and environmental sources. A machine learning framework 
integrated genomic surveillance with risk assessment to identify high-risk AMR 
traits (clinically relevant, MDR, mobile). Regression models linked trait 
prevalence to socioeconomic, climate, health, and antimicrobial consumption 
data, informing projections to 2050. Eighty-four high-risk traits, including 
carbapenem, colistin, and β-lactam resistance, are projected to rise, with 
antibiotic use, population growth, healthcare spending, and urbanisation. 
Projections were trait-specific: blaCTX-M-64 and blaTEM-1 may increase up to 
20%, while blaCTX-M-65 and blaCTX-M-14 remain below 5%. A mechanistic shift in 
fluoroquinolone resistance is projected: mutation-based resistance (gyrA 87) 
declines while plasmid-mediated genes (qnrB17, qnrS1) rise. Food workers emerged 
as a potential reservoir, showing higher trait prevalence than food sources, 
uniquely carrying last-resort antibiotic-resistance genes (blaTEM-30, blaNDM-5, 
blaCTX-M-64). Integrating genomic with socioeconomic surveillance could shift 
AMR interventions from reactive to preventive.

Food insecurity in the development of metabolic diseases.

Pérez-Escamilla R(1), Hernández-Cordero S(2), Franco-Lares B(2), Lara-Mejía 
V(2).

Author information:
(1)Yale School of Public Health, New Haven, CT, USA. 
rafael.perez-escamilla@yale.edu.
(2)Research Institute for Equitable Development (EQUIDE), Universidad 
Iberoamericana, Mexico City, Mexico.

This Review discusses the current evidence on the relationship between food 
insecurity, obesity, metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and 
identifies potential interventions to mitigate the effect of food insecurity on 
these conditions. Studies in adults (mainly cross-sectional) have consistently 
found associations between food insecurity and several cardiometabolic diseases, 
including obesity (mainly among women), hyperlipidaemia, metabolic syndrome, 
hypertension, cardiovascular disease and T2DM. These associations represent 
plausible causal relationships given that food insecurity can be a powerful 
psycho-emotional stressor that can cause distress, anxiety and depressive 
symptoms across the life course; poor dietary quality can increase the risk of 
metabolic syndrome and T2DM through increased visceral adiposity and insulin 
resistance, inflammation and an unhealthy microbiome; and food insecurity can 
cause healthcare behavioural trade-offs such as prioritizing purchasing food 
over medications for T2DM prevention or management. Community-based, healthy 
lifestyle promotion, early-life nutrition and Food as Medicine programmes could 
mitigate the negative effect of food insecurity on T2DM risk and metabolic 
health. There is a need to rigorously evaluate the results of promising 
large-scale interventions on food insecurity and cardiometabolic health 
outcomes.

Effects of routine laboratory parameter variations on diatom preservation: 
Implications for the standardization of forensic diatom testing.

Qiu H(#)(1)(2), Yu L(#)(3), Yin M(#)(4), Zhao Y(5), Zhou L(1), He X(6), Huang 
P(7), Zhang J(8).

Author information:
(1)School of Forensic Medicine, Shanxi Medical University, Shanxi, China.
(2)Shanghai Key Laboratory of Forensic Medicine, Shanghai Forensic Service 
Platform, Academy of Forensic Science, Ministry of Justice, Shanghai, China.
(3)Fujian Chengyuan Judicial Identification Center, Fujian, China.
(4)Institute of Forensic Science, Shenzhen Second People's Hospital, The First 
Affiliated Hospital of Shenzhen University, Guangdong, China.
(5)Fujian Hengxin Judicial Identification Center, Fujian, China.
(6)Shanghai Key Laboratory of Forensic Medicine, Shanghai Forensic Service 
Platform, Academy of Forensic Science, Ministry of Justice, Shanghai, China. 
hexd@ssfjd.com.
(7)Institute of Forensic Science, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. 
huangping@fudan.edu.cn.
(8)Shanghai Key Laboratory of Forensic Medicine, Shanghai Forensic Service

Forensic diatom testing remains controversial in drowning diagnosis and site 
inference, highlighting the need for standardized protocols. However, despite 
being involved in nearly all diatom testing methods, routine laboratory 
parameters have often been overlooked, and their effects on diatom preservation 
remain poorly investigated. This study systematically evaluated the effects of 
digestion parameters and washing procedure on diatom recovery and assemblage 
preservation, including digestion temperature and duration, centrifugation force 
and duration, washing frequency, and the residual pellet volume retained after 
each centrifugation. Controlled spiking experiments were performed using pooled 
natural water samples and human lung tissue. Procedural performance was assessed 
based on the diatom recovery rate and multiple assemblage-based indicators, 
including Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, Jaccard similarity, Spearman's rank 
correlation, and replicate dispersion. Both diatom recovery and assemblage 
integrity were better maintained under the selected combination of heating at 
≤ 80 °C for ≤ 60 min, centrifugation at 3,000 rpm (1,313×g) for 5 min, and one 
washing cycle with 500 µL retained after centrifugation. Based on these 
parameters, we established an optimized extraction workflow that increased 
diatom recovery rates from 16.45% to 41.00% for acid digestion and from 80.87% 
to 84.42% for enzymatic digestion, while maintaining assemblage composition 
comparable to that of the reference water samples. Our findings suggest that 
routine laboratory parameters should be incorporated into the standardization of 
forensic diatom testing, as their optimization can substantially improve diatom 
preservation.

Traumatic lumbar disc injury - radiology and biomechanics.

Rautenberg A(#)(1), Eckardt N(#)(1), Streng J(1), Schwarz F(2), Wilharm A(3), 
Hubig M(4), Muggenthaler H(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Radiology, Jena University Hospital, Friedrich Schiller 
University, Jena, Germany.
(2)Department of Neurosurgery, Jena University Hospital, Friedrich Schiller 
University, Jena, Germany.
(3)Department of Trauma Surgery, Jena University Hospital, Friedrich Schiller

(4)Institute of Legal Medicine, Jena University Hospital, Friedrich Schiller

(5)Institute of Legal Medicine, Jena University Hospital, Friedrich Schiller

BACKGROUND: Traumatic disc injury is typically diagnosed in patients with 
multiple injuries resulting from high-energy trauma. However, patients often 
claim a causal link between minor trauma and disc injury.
RESEARCH QUESTIONS: Do traumatic lumbar disc injuries occur in low-energy trauma 
or accidents? Are there always accompanying spinal injuries? What are the main 
injury mechanisms?
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Two data sources were surveyed: Patients treated at a 
tertiary centre (UKJ) and the NHTSA (National Highway Traffic Safety 
Administration) accident database. The UKJ data underwent a second 
neuroradiological look, and the discharge summaries and surgical protocols were 
analysed. In addition to the NHTSA case evaluation, an exploratory risk 
assessment based on cumulative frequency distributions is provided.
RESULTS: Of the 33 UKJ patients, most sustained falls from a standing height, as 
well as from a greater height. Trauma-related neuroradiological findings and 
accompanying spinal fractures (mostly compression-type) were present in all UKJ 
cases. Two out of ten occupants in the NHTSA database sustained low-velocity 
accidents without accompanying injuries.
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: Although rare, traumatic lumbar disc injuries can 
occur during low-energy events, such as falling from a standing height. However, 
this presumably affects older patients or those with relevant pre-existing 
spinal conditions. Due to the small number of NHTSA cases, it cannot be 
concluded that traumatic lumbar disc injuries are always associated with high 
accident severity. Nevertheless, the reliability of injury documentation in 
accident databases appears to be limited, particularly in cases of rare injury 
patterns.

Brain-based predictive models offer a promising approach to understanding 
individual differences in cognitive functioning across the lifespan. This review 
synthesizes current literature on brain-based cognitive predictions using 
large-scale datasets, examining how methodological choices and data-related 
factors impact model performance. We find that brain-based predictive models 
demonstrate relatively consistent, albeit wide ranging performance across the 
lifespan, explaining approximately 10-40% of variance in cognitive abilities. 
Key findings include: (1) models perform better when predicting general 
cognitive ability compared to specific functions; (2) crystallized abilities are 
more predictable than fluid abilities; (3) task-based functional connectivity 
generally outperforms resting-state approaches in younger populations, while 
structural measures become superior predictors in older adults; (4) multimodal 
approaches using hierarchical stacked models optimize prediction accuracy; and 
(5) elastic net and ridge regression provide optimal balance between predictive 
performance and computational efficiency. In summary, we propose methodological 
advances to improve the precision and utility of brain-based cognitive 
predictions.

Association of pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration with early 
postoperative hemostasis in patients undergoing head-pelvic ring traction and 
three-column osteotomy for severe spinal deformity: a retrospective study.

Li H(1), Liang Y(2), Liang Y(3), Zhao D(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Spine surgery, Peking University People's Hospital, Beijing, 
China.
(2)Department of Spine surgery, Peking University People's Hospital, Beijing, 
China. liangyan7503@163.com.
(3)Department of Spine Surgery, Chengdu BOE Hospital, Chengdu, China. 
yijiancq@163.com.
(4)Department of Orthopedics, The Second Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing 
Medical University, Chongqing, China. pkuzd87@sina.com.

BACKGROUND: Severe spinal deformity correction is associated with substantial 
perioperative blood loss. Evidence on pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen 
administration in this setting remains limited. This study evaluated whether 
pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration was associated with more 
favorable early postoperative hemostasis-related parameters.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 50 patients with severe 
spinal deformity who underwent head-pelvic ring traction followed by corrective 
surgery. Patients were classified into a fibrinogen group and a non-fibrinogen 
group according to whether they received pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen 
administration. Postoperative coagulation parameters, hemoglobin (Hb) levels, 
drainage volume, and radiographic correction outcomes were compared between 
groups.
RESULTS: Twenty-five patients were included in each group. Baseline 
characteristics, operative time, intraoperative blood loss, and radiographic 
correction outcomes were comparable between groups. Compared with the 
non-fibrinogen group, the fibrinogen group had lower postoperative prothrombin 
time and international normalized ratio, and higher prothrombin activity and 
fibrinogen levels (all P < 0.01). Hb levels on postoperative days 1 and 3 were 
higher in the fibrinogen group, whereas postoperative drainage volume and 
postoperative red blood cell transfusion volume were lower (P = 0.002, 0.036, 
0.005, and < 0.001, respectively). No significant between-group difference was 
observed in Hb level on postoperative day 7.
CONCLUSIONS: Pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration was associated 
with more favorable early postoperative hemostasis-related parameters in 
patients undergoing corrective surgery for severe spinal deformity. Given the 
retrospective design and potential residual confounding, these findings should 
be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require validation in prospective 
studies.
