Exploring Perspectives and Barriers in Implementing Home Monitoring for 
Pediatric Pulmonary Diseases: Mixed Methods Study.

Stoop MH(1)(2), Krul R(1), Manai BH(3), Groothuis I(1), Sprij AJ(1), Nuijsink 
M(1), Janssens HM(3)(4), Kruizinga MD(1)(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pediatrics, Haga Teaching Hospital, Juliana Children's 
Hospital, The Hague, South Holland, The Netherlands.
(2)Department of Pediatrics, MosaKids Children's Hospital, Maastricht University 
Medical Centre, Maastricht, Limburg, The Netherlands.
(3)Department of Pediatrics, Sophia Children's Hospital, Erasmus MC, Rotterdam, 
South Holland, The Netherlands.
(4)Cystic Fibrosis Core Network Group, ERN LUNG, Frankfurt, Hesse, Germany.
(5)Department of Pediatrics, Leiden University Medical Center, Leiden, South 
Holland, The Netherlands.

BACKGROUND: Home monitoring has the potential to enable early detection of 
disease progression in pediatric lung diseases such as asthma and cystic 
fibrosis (CF). There is minimal evidence regarding the opinions of caregivers 
and children on home monitoring.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore children's and caregivers' perspectives 
on home monitoring.
METHODS: This multicenter, mixed methods study included children aged 6 to 18 
years with asthma or CF and their caregivers. Participants were recruited from 
Juliana Children's Hospital and Erasmus MC Sophia Children's Hospital between 
September 2023 and June 2025. Participants completed a structured questionnaire 
assessing experiences, attitudes, and potential barriers and facilitators to 
home monitoring. Fourteen children and their caregivers took part in in-depth 
interviews. Conventional content analysis was applied to both open-text and 
interview data.
RESULTS: A total of 113 caregiver-child dyads (62 [54.9%] asthma and 51 [45.1%] 
CF) participated in this study. Willingness to use home monitoring was high 
among both children (asthma: n=47, 83.9%; CF: n=30, 62.5%) and caregivers 
(asthma: n=54, 87.1%; CF: n=44, 86.3%). Children with asthma and their 
caregivers showed significantly greater willingness to use the proposed types of 
home monitoring than children with CF and their caregivers. Caregivers who 
expressed difficulty with symptom interpretation were significantly more 
motivated to use home monitoring. Key barriers included time demands, usability, 
device size, and concerns about maintaining personal contact with health care 
providers. Facilitators included compact, user-friendly devices, clear 
instructions, and improved disease understanding.
CONCLUSIONS: High willingness to adopt home monitoring was observed among 
children with asthma and children with CF, but preferences and perceived 
barriers differ. Tailoring device choice and implementation strategies to 
patient needs, minimizing burden, and integrating medical oversight are 
important for successful uptake.

Comprehensive analysis of Lewis antigen expression patterns in a Chinese blood 
donor cohort.

Zheng J(1), Zhang Y(1), Jin S(1), Zhu X(1), Xiang D(1).

Author information:
(1)Blood Group Reference Laboratory, Institute of Blood Transfusion, Shanghai 
Blood Center, Shanghai, China.

BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: To characterise FUT2 and FUT3 haplotype and genotype 
frequencies among 529 Shanghai Han voluntary blood donors, and quantify 
erythrocyte Leᵃ and Leᵇ expression via flow cytometry. This study extends the 
established Seʷ/c.418A>T partial-secretor model to a large Chinese cohort using 
combined sequencing and quantitative red cell Lewis antigen flow cytometry.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Routine serological ABO grouping was performed. Flow 
cytometry was used to quantify Leᵃ and Leᵇ mean fluorescence intensity (MFI). 
Sanger sequencing combined with thymine-adenine (TA) cloning was applied to 
resolve FUT2/FUT3 cis-haplotypes. Owing to marked skewness and 
heteroscedasticity of MFI data, non-parametric Mann-Whitney U tests with 
Bonferroni correction were used for subgroup comparisons.
RESULTS: A total of 1046 FUT2 alleles were genotyped: secretor (Se, n = 575, 
54.3%), weak-secretor (Seʷ, n = 443, 41.9%), non-secretor (se, n = 28, 2.6%), 
with eight novel sequence variants. For FUT3, 1053 alleles were resolved: 
functional (Le, n = 806, 76.2%), loss-of-function (le, n = 247, 23.3%), 
alongside five novel variants (0.5%). Seʷ homozygosity elevated Leᵃ and reduced 
Leᵇ in carriers with functional FUT3. Considerable inter-individual variability 
persisted even among donors with identical ABO-FUT2-FUT3 genotypes.
CONCLUSION: Erythrocyte Lewis antigen abundance is primarily governed by 
competitive substrate utilisation of a common type 1 precursor glycan by FUT2 
and FUT3 glycosyltransferases. The residual heterogeneity indicates additional 
host factors beyond these three loci. This study validates the classic Seʷ 
partial-secretor model in a Chinese cohort and provides population reference 
data, rather than reporting unrecognised biosynthetic pathways.

Gao Y(1)(2), Shen Z(3)(4), Cui X(1)(2)(5), Chen M(1)(2)(5), Wang M(6), Liu

Whether female germline stem cells (fGSCs) exist in postnatal mammalian ovaries 
has been debated for decades. Since the fGSCs were first reported in 2004, a 
large number of studies have been conducted using different approaches. However, 
the persistent controversy surrounding the results has caused confusion among 
many researchers and clinicians. To clearly clarify this question, we developed 
advanced tracing system to label any possible fGSCs in adult female mice. Our 
results showed that no Stra8-expressing germ cells were detected in the ovaries

and postnatal oogenesis do not exist under both physiological and pathological 
conditions in mouse models, therefore reinforcing the notion that the primordial 
follicle pool established perinatally serves as the primary source of oocytes 
through the entire reproductive lifespan.

Workflow Topology-Guided Skill Loading for Agentic AI in Clinical Trial Data 
Pipelines: Sequential Exploratory Evaluation.

Yan J(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Data Science, Harrisburg University of Science and Technology, 
Harrisburg, PA, United States.

BACKGROUND: Clinical trial data pipelines must follow Clinical Data Interchange 
Standards Consortium (CDISC) standards, including the study data tabulation 
model (SDTM) and analysis data model (ADaM). General-purpose large language 
models (LLMs) can produce plausible artifacts that omit required variables, 
misuse terminology, or invent derivation logic. Curated context may reduce these 
errors, but the value of organizing that context by workflow topology has not 
been separated from corpus access alone.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine when workflow topology-guided skill 
loading adds value beyond a domain prompt, nonrouted curated context, or lexical 
retrieval, and whether bounded scheduling retains quality with less injected 
context.
METHODS: A 45-node, 7-layer directed acyclic workflow graph was linked to 59 
modular rule files (SKILL.md). A sequential exploratory evaluation examined 4 
evidence regimes spanning domain-context, component isolation, lexically 
reachable, and topology-dependent conditions (10 tasks, 90 runs; 10 tasks, 180 
and 120 runs; 24 tasks, 288 runs; and 18 tasks, 324 runs; the task, not the 
agent run, was the inferential unit). End points included LLM rubric scores, 
deterministic atomic criteria, required-evidence recall, and manifest checks. A 
blinded practicing statistical programmer independently rescored 60 outputs. 
Task-level paired inference used bootstrap 95% CIs, exact sign-flip tests, and 
Holm adjustment.
RESULTS: Routed context scored 4.63 versus 4.20 for prompt-only (difference 0.43 
on a 1-5 scale; 95% CI 0.25-0.63; Holm-adjusted P=.01) but did not exceed flat 
or random loading. The lower-context scheduler used 28.82% less context while 
retaining quality; all 559 injected fragments had recorded sources, and all 120 
manifests were reproduced exactly. On lexically reachable tasks, graph+Best 
Match 25 (BM25) and BM25-only were equivalent within a 0.05 margin (difference 
+0.009; 95% CI -0.028 to 0.046; P=.67), where BM25 already recalled 95.8% of 
required evidence. On topology-dependent stress tasks, graph-only selection 
outperformed BM25-only (difference 0.348; 95% CI 0.178-0.530; nominal P=.002; 
dz=0.89) and raised required-evidence recall from 0.500 to 1.000. Expert-judge 
agreement was substantial for terminology (weighted κ=0.61) and moderate overall 
(intraclass correlation coefficient=0.60).
CONCLUSIONS: Workflow topology serves as a conditional retrieval prior. It adds 
little when lexical retrieval already reaches the required evidence but recovers 
dependency-linked evidence when task wording does not identify it lexically. 
These findings, from a synthetic benchmark using one generator backbone and one

Chang CT(1), Lim XJ(2), Lee JCY(3), Chew CC(1), Wong YJ(4), Chan HK(5), Thum 
CC(6), Yew KM(7), Yeow SH(8), Rajan P(2).

Author information:

(2)Clinical Research Centre, Hospital Raja Permaisuri Bainun, Ipoh, Perak,

(4)School of Pharmacy, Monash University Malaysia, Subang Jaya, Selangor,

(6)Ministry of Communications, Putrajaya, Malaysia.
(7)Klinik Kesihatan Kampar, Ministry of Health Malaysia, Kampar, Perak,

BACKGROUND: AI is increasingly integrated into health care systems worldwide, 
with growing implications for pharmacy practice. Although studies have reported 
general perceptions of AI, gaps between awareness and practical implementation 
remain evident, particularly in middle-income settings.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the baseline knowledge, attitudes, and 
practices (KAP) of Malaysian pharmacists regarding AI adoption in pharmacy 
practice and identify factors associated with these domains.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted using a self-administered online 
questionnaire distributed to registered pharmacists practicing in Malaysia. The 
instrument comprised 12 knowledge items, 10 attitude items, and 5 practice items 
and underwent expert review and pilot testing. KAP scores were categorized using 
Bloom cutoff points as good (80%-100%), moderate (60%-79%), or poor (<60%). Data 
were analyzed using R statistical software.
RESULTS: A total of 407 pharmacists completed the survey. The median knowledge 
score was 75 (IQR 67-92), with 42.3% (172/407) of pharmacists demonstrating good

pharmacists exhibited positive attitudes toward AI. However, the median practice 
score was 56 (IQR 44-68), with 54.3% (221/407) of pharmacists classified as

correlations were observed among the 3 domains. Pharmacists with postgraduate 
qualifications demonstrated significantly higher knowledge scores (P=.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Malaysian pharmacists demonstrated moderate knowledge and positive 
attitudes toward AI. However, the practical integration of AI into routine 
pharmacy workflows remained limited. Strengthening institutional support, 
structured training, and implementation frameworks may be necessary to translate 
perceived readiness into clinical adoption.

Improved Hold Time, Unproven Benefit: Reassessing the Cervical Endurance Hold as 
an Outcome Measure in Fighter Pilots.

Acevedo A(1), Zeigler Z(1).

Author information:
(1)Exercise and Nutritional Sciences, College of Natural Science, Grand Canyon 
University, Phoenix, AZ 85017, United States.

Improvements in cervical endurance hold (CEH) time have been used as evidence 
that training interventions reduce neck pain risk in Air Force fighter pilots. 
This assumes that a longer hold time reflects a meaningfully lower risk of neck 
pain in this population, an assumption that remains unvalidated. We examine the 
reliability and validity evidence for the CEH and argue that its use as a 
surrogate for training success should be reconsidered. The CEH, known as 
Grimmer's test, shows strong intra-rater reliability but considerably weaker 
inter-rater reliability, particularly where test cessation depends on subjective 
examiner judgment rather than pain or exhaustion. No reliability data exist for 
this test in fighter pilots specifically. Validity evidence in this population 
was absent until a 2026 study of Royal Air Force Typhoon pilots found no 
significant correlation between neck flexor endurance and flight-related neck 
pain, despite high pain prevalence in the cohort. This is the first direct test 
of the assumption underlying the test's current use as an outcome measure, and 
it does not support that assumption. Prior evidence further suggests that neck 
pain in military pilots is more associated with coronal plane strength than the 
sagittal plane flexion this test assesses, and evidence that training cervical 
endurance reduces neck pain incidence remains mixed. An improvement in hold time 
is weak evidence that an intervention reduced neck pain risk. We recommend that 
the CEH be reported as a measure of endurance, not a proxy for pain outcomes, 
with future work evaluating coronal plane and extension-based alternatives.

Maternal Education in Context: Reassessing the Infant Health Paradox among Latin 
American Immigrants.

Liu TT(1), Hamilton TG(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Sociology and Office of Population Research, Princeton 
University, Princeton, NJ 08540, USA.

One aspect of the Hispanic Health Paradox is the longstanding observation that 
Latin American immigrants in the United States often experience equal or better 
health outcomes than U.S.-born counterparts despite greater socioeconomic 
disadvantage. This advantage extends to their infants and is most pronounced 
among mothers with the least education. Whether such patterns reflect selective 
migration remains unclear. This study evaluates the role of educational 
selectivity in explaining nativity disparities in infant health. Using U.S. 
natality data among immigrants from Mexico, Cuba, El Salvador, Guatemala, the 
Dominican Republic, Colombia, Honduras, and Venezuela (2012-2023), linked with 
internationally harmonized educational data, we assess preterm birth disparities 
using two measures of maternal education: absolute and relative attainment. 
Immigrants at the bottom of the U.S. education distribution often rank much 
higher in their origin countries, consistent with positive selection. For most 
births to Latin American mothers (except Colombian and Venezuelan), measuring 
education relative to origin-country distributions reverses immigrant 
advantages. At equivalent relative education ranks, immigrant mothers face 
comparable or higher risks of preterm birth than U.S.-born Hispanic mothers. 
These findings offer a new perspective on the Hispanic Health Paradox, 
highlighting the importance of relative education in understanding the 
association between maternal education and infant health.

Hat1 Orchestrates Heterochromatin Structure by Regulating Localization of H3K9 
Methyltransferases.

Martin CJ(1), Popova LV(1), Nagarajan P(1), Oser EA(1), Lovejoy CM(1), Sunkel 
BD(2), Stanton BZ(2), Freitas MA(1), Parthun MR(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biological Chemistry and Pharmacology, The Ohio State 
University, Columbus, OH 43210, USA.
(2)Abigail Wexner Research Institute at Nationwide Children's, Columbus, OH 
43205.
(3)Department of Biological Chemistry and Pharmacology, The Ohio State 
University, Columbus, OH 43210, USA. Electronic address: Parthun.1@osu.edu.

Many regions of heterochromatin associate with the nuclear periphery and are 
known as Lamin-associated domains (LADs). Histone acetyltransferase 1 (Hat1) is 
a highly conserved enzyme which acetylates newly synthesized histone H4 on 
lysines 5 and 12 prior to deposition on chromatin. Hat1 is required to preserve 
chromatin accessibility within a subset of LADs called Hat1-dependent 
accessibility domains (HADs). Here we profile a diverse set of histone 
modifications in Hat1 KO and WT immortalized mouse embryonic fibroblasts (iMEFs) 
and find that Hat1 regulates diverse aspects of the structure of HADs and 
non-HAD LADs (nhLADS). In HADs, these changes include the conversion of H3K9me2 
to H3K9me3. Analysis of H3K9-specific histone methyltransferases (HMTs) shows 
that Suv39h1 and Suv39h2 have distinct localization patterns, where only Suv39h2 
localizes to LADs. G9a only localizes to LADs in regions enriched for H3K9me2. 
We find that Hat1 loss results in an altered localization of these HMTs in both 
HADs and nh LADs. There is a decrease in the levels of G9a with a concomitant 
increase in Suv39h2. These results suggest Hat1 functions to restrain the 
formation of a more strongly heterochromatic state and highlight a role for Hat1 
as a regulator of heterochromatin structure.

(4)N.N. Burdenko National Scientific and Practical Center for Neurosurgery,

Vestibular schwannomas (VS) are benign neoplasms of the VIII cranial nerve; they 
account for 6-8% of all intracranial tumors and about 80% of tumors of the 
cerebellopontine angle. Cystic forms of VS may be particularly dangerous, as 
they demonstrate faster growth and worse postoperative outcomes. In this study, 
we performed proteomic analysis of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples obtained 
from patients with solid and cystic forms of VS, as well as cyst fluid from 
patients with cystic VS. CSF samples from patients with hemifacial spasm were 
used as controls. Mass spectrometric (MS) analysis resulted in identification of 
816 proteins in all samples and 111 proteins were upregulated in samples 
obtained from VS patients compared to the control group. The upregulated 
proteins belonged to the groups of components and regulators of the complement 
system, proteins associated with glucose and lipid metabolism. MS analysis of 
CSF obtained from patients with cystic and solid forms of VS resulted in 
identification of two proteomic clusters enriched in proteins associated with 
the development of the nervous system, cell adhesion, and myelination processes.

pathogenesis of cystic VS. SIGNIFICANCE: This study provides a comprehensive 
proteomic characterization of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and cyst fluid from 
patients with solid and cystic vestibular schwannomas (VS), offering valuable 
insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying these tumors. Our discovery

CSF and cyst fluid from VS patients, along with proteins involved in lipid 
metabolism, points to a potential mechanism of blood-brain barrier disruption 
and cyst formation, which is particularly relevant given the more aggressive 
clinical course of cystic VS. These findings not only contribute to 
understanding of VS pathogenesis but also suggest candidate protein targets for 
future diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic strategies, particularly for the 
more challenging cystic form of the disease.

Exploring heterogeneous treatment effects for GLP-1 receptor agonists in

Keele L(1), Bonvini M(2), Storås AM(3), Shirvaikar V(4), Li H(5), Jørgensen 
NB(3), Salsali A(3), Medici M(3), Mertens A(5), Kvist K(3).

Author information:
(1)University of Pennsylvania, United States.
(2)Rutgers University, United States.
(3)Novo Nordisk A/S, Denmark.
(4)Oxford University, United Kingdom.

Understanding treatment effect heterogeneity (TEH) is essential to improve care 
for patients living with chronic diseases like type 2 diabetes. Individual 
responses to treatment can vary substantially, and identifying the factors that 
drive TEH may enable increased personalization of treatment and follow-up. In 
this study, we conduct an exploratory analysis of TEH for glucagon-like 
peptide-1 receptor agonists used to treat type 2 diabetes. Endpoints are defined 
using hemoglobin A1c measurements, body mass index, and blood pressure. We use 
causal forests to conduct global tests for TEH, estimate variable importances to 
rank candidate effect modifiers, and estimate the magnitude of heterogeneity. 
Data from three clinical trials are analyzed: SUSTAIN 6 (subcutaneous 
semaglutide versus placebo, n=3297), PIONEER 6 (oral semaglutide versus placebo, 
n=3183), and LEADER (subcutaneous liraglutide versus placebo, n=9340), pooled to 
13,670 patients after exclusions. Baseline hemoglobin A1c ranks highest among 
candidate effect modifiers across methods, and kidney function ranks next in the 
relative risk causal forest; we discuss their clinical implications. The 
magnitude estimates, however, show that the variation these covariates jointly 
explain is small. As such, large covariate-driven heterogeneity can be ruled out 
in these trials, and the average treatment effect provides a reasonable summary 
for most patients.

Embryonic arrest poses a significant clinical challenge, yet the interplay 
between environmental toxicants and epigenetic modifiers remain poorly 
understood. This is the first study to systematically investigate whether 
genetic variants in N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation enzymes mediate the 
toxicity polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in early pregnancy loss. In a

gene-environment interaction underlying embryonic arrest and suggest that 
combining ALKBH5 rs4925144 genotyping with PAHs exposure assessment could serve 
as a valuable biomarker for early risk stratification, informing targeted

impairment. However, research on idiopathic developmental intellectual

in global ASDR, from 27.14 (95% UI: 26.9-27.4) per 100,000 in 2024 to 21.62 (95% 
UI: 11.5-31.8) per 100,000 in 2045. Since 1990, the global burden of IDII 
attributable to lead exposure has generally declined, especially in regions and 
sex groups with initially higher burdens. This pattern is compatible with the 
combined influence of period and cohort effects.

Tropospheric ozone (O3) is a major air pollutant that reduces crop productivity 
by altering photosynthesis, stomatal conductance, and carbon allocation. 
Process-based crop models are useful for assessing these impacts under changing 
environmental conditions. In this study, we developed and evaluated the CERES-O3 
model to simulate and quantify O3 impacts on wheat physiology and biomass 
production, using a flux-based approach. The model incorporates O3 effects on 
carboxylation and electron transport rates, as a function of the phytotoxic 
ozone dose (POD6). CERES-O3 was calibrated using data from a free-air fumigation 
experiment in Grignon, France, in 2009, with four O3 treatments, and evaluated 
using independent field experiments from 2003 and 2004 and FR-Gri ICOS ecosystem 
data from 2006, 2009, and 2012. CERES-O3 reproduced the O3-induced decline in 
photosynthesis and stomatal conductance. Agreement with ICOS GPP was good, with 
annual regression slopes ranging from 0.84 to 1.05 and R2 values from 0.79 to 
0.85. Simulated canopy stomatal O3 deposition accounted for 33-60% of measured 
total ecosystem deposition during cropping periods. Grain yield and above-ground 
biomass showed variable agreement, with particularly large yield underestimation 
in 2006 associated with strong simulated water stress. The fitted 
POD6-relative-yield relationship (RY = 1.003 - 0.041 POD6, R2 = 0.93) was 
consistent with established wheat flux-response relationships. Across ICOS 
years, the derived relationship indicated an estimated mean O3 -associated yield 
reduction of 6.5%. Overall, CERES-O3 provides an efficient framework for 
representing O3 impacts on wheat productivity, while highlighting remaining 
uncertainties in canopy scaling and the representation of crop responses to 
water limitation.

6:2 Fluorotelomer ethoxylates (6:2 FTEOs) are an emerging class of 
polyfluoroalkyl substances widely used in anti-fog products. Their increasing 
detection in environmental media and human serum has raised concerns regarding 
their potential toxicity and associated health risks. The association between 
6:2 FTEO exposure and intracranial aneurysm (IA) risk has not been evaluated in 
any epidemiological study to date. Here, we conducted a case-control study (137 
IA patients and 274 healthy controls), quantified seven serum 6:2 FTEO 
homologues, and performed metabolomic profiling of human serum samples. 6:2 
FTEO6, 6:2 FTEO9, and 6:2 FTEO11 dominated the 6:2 FTEO profile in human serum. 
Serum levels of 6:2 FTEO6, 6:2 FTEO8, and 6:2 FTEO9 showed significant (p < 
0.01) associations with IA risk, with adjusted odds ratios comparing the highest 
versus lowest quartile of 2.68 (95% CI: 1.61-3.70), 2.78 (1.78-3.81), and 1.98 
(1.10-3.58), respectively. Weighted quantile sum analysis indicated a 
significant effect of the combined 6:2 FTEO exposure on IA risk, driven mainly 
by 6:2 FTEO6. Random forest showed the strongest apparent discrimination, and 
its top-ranked metabolites were enriched in arachidonic acid metabolism and 
phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis. In exploratory mediation analyses, the 
observed indirect-effect estimates for 6:2 FTEO6 and 6:2 FTEO8 were 
statistically compatible with mediation through arachidonic acid metabolism and 
phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis. This study is the first to provide 
epidemiological evidence linking 6:2 FTEO exposure to increased IA risk, and 
provides hypothesis-generating evidence linking serum 6:2 FTEO concentrations, 
lipid metabolic perturbations, and IA status.

Author information:

Perfluorohexanesulfonic acid (PFHxS) refers to a persistent environmental 
pollutant associated with declining kidney function. Notably, the underlying 
mechanisms of PFHxS remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that chronic PFHxS 
exposure in mice induces renal fibrosis, as evidenced by collagen deposition, 
upregulated fibrotic markers, and impaired renal function. Mechanistically, we 
observed that PFHxS treatment reslulted in increased protein levels of PPARγ and

novel mechanism whereby PFHxS drives renal fibrosis through PPARγ and the 
subsequent NLRP1 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis, suggesting PPARγ and NLRP1 as 
promising therapeutic targets for PFHxS-associated kidney disease.

spinal stenosis (LSS) varies considerably and is likely multifactorial. It 
remains unclear how residual LBP differs by preoperative severity and which 
factors are independently associated with it.
PURPOSE: To examine how postoperative LBP improves across preoperative severity 
groups and to identify clinical and radiographic factors independently 
associated with residual LBP.
STUDY DESIGN/SETTING: Multicenter retrospective cohort study.
PATIENT SAMPLE: A total of 450 patients undergoing primary single-level 
posterior decompression for LSS at six institutions (2017-2023).
OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the 1-year postoperative numerical 
rating scale (NRS) score for LBP. Secondary outcomes were buttock and leg pain 
NRS, Oswestry Disability Index, EuroQol 5-Dimension, and postoperative 
satisfaction.
METHODS: Patients were stratified into three predefined preoperative LBP 
severity groups (Mild 0-3, Moderate 4-7, Severe 8-10). Inverse probability 
weighting (IPW) was applied for three-group comparisons. Unweighted 
multivariable linear regression for postoperative LBP NRS included preoperative 
LBP NRS together with patient, surgical, and radiographic factors as covariates. 
This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the 
public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The authors report no 
study-specific conflicts of interest.
RESULTS: The IPW-adjusted Severe group showed the largest LBP NRS improvement 
(4.5 points) but the highest residual LBP NRS (4.1). Dissatisfaction did not 
differ across groups (p=.244). Factors independently associated with residual 
LBP were preoperative LBP NRS (B=0.381, p<.001), pelvic incidence-lumbar 
lordosis (PI-LL) >20° (B=0.681, p=.024), and American Society of

CONCLUSIONS: Greater preoperative LBP severity was associated with both larger

Patients With Lumbar Spinal Stenosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Study.

BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Spinal epidural lipomatosis (SEL) is often regarded as a 
local consequence of obesity, yet its relationship with systemic lipid 
metabolism and symptom severity in lumbar spinal stenosis remains unclear. 
Apolipoprotein B (ApoB) is central to atherogenic lipid transport and ectopic 
fat deposition. Examining the association between systemic lipid metabolic 
abnormalities, including elevated ApoB levels, and epidural fat accumulation may 
provide insights into the metabolic pathogenesis and clinical relevance of SEL.
PURPOSE: To determine whether SEL is associated with systemic lipid metabolic 
abnormalities and greater preoperative symptom burden in patients undergoing 
surgery for lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS).
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study.
PATIENT SAMPLE: A consecutive series of 1,145 patients who underwent posterior 
decompression for symptomatic LSS between December 2023 and December 2025. After 
1:1 propensity score matching, 90 patients with SEL were compared with 90 
patients without SEL.
OUTCOME MEASURES: Serum lipid and other biochemical markers, epidural fat/spinal 
canal (EF/SpC) index on lumbar magnetic resonance imaging, Oswestry Disability 
Index (ODI), and visual analog scale (VAS) scores for leg and back pain.
METHODS: SEL was diagnosed and graded on preoperative lumbar MRI according to 
the Borré classification, using the epidural fat/spinal canal index. Propensity 
score matching was performed for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), smoking 
history, drinking history, hypertension, and diabetes. Biochemical variables and 
preoperative clinical scores were compared between matched SEL and non-SEL 
patients. Conditional logistic regression was used to identify factors 
associated with SEL. BMI-adjusted partial Spearman correlation analyses were 
performed to evaluate associations between the EF/SpC index and biochemical 
markers. Regression-based trend analyses were conducted to assess changes in 
lipid-related markers across increasing SEL severity grades.
RESULTS: Among 1,145 patients with LSS, 105 (9.2%) met the diagnostic criteria 
for SEL. After matching, 90 patients with SEL were compared with 90 non-SEL 
controls. The SEL group had higher apolipoprotein B (ApoB) levels than controls, 
as well as higher low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and total 
cholesterol. ApoB remained independently associated with SEL in conditional 
logistic regression (odds ratio per 0.1 g/L, 1.141; 95% confidence interval, 
1.019-1.277; P=0.022). Within the SEL group, the EF/SpC index correlated 
positively with triglycerides (ρ=0.43, q<0.001) and ApoB (ρ=0.40, q=0.002), 
while atherogenic lipid markers increased progressively with SEL severity. 
Patients with SEL also showed higher Oswestry Disability Index and leg-pain 
visual analog scale scores, whereas back-pain scores were similar between 
groups.
CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing surgery for LSS, SEL was associated with a 
more atherogenic lipid profile after matching for BMI and other major baseline 
characteristics, as well as greater preoperative disability and leg pain. The 
association of ApoB with SEL, together with the graded relationships of ApoB and 
triglycerides with epidural fat burden, suggests that SEL may reflect systemic 
lipid metabolic dysfunction rather than local epidural fat deposition alone.

Platinum-based chemotherapeutics remain central in oncology but are limited by 
systemic toxicity and poor tumor selectivity. Here, we investigate 
hydroxyapatite nanoparticles (HA NPs) as carriers for Pt(II) complexes, and 
compare the activity of free and NP-conjugated formulations across 2D cultures, 
static 3D tumor models, and flow-conditioned 3D systems using identical 
formulations, doses, and biological endpoints. Static 3D models impose 
diffusion-driven constraints that limit NP penetration, promote peripheral 
accumulation, and attenuate the apparent efficacy of NP-conjugated formulations. 
In contrast, quantitative spatial fluorescence profiling show that dynamic flow 
conditions partially alleviate these limitations, enhancing distal NP 
distribution and therapeutic activity. Notably, these transport-dependent 
effects influence the relative performance of free and nano-formulated drugs 
across models. Overall, our findings demonstrate that transport limitations in 
static systems can distort nanomedicine evaluation, highlighting the importance 
of incorporating flow-controlled conditions in preclinical screening.

ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Yupingfeng granules (YPF), derived from the 
classic traditional Chinese medicine prescription Yupingfeng powder, have been 
recommended in clinical practice guidelines for the management of allergic 
rhinitis (AR), and their clinical efficacy is widely recognized. However, the 
underlying pharmacological mechanisms have not been thoroughly investigated.
AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate whether YPF protects the nasal 
epithelial barrier and alleviates AR by modulating the gut microbiota and 
pathways related to its metabolites.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: An OVA-induced AR mouse model was established and 
phenotypically evaluated. The dependence of YPF efficacy on gut microbiota was 
assessed by 16S rRNA sequencing, antibiotic depletion, and fecal microbiota 
transplantation. 1H-NMR metabolomics was used to identify key metabolites, 
followed by exogenous supplementation for validation. Nasal mucosal 
transcriptome sequencing was performed to explore downstream pathways, and 
functional validation was conducted in OVA-induced HNEpCs through metabolite 
intervention, YPF co-treatment, mTOR knockdown, and MHY1485 treatment.
RESULTS: YPF dose-dependently reduced nasal rubbing and sneezing, attenuated 
IgE-mediated type 2 inflammation, and ameliorated nasal epithelial barrier 
injury in OVA-induced AR mice. YPF remodeled the gut microbiota and increased 
microbial diversity. Gut microbiota depletion attenuated the protective effects 
of YPF, whereas FMT from YPF donors reproduced them. Metabolomic analysis 
identified succinate as a key YPF-responsive metabolite, and exogenous succinate 
aggravated nasal epithelial barrier injury. Transcriptomic analysis suggested 
that succinate-induced nasal mucosal injury may involve mTOR signaling 
activation. In vitro, succinate aggravated OVA-induced barrier injury in HNEpCs, 
with disrupted Occludin distribution and enhanced mTOR/S6K phosphorylation, 
whereas YPF co-treatment reversed these changes. mTOR knockdown mimicked the 
protective effects of YPF, whereas MHY1485 attenuated them.
CONCLUSION: YPF alleviates OVA-induced AR by remodeling the gut microbiota, 
reducing succinate accumulation, and suppressing mTOR/S6K signaling to preserve 
nasal epithelial barrier integrity.

ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Abrus cantoniensis (AC) is a traditional Chinese 
medicinal herb used for hepatitis, with demonstrated lipid-regulating activity. 
However, as a multi-component herbal system, the specific bioactive monomers and 
their direct protein targets remain to be elucidated.
AIM OF THE STUDY: This study integrates target fishing with proteomics to 
capture hepatic protein targets of AC and elucidate its lipid-regulating 
mechanisms.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Abrine, a pharmacopoeial marker compound employed as a 
probe, was used to synthesize abrine-functionalized magnetic beads 
(Fe3O4-SH-BP-abrine, FSBA) via photo-crosslinking for target capture from mouse 
liver lysates. Proteins were identified by liquid chromatography-tandem mass 
spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Bioinformatic analyses, including Gene Ontology (GO) 
and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), were conducted. Molecular 
docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), 
real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), immunohistochemistry 
(IHC), and Western blotting (WB) were employed for validation.
RESULTS: AC ameliorated hepatic steatosis in HFD-induced dyslipidemic mice. KEGG 
enrichment identified the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) as the top-ranked 
pathway, consistent with its central role in NADPH-dependent lipid biosynthesis. 
Molecular docking and MD simulations predicted stable interactions between 
abrine and PPP enzymes. SPR verified a direct interaction between abrine and 
G6PD. RT-qPCR demonstrated downregulation of G6pd, Tkt, Taldo1, H6pd, and Aldoa 
at the mRNA level. IHC and WB consistently showed reduced protein expression of 
G6PD, PGD, and TKT after AC treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: Target fishing combined with proteomics uncovered AC's 
anti-dyslipidemic mechanism via the PPP. The identified PPP-related targets 
provide mechanistic insight into AC's lipid-regulating activity.

ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Vitiligo is an acquired depigmenting disorder 
characterized by CD8+ T cell-mediated melanocyte destruction. While JAK

effects, high costs, and pediatric contraindications. Carum carvi L. (CCL), an 
esteemed medicinal plant in traditional Uyghur and Tibetan medicine, is 
frequently prescribed to treat refractory skin diseases, notably vitiligo.
AIM OF THE STUDY: We aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of CCL against 
vitiligo, elucidate its underlying pharmacological mechanisms, and identify its 
potential active monomer.
METHODS AND MATERIALS: A monobenzone-induced vitiligo mouse model was utilized 
to assess macroscopic, histological, and molecular recovery following oral

RESULTS: In vivo, both the CCL and Rob restored repigmentation, restoring 
melanin deposition and functional follicular melanocytes. In vitro and in vivo

localized inflammation, characterized by decreased macrophage infiltration and a 
phenotypic shift toward pro-repair (CD206+) macrophages, and restricted CD8+ T

CONCLUSIONS: CCL and its active monomer Rob effectively mitigates 
immune-mediated melanocyte destruction and promotes repigmentation. Rob drives 
targeted therapeutic intervention by suppressing the STAT1-macrophage-CD8+ T 
cell inflammatory axis. These findings suggest CCL as a promising, 
multi-targeted natural therapy for vitiligo.

Radiolabelled cyclodextrins targeting prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) seem promising 
candidates for positron emission tomography (PET)-based molecular imaging of 
cervical cancer. Here, we evaluated the performance of gallium-68-labelled 
2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HPβCD) and randomly methylated β-cyclodextrin 
(RAMEB) for the in vivo PET detection of cervical cancer. P-glycoprotein 
positive (Pgp+) KB-V-1 and P-glycoprotein negative (Pgp-) KB-3-1 cervical 
carcinoma xenografts of varying sizes (small-, medium-, large-sized) were 
established and subjected to [68Ga]Ga-NODAGA-HPβCD and [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA-RAMEB PET 
imaging followed by ex vivo biodistribution and immunohistochemical (IHC) 
analysis of PGE2 and Pgp expression. In line with the IHC results, PET data 
revealed the capability of both radiotracers to reliably detect each tumor types 
independent of tumor size. Nevertheless, the modest increase in uptake observed 
with increasing size may indicate enhanced tumor aggressiveness and angiogenic 
activity. Comparable radiotracer accumulation in MDR-positive and MDR-negative 
tumors suggests that HPβCD and RAMEB derivatives are unlikely to serve as 
substrates of Pgp enabling tumor detection across different tumor types. 
Collectively, our findings demonstrate that radiolabelled cyclodextrins are 
promising PET tracers for the in vivo detection of cervical cancer, irrespective 
of tumor size and Pgp expression.

BACKGROUND: Family caregivers may experience prolonged grief disorder (PGD) and 
depressive symptoms after a relative's death.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate PGD prevalence and identify associated factors among 
family caregivers of patients who died in an oncology palliative care unit.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 80 family caregivers interviewed at 
least six months after the patient's death. Assessments included 
sociodemographic and perceived support questionnaires, the PG-13 instrument, and 
the Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II). Adjusted associations with PGD were 
estimated using hierarchical binary logistic regression.
RESULTS: PGD prevalence was 25.0% (20/80; 95% CI 16.0-35.9), and

caregivers. In the final adjusted model, higher odds of PGD were associated with

moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms (OR = 78.77, 95% CI 7.63-812.79; p < 
0.001). Lower odds were associated with routine physical activity (OR = 0.07, 
95% CI 0.01-0.84; p = 0.036) and perceived bereavement support (OR = 0.13, 95% 
CI 0.02-0.76; p = 0.024).
CONCLUSION: PGD affected one quarter of caregivers and was strongly associated 
with depressive symptom severity. Routine physical activity and perceived 
bereavement support were associated with lower adjusted odds of PGD. The 
cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

Background The posterolateral (PL) column is often the most difficult one to 
access and manage in tibial plateau fractures. Although multiple approaches have 
been described, many provide limited flexibility to address diverse fracture 
patterns. The Versatile Extended Anterolateral (EAL) Approach with four 
progressive windows has been previously introduced within the Main Deformity 
Direction (MDD) framework. In this cadaveric study, we provide a detailed 
anatomical and technical description of this modified approach, characterized by 
an optimized skin incision and four stepwise deep windows for PL column 
management. The primary aim was to assess the technical feasibility of this 
approach. Potential reduction and fixation options associated with each window 
were also explored descriptively. Materials and methods Four fresh-frozen 
cadaveric specimens were used to evaluate surgical exposure and relationships 
with relevant anatomical structures. Based on the anatomical exposure achieved 
with each window, potential reduction and fixation strategies were explored 
descriptively. Representative clinical cases were included to illustrate 
fixation techniques. Results The skin incision allowed access to all windows, 
achieving safe progressive PL column exposure. The four windows (pre-fibular, 
supra-fibular, retro-fibular, trans-fibular) expanded reduction and fixation 
possibilities stepwise. The trans-fibular window enabled complete articular and 
metaphyseal exposure. The anterior tibial artery crossing, located at a mean of 
3.5 cm from the tip of the fibular head, represented the distal anatomical limit 
of posterior exposure. Conclusion The versatile EAL Approach is a feasible 
option for managing lateral and PL columns in tibial plateau fractures. Its 
progressive four-window strategy may allow tailored exposure and fixation 
according to fracture-specific requirements.

BACKGROUND:  Plate fixation is the current gold standard for displaced midshaft 
clavicle fractures, despite concerns regarding surgical morbidity and implant 
prominence. The purpose of this study was to compare the clinical, radiographic, 
and surgical outcomes of an intramedullary screw system versus conventional 
plate fixation.
METHODS:  A comparative cohort study was performed on 72 patients (36 treated 
with the Screw system and 36 with plate fixation). Surgical variables (time and 
blood loss), radiographic consolidation (at 4, 8, and 12 weeks), and functional 
outcomes (DASH and Constant-Murley scores) were analyzed. Statistical 
significance was set at p < .05.
RESULTS:  The Screw group demonstrated a significantly shorter operative time 
(27.69+/- 9.39 vs. 105.47 +/- 55.18 minutes; p<.001) and minimal blood loss

DualTrack group, with an earlier return to physical activity 
(6.64 vs. 21.69 weeks; p<.001) and superior Constant scores (98.64 vs. 94.81; p 
= .0006). Radiographically, the screw group showed significantly lower fracture 
line visibility at 8 and 12 weeks compared to the plate group (p<.05). 
Complication rates were lower for the screw group (8.3%) than for the plate 
group (25.0%), although this did not reach statistical significance (p=.11).
CONCLUSION:  The intramedullary system is a highly effective alternative for 
clavicle fractures, providing superior surgical efficiency, faster functional 
recovery, and improved biological healing compared to conventional plate 
fixation. It should be considered a primary treatment option, particularly for 
patients seeking a rapid return to activity and minimally invasive surgery.

Ribeiro MR(1), de Morais Lima G(1), Siena A(1), Leite JA(2), Alves VF(1), Araujo

Obesity is a major metabolic disorder linked to neuroinflammation and cognitive 
decline. Beyond hypothalamic alterations, emerging evidence indicates that 
extra-hypothalamic regions, including the cerebellum, are vulnerable to 
obesity-induced neurotoxicity. This study investigated whether high-fat diet 
(HFD)-induced obesity causes cerebellar oxidative stress, impairs Na+,K+-ATPase 
(NKA) activity, and triggers molecular features resembling brain aging in female 
Balb/C mice. Chronic 10-week HFD intake established a marked obese phenotype, 
characterized by increased adiposity, fasting hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, and 
elevated serum TNF-α. In the cerebellum, obesity induced a selective, 
expression-independent reduction in α2,3-NKA isoform activity, accompanied by a 
marked depletion of tissue cGMP levels. This functional impairment was driven by 
an oxidative microenvironment, evidenced by elevated H2O2 and TBARS levels and 
increased 4-HNE accumulation. Concomitantly, obese animals mounted an adaptive 
antioxidant response characterized by increased GST, GR, and GPx activities, 
reduced glutathione (GSH) consumption, and ERK1/2-mediated nuclear translocation 
of Nrf2, alongside structural membrane lipid remodeling (elevated cholesterol 
and reduced phospholipids). In summary, chronic obesity induces robust 
lipoxidative stress and suppresses cerebellar cGMP signaling and α2,3-NKA 
activity in female mice, recapitulating key molecular hallmarks of natural brain 
aging.

AMPK signaling in cancer: Molecular insights and therapeutic opportunities.

Jiang W(1), Yan P(1), Wang J(1), Xue X(2), Huang D(1), Chen L(1), Yang Y(3),

AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) is a highly conserved serine/threonine 
kinase regarded as an indispensable energy sensor during metabolic stress, 
coordinating diverse biological processes, including glycolysis, the 
tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, mitochondrial dynamics, and multiple 
stress-responsive signaling pathways. Growing evidence shows that dysregulated 
AMPK signaling plays closely linked roles in tumorigenesis. Depending on the 
context, AMPK signaling can suppress or promote tumor growth. Mechanistically, 
dysregulated AMPK kinase activity contributes to metabolic reprogramming, 
mitochondrial dysfunction, and epigenetic alterations, all recognized hallmarks 
of cancer. Consequently, targeting AMPK signaling has emerged as a promising 
strategy for cancer therapy. In this review, we summarize the molecular 
mechanisms regulating AMPK signaling, discuss its dual functions in tumor 
biology, highlight recent advances in AMPK-targeted therapeutic strategies, and 
address current challenges and future perspectives for the clinical translation 
of AMPK-targeted cancer therapy.

Cancer-associated adipocytes (CAAs) are increasingly recognized as active and 
heterogeneous components of the tumor microenvironment. Initially defined as 
tumor-adjacent adipocytes characterized by lipid depletion, reduced expression 
of mature adipocyte markers, and inflammatory activation, CAAs are now 
understood to encompass a spectrum of context-dependent states. These states are 
shaped by anatomical location, preexisting adipocyte properties, tumor-derived 
signals, and therapeutic exposure. Through metabolic exchange, paracrine 
signaling, direct cell contact, extracellular-vesicle communication, and matrix 
remodeling, CAAs influence tumor-cell plasticity, metastatic colonization, 
immune dysfunction, stromal organization, and treatment response. In turn, 
signals from tumor, immune, and stromal cells continuously reshape adipocyte 
identity and function, placing CAAs within reciprocal multicellular networks. 
This review examines the evolving criteria used to identify CAAs, their lineage 
origins and plasticity, their spatial organization, and their interactions with 
tumor, immune, and stromal compartments. The contribution of CAAs to therapeutic 
adaptation is also discussed, together with potential intervention points 
involving CAA-derived outputs and the metabolic dependencies induced in 
recipient cells. Finally, major methodological challenges are considered. 
Adipocyte-resolved profiling, lineage tracing, spatial multiomics, lipid flux 
analysis, and physiologically relevant models will be needed to distinguish 
transient remodeling from stable state transitions and to identify 
context-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities.

Tumor heterogeneity is a universal feature of cancer and may arise as early as 
precancer stages during lung adenocarcinoma evolution, yet the emergence of 
aggressive transcriptional programs remains incompletely understood. Here, we 
integrated spatial transcriptomics with single-cell RNA sequencing to 
characterize inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity across hyperplasia, adenoma, 
and invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC) in a genetically engineered mouse model 
(129S4/Sv KrasLSL-G12D/+). Disease progression was accompanied by coordinated 
remodeling of epithelial, stromal, and immune compartments, along with dynamic 
changes in proliferation, immune response, and metabolic pathways. Notably, 
lesions of the same histological stage exhibited substantial transcriptional 
heterogeneity. By quantifying dedifferentiation states, we identified a subset 
of adenomas that had already diverged toward highly proliferative and 
metabolically active programs despite lacking invasive features. These lesions 
were further marked by early chromosome 6 amplification, whose corresponding 
human ortholog signature recapitulated aggressive proliferation-associated 
programs in early-stage human lung adenocarcinoma. Spatial analyses further 
revealed pronounced intratumoral heterogeneity within IAC, with tumor core 
regions showing increased proliferation and metabolism but reduced immune 
signaling compared to peripheral regions. In addition, immune checkpoint gene 
expression in T cells was transiently elevated at the hyperplasia stage, 
suggesting early immune modulation prior to overt malignancy. Together, these 
findings indicate that aggressive transcriptional divergence can emerge early 
during lung adenocarcinoma evolution and that spatial organization critically 
shapes tumor and immune programs before and after invasion.

While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized treatment of the 
patients with aero-upper digestive squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs), including 
esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and lung squamous cell carcinoma 
(LUSC), only a subset of patients benefit from ICIs, therefore entailing 
exploration of the mechanisms to regulate treatment responsiveness. POLE, as a 
subunit of DNA polymerase ε, possesses 3'-5' proofreading activity, and its 
mutations have been associated with favourable response to ICIs in several solid 
tumors. However, post-translational modification (PTM) of POLE and its impact on 
the therapeutic efficacy of ICIs are unknown. Here, this study demonstrates that 
ubiquitin-like protein 3 (Ubl3), whose expression is markedly downregulated in 
SCCs, covalently binds to Pole, reduces nuclear Pole levels, triggers DNA 
damage, and activates cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Notably, Ubl3 modification 
of Pole significantly primes the local immune microenvironment to mitigate the 
growth of murine aero-upper digestive SCC cells and boost the efficacy of αPD-1 
treatment in vivo. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis further 
revealed that UBL3 expression is positively correlated with better clinical 
outcomes in a cohort of ESCC patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy 
combined with αPD-1. Together, our findings unravel UBL3 modification as a novel 
PTM mechanism governing subcellular location of POLE and its influence on 
immunotherapy responsiveness, thus making UBL3 modification as a promising 
immunomodulatory approach to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in patients with 
aero-upper digestive SCCs.

Gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEAC) remains a highly aggressive malignancy 
with limited effective targeted therapies. Cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (CDK9), a 
key regulator of transcriptional elongation, has been implicated in oncogenic 
processes across multiple cancer types; however, its functional role and 
therapeutic potential in GEAC remain poorly defined. In this study, we 
systematically investigated CDK9 expression, function, and therapeutic targeting 
in GEAC, with particular emphasis on its interaction with the YAP/TEAD signaling 
axis. Immunohistochemical analysis of primary GEAC tumors and patient-derived 
xenografts revealed elevated CDK9 expression, which correlated with poor patient 
survival. Mechanistic studies using immunofluorescence and 
co-immunoprecipitation demonstrated a reciprocal regulatory interaction between 
CDK9 and YAP1, promoting transcriptional programs associated with tumor 
progression and radiation resistance. We developed novel CDK9-targeting 
proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) and identified YX0597 as a potent CDK9 
degrader. YX0597 effectively suppressed RNAP II Ser2 phosphorylation (RNAP II 
P-S2) and downregulated oncogenic drivers, including MCL-1. Functionally, CDK9 
degradation markedly inhibited GEAC cell proliferation, invasion, and tumor 
sphere formation, with enhanced efficacy in radiation-resistant cells. 
Integrated RNA sequencing and ATAC sequencing revealed that CDK9 degradation 
increased chromatin accessibility, reactivated epigenetically silenced genes, 
and profoundly suppressed YAP/TEAD transcriptional activity. These coordinated 
transcriptional and epigenetic alterations disrupted oncogenic homeostasis, 
resulting in broad cytotoxicity. Importantly, co-targeting CDK9 and YAP/TEAD 
signaling produced strong synergistic antitumor effects in vitro and in vivo. 
Collectively, our findings identify CDK9 as a critical oncogenic driver in GEAC 
and highlight CDK9 degradation, particularly in combination with YAP/TEAD 
inhibition, as a promising therapeutic strategy for refractory GEAC.

The Merlin protein, encoded by the tumor suppressor gene Neurofibromatosis type 
II (NF2), serves as a linker between the actin cytoskeleton, the plasma membrane 
receptors, and other intracellular signaling molecules. While there is a basic 
understanding of how Merlin regulates oncogenic signaling pathways, current 
targeted therapies have yet to demonstrate consistent clinical efficacy. Using a 
library of protein kinase inhibitors, we found that NF2-null Schwann cells (SCs) 
were uniquely sensitive to prexasertib, a drug that targets the DNA damage 
response pathway kinases CHK1/2 (Checkpoint Kinase 1 and 2). NF2-null SC 
proliferation was also sensitive to small molecule inhibitors of CHK1/2 
downstream effectors. At baseline, NF2-null SCs have increased RAC1 activity, 
elevated levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and higher levels 
of DNA damage. Exposing NF2-null SCs to DNA damaging agents such as doxorubicin 
or carboplatin, alone or in combination with prexasertib, further decreased 
their proliferation. Consistent with this idea, suppressing RAC1 or NOX2 
activity with small molecule inhibitors, decreased ROS production and restored 
resistance to prexasertib in NF2-null hSCs, suggesting that active RAC1 and high 
ROS render NF2-null hSC uniquely vulnerable to DNA damage. Furthermore, 
restoring NF2 expression in NF2-null Schwann cells restored their resistance to 
prexasertib, reduced RAC1 activity, and lowered levels of ROS and DNA damage. 
The intrinsic elevation of RAC1, ROS, and DNA damage in NF2-null hSCs suggest 
that inhibiting DNA damage response pathways might be clinically useful in 
patients with NF2-null schwannomas.

Macrophages possess intrinsic tumor-homing and tissue-infiltrating abilities, 
performing various effector functions, including phagocytosis and antigen 
presentation. These properties make chimeric antigen receptor macrophages 
(CAR-M) a promising approach to overcoming major barriers in cellular therapy 
for solid tumors. This review systematically compares and critically evaluates 
key design variables that determine the therapeutic activity and clinical 
feasibility of CAR-M, including CAR architecture, macrophage source, 
gene-delivery method, and manufacturing strategy. We also discuss emerging 
engineering approaches tailored to macrophage biology, including 
macrophage-adapted intracellular signaling, regulation of phagocytic 
checkpoints, metabolic and phenotypic reprogramming, and combinations with 
immunomodulatory therapies. Their therapeutic potential and translational 
boundaries are assessed based on current preclinical evidence and early clinical 
findings. Notably, the major barriers to clinical translation are shifting from 
focusing solely on antitumor potency to addressing system-level challenges 
involving cell source and product consistency, in vivo expansion and 
persistence, phenotypic stability, off-target toxicity, and scalable 
manufacturing. Therefore, we propose that next-generation CAR-M development 
should move beyond conventional optimization of the CAR construct to 
multidimensional engineering centered on macrophage biology. Coordinated 
optimization of receptor signaling, antigen recognition, cell-state control, 
delivery, and safety mechanisms will be essential to balance efficacy, 
persistence, safety, and manufacturability. This review provides an integrated 
framework for the rational design and clinical evaluation of CAR-M and the 
development of next-generation CAR-M cellular therapy platforms.

Plasma cholesterol is correlated with worse outcomes in breast and ovarian 
cancer. Prior work indicates that myeloid immune cells are highly responsive to 
cholesterol metabolism. Interestingly, Liver Receptor Homolog-1 (LRH-1, or 
NR5A2), a key transcriptional regulator of cholesterol homeostasis is highly 
expressed in neutrophils and is associated with increased survival time. 
However, the roles of LRH-1 within neutrophils remain unclear. We therefore 
focused on how LRH-1 influences neutrophil behaviors relevant to cancer. Small 
molecule ligands for LRH-1 regulated neutrophil migration towards cancer cells. 
Phagocytosis was also regulated by LRH-1 ligands, the extent being dependent on 
type of bait (e. coli vs. cancer cells). In T cell co-cultures, neutrophils 
pretreated with an LRH-1 agonist promoted greater T cell expansion, particularly 
in CD4+ cells, while LRH-1 inhibition suppressed this response. NETosis is a 
known trigger of recurrence from dormancy and subsequent tumor growth. 
Importantly LRH-1 activation reduced NETosis, while treatment with an antagonist 
or inverse agonist enhanced NETosis, likely through altered reactive oxygen 
species. Treatment of mice with an inverse agonist of LRH-1 increased the growth 
of mammary tumors in a NET-dependent manner. Mice harboring dormant D2.0R 
mammary cancer lesions treated with an LRH-1 inverse agonist exhibited earlier 
tumor recurrence and enhanced metastatic progression. In contrast, treatment 
with BL001, a small chemical LRH-1 agonist, delayed recurrence in D2.0R-grafted 
mice. These findings reveal that LRH-1 is a novel regulator of neutrophil-driven 
immune responses within the tumor microenvironment. LRH-1 is thus a promising 
therapeutic target to suppress the progression of breast and ovarian cancer.

Advanced-stage cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) frequently develops resistance to 
chemotherapy, highlighting an urgent unmet need for novel therapeutic 
strategies. Here, we analyzed 16 pairs of CCA and adjacent non-tumor tissues, 
and demonstrated that dysregulation of the cell cycle machinery is a hallmark of 
CCA, closely associated with chemoresistance and poor prognosis. Targeting 
aberrant cell cycle regulation therefore represents a promising approach to 
improve current treatment outcomes. We identify the CDC7 inhibitor XL413 as an 
effective agent capable of re-sensitizing gemcitabine-resistant tumors across 
multiple preclinical models of CCA. Mechanistic analyses, including 
transcriptomic profiling, reveal that combination therapy activates 
senescence-associated pathways, with therapeutic efficacy is mediated via a 
ROS-DNA damage-senescence cascade. Notably, synergistic induction of cellular 
senescence is observed in CCA cells upon co-treatment with a CDC7 inhibitor and 
gemcitabine. Collectively, these findings provide robust preclinical evidence 
supporting the combination of gemcitabine and CDC7 inhibitors as a viable 
therapeutic strategy to enhance the clinical management of CCA.

Reversible wall motion abnormalities do not predict long-term mortality if 
coronary flow reserve is accounted for: A 15-year contrast stress-echo study.

Gaibazzi N(1), Niccoli G(2), Sartorio D(2), Tuttolomondo D(2).

Author information:
(1)Cardiology Department, Parma University Hospital, Parma, Italy. Electronic 
address: ngaibazzi@gmail.com.
(2)Cardiology Department, Parma University Hospital, Parma, Italy.

BACKGROUND: Stress echocardiography (SE) is widely used to detect myocardial 
ischaemia in the scenario of chronic coronary syndromes (CCS). Despite that, the 
prognostic value of SE has been rarely assessed. We aim to establish whether the 
presence of reversible wall motion abnormalities (RWMA), remains independently 
associated with long-term mortality when considering myocardial perfusion (MP) 
and Doppler coronary flow velocity reserve in the left anterior descending 
artery (CFVR-LAD).
METHOD: 1002 subjects who underwent Dipyridamole contrast SE, for suspected CCS, 
between 2007 and 2012 at the Parma University Hospital were enrolled. The 
endpoint is all-cause mortality. The probability of survival was calculated 
using the Kaplan-Meier method and event-rate curves were compared using the 
log-rank test.
RESULTS: There were 376 deaths (37.5%) during a median follow-up of 13.8 years. 
Mean age was 66 ± 11 years, females represented 38%, 32% had known CCS. SE 
results showed RWMA in 17.5%, reversible MP abnormalities in 26.2%, and reduced 
CFVR-LAD in 42% of the study population. Revascularization within 3 months of 
the SE was performed in 185 subjects (18.5%). In multivariate Cox proportional 
hazard analysis, among the SE variables, only CFVR-LAD<2 remained associated 
with mortality (HR 2.44, 95% CI 1.94-3.5, p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: In the setting of CCS patients, CFVR-LAD is the only SE variable 
maintaining independent association with long-term mortality.

Temporal trends and outcomes of intravascular imaging in chronic total occlusion 
interventions: insights from the PROGRESS-CTO registry.

Akyel A(1), Carvalho PEP(1), Vichos T(1), Tsourous M(1), Desai P(1), Gavlasova

BACKGROUND: In this study we investigated temporal trends, indications, practice 
variation, and outcomes associated with intravascular imaging (IVI) use in a 
large, multicenter chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary 
intervention (PCI) registry.
METHODS: We analyzed CTO PCIs performed at 76 US and international centers in 
2012-2026 in the PROGRESS-CTO registry. Patients were categorized according to 
IVI use. P value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Among 18,024 CTO PCIs, IVI was used in 10,569 procedures (58.6%). IVI 
use increased over time. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was the predominant 
modality, accounting for 98.1% of IVI-guided procedures. Following 1:1 
propensity score matching, technical (85.8% vs 78.8%; p < 0.001) and procedural 
success (83.6% vs 78.1%, p = 0.003) remained higher in the IVUS-to-cross group. 
Difference was also pronounced when IVUS was used to cross ambiguous proximal 
cap: technical success was 85.1% versus 75.9% (OR, 1.81; 95% CI, 1.49-2.21), and 
procedural success was 83.0% versus 75.1% (OR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.34-1.99). Centers 
contributing <100 cases had lower IVI use than centers contributing ≥100 cases 
(47.7% vs 58.7%; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: IVI use during CTO PCI continues to increase. Procedures in which 
IVUS was used to facilitate lesion crossing were associated with higher 
technical and procedural success rates and similar in-hospital MACE rates. The 
association with success was also pronounced when IVUS was used to resolve 
proximal cap ambiguity. IVI use varied significantly among participating 
centers, highlighting differences in practice patterns and adoption of IVI 
during CTO PCI.

Advanced right heart failure stage at first documentation of severe tricuspid 
regurgitation: beyond the late-referral paradigm.

Fiore G(1), Ingallina G(2), Ancona F(2), Stella S(2), Biondi F(2), Gaspardone 
C(2), Margonato D(2), Denti P(3), Maisano F(4), Agricola E(5).

Author information:
(1)Unit of Cardiovascular Imaging, IRCCS Ospedale San Raffaele, Milan, Italy. 
Electronic address: fiore.giorgio@hsr.it.
(2)Unit of Cardiovascular Imaging, IRCCS Ospedale San Raffaele, Milan, Italy.
(3)Department of Cardiac Surgery, IRCCS Ospedale San Raffaele, Milan, Italy.
(4)Department of Cardiac Surgery, IRCCS Ospedale San Raffaele, Milan, Italy; 
Vita-Salute San Raffaele University, Milan, Italy.
(5)Unit of Cardiovascular Imaging, IRCCS Ospedale San Raffaele, Milan, Italy;

BACKGROUND: Patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) frequently present 
with advanced right heart failure (RHF), commonly attributed to delayed referral 
for intervention. Whether this reflects delayed referral or the stage at which 
severe TR is first documented remains uncertain.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 625 consecutive patients with a first 
echocardiographic diagnosis of severe TR. RHF severity was classified using a 
validated hierarchical staging system (Stages 1-4). In a subgroup of 310 
patients with a previous echocardiogram documenting non-severe TR, RHF stage was 
retrospectively assessed before severe TR was first documented. Two-year 
all-cause mortality was evaluated.
RESULTS: At first documentation of severe TR, 66.4% of patients were classified 
as Stage 3 and 17.3% as Stage 4, whereas only 16.3% were in Stages 1-2. 
Functional TR accounted for 85% of cases. RHF stage was associated with 
progressively higher TRI-SCORE and two-year mortality. Among patients with prior 
non-severe TR, 78% were already in Stage 3-4 before severe TR was first 
documented, whereas only 7% had reached Stage 4.
CONCLUSIONS: Severe TR was predominantly diagnosed in patients with stage 3-4 
RHF. Higher RHF stages were already present in most patients before severe TR 
was first documented. These findings suggest that delayed referral alone may not 
fully explain the advanced clinical profile of severe TR and that eligibility 
for guideline-directed intervention frequently coincides with an already 
advanced stage of disease.

Late gadolinium enhancement dispersion mapping predicts major arrhythmic events 
in patients with prior myocardial infarction.

Licordari R(1), Todiere G(2), De Gori C(2), Barison A(2), Grigoratos C(2), 
Marcucci A(3), Alberti M(4), Fulceri L(3), Emdin M(2), De Caterina R(4), Di 
Bella G(5), Aquaro GD(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Clinical and Experimental Medicine, University of Messina, 
Italy.
(2)Fondazione Toscana G. Monasterio, Pisa, Italy.
(3)Department of Surgical, Medical and Molecular Pathology and of Critical Area, 
University of Pisa, Pisa, Italy.
(4)Department of Translational Research and of New Technology, University of 
Pisa, Pisa, Italy.
(5)Department of Clinical and Experimental Medicine, University of Messina, 
Italy. Electronic address: dibellag@unime.it.

BACKGROUND: Myocardial scar heterogeneity is a key determinant of ventricular 
arrhythmias after myocardial infarction (MI). Late gadolinium enhancement 
dispersion mapping (LGE-DM) quantifies structural complexity, but its prognostic 
role in ischemic cardiomyopathy remains unevaluated.
METHODS: We retrospectively included 364 consecutive patients with prior MI 
(>90 days). For each LGE image, a parametric map was generated and each enhanced 
pixel scored (0-8) based on surrounding signal distribution; the global 
dispersion score (GDS) was calculated as the mean pixel score, quantifying 
pixel-to-pixel heterogeneity. The endpoint was a composite of sudden cardiac 
death (SCD), resuscitated cardiac arrest, sustained ventricular tachycardia, or 
appropriate ICD therapies.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 4 years, 42 arrhythmic events occurred. 
Patients with events showed significantly higher GDS than event-free patients 
(0.53 vs 0.32, P < 0.0001). Multivariable Cox regression confirmed GDS as an 
independent predictor (HR 1.16 per 0.1-unit increase, 95% CI 1.03-1.29), while 
LVEF and LGE extent were not, and GDS remained independently associated with 
events when LGE extent was forced into the model (HR 1.12 per 0.1-unit increase, 
P = 0.005). In patients with LVEF >35%, GDS was the only independent predictor 
across all multivariable models. Harrell's C-index was 0.682, with an optimism 
of 0.012 on bootstrap resampling. ROC analysis identified GDS >0.5 as a 
provisional cut-off derived within the same cohort (apparent AUC 0.74 overall; 
0.81 in the LVEF >35% subgroup). Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed worse prognosis 
in patients with GDS >0.5 (overall: p = 0.0002; LVEF >35%: p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: LGE dispersion independently predicts malignant ventricular 
arrhythmias post-MI, outperforming LGE extent and LVEF. GDS may improve SCD risk 
stratification particularly in patients with LVEF >35%, a population not 
adequately targeted by current LVEF-based criteria. External validation is 
required before the proposed threshold can be used clinically.

Relationship between coronary microvascular and epicardial spasm at 
intracoronary acetylcholine testing in patients with ANOCA.

Fischer A(1), Saccardi L(1), Hubert A(1), Martinez-Pereyra V(1), Bekeredjian 
R(1), Seitz A(1), Ong P(2).

Author information:
(1)Robert-Bosch-Krankenhaus, Department of Cardiology and Angiology, Stuttgart, 
Germany.
(2)Robert-Bosch-Krankenhaus, Department of Cardiology and Angiology, Stuttgart, 
Germany. Electronic address: Peter.Ong@rbk.de.

BACKGROUND: Patients with Angina and unobstructed coronary arteries (ANOCA) 
frequently suffer from coronary spasm. Intracoronary provocative testing may 
reveal microvascular and/or epicardial spasm. However, the relationship of these 
two spasm types has not been investigated systematically.
METHODS: We enrolled 142 ANOCA patients (mean age 63 years, 44% female) in whom 
intracoronary acetylcholine testing demonstrated epicardial spasm at the highest 
acetylcholine dose (i. e. 200 μg) in the left coronary artery according to the 
COVADIS criteria. In all patients, demographic data, cardiovascular risk factors 
and procedural data were recorded. The latter included symptoms and/or ischemic 
ECG shifts during lower acetylcholine doses. This enabled diagnosis of 
microvascular spasm before documentation of epicardial spasm.
RESULTS: 49 out of 142 patients (35%) had microvascular spasm before 
documentation of epicardial spasm. Thirty-one patients (22%) had an uneventful 
test and in 62 (43%) the acetylcholine test was inconclusive. Statistical 
analysis revealed no significant differences between patients with and without 
microvascular spasm regarding cardiovascular risk factors. However, patients 
with microvascular spasm were significantly more often female (55% vs. 29%, 
p = 0.037). Multivariable analysis revealed female sex as significant predictor 
for the occurrence of microvascular spasm (OR 3.0, 95% CI 1.15-7.80, p = 0.021).
CONCLUSION: In patients with epicardial spasm microvascular spasm at lower 
acetylcholine doses can be diagnosed in 35% of ANOCA patients. Independent of 
cardiovascular risk factors women are affected by this scenario three times more 
often than men. Our results underline the importance of the coronary 
microcirculation and sex-specific differences in the pathophysiology of coronary 
spasm.

Pressure-volume loop reconstruction of Impella support in severe aortic 
regurgitation: explaining a hemodynamic paradox.

Takagi H(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Cardiovascular Surgery, Shizuoka Medical Center, Shizuoka, 
Japan. Electronic address: kfgth973@ybb.ne.jp.

BACKGROUND: Severe aortic regurgitation (AR) causes left ventricular (LV) volume 
overload, while transvalvular Impella support may permit regurgitant 
recirculation. We constructed schematic pressure-volume (PV) loops to illustrate 
the interaction between ventricular unloading and systemic perfusion in severe 
AR.
METHODS: Conceptual LV PV loops were constructed from established principles of 
ventricular mechanics to depict progressive AR, cardiogenic shock (CS), and 
alternative hypothetical responses to Impella support. No patient-specific 
measurements or numerical simulation were used.
RESULTS: Increasing AR was depicted by rightward PV-loop displacement and 
greater LV volume excursion without quantifying effective forward stroke volume. 
The hypothetical transition to CS showed lower LV pressure and greater 
end-systolic volume. During Impella support, a leftward loop shift and smaller 
enclosed area were compatible with unloading; regurgitant recirculation could 
offset its benefit and permit recurrent LV distension. Pump flow, regurgitant 
flow, and effective systemic output could not be derived from the loops.
CONCLUSIONS: This qualitative framework illustrates a plausible hemodynamic 
paradox: LV unloading during Impella support may coexist with limited 
improvement in net systemic perfusion in severe AR. It does not establish the 
magnitude or temporal sequence of these responses.

Wang T(1), Li J(2), Liang Y(3), Zhang L(4), Wang J(5), Li Y(6), Zeng H(7), Dai

BACKGROUND: QY201 is a novel oral Janus kinase 1 and tyrosine kinase 2 
inhibitor.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of multiple QY201 doses in 
moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD), and to inform dose selection for 
phase 3 studies.
METHODS: In this phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 
200 adults with moderate-to-severe AD were randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive QY201 
(5 mg, 10 mg, or 20 mg twice daily [BID]) or placebo for 12 weeks. The primary 
endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving ≥75% improvement in Eczema 
Area and Severity Index (EASI-75) at week 12.
RESULTS: EASI-75 response rates at week 12 were 72.9%, 84.7% and 81.4% in the 5 
mg BID, 10 mg BID, and 20 mg BID groups, respectively, compared with 18.5% in 
the placebo group (all P<0.0001). Investigator's Global Assessment response 
rates were 44.7% (P=0.0011), 64.3% (P<0.0001), and 71.3% (P<0.0001), 
respectively, versus 12.4% with placebo. Treatment-emergent adverse events 
occurred in 74.0%, 75.5%, and 90.4% of patients receiving QY201, compared to 
69.4% with placebo; most were mild or moderate.
LIMITATIONS: Short follow-up and single-country population.
CONCLUSION: The phase 2 findings support further evaluation of QY201 at doses of 
10 mg BID and 20 mg BID in confirmatory phase 3 trials.

Parkinson's Disease-Associated Genetic Alterations Disrupt Behavior and Diurnal 
Activity in Drosophila melanogaster.

Witte C(1), Mitra S(2), Lackey K(1), Krishnan N(3), Chaudhuri A(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biological Sciences, University of Alabama, Tuscaloosa, AL 
35487, USA.
(2)Birla Institute of Technology & Science, Pilani, Telangana 500078, India.
(3)Department of Agricultural Science and Plant Protection, Mississippi State 
University, Mississippi State, MS 39762, USA; Department of Biochemistry, 
Nutrition and Health Promotion, Mississippi State University, Mississippi State, 
MS 39762, USA.
(4)Department of Biological Sciences, University of Alabama, Tuscaloosa, AL 
35487, USA; Department of Natural Sciences, Stillman College, Tuscaloosa, 
Alabama, USA. Electronic address: achaudhuri@stillman.edu.

Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder 
characterized by the loss of dopaminergic neurons, resulting in motor 
dysfunction and a variety of non-motor symptoms. Multiple genetic alterations, 
including increased α-synuclein expression and loss-of-function of parkin, 
PINK1, and DJ-1, have been associated with PD pathogenesis; however, their 
effects on stress tolerance, motor behavior, and daily activity remain 
incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of PD-associated 
genetic alterations on stress tolerance, motor behavior, and diurnal activity in 
Drosophila melanogaster. Four Drosophila lines representing PARK1 
(SNCA/α-synuclein; elav-GAL4>UAS-hSNCA), PARK2 (PRKN/parkin; parkinⁿᵘˡˡ), PARK6 
(PINK1; PINK1ᴮ⁹), and PARK7 (DJ-1; DJ-1βΔ⁹³) were evaluated using assays of 
starvation survival, larval vertical migration, adult negative geotaxis, jumping 
activity, and locomotor activity under a 12h light:12h dark cycle. Starvation 
stress tolerance differed among PD-associated fly lines in males and females 
separately. All PD-associated fly lines exhibited impaired larval vertical 
migration, whereas adult negative geotaxis and jumping behavior showed 
genotype-dependent patterns, with no significant genotype × sex interaction. 
Activity monitoring revealed disruptions in daily locomotor activity, with 
visually observed alterations in morning and evening activity patterns. Daily 
activity patterns also showed clear sex-specific differences. These findings 
show that PD-associated genetic alterations affect stress tolerance, locomotor 
behavior, and diurnal activity in D. melanogaster, with the nature of these 
effects varying by genotype, sex, and behavioral phenotype. The findings further 
highlight the importance of considering sex as a biological variable in PD 
research. Further studies are needed to define the molecular mechanisms 
underlying these behavioral and diurnal alterations.
