BACKGROUND: Anterior shoulder dislocation (ASD) is the most common joint 
dislocation in young patients with recurrence rates of nearly 90%. Multiple 
dislocations can cause progressive structural damage and bone loss, increasing 
the risk of instability. This study compares recurrence and postoperative 
complications following ASD between patients with a primary versus recurrent 
ASD. We hypothesized that surgical stabilization following recurrent ASD would 
be associated with an increased risk of subsequent instability and a higher 
complication burden.
METHODS: A retrospective query was conducted using the TriNetX database (January 
1, 2015 to January 1, 2025) in accordance with STROBE/RECORD guidelines. 
Patients aged 18 years or older undergoing surgical repair for primary or 
recurrent ASD were identified. Propensity score matching was applied in a 1:1 
ratio and estimated using logistic regression. Postoperative outcomes were 
evaluated at 3 and 6 months with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate 
correction (q=0.05) applied to cohort comparisons. Multivariate logistic 
regression analysis was performed to assess independent risk factors.
RESULTS: Pre-match cohorts included 2,312 patients who underwent surgical repair 
for primary ASD compared to 7,594 patients in the recurrent ASD cohort; 
propensity score matching yielded 2,302 patients per group (mean age: 29.7±14.5 
years vs. 28.8±13.6 years, respectively). Following Benjamini-Hochberg false 
discovery rate correction, recurrent ASD patients experienced significantly 
higher rates of subsequent dislocation (3-month: 21.4% vs. 1.3%, RD=-20.1%; 
6-month: 23.5% vs. 1.7%, RD=-21.8%; both p<0.0001) and shoulder instability 
(3-month: 44.0% vs. 21.8%, RD=-22.2%; 6-month: 47.8% vs. 24.0%, RD=-23.8%; both 
p<0.0001). At 6-months, reoperation rates differed between cohorts on unadjusted 
analysis (2.0% vs. 1.1%, RD=-0.9%, p=0.0159), but the difference did not retain 
significance following Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (q=0.089). No 
significant differences were observed in shoulder stiffness, rotator cuff tears, 
shoulder impingement, or shoulder pain. Logistic regression analysis 
demonstrated that elevated BMI significantly increased odds of postoperative 
shoulder instability at 3 and 6 months (p=0.022-0.038) in both the primary and 
recurrent ASD groups. Epilepsy or recurrent seizures were significantly 
associated with postoperative instability across both time points in primary and 
recurrent repair groups (p<0.01).
CONCLUSION: Patients undergoing surgical repair for recurrent ASD experienced 
significantly higher short-term rates of recurrent instability compared to those 
treated for primary ASD. Elevated BMI and seizure disorders were identified as 
independent risk factors associated with postoperative instability. These 
findings should be interpreted as associative and hypothesis-generating. 
Prospective cohort studies incorporating granular imaging and procedure-level 
data are needed to validate these relationships and evaluate whether surgical 
selection modifies recurrence risk in high-risk patients.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, Retrospective Cohort Comparison using Large 
Database, Prognosis Study.

Variation of the definition of "survival" in reverse total shoulder 
arthroplasty: a systematic review.

Fox HM(1), Glenn ER(2), Padley JH(1), Lee B(2), White J(3), Srikumaran U(1), 
McFarland EG(4).

Author information:
(1)Dept. of Orthopaedic Surgery, The Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, 
USA.
(2)School of Medicine, The Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA.
(3)Welch Medical Library, The Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA.
(4)Dept. of Orthopaedic Surgery, The Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, 
USA. Electronic address: emcfarl1@jhmi.edu.

BACKGROUND: Although studies have been published on long-term outcomes of 
reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA), various definitions of "survival" 
and "revision" are used, making comparisons of the findings difficult. 
Arthroplasty registries also vary in their definitions of these terms. The goal 
of this systematic review was to determine how variation in definitions of these 
terms affects the reported long-term results of rTSA.
METHODS: We systematically searched the PubMed and Embase databases to identify 
studies reporting ≥10-year follow-up after primary rTSA. Nine studies (493 
shoulders) met our selection criteria. The included clinical studies were 
predominantly Level IV retrospective cohort studies. Definitions of survival and 
revision were extracted from these studies. Previously published lists of 
national or regional arthroplasty registries were used to identify publicly 
available registry reports. When available, 10-year survival data for primary 
rTSA were extracted from these reports. Of the 11 registries reviewed, 3 had 
substantive 10-year survival data and definitions and were included in our 
analysis. Using standardized definitions of survival, we calculated pooled 
10-year survival rates from the included studies and compared them with those 
from the arthroplasty registries. We defined entire-construct survival as the 
percentage of shoulders in which neither the metal components (humeral stem 
and/or glenoid baseplate) nor the polyethylene component had been revised. 
Similarly, we assessed 10-year survival of the metal components (no revision of 
metal components, but shoulder underwent polyethylene exchange/revision). Using 
these definitions, we recalculated survival rates for both entire-construct 
survival and metal component survival.
RESULTS: Definitions of survival varied among clinical studies. The weighted 
average 10-year survival rates were 82.7% for the entire rTSA construct 
(polyethylene, humerus, and glenoid components), and 89.5% for the metal 
components only. The rate of isolated polyethylene liner exchange was 7%. 
Registry-reported 10-year survival rates for the entire construct were 
consistently higher (approximately 94%-95%) than the weighted averages from the 
included clinical studies.
CONCLUSION: With standardized definitions, 10-year revision-free survival was 
82.7% for the entire construct and 89.5% when isolated polyethylene liner 
exchange was excluded. Considerable inconsistency in the definition of long-term 
survival across clinical series and arthroplasty registries limits direct 
comparison and supports standardized reporting of survival endpoints.

Dhunna DP(1), Cook A(1), Nguyen KT(2), Wu KA(3), Mai E(3), Warburton C(3), Oza

Author information:
(1)Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine, Boston University, Boston, MA.
(2)Tulane University School of Medicine, New Orleans, LA.
(3)Department of Orthopaedics, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New

(4)American University of the Caribbean School of Medicine, Cupecoy, Sint

(5)Philadelphia College of Osteopathic Medicine, Philadelphia, PA.

BACKGROUND: Shoulder instability is a common and clinically significant 
condition, particularly among young and active populations, and represents a 
frequent indication for both nonoperative and operative intervention. As the 
volume of clinical research and comparative surgical literature continues to 
grow, systematic reviews and meta-analyses are increasingly relied upon to guide 
treatment selection, patient counseling, and return-to-sport expectations. In 
this setting, biased reporting within evidence syntheses may meaningfully 
influence clinical decision-making. The purpose of this study was to evaluate 
the prevalence and types of reporting bias (spin) in systematic reviews and 
meta-analyses addressing shoulder instability and to determine whether spin is 
associated with methodological rigor.
METHODS: This systematic review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO 
(CRD420261399489). Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were 
searched for systematic reviews and meta-analyses focused on shoulder 
instability in December 2025. Eligible studies were evaluated for 15 predefined 
types of spin using the Yavchitz taxonomy, and methodological quality was 
assessed using AMSTAR 2. Study characteristics included PRISMA adherence, 
protocol preregistration, level of evidence, publication year, and journal 
impact factor. Associations between spin and study characteristics were analyzed 
using Chi-square, Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, and Spearman rank correlation 
tests.
RESULTS: A total of 126 studies were included. Spin was identified in 86 studies 
(68.3%), most commonly involving misleading reporting (55.6%) and misleading 
interpretation (38.1%). Most studies were rated as critically low confidence on 
AMSTAR 2 (73.0%). The presence and burden of spin were significantly associated 
with lower numerical AMSTAR 2 scores (p < 0.01). Level of evidence was 
associated with spin burden but not spin presence. Journal impact factor and 
year of publication were not associated with spin.
CONCLUSION: Reporting spin is highly prevalent in systematic reviews and 
meta-analyses addressing shoulder instability and is strongly associated with 
lower methodological quality. Given the high prevalence of shoulder instability 
and the reliance on evidence syntheses to inform treatment decisions, patient 
counseling, and expectations regarding recurrence and return to sport, biased 
reporting may contribute to misinterpretation of treatment effectiveness and 
inappropriate clinical conclusions. These findings underscore the need for 
greater methodological rigor, transparency, and critical appraisal of evidence 
syntheses to support informed, evidence-based care for patients with shoulder 
instability.

HIF-1α-Driven Protein Lactylation Promotes Ferroptosis and Lipid Peroxidation in 
Ulcerative Colitis and Is Suppressed by Quercetin.

Yan C(1), Wang W(1), Ao J(1), Wang Z(1), Zhou S(1), Li X(1), Jiang H(1), Fang 
G(1), Mo S(1), Yang J(1), Luo L(2).

Author information:
(1)School of Ocean and Tropical Medicine. Guangdong Medical University, 
Zhanjiang, Guangdong, 524023, China.
(2)School of Ocean and Tropical Medicine. Guangdong Medical University, 
Zhanjiang, Guangdong, 524023, China. Electronic address: 
luolianxiang321@gdmu.edu.cn.

Ulcerative colitis (UC) is associated with a hypoxic microenvironment that 
stabilizes hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α), driving glycolytic flux and 
lactate accumulation. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent cell death process linked 
to lactate metabolism, has been implicated in UC pathogenesis; however, whether 
HIF-1α regulates ferroptosis through protein lactylation remains unclear. 
Bioinformatic analysis identified HIF-1α as a pivotal node connecting 
lactylation and ferroptosis signatures, with the lactylation score showing a 
strong positive correlation with ferroptosis activity, suggesting its upstream 
regulatory role. In cellular UC models, both protein lactylation and ferroptosis 
markers were significantly elevated. Inhibition of lactate synthesis reduced 
intracellular Fe2+ overload and normalized expression of ferroptosis-related 
proteins. Mechanistically, knockdown of HIF-1α in colonic epithelial cells 
downregulated key glycolytic enzymes, including HK2, decreased lactate 
production and subsequent protein lactylation, and ultimately attenuated lipid 
peroxidation and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, thereby suppressing 
ferroptosis. Conversely, HIF-1α overexpression promoted ferroptosis-associated 
alterations in a glycolysis-dependent manner, and exogenous lactate partially 
restored these alterations upon HIF-1α silencing, supporting a 
HIF-1α-lactate-lactylation-ferroptosis cascade. We further screened for 
pharmacological inhibitors of HIF-1α and identified quercetin as a candidate 
through molecular docking and binding kinetics. Functional validation in vitro 
and in vivo demonstrated that quercetin directly binds and inhibits HIF-1α, 
thereby blocking the lactylation-ferroptosis axis and ameliorating colitis. 
Collectively, this study elucidates a novel HIF-1α-lactylation-ferroptosis 
regulatory axis in UC and proposes quercetin as a potential therapeutic agent 
that targets this "metabolism-cell death" network.

(1)Laboratory of Molecular Electron Microscopy, The Rockefeller University, New

(FcγRIIa), potently blocking immune complex engagement without cross-reacting 
with the closely-related FcγRIIb. This specificity has made IV.3 invaluable for 
dissecting FcγRIIa-mediated activation in diverse conditions, including 
infection, autoimmunity, thromboinflammation, and platelet-mediated thrombosis.

R134-specific interaction network in the presence of S135. These findings 
provide a mechanistic framework for rational design of FcγRIIa-targeted

Insects offer promising opportunities for organic waste bioconversion; however, 
they cannot efficiently degrade synthetic polymers such as polyethylene 
terephthalate (PET). Here, we generated transgenic Drosophila melanogaster lines 
to express in vitro-evolved variants of two PET-degrading enzymes with distinct 
biochemical properties: an engineered Ideonella sakaiensis PETase variant 
(TS-ΔIsPET) and a leaf-branch compost cutinase variant (TA-ΔLCC). Both enzymes, 
fused to a Drosophila gut-derived secretory signal, were produced and secreted 
by Drosophila cultured S2R+ cells and transgenic larvae. Upon secretion, 
TS-ΔIsPET and TA-ΔLCC enzymes were glycosylated, a post-translational 
modification that did not abolish their catalytic activity. Notably, TA-ΔLCC 
displayed ∼6-fold higher esterase activity than TS-ΔIsPET in larval samples, and 
TA-ΔLCC-containing extracts depolymerised PET nanoparticles in vitro under 
enzyme-favourable conditions. Transgenic flies showed normal development, 
fertility and survival. Morphological and biochemical analyses confirmed that 
TA-ΔLCC expression did not alter midgut structure and function. Together, these 
results establish Drosophila melanogaster as a model for functional expression 
and comparative evaluation of engineered PET-degrading enzymes and identify 
TA-ΔLCC as a promising candidate for further evaluation in insect species 
relevant to plastic-contaminated waste bioconversion.

Major Plant Diseases and Regional Plant Health Priorities in Asia.

Kim KT(1)(2), Hue Y(3), Nam Y(3), Choi B(3), Kim J(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Agricultural Life Science, Sunchon National University, 
Suncheon 57922, Korea. kitaekim@scnu.ac.kr.
(2)Department of Plant Medicine, Sunchon National University, Suncheon 57922, 
Korea. kitaekim@scnu.ac.kr.
(3)Department of Plant Medicine, Sunchon National University, Suncheon 57922,

Asia supports major food, horticultural, and plantation crops, yet uneven loss 
data and surveillance capacity hinder continental-scale prioritization of plant 
diseases. This review integrates FAOSTAT crop statistics, EPPO pathogen 
occurrence and host records, Scopus affiliation- based publication data, and 
disease-specific literature to identify regional surveillance and management 
priorities. Wheat, rice, maize, and potato accounted for nearly three quarters 
of the documented crop-pathogen intersections, highlighting shared staple-crop 
vulnerabilities. Rice blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight, and viral diseases 
remain major concerns in Eastern, Southern, and South-eastern Asia, where 
intensive cultivation and changing pathogen populations complicate durable 
control. Wheat rusts, bunts, and cyst nematodes warrant attention in Central, 
Southern, and Western Asia, while wheat blast highlights the introduction risks 
in Southern Asian. Fusarium head blight and maize ear rots link crop protection 
with food and feed safety. Potato late blight, viral degeneration, and bacterial 
wilt emphasize seed-tuber health in temperate and highland systems. In 
South-eastern Asia, cassava mosaic disease, banana Fusarium wilt, and oil palm 
basal stem rot present challenges associated with infected planting material and 
persistent inoculum. Tomato viruses threaten Western Asian protected 
horticulture, while citrus huanglongbing and fire blight highlight the need for 
healthy nursery stock and early detection. These regional disease profiles call 
for management tailored to production systems and pathogen biology, prioritizing 
durable resistance in cereals, healthy planting material in vegetatively 
propagated crops, and containment of persistent soilborne diseases. Standardized 
diagnostics, coordinated surveillance, and resource sharing can strengthen 
disease management across regions with unequal research and surveillance 
capacity.

Perceptions of Maternal Mortality Risk and Influences Among Women of Color.

Renbarger K, Salahshoor S, Place JM.

OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to explore perceptions of maternal 
mortality among women of color who identify as Black, Hispanic, or multiracial, 
including their understanding of perceived risk factors and the influence of 
recent perinatal experiences on these perceptions.
DESIGN: A qualitative, descriptive design was used to conduct this study.
SETTING: Participants were recruited for a semistructured, virtual interview to 
discuss their perceptions related to maternal mortality.
PARTICIPANTS: Thirty women of color who identify as Black, Hispanic, or 
multiracial and live in Indiana participated in interviews.
RESULTS: Six themes emerged: (a) limited understanding of maternal mortality, 
(b) increased awareness of factors related to maternal mortality after 
experiences of perinatal complications, (c) fear due to perceived high risk of 
perinatal complications, (d) feeling dismissed during perinatal care, (e) 
barriers to quality perinatal care and lack of trust in health care systems, and 
(f) social support and advocacy as protective factors for preventing maternal 
mortality.
CONCLUSION: Women of color need more awareness of warning signs for maternal 
mortality; they frequently have negative perinatal care experiences and can 
benefit from social support. Nurses can improve perinatal practice by increasing 
knowledge of maternal mortality, promoting a respectful maternity care 
framework, and increasing social support.

Qualitative Descriptive Exploration of Women's Experiences of Outpatient 
Hysteroscopy in Ireland.

Henry C, Lloyd B, Bradshaw C.

OBJECTIVE: To explore women's experiences of outpatient hysteroscopy (OPH) and 
identify factors that influenced those experiences.
DESIGN: Qualitative descriptive.
SETTING: Ambulatory gynecology unit in Ireland.
PARTICIPANTS: Eleven women aged 40 to 49 years who underwent OHP at the research 
setting.
METHODS: We collected data using semistructured interviews and analyzed the data 
using a reflexive thematic analysis framework.
RESULTS: We identified three themes: The Experience of Pain, Preparation and the 
Procedure, and Importance of the Environment. Participants described a spectrum 
of pain experiences that ranged from mild discomfort to severe pain. They 
emphasized the importance of preparation for the procedure and the care provided 
during and after the procedure. Participants also identified environmental 
factors that enhanced their experience of OPH.
CONCLUSION: Health care practitioners should explicitly discuss the possibility 
of pain when providing information about OPH to ensure that women can make 
informed choices. Researchers should further investigate the optimal type and 
timing of pre-procedure analgesia. Health care practitioners should also 
recognize the importance of the environment in shaping women's experiences of 
intrusive and intimate procedures from a holistic perspective. These findings 
are relevant to all health care practitioners involved in OPH services, 
particularly nursing staff who provide care to women before, during, and after 
these procedures.

BACKGROUND: Although commonly accepted depressive subtypes reflect phenotypic 
differences, there has been minimal progress in identification of discrete 
pathophysiological pathways, biomarkers or differential therapeutic approaches 
to effectively guide clinical management.
AIMS: To test the biological validity and clinical utility of a circadian 
subtype of depression on the basis of clinical course, differential medication 
response (self-reported) and genetic risk profile.
METHOD: Cross-sectional data were drawn from the nationwide Australian Genetics 
of Depression Study. Participants were classified as having a 'circadian' or 
'non-circadian' subtype of depression on the basis of meeting criteria for at 
least three binary circadian-associated features: social jetlag, seasonality, 
delayed sleep midpoint, evening chronotype, morning tiredness and hypersomnia. 
Clinical course characteristics were compared. Associations with response to 
commonly prescribed antidepressants and polygenic risk scores for mental 
disorders and sleep, circadian, metabolic and inflammatory traits were 
investigated using logistic regression models.
RESULTS: A total of 2604 participants (23%; 80% female; mean age 37.87 ± 13.62 
years) had a circadian subtype. They reported an earlier age at onset (P < 
0.001), more severe clinical features including (hypo)manic-like and 
psychotic-like experiences, suicidality, psychological distress and somatic 
complaints (all P < 0.001), weight gain during depressive episodes (P < 0.001), 
poorer response to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.88 [95% 
CI 0.82, 0.94]) and serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.89 
[95% CI 0.83, 0.97]), and more side-effects compared with those with a 
non-circadian subtype. Having a circadian subtype was associated with higher 
polygenic risk scores for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (odds ratio 
1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 1.17]), major depression (odds ratio 1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 
1.16]), anxiety (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.04, 1.15]), bipolar disorder (odds 
ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.04, 1.14]), body mass index (odds ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.05, 
1.14]), triglycerides (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.06, 1.16]), interleukin-6 (odds 
ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]), higher insulin resistance (odds ratio 1.08 [95% 
CI 1.04, 1.13]), later sleep midpoint (odds ratio 1.15 [95% CI 1.10, 1.21]), 
insomnia (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]) and later chronotype (odds ratio 
0.68 [95% CI 0.65, 0.71]).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the face validity and potential clinical 
utility of a circadian subtype of depression as a clinical profile. Pending 
independent replication, investigation of its biology and predictive utility are 
warranted.

Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interaction of enavogliflozin, a 
sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, with glimepiride and metformin in 
healthy participants.

Chang K(1), Kim Y(1), Jung D(2), Cho JM(2), Cho JY(1)(3)(4), Lee S(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics, Seoul National 
University College of Medicine and Hospital, Seoul, Republic of Korea.
(2)Clinical Development Center, Daewoong Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd, Seoul, Republic 
of Korea.
(3)Department of Biomedical Sciences, Seoul National University College of 
Medicine, Seoul, Republic of Korea.
(4)Kidney Research Institute, Seoul National University Medical Research Center, 
Seoul, Republic of Korea.

AIMS: Enavogliflozin, a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, is expected to 
be coadministered with antihyperglycaemic drugs with different mechanisms of 
action. This study aimed to investigate the pharmacokinetic (PK) and 
pharmacodynamic (PD) interactions between enavogliflozin, glimepiride and 
metformin.
METHODS: A randomized, open-label, two-sequence, three-period crossover study 
was conducted. Participants received one of the following three treatments for 
6 days in each period: enavogliflozin 0.3 mg once daily (E), glimepiride 2 mg 
once daily and metformin 1000 mg twice daily combination (GM) or the combination 
of all three study drugs (E + GM). Serial blood and urine samples were collected 
for PK and PD assessments at steady state.
RESULTS: The geometric mean ratios (GMRs) and 90% confidence intervals (CIs) for 
the maximum plasma concentration (Cmax,ss) of enavogliflozin, glimepiride and 
metformin were 1.0811 (1.0273-1.1378), 1.1495 (1.0602-1.2464) and 1.0556 
(0.9937-1.1215), respectively. The corresponding values for the area under the 
plasma concentration-time curve within a dosing interval (AUCτ,ss) were 1.0031 
(0.9541-1.0545), 1.2264 (1.1383-1.3213) and 1.1638 (1.0958-1.2361) respectively. 
A 24-h urinary glucose excretion (UGE0-24h) induced by E was affected by 
coadministration of GM, with the GMR (90% CI) of 0.7834 (0.7307-0.8400). Serum 
glucose reduction was greatest with the E + GM, followed by GM, and then E.
CONCLUSIONS: No clinically meaningful PK interaction of enavogliflozin, 
glimepiride and metformin was observed. Although a reduction in UGE0-24h was 
observed, an additive PD interaction was observed in serum glucose levels. The 
results suggest that enavogliflozin can be coadministered with glimepiride and 
metformin without requiring dose adjustments of either of these drugs.

Bioinspired Janus-Structured Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Mask with 
Dual‑Scale Heterointerface for Ultrasensitive Exhaled H2S Detection in 
Periodontitis Diagnosis.

Hao B(1), Zhao J(1), Yang Z(2), Li X(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, National and Local Joint 
Engineering Research Center for Bioenergy Development and Utilization, Harbin 
Institute of Technology, Harbin150001, P. R. China.
(2)School and Hospital of Stomatology, Jilin University, Changchun130012, P. R. 
China.

The accurate detection of hydrogen sulfide (H2S) in exhaled breath is important 
for the early diagnosis of periodontitis; however, it is limited by high 
humidity in the oral environment, contaminant accumulation, and multicomponent 
interference. Herein, we present a Janus-structured surface-enhanced Raman 
scattering (SERS) platform featuring a dual-scale heterogeneous interface 
inspired by the asymmetric wettability of lotus leaves for sensitive detection 
of ppb-level H2S. Specifically, thermal treatment of polypropylene melt-blown 
fabric precoated with polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) induces hydrophobic residue 
migration, converting the surface to superhydrophobic. Moreover, the PDMS layer 
promotes dense growth of MgAl layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanosheets followed 
by Ag nanoparticle deposition, constructing the superhydrophilic SERS functional 
side. The spatially heterogeneous wettability design achieves diode-like 
unidirectional liquid transport properties, effectively resisting signal 
interference at 90% relative humidity in exhaled breath. Importantly, the 
gradient pore architecture functions as a molecular deceleration layer, 
retarding the diffusion of high-kinetic-energy H2S and enriching it within the 
hotspots of the MgAl LDH/Ag nanocavities, yielding a limit of detection of 1.54 
ppb. Clinical exhaled breath analysis has confirmed that this sensor integration 
strategy in KN95 masks exhibits feasibility and accuracy, holding promise as an 
effective technical means for early noninvasive screening and clinical 
diagnosis.

Moore VA(1)(2), Lam AB(3), Kola G(4), Soni U(3), Liles J(3), Watkins A(2),

BACKGROUND: Patients with cancer often require hospital-level care to address 
urgent needs and symptom concerns. However, little research has sought to 
identify patient factors, particularly rural-urban residence, associated with 
care outcomes in this population.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including adult patients with 
cancer admitted to the University of Oklahoma Medical Center from January 2017 
through December 2022. We extracted patients' sociodemographic (ie, age, sex, 
race, ethnicity, rural-urban residence [Rural-Urban Continuum Codes]) and 
clinical (ie, Charlson comorbidity index [CCI] score, cancer type, metastatic 
disease status) information from the electronic health record. We used 
multivariable models to explore associations of patient factors with clinical 
outcomes (time to hospital discharge for length of stay [LOS], time to first 
readmission, and time to death [overall survival]).
RESULTS: We identified 20,683 patients in our cohort (mean [SD] age, 62.6 [15.4] 
years; 52% female sex, 40% with a CCI score ≥3, 41% with metastatic cancer, 31% 
with nonmetropolitan residence). Median hospital LOS was 4.0 days, with 30- and 
90-day readmission rates of 15% and 23%, and median survival was 5.0 years. 
Older age (hazard ratio [HR], 0.93; P<.001), male sex (HR, 0.94; P<.001), higher 
comorbidity (CCI score ≥3: HR, 0.70; P<.001), and metastatic disease (HR, 0.88; 
P<.001) were associated with longer LOS. Higher comorbidity (CCI score ≥3: HR, 
2.70; P<.001) was associated with a greater risk of readmission. Older age (HR, 
1.50; P<.001), CCI score ≥3 (HR, 1.68; P<.001), and nonmetropolitan residence 
(HR, 1.08; P=.007) were associated with worse survival.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of hospitalized patients with cancer, we identified 
associations of patients' sociodemographic and clinical factors with their 
hospital LOS, risk of readmission, and survival. Findings from this work could 
help inform targeted efforts to enhance care delivery and outcomes for this 
population.

Polarization modulation is an effective approach for developing electromagnetic 
wave (EMW) absorbing materials. However, it is still a challenge to enhance the

(7)Zhejiang Key Laboratory of Advanced Polymer Materials Modification and

Chameleon-like adaptive coloration inspires dynamic information camouflage, yet 
translating temporally programmable optical behavior into synthetic soft 
materials remains challenging. Here, we develop a zwitterionic pVS hydrogel for 
time-gated information encryption, decryption, and irreversible optical erasure. 
The system uses the established alkali-responsive fluorescence of VPES-derived 
units as the optical basis, while the SBMA-rich zwitterionic network suppresses 
swelling and preserves pattern fidelity. Spatially separated UV- and thermally 
initiated polymerization pathways generate domains with distinct initial 
emission states and alkaline-response trajectories within the hydrogel, allowing 
polymerization history to function as an intrinsic optical key. Quantitative 
kinetic analysis reveals progressive fluorescence convergence between the UV- 
and thermally initiated domains, with the red-emission contrast decreasing from 
0.667 to 0.012 during prolonged alkaline treatment and preventing subsequent 
recovery of QR-code readability after acid treatment. This convergence 
establishes an operational time window for information security: short alkaline 
exposure produces a recoverable encrypted state, whereas excessive exposure 
permanently eliminates the optical contrast required for QR-code recognition, 
resulting in irreversible information self-destruction. This work provides a 
kinetically controlled hydrogel strategy for transient information protection 
and time-limited optical authentication.

Fast and Sensitive Ionogel Capacitive Sensing of Acetic Acid at Room Temperature 
for Early Plant Salt Stress Detection.

Yang G(1), Zheng W(2), Guo Z(1), Xiong C(1), Li Y(1), Pan C(1), Wang C(1), Zhang 
L(1), Yun J(1), Yang J(1), Huang J(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Materials Science and Engineering, Tongji University, 
Shanghai201804, P. R. China.
(2)Key Laboratory of Quality and Safety Control for Subtropical Fruit and 
Vegetable, Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, College of Horticulture 
Science, Key Laboratory of Quality and Safety Control for Subtropical Fruit and 
Vegetable, Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, College of Horticulture 
Science, Hangzhou, Zhejiang311300, P. R. China.

Acetic acid has been identified as an early biomarker of salt stress in plants, 
enabling precise monitoring of plant health and timely detection of stress. 
However, its rapid and selective detection at room temperature remains 
challenging. Herein, we report an ionogel capacitive chemical sensor based on a 
polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrix incorporating the ionic liquid 
1-butyl-3-vinylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate ([VBIM][BF4]). The resulting 
ionogel sensor exhibits high selectivity toward acetic acid over common volatile 
organic compounds, originating from solvent effects and electrostatic 
interactions between acetic acid molecules and the ionic liquid, as revealed by 
density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Owing to these interactions, the 
sensor achieves a rapid response time of approximately 6 s at room temperature, 
and the practical limit of detection is as low as 500 ppb. In addition, the 
sensor shows excellent long-term stability and mechanical flexibility. The 
sensor maintains stable sensing performance after 180 days of storage at room 
temperature and can be integrated with a wireless monitoring system. 
Furthermore, the sensor detects the acetic acid released by salt-stressed 
plants, highlighting its potential as an early-warning platform for agricultural 
stress monitoring.

Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) affects all ages, with infants and older 
adults most affected by severe disease. The RSV prevention landscape includes 39 
candidates in clinical development, alongside setbacks such as the 
discontinuation of a promising paediatric live-attenuated vaccine candidate. 
Several products have been approved, including a maternal vaccine, infant 
monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines for older adults and adults at high risk. 
Due to high cost, implementation of these products remains limited to 
higher-income settings. Real-world evidence confirms high effectiveness, with 
emerging benefits beyond respiratory disease, including reduced cardiovascular 
events in older adults. Despite comparable effectiveness of maternal vaccination 
and monoclonal antibodies, differences in uptake highlight that product 
availability alone will not ensure population impact. Achieving uptake requires 
integration into accessible routine care, recommendation by trusted providers, 
and context-sensitive delivery strategies. This Review summarises RSV preventive 
products, real-world effectiveness and uptake, and the opportunity of using 
communication in translating RSV prevention into impact.

Role of Ultrasound in Dynamic Sports Assessments.

Jones JC(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Scottish Rite for Children, Texas, United States, Dallas.
(2)University of Texas Southwestern, Departments of Orthopaedics and Pediatrics, 
Texas, United States, Dallas.

ABSTRACT: Musculoskeletal ultrasound offers a unique ability to perform dynamic, 
real-time assessment of musculoskeletal structures during motion, providing 
functional information that is not available with static imaging modalities. 
Dynamic ultrasound remains underutilized in pediatric sports-related 
musculoskeletal evaluation, where skeletal immaturity and pediatric-specific 
injuries present distinct diagnostic challenges.
ABSTRACT: This review outlines the principles and clinical applications of 
dynamic ultrasound in the pediatric athlete. Common dynamic assessment 
techniques in the pediatric population are illustrated across frequently 
evaluated joints, including the shoulder, elbow, wrist and hand, hip and pelvis, 
knee, and foot and ankle. Applications include evaluation of joint instability, 
ligamentous injury, tendon subluxation or snapping, apophyseal avulsion 
injuries, and motion-dependent conditions.
ABSTRACT: Dynamic ultrasound complements clinical and biomechanical assessment 
in pediatric athletes. Familiarity with pediatric-specific anatomy, conditions, 
and dynamic techniques can expand diagnostic confidence and enhance the role of 
ultrasound in sports-related musculoskeletal imaging.

[Development of a Shoulder Prevention Program for Overhead Sports: GOTS Shoulder 
Guard: Train Smart, Perform Strong!].

[Article in German; Abstract available in German from the publisher]

Ritterbusch A(1), Grim C(2), Tischer T(3), Lutter C(3), Mauch F(4), Beitzel 
K(5), Seil R(6), Hoppe MW(7).

Author information:
(1)University of Marburg: Philipps-Universität Marburg, Exercise Science, 
GERMANY, Marburg.
(2)Universität Osnabrück: Universität Osnabrück, Institut für 
Gesundheitsforschung und Bildung, GERMANY, Osnabrück.
(3)Universitätsmedizin Rostock, Orthopädische Klinik und Poliklinik, GERMANY, 
Rostock.
(4)Sportheum Sportklinik Fellbach, GERMANY, Fellbach.
(5)Athos Orthoparc Klinik, GERMANY, Köln.
(6)Centre Hospitalier de Luxembourg, Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, 
LUXEMBOURG, Luxembourg.
(7)Philipps-Universität Marburg: Philipps-Universität Marburg, 
Trainingswissenschaft, GERMANY, Marburg.

BACKGROUND: Shoulder injuries have a substantial impact on health economics in 
overhead sports. While prevention programs for knee injuries have already been 
extensively investigated, there remains a substantial research gap regarding 
shoulder injuries. This study aimed to develop a new, practical prevention 
program for shoulder injuries in overhead sports.
METHODS: To develop the program, a literature search was conducted to identify 
evidence-based risk factors and prevention programs in overhead sports. To 
ensure the highest possible level of evidence, only systematic reviews and 
randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were included. In addition, a 25-item online 
survey on epidemiology, diagnostics, prevention and implementation was conducted 
among 30 internationally recognized prevention experts. The survey was carried 
out by the Prevention Committee of the Society for Orthopaedic Traumatologic 
Sports Medicine (GOTS). The findings were subsequently discussed by consensus 
and integrated into a novel prevention program incorporating established 
principles of exercise and training science.
RESULTS: Based on the results of three systematic reviews (five evidence-based, 
modifiable risk factors) and five RCTs (five different prevention programs, all 
demonstrating positive effects) as well as the expert survey (with the primary 
requirement being for an evidence-based, practical, and time-efficient program) 
and the integration of established principles of exercise and training science 
(circuit training methodology, progression through block periodization, and 
repetition numbers until muscular fatigue), the "GOTS Shoulder Guard: Train 
Smart, Perform Strong!" was developed. The prevention program focuses primarily 
on controlling scapulothoracic mobility, mobilizing the glenohumeral joint, 
strengthening the external rotators, mobilizing/stabilizing the kinetic chain, 
and stabilizing the glenohumeral joint.
CONCLUSION: The "GOTS Shoulder Guard" differs from existing prevention programs 
through its stronger evidence base and the application of established principles 
of exercise and training science. These principles allow for a more practical, 
time-efficient and individualized load control, taking into account the 
athlete's performance level and fluctuations. Further evaluation studies are 
required to verify the effectiveness, compliance and feasibility of the program.

Publisher: Schulterverletzungen haben in den Überkopfsportarten eine hohe 
gesundheitlich-ökonomische Tragweite. Während Präventionsprogramme für 
Knieverletzungen bereits umfassend untersucht sind, existiert für 
Schulterverletzungen jedoch noch ein erheblicher Forschungsbedarf. Ziel dieser 
Studie ist es demnach, ein neues, praxisnahes Präventionsprogramm für 
Schulterverletzungen in den Überkopfsportarten zu entwickeln.Für die Entwicklung 
wurde eine Literaturrecherche hinsichtlich evidenzbasierter Risikofaktoren und 
Präventionsprogramme in den Überkopfsportarten durchgeführt. Zwecks 
höchstmöglicher Evidenz wurden dafür nur systematische Übersichtsarbeiten und 
randomisiert kontrollierte Studien (RCTs) eingeschlossen. Ferner erfolgte eine 
Online-Befragung zu 25 Items zur Epidemiologie, Diagnostik, Prävention und 
Implementierung von 30 international ausgewiesenen Präventionsexperten. Die 
Befragung wurde durch das Komitee „Prävention“ der Gesellschaft für 
Orthopädisch-Traumatologische Sportmedizin (GOTS) realisiert. Die gewonnenen 
Erkenntnisse wurden schließlich konsensuell diskutiert und unter Einbezug 
etablierter, trainingswissenschaftlicher Prinzipien in ein neues 
Präventionsprogramm integriert.Basierend auf den Ergebnissen aus drei 
systematischen Übersichtsarbeiten (fünf evidenzbasierte, modifizierbare 
Risikofaktoren) und fünf RCTs (fünf verschiedene Präventionsprogramme mit 
überwiegend positiven Effekten) sowie der Expertenbefragung (primäre Forderung 
nach einem evidenzgeleiteten, praktikablen und zeiteffizienten Programms) und 
Integration trainingswissenschaftlicher Prinzipien (Zirkeltrainingsmethodik, 
Progression mittels Blockperiodisierung und Wiederholungsanzahlen bis zur 
muskulären Ermüdung) wurde der „GOTS Shoulder Guard: Train Smart, Perform 
Strong!“ entwickelt. Das Präventionsprogramm adressiert schwerpunktmäßig die 
Kontrolle der skapulothorakalen Beweglichkeit, Mobilisierung des 
Glenohumeralgelenks, Kräftigung der Außenrotatoren, Mobilisierung/Stabilisierung 
der kinetischen Kette und Stabilisierung des Glenohumeralgelenks.Der „GOTS 
Shoulder Guard“ hebt sich von bestehenden Präventionsprogrammen durch eine 
höhere Evidenzgrundlage sowie die Anwendung etablierter, 
trainingswissenschaftlicher Prinzipien ab. Diese erlauben eine praktikablere, 
zeiteffizientere und individuellere Belastungssteuerung unter Berücksichtigung 
des Leistungsniveaus und tagesabhängiger Schwankungen. Um die Wirksamkeit, 
Compliance und Implementierbarkeit des Programms zu überprüfen, sind weitere 
Evaluationsstudien erforderlich.

[The development of the Law on the Protection of Non-Smokers in Bavaria: a model 
for the whole of Germany?].

[Article in German; Abstract available in German from the publisher]

Urlbauer M(1), Nowak D(2).

Author information:
(1)Klinikum Nürnberg Nord, Medizinische Privat-Universität Salzburg,

BACKGROUND: Bavaria is a special case in Germany when it comes to tobacco 
control policy. The Free State initially enacted a particularly strict law 
protecting nonsmokers in 2008, relaxed it again in 2009, and reinstated the 
strict protections following the July 4, 2010 referendum.
RESEARCH QUESTION: Can the Bavarian approach serve as a model for all of 
Germany, and what opportunities and obstacles arise when applying it to other 
federal states?
METHODS: A narrative review based on a targeted literature search, official 
documents, and two appended texts on developments in Bavaria. The review 
included political, legal, occupational health, and epidemiological studies 
related to the protection of nonsmokers in Bavaria and Germany.
RESULTS: The body of research consistently indicated that strict smoking bans 
significantly reduced exposure to secondhand smoke in indoor settings. In German 
restaurants and bars, fine particulate matter levels dropped dramatically after 
the smoking ban was introduced, and children's exposure to secondhand smoke at 
home and in cars decreased without any significant shift to private settings 
being confirmed. At the same time, the political literature showed that 
Bavaria's success was achieved only under specific conditions: a simple message, 
a clear health-based framework, strong mobilization of civil society, and a 
referendum question that did not hide behind exceptions.
CONCLUSION: Bavaria serves as a model, provided this is understood as an 
empirically sound and politically mobilizable reference case. The model is of 
limited use as a blueprint because the federal legal landscape remains 
heterogeneous and exceptions weaken its effectiveness. The most important lesson 
is therefore this: protection for nonsmokers is most sustainable where it is 
simple, has few exceptions, and is justified as a means of protecting the 
workplace, children, and public health.

Publisher: Bayern ist der deutsche Sonderfall der Tabakkontrollpolitik. Der 
Freistaat setzte 2008 zunächst ein besonders strenges Nichtraucherschutzgesetz 
in Kraft, lockerte es 2009 wieder und stellte den strikten Schutz nach dem 
Volksentscheid vom 4. Juli 2010 erneut her.Kann der bayerische Weg als Vorbild 
für ganz Deutschland gelten, und welche Möglichkeiten und Hürden zeigen sich bei 
der Übertragung auf andere Bundesländer?Narrative Übersichtsarbeit auf Basis 
einer gezielten Literatursichtung, amtlicher Dokumente und zweier beigefügter 
Texte zur bayerischen Entwicklung. Berücksichtigt wurden politische, 
juristische, arbeitsmedizinische und epidemiologische Arbeiten mit Bezug zum

dafür, dass strikte Rauchverbote die Belastung durch Passivrauch in Innenräumen 
deutlich reduzieren. In deutschen Gastronomiebetrieben sank die 
Feinstaubbelastung nach Einführung des Rauchverbots massiv, bei Kindern ging die 
Passivrauchexposition in der Wohnung und im Auto zurück, ohne dass sich eine 
relevante Verlagerung ins Private bestätigte. Zugleich zeigt die politische 
Literatur, dass der bayerische Erfolg nur unter besonderen Bedingungen zustande 
kam: einfache Botschaft, klare gesundheitliche Rahmung, starke 
zivilgesellschaftliche Mobilisierung und eine Abstimmungsfrage, die sich nicht 
hinter Ausnahmen versteckte.Bayern ist ein Vorbild, wenn man darunter einen

Publisher: PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility, anatomical outcomes, and early

Comparing Dual X-Ray Absorptiometry to Anthropometry to Determine the Lean 
Mass-to-Bone Ratio.

Dengel DR(1), Westerberg HE(1), Sydykova B(2), Dooley JS(1).

Author information:
(1)University of Minnesota, Laboratory of Integrative Human Physiology, School 
of Kinesiology, Minnesota, United States, Minneapolis.
(2)Kazakhstan Medical University KSPH, Department of Epidemiology, 
Evidence-Based Medicine and Biostatistics, Almaty Province, Kazakhstan, Almaty.

The muscle-to-bone ratio (MBR) is a body composition metric that examines the 
weight placed on the bone from muscle. Currently, two methods are used for 
calculating MBR: 1) dual X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), and 2) anthropometrics. 
This study compared these two methods of determining MBR. A total of 31 (n=16 
male, n=15 female) had their body composition assessed via a whole-body DXA and 
anthropometrics, which consisted of 43 measurements (i.e., skinfolds, girths, 
lengths, and breaths). Anthropometric measures were analyzed using the five-way 
fractionation method. Anthropometric-derived muscle mass, residual mass, and 
skin mass were combined to obtain a comparable measure of DXA-derived lean mass 
(LM). The lean mass-to-bone ratio (LMBR) for DXA and anthropometrics was 
determined by dividing LM by bone mass (BM). Statistical significance was 
determined at an alpha value of p≤0.05. DXA- and anthropometric-derived LMBR 
(22.8±3.1 vs. 5.2±1.0) were significantly different. This difference was due to 
significant differences in both DXA- and anthropometric-derived measures of LM 
(56.7±13.0 vs. 42.6±11.7 kg), and BM (2.5±0.5 vs. 8.2±2.0 kg). Bland-Altman 
analysis revealed a negative bias between DXA- and anthropometrics-derived LMBR 
that increased with rising anthropometric-derived BM and LM. Therefore, the LMBR 
determined by DXA and anthropometrics cannot be used interchangeably.

Auth JM(1), Eizenberg-Magar I(1), Erez Dekel O(1), Zachar O(1), Shmueli MD(2), 
Zigdon I(1), Shoham A(1), Mindel V(1), Olender T(1), Asulin Berrebi M(1), 
Tennenhouse A(3), Bar-Hai N(4), Ben-Yishay R(5), Ishay-Ronen D(4), Antebi YE(6).

Author information:
(1)Department of Molecular Genetics, Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot,

(2)Department of Systems Immunology, Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot,

(3)Department of Biomolecular Sciences, Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot,

The BMP and TGF-β signaling pathways control cellular fate decisions in diverse 
biological contexts, often playing opposing roles. Despite extensive knowledge 
of these pathways, understanding how cells respond to environments containing 
these opposing cues remains a challenge. Here, we systematically analyze the 
activation of these pathways under combinatorial signaling environments. We find 
that TGF-β ligands inhibit BMP signaling while BMP ligands enhance TGF-β 
transcriptional response across concentrations, ligand variants, and cell types. 
This asymmetric crosstalk results in the activation of a TGF-β-biased 
transcriptional response even under mixed-signaling conditions, effectively 
reducing signal ambiguity, with implications for processes such as 
epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). We show that this crosstalk 
originates downstream of SMAD protein phosphorylation. Using mathematical 
models, we predict and experimentally verify that promiscuous interactions 
between SMAD proteins provide the mechanism for the observed crosstalk. Our 
findings challenge the canonical models, suggesting an active role for mediator 
proteins in determining biological responses.

SRSF3 (SRp20), a member of the serine/arginine-rich protein family of splicing 
factors, plays a central role in constitutive and alternative splicing. The 
C-terminal arginine/serine-rich domain of SRSF3 undergoes dynamic 
phosphorylation cycles that regulate its subcellular localization,

BACKGROUND: The abscopal effect, regression of unirradiated tumors after 
localized radiotherapy, is rare. Whether hypofractionated radiotherapy (HFRT) 
plus the innate immune agonist polyinosinic-polycytidylic acid [Poly(I:C)] 
amplifies systemic antitumor immunity in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma is 
unclear.
METHODS: In this single-arm, phase 2 trial (ChiCTR2100053441), 37 patients 
received HFRT plus subcutaneous Poly(I:C); 33 were response evaluable. Outcomes 
were compared with 33 propensity score-matched patients treated with HFRT alone. 
The primary endpoint was the objective response rate per RECIST v.1.1; secondary 
endpoints included progression-free survival, overall survival, and safety; and 
abscopal response was prespecified. Mechanisms were explored by single-cell RNA 
sequencing and flow cytometry in patients and by CD8 depletion and CD28 blockade 
in mice.
FINDINGS: HFRT plus Poly(I:C) was well tolerated; it was associated with a 
higher objective response rate (54.5% vs. 21.2%; p = 0.011) and abscopal 
response rate (45.0% vs. 10.5%; p = 0.042) as well as longer progression-free 
survival (8.4 vs. 4.6 months; adjusted hazard ratio = 0.542; p = 0.042) and 
overall survival (not reached vs. 13.6 months; adjusted hazard ratio = 0.386; p 
= 0.011) vs. HFRT alone. The progression-free survival benefit was also higher 
in patients concurrently receiving tyrosine kinase inhibitors (p for interaction 
= 0.013). Peripheral CD8+CD28+ T cell expansion correlated with abscopal tumor 
control; in mice, CD8+ T cells and CD28 co-stimulation were required for this 
effect.
CONCLUSIONS: HFRT plus Poly(I:C) showed promising systemic antitumor activity 
with manageable safety in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, with CD8+CD28+ T 
cells as an immune correlate of response. These exploratory findings warrant 
confirmation in randomized trials.

Blood biomarkers are transforming Alzheimer's disease diagnostics by enabling a 
scalable, minimally invasive assessment of pathology. Food and Drug 
Administration clearances and European market certifications of different plasma 
tests mark a shift toward biological diagnosis in routine care. However, 
clinical implementation is not guided by diagnostic accuracy alone but will 
depend on improved patient-centered and pathway-level outcomes, including 
diagnostic confidence, the appropriate use of CSF and PET assessments, time to 
diagnosis, amyloid-targeting treatment eligibility assessment, and trial 
recruitment. Digital biomarkers may complement blood tests by providing repeated 
measures of cognition, speech, and mobility. Yet, their evidence base remains 
more heterogeneous regarding construct validity, supervision requirements, 
device dependence, adherence burden, cultural portability, interpretability, and 
regulatory classification. This review defines how combined blood-digital 
workflows could be evaluated beyond accuracy, including the context of use, 
downstream decisions, ethical aspects, governance, and post-market monitoring, 
ultimately aiming to translate biomarker innovation into meaningful benefits for 
patients and health systems.

Reduced insulin secretion by β cells is a pivotal factor in diabetes onset and 
progression. The small molecule NPD976 was identified as a potent insulin 
secretagogue using high-throughput chemical screening employing an insulin 
secretion assay system. Even part of the molecular structure of NPD976, 
designated as DPEU (N-[2-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)ethyl]urea), retains insulin 
secretagogue activity. DPEU enhances insulin secretion specifically under 
glucose stimulation in β cells derived from mice, rats, and humans. The compound 
localizes to mitochondria in a manner independent of high glucose stimulation. 
Biochemical analyses revealed that DPEU directly interacts with 
voltage-dependent anion channels (VDACs) located in the mitochondrial outer 
membrane, enhancing ATP efflux from mitochondria into the cytosol during glucose 
stimulation. To our knowledge, DPEU is a positive small-molecule modulator of 
VDAC function that promotes ATP flux in β cells through a mechanism distinct 
from the classical KATP or cAMP pathways. These findings identify VDAC as a 
potential target for enhancing insulin secretion.

Bacteria-phage interactions are often studied in relatively simple experimental 
systems involving a single bacterial strain infected by a single phage.1 In 
natural environments, however, bacteria typically inhabit complex multispecies 
communities where species compete for limited resources and ecological 
niches.2,3,4 Recent studies show that the microbial community context can have 
profound effects on the evolution of phage resistance.5 For example, Pseudomonas 
aeruginosa evolves phage resistance primarily through receptor loss when grown 
in isolation but switches to CRISPR-based immunity in the presence of bacterial 
competitors.6,7 Previous work showed that interspecies competition can favor 
CRISPR-immune bacteria over surface mutants after phage resistance has evolved.6 
However, it remains unknown whether competition also alters the initial 
generation of CRISPR immunity by changing CRISPR-Cas expression and spacer 
acquisition before selection among resistance phenotypes occurs. Here, we show 
that interbacterial competition can trigger CRISPR-Cas activation and adaptation 
in P. aeruginosa. When co-cultured with Acinetobacter baumannii, P. aeruginosa 
exhibited markedly increased expression of CRISPR-Cas genes and a higher 
frequency of new spacer acquisition, whereas no such induction occurred in 
monoculture or mixed communities lacking A. baumannii. This upregulation was 
associated with markers of DNA damage and stress signaling, indicating that 
competition-induced stress primes the bacterial adaptive immune response. These 
findings identify interbacterial antagonism as an ecological and physiological 
trigger for CRISPR activation, linking competitive interactions to enhanced 
antiphage defense. More broadly, our results suggest that bacteria sense and 
respond to competitive stress in complex microbial communities by increasing the 
generation of more adapted genotypes.

Phage defense systems in bacteria exhibit high degrees of modularity, with 
sensing, signal transmission, and effector enzymes frequently exchanged among 
phage defense gene clusters. In this study, we capitalize on this modularity to 
discover phage defense systems by searching for defense-associated modules in 
new gene contexts across Pseudomonas aeruginosa genomes. This approach reveals a 
large and interconnected network of modular components distributed across 
diverse gene clusters. From over 500 candidate defense systems, we select five

infection; and Hercules, a tightly regulated restriction-modification (RM)-like 
system. Collectively, we demonstrate that leveraging the modular architecture of 
phage defense systems is an effective approach to their discovery.

Regulatable in vivo gene expression via adaptamers.

Bryant J(1), Herron L(1), Doctor Y(1), McRae F(1), Wang J(1), Hirsch T(1),

Precise, reversible control of transgene expression is essential for safe and 
durable gene therapy, yet current inducible systems remain difficult to 
translate in vivo due to large size, limited induction duration, and dependence 
on immunogenic regulators. Here, we present the adaptamer (adenosine deaminases 
acting on RNA [ADAR]-modulatable aptamer), a compact (<120 base pair) RNA switch 
that couples FDA-approved small-molecule-responsive aptamers with endogenous

steatosis. This minimal, programmable system offers a clinically compatible 
approach for tunable genetic medicines and safe deployment of pleiotropic and 
dose-limited proteins.

Local Tissue Damage Induced by Snakebite Envenoming: Mechanisms and Therapeutic 
Advances.

Luo J(1), Xiong W(1), Gu J(1), Xie Y(2), Zheng X(2), Wang W(2), Dong D(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Jiangxi University of Chinese 
Medicine, Nanchang, China.
(2)Department of Traditional Chinese Surgery, The Affiliated Hospital of Jiangxi 
University of Chinese Medicine, Nanchang, China.

Snakebite envenoming is a serious and often neglected tropical disease 
associated with high mortality and disability rates. Local tissue injury is one 
of the main causes of long-term functional impairment after snakebite. 
Clinically, it may present as local hemorrhage, edema, myonecrosis, and tissue 
fibrosis. Accumulating evidence indicates that several venom components, 
including snake venom metalloproteinases, snake venom phospholipase A2s, 
three-finger toxins, and L-amino acid oxidases, are involved in local tissue 
injury. These toxins can induce direct cellular and microvascular damage. They 
can also trigger inflammatory responses, immune dysregulation, and oxidative 
stress. Compared with systemic toxicity, local tissue damage often has more 
persistent effects on patients. Antivenom is currently the main treatment of 
snakebite envenoming. It can neutralize venom toxins and reduce mortality. 
However, its effect on established local tissue injury remains limited. In 
recent years, several adjunctive therapies have shown potential. These include 
small-molecule enzyme inhibitors, photobiomodulation therapy, and stem 
cell-based therapies. However, most studies still lack sufficient clinical 
evidence. This review summarizes the major venom components involved in 
snakebite-induced local tissue injury, the underlying pathophysiological 
mechanisms, and potential therapeutic strategies. The aim of this review is to 
provide new perspectives for future mechanistic studies and clinical 
intervention.

The term "tropical medicine" has sparked many discussions on its appropriateness 
because of its colonial history. The aim of this study was to analyze 
perceptions of the term among international medical professionals. An open 
online survey, conducted between August 2023 and September 2024, was distributed 
via professional networks and social media. Of 590 respondents from 66 
countries, 80% were employed in the global north. Participants employed in the 
global south associated "tropical medicine" more with a geographical connotation 
(77/85 versus 346/471, P <0.001). Only 21% saw the need to replace the term, 
with stigmatization (35%) mentioned as a major association. Free-text responses 
showed varying perceptions. Some respondents pointed out that replacing the term 
is not sufficient to achieve "genuine change". The study's results raise the 
question whether a change in terminology can act as a driver of decolonization, 
stressing that the need for structural reforms is far more important.

Bordier E(1), Vidal C(1), Delmas B(2), Jabot J(1), Traversier N(3), Miltgen

Leptospirosis is a zoonosis prevalent on Réunion Island. Severe forms with acute 
respiratory failure can lead to refractory hypoxemia, requiring the use of 
extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). The aim for the present study was to 
describe all cases of leptospirosis complicated by refractory acute respiratory 
distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring veno-venous ECMO on Réunion Island and to 
conduct a literature review. This retrospective observational study was 
conducted in a multidisciplinary intensive care unit of the University Hospital 
of Réunion Island. The aim was to describe the clinical, biological, and 
prognostic characteristics of patients who developed leptospirosis complicated 
by refractory ARDS requiring ECMO between January 2011 and December 2024. A 
total of 14 patients with a median age of 38 years and few comorbidities were 
included. The organ failure most commonly associated with respiratory 
involvement was acute kidney injury (93%). The median delay between mechanical 
ventilation and ECMO support was 0 (0-1) days. The median duration of ECMO 
support was short (7 [4-12] days). The mortality rate in this population was 
29%. A systematic literature review revealed 50 cases of patients with 
leptospirosis requiring ECMO, with a median age of 34 years and a mortality rate 
of 20%. The favorable prognosis of patients with refractory ARDS due to 
leptospirosis justifies the use of ECMO. Early referral to a center equipped 
with ECMO is essential, given the rapid decline in respiratory function.

Headache in Calcified Neurocysticercosis: Emerging Insights into an 
Inflammation-Driven Phenotype.

Del Brutto OH(1).

Author information:
(1)Research Center, Universidad Espíritu Santo-Ecuador, Samborondón, Ecuador.

Calcified neurocysticercosis (NCC), traditionally considered an inert marker of 
past infection, is increasingly recognized as a clinically meaningful condition 
associated with migraine-like headaches. Evidence from population-based cohorts, 
clinical series, and imaging studies consistently shows that individuals with 
calcified NCC have a higher prevalence and severity of headache than those 
without lesions. Prospective neuroimaging demonstrates that intermittent 
perilesional inflammation, including edema and blood-brain barrier disruption, 
can activate migraine-generating pathways, with calcitonin gene-related 
peptide-mediated trigeminovascular sensitization emerging as a key mechanism.

Validation of a Rapid Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification-Based Test for the

has been validated as a simple, sensitive, and rapid tool for detecting Shigella

indicating a practical alternative to stool for detecting Shigella. The assay 
was also reliable with stool collected in BGS and SDSs. Broader adoption of 
RLDTs could improve diagnostic capacity and strengthen surveillance and control 
efforts.

Latent Melioidosis Reactivation Following Immunosuppression in Malaysia: A

Sia T(1), Gan TY(1), Lim GY(2), Chong WK(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Medicine, Miri Hospital, Miri, Sarawak, Malaysia.

Melioidosis, caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, is endemic in Southeast Asia. 
Over 90% of cases present acutely. The reactivation of latent melioidosis in 
endemic regions is difficult to diagnose, and the incidence is unknown. We 
report two previously healthy middle-age women from Limbang, Malaysian Borneo,

and initiating targeted therapy early are critical during the initiation and 
administration of immunosuppressive treatment. Pre-immunosuppression risk 
assessment and potential prophylactic strategies in high-risk individuals may 
help reduce the associated morbidity and mortality.

Intestinal fibrosis is a major complication of Crohn's disease, for which 
targeted therapies remain unavailable. Fibrosis is defined by excess matrix 
deposition, which may result from inadequate phagocytic clearance, yet how 
phagocytosis shifts here is unclear. Using single-cell and spatial 
transcriptomics, we identify fibrosis-associated CD47hi fibroblasts coupled to 
SIRPAhi macrophages in fibrotic regions. Cell-cell communication analyses and 
neutralizing-antibody experiments identify interleukin-1β as a mediator of their 
crosstalk, forming a profibrotic niche characterized by phagocytic evasion.

models with schedule-dependent efficacy. Collectively, these findings support 
CD47-mediated phagocytic evasion as a key pathogenic mechanism in intestinal 
fibrosis and identify CD47-SIRPα blockade as a promising therapeutic target.

(1)Warwick Clinical Trials Unit, Warwick Medical School, University of Warwick,

INTRODUCTION: Biomarker-guided antibiotic protocols using daily procalcitonin or 
C-reactive protein have been proposed to optimise antibiotic duration in sepsis. 
This pre-planned process evaluation of the ADAPT-Sepsis trial examined delivery 
and clinician adherence to procalcitonin- and C-reactive protein-guided 
protocols.
METHODS: An embedded descriptive process evaluation was conducted within the 
multicentre ADAPT-Sepsis trial including 2760 adults across 41 UK critical care 
units. Patients were assigned to procalcitonin-guided, C-reactive protein-guided 
or standard care. Algorithm-generated recommendations (strong stop, suggest stop 
or standard care) were relayed to research staff and clinicians who remained 
blinded to group allocation. Adherence was defined as stopping biomarker 
sampling after advice. Advice timings, frequencies, adherence rates and reasons 
for non-adherence were recorded and analysed.
RESULTS: Among 2760 patients, strong stop advice occurred earlier in those 
allocated to the procalcitonin-guided group compared with the C-reactive 
protein-guided group (mean difference -1.7 days, 95%CI -2.5 to -0.9, p < 0.001). 
C-reactive protein guidance generated a higher proportion of standard care 
advice (mean difference -9.1%, 95%CI -10.9% to -7.3%, p < 0.001). Overall advice 
adherence was greater in patients allocated to the C-reactive protein group than 
those allocated to the procalcitonin group (mean difference -6.8%, 95%CI -9.0 to 
-4.5, p < 0.001), driven by the higher proportion of standard care advice and 
later stronger stop advice with higher adherence (mean difference -14.3%, 95%CI 
-21.8 to -6.8, p < 0.001). Reasons for advice non-adherence included 
fixed-duration microbiology guidance, illness severity, continuing fever and 
elevation of routine inflammatory markers, which did not differ between groups.
DISCUSSION: A C-reactive protein-guided discontinuation protocol achieved higher 
clinician adherence, probably because its recommendations aligned more closely 
with established prescribing norms. In contrast, procalcitonin guidance produced 
earlier and more frequent stop signals, offering greater potential to reduce 
antibiotic exposure but requiring clinicians to accept earlier discontinuation 
than usual practice.

Plain Language Summary: WHAT WE DID: As part of a large clinical research study 
across 41 NHS hospitals, we studied how well medical doctors followed daily 
advice to stop antibiotics early using two different infection marker blood 
tests – procalcitonin (PCT) and C‐reactive protein (CRP) – in adults with 
suspected serious life‐threatening infection (sepsis). Based on daily PCT or CRP 
laboratory results, a computer system sent messages each day telling doctors 
either to stop antibiotics or continue their usual care without revealing the 
blood test results.
WHY WE DID IT: Blood marker‐guided advice to stop antibiotics when they are no 
longer needed could help protect patients and reduce antibiotic resistance. But 
these systems only work if doctors trust and act on the advice. We wanted to 
understand which of the two blood tests worked better in practice and why 
doctors sometimes chose not to follow the advice.
WHAT WE FOUND: Procalcitonin gave earlier and more frequent ‘stop antibiotic’ 
signals than CRP. C‐reactive protein advice was followed more often, mainly 
because it gave fewer early stop messages and felt more in line with usual 
practice. Doctors often ignored early stop advice because they were following 
fixed treatment plans, the patient was still very sick, or other laboratory 
tests were still high. The reasons for not following advice were the same for 
both tests. Overall, PCT has more potential to shorten antibiotic treatment, but 
doctors were less comfortable acting on its early stop signals. C‐reactive 
protein was easier for clinicians to follow but less effective at prompting 
early discontinuation. To get the most value, blood markers such as PCT alone 
are not enough. Healthcare professionals also need support, clear guidance and 
confidence to work together and safely stop antibiotics when they are no longer 
needed. This could improve patient care while reducing unnecessary antibiotic 
use.

Ehab A(1), Abdelwahab HW(2), Hamoda M(3), Elhosiny MM(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chest Medicine, Faculty of Medicine, Mansoura University, 
Mansoura, Egypt; DGD Hemer Lung Center, Hemer, Germany. Electronic address:

BACKGROUND: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) counts respiratory events but not the 
depth or duration of accompanying desaturation. We examined AHI-ODI discordance 
(AHI minus oxygen desaturation index, ODI) and its associations with daytime 
symptom burden and prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity.
METHODS: Single-center retrospective cross-sectional study of 200 adults with 
OSA (January 2023-January 2025). Five indices (AHI, ODI, mean SpO2, T90 and 
AHI-ODI discordance) were examined; excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS; Epworth 
Sleepiness Scale ≥ 11) was the primary outcome. Multivariable logistic 
regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI and an AHI-ODI × sex interaction.
RESULTS: The cohort was 77.5% male, median age 57 years (48.8-64.2). For EDS, 
AHI-ODI discordance showed the numerically highest AUC (0.639, p < 0.001), 
followed by T90 (0.627), and mean SpO2 and ODI (0.609 each); AHI was not 
significant (0.546, p = 0.264). No pairwise difference was significant. AHI-ODI 
discordance remained independently associated with EDS after adjustment (OR 1.04 
per event/h, 95% CI 1.01-1.07, p = 0.008), with no significant sex interaction. 
Among secondary outcomes, T90 showed the highest AUCs for diabetes mellitus 
(0.644) and hypertension (0.615), and mean SpO2 for heart failure (0.608). No 
index discriminated against previous stroke or atrial fibrillation.
CONCLUSIONS: AHI-ODI discordance was independently, but only modestly, 
associated with EDS, whereas oxygenation indices were related to prevalent 
cardiometabolic comorbidity. The discrimination was insufficient, and all 
reported cut-offs are exploratory. AHI-ODI discordance is not a measure of sleep 
apnea-specific hypoxic burden.

BACKGROUND: Reduced exercise capacity, measured by the 6-min walk distance 
(6MWD), is a critical prognostic factor in interstitial lung disease (ILD). 
However, conventional physiological markers often fail to identify early 
functional decline. We aimed to evaluate whether the foot-to-foot lower-limb 
phase angle (F-F PhA), a non-invasive surrogate marker of muscle quality, 
predicts reduced exercise capacity better than traditional muscle mass and 
pulmonary function indices.
METHODS: In this retrospective study of 68 patients with ILD, F-F PhA was 
measured using bioelectrical impedance analysis, and erector spinae muscle area 
(ESM_CSA) via computed tomography. Reduced exercise capacity was defined as 6MWD 
< 450 m. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age and pulmonary 
function (%DLCO or %FVC), with internal validation performed via 1000-resample 
bootstrapping.
RESULTS: In multivariable analysis, F-F PhA was independently associated with a 
6MWD < 450 m when adjusted for age and %DLCO (OR: 0.228, 95% CI: 0.088-0.591, 
p = 0.002; bootstrap p = 0.005) or %FVC (OR: 0.213, 95% CI: 0.091-0.496, 
p = 0.001; bootstrap p = 0.001). ROC analysis showed F-F PhA had the highest 
discriminative accuracy (AUC: 0.802), outperforming %DLCO (AUC: 0.729) and 
ESM_CSA (AUC: 0.701). Combining age, %DLCO, and F-F PhA achieved the highest 
performance (AUC: 0.833).
CONCLUSIONS: F-F PhA serves as a robust, independent indicator for predicting 
reduced exercise capacity in ILD, outperforming conventional muscle mass. As a 
non-invasive tool, F-F PhA complements established functional tests in screening 
for early physical decline.

BACKGROUND: The study aim was to examine trends in non-4-valent and non-9-valent 
vaccine-type HPV detection over the first 17 years after U.S. HPV vaccine 
introduction among young women.
METHODS: We recruited 13-26 year-old sexually experienced women (N = 2335) from 
hospital and community clinics for six surveillance studies from 2006 to 2023, 
with testing for HPV DNA by Roche Linear Array or TypeSeq2. Outcome variables 
were: 1) potentially carcinogenic alpha-9 and -7 non-vaccine-type HPV 
genetically related to HPV16 or 18 but not targeted by the 4- or 9-valent 
vaccines (to assess for cross-protection) and 2) potentially carcinogenic 
alpha-5, -6, and - 11 non-vaccine-type HPV not closely genetically related to 
types targeted by the 4- or 9-valent vaccines (to assess for type replacement). 
We used inverse probability of treatment weighting with propensity score to 
balance between-wave differences in participant characteristics in prevalence 
estimates and in tests of linear trend using surveillance study as a continuous 
variable.
RESULTS: Among all, vaccinated, and unvaccinated participants, there were no 
significant trends in the prevalence of at least 1 non-vaccine-type HPV 
genetically related to HPV16 and/or HPV18 but not targeted by the 4- or 9-valent 
vaccines. Positivity for non-vaccine-type HPV genetically unrelated to types 
targeted by the 4- or 9-valent vaccines remained stable from 2006 to 2015 but 
increased from 2016 to 2023; the trend was significant for all groups.
CONCLUSIONS: We did not find evidence for cross-protection against types not 
targeted by the 4-valent or 9-valent vaccines, but did find a signal for

Quantifying the impact of pathogen interactions on vaccine effectiveness 
estimates in the test-negative design.

Cai Z(1), Wang L(2), Ji S(1), Deng X(3), Qiu L(3), Wang S(4), Lei H(5).

Author information:
(1)School of Public Health, the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University 
School of Medicine, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, PR China.
(2)Department of Preventive Medicine, Children's Hospital, Zhejiang University 
School of Medicine, National Clinical Research Center for Children and 
Adolescents' Health and Diseases, Hangzhou, PR China.
(3)Zhejiang Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention, Hangzhou, PR 
China.
(4)Zhejiang Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention, Hangzhou, PR 
China; Zhejiang Key Lab of Vaccine, Infectious Disease Prevention and Control,

(5)School of Public Health, the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University

The test-negative design (TND) has been widely adopted for real-world vaccine 
effectiveness (VE) assessment, assuming that control selection is independent of 
vaccination status. However, pathogen interactions may contradict this 
assumption, posing challenges to VE evaluations. We developed a theoretical 
framework to quantify the pathogen-dependence-related biases in VE estimates. 
The framework was further empirically evaluated using data from 66,117 pediatric 
patients tested for multiple respiratory pathogens during 2023-2024, comparing 
influenza VE estimates using standard influenza-negative controls with those 
using specific non-influenza pathogen positive or negative controls. The 
theoretical framework indicated that the TND may overestimate VE even without 
pathogen dependence. Pathogen dependence further modified influenza VE estimates 
in a pathogen-specific direction, i.e., positive pathogen dependence with 
influenza tended to overestimate influenza VE, whereas negative pathogen 
dependence biased VE estimates downward. However, the magnitude of 
dependence-related bias was generally smaller than the bias attributable to the 
baseline model-specific discrepancy. The use of all-pathogen-negative controls 
minimized estimation bias. These findings suggest that pathogen dependence and 
control selection should be considered when using TND for VE estimation.
