Timing of supervised exercise and cardiometabolic risk markers in adults: A 
systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

Chen B(1), Cui X(1), Feng M(1), Qu A(1), Wang H(1), Zhang H(2), Zhang L(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Epidemiology and Health Statistics, School of Public Health, 
Capital Medical University, Beijing, 100069, China; Beijing Key Laboratory of 
Environment and Aging, Beijing, 100069, China.
(2)Department of Epidemiology and Health Statistics, School of Public Health, 
Capital Medical University, Beijing, 100069, China; Beijing Key Laboratory of 
Environment and Aging, Beijing, 100069, China; School of Public Health, Hainan 
Medical University, Hainan, 571199, China.
(3)Department of Epidemiology and Health Statistics, School of Public Health, 
Capital Medical University, Beijing, 100069, China; Beijing Key Laboratory of 
Environment and Aging, Beijing, 100069, China. Electronic address: 
zlilyepi@ccmu.edu.cn.

OBJECTIVES: Regular exercise improves cardiometabolic health; however, the 
magnitude of its benefits may vary by time of day. To evaluate whether the 
timing of supervised exercise training is associated with differences in 
cardiometabolic outcomes in adults.
STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled 
trials.
METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus were 
searches from inception to March 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of ≥2 
weeks comparing supervised exercise performed at different times of day in 
adults and reporting cardiometabolic outcomes were eligible. Mean difference 
(MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models 
with restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Knapp-Hartung and leave-one-out 
sensitivity analyses, exploratory subgroup analyses, and GRADE assessment were 
performed.
RESULTS: Twelve RCTs (n = 879) were included. Later-day exercise was associated 
with a small reduction in fasting blood glucose compared with earlier exercise 
(MD = 0.16 mmol/L, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.29; I2 = 0.0%). This finding remained 
statistically significant with Knapp-Hartung adjustment. No clear timing-related 
differences were observed for HbA1c, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, blood lipids, 
systolic or diastolic blood pressure, BMI, or fat mass. Systolic blood pressure 
showed substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 72.5%). Certainty of evidence ranged from 
very low to moderate across outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Later-day exercise was associated with a small reduction in fasting 
blood glucose, but current evidence does not support a consistent advantage of a 
specific exercise time for other cardiometabolic outcomes. Larger, 
well-standardized RCTs are needed before specific exercise-timing 
recommendations can be made.

OBJECTIVE: To determine if the spatial extent of interictal fast ripples in 
focal epilepsy patients is associated with brain dysfunction.
METHODS: Thirty pediatric focal epilepsy patients who underwent SEEG 
investigation had their cognitive and language deficits assessed in scales of 0 
to 4. Fast ripples (250-500 Hz), ripples (80-250 Hz), and IEDs were 
automatically detected in 10 min during NREM sleep. We fitted linear models to 
the relationship between the cognitive deficit scale and the spatial spread of 
the interictal neurophysiologic events (number of channels with rate of 
events > 10 % of maximum rate). For the language deficit, we computed the 
Spearman correlation between the median rate of events in all brain regions and 
the deficit scale.
RESULTS: Cognitive deficit scale was significantly associated with the number of 
channels with fast ripples (p = 0.049), not so with ripples (p = 0.31), IEDs 
(p = 0.31). The potential confound of number of explored channels did not 
improve the fitting of the models. Language deficits were not correlated with 
the number of channels showing interictal events. However, from all brain 
regions the most statistically significant correlations (p < 0.01) were between 
median fast ripple rates in the left and right pars opercularis and triangularis 
of the inferior frontal gyrus (Broca's area and its contralateral counterpart) 
with r = 0.66, p = 0.003 (18 patients), in the superior temporal gyrus in the 
language dominant hemisphere with r = 0.72, p = 0.005 (13 patients), and the 
dominant basal temporal region with r = 0.79, p = 0.006 (10 patients). Median 
rates of IEDs and ripples exhibited lower correlation with language deficits in 
these regions.
CONCLUSION: Widespread fast ripples are associated with increased cognitive 
deficits, and language deficiencies are correlated with fast ripple rates in 
brain regions associated with language. The extent of fast-ripple activity was 
associated with cognitive deficit severity in this cohort, whereas the 
corresponding associations for ripples and IEDs did not reach statistical 
significance.

(3)Federal University of São Paulo, São Paulo, Brazil.
(4)Institute of Primary Care, University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland; Medbase 
St. Gallen Am Vadianplatz, St. Gallen, Switzerland. Electronic address: 
beat.knechtle@hispeed.ch.

Medication adherence is a major determinant of seizure control in people with 
epilepsy, yet nonadherence remains frequent and is associated with breakthrough 
seizures, increased healthcare utilization, and higher mortality. Despite the 
central role of antiseizure medications (ASMs), adherence is a multifactorial 
behavior shaped by routine stability, health beliefs, self-efficacy, mood, and 
social support, and it cannot be improved by prescription alone. Physical 
exercise has emerged as a promising complementary strategy in the management of 
chronic diseases, with benefits that extend beyond general health. This short 
communication examines the potential of regular physical exercise to act as an 
adjunct to the pharmacological treatment of epilepsy, with particular emphasis 
on how it may favor medication adherence. At the behavioral level, physical 
exercise may stabilize daily routines, improve mood and self-efficacy, and 
reinforce treatment engagement factors that plausibly support consistent 
medication taking. At the physiological level, physical exercise modulates 
hemodynamic, metabolic, and neurobiological pathways, although direct evidence 
of clinically relevant effects on ASM disposition remains scarce. Nonetheless, 
exercise-induced pharmacokinetic alterations depend on the type, intensity, and 
duration of exertion-ranging from sustained aerobic exercise to high-intensity 
resistance training-which differentially modulate hemodynamics, metabolic 
pathways, and plasma protein binding, with the greatest potential relevance for 
antiseizure medications with a narrow therapeutic index. Barriers to physical 
exercise participation, including fear of seizures, stigma, and limited 
professional counseling, parallel those that compromise adherence and deserve 
systematic attention. We conclude that physical exercise should be regarded as a 
safe, low-cost, complementary component of epilepsy care, and that prospective 
studies examining its effects on medication adherence and pharmacological 
outcomes represent a research priority.

OBJECTIVE: Generalized spike-wave discharges (GSWD) are occasionally observed in

clinical implications.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of 148 children diagnosed 
with SeLECTS at Xuanwu Hospital from June 2015 to October 2025. Patients with

Real-world effectiveness and safety of cenobamate in children and adolescents 
with drug-resistant epilepsy: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and 
meta-regression.

Samanta D(1), Ramani PK(2), Jain P(3).

Author information:
(1)Division of Child Neurology, Department of Pediatrics, University of AR for 
Medical Sciences (UAMS), Little Rock, AR, USA. Electronic address: 
dsamanta@uams.edu.
(2)Division of Child Neurology, Department of Pediatrics, University of AR for 
Medical Sciences (UAMS), Little Rock, AR, USA.
(3)Epilepsy Program, Division of Neurology, Department of Pediatrics, The 
Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), University of Toronto, Toronto, Ontario, 
Canada.

BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Cenobamate is a third-generation antiseizure 
medication (ASM) approved for focal-onset seizures in adults; pediatric use 
remains off-label and supported primarily by retrospective studies. We conducted 
a systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-regression to evaluate the 
real-world effectiveness and safety of adjunctive cenobamate in pediatric 
drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE).
METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and 
meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD420261475361) of real-world studies including 
patients ≤18 years with DRE. Single-arm proportions were pooled using 
random-effects generalized linear mixed models. Heterogeneity was assessed using 
I2 and τ2. Pre-specified random-effects meta-regression explored study-level 
moderators of ≥50 % seizure reduction. Risk of bias was assessed using the JBI 
Critical Appraisal Checklist for Case Series.
RESULTS: Sixteen retrospective cohorts comprising 720 pediatric patients from 10 
countries were included. The pooled proportion achieving ≥50 % seizure reduction 
was 59.9 % (95 % CI, 51.4 %-67.9 %; 95 % prediction interval, 30.2 %-83.8 %; 
I2 = 68.2 %). Pooled estimates were 41.9 % (95 % CI, 26.4-59.2 %) for >75 % 
seizure reduction, 18.6 % (95 % CI, 12.3-27.1 %) for seizure freedom, and 49.9 % 
(95 % CI, 44.1-55.7 %) for any adverse effect. Leave-one-out analysis showed 
that no individual study disproportionately influenced the pooled ≥50 % 
seizure-response proportion (58.3-61.9 %). Visual and regression-based 
assessments did not detect marked funnel-plot asymmetry or an association 
between study size and effect estimates. No pre-specified moderator, including 
age, prior ASM burden, cenobamate dose, follow-up duration, focal epilepsy, 
clobazam exposure, or etiology, was significantly associated with response.
CONCLUSIONS: Approximately six in ten pediatric patients with DRE achieved ≥50 % 
seizure reduction with cenobamate. However, persistent unexplained heterogeneity 
and exclusively retrospective evidence limit subgroup-level inference. 
Prospective individual-patient-data registries with standardized outcome and 
dosing measures are needed to better define effectiveness, safety, and 
predictors of response in pediatric populations.

Machine learning-empowered nanobody-based dual-mode immunosensor using 
gold-silver nanoclusters for the accurate detection of Shigella flexneri in 
food.

Fan X(1), Zheng K(1), Wang M(1), Ge G(1), Miao Y(1), Yao Q(1), Chen P(1), Ma 
M(1), Wang J(1), Wang Y(2).

Author information:
(1)College of Food Science and Engineering, Northwest A&F University, Yangling, 
Shaanxi, 712100, China.
(2)College of Food Science and Engineering, Northwest A&F University, Yangling, 
Shaanxi, 712100, China. Electronic address: yanruwang22@163.com.

Sensitive and rapid detection of Shigella flexneri (S. flexneri) is of great 
significance for food safety and public health. In this study, a nanobody-based 
colorimetric/fluorescent dual-mode immunosensor was developed for the first 
time, and a machine learning model was integrated for intelligent fusion of the 
dual signals. A phage-displayed nanobody library was constructed by immunizing 
Bactrian camels with formalin-inactivated S. flexneri and specific nanobodies 
were obtained after four rounds of solid-phase panning. Using bovine serum 
albumin-protected gold-silver bimetallic nanoclusters (Au-Ag NCs) as fluorescent 
probes, a dual-signal output platform was established. Under optimized 
conditions, the colorimetric mode achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 
2.992 × 104 CFU/mL, and exhibited no cross-reactivity with other common 
foodborne pathogens. The LOD in the fluorescent mode was as low as 
4.074 × 103 CFU/mL, which is 7.3 times lower than that of the colorimetric mode. 
A machine learning model combining K-Nearest Neighbors classification and Random 
Forest regression was employed for intelligent calibration of the dual signals, 
significantly improving the reliability and stability of the assay. With the 
assistance of the machine learning model, the coefficient of determination (R2) 
between predicted and actual concentrations reached 0.9953. Spike-and-recovery 
experiments in food samples yielded recovery rates ranging from 81.53% to 
109.46%, demonstrating high accuracy. This study provides a novel, rapid, 
accurate, and environmentally friendly strategy for the detection of S. 
flexneri, holding great promise for applications in food safety monitoring.

Clustering of takeaway outlets around London schools: A geospatial analysis.

Gericke C(1), Llewellyn C(2), Burgoine T(3), Dennett A(4).

Author information:
(1)Research Department of Behavioural Science and Health, University College 
London, United Kingdom; Centre for Advanced Spatial Analysis (CASA), The

Chiara.gericke.20@ucl.ac.uk.
(2)Research Department of Behavioural Science and Health, University College

(3)MRC Epidemiology Unit, University of Cambridge, United Kingdom.
(4)Centre for Advanced Spatial Analysis (CASA), The Bartlett, University College

BACKGROUND: Rising childhood obesity has been linked to unhealthy built food 
environments, prompting the inclusion of takeaway management zones in the 
revised 2024 National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF). This study examines 
where takeaway outlet density is greatest around London schools, to guide 
policymakers on distance thresholds for takeaway management zones.
METHODS: We used Ordnance Survey data on takeaway outlets and UK Government data 
on Greater London schools from December 2021. Deprivation was assessed using the 
2019 Index of Multiple Deprivation. Extended spatial point pattern analyses were 
applied to assess takeaway outlet density by Euclidean distance and walking-time 
catchments from schools, and area-level deprivation of schools.
FINDINGS: Across London, takeaway outlet density peaked within approximately 
200 m of schools at around 12 outlets per km2, approximately twice the Greater 
London average of 6 outlets per km2, and remained above average up to around 
400 m. The highest density within walking catchments was within 10 min, although 
distributions varied, reflecting four patterns: (i) localised peak with gradual 
decline, (ii) extended peak with further peaks, (iii) sustained high density 
with sharp decline, and (iv) low density with extended decline. Among outlets 
located within 400 m of schools, density peaked at approximately 9 takeaway 
outlets per km2 in the 20-30% most deprived areas, compared with around 0.8 
takeaway outlets per km2 in the 10% least deprived areas - approximately 12 
times higher. This deprivation gradient was not observed among takeaway outlets 
located more than 400 m from schools.
INTERPRETATION: Findings support the implementation of takeaway management zones 
in London as outlined in the NPPF, set at 400m, or a 10-min walk from schools. 
However, variation across boroughs suggests local authorities may need to adjust 
the size or design of these zones. In the most deprived areas and central 
London, school-only measures may be insufficient, requiring complementary 
planning policies.

Mosca O(1), Zucca G(2), Tupputi A(3), Silletti A(3), Mocenni M(4), Chiodino 
E(2), Mureddu C(2), Guicciardi M(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pedagogy, Psychology, Philosophy, University of Cagliari,

(2)Department of Pedagogy, Psychology, Philosophy, University of Cagliari,

(3)Department of Dynamic, Clinical and Health Psychology, "Sapienza", University

(4)APIAFCO - Italian Psoriatic Association Friends of the Corazza Foundation, 
Bologna, Italy.

BACKGROUND: Chronic dermatological conditions, particularly psoriasis, are 
associated with substantial psychological burden and impaired quality of life. 
However, the psychosocial factors accounting for the relationship between 
psychological distress, dermatology-specific quality of life, and overall life 
satisfaction remain insufficiently understood.
OBJECTIVE: This study examined key risk and protective psychological factors 
associated with the relationship between distress and well-being among 
individuals with psoriasis and other chronic dermatological conditions.
METHODS: A total of 108 adults diagnosed with psoriasis or other chronic skin 
diseases (mean age = 48.32 years; 67.6% women) completed validated self-report 
measures assessing psychological distress, affect, acceptance of living with the 
disease, perceived stigma, social anxiety, perceived social support, 
self-compassion, mindfulness, dermatology-related quality of life, and 
satisfaction with life. Parallel mediation analyses were conducted while 
controlling for age and sex.
RESULTS: Higher psychological distress was statistically associated with greater 
impairment in dermatology-related quality of life both directly and indirectly 
through several psychosocial processes. Negative affect and perceived stigma 
were associated with greater distress-related impairment in dermatological 
quality of life, whereas acceptance of living with the disease emerged as a 
protective factor associated with lower impairment. In contrast, the indirect 
association between distress and lower life satisfaction was statistically 
accounted for by maladaptive self-compassion components, specifically isolation 
and over-identification. Dispositional mindfulness and perceived social support 
did not show significant mediating effects.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings highlight distinct psychological factors associated 
with distress and reduced well-being in individuals with chronic dermatological 
conditions. Acceptance-related processes may protect against 
dermatology-specific quality of life impairment, whereas stigma and negative 
affect are associated with greater vulnerability. In addition, self-critical and 
isolating responses to distress appear particularly relevant for diminished life 
satisfaction. These results support the integration of acceptance-based, 
compassion-focused, and stigma-reduction approaches within psycho-dermatological 
care.

Initial psychometric evaluation of the SER5: A forced-choice Big Five inventory 
scored with Thurstonian item response theory.

Parra-Gaete C(1), Samaniego-Frixone JJ(2), Vinueza-Cabezas A(3).

Author information:
(1)Grupo de Investigación Bienestar, Salud y Sociedad, Escuela de Psicología y 
Educación, Universidad de Las Américas, Quito, 170125, Ecuador. Electronic 
address: cesar.parra@udla.edu.ec.
(2)Grupo de Investigación Bienestar, Salud y Sociedad, Escuela de Psicología y 
Educación, Universidad de Las Américas, Quito, 170125, Ecuador. Electronic 
address: juan.samaniego.frixone@udla.edu.ec.
(3)Grupo de Investigación Bienestar, Salud y Sociedad, Escuela de Psicología y 
Educación, Universidad de Las Américas, Quito, 170125, Ecuador. Electronic 
address: andrea.vinueza@udla.edu.ec.

This study reports an initial psychometric evaluation of the SER5, a 
forced-choice Big Five inventory scored with Thurstonian item response theory 
(TIRT), and compares its trait estimates with a Likert-type comparison measure, 
the Big Five Personality Trait Short Questionnaire, in a Latin American 
personnel-selection context. A total of 6583 job applicants completed the SER5, 
presented as non-consequential, during real selection processes on an online 
recruitment platform used across Latin America. A confirmatory TIRT model 
supported the intended five-factor structure with good global fit; however, 
exploratory analyses (parallel analysis and the Maximal Kaiser Criterion) did 
not recover five dimensions, consistent with the rank-deficiency expected for 
the instrument's all-homopolar block design. Marginal reliability exceeded 0.70 
for all factors except Emotional Stability (ρ = 0.62), and conditional precision 
varied markedly across the trait range. Discriminant validity was weak, with a 
mean absolute inter-trait correlation less favorable than that of every 
forced-choice inventory in a recent benchmark, consistent with a block-design 
limitation, although alternative designs were not compared. In a subsample of 
714 complete cases, convergent correlations with the Likert comparison measure 
were modest, although TIRT scores converged significantly better than raw 
forced-choice scores for Extraversion and Agreeableness; for Openness, TIRT 
scoring only removed a negative raw-score association. Overall, forced-choice 
and Likert scores were not interchangeable: TIRT scoring appears necessary but 
not sufficient, block design is a plausible key constraint, and the SER5, 
designed as a supplementary screening tool, still requires criterion validation. 
Organizations should not transfer norms or cut-off scores across response 
formats.

Changes in students' self-reported psychological flexibility scores and

Pančocha K(1), Kingsdorf S(2), Dostál D(3).

Author information:
(1)Institute for Research in Inclusive Education, Faculty of Education, Masaryk 
University, Brno, Czech Republic. Electronic address: pancocha@ped.muni.cz.
(2)Institute for Research in Inclusive Education, Faculty of Education, Masaryk 
University, Brno, Czech Republic.
(3)Department of Psychology, Faculty of Arts, Palacký University Olomouc, 
Olomouc, Czech Republic.

This study examined longitudinal changes and social validity during 
implementation of a culturally adapted, teacher-delivered social-emotional 
learning curriculum grounded in acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) and 
applied behavior analysis (ABA) in Czech public primary schools. Participants 
were 448 children in Grades 2-5 from 23 classrooms across 10 schools. The 
year-long program was implemented as part of routine classroom practice, with 
assessments at baseline, midyear, and post-implementation. Students completed a 
shortened Czech adaptation of the Children's Psychological Flexibility 
Questionnaire (CPFQ), and teachers completed the Strengths and Difficulties 
Questionnaire (SDQ) and rated program social validity. Psychometric evaluation 
indicated substantial limitations in the CPFQ, including suboptimal factorial 
fit and low reliability of some subscales; the Present Moment subscale was 
excluded from longitudinal analyses, and changes in the remaining subscale 
scores were treated as exploratory. Linear mixed-effects models showed small 
increases in Acceptance and Defusion subscale scores, no clear linear change in

direction, including teacher-perceived reductions in emotional symptoms, conduct 
problems, hyperactivity, peer problems, and total difficulties, alongside 
increased prosocial behavior. Because the same teachers delivered the curriculum 
and rated children's behavior, with no parent, independent, or blinded 
assessments, these findings reflect teacher-perceived change. Teachers generally 
evaluated the program favorably while identifying time demands as the main 
constraint on implementation. Overall, the findings document favorable changes 
during implementation, particularly in teacher-rated functioning, while 
highlighting limitations in the measurement of psychological flexibility and the 
need for controlled evaluation.

Recently, the emotional aspects of using Artificial Intelligence (AI) 
technologies in second/foreign language (L2) education have been emphasized in 
the literature. Nevertheless, the way teachers may support their learners' 
emotional experiences via scaffolding practices has received comparatively 
limited attention in English as a foreign language (EFL) contexts. To address 
this gap, the present descriptive qualitative research explored Chinese EFL 
teachers' perceived and reported emotional scaffolding strategies used to 
regulate learners' emotions in AI-mediated L2 education. The data were gathered 
through interviews with 20 Chinese EFL teachers. The results of thematic 
analysis revealed five common emotional scaffolding strategies, which were 
perceived by the participants as useful for regulating their learners' 
AI-induced emotions. Particularly, they had used 1) personal stories and 
narratives, 2) technical-emotional support, 3) scaffolded tasks with positive 
reinforcement, 4) friendly and collaborative atmosphere, and 5) immediate and 
constructive feedback to support their learners' emotions in AI-mediated 
classes. The study invites teacher education programs to focus on the 
psycho-affective aspect of AI integration in L2 education.

Processing of second language emotion-laden words during sentence reading: 
Evidence from eye movements.

Alarjani FA(1), El-Dakhs DAS(2), Altarriba J(3).

Author information:
(1)Prince Sultan University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Electronic address: 
farjani@psu.edu.sa.
(2)Prince Sultan University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Electronic address:

(3)University at Albany, State University of New York, USA. Electronic address:

Research on emotional word processing has consistently reported an emotionality 
advantage for emotional over neutral words, particularly among first language 
(L1) speakers. However, evidence from bilingual populations remains limited and 
inconclusive, especially for emotion-laden words examined during natural 
reading. Extending previous eye-tracking research, the present study 
investigated the processing of positive and negative emotion-laden words during 
sentence reading among late Arabic-English bilinguals. Two eye-tracking 
experiments were conducted with Saudi EFL (English as a Foreign Language) 
learners who read sentences containing positive emotion-laden and neutral words 
(Experiment 1) or negative emotion-laden and neutral words (Experiment 2). 
Thirteen eye-movement measures representing early, late, and post-target 
processing stages were analyzed using mixed-effects models. In addition to 
emotionality, the analyses examined the effects of vocabulary knowledge, age, 
word frequency, and word length. Contrary to findings reported for L1 speakers, 
neither positive nor negative emotion-laden words demonstrated a robust 
processing advantage over neutral words once lexical and participant-related 
variables were controlled for. Vocabulary knowledge and age showed limited 
influence on emotional word processing, whereas word frequency emerged as the 
most consistent predictor of reading behavior. The findings support accounts 
emphasizing the role of language experience and learning context in shaping 
emotional representations and suggest that emotional facilitation may be 
attenuated during second-language (L2) reading, particularly for emotion-laden 
words.

To investigate how fatty acids (FA) modulate the structural evolution of 
granular rice starch-FA complexes under ultrasound (40-60 °C), lauric acid (LA), 
stearic acid (SA), oleic acid (OA), and linoleic acid (LOA) were selected to 
form complexes with rice starch. Ultrasonication alone partially reduced the 
structural order of rice starch, as evidenced by decreased relative 
crystallinity and short-range molecular order, while largely preserving the 
granular morphology and A-type crystalline polymorph. FA addition promoted the 
formation of V-type crystalline structures, with the degree of structural 
ordering depending on FA type and ultrasonic treatment conditions. Specifically, 
starch-LA exhibited the highest complex index (63.40%) and relative 
crystallinity (27.37%) at 60 °C, indicating a greater extent of complexation and 
structural ordering. In contrast, starch-SA exhibited a higher thermal 
transition temperature than starch-LA, suggesting that FA chain length affected 
complexation extent and thermal stability differently. Starch-LA displayed the 
lowest rapidly digestible starch (RDS, 64.31%) and highest resistant starch (RS, 
17.53%) contents at 60 °C. These findings provide a feasible strategy to tailor 
starch functionality through FA selection and ultrasonic treatment.

Rosas Diaz AN(1), Stabenau HF(2), Tung P(1), Nelson J(3), Hurtado GP(1), Warack

BACKGROUND: Anthracycline use is limited by cardiotoxicity resulting in heart 
failure (HF). The spatial ventricular gradient (SVG) is a vectorcardiographic 
measurement of myocardial electrical heterogeneity associated with sudden death 
and incident HF. It is unclear if serial measurement of SVG after anthracycline 
initiation can help predict subsequent HF.
OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to determine if time-varying SVG 
measurements are associated with anthracycline HF.
METHODS: Retrospective, single-center study of adult patients with cancer 
treated with anthracyclines between 1992 to 2019. Standard 12-lead 
electrocardiograms obtained within 6 months before and up to 5 years after 
anthracycline initiation were analyzed. Patients with prior HF or ≤1 
electrocardiogram within 5 years were excluded. Median vectorcardiograms were 
constructed, and the SVG vector was obtained by integrating under the X, Y, and 
Z QRST complexes. Multivariable competing-risks regression was performed with 
SVG parameters included as time-varying covariates, incident HF as the main 
outcome, and death as a competing outcome.
RESULTS: Among 594 patients (median age 61 years, 48% male), 83 (14%) developed 
HF within 5 years. In multivariable competing-risks regression, time-varying SVG 
azimuth (circular angle in the transverse plane) was independently associated 
with HF (P = 0.0024), demonstrating a 9.4-fold gradient in risk across values. 
Leftward/anterior azimuth values were the lowest risk areas, whereas 
posterior/rightward orientations were the highest risk.
CONCLUSIONS: Time-varying SVG azimuth was independently associated with HF risk 
in patients treated with anthracyclines. Assessing dynamic changes in SVG 
azimuth during anthracycline treatment may enhance early identification of 
patients at risk for HF and inform the use of cardioprotective strategies during 
cancer therapy.

Atrial Fibrillation in Valvular Heart Disease: Assessing the Impact of Genetics 
in the UK Biobank.

Cristin L(1), Tang JJ(1), Tastet L(2), Jhawar R(1), Glidden DV(3), Marcus GM(1), 
Delling FN(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Medicine (Cardiovascular Division), University of 
California-San Francisco, San Francisco, California, USA.
(2)Department of Medicine (Cardiovascular Division), University of 
California-San Francisco, San Francisco, California, USA; Institut Universitaire 
de Cardiologie et de Pneumologie de Québec-Université Laval, Québec, Québec, 
Canada.
(3)Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, University of California-San 
Francisco, San Francisco, California, USA.
(4)Department of Medicine (Cardiovascular Division), University of 
California-San Francisco, San Francisco, California, USA. Electronic address: 
francesca.delling@ucsf.edu.

BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) in valvular heart disease (VHD) is 
generally attributed to pressure or volume overload with atrial remodeling, but 
the independent contribution of genetic predisposition remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: The authors evaluated the predictive value of a previously developed 
AF polygenic risk score (PRS) across VHD subtypes in the UK Biobank.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study (UK Biobank, 2000-2022), incident AF 
and VHD status were defined using ICD codes. VHD subtypes included mitral valve 
(MV) disease (MV prolapse [MVP], mitral regurgitation, mitral stenosis) and 
aortic valve (AV) disease (aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation). PRS was 
categorized into quintiles and grouped as low, intermediate, and high.
RESULTS: Among 452,841 participants with available PRS, 385 had MVP, 1,058 
mitral regurgitation, 81 mitral stenosis, 421 aortic regurgitation, and 509 
aortic stenosis. In Cox models, PRS was independently associated with incident 
AF in MV disease (HR: 1.7, P = 0.03 for intermediate PRS; HR: 2.3, P = 0.002 for 
high PRS), with the strongest effect in MVP (HR: 3.1, P = 0.03 for high PRS). In 
AV disease, PRS was not significantly associated with AF risk (P = 0.93 and P = 
0.07 for intermediate and high PRS, respectively). Interaction analyses 
confirmed attenuation or absence of the PRS effect in AV disease (P = 0.04 and P 
= 0.004 for intermediate and high PRS, respectively), whereas no significant 
interaction was observed in MV disease (P = 0.80 and P = 0.11, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: In VHD, AF PRS predicts AF risk, but the genetic impact differs by 
subtype. AV disease shows minimal genetic contribution, suggesting predominantly 
hemodynamic risk, while MV disease-particularly MVP-shows substantial genetic 
influence.

BACKGROUND: We assessed contemporaneous changes in gastric adenocarcinoma 
incidence, presentation, registry-recorded treatment, and survival.
METHODS: Two complementary analyses used Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End 
Results (SEER) 17 data. Incidence during 2000-2023 was analyzed using Joinpoint 
regression. A clinical cohort diagnosed during 2004-2023 at prespecified stomach 
subsites (C16.1-C16.6, C16.8, and C16.9) was compared across four periods. 
Surgery trends were decomposed into stage-composition and within-stage 
components. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), cause-specific survival 
(CSS), and 36-month restricted mean survival time (RMST); adjusted Cox models 
separately summarized associations over 0-60 months.
RESULTS: The clinical cohort comprised 66,391 tumor records from 66,025 
patients. Incidence declined during 2000-2019 (annual percent change, -1.32%; 
95% CI, -1.61% to -1.08%) and increased during 2019-2023 (4.96%; 95% CI, 
2.51-9.91%). Comparing 2004-2008 with 2019-2023, distant-stage disease increased 
from 36.1% to 43.0%, whereas surgery among records with known surgery status 
decreased from 51.9% to 36.3%. Stage-composition change represented 25.7% of the 
surgery decline. Recorded chemotherapy increased from 35.7% to 54.4%. Median 
potential follow-up was 206.0 versus 27.4 months; latest-period fixed-time 
estimates were reported at 12 and 36 months. Three-year OS increased from 25.2% 
to 29.1% and CSS from 31.4% to 35.6%. Unadjusted 36-month RMST differences were 
1.80 months (95% CI, 1.47-2.15) for OS and 1.86 months (95% CI, 1.53-2.22) for

Comprehensive insights into the toxicological disruption of cadmium to juvenile 
Tachypleus tridentatus: From physiological impairments to multi-omics 
alterations.

Li Y(1), Li G(1), Li Z(1), Hu F(2).

Author information:
(1)State Key Laboratory of Mariculture Breeding, Key Laboratory of Marine 
Biotechnology of Fujian Province, Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University, 
Fuzhou, 350002, China.
(2)State Key Laboratory of Mariculture Breeding, Key Laboratory of Marine 
Biotechnology of Fujian Province, Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University, 
Fuzhou, 350002, China. Electronic address: hufengxiao@fafu.edu.cn.

Cadmium (Cd) is highly toxic to aquatic organisms. This study investigated the 
toxic effects and mechanisms of environmentally relevant Cd concentrations on 
juvenile Tachypleus tridentatus using physiological, biochemical, lipidomic, and 
transcriptomic analyses. After 28 days, 0.5 and 5 μg/L Cd significantly 
inhibited growth, reducing body weight and carapace width. This growth 
retardation was linked to biphasic molting dysregulation, with initial 
suppression and subsequent premature activation of chitinase and β-NAGase, 
disrupting the molting rhythm. Dynamic antioxidant responses were observed: SOD 
increased only in the 0.5 μg/L group at days 7 and 28, while CAT increased at 
day 7 but decreased at day 28 in both Cd treatments. The glutathione-dependent 
pathway was impaired, with no significant MDA elevation. Innate immunity showed 
a time-dependent pattern: ACP decreased at day 7 in the 5 μg/L group but 
increased at day 28 in both treatments; AKP increased at day 28 in both 
treatments; LZM increased at day 7 but decreased at day 28 in both treatments. 
Key immune-related genes (e.g., Dscam, PGRP-SC2, Ctsz) were downregulated. 
Lipidomics analysis revealed a global downregulation of core lipids, including 
triglycerides, diacylglycerols, phosphatidylcholines, and 
phosphatidylethanolamines, indicating disrupted lipid homeostasis and energy 
reserve utilization. Transcriptomic profiling further demonstrated that Cd 
exposure triggered the upregulation of defensive signaling pathways while 
concurrently downregulating genes associated with the cytoskeleton, cathepsins, 
and caspase-independent apoptosis, collectively impairing cellular homeostasis 
and immune function. These findings fill a critical knowledge gap in the 
ecotoxicological risk assessment of this ancient and endangered species under 
subchronic, low-level heavy metal exposure.

vertical migration of MCCPs and SCCPs in surface, bottom seawater, and sediments

identify maritime discharge from shipping lanes and inputs from aquaculture as 
the primary contamination sources. Both MCCPs and SCCPs were ubiquitously found 
across all samples, with higher levels of SCCPs than MCCPs in sediments. Bottom 
seawater exhibited higher CP concentrations than surface seawater, attributing 
to the hydrophobicity-driven sorption to suspended particles and subsequent 
settling/resuspension processes. Sediment-water partitioning and fugacity 
fraction (ff) analyses indicated congener-specific behavior played a key role in 
the vertical migration of CPs. Most CP congeners showed low ff values (<0.2), 
confirming sediments as a primary sink, whereas congeners with shorter carbon 
chain and lower chlorine substitution (e.g., C10Cl5) displayed a potential for 
remobilization, with a mean ff value of 0.897. Ecological risk assessments 
revealed a medium risk in seawater, and a low but persistent risk in sediments. 
These findings highlight the critical roles of hydrodynamics, organic matter, 
and marine anthropogenic emissions in governing CP fate in the NYS coastal 
zones.

Benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) contamination in highly saline environments has received 
increasing attention; however, efficient degradation of BaP by halotolerant

The Pakistani coast holds economic potential through its rich marine resources, 
including a thriving mud crab fishery. However, it faces increasing trace metal 
contamination from both anthropogenic and natural sources. Coastal sediments act 
as reservoirs for these pollutants, facilitating their spread and endangering 
marine ecosystems, marine life, and human health. Hence, effective and 
continuous monitoring is essential to detect potential problems and ensure the 
safety of mud crab (Scylla olivacea) consumption. In order to provide baseline 
data, concentrations of 14 trace metals were measured in 24 sediment samples 
from eight sites and 50 mud crab claws from five sites at the Pakistani coast 
using Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS). The Metal Pollution 
Index (MPI) was highest in Sandspit (75) and Keti Bandar (60). The Ecological 
Risk Index (RI) highlights elevated risks in Khor Kalmat, Sandspit, and Gwadar, 
with values exceeding 60. The Biota Sediment Accumulation Factor (BSAF) 
indicates bioaccumulation, with Zn (10.5) and As (5.5) in Ibrahim Hyderi and 
Sonmiani exceeding the threshold of 1, signalling ecological concerns. Total 
Hazard Index (THI) values were below 1 for all trace metals but were close to 1 
for Hg (0.7) and Cu (0.7). A THI value >1 indicates potential hazard to health 
from trace metal ingestion through consumption of mud crabs. Lifetime cancer 
risk (CR) exceeded the 10-5 threshold for As at all sites and for Cd at Ibrahim 
Hyderi, indicating non-negligible lifetime cancer risk.

Land meets sea: How upland clearing threatens coral reef health in Ambon Bay, 
Maluku Province, Indonesia.

Land-sea interactions play a crucial role in determining coral reef health. 
However, comprehensive evaluations connecting terrestrial disturbances, climatic 
influences, and reef health conditions are limited in small island systems, such 
as Ambon Island, Indonesia. This study examined the effects of upland clearing 
(UC) on coral reef deterioration by conducting a multi-temporal analysis that 
integrated land cover changes with normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) 
data, rainfall variations, and field surveys using the line intercept transect 
(LIT) method and coral reef health index (RHI). The findings revealed a rapid 
increase in bare soil in upland regions, from 31 ha to 2900 ha, whereas dense 
vegetation decreased from 12,389 ha to 8655 ha. This alteration in the landscape 
heightened the erosion risk and sediment transport to coastal waters, with 
sedimentation rates reaching 0.40 g/cm2/day during intense rainfall events, 
exceeding the coral tolerance threshold (0.015 g/cm2/day). The RHI indicated a 
significant decline in reef health over the study period. These results support 
a mechanism in which upland clearing driven by growth increases sediment 
availability, while rainfall variability intensifies transport, contributing to 
sediment-associated stress on coral reef ecosystems. This interaction 
underscores nonlinear land-sea connections. This study advances land-sea 
connectivity by integrating terrestrial and marine data in a ridge-to-reef 
framework, showing that bare soil expansion was negatively correlated with reef 
fish biomass (ρ = -0.90) and the reef health index (ρ = -0.80). Ridge-to-reef 
management considering upstream land-use practices is critical to protect coral 
reefs during increasing climate variability.

Limited post-stress recovery and constrained physiological resilience: 
Multi-biomarker evidence for metabolic trade-offs in a gastropod under ocean 
acidification.

Cheng F(1), Wu X(1), Yang S(1), Tang X(2), Wu Q(3).

Author information:
(1)Hainan Tropical Ocean University, Hainan Academy of Ocean and Fisheries 
Sciences, Hainan Provincial Key Laboratory of Technology for Tropical Seawater 
Aquaculture, Haikou, 571126, China.
(2)Hainan Tropical Ocean University, Hainan Academy of Ocean and Fisheries 
Sciences, Hainan Provincial Key Laboratory of Technology for Tropical Seawater 
Aquaculture, Haikou, 571126, China; Sanya Tropical Fisheries Research Institute, 
Sanya, Hainan, 572000, China. Electronic address: Hn.tangxm@aliyun.com.
(3)Hainan Tropical Ocean University, Hainan Academy of Ocean and Fisheries 
Sciences, Hainan Provincial Key Laboratory of Technology for Tropical Seawater 
Aquaculture, Haikou, 571126, China. Electronic address: wuq199502@163.com.

Ocean acidification (OA), driven by increasing atmospheric CO2 absorption, 
represents a critical environmental stressor that disrupts hepatopancreas 
function in aquatic organisms, particularly affecting metabolic homeostasis and 
immune competence. This study employed an integrated multi-biomarker approach 
combining histopathology, integrated biomarker response (IBR) indices, and 
transcriptomics to systematically investigate the effects of short-term (14 d), 
medium-term (28 d) CO2-driven acidification exposure and a subsequent recovery 
period on the whelk Brunneifusus ternatanus. Hepatopancreatic cells suffered 
progressive structural and functional damage during 14-28 d of acidification, 
characterized by reduced hemocyte counts, disruption of rough endoplasmic 
reticulum membranes, and obscured cell boundaries. During recovery, damage was 
attenuated yet persistent, manifesting as intracellular matrix edema, hemocyte 
rebound, and restored membrane integrity-but cell boundaries remained altered 
relative to controls. The IBR index (integrating oxidative stress markers and 
hepatopancreas function enzyme indices) increased continuously during early and 
medium exposure, then decreased significantly during recovery yet remained 
elevated above control levels, indicating partial but incomplete physiological 
restoration. Transcriptomic analysis revealed time-specific molecular 
reprogramming: energy metabolism and mitochondrial function pathways were 
downregulated during early acidification and recovery stages, whereas 
medium-term exposure significantly activated immunity- and metabolism-associated 
pathways. These findings demonstrate that B. ternatanus mounts vigorous 
physiological regulatory responses to OA stress at a demonstrable energetic 
cost, characterized by immune-metabolic trade-offs and sustained metabolic 
reprogramming even after stress removal. This study provides evidence for 
assessing OA impacts on gastropod mollusks and contributes to predictive 
frameworks for evaluating marine ecosystem vulnerability under climate change.

Stress-induced maternal effects on offspring: linking multivariate egg 
investment to environmental quality.

Mouton JC(1), Gee HK(2), Paitz RT(3), Potticary AL(4), Duckworth RA(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Evolution, Ecology and Organismal Biology, The Ohio State 
University, Columbus, OH, 43210-1293, USA. Electronic address: 
mouton.13@osu.edu.
(2)Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, University of Arizona, 
Tucson, AZ, 85721, USA.
(3)School of Biological Sciences, Illinois State University, Normal, IL, 61790, 
USA.
(4)Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, University of Arizona, 
Tucson, AZ, 85721, USA; Department of Biology, Northern Michigan University, 
Marquette, MI, 49855, USA.

Hormone-mediated maternal effects can shape offspring development in variable 
environmental conditions resulting in adaptive behavioral phenotypes. Numerous 
hormones can vary with environmental conditions and lead to different adaptive 
offspring responses. However, most of what we know about hormone-mediated 
maternal effects comes from studies on individual hormones even though the 
endocrine response to the environment is multifaceted and complex. Physiological 
stress responses in mothers may lead to greater offspring exposure to 
glucocorticoids or influence the allocation of other classes of maternal 
steroids (e.g. androgens, estrogens, progestogens) and any of these hormones may 
induce adaptive responses in offspring. Examining how the multivariate suite of 
yolk hormones responds to ecologically relevant environmental variation in 
natural systems is critical for assessing their role as potential cues of 
environmental conditions. Female western bluebirds (Sialia mexicana) in 
challenging environmental conditions have increased circulating glucocorticoids 
and produce better adapted offspring that are more aggressive and are more 
likely to disperse. We used this well-characterized adaptive maternal effect to 
test the functional importance of multiple classes of steroids using liquid 
chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS-MS). We found that in more challenging 
environments - fewer nest sites, smaller territories - the multivariate yolk 
steroid profile shifted, with the strongest change in glucocorticoid 
metabolites, suggesting that maternal glucocorticoid processing varies with 
ecological context. We also found that estrone and etiocholanolone, but not 
other androgens, covaried with maternal environment. Overall, our results 
advance our understanding of the mechanisms underlying adaptive maternal effects 
in nature and highlight novel steroid pathways that may influence offspring 
phenotypes.

ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent 
endocrine and metabolic disorder among women of reproductive age, currently has 
no definitive treatment. Qigong Wan (QGW), first documented in Yifang Jijie, is 
a classic prescription for infertility in obese women. Given the heterogeneous 
and complex nature of PCOS, Wenjian Qigong Decoction (WJQG), a modified formula 
derived from QGW that incorporates medicinal ingredients from Jiawei Buzhong 
Yiqi Decoction (JWBZYQ), Guishen Wan (GSW), and Jiaotai Wan (JTW), exhibits 
remarkable therapeutic efficacy for obese PCOS in clinical practice. The 
efficacy of all constituent herbs in WJQG has been confirmed, whereas its 
pharmacological mechanisms remain to be clarified.
AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the potential therapeutic benefits of WJQG for 
the treatment of PCOS and provide mechanistic insights into its mode of action.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: An obese PCOS rat model was established via testosterone 
propionate (TP) injection combined with a 45% high-fat diet (HFD). The 
therapeutic efficacy of WJQG, as well as the validity of the model, was 
evaluated by assessing body weight, visceral fat content, estrous cycle, 
clinical chemistry indicators, and histopathology. Furthermore, a comprehensive 
approach integrating ovarian untargeted metabolomics, serum pharmacochemistry , 
network pharmacology, molecular docking, and experimental validation was 
employed to systematically elucidate the potential mechanism of action of WJQG 
in treating obese PCOS.
RESULTS: WJQG significantly attenuated body weight gain, reduced abdominal 
visceral fat, restored estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian morphology, and 
corrected hyperandrogenemia and endocrine dysregulation in obese PCOS rats. 
Serum pharmacochemistry identified 22 bioactive prototype compounds absorbed 
into the blood. Network pharmacology predicted hub targets including TNF, IL6, 
CASP3, and PTGS2. Subsequent molecular docking simulations indicated favorable 
binding affinities between these proteins and representative prototype 
constituents such as narirutin, ginsenoside Rc, and hyperoside. Untargeted 
metabolomics suggested that WJQG substantially remodeled the ovarian metabolome, 
specifically suppressing the hyperactivated arachidonic acid metabolism pathway 
and downregulating downstream pro-inflammatory lipid mediators (PGF2α, PGA2, 
PGE2, and 10,11-dihydro-20-hydroxy-LTB4). Mechanistically, WJQG inhibited the 
enzymatic cascade of p-cPLA2, COX-2 (encoded by PTGS2), and 5-LOX. Meanwhile, 
WJQG treatment was associated with restored ADPN/PPARα/p-AMPK signaling, a 
predominance of M2-type macrophages, a suppressed NLRP3/NF-κB inflammatory 
cascade accompanied by reduced TNF-α and IL-6 levels, and alleviated 
granulosa-cell apoptosis alongside decreased caspase-3 activation.
CONCLUSIONS: WJQG alleviates key disease manifestations in obese PCOS rats, 
which correlates with modulation of the interconnected pathological triad of 
intra-ovarian arachidonic acid metabolism hyperactivation, chronic inflammation, 
and granulosa-cell apoptosis. These findings provide supportive scientific 
evidence and pharmacodynamic rationale to support further pre-clinical 
investigation of WJQG as a potential integrative therapeutic candidate for PCOS.

Wang X(1), Zhang J(1), Ding T(1), Liao X(2), Ahn J(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Food Science and Nutrition, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou,

(2)Department of Food Science and Nutrition, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou,

This study characterizes genomic and phenotypic diversity among Vibrio 
parahaemolyticus isolates from shrimp aquaculture by integrating phenotypic 
profiling with pangenomic analysis. Growth was quantified under temperature, 
salinity, pH, nutrient, and ethanol stresses, together with motility, hemolysis, 
and antibiotic susceptibility. Core-genome SNP phylogeny identified genetic 
differentiation among representative isolates, with relationships not 
consistently associated with sampling location, sample type, or collection 
period. Comparative genomics showed variation in accessory-gene composition and 
isolate-specific distributions of blaCARB variants, whereas tet(34), tet(35), 
and several motility and chemotaxis genes were widely detected. Phenotypic 
assays showed isolate- and condition-dependent variation in stress responses, 
antimicrobial susceptibility, hemolysis, and motility. Neither tdh nor trh was 
detected by PCR or WGS-based screening. No clear hemolytic zones were observed 
on Columbia blood agar, whereas Ref, 1P1, 2P2, 3P2, 4 M2, and 4 N2 showed 
hemolytic activity on Wagatsuma agar, indicating a discrepancy between the 
Wagatsuma phenotype and molecular detection of these hemolysin genes. Isolate 
1 M1 exhibited greater swimming without increased swarming activity. 
Accessory-genome principal coordinate analysis (PCoA) and phenotypic principal 
component analysis (PCA) showed partial correspondence between genomic and 
phenotypic relationships. The close accessory-genome relationship between 2P2 
and 3P2 was not reflected phenotypically, whereas 2Q2 and 3P2 showed phenotypic 
similarity despite greater accessory-genome separation. These contrasting 
relationships indicate that accessory-gene presence and absence alone did not 
reproduce the measured multivariate phenotypic patterns. These findings indicate 
that genomic and phenotypic variation represent related but non-equivalent 
dimensions of strain-level diversity and support integrated genomic and 
phenotypic characterization for surveillance in aquaculture environments.

INTRODUCTION: Blood culture contamination (BCC) is an important diagnostic

changes in BCC rates before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic using 
patient-month Poisson generalized estimating equations (GEE).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included blood culture sets 
obtained at a tertiary hospital in Japan from April 2017 to June 2025. Eligible 
episodes had at least two sets drawn within 24 h. Interrupted time-series 
analysis estimated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for level and slope changes at 
pandemic and post-reclassification transitions, with the number of sets as an 
offset and adjustment for seasonality and within-patient correlation.
RESULTS: Among 85,955 blood culture sets, 84,213 sets from 41,732 episodes in 
23,705 patients were analyzed. Crude BCC rates were 1.05%, 1.55%, and 1.49% in 
the prepandemic, pandemic, and post-reclassification periods. No significant 
overall level or slope changes were observed: prepandemic-to-pandemic 
level-change IRR, 1.23 (95% CI, 0.93-1.62); slope-change IRR, 1.00 (95% CI, 
0.99-1.01); pandemic-to-post-reclassification level-change IRR, 0.88 (95% CI, 
0.68-1.14); and slope-change IRR, 0.99 (95% CI, 0.98-1.01). Exploratory subgroup 
analyses suggested setting-specific post-reclassification changes in the 
intensive care unit. Sensitivity analyses were generally consistent, although 
the Omicron-era breakpoint analysis suggested sensitivity to breakpoint 
specification.
CONCLUSION: Patient-month Poisson GEE-based analysis showed that crude increases 
in BCC rates were not accompanied by statistically significant overall level or 
slope changes after accounting for repeated patient-level sampling and 
seasonality. Crude BCC trends should therefore be interpreted cautiously in 
longitudinal microbiology surveillance.

Experimental study on the radon barrier performance of cover materials under 
frozen and unfrozen isothermal conditions.

Ye Y(1), Huang A(2), Yu T(2), Mou S(2).

Author information:
(1)School of Resources Environment and Safety Engineering, University of South 
China, Hengyang, 421001, China; Key Discipline Laboratory for National Defense

Seasonal temperature variations, particularly frozen and unfrozen conditions, 
exert a considerable influence on radon exhalation from the surfaces of uranium 
tailings impoundments. To evaluate the radon barrier performance of cover 
materials under frozen and unfrozen isothermal conditions, three indoor-cured 
materials-pure laterite, a laterite-bentonite mixture (1:1 mass ratio), and a 
laterite-zeolite powder mixture (1:1 mass ratio)-were tested across five 
temperature setpoints (-20 °C, -10 °C, 0 °C, 10 °C, and 20 °C) in a 
temperature-controlled test chamber, using bare uranium tailings as a control. 
The results indicate that: (1) At a cover thickness of 15 cm, the radon barrier 
efficiencies of pure laterite, the laterite-zeolite powder mixture, and the 
laterite-bentonite mixture ranged from 89.07% to ∼100%, 81.99% to ∼100%, and 
98.59% to ∼100%, respectively, with barrier efficiency gradually increasing as 
temperature decreased. (2) For all materials, the rate of change in radon 
barrier efficiency with temperature was lower above 0 °C than below 0 °C. The 
temperature sensitivity followed the order: laterite-zeolite powder 
mixture > pure laterite > laterite-bentonite mixture, demonstrating that the 
laterite-bentonite mixture maintained the most stable performance across thermal 
fluctuations. Additionally, preliminary empirical piecewise equations were 
established to describe the relationship between barrier efficiency and 
temperature across frozen and unfrozen regimes. Overall, this study demonstrates 
that radon exhalation barrier by cover materials depends not only on their 
intrinsic physical properties and ambient temperature, but also exhibits 
distinct behavioral shifts between frozen and unfrozen states.

Hyperosmotic stress in renal tubular epithelial cells promotes TFEB-dependent 
autophagy in interstitial fibroblasts by involving extracellular glutamate.

Miyano T(1), Yamagishi Y(2), Sakamoto N(3), Sera T(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Medical and Robotic Engineering Design, Tokyo University of 
Science, Tokyo, Japan; Department of Mechanical Systems Engineering, Graduate 
School of Systems Design, Tokyo Metropolitan University, Tokyo, Japan. 
Electronic address: miyanot@rs.tus.ac.jp.
(2)Department of Legal Medicine, Graduate School of Medicine, Chiba University, 
Chiba, Japan.
(3)Department of Mechanical Systems Engineering, Graduate School of Systems 
Design, Tokyo Metropolitan University, Tokyo, Japan.
(4)Department of Medical and Robotic Engineering Design, Tokyo University of 
Science, Tokyo, Japan. Electronic address: toshihiro.sera@rs.tus.ac.jp.

Renal tubular epithelial-interstitial fibroblast communication maintains kidney 
homeostasis but promotes disease when dysregulated. Tubular epithelial cells 
undergo large physiological osmotic fluctuations; however, it remains unclear 
whether epithelial hyperosmotic stress sends signals to neighboring fibroblasts. 
Herein, we examined how epithelial hyperosmotic stress regulates fibroblast 
autophagy and transcription factor EB (TFEB) activity. We used a Transwell 
co-culture system with rat proximal tubular epithelial cells (NRK-52E) and renal 
interstitial fibroblasts (NRK-49F), which allowed evaluation of the paracrine 
effect on fibroblasts mediated by tubular epithelial cells. Hyperosmotic stress 
in epithelial cells induced the robust nuclear translocation of TFEB in 
fibroblasts, increased the expression of lysosomal and autophagy-related genes, 
and enhanced autophagic flux without altering fibroblast viability or 
proliferation. Although fibroblasts internalized epithelial-derived 
extracellular vesicles, they did not activate TFEB, suggesting an extracellular 
vesicles-independent mechanism. RNA sequencing revealed that hyperosmotic stress 
markedly alters the expression of epithelial solute carrier genes, particularly 
those encoding amino acid transporters. Analysis of amino acid metabolism 
revealed corresponding changes in conditioned media, including an increase in 
extracellular glutamate. Glutamate alone induced TFEB nuclear translocation and 
autophagy activation in fibroblasts. Both epithelial hyperosmotic co-culture and 
glutamate treatment activated AMP-activated protein kinase and inhibited mTORC1 
signaling, thereby enabling TFEB activation. These results identify 
extracellular glutamate as a metabolite-based paracrine signal that couples 
epithelial osmotic stress with TFEB-dependent autophagy in interstitial 
fibroblasts.

BACKGROUND: We aimed to examine ICU professionals' perceptions, opinions, and 
understanding of post-mortem organ donation, and their associations with 
personal and professional experiences.
METHODS: Between October 2024 and April 2025, we conducted a cross-sectional 
survey in three Swiss ICUs, assessing perceptions, beliefs, and understanding of 
organ donation (primary endpoints), and their relationship with demographic 
characteristics and professional experiences (secondary endpoints). Emotional 
and ethical perspectives were rated using Likert scales.
RESULTS: Among 338 professionals (median age 39 years; 75% women; 80% nurses; 
median ICU experience 15 years), most had cared for brain dead organ donors, and 
understanding/approval were high. While 75% would accept organs, 70% were open 
and 41% fully committed to donating; "helping others" motivated 30.7% of the 
open and 13.9% of the committed. Reluctance stemmed from dignity concerns, 
doubts on brain death, or fear to burden relatives. Lower willingness to donate 
correlated with higher age (ρ = -0.309), longer ICU experience (ρ = -0.335), and 
belief in life after death (ρ = -0.168), while approval of the brain death 
concept was positively correlated (ρ = 0.253; all p ≤ 0.002); physicians were 
more willing than nurses (10 vs. 9; p = 0.001), and willingness aligned with 
wishing to receive organs (10 vs. 2; p < 0.001). The latter was linked to lower 
age (36 vs. 50), fewer ICU years (13 vs. 28), stronger wish to donate (10 vs. 
2), and better understanding of brain death (10 vs. 9; all p = 0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Swiss ICU professionals support organ donation, though strong 
commitment to donate their own organs is limited and helping others was not 
reported as a predominant motivation.

BACKGROUND: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has demonstrated substantial clinical 
benefit in patients with advanced human epidermal growth factor receptor 2

events-particularly interstitial lung disease (ILD) or pneumonitis-represent a 
clinically relevant limitation. While UGT1A1 polymorphisms influence toxicity

T-DXd-related toxicity appears limited. The PROCURE project aimed to investigate 
germline pharmacogenetic variants beyond UGT1A1 associated with T-DXd-induced 
ILD.

conducted across 26 Spanish institutions. Germline DNA from patients with 
advanced HER2-positive or HER2-low breast cancer treated with T-DXd was 
genotyped using the Infinium Global Diversity Array enriched for pharmacogenomic 
variants. A candidate gene approach was applied to 14 genes involved in drug 
metabolism, transport, pharmacodynamics, and immune-mediated drug 
hypersensitivity. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations 
with ILD/pneumonitis.

in the analysis. The median age was 58 years (range, 34-94 years). After a 
median follow-up of 18.3 months [95% confidence interval (CI): 15.4-20.5], the

signals mapped to variants within the human leukocyte antigen (HLA) region, with 
the top single nucleotide polymorphism near HLA-F (rs9258213; OR 6.8, 95% CI 
2.6-17.9, P = 9.5 × 10-5). Additional associations were observed in SLCO1B1 and 
CYP3A4, genes involved in T-DXd transport and metabolism.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies host genetic variation within the HLA locus 
and drug pharmacokinetic pathways as potential contributors to T-DXd-induced ILD 
in patients with advanced breast cancer. Although no definitive pharmacogenomic 
predictor was identified, these findings provide insights into the biological 
mechanisms underlying this toxicity and support further investigation of 
pharmacogenomic biomarkers to improve risk stratification and guide personalized 
T-DXd therapy.

Cryopreservation of chicken feather follicle-derived cells using chicken 
serum-based media: broadening cellular diversity in avian biobanking.

Mota BD(1), Facciotti PR(1), Pieri NCG(1), da Silva CGB(2), de Souza Munhoz 
LL(1), Netto RGF(3), Martínez SEB(3), Muñoz BXM(3), da Silva VC(1), Ambrósio 
CE(2), Martins DDS(4).

Author information:
(1)Immunohistochemistry and Experimental Physiology Laboratory, School of Animal 
Science and Food Engineering, University of São Paulo, Pirassununga, São Paulo, 
Brazil.
(2)Stem Cell Culture and Gene Therapy Laboratory, School of Animal Science and 
Food Engineering, University of São Paulo, Pirassununga, São Paulo, Brazil.
(3)Poultry Nutrition Laboratory, School of Animal Science and Food Engineering, 
University of São Paulo, Pirassununga, São Paulo, Brazil.
(4)Immunohistochemistry and Experimental Physiology Laboratory, School of Animal 
Science and Food Engineering, University of São Paulo, Pirassununga, São Paulo,

Feather follicles are dynamic and heterogeneous mini-organs containing 
epithelial, mesenchymal, pigmentary, and progenitor cell populations. However, 
cryopreservation studies have focused mainly on fibroblasts, and other 
follicular populations remain poorly explored. This study aimed to establish 
favorable cryopreservation conditions for cells isolated from growing feathers 
of Gallus gallus domesticus using chicken serum. Primary cultures were assessed 
by morphology, differentiation-associated staining, and reverse transcription 
quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Cells were cryopreserved for 
60 days in media containing 10% or 80% chicken serum combined with 5%, 7.5%, or 
10% dimethyl sulfoxide (Me2SO). Post-thaw cell status was evaluated by Annexin 
V/propidium iodide flow cytometry immediately after thawing and after 72 h of 
recovery, and metabolic activity was assessed using a colorimetric tetrazolium 
assay. Cultures progressively became dominated by small, rounded cells arranged 
in compact colonies. Morphological and molecular findings were consistent with 
preferential maintenance of a population displaying epithelial-associated 
characteristics after culture and cryopreservation. Media containing 80% chicken 
serum produced more favorable post-thaw outcomes than media containing 10%, with 
lower late apoptosis immediately after thawing, greater metabolic recovery, and 
higher retention of adherent cells. Serum concentration accounted for 77.87% of 
the variation in metabolic activity and had a stronger effect than Me2SO 
concentration. Overall, the 80% chicken serum formulations containing 5% or 7.5% 
Me2SO showed the most consistent recovery across the evaluated endpoints. These 
findings support the use of chicken serum-based media for cryopreservation of 
feather follicle-derived cells and broaden the range of cellular resources 
available for avian biobanking and conservation-oriented biotechnologies.

Effects of cryopreservation on the viability and function of Larimichthys crocea

Chen J(1), Chen M(1), Sun Z(2), Han K(1), Zhou L(3).

Author information:
(1)Ningde Engineering Research Center of Mindong Aquatic Product

352100, China.
(2)Ningde Yiye Marine Industry Development Co., Ltd., Ningde, 352100, China.
(3)Ningde Engineering Research Center of Mindong Aquatic Product 
Deep-Processing, College of Ocean Studies, Ningde Normal University, Ningde, 
352100, China. Electronic address: zhoulisdta@163.com.

Cryopreservation of mature fish eggs and embryos remain major barriers to the 
preservation of maternal genetic information because of their large size and 
high yolk content. This study developed a cryopreservation protocol for ovarian 
tissue from juvenile large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) to preserve 
oogonial stem cells as an alternative approach. A screening of permeable and 
non-permeable cryoprotectants, alone and in combination, was performed using a 
simple two-step freezing procedure (-80°C for 1 h followed by liquid nitrogen 
immersion). Post-thaw cell viability was assessed by trypan blue exclusion, and 
the optimal combination of 10% Me2SO, 15% PG, and 15% FBS was identified, 
yielding the highest viability of 72.12 ± 8.87%. Histology revealed that oogonia 
and Perinucleolus stage oocytes maintained intact morphology 
post-cryopreservation, whereas vitellogenic oocytes sustained significant 
cryodamage, including oolemma shrinkage, vacuolization, and rupture. qRT-PCR 
results further revealed upregulated germline stem cell markers of vasa, klf4, 
oct4, and nanos2, alongside downregulated sycp3 and nanog gene, suggesting that 
the high viability of oogonia, which consistent with the results of histology. 
In addition, ccnd1, rhoA, and cirbpa exhibited reduced transcript levels and 
hsp70 showed elevated levels, indicating that cryopreservation is associated 
with altered expression of genes involved in cell cycle regulation, cytoskeletal 
signaling, and stress response. Finally, functional validation via 
intraperitoneal transplantation into 12 dpf larvae confirmed that cryopreserved 
oogonia retained the abilities to migrate and colonize on the genital ridge at 
15 days post-transplantation. The study established cryopreservation protocol of 
ovarian tissue that can effectively safeguard the oogonial stem cells, providing 
a feasible approach for conservation of maternal germplasm in L. crocea and 
serving as a valuable reference for germplasm conservation of other economically 
important and endangered fish species.

The development of innovative photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensing strategies with 
exceptional selectivity and operational efficiency holds paramount strategic 
importance for advancing the frontiers of PEC technology. In this work, we 
present a novel congruent intercalation-induced symmetry breaking strategy to 
construct a highly selective PEC analysis platform. The near-perfect dimensional 
match between the ionic diameter of iodide (I-, 4.40 Å) and the interlayer 
spacing of BiOIO3 (4.41 Å) enables selective intercalation of I- while 
effectively excluding analogous halide ions (Br-, Cl-, and F-). This unique 
intercalation process induces charge distribution symmetry breaking around the 
IO3 motifs, resulting in a remarkable enhancement of the macroscopic 
polarization electric field in BiOIO3 and consequently amplifying photocurrent 
generation. The proposed system achieves ultrasensitive I- detection with an 
outstanding detection limit of 0.06 μM (S/N = 3), while maintaining exceptional 
selectivity. Furthermore, the PEC assay demonstrates superior operational 
efficiency, featuring a simplified workflow and rapid response time (3 min). 
This study offers a promising approach to induce symmetry breaking through 
spontaneous intercalation of exogenous species, circumventing the harsh 
high-temperature/pressure conditions typically required for chemical bond 
cleavage in conventional doping methods. The proposed strategy offers distinct 
advantages, including low energy consumption, mild operational conditions, and 
fast kinetics. More significantly, the introduction of symmetry breaking opens a 
new avenue for exploration of PEC sensing mechanisms, demonstrating broad 
application prospects and considerable potential for future development in 
advanced PEC systems.

Byrne T(1), Zapata A(2), Smithing F(2), MacLeod J(2), Xiao Z(2), Pickert J(2),

Author information:
(1)Laboratory for Phenomenological Research, Coordinated Science Lab, University

Studies of cancer survivorship and social media have treated survivors as 
audiences of online cancer content, examining how cancer survivors receive 
support and information from what others post. This study, in contrast, shifts 
attention from the consumption of online cancer content to its creation. In this 
article, we employed a theory-led phenomenological approach to examine how 
creating cancer content on social media did not merely represent survivorship, 
but - in participants' accounts - substantially transformed their embodied 
experience of illness. Drawing on interviews conducted between January and May 
2026 with 18 cancer content creators in the United States and Europe, findings 
revealed three ways participants described content creation as reshaping how 
they lived with cancer. 1) Becoming recognizable showed how participants 
described their own public cancer brands as becoming part of their 
self-understanding. 2) Becoming believable showed how participants - who 
reported that followers doubted whether they really had cancer - came to 
experience visible bodily changes and clinical spaces as evidence that could 
prove their illness was real. 3) Becoming valuable revealed how participants 
perceived suffering and medical crisis as drawing greater audience attention 
than recovery - creating a paradox in their experience of healing. Namely, as 
participants recovered and audience attention appeared to decline, some 
participants came to feel less valuable. Building on these findings, this study 
demonstrates that social media is not only a repository of cancer information, 
but a lived cancer environment in which survivorship itself takes shape.

Zanini MT(1), Kikuchi M(2).

Author information:

Public health emergencies confront officials with the challenge of communicating 
guidance that evolves as scientific evidence and institutional recommendations 
change. Although institutional trust is associated with adherence to public 
health measures, less is known about the interpretive and communicative work 
through which public officials seek to make changing guidance understandable, 
legitimate, and credible. Drawing on a comparative qualitative study of Brazil 
and Japan, this article examines trust-building communication among public 
officials involved in implementation, coordination, and policy oversight. The 
study is based on 122 semi-structured interviews and a 239-document corpus 
covering 2020-2022. Using abductive comparative analysis, we identify Public 
Health Sensegiving as the process through which officials interpret evolving 
scientific and institutional guidance and translate it into public-facing 
explanations. Empirical episodes show a recurrent sequence in which officials 
interpret ambiguous guidance, communicate workable explanations, and refine them

explaining and translating guidance, contextualizing risk and uncertainty, 
legitimizing recommendations, and encouraging voluntary cooperation. Comparisons 
within and across countries show that competing messages increased the need for 
reconciliation, whereas more consistent messaging allowed greater emphasis on 
continuity and shared responsibility. These differences reflect contextual 
communicative demands rather than fixed national types. Rather than 
demonstrating changes in citizens' trust or behaviour, the findings identify how

New horizons in cooking and mealtime interventions for mild cognitive impairment

Bannon SM(1), Elizalde Carrillo R(2), McCage S(2), Shahab MH(2), Allison GO(2), 
Aminpour A(2), Levinson C(3), Presciutti AM(2), Fishel A(4).

Author information:
(1)Brain Injury Research Center, Department of Rehabilitation Medicine and Human 
Performance, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai Hospital, New York, NY, 
United States of America. Electronic address: Sarah.bannon@mountsinai.org.
(2)Brain Injury Research Center, Department of Rehabilitation Medicine and Human 
Performance, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai Hospital, New York, NY,

(3)Gustave L. and Janet W. Levy Library, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

(4)Department of Psychiatry, Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, MA, United

BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRDs) are increasingly 
common conditions that are highly disruptive to individuals and families. ADRDs 
impact cognition and can undermine a person's ability to participate in cooking, 
preparing meals, and engaging in conversations. Mealtime participation 
implicates key determinants of adequate nutritional intake and social 
connectedness. However, engaging in mealtime routines amid challenges can also 
exacerbate the stress and burden felt by family caregivers. Behavioral 
interventions can mitigate these downstream impacts, though they are currently 
underdeveloped.
OBJECTIVE: To summarize the literature on cooking and mealtime interventions for 
community-dwelling people with dementia and their caregivers.
DESIGN: Scoping review.
METHODS: We searched databases up to May 2025 for English-language publications 
that described qualitative and quantitative research surrounding interventions 
focused on cooking and mealtime interventions for individuals living with 
subjective cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment, and ADRDs. At least two 
reviewers independently identified publications and extracted population 
characteristics, intervention components, and intervention outcomes. Included 
articles were published between 2007-2024.
RESULTS: Qualitative and mixed methods studies (n=12) highlighted potential 
mechanisms for intervention, including cultivating routines for mealtimes (e.g., 
eating together, minimizing distractions, adaptive tools) and caregiver coping 
skills and training (e.g., distress tolerance, communication to emphasize 
respect/dignity, and social routines). Intervention studies (n=10) included 
caregiver skills training, education and cognitive rehabilitation-integrated 
cooking. Interventions were generally feasible; however, few were evaluated in 
randomized trials, and none underwent efficacy testing.
CONCLUSION: Cooking and mealtime interventions hold promise for addressing 
determinants of aging in ADRDs, though further randomized controlled efficacy 
trials are needed.
