A Recipe for Better Diabetes Management: The DASH4D Dietary Pattern.

Selvin E(1)(2)(3), Sullivan V(1)(3), Yeh HC(2)(3), Fang M(1)(3), Pilla S(2)(3), 
Mitchell C(1)(3), Appel L(1)(2)(3), Rebholz C(1)(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Epidemiology, Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, 
Baltimore, MD.
(2)Division of General Internal Medicine, Department of Medicine, Johns Hopkins 
School of Medicine, Baltimore, MD.
(3)Welch Center for Prevention, Epidemiology and Clinical Research, Johns 
Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD.

The 2026 American Diabetes Association "Standards of Care in Diabetes" includes 
extensive nutrition recommendations for people with diabetes but stops short of 
recommending a specific dietary pattern. Instead, the guidelines recommend that 
all patients be referred for individualized nutrition therapy. This approach 
appropriately acknowledges diverse patient needs; however, it is difficult for 
providers to deliver any form of individualized dietary guidance without a clear 
starting point to guide them. In this article we examine the tension between the 
needs for individualization and evidence-based nutritional standards in diabetes 
care. We argue that the DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) dietary 
pattern stands out as being supported by decades of evidence from rigorous 
randomized clinical trials, meta-analyses, and large observational studies that 
have established its benefit for cardiovascular health. We summarize the 
recently completed DASH for Diabetes (DASH4D) trial, which demonstrated that a 
modified version of the original DASH eating plan, adapted for adults with 
diabetes, significantly reduced blood pressure and improved glycemic control in 
participants with type 2 diabetes and hypertension. We conclude that while 
individualized dietary counseling remains the standard of care, the DASH4D diet

Disenfranchised Grief: The Silent Price of Minimising Negative Behaviours in 
Nursing.

Cleary M(1), West S(2), Jackson D(3), Kornhaber R(4).

Author information:
(1)School of Nursing and Midwifery, Faculty of Health, University of Technology 
Sydney, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia.
(2)School of Health - Nursing, University of New England, Armidale, New South 
Wales, Australia.
(3)Susan Wakil School of Nursing, University of Sydney, Camperdown, New South 
Wales, Australia.
(4)School of Nursing and Midwifery, Adelaide University, Adelaide, South 
Australia, Australia.

Workplace bullying can damage nurses' mental health, professional identity, 
relationships, psychological safety, and belonging. When these losses are 
unsupported, the associated grief may become disenfranchised. This discursive 
paper examines bullying, exclusion, professional undermining, vexatious 
complaints, and weaponised complaints through a grief-informed lens. It proposes 
that workplace harm can create losses of trust, reputation, career opportunity, 
safety, identity, and belonging. Bullying does not inevitably produce grief, but 
grief may arise when valued aspects of professional life are damaged and may 
become disenfranchised when colleagues or organisations do not recognise it. 
This connection has received limited attention in nursing. Organisational 
responses may compound the harm when nurses are minimised, silenced, isolated, 
or expected to recover without acknowledgement. A grief-informed response 
requires listening, validation, psychosocial support, fair processes, protection 
from retaliation, leadership accountability, and opportunities for restoration. 
For mental health nursing, this perspective supports non-pathologising 
assessment, therapeutic acknowledgement, referral, and attention to how 
workplace grief may intersect with psychological distress, mental ill health, 
wellbeing, professional functioning, and safe care. It directs attention beyond 
resilience to organisational conditions that produce or prolong harm. 
Recognising these losses may strengthen nurses' wellbeing, help-seeking, 
speaking up, workforce retention, and patient care.

Relationships Among Physical Activity, Functional Fitness, and Cognitive Task 
Performance in Adults with Down Syndrome.

Ballenger BK(1), Haider M(2), Motl RW(3), Fernhall B(4), Agiovlasitis S(2).

Author information:
(1)Transylvania University.
(2)Mississippi State University.
(3)University of Illinois Chicago.
(4)University of Massachusetts.

Physical activity (PA) and functional fitness (FF) are associated with cognitive 
task performance in the general population; however, such relationships remain 
understudied in adults with Down syndrome (DS). The purpose of this study was to 
examine associations among moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA), FF, and cognitive 
task performance, and explore whether FF may statistically account for 
associations between MVPA and cognitive task performance. Thirty-seven adults 
with DS (35 ± 10 years) completed the Timed-Up-and-Go (TUG) and handgrip 
strength (HGS) tests to assess FF, and the Eriksen Flanker Task (FT) to assess 
cognitive task performance. MVPA was measured by an accelerometer device over 7 
days. Pearson's correlation indicated that MVPA was significantly associated 
with TUG (r = -.52, p < .001) and the Flanker effect (r = -.32, p = .047). TUG 
was associated with FT accuracy (r = -.44, p = .006) and Flanker effect 
(r = .33, p = .048). Exploratory mediation analysis suggested that TUG 
performance may partly explain an indirect association between MVPA and FT 
accuracy, with higher MVPA associated with better FF (i.e. lower TUG time) 
(β = -.48, p = .003), and better FF was also associated with greater FT accuracy 
(β = -.52, p = .008). Both MVPA and FF are associated with components of 
cognitive task performance in adults with DS. Mobility‑related FF showed an 
exploratory indirect association between MVPA and FT accuracy, suggesting that 
FF may represent a potential pattern of associations among PA and components of 
cognitive task performance in this population.

Osteoarthritis and arthritis related pain can lead to functional limitation, 
reduced mobility, and poorer quality of life. This systematic review examined

with osteoarthritis or arthritis related pain in routine care and perioperative 
settings. The review followed PRISMA 2020 and searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase,

Makhmudah S(1), Shatri H(2), Jongsma MLA(3), Wahyu Yuniarti K(1).

Chronic non-cancer pain requires multimodal management, and clinical hypnosis 
has been examined as a complementary intervention. This PRISMA ScR scoping 
review mapped the extent and characteristics of the evidence base, intervention 
features, and research gaps for clinical hypnosis in chronic non-cancer pain. We 
included 48 intervention studies involving 3,166 participants, encompassing 
randomized controlled trials and other study designs. Hypnosis was applied to

frequent use of passive comparators, limited demographic reporting and 
diversity, and variable intervention reporting. This review extends prior 
syntheses by detailing how clinical hypnosis has been operationalized for 
chronic non-cancer pain and by identifying methodological and reporting gaps to 
guide future research.

Quantitative Analysis of Electroencephalography in Hypnosis: A 
Neurophysiological Approach.

Baghdadi G(1), Motie Nasrabadi A(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biomedical Engineering, Amirkabir University of Technology, 
Tehran, Iran.
(2)Department of Biomedical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Shahed 
University, Tehran, Iran.

Hypnosis is a unique state of consciousness marked by heightened response to 
suggestions, focused attention, and altered cognitive control. This article 
explores the neural connections involved in hypnosis through 
electroencephalography (EEG) studies, examining brain changes during hypnosis 
and their relationship to hypnotic depth and susceptibility. Theta waves, linked 
to hypnotic depth, are stronger in highly hypnotizable individuals, while gamma 
waves are associated with focus, suggestion acceptance, and emotional responses. 
Hypnosis also induces frequency-dependent reorganization of large-scale brain 
connectivity, particularly in frontal-parietal and attentional networks, 
enhancing subjective experiences and responsiveness. EEG patterns reveal more 
dynamic neural activity during hypnosis, which cannot be captured by linear 
metrics alone. Hemispheric analysis shows greater left-hemisphere activity in 
highly hypnotizable individuals, particularly in emotionally and verbally 
mediated tasks, challenging the right-hemisphere dominance model. Event related 
potential (ERP) findings show that hypnosis affects information processing at 
both pre-attentional and cognitive levels. These insights contribute to 
understanding hypnosis' impact on the brain and its potential for personalized 
therapeutic interventions.

Although acetone in exhaled breath is a reliable biomarker for diabetes 
mellitus, its trace-level detection under high-humidity conditions remains 
challenging for early noninvasive diagnosis. In this study, Au-loaded ZnO 
nanocages derived from ZIF-8 were synthesized. The 0.4 wt % Au/ZnO-based sensor

provide new insights into the activation of active sites by noble metal loading

various liver diseases. Compared with conventional pharmacological and surgical 
therapies, natural antioxidant enzymes represent promise for liver disease 
therapy due to high ROS scavenging and low immunogenicity. However, their 
clinical translation is limited by instability and complex preparation. 
Antioxidant nanozymes not only mimic natural enzymes, but possess advantages 
including simple structure, low cost and high stability. They have emerged as 
ideal therapeutic options for liver diseases by mitigating OS, modulating 
inflammation, and remodeling the pathological microenvironment. This review 
innovatively elucidates hepatic OS pathogenesis from a synergistic perspective, 
integrating indirect (inflammatory pathways) and direct (organelle stress,

literature. Subsequently, we systematically summarize advances in five

and metal-organic frameworks (MOF)-based, and emphasize catalytic mechanisms and 
activity regulation strategies to guide the design of effective, low-toxicity 
antioxidant nanozymes. Furthermore, this review highlights recent progress of 
antioxidant nanozymes in typical liver diseases, including drug-induced liver 
injury, hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury, liver fibrosis, and acute liver 
failure, alongside clinical translation bottlenecks. Finally, current challenges 
and future perspectives for antioxidant nanozymes are outlined.

long-term durability, and charge-storage functionality, yet hydrated tungsten

repeated ion insertion/extraction. Here, we present a carbon nitride-driven 
phase transformation strategy for a durable energy-storing electrochromic 
hydrated tungsten oxide. Under mild hydrogen annealing, orthorhombic WO3·H2O

rearrangement while providing nitrogen-rich Li+-interactive sites that regulate

Strobel OR(1), Xia H(2), Ropa JP(3), Strand DW(4), Jerde TJ(1), Arrizabalaga

(1)Department of Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, & Pharmacology, Indiana

(3)Department of Medical & Molecular Genetics, Indiana University School of

(4)Department of Urology, UT Southwestern Medical Center, Dallas, Texas, USA.
(5)Department of Microbiology and Immunology, Jacobs School of Medicine &

BACKGROUND: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and lower urinary tract symptoms 
are strongly associated with chronic prostate inflammation and stromal 
remodeling, yet the stromal cell programs that emerge during inflammatory, 
nodular remodeling remain incompletely defined. A Toxoplasma gondii infection 
model produces persistent inflammation and nodular formations, providing an 
experimentally tractable system to map inflammation-linked stromal states.
METHODS: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of prostates from control and 
chronically infected male CBA/J mice harvested at 28 days post-infection (DPI). 
Stromal subset reprogramming was assessed by cluster-resolved pseudobulk 
differential expression and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. Stromal expansion and 
Cd52+ fibroblast subset changes were validated by whole-section 
immunofluorescence at 28 and 60 DPI using a CellposeSAM-based tissue cytometry 
pipeline. To assess human relevance, CD52+ fibroblasts were evaluated in FFPE

immune, and seminal vesicle compartments. Infection increased immune-cell

Law KL(1), de Mille P(2), Prather H(2), Skolnik H(2), Chiaia TA(2), Lewis CL(3),

(4)Weill Cornell Medical College, New York, NY.
(5)National Chung Hsing University, Taichung, TAIWAN.

PURPOSE: To describe the career and post-career surgeries in female elite-level 
soccer players and evaluate their association with long-term musculoskeletal 
health.
STUDY DESIGN: This is a cross-sectional study.
METHODS: Surgical data (the number and type of surgeries during and after the 
career) from an anonymous online survey was obtained from a previously published 
cohort of 560 retired elite women's soccer players. Correlation coefficients 
were used to evaluate the relationship between the number of surgeries and 
physical activity levels (UCLA activity scale), joint function (SANE), and 
physical and mental health (PROMIS-10), which were all collected on the same 
survey.

number of post-career surgeries was 0.5 (SD=1). The most common career surgery

(4%). The most common knee procedures involved ligament reconstruction, 
primarily of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), followed by meniscus and 
cartilage surgery. The most frequent post-career surgery sites were knee 
(24.0%), foot/ankle (5.1%), and leg (3.2%). Knee ligament and meniscus surgeries 
were equally reported. More career and post-career surgeries were associated

associated with lower UCLA activity levels.

suggesting a possible association with long-term musculoskeletal impairment, 
particularly to the knee, in a cohort of mostly White collegiate former players.

and activity levels after retirement, though the correlations were weak or 
moderate. These findings suggest the need for the development of preventive 
interventions that address the specific needs of female athletes, implementation 
of injury prevention programs and strategies to maximize adherence, and 
long-term musculoskeletal assessments of players after retirement.

Mercury speciation and nanoparticle analysis in foods from the Danish market.

Abouelenein D(1), Amlund H(1), Lund YO(1), Duedahl-Olesen L(1), Sloth JJ(1),

Author information:

Mercury toxicity depends strongly on chemical form, yet dietary exposure 
assessments and regulatory monitoring are typically based on total mercury 
(THg). This study evaluated inorganic mercury (iHg), methylmercury (MeHg), THg, 
selenium (Se), and Hg- and Se-containing nanoparticles (NPs) in 44 seafood and 
10 non-seafood products from the Danish market. A rapid reversed-phase 
HPLC-ICP-MS method was validated in-house and applied for Hg speciation, 
providing baseline separation of iHg and MeHg within 3.5 min. MeHg recoveries in 
certified reference materials were 94-101%, within-laboratory reproducibility 
was ≤12.3%, and the limit of quantification (LOQ) for fresh seafood samples was 
0.29 µg kg-1 wet weight. The sum of speciated Hg (∑Hg = iHg + MeHg) agreed with 
acid-digestion THg within 80-105% across seafood samples. In fish and 
crustaceans, MeHg was the predominant Hg species, accounting for approximately 
90-94% of THg, supporting the use of THg as a practical proxy for MeHg exposure 
in these categories. In contrast, MeHg accounted for only 22.6-44.5% of THg in 
mussels and was below the LOQ in all non-seafood matrices except one pig liver 
sample, demonstrating that fixed species-proportion assumptions may overestimate 
MeHg exposure in some food categories. The highest THg concentration was 
observed in common dab (Limanda limanda) at 0.33 mg kg-1 wet weight, slightly 
above the 0.30 mg kg-1 EU maximum level applicable to this species group under 
Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915. Hg-containing NPs represented approximately 
1% of the iHg fraction within the detectable particle size range across analysed 
samples, indicating a minor contribution to the measured iHg pool.

Subsequent Detection of Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer After Suspicious 
MRI and an Initial Biopsy Negative for csPCa: A Longitudinal Subgroup Analysis 
of the MULTIPROS Trial.

Aloufi WD(1)(2), Szewczyk-Bieda M(3), Nabi G(1), Zhang X(4), Zhang Y(5), Wei 
C(1), Manfredi L(6).

Author information:
(1)Division of Imaging Sciences and Technology, School of Medicine, University 
of Dundee, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee, UK.
(2)Department of Radiological Sciences, College of Applied Medical Sciences, 
Taif University, Taif, Saudi Arabia.
(3)Department of Clinical Radiology, Ninewells Hospital and Medical School, 
Dundee, UK.
(4)Division of Population Health and Genomics, School of Medicine, University of 
Dundee, Dundee, UK.
(5)School of Science and Engineering, University of Dundee, Dundee, UK.
(6)Division of Respiratory Medicine and Gastroenterology, School of Medicine,

BACKGROUND: Management after suspicious multiparametric MRI (mpMRI; PI-RADS ≥ 3) 
and an initial biopsy negative for clinically significant prostate cancer 
(csPCa) remains uncertain. We described the frequency of subsequent csPCa 
detection and explored baseline factors.
METHODS: This post hoc longitudinal analysis of MULTIPROS trial data included 
153 men with PI-RADS ≥ 3 lesions and no csPCa detected on baseline transrectal 
systematic biopsy, with or without targeted biopsy. Participants contributed 
follow-up from the date of the initial mpMRI until csPCa detection or their last 
available clinical follow-up, with records reviewed through May 2025. Follow-up 
was not protocol-mandated, and repeat biopsy was guided by clinical findings. 
The primary outcome was time to histological csPCa detection. Kaplan-Meier and 
multivariable logistic regression analyses were exploratory.

detected within 6 months, and the median time to detection was 3 months. This 
early clustering was compatible with possible baseline sampling limitations, 
although timing alone could not establish this mechanism. Overall, 84/153 men 
underwent repeat biopsy and 69/153 did not; 69/116 men without detected csPCa 
lacked repeat histological confirmation. The between-group Kaplan-Meier

associated with detection. The hypothesis-generating model had moderate apparent 
discrimination (AUC 0.756) but low sensitivity at a 0.50 threshold (24.3%).

baseline sampling limitations, although the biological timing of disease onset 
cannot be established from these data. Selective follow-up limits the 
interpretation of the detection proportion and between-group comparison. The 
identified associations require external validation, and the model should not be 
used clinically.

Toward Cadaveric Proteomics: A Theoretical Framework for Mass Spectrometry 
Analysis of Embalmed Human Tissues.

Nagshabandi LN(1), AlHammadi SA(1), Sukkarieh HH(2), Abdelhadi OE(3), Aljada 
A(4).

Author information:
(1)College of Medicine, Alfaisal University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
(2)Department of Pharmacology, College of Medicine, Alfaisal University, Riyadh, 
Saudi Arabia.
(3)Department of Anatomy & Genetics, College of Medicine, Alfaisal University, 
Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
(4)Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Medicine, College of Medicine, 
Alfaisal University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

Mass spectrometry-based proteomics has been applied with considerable success to 
the analysis of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues, and this 
success raises the question of whether the same methods can be applied to the 
embalmed human cadaveric specimens that are used in anatomical education and 
research. In this review, a theoretical framework is presented for the 
application of proteomic methods to embalmed cadaveric tissues, in which the 
feasibility of the approach is evaluated on the basis of the methods that have 
been established for FFPE tissue, and the critical gaps in the evidence are 
identified. Four questions are addressed: which of the methods that have been 
established for FFPE tissue can be transferred to embalmed tissue; how the 
post-mortem interval and the chemistry of the embalming fluid limit that 
transfer; which acquisition and quantification strategies are suited to proteins 
that carry a heavy burden of chemical modification; and which applications are 
already established in preserved human tissue and which of them still require 
validation in embalmed specimens. A comprehensive review of the literature was 
carried out on the proteomic methods for FFPE tissue, on the kinetics of 
post-mortem protein degradation, on the chemistry of embalming, and on the 
strategies for the reversal of crosslinks. Studies of post-mortem protein 
degradation place the critical threshold for embalming at 24 h if protein 
integrity is to be maintained; preservation is best when embalming takes place 
within 6-12 h. Embalming with formaldehyde produces extensive crosslinks between 
the proteins that are similar to those of the FFPE processing, and this suggests 
that the strategies for the reversal of the crosslinks that have been 
established for FFPE tissue may be compatible with embalmed tissue. The 
alternative methods of embalming, which include the ethanol-based and the 
salt-based approaches, may offer a better preservation of the proteins. However, 
the extended periods of preservation and the multi-component chemical 
environment of cadaveric embalming present challenges that exceed those of the 
clinical FFPE specimens. No published study has yet carried out a full proteomic 
analysis of an embalmed human cadaver. The rates of protein identification and 
the effectiveness of the processing remain theoretical projections that require 
experimental validation. Although the theoretical considerations suggest that 
the approach is feasible, there are significant gaps in the evidence between the 
established methods for FFPE tissue and the requirements of cadaveric specimens. 
The framework identifies the priority areas for experimental validation, which 
are the optimization of the reversal of the crosslinks, the assessment of the 
recovery of proteins with the different methods of embalming, and the 
development of specialized protocols for processing. The successful development 
of cadaveric proteomics could improve anatomical education through the 
characterization of the tissues at the molecular level, could support forensic 
applications, and could enable biomedical research on human specimens that are 
well characterized. However, extensive experimental validation will be required 
before what is possible in theory can be turned into a method that is used in 
practice.

The Clinical Efficacy of Cardiac Rehabilitation in Takotsubo Syndrome.

Tayon KG(1), Carlisle AE, Schneider A, Shapiro BP, Dineen EH, Cooper LT, Taylor 
BJ.

Author information:
(1)Author Affiliations: Department of Cardiovascular Medicine, Mayo Clinic in 
Florida, Jacksonville, Florida.

PURPOSE: Despite normalization of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), 
symptoms and impaired exercise capacity can persist ~1 year after Takotsubo 
syndrome (TTS). We evaluated the impact of cardiac rehabilitation (CR) on 
cardiac structure and function, functional exercise capacity, and health-related 
quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with TTS.
METHODS: Patients with TTS who completed (TTS-CR, n = 33) and did not complete 
(TTS-CTL, n = 24) CR were retrospectively analyzed. Cardiac structure and 
function (via echocardiogram) were assessed at index hospitalization and 
follow-up (post-CR in TTS-CR; >1 month later in TTS). The 6-minute walk test 
distance and Dartmouth Cooperative Functional Assessment Charts quality-of-life 
score were assessed pre- and post-CR (TTS-CR). Major adverse cardiovascular 
events within 1-year post index hospitalization were recorded (all groups).
RESULTS: The LVEF improved similarly in TTS-CR (39 ± 9% vs 60 ± 6%) and TTS 
(39 ± 10% vs 60 ± 7%, P = .58). The left ventricular end-diastolic volume 
decreased similarly in TTS-CR (125 ± 40 vs 105 ± 37 mL) and TTS-CTL (126 ± 26 vs 
109 ± 27 mL, P = .81). In TTS-CR, 6-minute walk test distance (330 ± 126 vs 
364 ± 97 m, P = .007) and Dartmouth Cooperative Functional Assessment Charts 
quality-of-life score (22 ± 6 vs 19 ± 7 m, P = .04) improved significantly from 
pre- to post-CR. Rates of major adverse cardiovascular events were similar 
between groups (P > .05).
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac rehabilitation did not enhance cardiac structural or 
functional recovery but did improve functional exercise capacity and HRQoL in 
patients with TTS.

Ex vivo evaluation of corneal permeation and irritation potential associated 
with proparacaine hydrochloride misuse.

Gonzalez-Jimenez NC(1)(2), Lozano MC(1), Baena Y(1).

Author information:
(1)Departamento de Farmacia, Facultad de Ciencias, Universidad Nacional de 
Colombia, Sede Bogotá, Bogotá, D.C., Colombia.
(2)Programa de Optometría, Facultad de Ciencias de la Salud y del Deporte, 
Fundación Universitaria del Área Andina, Bogotá, D.C., Colombia.

INTRODUCTION: Proparacaine hydrochloride is a topical ocular anesthetic widely 
used in diagnostic procedures. Although generally safe when properly 
administered, repeated or unsupervised use has been associated with clinically 
relevant corneal injury. In contexts where access to topical anesthetics is 
insufficiently controlled, misuse may result in cumulative epithelial damage and 
vision-threatening complications. Despite clinical reports and experimental 
evidence of corneal toxicity, quantitative data linking exposure conditions to 
structural corneal damage under controlled ex vivo settings remain limited, 
particularly regarding dose-injury relationships at the tissue level.
METHODS: Porcine corneas were mounted in Franz diffusion cells to quantify 
permeation by UV-Vis spectrophotometry and evaluate corneal histopathological 
changes. Both pure proparacaine and the commercial 0.5% proparacaine 
hydrochloride ophthalmic solution (Alcaine®, Alcon) were assessed under 
therapeutic (2.25 mg/mL), abuse (4.5 mg/mL), and infinite-dose (53.152 mg/mL) 
conditions. Negative (phosphate-buffered saline) and positive (99.5% ethanol) 
controls were included for histopathological assessment. ANOVA was applied to 
permeation data, and histopathological scores were analyzed using non-parametric 
tests.
RESULTS: Proparacaine showed low permeability (9.33 × 10-7 cm/s), with only a 
small fraction of the applied dose permeating across the cornea during the 
experimental period. Permeation increased in a concentration- and time-dependent 
manner. High-dose and infinite-dose exposure conditions resulted in marked 
epithelial damage, including spongiosis, chromatin condensation, and 
desquamation, with severity comparable to that induced by ethanol used as a 
positive control. Differences between formulations were primarily driven by 
concentration rather than formulation composition, and a correlation was 
observed between cumulative permeation and the extent of epithelial injury.
CONCLUSION: Proparacaine demonstrates dose-dependent permeation and 
histopathological changes, emphasizing the risks associated with misuse. The ex 
vivo model provides relevant and ethically aligned evidence to support ocular 
hazard assessment through the characterizing of histopathological changes.

Reduced Crude Protein Nutrition in Poultry: Mechanistic Links Between Nitrogen 
Metabolism, Gut Microbial Ecology, and Intestinal Physiology.

Naeem M(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Poultry Science, Auburn University, Auburn, Alabama, USA.

Reducing dietary crude protein (CP) has emerged as an effective nutritional 
strategy to improve nitrogen utilisation efficiency and reduce environmental 
nitrogen losses in poultry production. Beyond these practical benefits, dietary 
protein concentration and digestibility influence nitrogen flow, microbial 
substrate availability, and metabolic interactions within the gastrointestinal 
tract, thereby shaping host-microbiota function. This review synthesises current 
evidence on the mechanistic links between reduced crude protein nutrition, 
nitrogen metabolism, gut microbial ecology, and intestinal physiology in 
poultry. Quantitative evidence indicates that responses depend strongly on the 
magnitude of CP reduction and dietary formulation. For example, a 
2-percentage-point CP reduction with balanced lysine, methionine, and threonine 
improved growth and intestinal morphology, whereas a 3-percentage-point 
reduction has been associated with decreased duodenal and ileal villus height; 
in contrast, a 1.5-percentage-point reduction produced no significant 
morphological impairment. Recent evidence further shows that a 2% lower-protein 
diet can increase ileal microbial richness and diversity, while bacteriophage 
supplementation significantly improves nitrogen digestibility (p = 0.045), and 
dietary protein level itself affects nitrogen digestibility (p = 0.017). 
Collectively, moderate CP reduction supported by adequate digestible amino acids 
and highly digestible ingredients can decrease undigested nitrogen flow and 
proteolytic fermentation while maintaining intestinal function. However, 
excessive protein restriction, poor amino acid balance, or reduced ingredient 
digestibility may disrupt microbial metabolism and compromise intestinal 
integrity. These findings position reduced crude protein nutrition as a 
precision nutritional strategy in which the magnitude of protein reduction, 
amino acid adequacy, digestibility, and microbial substrate availability 
collectively determine productive, intestinal, and environmental outcomes.

PURPOSE: The increasing use of computed tomography (CT) has been linked to a 
higher risk of brain tumors and leukemia in pediatric populations. CT causes 
direct DNA damage and generates reactive oxygen species, leading to 
double-stranded DNA breaks. Folic acid, known for its role in DNA stabilization, 
was supplemented before radiation exposure to reduce these effects. This study 
assessed the genotoxic impact of CT in mice with and without folic acid 
supplementation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Three groups of Balb-C mice were formed: Group 1 - 
negative control; Group 2 - exposed to total body X-rays (4 mGy per day for 2 
consecutive days); and Group 3 - treated like group 2 but also given folic acid 
in their drinking water (Lab. Valdecasas, S.A., 2.12 mg/kg) from the start of 
the experiment. Blood smears were made to analyze micronucleated erythrocytes 
and micronucleated polychromatic erythrocytes under a microscope (100×).
RESULTS: At 72 hours, group 3 showed a reduction in micronucleated polychromatic 
erythrocytes compared to group 2. Both intragroup and intergroup analyses 
revealed a decreased proportion of micronucleated erythrocytes at 72 hours in 
group 3, with further reductions seen in intragroup comparisons at 96 hours.
CONCLUSION: Folic acid reduced radiation-induced DNA damage in group 3 (CT plus 
folic acid) compared to group 2 (CT only), indicating a possible protective 
effect. However, since a murine model was used, these findings require cautious 
interpretation and thorough translational evaluation before validating 
antioxidant supplementation in pediatric patients undergoing radiation.

Widespread plasma jets in the Martian magnetosheath revealed by dual-spacecraft 
observations.

Tadlock A(1), Dong C(1)(2), Zhang C(1), Raptis S(3), Zhou H(1), Li X(1), Gao 
J(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Astronomy, Center for Space Physics, Boston University, Boston, 
MA 02215.
(2)School of Natural Sciences, Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, NJ 
08540.
(3)The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, Laurel, MD 20723.

Plasma jets in planetary magnetosheaths are transient, high dynamic pressure 
structures capable of strongly perturbing downstream magnetospheres and 
modulating solar wind energy transfer. Although recently identified at Mars, 
their formation mechanisms and global occurrence remain poorly constrained. 
Using dual-spacecraft observations from Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN 
and Tianwen-1, we show that magnetosheath jets occur throughout the Martian 
magnetosheath, in striking contrast to Earth where jet occurrence is strongly 
controlled by interplanetary magnetic field orientation and largely confined to 
quasi-parallel shock regions. We propose that this widespread distribution is 
linked to Mars' extended hydrogen corona, which generates pickup ions that drive 
proton-cyclotron waves upstream of the bow shock. Because this mechanism is 
generic to any body with an extended corona (or exosphere) embedded in a stellar 
wind, this finding bears on solar-wind interactions at comets and other small 
bodies, and on the space environments of unmagnetized terrestrial exoplanets. 
These results indicate that magnetosheath jet formation can be governed not only 
by external solar wind forcing but also by intrinsic planetary properties, 
pointing to a previously unrecognized pathway for solar wind-planet coupling at 
unmagnetized worlds.

Human prion diseases, including sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (sCJD) and 
Gerstmann-Sträussler-Scheinker disease (GSS), are fatal neurodegenerative 
disorders characterized by misfolded prion protein (PrP) accumulation. Although 
type I interferon (IFN) signaling and downstream IFN-stimulated genes are well 
characterized as essential components of host defense in experimental animal 
models, their roles in human prion pathology remain poorly defined. Myxovirus

functions, yet their histopathological expression in prion diseases is

with sCJD. Myxovirus resistance protein A and PKR showed astrocytic

astrocytes. In contrast, PKR expression was confined to astrocyte somata. This 
differential localization indicates distinct functional contributions to 
astrocytic responses. These findings indicate that astrocytic MxA and PKR are 
direct type I IFN signaling targets; moreover, the close association of MxA with

Variability in automated sepsis case detection: a systematic analysis of 
implementation methods in clinical data repositories.

Meyer-Eschenbach F(1)(2)(3), Schmiedler R(1), von Stoephasius J(3), Zhang C(2), 
Kronfli L(1), Frey N(1), Näher AF(4), Ehret J(2), Nothacker J(2), von Kalle 
C(2), Kohler S(5)(6), Grünewald E(1), Edel A(7), Kumpf O(7), Barrenetxea J(1), 
Balzer F(1).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Medical Informatics, Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin, 
Berlin 10117, Germany.
(2)Clinical Study Center, Berlin Institute of Health at Charité - 
Universitätsmedizin Berlin, Berlin 10117, Germany.
(3)Department of Computer Science, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Berlin 12489, 
Germany.
(4)Digital Global Public Health, Hasso Plattner Institute, University of 
Potsdam, Potsdam 14482, Germany.
(5)Department of Computer Science, Freie Universität Berlin, Berlin 14195, 
Germany.
(6)Health Data Science Unit, University Hospital Heidelberg, Heidelberg 69120, 
Germany.
(7)Department of Anesthesiology and Intensive Care Medicine (CCM|CVK), Charité - 
Universitätsmedizin Berlin, Berlin 10117, Germany.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically review and characterize methodological 
heterogeneity in sepsis case detection using the Medical Information Mart for 
Intensive Care III (MIMIC-III) and eICU-CRD databases.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of PubMed 
and Web of Science (publication years 2016-2024). Studies were eligible if they 
applied the SOFA-based Sepsis-3 definition to MIMIC-III or eICU-CRD, provided at 
least one explicit label-calculation detail, reported a traceable detection 
rate, and met further criteria detailed in the PRISMA flow diagram. We 
classified each study by study type and unit of analysis (patients, admissions, 
or ICU stays) and extracted methodological details on sepsis case detection 
across 6 domains. For studies with available source code, we additionally 
examined code structure and repository dependencies to identify methodological 
decisions across these domains.
RESULTS: Of 396 publications screened, 64 met inclusion criteria and 12 provided 
source code. Sepsis detection rates ranged from 3.4% to 65.2% in MIMIC-III and 
from 9.8% to 47.9% in eICU-CRD. Substantial variability persisted among studies 
using identical cohort definitions within both databases (MIMIC-III: 
16.9%-42.2%; eICU-CRD: 13.9%-31.4%). In a generalized linear mixed model, 
between-study heterogeneity was extreme (overall τ²≈0.79; 95% prediction 
interval for a new study's detection rate 5%-63%), and study-level 
characteristics-including database, study type, infection detection method, code 
availability, and unit of analysis-explained only a small proportion of this 
variance (≈9%), with no characteristic reaching statistical significance. The 
overall proportion of studies reporting methodological details varied by domain: 
SOFA calculation (53.1%), infection detection methods (42.2%), temporal windows 
(37.5%), aggregation methods (26.6%), and missing-data handling (17.2%). Source 
code analysis identified 321 implementation decisions, revealing heterogeneity 
in baseline SOFA definitions (SOFA = 0 vs dynamic baseline), temporal windows 
(infection-centered vs ICU-admission-centered) and infection detection methods 
(antibiotic-culture matching vs APACHE-based diagnosis). Dependencies among 
several MIMIC-III repositories suggested propagation of implementation decisions 
across studies.
DISCUSSION: Clinically validated sepsis definitions yield substantially 
different detection rates across studies using identical datasets. Statistical 
modeling showed that this variability is driven almost entirely by between-study 
implementation differences rather than sampling error or study characteristics.
CONCLUSION: To improve reproducibility in sepsis research and the robustness of 
sepsis prediction models, we recommend standardized reporting of sepsis case 
detection methodology and the publication of version-controlled source code.

France.
(16)Bridge Institute of Experimental Tumor Therapy, West German Cancer Center, 
University Medicine Essen, 45147 Essen, Germany.

Stimulation of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) that couple to Gi/o leads to 
the activation of G protein-activated inward rectifier K+ (GIRK) channels and 
membrane hyperpolarization in excitable cells. GIRK channel availability can 
determine the success of optogenetic silencing strategies based on Gi/o-coupled 
GPCRs. To selectively enhance Gi/o-mediated GIRK currents, we created expression 
cassettes that coupled the activity of a GIRK subunit to the light-activated 
Gi/o-coupled GPCRs Opn4L (an opsin also known as melanopsin), longwave-sensitive 
opsin Opn1, parapinopsin, or Opn7b. We used the GIRK1 F137S mutant because of 
its fast activation, generation of large currents, and formation of homomeric 
channels, which reduced the size of the expression cassette. We demonstrated 
that light-mediated activation of GIRK1F137S through the opsins induced robust 
GIRK currents in HEK293 cells, cardiomyocytes, and cerebellar Purkinje neurons. 
Moreover, coupling GIRK1F137S activation to the promiscuous Opn4L changed the 
net effect of G protein signaling from Gq/11-mediated excitation to 
Gi/o-mediated inhibition in cerebellar Purkinje neurons and cardiomyocytes. 
Thus, our tools optimize the use of GIRK activity in the optogenetic control of 
the Gi/o pathway in excitable cells.

Brain vasculature is essential for central nervous system function. Here, we 
found a cerebrovascular signaling axis in which the arginine methyltransferase 
PRMT5 in endothelial cells promoted proper inhibitory synaptogenesis and motor

findings define the endothelial PRMT5-ANGPTL4 axis as a key regulator of 
cerebellar inhibitory circuitry and motor function, highlighting cerebrovascular 
mechanisms as potential therapeutic targets for motor coordination disorders.

Digitally Printed Gold Nanoelectronics for Tap-to-Detect Electrochemical

Printed electrochemical sensors offer a promising route toward decentralized 
diagnostics and environmental monitoring, but their practical use remains 
constrained by complex electrode fabrication and instrument-dependent readout. 
Here, we present a tap-to-detect sensing platform that couples digitally printed 
gold nanoparticle nanoelectronics with a battery-free near-field communication 
(NFC) potentiostat. Single-pass digital materials deposition enables direct 
fabrication of ready-to-use AuNP working/counter electrodes and AgNP reference 
electrodes on a flexible polyimide substrate, producing mechanically robust and

42.5 ng mL-1, without additional electrode modification. This digitally printed, 
smartphone-readable gold nanoelectronic platform provides a scalable pathway 
toward portable electrochemical sensing for healthcare and environmental 
applications.

Hollow Silica Nanoparticles with Tunable Morphology and Porosity.

Hwang U(1)(2), Koo J(2), Kim JH(1), Rosenfeld J(1), Nam JD(2), Lee D(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, School of Engineering 
and Applied Science, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia,

(2)Department of Polymer Science and Engineering, Sungkyunkwan University,

Hollow silica nanoparticles (HSNPs) are promising nanomaterials for applications 
such as antireflection coatings, catalysis, and gas separation membranes. Their 
hollow cores and tunable porosity provide a unique combination of a low 
refractive index, a high surface area, and selective transport properties. 
However, precise control of the structure of HSNPs remains challenging because 
the formation pathways are highly sensitive to synthesis conditions. We 
systematically examine the influence of poly(acrylic acid) (PAA), tetraethyl 
orthosilicate (TEOS), and ammonia concentrations on particle morphology to gain 
insight into the mechanisms governing the formation of HSNPs. Distinct regimes 
of nanospheres, nanochains, and aggregates are identified, with the core size 
and shell thickness of nanospheres independently governed by the concentrations 
of PAA and TEOS. Increasing the PAA/TEOS ratio promotes the formation of 
nanochains with higher aspect ratios and increased porosity. Elevated ammonia 
concentrations induce a transition to yolk-shell nanochains by accelerating 
silica condensation and entrapping sub-10 nm particles within the hollow cores. 
Applying this mechanistic insight, we extend the approach to fabricate 
ceria-silica yolk-shell composites. These results highlight a versatile design 
principle for tailoring HSNP morphology and porosity, providing practical 
guidelines for scalable synthesis and application across diverse structures.

ROS-Responsive Hydrogel for Spatiotemporal Cascade Regulation of Ferroptosis and 
Fibrosis for Myocardial Protection.

Zhai S(1), Wang Z(1)(2), Wang J(2), Guo X(1), Tan X(1), Zhang H(2), Zhang R(3), 
Hu N(1).

Author information:
(1)Third Hospital of Shanxi Medical University, Shanxi Bethune Hospital, Shanxi 
Academy of Medical Sciences, Tongji Shanxi Hospital , Taiyuan030032, China.
(2)School of Basic Medical Science, Shanxi Medical University, Taiyuan030001,

(3)Department of Radiology, Shanxi Provincial People's Hospital Affiliated to 
Shanxi Medical University, Taiyuan030001, China.

Myocardial infarction (MI)-induced cardiac injury is mainly divided into two 
phases: the acute necrotic phase and the repair phase. Given the distinct 
therapeutic requirements of each phase-salvaging dying cardiomyocytes and 
reducing infarct size in the acute phase, while achieving controlled fibrosis to 
promote effective ventricular remodeling in the repair phase-we designed an 
ROS-responsive hydrogel co-delivery system (Met/Anti-34a@Gel) loaded with 
metformin (Met) and Anti-34a liposomes (Anti-34a Lip) to achieve precise 
regulation of both the acute and repair phases of MI. In the highly oxidative 
stress microenvironment following MI, the hydrogel gradually degrades and 
releases Met and Anti-34a Lip in a stage-specific manner. Met improves 
mitochondrial function, inhibits oxidative stress and ferroptosis, thereby 
effectively salvaging cardiomyocytes in the acute phase. Anti-34a Lip modulates 
the differentiation behavior of cardiac fibroblasts, suppressing excessive 
fibrosis and promoting favorable ventricular remodeling in the repair phase. 
Echocardiography revealed that Met/Anti-34a@Gel preserved left ventricular 
ejection fraction (EF) and fractional shortening (FS) at 72 h post-MI, reduced 
serum MDA levels in the acute phase, and maintained EF at approximately 60.92 ± 
8.37% with a lower collagen I/III ratio at 4 weeks, collectively demonstrating 
both acute cardioprotection and long-term anti-fibrotic remodeling. In this 
combined therapeutic strategy, the early mitochondrial protection and 
anti-ferroptosis effects establish a favorable tissue and functional foundation 
for subsequent precision anti-fibrotic therapy, while the later anti-fibrotic 
treatment further consolidates the early protective effects. The two actions 
synergistically form a positive feedback loop, ultimately achieving sustained 
long-term cardiac functional improvement.

Adhesive, Chemically Resistant and Antibacterial Protein Films by Coacervating 
Mineralization of Noble Metal-Binding Elastin-Like Polypeptides.

Muthukumar S(1), Naser NY(2), Lin Z(3), Wixson WC(2), Baneyx F(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chemistry, University of Washington, Seattle, Washington98195,

Protein films (PFs) provide a sustainable, biocompatible platform for food 
packaging, biomedical, and advanced technological applications. However, 
chemical resistance and the incorporation of desirable characteristics imparted 
by nanoparticles are often difficult to achieve and require multi-step 
processing. Here, we describe a one-pot strategy for fabricating 
chemically-resistant PFs using fusion proteins that combine the noble-metal 
mineralization activity of Au/Ag-binding peptides with the thermally controlled 
liquid-liquid phase separation of elastin-like polypeptides (ELPs). While 
protein-aided mineralization of an Au3+ precursor solution at room temperature 
yields monodisperse gold nanoparticles capped by a thermoresponsive corona that 
drives the reversible assembly of approximately 100 nm plasmonic clusters, 
immediate transfer of the mixture to 45 °C produces a continuous composite film 
that conformally adheres to glass, polystyrene, and curved substrates. These PFs 
withstand prolonged exposure to ethanol, toluene and nitric acid, and can be 
activated with water and heat to bond to glass, supporting loads of up to 2 kg. 
The films are stabilized by metallic nanoparticle cross-links. Spectroscopic 
measurements suggest that they are formed in a three-step mineralization-phase 
separation pathway involving metal nucleation, coacervation-driven 
sedimentation, and interfacial reconstruction. We extend the approach to silver 
to produce PFs exhibiting antimicrobial activity against E. coli.

Santa Cruz R(1)(2), Matesa A(3), Jara M(1)(4), Nadur J(1), Loudet C(5),

OBJECTIVES: Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is widely used in acute respiratory 
failure (ARF), yet the association between high tidal volume (Vt) and clinical 
outcomes remains incompletely defined. We evaluated the association between Vt 
and NIV failure overall and by ARF type, and its relationship with respiratory 
and clinical outcomes.
DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of 
Science, and Latin American and Caribbean Health Science Literature (1976 to 
September 2025).
STUDY SELECTION: Observational studies of adults with ARF treated with NIV 
reporting Vt or Vt normalized to predicted body weight (Vt/PBW) in NIV success 
and failure groups.
DATA EXTRACTION: Three pairs of reviewers identified studies and extracted data 
independently. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed. Risk of bias and 
certainty of evidence were assessed using Risk of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies 
of Interventions and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and 
Evaluation.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Eleven studies (1136 patients) were included. Vt/PBW was higher 
in NIV failure vs. success (mean difference [MD], 1.02 mL/kg [95% CI, 
0.60-1.45 mL/kg]), whereas absolute Vt did not differ (MD, 1.30 [-33.31 to 
35.91]). In hypoxemic ARF, Vt/PBW remained higher in NIV failure (MD, 0.89 mL/kg 
[95% CI, 0.04-1.73 mL/kg]); no data were available for hypercapnic ARF. Post hoc 
analyses showed that higher Vt/PBW was associated with increased mortality (odds 
ratio, 9.11; 95% CI, 3.88-21.37), higher respiratory rate (RR; MD, 3.14 
breaths/min [95% CI, 1.36-4.92 breaths/min]), and lower Paco2 (MD, -2.38 mm Hg 
[95% CI, -4.16 to -0.5938 mm Hg]), but no with pressure support (PS) level (MD, 
0.24 [95% CI, -0.81 to 1.29]). Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to 
moderate.
CONCLUSIONS: In adults with ARF treated with NIV, higher Vt/PBW was associated 
with NIV failure and worse outcomes. These findings reflect prognostic 
associations rather than causality, and interventional studies with systematic 
Vt monitoring are needed. Importantly, elevated Vt/PBW, higher RR, lower Paco2, 
and increased mortality, without differences in PS, collectively implicate 
elevated respiratory drive as a driver of increased mortality (PROSPERO 
[CRD42024584977]).Findings: Higher Vt/PBW was associated with NIV failure, 
particularly in hypoxemic respiratory failure; post hoc analyses showed 
associations with increased mortality, higher respiratory rate, and lower Paco2.

PURPOSE: To provide normative values for retinal vascular parameters and their 
determinants in healthy Turkish children aged 2 to 10 years.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 513 healthy children (247 girls, 266 
boys) attending outpatient clinics for routine or well-child visits were

Investigating the role of drama-based strategies in addressing psychological 
trauma: a systematic review.

Oliver E(1)(2), Grummitt L(1), Ewing R(2), Birrell L(1).

Author information:
(1)The Matilda Centre for Research in Mental Health and Substance Use, 
University of Sydney, Sydney, Australia.
(2)The CREATE Centre, University of Sydney, Sydney, Australia.

Background: Drama-based techniques have been increasingly implemented with 
trauma-exposed populations. However, the evidence base remains conceptually and 
methodologically heterogeneous, with substantial variation in how trauma is 
defined, how interventions are described, and which trauma-related outcomes are 
assessed.Objective: This review aimed to synthesise empirical studies examining 
drama-based interventions for individuals exposed to trauma. The review 
describes the characteristics of drama-based interventions, the types of trauma 
addressed, the pattern and range of trauma-related psychological outcomes 
assessed, and the methodological quality and certainty of the available 
evidence.Methods: A search was conducted across Scopus, PsycINFO, MEDLINE, and 
Web of Science Core Collection databases on 29 October 2025. Studies published 
in English within the past 20 years were eligible if they examined a drama-based 
intervention in a trauma-exposed population and reported trauma-related 
psychological outcomes. Methodological quality was appraised using the Mixed 
Methods Appraisal Tool and certainty of evidence was assessed using 
GRADE.Results: Twenty-six studies met inclusion criteria out of 1,461 screened 
papers. Interventions were grouped as psychodrama, dramatherapy, applied 
theatre, other drama-based psychotherapeutic interventions, and other. The most 
commonly examined outcomes were depression, anxiety, and PTSD symptoms. Across 
intervention types, some studies reported improvements in trauma-related and 
broader psychological outcomes. However, findings were mixed and frequently 
constrained by small samples, uncontrolled designs, heterogeneous outcome 
measurement, limited intervention reporting and inconsistent use of terminology. 
Certainty of evidence was rated as very low.Conclusions: Drama-based 
interventions show preliminary potential for supporting trauma-exposed 
populations, but the evidence base remains limited by substantial heterogeneity 
and low methodological quality. More rigorous study designs, clearer reporting 
of intervention content and delivery, and greater consistency in outcome 
assessment are needed to strengthen the evidence base and clarify how 
drama-based strategies may contribute to trauma-related mental health care.

Plain Language Summary: Drama-based interventions are being used with 
trauma-exposed people across clinical, community, and education settings.Across 
26 studies, some findings suggested improvements in post-traumatic stress, 
anxiety, depression, and broader psychological wellbeing.The evidence remains 
uncertain because studies used varied methods, inconsistent terminology, and 
limited descriptions of the interventions.

Depth-dependent soil water-salt relationships in the Hetao Irrigation District, 
arid Northwest China: Implications for sustainable management.

Cao Y(1), Wang H(1), Chen X(2), Zhu L(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Hetao College, Bayannur, 
Inner Mongolia, China.
(2)Department of Hydraulic and Civil Engineering, Hetao College, Bayannur, Inner 
Mongolia, China.

Soil salinization threatens agricultural productivity in arid gravity irrigation 
systems worldwide, yet the depth-stratified relationships between soil water and 
salt content remain poorly characterized. We monitored soil moisture and 
electrical conductivity (EC) at six depths (0-100 cm) across 15 sites in the 
Hetao Irrigation District, China, during the 2025 growing season. Our results 
indicate a depth-dependent divergence in water-salt associations. The EC-derived 
salinity index varied from 0.08 to 42.91 g/kg, exhibiting extreme spatial 
heterogeneity (coefficient of variation (CV) = 185.2%) across the salinity 
gradient. However, moisture-salinity relationships showed marked depth 
dependency. Surface soils (0-20 cm) exhibited non-statistically significant 
correlations (r = 0.07), whereas deep layers (60-100 cm) showed a statistically 
significant but weak positive correlation (r = 0.25, p < 0.01, R2 = 0.06), 
indicating limited explanatory power. This pattern is consistent with a subtle 
tendency of downward salt redistribution. The EC-derived salinity index showed a 
42% increase in deep layers (from 1.59 to 2.26 g/kg) over the season, compared 
to a 136% fluctuation in surface layers. These results highlight limitations of 
surface-focused monitoring approaches and indicate patterns consistent with 
subsurface salt redistribution. Compared with previous studies, this work 
provides a depth-resolved, multi-site observational dataset combined with a 
stratified analytical approach, offering additional evidence for interpreting 
soil salinity dynamics under heterogeneous field conditions.

The impact and cost of reaching the UNAIDS global HIV targets.

Stover J(1), Mattur D(2), Siapka M(3), Pliakas T(3), Valladares-Cardona R(4).

Author information:
(1)Center for Modeling and Analysis, Avenir Health, Glastonbury, Connecticut, 
United States of America.
(2)Strategic Information Department, UNAIDS, Geneva, Switzerland.
(3)Impact Epilysis, Thessaloniki, Greece.
(4)Department of Richdata, Strategy & Analytics, Guatemala City, Guatemala.

HIV funding has been declining in the past decade creating a large gap in 
required funding. In 2024, UNAIDS (Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS) 
convened a Global Task Team in 2024 to recommend new targets and approaches for 
2030 for key HIV interventions. This paper describes the approach to estimate 
the impact and cost of achieving those targets. We calibrated an HIV simulation 
model, Goals, to the historical HIV epidemic in 134 countries and used the model 
to project the impact of achieving the UNAIDS targets by 2030. Resource needs 
were estimated for 118 low-, lower-middle and upper-middle income countries 
(LMIC). To estimate the cost of achieving the targets we compiled a database of 
the unit costs for each intervention from published studies, country reports and 
commodity costs. Achieving the UNAIDS 2030 targets would reduce the annual 
number of new HIV infections globally by 77% from 2023 to 2030, from 1.3 million 
to 300,000. The number of AIDS deaths would decline by 50% over the same period. 
Resources needed to achieve the targets in all LMIC would rise to US$21.9 
billion by 2030. Of this amount, 17% is needed in low-income countries, 38% in 
lower-middle income countries and 45% in upper-middle income countries. 
Achieving the UNAIDS targets for 2030 would reduce the annual number of new HIV 
infections to just 9% of the peak value in 1995 and AIDS deaths to 13% of the 
peak value in 2004. The resources required to achieve these targets are 
substantial but $7 billion less than previous estimates of $29.3 billion.

Reinforcement learning-driven optimal capital allocation for intelligent 
finance.

Luo Y(1), Qi M(1), Cheng M(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Intelligent Logistics and Supply Chain, Sichuan Vocational and 
Technical College, Suining, Sichuan, China.

Optimal capital allocation in financial markets has long been a challenging task 
due to the dynamic nature of market conditions, risk factors, and the complexity 
of financial data. Traditional methods of portfolio management often fail to 
adapt to market shifts and do not fully leverage potential of modern machine 
learning techniques. To develop a model that dynamically optimizes capital 
allocation, leveraging reinforcement learning (RL), with focus on risk 
management, stability, and adaptability. Proposed model, Dynamic Actor-Critic 
(DAC)-enriched Clipped Proximal Policy Optimization (DAC-CPPO) model for 
portfolio optimization. A Dynamic Actor-Critic (DAC)-enriched Clipped Proximal 
Policy Optimization (DAC-CPPO) model is developed for portfolio optimization. 
The Dynamic Actor-Critic module learns optimal portfolio policies by evaluating 
actions and maximizing long-term returns, while the CPPO mechanism ensures 
stable policy updates and risk-controlled portfolio optimization. The 
Intelligent Finance Assets dataset contains 7,000 records with 32 features, 
whereas the Massive Yahoo Finance dataset includes 603k records with 9 features, 
collected from publicly available Kaggle sources for financial analysis.

readiness, and LDA extracts discriminative financial features to improve 
portfolio allocation prediction performance. Experimental settings are 
implemented using Python. Proposed DAC-CPPO model, achieving 97.6% accuracy, 
0.074 MAE, 0.081 RMSE, 1.91 Sharpe ratio, 1.12 Cumulative return, and 0.14 
Volatility, demonstrates superior risk-adjusted performance, offering higher 
returns while managing market risks effectively compared to other existing 
models. The DAC-CPPO model offers a robust solution for practical capital 
allocation by combining advanced RL techniques, ensuring effective 
decision-making while managing risks in dynamic financial environments.

explored whether lipid-lowering therapy can reverse these effects.

BACKGROUND: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by chronic 
inflammation intertwined with fibrosis and increased necroptosis. Vimentin, an 
intermediate filament protein closely associated with fibrosis and several 
inflammatory pathways, is elevated in IBD tissues. We conducted experiments to

anti-vimentin Ab reduced the levels of fibrosis-related factors.
CONCLUSION: This is the first report of the therapeutic effect of an 
anti-vimentin Ab on the pathogenic mechanisms of IBD. Further studies are needed

Integrating machine learning and geospatial technologies for spatio-temporal 
analysis of urban expansion and land use transformation in Gambella Town, 
Ethiopia.

Dararo KF(1), Jal Dup G(2), Chemeda WM(1), Karuppannan S(3)(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Spatial Decision Support, Space Science and Geospatial 
Institute, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
(2)Department of Geography and Environmental Studies, Addis Ababa University, 
Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
(3)Department of Applied Geology, College of Applied Natural Science, Adama 
Science and Technology University, Adama, Ethiopia.
(4)Department of Research Analytics, Saveetha Dental College and Hospitals, 
Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences (SIMATS), Saveetha 
University, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India.

Rapid urbanization and the associated expansion of built-up areas are 
transforming land resources, ecosystem functions, and the spatial structure of 
cities. Distinguishing urban growth, urban expansion, and urban sprawl is 
essential for understanding the processes and patterns of urban transformation 
and supporting sustainable urban planning. This study integrates machine 
learning and geospatial technologies to analyze spatio-temporal land use and 
land cover (LULC) dynamics and urban expansion in Gambella Town, Ethiopia. 
Multi-temporal Landsat satellite images from 2005, 2015, and 2025 were processed 
using remote sensing techniques and a supervised machine learning approach based 
on the Random Forest (RF) classifier. Six major LULC classes were identified: 
Agricultural Land, Bush with Grass, Built-Up Area, Bare Land, Forest Land, and 
Water Bodies. The classification achieved overall accuracies of 90%, 90%, and 
89% for 2005, 2015, and 2025, respectively. The results revealed substantial 
land transformation and rapid physical urban expansion, with the built-up area 
increasing from 93 ha (2.0%) in 2005-1,956 ha (41.3%) in 2025. This expansion 
was accompanied by major transformations of surrounding land resources, 
particularly the conversion of Bush with Grass and other open areas to built-up 
land. Agricultural land increased from 634 ha (13.4%) to 1,750 ha (36.9%), 
whereas Bush with Grass declined from 3,375 ha (71.1%) to 652 ha (13.7%). 
Socio-economic information collected from 277 respondents indicated that 
population growth, rural-urban migration, housing demand, employment 
opportunities, and infrastructure development were major drivers of urban 
expansion. The study distinguishes urban expansion, represented by the increase 
in built-up land, from urban sprawl, which refers to the spatial pattern and 
form of outward urban development. The integration of Random Forest 
classification and GIS-based spatial analysis provides valuable evidence of land 
transformation, vegetation loss, and increasing pressure on urban services, 
supporting more sustainable urban planning and land management in Gambella Town.

BACKGROUND: Vancomycin combined with gentamicin (VGA) is used as an alternative 
antibiotic prophylaxis in cardiac surgery when cephalosporins are 
contraindicated. However, the nephrotoxic potential of this combination raises 
concerns regarding postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI).
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the association between VGA prophylaxis 
and AKI occurrence in patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary 
bypass (CPB), while accounting for preoperative risk factors.
DESIGN: Retrospective single-centre study. AKI was defined according to KDIGO 
criteria within 7 postoperative days.
PATIENTS: Of the 8895 eligible patients between April 2013 and December 2021, 
8198 were included. Subgroup analyses were performed according to preoperative 
AKI risk status (high-risk: insulin-dependent diabetes, cirrhosis, acute 
endocarditis, preoperative critical state, emergency surgery, or cardiac 
transplantation).
RESULTS: In our cohort, 7469 (91%) received cephalosporins and 729 (9%) received 
VGA. The overall AKI incidence was 16%. AKI occurred more frequently in the VGA 
group (29% vs. 15%, P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, VGA remained 
independently associated with AKI [odds ratio (OR) 1.29, 95% confidence interval 
(CI) 1.03 to 1.62, P = 0.024], confirmed by propensity score analysis (OR 1.32, 
95% CI 1.09 to 1.60, P = 0.005). In subgroup analyses, VGA was significantly 
associated with AKI in high-risk patients (OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.14 to 2.04, 
P = 0.004), but not in low-risk patients (OR 1.19, 95% CI 0.87 to 1.64, 
P = 0.285).
CONCLUSION: In this large retrospective cohort, VGA antibiotic prophylaxis was 
independently associated with increased AKI risk following cardiac surgery with 
CPB. This association was driven primarily by patients with preoperative risk 
factors for AKI. Alternative prophylactic regimens should be considered in 
high-risk patients when possible.

A cost-effective data assimilation system for improving ROMS simulations in the 
Southwest Atlantic.

Dorfschäfer GS(1)(2), Tanajura CAS(1)(3), De Paula TP(4)(5), Costa FB(6), 
Pereira J(1)(3).

Author information:
(1)Oceanographic Modeling and Observation Network (REMO), Salvador, Bahia, 
Brazil.
(2)Graduate Program in Geophysics, Federal University of Bahia (UFBA), Salvador, 
Bahia, Brazil.
(3)Department of Earth and Environmental Physics, Physics Institute, Federal 
University of Bahia (UFBA), Salvador, Bahia, Brazil.
(4)Department of Oceanic Engineering Technology, Petrobras Research and 
Development Center (CENPES), Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
(5)Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), Alberto Luiz Coimbra Institute 
for Graduate Studies and Research in Engineering (COPPE), Rio de Janeiro, Rio de 
Janeiro, Brazil.
(6)CMCC Foundation - Euro-Mediterranean Center on Climate Change, Lecce, Italy.

This study presents for the first time the integration of the low-cost REMO 
Ocean Data Assimilation System (RODAS) into the Regional Ocean Modeling System 
(ROMS) for assimilating Sea Surface Temperature (SST) observations. RODAS is an 
Ensemble Optimal Interpolation (EnOI)-based data assimilation system originally 
developed for use with the HYCOM model. Here, it is adapted to ROMS and applied 
to the Southwest Atlantic, with a focus on evaluating its impact on short-term 
ocean hindcasts. We conducted 4-years simulations with and without SST 
assimilation, referred to as RODAS_SST and Free, respectively. The RODAS_SST 
experiment showed a 70% reduction in SST root mean square deviation (RMSD) 
relative to the Free run, and a 55% reduction compared to 72-hour hindcasts 
generated from previous analysis cycles. When compared with the GLORYS 
reanalysis, SST RMSD was reduced by 64%. Ocean heat content estimates also 
improved, with reductions in mean absolute error of 15% during summer and 25% in 
winter. While assimilation improved surface and subsurface thermal structure in 
general, comparisons with Argo profiles revealed occasional degradations near 
the thermocline, highlighting the need for better multivariate covariance 
representation in the EnOI scheme. The successful implementation of RODAS in 
ROMS provides a cost-effective tool for enhancing model initial conditions and 
regional ocean simulations. Future developments will include the assimilation of 
Argo temperature and salinity profiles, sea level anomaly (SLA) data, and 
observations from the SWOT satellite. The code will be openly released, aiming 
to broaden access to ocean data assimilation by enabling robust performance even 
on limited computational resources.

Selective persistence of HIV-1-infected T cell clones can occur through immune 
reprogramming driven by defective, transcriptionally active proviruses.

Hamann MV(1), Brauckmann L(1), Schwarz C(1), Spohn M(2), Stoeck R(1), Leddy 
SM(1)(3), Frouard J(4)(5), Adiba M(1), Winzer R(6)(7), Hausmann F(8), Virdi

Author information:
(1)Research Unit Genomics of Retroviral Infections, Leibniz Institute of 
Virology, Hamburg, Germany.
(2)Bioinformatics Core, University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf, Hamburg,

(3)Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Cornell University, Ithaca, New

(4)Gladstone Institutes, University of California San Francisco (UCSF), San

(5)Department of Urology, University of California San Francisco (UCSF), San

(6)Institute of Immunology, University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf,

(7)Hamburg Center for Translational Immunology, University Medical Center 
Hamburg-Eppendorf, Hamburg, Germany.
(8)Research Department Integrative Virology, Leibniz Institute of Virology, 
Hamburg, Germany.
(9)Research Department Virus Genomics, Leibniz Institute of Virology, Hamburg, 
Germany.
(10)Institute for Medical Virology and Epidemiology of Viral Diseases, 
University Hospital Tübingen, Tübingen, Germany.
(11)Department of Infectious Diseases, Virology, Heidelberg University, 
Heidelberg, Germany.
(12)German Center for Infection Research (DZIF), Braunschweig, Germany.
(13)Institute for Infection Research and Vaccine Development, University Medical

People living with HIV (PLWH) on antiretroviral therapy (ART) accumulate 
primarily defective proviral sequences in genomes of often clonally expanded 
CD4 + HIV-1 target cells. The majority of viral-derived DNA is transcriptionally 
active and preferentially found at distinct genomic loci suggesting a selective 
process driven by integration site-specific crosstalk between viral and host 
sequences. Focusing on one of the most prominent selected integration loci, the 
BTB Domain and CNC Homolog 2 (BACH2) gene, we here show mechanistic insights how 
CD4 + T cells are functionally reprogrammed via exaptation of provirus-derived 
regulatory sequences during long-term ART. Using a cellular model of 
BACH2-integrated proviruses, we find that proviral transcription drives aberrant 
BACH2 protein levels that escape autoregulatory feedback and impose 
BACH2-dependent transcriptomic changes. By mimicking these changes in primary 
CD4 + T lymphocytes, we observe that BACH2 drives reprogramming of cells toward 
a proliferative, precursor memory-like type. These reprogrammed CD4 + T cells 
possess traits of immune evasion and cellular survival that are signatures of 
persistent HIV reservoir cells in PLWH. Inhibition of provirus transcriptional 
activity can mitigate exaptation, suggesting a strategy to offset HIV-driven 
differentiation and expansion of CD4 + T cells. Finally, our data suggest that 
provirus exaptation at a second prominently selected proviral integration gene, 
the Signal Transducer And Activator of Transcription 5B (STAT5B) gene, drives a 
contrary, effector-like T cell fate, suggesting a multifaceted impact of 
exaptation on immune homeostasis. Overall, our data suggest that 
transcriptionally active proviruses, even if structurally defective, modulate 
target cells through insertional activation of integration genes, a process 
which we postulate to contribute to the complex immune modulation and 
dysregulation experienced by ART-suppressed PLWH.

Evaluating the Automated Extraction of Radiation Oncology Trial Data at Scale 
from the ClinicalTrials.gov Database Using a Large Language Model.

Dennstaedt F, Kretzschmar L, Cihoric N, Heesen P, Fritsak M, Roohani S, 
Aebersold DM, Guckenberger M, Christ SM.

Background The rapid growth of biomedical publishing in radiation oncology has 
created a need for automated methods to extract structured information from 
unstructured text. Large language models (LLMs) show promise in biomedical 
natural language processing, but their use for clinical trial data curation 
remains to be systematically evaluated. Methods We evaluated an LLM-based 
extraction system for radiation oncology trials on ClinicalTrials.gov. 
Forty-five classification questions spanning variables such as trial design, 
tumor type, stage, radiotherapy modality, systemic therapy, and outcomes were 
implemented using the data-element-extractor Python library with three 
open-source LLMs (GPT-OSS-20B, GPT-OSS-120B, and Qwen-3.6-27B). A manually 
curated ground-truth of 94 trials was used for performance evaluation based on 
accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Results Qwen-3.6-27B achieved the 
highest overall accuracy of 92.0% across all questions. For the 39 Boolean 
questions, it demonstrated 93.0% accuracy, 81.6% precision, 83.7% recall, and an 
F1-score of 82.6%, with 23 Boolean questions achieving an F1-score ≥80.0%. Three 
numerical questions reached accuracy ≥80.0%. Applied to the full dataset, the 
system characterized the clinical landscape of radiotherapy trials, detailing 
the prevalence of advanced techniques (e.g., 13.7% SBRT) and the integration of 
systemic agents, including chemotherapy (57.3%) and immunotherapy (26.1%). 
Conclusion LLM-based extraction can enable accurate, scalable curation of 
radiotherapy trial data. While challenges remain with complex categorical or 
numerical variables, open-source LLMs can serve as effective components of 
transparent, auditable clinical research pipelines.

Transparency, accountability, and scholarly integrity: A systematic narrative 
review of artificial intelligence governance frameworks in healthcare 
publication.

Silva A(1), Canever B(1)(2), Lino M(3), Silva E Silva V(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Nursing, Brock University, St Catharines, Canada.
(2)Nursing Department, Federal University of Santa Catarina, Florianopolis, 
Brazil.
(3)School of Nursing, University of Central Florida, Orlando, Florida, United 
States of America.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare research and 
scholarly publication has produced a rapidly expanding but fragmented ecosystem 
of reporting guidelines, governance frameworks, editorial policies, and 
regulatory instruments, imposing significant burdens on researchers, reviewers, 
and editors. This systematic narrative review identified, stratified, and 
synthesized governance frameworks and reporting standards addressing transparent 
and ethical AI use in healthcare publications, and characterized the governance 
trajectory from predictive model standards to generative AI oversight. Fourteen 
Boolean search strings were executed in PubMed (MEDLINE) covering 1 January 
2018-19 May 2026, supplemented by manual searching of the EQUATOR Network 
guideline library. Records were deduplicated and prioritized using a 
relevance-scoring algorithm. Of 30,276 deduplicated records, 888 progressed to 
human screening; 100 publications were included, comprising 69 governance 
instruments and policies classified across four evidence tiers and 31 contextual 
evidence sources. Included sources spanned six thematic groups: predictive and 
diagnostic AI frameworks (G1); sociotechnical and lifecycle governance (G2); 
generative AI and LLM-specific standards (G3); specialty-specific extensions 
(G4); surgical reporting updates (G5); and editorial and publication policy 
(G6). Analysis identified four consecutive phases of governance development from 
2018 to 2026, characterized by a shift from model performance transparency 
toward comprehensive sociotechnical accountability. Three governance tensions 
emerged: the trade-off between framework specificity and universal 
applicability; the gap between disclosure-focused standards and lifecycle 
governance; and the risk of epistemic conflation, whereby heterogeneous 
instruments are perceived as carrying equivalent authority when treated as 
interchangeable. AI governance in healthcare publications remains fragmented and 
epistemically uneven. Advancing the field requires harmonization across evidence 
tiers, adaptive updating mechanisms, and lifecycle-oriented governance 
frameworks.

Huang Y(1), Gao R(1), Li J(1), Yang B(1), Huang K(1), Chen S(1), Cao J(1), Liu

(1)Department of Epidemiology, State Key Laboratory of Cardiovascular Disease,

(2)Division of Epidemiology, Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital and

(3)Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, Center for Global Health,

BACKGROUND: Existing risk stratification tools inadequately identify individuals 
with subclinical atherosclerosis (SA) who could benefit from early intervention. 
This study aimed to develop protein risk scores (ProtRSs) for SA progression and 
assess their incremental value for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease 
(ASCVD) risk prediction.
METHODS AND FINDINGS: In a community cohort consisting of 903 individuals 
undergoing repeated SA assessments (coronary artery calcium [CAC] or carotid 
plaque) over 6 years (2008-2009 to 2013-2014), protein biomarkers were selected 
from a panel of 117 proteins using least absolute shrinkage and selection 
operator (LASSO) regression to construct SA ProtRSs for CAC and plaque 
progression, respectively, and their predictive abilities for incident ASCVD 
risk were evaluated based on a guideline-recommended traditional risk score in a 
case-cohort of 1,835 individuals (2007-2008 to 2018-2021, median follow-up of

progression, explaining 17.1% and 18.4% of respective variances. Effect sizes of 
these proteins on SA progression showed strong concordance with those on 
incident ASCVD (r  > 0.75). Each standard deviation increase in CAC and plaque 
ProtRSs was associated with hazard ratios of 1.36 (95% confidence interval [CI] 
[1.20,1.54]) and 1.38 (95% CI [1.23,1.54]) for ASCVD risk, respectively. 
Addition of the SA ProtRSs to the traditional risk score yielded a net 
reclassification improvement of 0.127 (p < 0.001). Importantly, 18.6% of 
traditional intermediate-risk individuals were reclassified into the high-risk 
category (10-year ASCVD event rate: 10.9%), indicating the need for preventive 
interventions, whereas 32.8% of traditional high-risk individuals were 
identified as having an even higher rate (13.7%), suggesting the requirement for 
intensified management. The main limitation is that the predictive value of 
ProtRSs warrants further large-scale external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: SA ProtRSs of coronary calcification and carotid plaque progression 
may provide additional value over traditional risk assessment, highlighting 
their potential in refining risk stratification and guiding targeted 
intervention strategies.
