Addressing heterogeneity in trauma responses in research and clinical practice: 
reflections and recommendations from early career researchers.

Dasen L(1), Alison Büeler L(2), Kemmere B(3)(4), Belt L(4), Hofmann VXC(2), 
Karaban I(4)(5), Nava F(3)(6), Piwanski G(3)(6), Ravn Stein A(7), Rochon E(3), 
Juri Weinreich K(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry and Psychosomatic Medicine, 
University Hospital Zurich, University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland.
(2)Department of Psychology, University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland.
(3)Department of Psychiatry, Amsterdam UMC, Amsterdam, The Netherlands.
(4)ARQ National Psychotrauma Centre, Diemen, The Netherlands.
(5)Department of Psychology, Utrecht University, Utrecht, The Netherlands.
(6)Amsterdam Public Health, Mental Health, Amsterdam, The Netherlands.
(7)Department of Psychology, Danish Center of Psychotraumatology, University of

Background: There is considerable heterogeneity in how individuals respond to 
potentially traumatic events (PTEs). Recognising and addressing this 
heterogeneity has become an increasingly important focus within 
psychotraumatology, leading to the development of diverse research and clinical 
approaches. Yet, there remains an opportunity to further integrate these 
developments into research and clinical practice.Objective: This letter 
critically reflects on recent developments in psychotrauma research and practice 
and discusses complementary methodological and clinical approaches that may 
further account for heterogeneity in trauma-related responses.Methods: Drawing 
on current literature and reflections from a recent international early career 
researcher networking event, we present reflections and practical 
recommendations across five domains: conceptualisation, sampling and 
eligibility, measurement and outcomes, analysis, and intervention.Results: We 
identify several promising developments and opportunities for further advancing 
the field: (1) complementing categorical diagnostic frameworks with 
transdiagnostic and adiagnostic approaches; (2) broadening eligibility criteria 
to include comorbid, subclinical, and diverse trauma-exposed populations; (3) 
expanding outcome assessment beyond PTSD symptom reduction to include 
transdiagnostic, culturally sensitive outcome measures valued by patients; (4) 
incorporating person-centered analytic strategies to better capture 
within-sample heterogeneity; and (5) prioritising the development and evaluation 
of transdiagnostic, indicated, and scalable interventions.Conclusions: 
Considerable progress has been made in developing approaches that acknowledge 
the heterogeneity of responses to PTEs. Addressing heterogeneity in responses to 
PTEs requires inclusive, flexible, and diverse approaches in both research and 
clinical practice. The recommendations outlined here aim to further promote 
ecologically valid and representative psychotrauma research, ultimately 
improving care for diverse trauma-exposed populations.

Plain Language Summary: Responses to potentially traumatic events are highly 
heterogeneous, yet often insufficiently captured in current research and 
practice.Transdiagnostic and adiagnostic approaches can complement categorical 
diagnostic frameworks, while broader eligibility criteria and expanded outcome 
assessment can improve representativeness and relevance.Person-centered analytic 
approaches and transdiagnostic, indicated, scalable interventions offer 
promising avenues to address heterogeneity and reduce treatment gaps.

MI-Random rPQL: A Variable Selection Method for Linear Mixed Models with Missing 
Data.

Thompson YT(1), Li Y(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biostatistics, Arkansas Children's Research Institute, 
University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences, Little Rock, AR, USA.
(2)Department of Pediatrics, University of Oklahoma Health Sciences Center, 
Oklahoma City, OK, USA.

Variable selection, a statistical approach for identifying important predictors 
of an outcome, becomes particularly challenging when data are both clustered and 
incomplete. Despite the widespread use of linear mixed models (LMMs) in social 
and behavioral research, limited work has addressed variable selection in LMMs 
with incomplete data. Missing data can reduce estimation precision and distort 
the relationships between predictors and outcomes. Although multiple imputation 
(MI) is commonly used to handle missing data in clustered settings, aggregating 
variable selection results across imputed datasets, especially for both fixed 
and random effects, remains a methodological challenge. This issue is further 
compounded in high-dimensional contexts, where the number of predictors equals 
or exceeds the number of within-cluster observations. To address these 
limitations, we propose MI-random rPQL, a regularization-based method for 
variable selection in LMMs with incomplete clustered data. The method integrates 
multiple imputation with random rPQL to jointly identify important fixed and 
random effects. A simulation study was conducted to evaluate its performance. 
The results show that MI-random rPQL effectively selects important predictors 
even under substantial missingness, offering a flexible and robust solution for 
variable selection in high-dimensional, clustered datasets with incomplete data.

The use of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) to enhance delivery and immunogenicity of 
mRNA vaccines raises safety concerns due to strong reactogenicity. Developing 
naked mRNA vaccines, which can be delivered through liquid jet-injection to the 
skin, may offer a safer alternative, but their immunogenicity has been limited.

the efficacy of N1-methyl-pseudouridine-modified naked mRNA jet-injection

and influenza A virus (A/California/7/2009 H1N1) in plaque-forming assays.

effective, and safe platform against infectious diseases, with potential for 
clinic-ready translational applications.

Primary central nervous system (CNS) vasculitis is a rare and devastating 
inflammatory cerebrovascular disease for which pathogenic mechanisms remain 
poorly defined, largely due to limited access to human tissue and the absence of 
validated experimental models. Here, we present a mouse model of CNS-restricted 
vasculitis based on inducible, endothelial-biased neoantigen expression, termed 
brain endothelial ovalbumin (BrEndO). In BrEndO mice, tamoxifen-induced

regulated process whose breakdown precipitates CNS-restricted vasculitis and 
establish BrEndO as an experimentally tractable platform to investigate 
mechanisms and modifiers of immune-mediated cerebrovascular inflammation.

Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a hyperinflammatory syndrome with 
multiple contributors, often including an infectious trigger. The Macrophage 
Activation Syndrome (MAS) subtype is linked to marked IL-18 excess, cytotoxic 
T-lymphocyte (CTL) activation, and natural killer (NK) cell abnormalities. We 
asked how excess IL-18 shapes NK and CTL responses to viral challenge. Mice with 
chronic IL-18 overproduction (Il18tg), showed baseline NK-cytopenia and CTL

Heart failure (HF) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. 
Breathing instability and exaggerated chemoreflex activation contribute to 
adverse HF outcomes, yet the central mechanisms linking respiratory control to 
cardiac dysfunction remain poorly defined. The retrotrapezoid nucleus (RTN) is a 
key brainstem chemosensory region regulating ventilatory and autonomic output, 
but whether glial dysfunction within this circuit contributes to HF

accumulation and attenuated chemoreflex-driven respiratory instability. These 
findings identify loss of astrocytic GLT-1-mediated glutamate homeostasis in the

therapeutic strategy requiring further investigation.

The inflammasome is an innate immune complex responsible for aberrant 
interleukin-1β (IL-1β) signaling in numerous chronic inflammatory diseases, 
including gout and Alzheimer's disease. The inflammasome is composed of several 
proteins, including the apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a

comorbidities. This is underpinned by a chronic inflammatory environment and 
significant immune dysregulation. γδ T cells are unconventional T cells that 
display innate and adaptive characteristics, the predominant one being their

Food insecurity in young rats induces metabolic remodeling in a sex- and 
diet-dependent manner.

An J(1), Cannavino J(1), Williams A(1), Bareja A(1), Tong W(1), Ilkayeva O(1), 
Muehlbauer M(1), Lu D(1), Hollander RA(1), Armstrong S(2), Gupta RK(1), Newgard 
CB(1).

Author information:
(1)Duke Molecular Physiology Institute and Sarah W. Stedman Nutrition and Meta, 
Duke University Medical Center, Durham, United States of America.
(2)Department of Pediatrics and Duke Center for Childhood Obesity Research, Duke 
University Medical Center, Durham, United States of America.

Exposure of humans to food insecurity (FI), involving sporadic access and low 
nutritional quality, is associated with later life development of metabolic 
disease phenotypes, but mechanisms are poorly understood. We exposed very young 
rats to a 20-day FI intervention or ad-lib (AL) feeding, using either standard 
chow (SC) or high fat/high sucrose (HF/HS) diets, followed by continued AL 
feeding on the respective diets for 10-13 weeks. We found that male, but not 
female rats subjected to FI on the HF/HS diet had increased body fat percentage, 
ratio of adipose to body weight, and fat cell size compared to AL rats, coupled 
with metabolomic and transcriptomic profiles consistent with reduced fatty acid 
oxidation in the liver and maladaptive remodeling of adipose tissue. These 
changes were specific to HF/HS feeding and did not occur with SC diet. Our study 
defines sex- and diet-specific metabolic remodeling responses to FI that may 
contribute to future disease phenotypes.

Restoration of full length filamin C is sufficient to prevent FLNC deficient 
cardiomyopathy in mice.

Jiang Z(1), Feng W(1), Chen Z(1), Bogomolovas J(1), Li M(1), Ye M(1), Gu Y(1), 
Zhou X(1), Chen J(1).

Author information:
(1)Division of Cardiology, University of California San Diego, La Jolla, United 
States of America.

Filamin C (FLNC) is an essential cytoskeletal protein required for cardiomyocyte 
structural integrity and mechanotransduction. Truncating FLNC variants cause 
haploinsufficiency associated with dilated and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathies, 
yet no therapies currently address the underlying defect of FLNC deficiency. 
Gene replacement is challenging because the approximately 8.2-kb FLNC coding 
sequence exceeds the packaging capacity of conventional adeno-associated virus 
(AAV) vectors. Here, we engineered a triple-AAV strategy optimized for 
full-length FLNC reconstitution in the heart. Screening in HEK293 cells 
identified GP41-1 and IMPDH as a compatible orthogonal pair for efficient 
full-length FLNC reconstitution. In tamoxifen-inducible, cardiomyocyte-specific 
Flnc knockout mice, systemic delivery of optimized MyoAAV2A vectors restored 
full-length FLNC expression and re-established sarcomeric localization following 
cardiomyocyte FLNC depletion. A total vector dose of 1 × 10¹³ genome copies/kg 
restored FLNC to approximately endogenous abundance, preserved systolic function 
and ventricular dimensions, limited cardiac enlargement, attenuated fibrotic 
remodeling and prevented premature death. FLNC replacement also attenuated 
pathological transcriptional remodeling and compensatory changes in cytoskeletal 
and junction-associated proteins. These findings demonstrate that systemic 
split-intein-mediated reconstitution of full-length FLNC can preserve cardiac 
structure and function in vivo, providing preclinical support for a 
mutation-independent therapeutic strategy for FLNC-associated cardiomyopathy.

Case report: Meningitis of a 66-year-old dog owner caused by Capnocytophaga 
canimorsus.

Roth M(1)(2), Uibel C(2), Mäurer M(2), Pauly S(1), Zautner AE(1)(3).

Author information:
(1)1Department of Laboratory Medicine and Microbiology & Vaccination Center, 
Klinikum Würzburg Mitte gGmbH, Würzburg, Germany.
(2)2Department of Neurology, Klinikum Würzburg Mitte gGmbH, Würzburg, Germany.
(3)3Institute of Medical Microbiology and Hospital Hygiene, Faculty of Medicine, 
Otto-von-Guericke-University, Magdeburg, Germany.

Capnocytophaga canimorsus is a fastidious Gram-negative rod transmitted from dog 
saliva and typically associated with immunocompromised hosts. We report 
meningitis in a 66-year-old immunocompetent dog owner with prior cerebral 
amyloid angiopathy who presented with acute global aphasia, fever and 
inflammatory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) consistent with bacterial meningitis, but 
without meningism or history of any dog bite. Fusiform Gram-negative rods in CSF 
prompted extended culture in thioglycolate broth, enabling growth and subsequent 
species identification by MALDI-TOF MS as C. canimorsus within five days. 
Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed according to EUCAST guidance 
for situations without species-specific breakpoints and supported continuation 
of ceftriaxone-based therapy for a total of 15 days, resulting in complete 
clinical remission and normalization of CSF parameters. This case underlines 
that C. canimorsus meningitis can occur in apparently immunocompetent elderly 
patients, illustrates the diagnostic value of targeted culture strategies, and 
emphasizes the feasibility of EUCAST-guided susceptibility testing for this rare 
pathogen.

RSPO2 synergizes with BMP2 to enhance Wnt-dependent bone healing.

Jiang B(1), Meymarian EB(1), Shahin S(1), Wilkening JT(1), Knights AJ(1), Sanjay 
A(2), Maerz T(1), Wagley Y(1), Hankenson KD(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, United 
States of America.
(2)Department of Orthopaedics, Musculoskeletal Institute, School of Medicine, 
UConn Health, Farmington, United States of America.

Bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP2) is used clinically to promote bone 
regeneration, but dose-limiting side effects restrict its clinical utility. 
Canonical Wnt signaling is essential for bone formation, and R-spondin-2 (RSPO2) 
is a secreted Wnt agonist highly expressed by osteoprogenitors. We found that 
BMP2 strongly induced RSPO2 during early human mesenchymal stem cell (hMSC) 
osteoblast differentiation. Recombinant RSPO2 synergized with BMP2 in both hMSCs 
and MC3T3-E1 preosteoblasts, whereas RSPO2 silencing impaired BMP2-driven 
osteogenic responses. In a murine critical-size calvarial defect model, 
co-delivery of RSPO2 and a suboptimal dose of BMP2 yielded significantly more 
new bone than BMP2 alone, while RSPO2 alone was ineffective. Enhanced canonical 
Wnt activation with BMP2-RSPO2 co-treatment was shown with an in vivo Wnt 
reporter mouse. Bulk RNA sequencing of MC3T3-E1 cells revealed that BMP2-RSPO2 
co-treatment differentially activated osteogenesis-related genes and pathways 
compared to BMP2 alone. The guanine exchange factor (GEF), Prex1, was 
selectively upregulated by BMP2-RSPO2 co-treatment, and was required for 
RSPO2-mediated enhancement of BMP2-induced osteoblastogenesis. These findings 
identify RSPO2 as an enhancer of BMP2-driven osteogenesis, amplifying Wnt 
activation and involving PREX1-dependent signaling. RSPO2 or PREX1 activation 
may represent a co-therapy that could enhance BMP2 efficacy while mitigating the 
adverse effects of high-dose BMP2.

Lightweight and Robust Bamboo Fiber Composite for Efficient Infrared Stealth.

Jiang L(1), Hou G(1), Xu W(1), Liu J(1), Du T(1), Shi Y(2), Wang Y(3), Shi Z(4), 
Wang X(5), Xiao X(1)(6)(7).

Author information:
(1)College of Biomass Science and Engineering, Sichuan University, 
Chengdu610065, China.
(2)College of Architecture & Environment, Sichuan University, Chengdu610065, 
China.
(3)Institute of Advanced Study, Chengdu University , Chengdu610106, China.
(4)Key Laboratory for Forest Resources Conservation and Utilization in the 
Southwest Mountains of China, Ministry of Education, Southwest Forestry 
University, Kunming650224, China.
(5)Chongqing Key Laboratory of Speciality Food Co-Built by Sichuan and 
Chongqing, College of Food Science, Southwest University, Chongqing400715, 
China.
(6)National Engineering Research Center of Clean Technology in Leather Industry, 
Sichuan University, Chengdu610065, China.
(7)Key Laboratory of Leather Chemistry and Engineering (Sichuan University), 
Ministry of Education, Chengdu610065, China.

With the continuous advancement in modern infrared detection technologies, 
efficient infrared stealth materials with features of lightweight and high 
mechanical strength are urgently desired in many fields. In this study, natural 
bamboo fibers were employed as a renewable substrate and were processed into 
lightweight and robust infrared stealth bamboo fibrous (HsIs-Bamboo) via 
oxidative defibration, ionic cross-linking, vacuum-assisted loading, and hot 
pressing. The fabricated bamboo fibrous composite enables uniform dispersion of 
functional particles, resulting in low infrared emissivity (65-73% in 8-14 μm), 
lightweight (0.80 g cm-3), and high mechanical strength (specific tensile 
strength of 385.9 MPa cm3 g-1). The composite also exhibits low-cost, efficient 
flame retardancy, and superior infrared shielding performance with a 10.6 °C 
decrease in the infrared thermal imaging test. This novel infrared stealth 
material from natural bamboo offers a promising solution for the stealth 
protection of critical facilities and holds substantial application potential as 
a highly robust infrared stealth material in weight-sensitive circumstances.

Ask the experts: a practitioner-centred approach to resilience in emergency 
medical services.

Butterworth J(1), Tangen J(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Psychology, University of Queensland, St Lucia, Australia.

Background: Resilience in high-stress occupations is commonly framed as a trait, 
an outcome, or the absence of psychopathology. None of these framings captures 
what practitioners in emergency medical services actually do, and interventions 
built on trait-based models have produced weak or inconsistent 
effects.Objective: This study argues that frontline resilience in emergency 
medical services is better understood as a domain-specific expert skill, and 
that work mode - a deliberately entered state, akin to an athlete's game face, 
in which the demands of the task rather than the emotional force of the scene 
govern functioning - is its central empirical signature. The aims were to 
identify factors that intensify traumatic impact, characterise the strategies 
practitioners use to maintain functioning, and explore systemic and relational 
barriers that constrain coping.Method: Twenty Queensland Ambulance Service 
paramedics and dispatchers (tenure 2-38 years) participated in semi-structured 
interviews, analysed via reflexive thematic analysis.Results: Three intensifiers 
of traumatic impact (unpredictability, moral weight, personal threat) defined 
the operational demands against which resilience was enacted. Three coping 
themes (baseline buffers, work mode, social scaffolding) described the 
architecture of sustained functioning. Work mode exhibited the defining features 
of skilled performance: domain specificity, a phased temporal structure 
(preparation, containment, recovery), and a developmental trajectory from 
effortful to automatic execution. Two further themes (organisational distrust, 
the outsider gap) described the systemic and relational conditions that 
constrain coping.Conclusions: Treating resilience as expertise shifts the field 
from descriptive stressor-outcome accounts towards assessable, trainable 
capacities, and exposes the limitations of trait-based self-report measures that 
cannot distinguish genuine resilience from unsustainable stoicism.

Plain Language Summary: Interviews with 20 paramedics and emergency medical 
dispatchers (2–38 years of service) suggest that frontline resilience is better 
understood as a practiced skill than as a trait.Experienced responders describe 
a deliberate work mode with three phases – preparing before a case, containing 
impact during it, and recovering afterwards – that becomes more automatic as 
experience accumulates.Current resilience questionnaires cannot distinguish 
genuine resilience from unsustainable stoicism; testing resilience through 
behaviour on representative job-like tasks is the logical next step.

Does the HPB surgeon need a vascular surgeon?

Oldhafer KJ(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)1Department of Surgery, Division of Liver, Biliary and Pancreatic Surgery, 
Asklepios Hospital Barmbek, Hamburg, Germany.
(2)2Semmelweis University Budapest, Asklepios Campus Hamburg, Germany.

Complex HPB surgery increasingly requires vascular resection and reconstruction. 
Therefore, vascular expertise is an essential part of surgical planning, 
technical execution, and oncological decision-making. While highly complex 
arterial, caval, or ex situ procedures should remain concentrated in specialised 
centres, every HPB surgeon should possess core vascular competence. Vascular and 
transplantation training should therefore become an integral part of advanced 
HPB education.

Complex post-traumatic stress disorder in refugees, asylum seekers, and 
internally displaced people: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

Melkam M(1)(2), Xu C(1)(3), Maccallum F(1), Oestreich L(1)(4).

Author information:
(1)School of Psychology, The University of Queensland, Brisbane, Australia.
(2)Department of Psychiatry, College of Medicine and Health Science, University 
of Gondar, Gondar, Ethiopia.
(3)School of Psychology and Cognitive Science, East China Normal University, 
Shanghai, People's Republic of China.
(4)Australian Institute for Bioengineering and Nanotechnology, The University of 
Queensland, Brisbane, Australia, Australia.

Background: Forcibly displaced populations, including refugees, asylum seekers, 
and internally displaced persons, are frequently exposed to severe, prolonged 
and repeated trauma from which escape is difficult or impossible. Such exposures 
increase the risk for complex post-traumatic stress disorder (CPTSD), defined by 
core PTSD symptoms alongside disturbances in self-organisation (DSO), including 
affective dysregulation, negative self-concept, and relational difficulties. 
However, the prevalence of CPTSD in forcibly displaced populations has not yet 
been quantitatively synthesised, and the added value of the CPTSD construct over 
PTSD in this population has not been examined.Methods: This systematic review 
and meta-analysis searched five databases from inception to January 2026. A 
random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to estimate pooled CPTSD prevalence, 
with pre-specified subgroup analyses, meta-regression, and sensitivity 
analyses.Results: Twenty studies met inclusion criteria, representing 17 
independent samples (n = 12,504). Reported CPTSD prevalence varied from 3.0% to 
74.6%. The random-effects pooled prevalence, retained as a descriptive summary 
of the included studies, was 20.9% (95% CI [12.6%, 32.6%]), the 95% prediction 
interval was [1.7%, 80.3%]. Between-study heterogeneity was very high 
(I² = 98.3%). Recruitment context was strongly associated with prevalence: 
estimates averaged 10.6% in community-based samples and 55.2% in 
treatment-seeking samples. Asylum seekers exhibited markedly higher prevalence 
than refugees. Across four studies, post-migration living difficulties, 
including legal insecurity, poverty, and marginalisation, were more strongly 
associated with DSO symptoms than with core PTSD symptoms, suggesting that 
ongoing structural adversity actively perpetuates complex trauma psychopathology 
beyond pre-migration trauma alone.Conclusion: Available evidence indicates 
marked variation in CPTSD prevalence across forcibly displaced populations 
rather than a single generalisable prevalence rate. Recruitment context accounts 
for part of this variation, but the limited and geographically uneven evidence 
base prevents global population-level inference. Future studies should use 
representative sampling and consistently report displacement, trauma, and 
post-migration characteristics to permit more informative explanations of 
between-population variation.

Plain Language Summary: Reported complex post-traumatic stress disorder (CPTSD) 
prevalence varied markedly across forcibly displaced populations and 
settings.Rates of CPTSD were especially high among people seeking treatment and 
among asylum seekers, suggesting that ongoing uncertainty and adversity may 
intensify psychological distress.Ongoing challenges after displacement, 
including poverty, legal insecurity, and social exclusion, were more strongly 
linked to complex trauma symptoms than past trauma alone, underscoring the need 
for both psychological care and social support.

The Impact of Oxide Transport Layers and Active Layer Composition on the Energy 
Band Alignment of the Frontier Orbitals in Non-Fullerene Acceptor Organic Solar 
Cells.

Vannucchi N(1)(2), Wang K(3)(4), Johansson FOL(1), Ho CY(3)(4), Ahmad M(3)(4), 
Kumari T(3), Cruguel H(2), Li Z(5), Félix R(6), Madsen M(3)(4), Lindblad A(1), 
Witkowski N(2).

Author information:
(1)Division of X-ray Photon Science, Department of Physics and Astronomy, 
Uppsala University, P.O. Box 256, 752 37Uppsala, Sweden.
(2)Institut des Nanosciences de Paris, Sorbonne Université, 4 Pl. Jussieu, 
F-75005Paris, France.
(3)Centre for Advanced Photovoltaics and Thin-Film Energy Devices, Mads Clausen 
Institute, University of Southern Denmark, Alsion 2, 6400Sønderborg, Denmark.
(4)SDU Climate Cluster, University of Southern Denmark, Campusvej 55, 
5230Odense, Denmark.
(5)Centre for Storage Ring Facilities, Department of Physics and Astronomy, 
Aarhus University, 8000Aarhus C, Denmark.
(6)Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie GmbH, 
Albert-Einstein-Str. 15, 12489Berlin, Germany.

The PM6:Y7 blend is a leading system for non-fullerene acceptor organic 
photovoltaics (OPV), achieving power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) above 16%. 
In bulk heterojunction architectures, it is typically combined with 
transition-metal-oxide transport/extraction layers to enable efficient 
energy-level alignment and charge transport toward the electrodes. However, 
accurate determination of the frontier orbital band alignment across the device 
interfaces remains challenging and is the subject of ongoing debate. This work 
aims to map the energetic landscape within an inverted OPV device architecture 
by investigating how variations in the PM6:Y7 donor-to-acceptor mass ratio (1:1, 
1:2, and 2:1) affect device performance and assessing the role of the oxide 
transport/extraction layers (MoO3 and ZnO). By combining valence band 
photoemission and X-ray absorption spectra relative to the Fermi level, we map 
the frontier orbital alignment between the blend active layer and the charge 
transport/extraction layers. Moreover, by exploiting the element selectivity of 
X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we are able to follow the evolution of the Y7 
acceptor LUMO level in the blends with different compositions. We observe a 
nonlinear behavior in the acceptor LUMO level with the blend composition and 
find that the 1:1 blend exhibits a relative maximum, reflecting a maximized 
effective donor-acceptor dipole interaction. Combining this trend with the 
optimal 1:1-1:2 composition window, identified from band alignment analysis, 
suggests that stronger molecular dipole interactions in the PM6:Y7 1:1 blend can 
promote a favorable electronic structure for efficient charge extraction and 
reduced recombination effects. These findings are consistent with the PCE trend 
resulting from our device measurements, providing a general framework for 
correlating frontier-orbital alignment with device performance and guiding the 
design and optimization of OPV architectures beyond the specific system 
investigated here.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied a single-centre cohort of biopsy-proven LN 
receiving add-on belimumab (2015-2025), with follow-up to 24 months and a 
paired-biopsy subgroup. We explored a study-specific stringent composite 
endpoint, deep clinical renal response (DCRR): urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 
(uPCR) <200 mg/g, absence of active glomerular haematuria and stable renal 
function, benchmarked against conventional CRR (uPCR <500 mg/g, stable renal 
function).
RESULTS: Of 51 patients, 43 not in CRR at initiation were analysed. DCRR was 
achieved by 38.5% at 12 and 53.8% at 24 months, versus 66.7% and 76.9% for CRR, 
in available-case analysis; deep responses accrued gradually (median 17.7 vs 7.5 
months), still increasing during the second year. Baseline uPCR was the only 
variable consistently associated with 12-month response. Renal response occurred 
alongside improvements in systemic activity, serological markers, and 
glucocorticoid exposure (SLEDAI-2K 13 to 2; anti-dsDNA 205 to 54 IU/mL and 
glucocorticoid reduction in 72%). In eight paired biopsies, activity index fell 
from 5.5 to 2 (p = 0.016) with attenuated glomerular C3 deposition (3+ to 1+, 
p = 0.031), whereas chronicity indices rose; these findings are exploratory 
given the small, uncontrolled sample.
CONCLUSION: Deep renal response, accompanied by regression of histological 
activity, appears achievable in a growing proportion of patients. However, its 
impact on long-term renal protection remains to be established.

Distilling Direct Effects via Conditional Differential Gene Expression Analysis.

Gu J(1), Skelton A(2), Staley J(2), Popson P(3), Peng L(3), Song X(4), Knowles 
J(3), He Z(3)(5)(6).

Author information:
(1)Department of Mathematics and Statistics, University of South Florida, Tampa, 
FL 33620, USA.
(2)UCB Pharma, Slough, United Kingdom.
(3)Department of Neurology and Neurological Sciences, Stanford University, 
Stanford, CA 94305, USA.
(4)Centre for Quantitative Medicine, Duke-NUS Medical School, Singapore.
(5)Quantitative Sciences Unit, Department of Medicine, Stanford University, 
Stanford, CA, 94305, USA.
(6)Department of Biomedical Data Science, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 
94305, USA.

MOTIVATION: Differential gene expression (DGE) analysis is foundational for 
interpreting RNA sequencing data, but it conflates direct biological effects 
with correlations propagated through gene co-expression. Across three RNA 
sequencing datasets (including a genome-scale perturb-seq experiment), we find 
that only a small fraction of differentially expressed genes have direct effects 
on the trait of interest, while the majority are undirected or passengers whose 
associations are mediated through other genes.
RESULTS: To distinguish direct effect genes, we introduce conditional 
differential gene expression (CDGE) analysis, a framework that tests for 
conditional rather than marginal association between each gene and the trait of 
interest. Implemented via the GhostKnockoff procedure with lasso regression, 
CDGE delivers false discovery rate control, operates on summary statistics from 
existing DGE pipelines, and accommodates batch effects. The genes identified by 
CDGE mediate the effects of most other differentially expressed genes and show 
stronger enrichment for known protein-protein interactions and biological 
pathways than DGE-identified genes. These results suggest that the field has 
been systematically over-interpreting DGE outputs, and that distinguishing 
direct from mediated effects is essential for prioritizing genes for functional 
follow-up and therapeutic development.
AVAILABILITY: To facilitate public access to knockoff-based CDGE analysis, we 
have developed the R package "KnockoffCDGE" as an integrated implementation, 
which is freely available at https://github.com/GuJQ5/KnockoffCDGE (DOI: 
10.5281/zenodo.23241517).

(1)Thoracic Oncology Ward, Cancer Center, and State Key Laboratory of

(3)Department of Biotherapy, Cancer Center, and State Key Laboratory of

(4)Institute of Respiratory Health, Frontiers Science Center for Disease-related

Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy is less effective in solid 
tumors than in selected hematologic malignancies because vascular, stromal, 
spatial, and immunosuppressive barriers restrict cell delivery and function. 
Local hydrogels and related biomaterials can convert a transient administration 
into a spatially organized depot, but their benefit depends on more than polymer 
identity. This review therefore combines a scenario-driven framework-depot 
versus bolus, intratumoral versus peritumoral placement, unresected versus 
postsurgical disease, and cell-loaded versus cell-free support-with a 
materials-centered analysis of formation, administration, time-dependent 
mechanics, architecture, degradation, biochemical presentation, and 
manufacturing. Direct evidence is distinguished from adjacent mechanistic 
evidence and design hypotheses. Across the available studies, the best-supported 
functions are improved delivered-cell recovery, regional persistence, controlled 
presentation of supportive cues, and enhanced antitumor activity in selected 
preclinical models. By contrast, universal material-property optima, clinically 
validated hydrogel-CAR-T products, and cryopreservation of a final cell-loaded 
depot have not been established. We define practical tests for gelation and 
device compatibility, productive egression, material-to-cell fitness, component 
attribution, and integrated-product safety. A materials-focused comparative 
table and a 30-study evidence map separate measured values from inferred 
mechanisms and identify where CAR-T cells were directly loaded, administered 
separately, manufactured in a matrix, or generated in situ. The resulting 
framework emphasizes that successful platforms must coordinate material 
behavior, CAR-T quality, anatomical placement, and clinical workflow rather than 
maximizing retention or chemical complexity alone.

Kostiuk K(1), Igumnov D(1), Fedichev P(1), Feizi A(1).

SUMMARY: Human genetic evidence provides a strong foundation for selecting drug

evaluates whether target-indication pairs supported by specific evidence sources

2.34 vs 2.55 without oncology). However, aggregating open clinical trial 
registries compresses this signal (RS = 1.52); this loss is primarily driven by 
the breadth of the indication data rather than the genetic evidence.
AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: ct-validation is implemented in Python (version 
3.11 or higher), distributed via pip, and freely available at

Calcium pyrophosphate deposition (CPPD) disease is a common crystalline 
arthritis that has historically been under-studied compared to other rheumatic 
diseases including gout. For decades, the presence of CPPD in joints has been

associations, and updates in the nomenclature for this crystalline arthritis.

Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) represent a clinically relevant 
cell source for skeletal muscle tissue engineering, yet transgene-free 
maturation remains challenging. Moreover, the potential of spheroids as building 
blocks for muscle engineering remains poorly defined. This study evaluated 
whether hiPSC-derived myogenic spheroids enhance biofabrication outcomes in an 
in vitro bio-artificial muscle (BAM) system compared to a conventional single 
cell approach.&#xD;Methods. CD56+ hiPSC-derived myoblasts were generated using a 
transgene-free protocol and differentiated toward 2D myotubes. In 3D, myoblasts 
were aggregated into 140-200 µm spheroids. Spheroids or single cells were 
encapsulated in a fibrin-based BAM, kept under tension using metal pins.

improving hiPSC differentiation efficiency, implementing spheroids in earlier

specific biofabrication contexts. &#xD.

Depth or Breadth? Domain-Specific Expertise and Cross-Domain Engagement in the 
Development of Scholarly Excellence.

Hartman LM(1).

Author information:
(1)Translational Research Program, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of 
Toronto.

Scholarly excellence is often equated with deep specialization within a single 
domain, a premise embedded in doctoral training, peer review, and 
academic-evaluation systems. However, research from the emerging "science of 
science," drawing on large-scale analyses of publications, citations, and career 
trajectories, suggests a more complex relationship between expertise, 
cross-domain engagement, and scholarly impact. This conceptual article 
synthesizes insights from the science of science, cognitive research on 
expertise, and organizational studies to examine the roles of domain-specific 
depth and different forms of cross-domain engagement in the development of 
scholarly excellence. We argue that depth and breadth are complementary 
capacities whose contributions vary across career stages and institutional 
contexts. We distinguish between multidisciplinary exposure, interdisciplinary 
integration, and, in rarer cases, transdisciplinary contributions that extend 
beyond existing boundaries. Domain-specific expertise supports technical 
mastery, credibility, and efficient knowledge accumulation, whereas integrative 
forms of cross-domain engagement facilitate recombination, problem reframing, 
and long-term intellectual influence. We further show how academic-reward 
structures favor depth while discounting integrative contributions. We conclude 
by outlining implications for doctoral education, faculty evaluation, and 
research policy, and by proposing a developmental framework that supports 
diverse trajectories of scholarly excellence.

BACKGROUND: Patient safety culture is a fundamental component of healthcare 
quality, yet empirical evidence on how it evolves during the early life cycle of

target in highly vascularized cancers such as clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

BACKGROUND: Clinical and molecular features of pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) 
according to involved metastatic sites have not been well characterized.

patients with metastatic PDAC at MD Anderson Cancer Center. Involved metastatic 
sites were extracted using natural language processing from imaging reports and 
verified by chart reviews. Overall survival (OS) and next generation sequencing 
(NGS) data were analyzed.

months), lung-only metastasis was associated with longer median OS (57.6 months,

Organofluorine compounds play an indispensable role in modern pharmaceuticals, 
agrochemicals, and functional materials. Fluorine-containing groups such as 
trifluoromethyl (CF3) and difluoromethoxy (OCF2H) can significantly enhance 
lipophilicity, metabolic stability, hydrogen-bonding capability, and 
target-binding affinity, thereby serving as key structural units in drug design 
and activity optimization. Among various trifluoromethylation strategies, 
(bpy)Cu(CF3)3-an isolable and storable high-valent Cu-CF3 species-exhibits 
tunable reactivity that enables direct trifluoromethylation, defluorinative

systematically summarizes recent advances in the application of (bpy)Cu(CF3)3 to 
fluorination and fluoroalkylation reactions and classifies these reactions into 
three mechanistic pathways: two-electron, single-electron radical, and 
difluorocarbene/fluoride pathways. The reaction mechanisms, structural 
characteristics, substrate scope, and synthetic applications are discussed in 
detail. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities in this field are 
discussed, aiming to provide guidance for the design of next-generation 
multifunctional fluorinating reagents and for the further development of 
organofluorine chemistry.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the retention and disease activity trajectories of 
subsequent biologic and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs 
(b/tsDMARDs) after Janus kinase inhibitor (JAKi) discontinuation in patients 
with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

subsequent b/tsDMARDs were initiated after JAKi discontinuation. Subsequent 
treatments were classified as TNF inhibitors (TNFi), anti-IL-6 receptor 
antibodies (aIL-6R), CTLA4-Ig and JAKi. Drug retention was stratified by the

BACKGROUND: Excess sugar consumption increases the risk for hypertension. We 
previously reported pilot data demonstrating that male mice drinking 2% sucrose 
water develop hypertension. However, the sucrose effects on left ventricular 
hypertrophy, kidney fibrosis, or sex difference in hypertension remain unclear. 
In the present study, we characterized the cardiac and renal pathology in a 
larger cohort including female mice to establish a novel sucrose-induced mouse 
model of hypertension associated with cardiovascular remodeling.
METHODS: Eight- to nine- week-old C57BL6 mice were given drinking water 
containing 2% sucrose or regular water for 4 weeks. Blood pressure was monitored 
using a tail-cuff system. Echocardiography was performed to evaluate cardiac 
remodeling. Sirius red staining was performed to evaluate heart and kidney 
fibrosis.
RESULTS: Male mice drinking the sucrose water developed hypertension (systolic 
blood pressure 122.0±1.3mmHGvs 162.2±4.3 mmHG at day 28). Sucrose treatment 
increased left ventricular wall thickness and induced perivascular fibrosis of 
the heart and kidney compared to control mice. Cardiac functions were preserved. 
In female mice, sucrose treatment induced milder hypertension than male mice 
(126.9±2.4 mmHg vs 143.7±3.2 mmHg at day 28). However, sucrose treatment caused 
similar degree of left ventricular hypertrophy in female mice.
CONCLUSION: Sucrose water induced hypertension, cardiac hypertrophy, and 
fibrosis of the heart and kidney in male mice. Female mice were partially 
protected from hypertension but not from cardiac hypertrophy. This mouse model 
represents a useful tool to investigate molecular mechanisms by which 
hypertension and end organ damage develop with excess sugar consumption.

Endo-ACDF with a rigid bendable burr for lesions located at posterior vertebral

Meng Y(1)(2), Gao S(2), Li T(2), Meng F(2), Li Z(2), Li W(2), Li M(1)(2), Niu

Author information:
(1)Hebei North University, Zhangjiakou, China.
(2)Department of Orthopedics, Hebei General Hospital, Shijiazhuang, China.

Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF), featuring a high fusion rate and 
favourable clinical outcomes, has always been the gold standard technique for 
treating cervical spondylosis.1 With significant advancements in optical 
technology, surgical instruments, and imaging systems, a variety of new devices 
have been successively applied in ACDF to enhance its advantages. However, 
lesions located at posterior vertebral body remains a challenge for ACDF. To 
solve this problem, we have explored a technique that utilizes 
endoscope-assisted ACDF (Endo-ACDF) with a rigid bendable burr. During the 
surgery, a rigid bendable burr is used to perform bone resection on the upper 
and lower endplates of the target intervertebral space to expose the lesion, and 
then other instruments are used to complete the removal. The rigid bendable burr 
and the clear endoscopic field of view can help the surgeon achieve complete 
removal of lesions through a single-segment discectomy, while maintaining the 
advantages of traditional ACDF. Compared with the use of nonbendable burr, we 
speculate that this technique can achieve the removal of posterior vertebral 
lesions while preserving more vertebral bone mass. Therefore, in this article, 
we elaborated in detail on the technique of utilizing Endo-ACDF with a rigid 
bendable burr.

Exploring the photovoltaic potential of perovskite-based multilayer solar cells: 
a computational investigation for solar energy applications.

Shakir I(1), Khan H(2), Amin MT(3), Hussain F(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Physics, Faculty of Science, Islamic University of Madinah, 
Madinah 42351, Saudi Arabia.
(2)Department of Chemical Engineering, College of Engineering, King Faisal 
University, Al-Ahsa 31982, Saudi Arabia. Khan@kfu.edu.sa.
(3)Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, College of Engineering, 
King Faisal University, Al-Ahsa 31982, Saudi Arabia.
(4)Department of Mechanical Engineering, Gachon University, Seongnam-si, 
Gyeonggi-do, 13120, South Korea. fiaz415@gachon.ac.kr.

Approximately 80% of our energy needs are fulfilled by fossil fuels, leading to 
carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions and environmental deterioration. Consequently, 
there is a growing global effort to identify sustainable alternatives for power 
generation. Among renewable resources, solar energy is prominent because of its 
minimal environmental impact. In this study, a numerical simulation of a 
lead-free organic-inorganic photovoltaic device based on the 
ZnSe/Na2AgRhBr6/CsSnI3/Spiro-OMeTAD heterostructure was performed using COMSOL 
Multiphysics. ZnSe functioned as an electron-transport layer, while Na2AgRhBr6 
and CsSnI3 served as absorber layers for efficient photon harvesting, and a 
hole-transport layer was formed using Spiro-OMeTAD. The device characteristics 
were assessed by varying the thickness of layers, temperature, and carrier 
concentrations. The simulation yielded a short-circuit current density of 31.192 
mA cm-2 when the acceptor concentration was 1 × 1020 cm-3. At the lowest 
investigated temperature of 275 K, the maximum power density (211.32 W m-2) was 
attained by the device, with a corresponding efficiency of 21.13%. The elevated 
temperatures caused thermal vibrations, resulting in reduced efficiency 
(19.01%). The resistance analysis revealed that for a device to work 
efficiently, lower series resistance, higher shunt resistance, and moderate 
values of the characteristic resistance are required. These results demonstrate 
the potential of the proposed structure for efficient photovoltaic applications.

Expanding the Chemical Space of Analytes in the 2G Crystalline Sponge Method: 
Size-Compensation Strategy for the Structural Analysis of Low-Polarity Small 
Molecules.

He W(1), Soliman L(2), Takezawa H(2), Fujita M(1)(3).

Author information:
(1)Division of Advanced Molecular Science, Institute For Molecular Science 
(IMS), Okazaki, Aichi, Japan.
(2)Department of Applied Chemistry, School of Engineering, Mitsui Link Lab 
Kashiwanoha 1, FS CREATION, The University of Tokyo, Kashiwa, Chiba, Japan.
(3)Tokyo College, UT Institutes for Advanced Study (UTIAS), Mitsui Link Lab 
Kashiwanoha 1, FS CREATION, The University of Tokyo, Kashiwa, Chiba, Japan.

The second-generation crystalline sponge (2G-CS) is a novel type of crystalline 
sponge that incorporates hollow cages as molecular recognition modules within 
its crystalline framework. This advanced CS technology provides a versatile 
structural analysis technique applicable to a broad range of guest 
molecules, regardless of polarity, with molecular weights ranging from 300 to 
1500. However, the method often fails when analyzing rather low-polarity small 
molecules (MW 200-300) due to an "unfavorable chemical space," where the host 
cavities are too large to facilitate sufficient host-guest interactions. Here we 
overcome this limitation by establishing a size-compensation strategy based on 
cage-mediated pair-selective bimolecular recognition. By co-encapsulating a 
target analyte with a shape-complementary "modulator" (e.g., phenanthrene), we 
precisely tailor the cavity environment without the need for chemical 
modification of the host. This adaptive approach enabled the x-ray structural 
determination of 24 of 30 low-polarity C15 analytes, predominantly 
sesquiterpenoids, including absolute configuration determination for selected 
chiral analytes. This work translates a decades-old molecular recognition 
phenomenon into a practical approach to crystallographic structure determination 
of low-polarity sesquiterpenoids.

Dual-channel digital surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy resolves GPC1(+)MUC4(+) 
single-exosome heterogeneity released by PANC-1 and BxPC-3 pancreatic cancer 
cells.

Wang X(1)(2), Zhang Z(3)(4), Zheng B(1)(5)(6).

Author information:
(1)Medical School, Faculty of Medicine, Tianjin University, Tianjin, 300072, 
China. binzheng0809@163.com.
(2)Emergency Department, Surgery Department, The 4th Center Hospital, Tianjin, 
300140, China.
(3)Academy of Medical Engineering and Translational Medicine, Department of 
Medicine, Tianjin University, Tianjin 300072, China.
(4)School of Biomedical Engineering and Technology, Tianjin Medical University, 
Tianjin 300070, China.
(5)The Province and Ministry Co-sponsored Collaborative Innovation Center for 
Medical Epigenetics, School of Biomedical Engineering and Technology, Tianjin 
Medical University, Tianjin, 300070, China.
(6)State Key Laboratory of Synthetic Biology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, 
300072, China.

Extracellular-vesicle populations average molecular signals across particles and 
can conceal rare, co-expressing phenotypes. We developed a dual-channel digital 
surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy platform that partitions individual 
CD63-captured vesicles and identifies glypican-1 (GPC1) and mucin 4 (MUC4) with 
4-mercaptobenzoic acid and 5,5'-dithiobis(2-nitrobenzoic acid) nanotags. The 
method was evaluated with eight independent batches from each of PANC-1, BxPC-3, 
HPDE and hTERT-HPNE cell models, seven blinded PANC-1/BxPC-3 mixtures, 
artificial-serum spikes and defined interferents. Across 49 256 single-vesicle 
events, beta-binomial modelling estimated GPC1+MUC4+ fractions of 13.8% for 
PANC-1 and 37.8% for BxPC-3. The adjusted between-model difference was 24.1 
percentage points (batch-cluster bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 21.6-26.5; P 
= 5.47 × 10-9). The response was linear against log10 concentration from 1.0 × 
105 to 1.0 × 109 particles per mL; the extrapolated detection-limit estimate was 
1.0 × 104 particles per mL, the overall precision was 6.49% coefficient of 
variation, and the mean artificial-serum recovery was 100.5%. Blinded mixture 
estimates tracked the nominal BxPC-3 fraction, while grouped nested 
cross-validation classified the four cell sources with 90.6% accuracy. Digital 
SERS agreed with nanoflow cytometry, giving a concordance correlation 
coefficient of 0.980 and a mean relative bias of 1.51%. These results show that 
marker co-occurrence, rather than bulk abundance alone, can distinguish 
pancreatic-cell vesicle phenotypes and provide a quantitative route for studying 
source-dependent vesicle heterogeneity.

Effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy on pain intensity and functional 
disability in chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

Stachelski RA(1), Rosângela Buzanello M(1), Flor Bertolini GR(1), Carvalho 
AR(1).

Author information:
(1)Biosciences and Health Program of the State University of Western Paraná 
(UNIOESTE), Cascavel, Brazil.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT) on 
pain intensity and functional disability in individuals with chronic low back 
pain (CLBP).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, LILACS, 
Google Scholar, and ProQuest were searched. The PICOS framework included 
individuals with CLBP receiving ESWT, compared with placebo, usual care, 
exercise, or physiotherapy. Randomized controlled trials reporting pain 
intensity and/or functional disability were included. Data on participant 
characteristics, interventions, comparators, and ESWT dosimetry were extracted.
RESULTS: Of 430 records identified, nine randomized controlled trials were 
included. Radial ESWT (rESWT) significantly reduced pain (SMD = -0.72; 95% CI 
-1.30 to -0.14; I2 = 76%), whereas focused ESWT (fESWT) showed benefit in one 
trial. Functional disability significantly improved overall (MD = -6.12; 95% CI 
-10.02 to -2.22; I2 = 75%), but the effect did not reach the minimal clinically 
important difference. Most studies evaluated outcomes only immediately 
post-intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicated influence of methodological 
quality and heterogeneity.
CONCLUSION: ESWT, particularly rESWT, may reduce pain in CLBP, but functional 
improvements are not clinically meaningful. Short follow-up and substantial 
heterogeneity limit the strength of recommendations. rESWT and fESWT should not 
be considered interchangeable.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION NUMBER: International Prospective Register of 
Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) under the registration number CRD420251085206.

Plain Language Summary: Extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) appears 
effective for short-term pain reduction in chronic low back pain.ESWT may be 
considered as an adjunct to conventional rehabilitation, particularly in 
non-responsive patients.Functional improvements are modest and may not reach 
clinically meaningful thresholds.ESWT should complement, not replace, 
exercise-based rehabilitation and patient education; standardized protocols are 
still needed.

Mutational Signatures and Hypermutation Phenotypes Define Bladder Cancers 
Arising in Waterpipe and Cigarette Smokers.

Shamseddine A(1), Abbas N(2), Eichholz J(3), Chatila WK(4), Walch H(3), Mahfouz 
R(5), Basar M(6), Schultz N(3), Solit D(4), Al Mahmasani L(1), Charafeddine 
M(1), Al Darazi M(5), Rosenberg JE(4), Iyer G(6), Bochner BH(3), Pietzak EJ(3), 
Reuter VE(3), Zaatari G(7), Abou-Alfa GK(3), Al-Ahmadie H(8).

Author information:
(1)American University of Beirut Medical Center Beirut Lebanon.
(2)American University of Beirut Medical Center.
(3)Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center New York, NY United States.
(4)Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center New York, New York United States.
(5)American University of Beirut Medical Center Lebanon.
(6)Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center New York United States.
(7)American University of Beirut Beirut Lebanon.
(8)Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center NY, NY United States.

Bladder cancer is a major malignancy worldwide. Although cigarette smoking is 
the leading modifiable risk factor, the contribution of waterpipe smoking (WPS), 
which is increasingly popular globally and often misperceived as safer, remains 
unclear. In 2019, Lebanese males had the highest bladder cancer incidence in the 
Arab world (five times the global average), prompting investigation of WPS as a 
potential carcinogen. We performed a cross-sectional genomic analysis of 
patients with exclusive WPS and urothelial carcinoma treated at the American 
University of Beirut Medical Center (n=250 screened; 14 exclusively WPS), 
integrating targeted sequencing (MSK-IMPACT®) and whole-exome sequencing (TEMPO 
pipeline). Tumor mutational burden (TMB), microsatellite instability, mutational 
signatures, and oncogenic alterations were assessed. Previously profiled bladder 
cancer tumors from cigarette smokers and non-smokers at Memorial Sloan Kettering 
Cancer Center (n=751) served as comparators. MSK-IMPACT® successfully profiled 
13 tumors. WPS-associated tumors exhibited a numerically higher median TMB than 
cigarette (20 vs. 10 mut/Mb; p=0.10, q=0.2), with 38.5% classified as 
MSS-hypermutated, a phenotype associated with elevated mutational load despite 
microsatellite stability. Common mutations included TERT promoter (62%), TP53 
and FGFR3 (46%), and PIK3CA (38%). APOBEC mutational signatures predominated 
across all cohorts, suggesting shared mutagenic processes, while 
chromatin-modifying gene alterations were less frequent. PD-L1 expression was 
generally low. Implications: Exclusive WPS induces bladder tumors with overall 
genomic features resembling cigarette-associated disease, yet with numerically 
higher TMB and enrichment of MSS-hypermutated phenotypes. These findings provide 
novel mechanistic evidence of tobacco-related carcinogenesis beyond cigarettes 
and highlight potential biomarker relevance for immunotherapy in a globally 
rising exposure group.

An intervention mapping study to adapt trauma-focused social adjustment therapy 
for adolescents with trauma-related interpersonal difficulties.

Ong SE(1), Forooshani SA(2), Izadikhah Z(1), Krishnamoorthy G(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Psychology and Wellbeing, University of Southern Queensland, 
Ipswich, Australia.
(2)Adelaide University Online, Adelaide University, Adelaide, Australia.

Background: Interventions that effectively reduce posttraumatic stress disorder 
(PTSD) symptoms are not necessarily effective in improving interpersonal 
functioning among adolescents with complex trauma histories. Despite the 
developmental significance of interpersonal functioning during adolescence, 
there remains a lack of interventions specifically targeting trauma-related 
interpersonal difficulties in this population.Objective: This study aimed to 
adapt the Trauma-Focused Social Adjustment Therapy (TF-SAT) protocol for 
adolescents. The original protocol was developed for young adults with trauma 
histories, and the adaptation focuses on adolescents with complex trauma 
histories and trauma-related interpersonal difficulties.Method: The TF-SAT 
intervention protocol was systematically adapted using the Intervention Mapping 
Protocol (IMP), informed by two meta-analyses, a quantitative study, and 
relevant theoretical literature.Results: The intervention development process 
resulted in an adapted TF-SAT protocol targeting trauma-related cognitive (i.e. 
cognitive avoidance), emotional (i.e. dissociation and alexithymia), and 
interpersonal (i.e. social problem-solving) processes hypothesised to underlie 
interpersonal difficulties. The original TF-SAT framework was extended to 
propose differential cognitive and emotional pathways across different trauma 
symptom patterns. Intervention implementation and evaluation procedures were 
also developed to guide future feasibility and effectiveness testing, as well as 
ongoing protocol refinement.Conclusions: This study provides a theory- and 
evidence-informed intervention protocol designed to address trauma-related 
interpersonal difficulties among adolescents with complex trauma histories. The 
adapted TF-SAT protocol provides a foundation for future feasibility testing and 
the development of more targeted, developmentally appropriate trauma 
interventions tailored to different trauma response patterns.

Plain Language Summary: Trauma-Focused Social Adjustment Therapy (TF-SAT) was 
systematically adapted to address trauma-related interpersonal difficulties in 
adolescents.The adapted intervention aims to target cognitive, emotional, and 
interpersonal processes potentially underlying trauma-related interpersonal 
difficulties.The original framework was extended to incorporate therapeutic 
strategies tailored to different trauma response patterns.

Drastically reducing the cost of the XsTD-DFT family of methods using a minimal 
auxiliary basis set (ηXsTD-DFT) to efficiently treat ultra large systems.

Liger A(1), Satisha A(1), Beaujean P(2), de Wergifosse M(1).

Author information:
(1)Theoretical Chemistry Group, Molecular Chemistry Materials and Catalysis 
Division (MOST), Institute of Condensed Matter and Nanosciences, Université 
Catholique de Louvain, Louvain-la-Neuve, Belgium. 
marc.dewergifosse@uclouvain.be.
(2)Laboratory of Theoretical Chemistry, Unit of Theoretical and Structural 
Physical Chemistry, Namur Institute of Structured Matter, Université de Namur, 
Namur, Belgium. pierre.beaujean@unamur.be.

This contribution introduces the ηXsTD-DFT family of methods in which the exact 
integral simplified time-dependent density functional theory (XsTD-DFT) is 
adapted considering the resolution of identity (RI) approximation with a minimal 
auxiliary basis set. The main goal of this is to provide to the community the 
most efficient simplified quantum chemistry method to compute excited states and 
response properties for all-atom quantum mechanical (AQM) methodologies. This 
auxiliary set is composed of 1s orbitals with the square of the atomic chemical 
hardness η scaled by a global factor θ as parameters into the exponent. This 
approximation allows a drastic reduction of the computational cost. The θ in the 
ηXsTDA was globally fitted to reproduce reference excitation energies and 
oscillator strengths for the 17 first molecules of the XsTD-DFT benchmark set. 
The method was then tested for the entire set of 77 molecules. For B3LYP, the 
ηXsTDA scheme deviates on average by only 0.12 eV with respect to TDA, similarly 
to the TDA-ris scheme. Thanks to the fitting of the θ parameter that absorbs 
some of the error, MADs with respect to TDA are slightly lower than those for 
the XsTDA method. For this set, on average, the ηXsTDA is 147 times faster than 
TDA, outperforming both TDA-ris (32×) and XsTDA (82×) schemes. These results 
highlight the computational efficiency and robustness of the ηXsTD-DFT and 
suitability for applications in AQM methodologies. To showcase the performance 
of the method, three increasingly-large systems were selected: a mixed 
donor/acceptor ligand Pd(II) double cage (395 atoms), photoactive yellow protein 
(PYP, 1931 atoms), and bacteriorhodopsin (bR, 3835 atoms). In all cases, 
striking comparisons with respect to experiment were obtained. For bR, the 
largest system of this study, one- and two-photon absorption spectra were 
computed at the ηXsTD-DFT level in only 2 h 25 min on a desktop computer using 
∼500 GB of RAM. The ηXsTDA shows also excellent performance in computing 
core-valence excitations, well reproducing the oxygen K-edge NEXAFS spectrum of 
collagen. A spin-flip version was also implemented and tested for 9 diradicals 
and a large μ-hydroxo-bridged dimer of corrole tape Ga(III) complexes 
derivative.

A biopolymer modified Pd nanocomposite for CO gas-free carbonylation reactions 
and in silico profiling of synthesized molecules.

Chamanmalik MI(1), Bharadhwaj SC(1), Salimath SV(1), Kumbhar PD(1), Patil SA(1).

Author information:
(1)Centre for Nano and Material Sciences, JAIN (Deemed-to-be University), Jain 
Global Campus, Kanakapura, Bangalore-562112, Karnataka, India. 
p.siddappa@jainuniversity.ac.in.

The utilization of a CO-gas-free carbonylation approach using palladium-based 
nanocomposites provides a green avenue for the synthesis of value-added 
chemicals. In this article, palladium nanoparticles were impregnated on a 
biopolymer chitosan-modified Mg-Al layered double hydroxide (MgAl-LDH@CS) to 
develop a stable and sustainable MgAl-LDH@CS@Pd nanocomposite. The comprehensive 
physicochemical analyses confirmed a Pd loading of 8.26 wt/wt%, as determined by 
ICP-OES, with a uniform dispersion of palladium nanoparticles on the 
chitosan-modified MgAl-LDH support, thereby imparting enhanced structural 
robustness to the nanocomposite. The MgAl-LDH@CS@Pd nanocomposite demonstrates 
exceptional catalytic performance for CO-gas-free and ligand-free carbonylation, 
enabling both alkoxy- and aminocarbonylation reactions with a greener CO 
surrogate and achieving higher conversions and yields. The prominent efficiency 
of the nanocomposite could be attributed to its structural integrity, which 
additionally enabled a broad range of substrate studies with excellent tolerance 
for different functional groups. It was noted that the MgAl-LDH@CS@Pd 
nanocomposite was recycled for up to five successive cycles, confirming its 
durability and feasibility, offering a viable opportunity for a CO-gas-free 
carbonylation reaction. Furthermore, the synthesized molecules were screened for 
ADMET profiles, wherein compounds 4b, 6h, 6i, 6j, 7a, and 7b exhibited 
favourable pharmacokinetic and drug-like characteristics. Moreover, the screened 
molecules were further evaluated for in silico molecular docking with (1JNX and 
2XAO) target protein receptors to determine their binding efficacy and subjected 
to TD-DFT studies to gain molecular insights.

VASP plugins: linking the Viennaab-initioSimulation Package with Python.

Vijay S(1), Marsman M(2), Kresse G(2)(3), Schlipf M(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chemical Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, 
Powai, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400076, India.
(2)VASP Software GmbH, Berggasse 21, 1090 Vienna, Austria.
(3)Faculty of Physics and Center for Computational Materials Science, University

Implementing novel features and experimental algorithms into widely adopted 
density functional theory (DFT) codes is frequently hindered by complex legacy 
architectures and the use of compiled languages such as Fortran. These 
production codes, while optimized for high-performance computing clusters, 
present significant hurdles for software development and rapid prototyping, 
often requiring deep expertise in the code's internal structure to modify. To 
address this challenge, we present a Python plugin infrastructure for the 
Viennaab-initioSimulation Package (VASP) that combines computational efficiency 
with the flexibility of high-level scripting. Our architecture uses a C++ 
intermediate layer andto expose VASP data asarrays via shared memory buffers, 
ensuring high performance without data duplication. We implement two categories 
of plugins: those that modify quantities at the end of each converged 
self-consistent field (SCF) cycle, such as,and, and those that operate during 
the SCF cycle, such as. We demonstrate the utility of our implementation through 
three applications, structure relaxation using thelibrary, implementing an 
implicit solvent model, and adding thedispersion corrections. For a 
representative post-SCF plugin (), this coupling introduces a callback overhead 
of well underper ionic step relative to a natively linked implementation. This 
infrastructure effectively bridges the gap between high-performance electronic 
structure routines and the widespread scientific Python ecosystem.

Lysozyme solvation in monohydric alcohols with low water content: a calorimetric 
and preferential solvation study.

Sirotkin VA(1).

Author information:
(1)Kazan Federal University, A. M. Butlerov Institute of Chemistry, Kremlevskaya 
str., 18, Kazan, 420008, Russia. vsir@mail.ru.

The main focus of this work is to clarify how protein macromolecules become 
solvated in monohydric alcohols with low water content. Alcohols with varying 
hydrophobicity (1-propanol, ethanol, and methanol) were used as model organic 
liquids. Two independent experimental techniques (isothermal immersion 
calorimetry and water/alcohol adsorption) were employed to provide complementary 
thermodynamic functions of the preferential solvation of hen egg-white lysozyme 
in alcohols with low and high water contents at 298.15 K. The advantage of this 
approach is that the enthalpies and Gibbs energies of water and alcohols can be 
simultaneously studied during the deep dehydration of lysozyme. Three distinct 
composition regimes are operative in water-alcohol mixtures. Protein 
stabilization, as a result of the preferential hydration of lysozyme, was 
observed in the water-rich region, which was driven by a positive change in 
entropy, with the residual enzyme activity values close to 100%. Alcohol-induced 
inactivation of lysozyme was detected in the middle region, with the residual 
catalytic activity close to zero. In the water-poor region, the bulky ethanol 
and 1-propanol molecules, unlike methanol, were preferentially excluded from the 
protein surface. In the water-rich region, protein stabilization was driven by 
an exothermic (favorable) enthalpy change. The pairwise (adsorbate-adsorbate) 
interaction coefficients demonstrated that alcohols with longer alkyl chains 
stabilize water-water association at low water contents to a larger extent than 
methanol with a shorter alkyl chain. The results obtained may be highly relevant 
for elucidating the distinct roles of water bound to the amphiphilic surfaces of 
biomacromolecules.

prickle-mediated epilepsy in flies is a brain-derived neurodevelopmental defect.

Lilienthal AJ(1), Nukala KM(1), Williquett B(1), Manak JR(1)(2)(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biology, University of Iowa, Iowa City, IA, USA.
(2)Department of Pediatrics, University of Iowa Carver College of Medicine, Iowa 
City, IA, USA.
(3)Lead contact.

Damaging DNA variants in PRICKLE genes cause epilepsy from flies to humans. 
While classic work, primarily in flies, has demonstrated that PRICKLE proteins 
work with other planar cell polarity proteins to polarize epithelial sheets, the 
function of PRICKLE proteins in the nervous system is still unclear and may play 
distinct roles in the nervous system of different organisms. We thus sought to 
compare and contrast Drosophila prickle with PRICKLE genes in vertebrate systems 
in order to identify unifying roles across species. First, we find that similar 
to expression of the mouse Prickles, fly prickle is expressed in a wide variety 
of CNS neurons, in particular post-mitotic maturing neuroblasts and neurons. 
However, unlike in the mouse, fly prickle is not enriched in the axon initial 
segment (AIS) but is broadly distributed across the entire length of the 
expressing neurons. Second, we find that targeted expression of the 
prickle-spiny-legs (pksple) isoform in a) glutamatergic neurons or b) a region 
analogous to the human brain stem in pksple mutant animals suppresses seizures, 
implicating dysfunction of these neurons in seizure progression. Strikingly, 
targeting prickle expression to only larval/pupal stages can fully rescue adult 
seizures, demonstrating that this form of epilepsy can be considered a 
neurodevelopmental defect such that an abnormality that occurs during 
development leads to a disorder that is late-onset. Finally, targeting pksple 
expression exclusively in pksple mutant brains suppresses seizures, 
demonstrating that, similar to humans, prickle-associated epilepsy arises in the 
brain. Consistent with this result, removal of the head of pksple mutants also 
significantly reduces seizures, confirming that brain neuronal dysfunction 
contributes to fly seizures.

A structured framework for assessment of rehabilitation and sick-listing (STARS) 
- experiences among healthcare professionals.

Sundkvist EM(1)(2), Jansson I(1), Sverker A(3)(4), Karlsson E(2), Rosenberg 
L(1), Israelsson Larsen H(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Rehabilitation, School of Health and Welfare, Jönköping 
University, Jönköping, Sweden.
(2)Department of Health, Medicine, and Caring Sciences, Linköping University, 
Linköping, Sweden.
(3)Department of Activity and Health, Linköping University, Linköping, Sweden.
(4)Pain and Rehabilitation Center, Linköping University, Linköping, Sweden.

BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: The sick-listing process is often perceived uncertain and 
unclear by both patients and staff. To improve the process, a framework for 
structured assessment of rehabilitation and sick-listing (STARS) has been 
developed in the South-Eastern Healthcare Region in Sweden. STARS consists of 
seven methodological tools supporting healthcare professionals in sick-listing 
and rehabilitation. The purpose of this study was to investigate how primary 
healthcare staff clinically involved in the sick leave process experience 
working according to STARS.
METHOD: We used a qualitative design conducting focus group discussions (n = 7) 
with healthcare staff (n = 37). Eligible participants were physicians, 
rehabilitation coordinators and other healthcare professionals working 
clinically with patients. The focus group conversations were analyzed with 
thematic content analysis according to Braun and Clarke. The study was 
registered in clinicaltrials.gov (number NCT05655962).
RESULT: The participants' experience of working according to STARS were 
described by the overarching theme 'STARS as an enabling structure' formed by 
three themes and eight subthemes. The themes were 'Clearer roles and 
responsibilities through the RECO function', 'Moving from individual work to 
teamwork' and 'A more active and personalized rehabilitation and sick-listing 
process'.
CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that implementing the STARS framework may 
provide a supportive structure for a uniform and consistent way of working 
across primary healthcare centers. By clarifying RECOs' roles and strengthening 
interprofessional collaboration, the framework may support a more 
patient-centered approach across services.

Defining selective chelation windows for Ca(2+)-Mg(2+) discrimination in saline 
matrices: comparative performance of EDTA and EGTA.

Albalawi GH(1)(2), Albalawi I(2), Ayaz M(2), Alotaibi FA(1), Iqbal M(1)(3), 
Almashhori AG(1), Alharthi FA(4), Michael C(4)(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chemistry, Faculty of Science, University of Tabuk, Tabuk 
71491, Saudi Arabia. g_halbalawi@ut.edu.sa.
(2)Artificial Intelligence and Sensing Technologies (AIST) Research Center, 
University of Tabuk, Tabuk 71491, Saudi Arabia.
(3)Zero Emission Technologies Innovation Center, University of Tabuk, Tabuk, 
47913, Saudi Arabia.
(4)Water Technologies Innovation Institute & Research Advancement (WTIIRA), 
Saudi Water Authority(SWA), PO Box 8284, Al-Jubail 31951, Kingdom of Saudi 
Arabia.
(5)School of Science and Technology, The University of New England, Armidale, 
New South Wales 2351, Australia.

Selective discrimination of Ca2+ from Mg2+ remains challenging in saline 
matrices because both ions exhibit similar coordination behaviour and their 
chelation responses can be altered by solution conditions. EDTA and EGTA were 
systematically compared for Ca2+ and Mg2+ complexometric titration over 0-1000 
ppm. The effects of pH (3-12), temperature (25-45 °C), NaCl (0-30 mM), KCl 
(0-19 000 mg L-1), SO42- (0-2700 mg L-1), and K+ (0-600 mg L-1) were evaluated 
in individual and equimolar Ca2+ : Mg2+ systems. Both chelators produced highly 
linear calibrations, but their responses differed markedly. EGTA increased Ca2+ 
calibration sensitivity by 32.9% relative to EDTA and showed substantially 
greater thermal stability. EDTA responded to both metals across pH 3-12, whereas 
EGTA produced no measurable Mg2+ endpoint at pH 3-7. Crucially, this 
Ca2+-selective response persisted in mixed Ca2+ : Mg2+ solutions containing 
chloride, sulphate, and potassium at the investigated concentrations. The study 
identifies an experimentally observed operational selectivity interval at pH 
3-7, defined by differential endpoint detectability, in which Ca2+ remains 
measurable with EGTA while no stable visual Mg2+ endpoint is obtained under the 
investigated conditions. This matrix-resilient behaviour provides a practical 
basis for selective calcium analysis and future Ca2+/Mg2+ separation strategies.

Emissions from industrial sites: how to improve exposure assessment for local 
residents? Feedback on a national level in France.

Karr G(1), Bonnard R(1).

Author information:
(1)Ineris (French National Institute for Industrial Environment and Risks), Parc 
Technologique Alata, Verneuil-en-Halatte (60), France. 
roseline.bonnard@ineris.fr.

To obtain an environmental operating permit for an industrial site, studies must 
be carried out to demonstrate that the projected environmental emissions will 
not cause health issues for neighboring populations. In France, for industrial 
sites associated with the highest expected risks, these studies include an 
application of the health risk assessment (HRA) approach. In this context, 
carrying out an HRA has two main high-stakes objectives: (i) ensuring that there 
is no "unacceptable" health risk for people living near the site and (ii) 
identifying the main determinants of total health risk (substances, locations of 
interest, and pathways) to be able to prioritize a monitoring program and 
efforts to reduce emissions. Exposure assessments play a central role in HRAs. 
However, despite the guidelines described in reference guides, recurring 
inappropriate practices-not corresponding to what is expected of a rigorously 
conducted HRA, whether intentionally or not-are still observed in HRAs, and 
these practices may have a high influence on the quantified health risks. Seven 
feedbacks are presented and discussed, corresponding to proposals for best 
practice: (i) clarifying the objective of the assessment and therefore the 
rationale of the choices made, (ii) specifying and taking into account how the 
data used were produced, (iii) quantitatively assessing uncertainties, (iv) 
taking atmospheric deposition into account when selecting locations of interest, 
(v) considering the potential contamination of plants by dry gaseous deposits, 
(vi) calculating non-threshold risks over a lifetime only, and (vii) considering 
reasonably possible uses. These good practices are based on feedback gathered at 
the national level in France. They are not specific to the French context, 
however, and are just as useful for managing emissions from industrial sites in 
other countries.
