BACKGROUND: Acute Aortic Syndrome (AAS) is a life-threatening condition that 
presents diagnostic challenges due to variable clinical presentations. Limited 
data exists regarding Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) utilisation patterns 
and outcomes for patients with suspected AAS in Irish emergency departments 
(ED). This study evaluates trends in CTA utilisation and positivity rate for 
patients with suspected AAS presenting to a level 4 hospital ED.
METHODS: A retrospective single-centre chart review was conducted of all adult 
patients (≥ 16 years) who underwent CTA aorta imaging requested by emergency 
medicine physicians in Tallaght University Hospital between January 2018 and 
December 2025. Patient demographics, imaging findings, time metrics, disposition 
and mortality were analysed.
RESULTS: Among 457,735 ED attendances, 797 eligible CTA aorta studies were 
performed. There was a 2.86 fold increase in CTA scans done across the study 
period from 37 studies in 2018 to 106 in 2025. Overall positivity rate for AAS 
was 2.76% (n = 22). Acute aortic dissection accounted for 77% of positive cases 
(n = 17), followed by penetrating atherosclerotic ulcers (n = 3) and intramural 
hematomas (n = 2). Overall mortality among patients with confirmed AAS was 
27.27%.
CONCLUSION: This study highlights the low positivity rate of CTA aorta scans in 
an Irish ED but high mortality of patients diagnosed with acute aortic syndrome. 
Increasing CTA utilisation, alongside the overall low incidence of AAS, suggests 
opportunities to improve diagnostic efficiency.

BACKGROUND: Prostatic artery embolization (PAE) is an emerging minimally 
invasive treatment option for symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) 
which is not yet widely available nor reported on in the Irish setting.
AIMS: This study aimed to summarise our single-centre experience implementing 
PAE in an Irish setting.
METHODS: Medical records of patients who underwent bilateral PAE at our 
institution between January 2020 and July 2024 were retrospectively reviewed and 
those with incomplete primary outcome data or prostate cancer were excluded.
RESULTS: Twenty-one participants were included. The mean age was 72.8 ± 8.9 
years and mean prostatic volume was 188 ± 106 cc. In those who were catheter 
dependent pre-operatively (n = 13), eleven (84.6%) were voiding independently at 
a median longest follow up of 292 [20-1112] days (P < 0.0001). In those who 
could void independently at baseline (n = 8), the mean IPSS decreased from 
22.1 ± 5.8 at baseline to 8.3 ± 7 at a median follow-up of 68 [43-184] days post 
procedure (P < 0.001). There was one severe (Society for Interventional 
Radiology grade > 2) complication from which the participant made a full 
recovery to baseline.
CONCLUSIONS: Our experience demonstrates PAE as a feasible and promising 
treatment option for BPH-related symptoms and catheter-dependence in the Irish 
setting. Notably, the strength of conclusions is limited by the small, 
single-centre, retrospective nature of this study and future research is 
required to establish safety and efficacy.

With the application of nanoscale materials, nanomedicine is redefining and 
improving the delivery of pharmaceuticals and molecular bioimaging probes, 
providing novel approaches to disease diagnosis, management, and treatment. As 
in many other fields, renewable materials are becoming increasingly important in 
nanomedicine because they offer sustainable alternatives to fossil-based 
resources and are often biodegradable and biocompatible. Additionally, these 
materials are replenishable in nature, and some can be derived or recovered from 
industrial and agro-industrial waste streams. In this review, we critically 
evaluate nanomedicines fabricated from renewable polymers, polysaccharides, 
proteins, and lipids for drug delivery and biomedical imaging, together with 
their physicochemical and biological characterization. Particular emphasis is 
placed on how material origin and physicochemical properties influence 
formulation performance and clinical readiness. Rather than considering 
renewable origin alone as an indicator of translational suitability, the major 
material classes are compared in terms of source consistency, biodegradability, 
imaging functionality, and regulatory maturity. Recent developments reported 
during 2020-2026 are discussed, with particular attention to the objectives and 
key findings of the developed nanomedicines. Additionally, their applications in 
the treatment of various diseases and in biomedical imaging are reviewed. The 
review also highlights key translational barriers, and evidence gaps that must 
be addressed to advance renewable material-based nanomedicines from 
proof-of-concept systems toward reproducible, scalable, and clinically relevant 
products.

Previously, we reported the discovery, chemical characterization, and 
preliminary anticancer activity of Miliusin B (MB), a natural neolignan from 
Miliusa sessilis, demonstrating cytotoxicity and selectivity against the human 
cervical cancer cell line HeLa. In the present study, we further investigated 
the underlying anticancer mechanisms of MB. Consistent with our earlier 
findings, MB exhibited sub-micromolar cytotoxicity toward HeLa cells with 
>60-fold selectivity relative to non-cancerous controls. Mechanistic analyses

5 µM. Finally, combinatorial assays with standard cisplatin (Cis)-based cervical 
cancer chemotherapeutics (Cis monotherapy and Cis doublet regimens) demonstrated 
that MB enhanced the anti-proliferative effects of all treatments tested. 
Collectively, these findings highlight MB as a promising selective cytotoxic and 
anti-migratory candidate for further development as a potential therapeutic 
agent against cervical cancer.

rotation is often recommended to improve soil health. However, few field studies 
have followed both soil bacterial diversity and fumonisin-producing pathogens 
over several seasons in tropical no-till systems. We compared continuous maize,

quantified by qPCR in soil and in maize stalks left on the soil surface. In the

although statistical power was low (n = 4 plots; post-hoc power 12-61%). 
Community composition differed among seasons and was associated with antecedent 
precipitation as Actinobacteria were most abundant in the driest season. In the 
fourth season, a continuous-soybean history was associated with higher bacterial 
richness and Shannon diversity in the maize rhizosphere at tasselling than a 
rotation history, whereas bulk-soil diversity did not differ among land uses. A 
rotation history was associated with lower fum1 abundance in bulk soil. In 
contrast, continuous maize was associated with lower fum1 in stalks (third 
season), less stalk rot and fewer infected grains. Soil and crop residues 
therefore responded differently to rotation. Given the single site and limited 
plot-level replication, these findings should be regarded as 
hypothesis-generating.

molecular heterogeneity and therapeutic resistance, highlighting the need to 
identify alternative pathways involved in tumor progression. Purinergic 
signaling, particularly the conversion of extracellular ATP to immunosuppressive 
adenosine mediated by ectonucleotidases CD39 (NTPDase1) and CD73

Sagittal spinopelvic parameters in children and adolescents: a retrospective 
cross-sectional radiographic study from Turkey.

Dursun MA(1), Kaya S(2), Karabak B(2), Kocaslan M(3).

Author information:
(1)Tavsanli State Hospital, Kavakli, Haci Ahmet Kiri Mevkii No:1, Kütahya, 
Kütahya, 43300, Türkiye. drmehmetalidursun@gmail.com.
(2)Erzurum City Hospital, Erzurum, Turkey.
(3)Afyonkarahisar State Hospital, Afyonkarahisar, Turkey.

BACKGROUND: Sagittal spinal parameters are used to assess upright alignment 
during growth.
OBJECTIVE: To describe sagittal spinopelvic parameters and assess their 
associations with age and sex in children and adolescents in Turkey.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study at a single 
tertiary orthopedic center included 344 children aged 6-17 years (186 boys, 158 
girls) who underwent clinically indicated standing full-spine radiography. 
Pelvic incidence, pelvic tilt, sacral slope, lumbar lordosis, thoracic kyphosis, 
sagittal vertical axis, cervical vertebra (C) 2 tilt, thoracic vertebra (T) 4 
tilt, lumbar vertebra (L) 1 tilt, T4 pelvic angle, and L1 pelvic angle were 
assessed. Age-group comparisons and age- and sex-adjusted linear models were 
used.
RESULTS: Mean (standard deviation) pelvic incidence, pelvic tilt, sacral slope, 
lumbar lordosis, and thoracic kyphosis were 45.4 (12.3)°, 11.3 (6.9)°, 34.2 
(10.4)°, 57.5 (13.8)°, and 46.0 (13.4)°, respectively; sagittal vertical axis 
was 46.6 (27.6) mm. C2, T4, and L1 tilts were 5.0 (2.9)°, 10.4 (4.6)°, and 9.0 
(4.7)°; T4 pelvic angle and L1 pelvic angle were 4.1 (3.1)° and 3.4 (3.1)°. 
Lumbar lordosis showed the largest adjusted age coefficient (1.81°/year; 95% 
confidence interval (CI) 1.28-2.34; adjusted R2=0.121). T4 pelvic angle and L1 
pelvic angle did not differ significantly across age groups (P=0.308 and 
P=0.966).
CONCLUSION: In children and adolescents without radiographic spinal or pelvic 
deformity, lumbar lordosis had the clearest cross-sectional association with 
age. No statistically significant age-group differences were detected for T4 
pelvic angle or L1 pelvic angle. These data provide clinically relevant 
standing-radiograph reference data for sagittal spinopelvic parameters.

Social vulnerability as a key dimension of frailty in Alzheimer's disease and 
frontotemporal dementia.

Panzavolta A(1), Dodich A(2), Picascia M(3), Ramusino MC(3), Perini G(3), Meli 
C(2), Funghi G(2), Costa A(3)(4), Cerami C(5)(6).

Author information:
(1)Istituti Clinici Scientifici Maugeri IRCCS, Brain e-Health Aging (BeA) 
Laboratory, Department of Neurorehabilitation, Milan, Italy. 
andrea.panzavolta@icsmaugeri.it.
(2)Center for Mind/Brain Sciences CIMeC, University of Trento, Rovereto, Italy.
(3)Unit of Behavioral Neurology and Dementia Research Center, IRCCS Mondino 
Foundation, Pavia, Italy.
(4)Department of Brain and Behavior, University of Pavia, Pavia, Italy.
(5)Istituti Clinici Scientifici Maugeri IRCCS, Brain e-Health Aging (BeA) 
Laboratory, Department of Neurorehabilitation, Milan, Italy.
(6)IUSS Cognitive Neuroscience (ICoN) Center, Scuola Universitaria Superiore 
IUSS, Pavia, Italy.

OBJECTIVES: Frailty and social vulnerability are two dynamic and 
multidimensional constructs able to capture susceptibility to adverse health 
outcomes related to physical decline or arising from weakened social 
connections, support, and resources. While the burden of physical frailty in 
dementia has been well established, the impact of disadvantageous social 
conditions is less known. In this study, we investigated these dimensions in 
Alzheimer's disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) with the aim of 
describing possible common and individual trajectories.
METHODS: 47 individuals living with AD and 24 with FTD, as well as 66 healthy 
control (HC) subjects, were included. An ad hoc developed 60-item bidimensional 
Frailty Index (FI) questionnaire was administered to explore the two dimensions. 
Global (gFI), physical (pFI) and social (sFI) FI scores were derived and 
compared among groups with ANCOVA, including age and education as covariates. 
Pearson's correlation analyses explored the relationship between FI scores and 
clinical-neuropsychological measures.
RESULTS: No group effect was observed for pFI. Both patient groups showed 
significantly higher gFI and sFI levels compared to HC. sFI positively 
correlated with disease severity and cognitive patterns in both dementias.
CONCLUSION: Our findings point to an urgent need for person-centered care 
strategies that extend beyond biomedical models. Deficits in social connections 
and support represent a primary and common underpinning of vulnerability in 
dementia populations. A timely periodic evaluation of non-physical determinants 
of vulnerability may contribute to a better and earlier detection of maladaptive 
trajectories with a consequent beneficial effect on the well-being and burden of 
the patient-caregiver dyad.

MUC5B/TGF-β/KL-6 Signaling in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Genetic 
Susceptibility to Profibrotic Progression and Clinical Perspectives.

Venkatesharao SM(1), Jayaraman A(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pharmacology, M. S Ramaiah College of Pharmacy, Faculty of 
Pharmacy, M. S. Ramaiah University of Applied Sciences, Gnanagangothri Campus, 
New BEL Road, M. S. R. Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka, 560054, India.
(2)Department of Pharmacology, M. S Ramaiah College of Pharmacy, Faculty of 
Pharmacy, M. S. Ramaiah University of Applied Sciences, Gnanagangothri Campus, 
New BEL Road, M. S. R. Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka, 560054, India. 
anbu.pg.ph@msruas.ac.in.

Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic lung disorder 
strongly mediated by genetic susceptibility and aberrant epithelial repair 
mechanisms. Among the identified genetic factors, the MUC5B promoter 
polymorphism rs35705950 represents the most significant and frequently 
replicated risk variant associated with both familial and sporadic IPF. This 
review focuses on the mechanistic role of MUC5B dysregulation in promoting 
epithelial dysfunction and profibrotic signalling, with particular emphasis on 
its interaction with transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signalling and 
KL-6-associated epithelial injury. Excessive MUC5B expression within distal 
airways disrupts mucociliary homeostasis, prolongs epithelial exposure to 
inhaled toxic stimuli, and enhances persistent alveolar stress, thereby 
facilitating chronic epithelial injury and aberrant tissue repair. Sustained 
epithelial damage subsequently activates TGF-β-mediated SMAD signalling 
pathways, promoting fibroblast activation, myofibroblast differentiation, and 
extracellular matrix deposition. Emerging evidence further suggests a close 
relationship between MUC5B-associated epithelial dysfunction and elevated KL-6 
expression, indicating that KL-6 may function as a downstream biomarker 
indicating ongoing epithelial injury and fibrotic progression. The proposed 
MUC5B/TGF-β/KL-6 mechanistic signaling provides an integrated molecular network 
linking genetic susceptibility, epithelial dysfunction, biomarker elevation, and 
progressive fibrosis in IPF. In addition, telomere-related and 
surfactant-associated gene mutations further lead to epithelial instability and 
impaired regenerative capacity. Together, these interconnected molecular 
mechanisms provide significant insights into IPF progression and may support the 
development of biomarker-driven prognostic approaches and targeted precision 
therapies for improved disease management.

Possible involvement of a villin-like protein in chloroplast anchoring in 
spinach mesophyll cells.

Takamatsu H(1), Morii M(1), Yokota E(2), Sakamoto Y(3)(4), Takagi S(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biological Sciences, Graduate School of Science, The University 
of Osaka, Toyonaka, Osaka, 560-0043, Japan.
(2)Department of Life Science, Graduate School of Life Science, University of 
Hyogo, Harima Science Park City, Hyogo, 678-1297, Japan.
(3)Department of Biological Sciences, Graduate School of Science, The University 
of Osaka, Toyonaka, Osaka, 560-0043, Japan. yuki_sakamoto@shinshu-u.ac.jp.
(4)Department of Biology, Faculty of Science, Shinshu University, Matsumoto, 
Nagano, 390-8621, Japan. yuki_sakamoto@shinshu-u.ac.jp.

Chloroplasts maintain specific intracellular distribution patterns in response 
to environmental conditions to maximize photosynthetic performance and prevent 
photodamage. We previously proposed that a chloroplast anchoring mechanism 
functions to fix chloroplasts at appropriate positions and reported that this 
machinery is actin-dependent and regulated by Ca2+ (Takamatsu and Takagi 2011). 
In the present study, we examined the possible involvement of villin, a 
Ca2+-sensitive actin-binding protein (ABP), in chloroplast anchoring in spinach 
mesophyll cells. Two antibodies against lily villin proteins, anti-P135ABP and 
anti-P115ABP, recognized polypeptides of 135 and 120 kDa, respectively, in 
spinach leaves. These proteins were purified as Ca2+-sensitive ABPs by DNase I 
affinity chromatography. Immunolocalization analysis revealed distinct labeling 
patterns for the two proteins. Whereas immunostaining with the anti-P115ABP 
antibody produced randomly distributed punctate signals in the cytoplasm, the 
135-kDa villin-like protein was preferentially localized around chloroplasts and 
was also detected on isolated chloroplasts. Biochemical analyses further 
revealed that both villin-like proteins bound phosphatidic acid (PA) and 
phosphoinositides. Functional analysis further showed that addition of the 
anti-P135ABP antibody induced detachment of a substantial number of chloroplasts 
and reduced actin filaments on plasma membrane (PM) ghosts. These results 
indicate that at least two distinct Ca2+-sensitive villin-like proteins exist in 
spinach leaves and suggest that the 135-kDa isoform contributes to chloroplast 
anchoring by maintaining actin organization around chloroplasts.

Seasonal variation in the content of β-asarone and related phenylpropenes and 
their associated transcriptomic profiles in Acorus calamus.

Ganbat O(1), Kashimoto N(1), Matsumoto M(1), Ogawa T(1), Koeduka T(2), Ulziibat 
B(3)(4), Okazawa A(5).

Author information:
(1)Graduate School of Agriculture, Osaka Metropolitan University, 1-1 
Gakuen-cho, Naka-ku, Sakai, 599-8531, Osaka, Japan.
(2)Graduate School of Science and Technology for Innovation, Yamaguchi 
University, 1677-1 Yoshida, Yamaguchi, 753-8515, Yamaguchi, Japan.
(3)Department of Research and R&D Policy, Mongolian Academy of Sciences, 
Enkhtaivan Avenue 54b, Bayanzurkh District, 13330, Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.
(4)Institute of Botanic Garden and Research, Mongolian Academy of Sciences, 
Peace Avenue-54B, Bayanzurkh District, 13330, Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.
(5)Graduate School of Agriculture, Osaka Metropolitan University, 1-1 
Gakuen-cho, Naka-ku, Sakai, 599-8531, Osaka, Japan. okazawa.atsushi@omu.ac.jp.

Acorus calamus L. is a monocotyledonous medicinal plant possessing bioactive 
compounds, including β-asarone, which exhibits anti-microbial, neuroprotective, 
and antioxidant effects. However, the biosynthetic pathway of β-asarone in A. 
calamus remains poorly understood. This study investigated seasonal changes in 
the accumulation of β-asarone and related phenylpropenes and their associated 
transcriptome. Leaf, root, and rhizome samples were analyzed by gas 
chromatography, and leaf samples representing periods with the lowest and 
highest levels of β-asarone and its related phenylpropene (Z)-methylisoeugenol 
were selected for comparative transcriptome analysis. Kyoto Encyclopedia of 
Genes and Genomes pathway enrichment analysis revealed distinct gene expression 
patterns during β-asarone accumulation, including the downregulation of most 
phenylpropanoid biosynthetic genes and upregulation of the genes encoding 
4-coumarate-CoA ligase and caffeoyl-CoA O-methyltransferase. Conversely, these 
genes exhibited different expression patterns during the periods of high 
(Z)-methylisoeugenol accumulation. This study suggests that β-asarone 
biosynthesis involves different pathways from predicted phenylpropene routes and

[Specific respiratory tract infections in acute cough-when is targeted diagnosis 
and treatment required?].

[Article in German; Abstract available in German from the publisher]

Holzinger F(1), Gehrke-Beck S(2).

Author information:
(1)Institut für Allgemeinmedizin, Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin, 
Charitéplatz 1, 10117, Berlin, Deutschland. felix.holzinger@charite.de.
(2)Institut für Allgemeinmedizin, Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin,

In most cases, acute cough is caused by a self-limiting respiratory infection. 
However, symptoms, pre-existing conditions, or environmental factors may 
indicate a cause requiring treatment; red flags point to dangerous courses, the 
NEWS2 score can assess the risk of septic deterioration, and the CRB-65 score 
supports decision-making regarding hospital admission in pneumonia. Pneumonia 
cannot be reliably diagnosed clinically but is unlikely in the absence of 
clinical indicators. Laboratory tests can support the decision for antibiotic 
treatment, while the diagnosis is confirmed by chest X‑ray. An infection-related 
exacerbation of pre-existing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) should 
be specifically treated. In influenza, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), and 
respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), complications and severe courses may occur 
more frequently in risk populations. However, routine diagnostic confirmation of 
these pathogens is not useful in the absence of therapeutic consequences. With 
appropriate exposure and waning vaccine protection, pertussis can also be 
a cause of acute cough in adults.

Verläufe häufiger. Ein regelhafter diagnostischer Nachweis dieser Erreger bei

Antibody-drug conjugates and tumor immunity in breast cancer.

Kashiwagi S(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Breast Surgical Oncology, Graduate School of Medicine, Osaka 
Metropolitan University, 1-4-3 Asahi-machi, Abeno-ku, Osaka, 545-8585, Japan. 
spqv9ke9@view.ocn.ne.jp.

Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) combine antigen-directed delivery with cytotoxic 
or immunostimulatory payloads. Their antitumor activity can involve direct 
tumor-cell killing, but the extent to which conventional ADCs remodel human 
breast-cancer immunity remains incompletely defined. This review critically 
separates established cytotoxic mechanisms from immune-mediated effects and 
incorporates emerging STING agonist ADCs, neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) 
trafficking, and quantitative antigen measurement. A focused narrative synthesis 
of mechanistic, translational, and clinical literature was performed, 
emphasizing primary studies of HER2-, TROP2-, and HER3-directed ADCs and 
tumor-targeted STING agonist conjugates. Peer-reviewed studies were prioritized; 
congress abstracts and non-peer-reviewed sources were used only when 
specifically requested or when no full report was available. Evidence was 
classified as preclinical, translational, or clinical, and causal claims were 
restricted accordingly. Conventional ADCs first produce antigen-dependent 
internalization, intracellular payload release, and direct cytotoxicity. 
Bystander killing can extend cytotoxic exposure beyond antigen-high cells. In 
selected preclinical systems, payload-induced stress or DNA damage can generate 
immunogenic-cell-death signals, engage cGAS-STING signaling, preserve Fcγ 
receptor-dependent effector functions, and support antigen presentation. These 
effects are platform- and context-dependent and are not uniformly demonstrated 
in patients. By contrast, STING agonist ADCs and immune-stimulating antibody 
conjugates are designed to deliver an innate agonist to antigen-bearing tumors 
and can activate STING in tumor and myeloid compartments in mouse models; their 
clinical value in breast cancer remains investigational. FcRn primarily rescues 
pinocytosed IgG in acidic endosomes and governs exposure and tissue disposition; 
wild-type IgG uptake at neutral pH is predominantly fluid-phase, whereas 
residual neutral-pH FcRn binding in engineered variants may increase uptake when 
FcRn is abundant. Current HER2 and TROP2 immunohistochemistry does not quantify 
accessible membrane antigen, internalization, or immune contribution with 
sufficient precision. Quantitative continuous scoring and membrane-localization 
metrics are promising but require prospective, breast-cancer-specific 
validation. ADC efficacy should not be interpreted as proof of immune 
activation. A rigorous framework must measure antigen abundance and 
localization, ADC delivery and trafficking, payload pharmacology, and serial 
immune changes, while separately evaluating target-independent toxicity. 
Mechanism-linked sampling and prospective validation are required before immune 
biomarkers, FcRn-related variables, or quantitative antigen metrics can guide 
routine ADC selection.

BACKGROUND: This correspondence is a commentary to the recently published report 
from the OSAN trial by Fiedorowicz et al. but with applicability to the broader 
research involving blue-blocking glasses and patients in a manic episode.
METHOD: Clinical studies on dark therapy are still rare, and we read with great 
interest the report from the OSAN trial published in Journal of Affective 
Disorders the 1st of April 2026.
RESULTS: The sample was significantly higher in manic symptoms, more medicated 
and less adherent to the intervention than in preceding studies on effects of 
dark therapy for mania. Efforts to comply with the gold standard of blinding of 
raters may have come with the cost of underestimating the symptom level. 
Extended intervention period (2 weeks) may have caused the extensive loss to 
follow up (35/42 (83%) at 2 weeks). Several issues with the statistical methods 
and data reporting make the results difficult to interpret.
CONCLUSIONS: The statistical power of the OSAN trial may have been substantially 
reduced by attrition and multiple sources of variance to the data. The results 
from the trial should be interpreted with caution.

Enhancing soil organic carbon mapping in Northeast China by incorporating 
laboratory-based soil hyperspectral measurements into spatial covariates and 
machine learning.

Yan G(1)(2), Chen J(1)(2), Xie E(1)(2), Zhang Y(1)(2), Zou T(1)(2), He J(1)(2), 
Tian K(1)(2), Hu W(1)(2)(3), Zeng Y(4), Zhao Y(5)(6)(7).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Soil Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Nanjing, 211135, 
China.
(2)University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, 100049, China.
(3)University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Nanjing, 211135, China.
(4)Laboratory of Karst Environmental Evolution and Ecological Security, 
Institute of Geochemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Guiyang, 550081, China.
(5)Institute of Soil Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Nanjing, 211135, 
China. yczhao@issas.ac.cn.
(6)University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, 100049, China. 
yczhao@issas.ac.cn.
(7)University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Nanjing, 211135, China. 
yczhao@issas.ac.cn.

Information on the spatial distribution of soil organic carbon (SOC) is 
essential for environmental monitoring and assessment. However, limitations of 
commonly used environmental covariates and satellite multispectral data 
constrain the accurate prediction of SOC at large spatial scales. In this study, 
647 topsoil (0-20 cm) samples and the corresponding Vis-NIR hyperspectral data 
were collected from croplands in Northeast China. Machine learning (ML) 
algorithms, including random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) 
and light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), were combined with environmental 
covariates, satellite multispectral covariates, and hyperspectral-informed 
intermediate variables derived by spatializing the principal components of 
laboratory-based hyperspectral measurements to predict SOC across croplands in 
Northeast China. The results showed similar spatial patterns of SOC across the 
ML models, with high SOC contents in the north and northeast and low contents in 
the west and southwest. Incorporating multisource satellite data, spectral 
indices, and moving-window averages of satellite multispectral data improved the 
prediction performance of SOC, with the R2 of RF model (R2 = 0.55) increased by 
11%, in comparison with those using satellite multispectral data alone 
(R2 = 0.44). While combining environmental covariates and the developed 
hyperspectral-informed intermediate variables in the RF model yielded the 
highest R2 of 0.61. Although environmental covariates were the most important 
predictors of SOC (e.g., mean annual temperature accounts for 32% of the total 
variable importance), the developed hyperspectral-informed intermediate variable 
PC2 accounted for the additional 16% importance of the SOC prediction. These 
results highlight the importance of incorporating laboratory-based soil 
hyperspectral information into spatial covariates to improve large-scale SOC 
mapping.

Mapping Perioperative Vulnerability and Optimization in Hepatectomy: A 
Bibliometric and Scientometric Analysis of Sarcopenia, Frailty, and 
Prehabilitation.

Liao L(1), Qiao J(2), Mao R(1), Huang X(1), Huang J(1), Yao L(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of General Surgery, Punan Hospital, Pudong New Area , Shanghai, 
China.
(2)Department of Ophthalmology, The Second Hospital of Lanzhou University, 
Lanzhou, Gansu Province, China.
(3)Department of General Surgery, Punan Hospital, Pudong New Area , Shanghai, 
China. ylwy992421@126.com.

PURPOSE: Risk assessment before hepatectomy is no longer based only on tumor 
burden, liver function, and technical resectability. Muscle status, frailty, 
nutrition, exercise capacity, and prehabilitation are now discussed more often 
in this setting. This study reviewed how these topics appear in the hepatectomy 
literature and how they relate to the more established body composition 
literature.
METHODS: Relevant publications were retrieved from the Science Citation Index 
Expanded of the Web of Science Core Collection. CiteSpace (version 6.4.R1), 
VOSviewer (version 1.6.20), and RStudio (version 2025.05.1 + 513) were used to 
analyze publication trends, collaboration networks, journal distributions, 
co-citation structures, keyword co-occurrence, citation bursts, and temporal 
patterns.
RESULTS: A total of 498 publications were included. Publication output increased 
during the study period, especially after 2021. Japan, China, and the United 
States contributed the most papers, whereas several European countries had 
stronger positions in the collaboration network. Sarcopenia and body composition 
remained the main basis of this literature. Frailty, functional vulnerability, 
nutritional support, exercise, and prehabilitation appeared more often in recent 
years, but collaboration between institutions and author groups was still 
incomplete.
CONCLUSIONS: Current hepatectomy research in this area is still centered on body 
composition-based risk assessment. Newer studies have added frailty, functional 
reserve, nutrition, exercise capacity, and prehabilitation to the same 
perioperative discussion. Future work should test practical pathways that 
connect these measures with surgical decision-making, patient selection, and 
preoperative optimization.

Nephrometry scores differ in their association with warm ischemia time during 
robot-assisted partial nephrectomy: comparison of RENAL, RPN, PADUA, and SPARE.

Komeya M(1), Kobayashi K(2), Jikuya R(2), Tatenuma T(2), Noguchi G(2), Ito H(2), 
Ito Y(2), Muraoka K(2), Hasumi H(2), Makiyama K(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Urology, Yokohama City University Hospital, Yokohama, Japan. 
komeyam@yokohama-cu.ac.jp.
(2)Department of Urology, Yokohama City University Hospital, Yokohama, Japan.

Nephrometry systems are widely used before robot-assisted partial nephrectomy 
(RAPN), but their relation to intraoperative complexity may differ. We compared 
RENAL, RPN, PADUA, and SPARE using continuous warm ischemia time (WIT) and 
assessed whether the scores added information beyond tumor diameter and routine 
clinical variables. We retrospectively analyzed 579 single-tumor RAPN cases with 
complete data for all four scores (2016-2023). Associations with WIT were 
assessed using Spearman correlations and patient-level paired bootstrap 
comparisons. Tumor diameter was evaluated as an additional comparator. 
Incremental value was assessed by adding each nephrometry score to a baseline 
model containing tumor diameter, age, sex, body mass index, laterality, surgeon 
experience, surgical approach, and fiscal year. Model performance was evaluated 
using adjusted R² and 10-fold cross-validation. RPN showed the strongest 
correlation with WIT (ρ = 0.553), followed by tumor diameter (ρ = 0.519). The 
difference between them was small (Δρ = 0.034, 95% CI - 0.020 to 0.089). RPN had 
the highest adjusted R² (0.341) among single-predictor models. All four scores 
improved the baseline model; the numerically largest improvement was observed 
with PADUA (Δ adjusted R²=0.096; Δ cross-validated RMSE = - 0.397 min). RPN had 
the strongest stand-alone association with WIT, but its correlation was not 
clearly stronger than that of tumor diameter. Each nephrometry score added 
information beyond tumor diameter and routine clinical variables, with the 
magnitude of incremental improvement differing among systems.

Methylmalonic Acid in Skeletal Aging and Osteoporosis: Linking Vitamin B12 
Metabolism to Mitochondrial Dysfunction.

Ji T(#)(1), Pei T(#)(1), Yang J(2), Wan T(1), Zhang Y(1), Ma X(1), He M(1), Gu 
T(1), Lu R(3), Guo W(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Medical Laboratory, Xianyang Central Hospital, Xianyang, 
Shaanxi, 712000, China.
(2)Department of Orthopedics, Xianyang Central Hospital, Xianyang, Shaanxi, 
712000, China.
(3)Department of Hepatobiliary Surgery, Xianyang Central Hospital, Xianyang, 
Shaanxi, 712000, China. 1027098857@qq.com.
(4)Department of Clinical Laboratory, Tangdu Hospital, The Fourth Military 
Medical University, Xi'an, Shaanxi, 710038, China. guowentao2012@126.com.
(#)Contributed equally

Methylmalonic acid (MMA) is a functional marker of vitamin B12 insufficiency and 
an emerging metabolic factor associated with skeletal aging and osteoporosis. 
This review synthesizes epidemiological, experimental, and mechanistic evidence 
linking the vitamin B12-MMA axis to impaired bone homeostasis. Population 
studies associate elevated circulating MMA with lower bone mineral density, 
higher odds of osteoporosis, and lower knee extensor strength, while disturbed 
vitamin B12 metabolism has also been linked to altered bone turnover. 
Experimental MMA exposure and models of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (MMUT) 
deficiency reveal context-dependent abnormalities in mitochondrial respiration, 
energy metabolism, redox balance, and quality control. These findings provide a 
rationale for investigating skeletal effects, but the broader consequences of 
vitamin B12 deficiency and inherited metabolic defects should be distinguished 
from direct MMA actions in bone cells. Concurrent homocysteine accumulation and 
reduced S-adenosylmethionine availability may further impair collagen 
cross-linking, epigenetic regulation, and skeletal remodeling. These pathways 
support a metabolic-mitochondrial framework in which functional vitamin B12 
deficiency contributes to bone loss through coordinated effects on 
bioenergetics, redox balance, cell fate, and extracellular matrix quality. MMA 
may therefore complement vitamin B12, homocysteine, renal function, and 
conventional bone markers in the assessment of skeletal metabolic risk. 
Prospective human studies, bone-specific mechanistic experiments, and 
intervention trials are needed to establish causality, clinically useful 
thresholds, and the skeletal benefits of correcting vitamin B12 deficiency or 
targeting mitochondrial dysfunction.

Osteocyte-Derived Extracellular Vesicles: Bridging the Gap in Skeletal 
Physiology and Pathophysiology.

Yang D(1)(2), Yang J(3).

Author information:
(1)Houston Methodist Neal Cancer Center, Houston Methodist Research Institute, 
Houston Methodist Hospital, Houston, TX, 77030, USA.
(2)Institute for Common Diseases, JinJiang Hospital, School of Medicine, Xiamen 
University, Xiamen, 361102, China.
(3)Houston Methodist Neal Cancer Center, Houston Methodist Research Institute, 
Houston Methodist Hospital, Houston, TX, 77030, USA. 
jyang2@houstonmethodist.org.

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Osteocytes are the most abundant cells in bone and serve as 
central skeletal regulators. Recent findings from our and other groups 
demonstrate that beyond soluble mediators, osteocytes communicate by releasing 
extracellular vesicles (EVs). This review provides a systematic overview of 
osteocyte-derived EVs and highlights their importance in diagnostic and 
therapeutic innovation.
RECENT FINDINGS: Accumulating evidence has linked osteocyte mechanotransduction 
to EV biogenesis and secretion. Mechanically induced calcium oscillations and 
signaling pathways impact load-induced EV release. Under normal conditions, 
osteocyte-derived EVs contribute to local and systemic intercellular 
communication within experimental models, whereas their direct role in 
immune-microenvironment remodeling remains insufficiently defined. In 
pathological states, alterations in osteocyte EV release and cargo composition 
are associated with both benign diseases and malignancies. Engineered 
osteocyte-derived EVs and EV-inspired delivery systems are being investigated as 
cell-free therapeutic platforms for skeletal regeneration. Continued research in 
osteocyte-derived EVs will deepen understanding of bone communication networks 
and resolve the principal conceptual and technical challenges.

Continuous and asymmetric dorsal-ventral abundance associations along the wing 
in feather mite communities.

Takagi M(1), Iwasaki M(2), Yasuda N(3), Shiraiwa S(2), Katoh T(2), Takaku G(4).

Author information:
(1)Graduate School of Science, Hokkaido University, Sapporo, 060-0806, Hokkaido, 
Japan. mtakagi@eis.hokudai.ac.jp.
(2)Graduate School of Science, Hokkaido University, Sapporo, 060-0806, Hokkaido, 
Japan.
(3)Faculty of Science, Hokkaido University, Sapporo, 060-0806, Hokkaido, Japan.
(4)Hokkaido University of Education, Sapporo, 002-8501, Hokkaido, Japan.

Feather mites are permanent ectosymbionts that occupy discrete feather 
microhabitats; however, little is known about how associations between dorsal 
and ventral taxa vary along continuous wing gradients. We examined feather-level 
spatial abundance associations between dorsal and ventral feather mites along 
the proximodistal axis of the wing in the Siberian Rubythroat (Calliope 
calliope) via nonlinear mixed-effects models. Dorsal feather mites (Trouessartia 
calliope) were largely absent from distal outer remiges (flight feathers) and 
increased toward proximal body-side remiges, whereas ventral feather mites 
(Proctophyllodes sp.) exhibited a positional gradient along the wing. When 
averaged across positions, the dorsal and ventral abundances showed only weak 
overall associations. However, position-specific analyses revealed that the 
dorsal-ventral slope was positive in distal outer remiges, declined toward 
mid-wing positions, and approached weakly negative values in the innermost 
secondaries. Because dorsal abundance was minimal distally, positive slopes in 
that region should not be interpreted as evidence of stable coexistence and may 
reflect responses to environmental constraints associated with distal wing 
positions. This position-dependent association was detected in breeding adult 
birds but not in juvenile birds, suggesting age-related differences in 
within-host spatial organization that may reflect the shorter time since mite 
transmission to juveniles and subsequent community assembly. Feather mite 
abundances were bilaterally symmetrical and showed no consistent effects of sex, 
date, or year, suggesting that host-level morphological stability provides a 
consistent spatial template for parasite organization. Together, these findings 
demonstrate that within-host feather mite assemblages exhibit spatially 
heterogeneous abundance associations along the wing, highlighting the importance 
of fine-scale spatial variation for understanding the organization and potential 
ecological relationships of cooccurring parasite taxa.

Robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for uterus transplantation: a 
systematic review of surgical techniques, donor safety, and recipient outcomes.

Baradwan S(1), Latifah HM(2), Hafedh B(2), Alyafi M(2), Badghish E(3), Aazam 
L(4), Awadh N(5), Alshahrani MS(6).

Author information:
(1)Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, King Faisal Specialist Hospital and 
Research Center, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. dr.saeed_bardwan@yahoo.com.
(2)Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, King Faisal Specialist Hospital and 
Research Center, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
(3)Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Maternity and Children Hospital, 
Makkah, Saudi Arabia.
(4)Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, University of Jeddah, Jeddah, Saudi 
Arabia.
(5)Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Faculty of Medicine, King Abdulaziz 
University, Rabigh, Saudi Arabia.
(6)Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Faculty of Medicine, Najran 
University, Najran, Saudi Arabia.

Uterus transplantation (UTx) has emerged as a promising treatment for women with 
absolute uterine factor infertility (AUFI), enabling pregnancy and live birth 
with their own genetic offspring. Living-donor uterus procurement remains the 
most technically demanding component of the procedure. Robotic-assisted donor 
hysterectomy has been introduced to improve surgical precision, reduce donor 
morbidity, and preserve graft quality, while recipient implantation is performed 
via laparotomy. This systematic review evaluated current evidence on 
robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for UTx, focusing on surgical 
techniques, donor safety, recipient outcomes, and reproductive success. 
Databases and trial registries were searched from inception through June 2026. 
Six studies reporting 29 unique robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomies 
across five countries met the inclusion criteria. All procedures used the da 
Vinci Xi robotic platform. Operative time and estimated blood loss decreased 
with increasing surgical experience, while major donor complications 
(Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher) were less frequent in later series. Among 
cases with reported follow-up, no graft loss was observed; restoration of 
menstruation, embryo transfer, clinical pregnancy, and live birth were achieved, 
including ten live births in the largest programme. Robotic-assisted 
living-donor hysterectomy for uterus transplantation appears technically 
feasible and has been associated with viable grafts and successful pregnancies 
in highly selected cases. However, major donor complications, including ureteric 
injury requiring reimplantation and bilateral oophorectomy, were observed, and 
the true incidence of donor morbidity remains uncertain. Current evidence 
remains limited to small observational studies, and these findings support 
careful evaluation within structured, multidisciplinary programmes and 
international registries rather than widespread expansion.

Pial arteriovenous fistulas (PAVFs) are rare high-flow vascular lesions 
requiring precise characterization of the fistulous angioarchitecture before 
treatment. We report a pediatric PAVF in which an enlarged artery adjacent to 
the fistula initially appeared suspicious for additional fistulous supply. 
Superselective angiography demonstrated normal cortical arterial arborization 
and parenchymal perfusion without early venous drainage, confirming that the 
enlarged vessel did not participate directly in the arteriovenous shunt. 
Selective coil embolization achieved complete immediate occlusion of the 
fistulous communication while preserving the adjacent normal cortical arterial 
supply. This case illustrates that arterial enlargement alone does not establish 
participation in a PAVF and highlights an angiographic pitfall relevant to 
treatment planning.

Dual-potential ratiometric electrochemiluminescence sensor based on 
ZnO@g-C(3)N(4) and GO@luminol for metronidazole detection.

Han P(1), Tian L(2), Ma G(1), Wang W(1), Jiang H(1), Mao H(1), Li R(1), Ma T(1), 
Lu J(1), Wang J(3).

Author information:
(1)College of Chemistry, Changchun Normal University, Changchun, 130032, P.R. 
China.
(2)College of Chemistry, Changchun Normal University, Changchun, 130032, P.R. 
China. tianli308cc@163.com.
(3)College of Chemistry, Changchun Normal University, Changchun, 130032, P.R. 
China. zixi21@163.com.

A dual-potential ratiometric electrochemiluminescence (RECL) sensor for 
metronidazole (MNZ) detection has been developed. The sensor was constructed by 
sequentially depositing a ZnO@g-C3N4 cathodic layer serving as the response 
signal and a graphene oxide(GO)@luminol anodic layer serving as the reference 
signal. In the persulfate system, the maximum initial cathodic signal was 
obtained from ZnO@g-C3N4, with the addition of MNZ, the cathodic signal was 
selectively quenched whereas the anodic signal remained unchanged. The mechanism 
was verified by radical-scavenging experiments. Under optimal conditions, the 
ratiometric signal (Ia/Ic) exhibited a linear relationship with the logarithm of 
MNZ concentration (lgCMNZ) over 1.0 × 10- 10 to 1.0 × 10- 6 mol L- 1. The limit 
of detection was 3.3 × 10- 11 mol L- 1 (S/N = 3). The proposed RECL sensor was 
further applied to real samples, demonstrating its feasibility and potential for 
MNZ determination in complex matrices.

Levetiracetam versus valproate for new-onset or previously treated but 
inadequately controlled epilepsy in children: a systematic review and 
meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

Alharran AM(1), Alsaleeli KM(2), Alkhamis AS(2), Taqi BA(2), Altaher R(3), 
Alenezi RA(4), Mohammad HF(4), Dashti RH(2), Mugheer AM(4), Alshemeri RG(4), 
Alarki AA(4), Abdalkareem SO(2).

Author information:
(1)College of Medicine and Medical Sciences, Arabian Gulf University, Manama, 
Kingdom of Bahrain. Dr_alharran@outlook.com.
(2)Kuwait Institute for Medical Specialization, Kuwait City, Al Asimah, Kuwait.
(3)Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland, Dublin, Ireland.
(4)College of Medicine and Medical Sciences, Arabian Gulf University, Manama, 
Kingdom of Bahrain.

PURPOSE: To compare the efficacy and safety of levetiracetam versus valproate in 
children with new-onset or previously treated but inadequately controlled 
epilepsy.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane 
Library from inception to April 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) 
comparing levetiracetam versus valproate in children (aged 0-18 years) with 
new-onset or previously treated but inadequately controlled epilepsy. Outcomes 
included seizure freedom, exploratory analyses of survival time without seizure 
and time to first seizure recurrence, change in aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 
levels, and adverse events.
RESULTS: Eight RCTs involving 1,000 participants were included. Seizure freedom 
did not differ significantly between treatments (5 studies, 655 participants; 
RR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.83-1.09; P = 0.45; I² = 59.5%; low-certainty evidence). 
Exploratory time-related outcomes favored valproate but were limited by 
low-certainty evidence and inadequate handling of censoring. Levetiracetam was 
associated with lower AST levels, although this did not establish superior 
hepatic safety, and with fewer overall adverse events and less weight gain.
CONCLUSIONS: No significant difference in seizure freedom was detected between 
levetiracetam and valproate, although the low-certainty finding was sensitive to 
one trial. Time-related outcomes favored valproate but were exploratory and 
limited by inadequate handling of censoring. Levetiracetam was associated with 
fewer overall adverse events and less weight gain, while behavioral and hepatic 
safety remained uncertain. Treatment should be individualized based on patient 
and medication-related factors.

Effectiveness and Influencing Factors of Drama-Based Interventions for Social 
Skills in Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A 
Meta-Analysis.

Geng K(1), He Y(2).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Special Education, Faculty of Education, Beijing Normal 
University, 100875, Beijing, China.
(2)Institute of Special Education, Faculty of Education, Beijing Normal 
University, 100875, Beijing, China. 202321010106@mail.bnu.edu.cn.

Deficits in social skills are a core challenge for children and adolescents with 
autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This meta-analysis examined the effects of 
drama-based interventions on social skills in this population and explored 
potential moderators. A systematic search was conducted in Web of Science, 
PubMed, ProQuest, EBSCO, and CNKI. Overall effects were estimated using Hedges' 
g, and subgroup analyses and meta-regressions were conducted to examine 
heterogeneity. Publication bias and sensitivity analyses were also assessed. 
Sixteen controlled studies involving 703 participants contributed data to the 
meta-analysis. Drama-based interventions showed a significant medium effect on 
social skills (g = 0.54, 95% CI [0.21, 0.88], p = 0.002), with substantial 
heterogeneity (Q(15) = 62.59, p < 0.001; I² = 76.04%). Drama approach 
(Q(2) = 10.78, p = 0.005), intervention setting (Q(2) = 11.30, p = 0.010), and 
intervention agent (Q(2) = 6.64, p = 0.036) significantly moderated effects. 
Participant age was not a significant moderator, and dosage indicators were not 
significantly associated with effect sizes. These findings suggest that 
drama-based interventions may support social skills in autistic children and 
adolescents, with effects varying by intervention organization and delivery 
context.

Porcine Teschovirus (PTV) is an economically significant swine pathogen with a 
global distribution that can cause severe neurological, respiratory, and 
reproductive diseases. However, no specific vaccines or antiviral drugs are 
currently available. To address the absence of specific antiviral therapies for 
PTV, this study aimed to identify a clinically promising antiviral candidate 
through in vitro compound screening. We began by isolating and purified a 
contemporary PTV strain (PTV/Shandong/2024) from a clinical swab of a dead 
piglet. We also established a strain-specific RT-qPCR assay to accurately 
quantify PTV RNA load. A subsequent targeted screen of a hepatitis C virus (HCV) 
inhibitor library identified the nucleoside analog 4'-fluorouridine (4'-FLU) as 
a potent inhibitor of PTV replication in vitro. Treatment with 4'-FLU 
significantly reduced viral load and cytopathic effects in infected PK-15 cells. 
The compound exhibited potent antiviral activity, with a half maximal inhibitory 
concentration (IC₅₀) of 1.234 µM, and low cytotoxicity, with a half maximal 
cytotoxic concentration (CC₅₀) of 295.7 µM. This resulted in a high selectivity 
index of 239.6, indicating a wide therapeutic window. Time-of-addition 
experiments revealed that 4'-FLU acts primarily during the early stages of viral 
replication. These results provide the first evidence that 4'-FLU suppresses PTV 
replication in vitro supporting its further evaluation as a candidate antiviral 
against PTV.

PURPOSE: Scoliosis is frequently associated with CM1 and TCS, but its course 
following neurosurgical treatment remains incompletely understood. The aim of 
this study was to describe scoliosis development following posterior fossa 
decompression for CM1 or de-tethering for TCS. A secondary aim was to describe 
postoperative brace treatment and its association with scoliosis progression.
METHODS: This was a retrospective study including children operated 
consecutively from the age of one to eighteen years for CM1 or TCS. We included 
patients with and without preoperative scoliosis who had a last follow-up from

progressed less frequently than non-compliant patients (p = 0.025).

Impact of surgeon experience on the safety and accuracy of robot-assisted vs. 
navigation-guided percutaneous pedicle screw placement: a matched cohort study.

Backhaus P(1), Albrecht C(2), Kraus LM(2), Karschnia P(2), Negwer C(2), Meyer 
B(2), Wagner A(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Neurosurgery, TUM School of Medicine and Health, Technical 
University of Munich, Klinikum rechts der Isar, Munich, Germany. 
Paul.Backhaus@mri.tum.de.
(2)Department of Neurosurgery, TUM School of Medicine and Health, Technical 
University of Munich, Klinikum rechts der Isar, Munich, Germany.

PURPOSE: To compare intraoperative screw revision and outcomes of robot-assisted 
versus navigation-guided percutaneous pedicle screw placement and to explore 
whether outcomes differed by surgeon experience.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A prospective cohort of 43 consecutive patients 
undergoing robot-assisted percutaneous pedicle screw fixation between September 
2024 and March 2026 was compared with a matched historical cohort of 129 
patients treated using navigated conventional percutaneous instrumentation. 
Propensity score matching included age, sex, ASA physical status, anatomical 
region, surgical indication, and surgeon expertise. Surgeons were stratified 
according to prior spondylodesis case volume. Outcomes included screw revision 
rates (as a measure of screw accuracy), screw placement time, operative time, 
blood loss, and perioperative complications.
RESULTS: Unadjusted screw-level revision proportions were 2.3% with robotic 
assistance and 3.5% with navigation-guided instrumentation. In adjusted 
patient-level analysis, greater surgeon experience, but not robotic assistance, 
was associated with fewer revisions. In the lowest-experience group, the 
proportions were descriptively 4.3% and 8.2%, but the technique-by-experience 
interaction was not statistically significant. Median screw-placement time was 
longer with robotic assistance (7.8 vs. 5.5 min per screw, p < 0.001). No 
statistically significant between-group differences were detected in blood loss, 
length of stay, or complication rates.
CONCLUSION: Robot-assisted pedicle screw placement is safe and accurate, with 
comparable complication rates to conventional navigation. The observed increase 
in screw placement time may reflect the early adaptation phase of the robotic 
technique rather than an inherent limitation of the system. The descriptive 
reduction in revision rates among less experienced surgeons suggests a potential 
role for robotic assistance in supporting standardization and surgical training; 
however, this exploratory finding warrants confirmation in larger studies.

PURPOSE: Regenerative medicine (RM) trials for intervertebral disc degeneration 
(IDD) are gaining increasing visibility and clinical relevance, yet reporting 
quality remains inconsistent and often incomplete. Critical details on trial 
methodology, biologic product specifications, imaging criteria, and outcome 
assessment are frequently insufficiently reported, limiting reproducibility and 
hindering the interpretation of available evidence. The aim of this study was to 
develop a spine-specific reporting guideline to support authors, reviewers, and 
readers in producing transparent and interpretable RM clinical trial reports.
METHODS: A three-stage process was undertaken to establish a consensus-based 
reporting guideline. First, a systematic review of published RM trials employing 
intradiscal biologic treatments was conducted to identify recurring reporting 
deficiencies. Second, an expert focus group and subsequent international survey 
hosted by the International Society for the Study of the Lumbar Spine (ISSLS) 
generated and prioritized candidate reporting items. Third, the finalized 
VERTEBRA checklist was applied to an updated cohort of clinical trials to 
evaluate reporting completeness across predefined domains.
RESULTS: Across 36 eligible clinical trials, the mean VERTEBRA completeness 
score was 53.8%, with substantial variability among studies. Recurrent 
deficiencies were consistently observed in product characterization, 
methodological transparency, imaging acquisition and analysis, baseline 
reporting, and management of missing data. Only a minority of studies referenced 
established reporting guidelines. Reporting quality showed an association with 
journal impact factor, but not geographic region or funding disclosures. Expert 
polling demonstrated strong agreement on the need for a spine-specific reporting 
tool, resulting in the development of a 50-item checklist organized across five 
domains.
CONCLUSION: The VERTEBRA reporting guideline provides a structured, 
field-specific framework to elevate transparency, reproducibility, and 
interpretability in RM trials for IDD. Its adoption may enhance manuscript 
quality, strengthen peer review, and improve the reliability of evidence guiding 
the development and clinical translation of future regenerative therapies for 
IDD.

Modic changes, chronic low back pain, and lifestyle and mental health factors: a 
cross-sectional analysis of a cohort study.

Mitchell UH(1), Clay KD(2), McCauley M(2), Wengreen M(2), Samanna CL(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Exercise Sciences, Brigham Young University, Provo, USA. 
rike_mitchell@byu.edu.
(2)Department of Exercise Sciences, Brigham Young University, Provo, USA.
(3)Eastern Health Clinical School, Monash University, Melbourne, Australia.

PURPOSE: Modic changes (MC) are vertebral endplate and adjacent bone marrow MRI 
findings that have been associated with chronic low back pain (CLBP), although 
their clinical relevance remains debated. This study examined whether MC 
presence and extent are associated with CLBP status, pain intensity, and 
disability, and whether lifestyle or mental health factors moderate the MC-pain 
relationship.
METHODS: This exploratory cross-sectional sub-study included 239 adults: 135 
with CLBP and 104 controls without. Lumbar MRI scans were evaluated for MC 
presence, type, craniocaudal extent of vertebral body involvement, and 
transverse extent of endplate involvement. Firth penalized logistic regression 
examined associations of MC presence, type and extent with CLBP status. Linear 
regression models examined associations between aggregated MC count and 
vertebral body and endplate extent with low back pain intensity and disability 
within CLBP and control groups. Moderation analyses tested whether sleep 
disturbance, physical activity, anxiety, depression, or pain catastrophizing 
modified the association between MC count and low back pain intensity among 
individuals with CLBP. All models were adjusted for age, sex, smoking, and body 
mass index.
RESULTS: Any MC were associated with higher odds of CLBP (OR 2.50, 95% CI 
1.45-4.30; p = 0.001), with similar associations for Type 1 and Type 2 MC. 
Greater vertebral body involvement showed a graded association with CLBP, with 
> 50% vertebral body involvement associated with the highest odds (OR 4.88, 95% 
CI 1.14-20.92; p = 0.033). Among individuals with CLBP, aggregated MC count 
(β = 0.30, 95% CI 0.05-0.55; p = 0.019) and vertebral body extent (β = 0.11, 95% 
CI 0.01-0.21; p = 0.039) were associated with higher pain intensity, but not 
disability. Endplate extent was not associated with pain or disability. None of 
the examined lifestyle or psychological factors significantly moderated the 
MC-pain association.
CONCLUSION: This exploratory analysis revealed that MC, particularly those with 
greater vertebral body involvement, were associated with CLBP status and low 
back pain intensity. Lifestyle and psychological factors were related to pain 
severity but did not significantly modify the MC-pain relationship. These 
findings suggest that MC extent may be a clinically relevant imaging 
characteristic, although longitudinal studies are needed to clarify causality 
and prognostic significance.

BACKGROUND: Breast reduction surgery is a common aesthetic procedure associated 
with significant postoperative pain. Effective analgesia plays an important role 
in reducing opioid consumption, minimizing adverse effects, facilitating 
postoperative recovery, and improving patient satisfaction. Fascial plane blocks 
have recently gained popularity for breast surgery. This randomized study aimed 
to compare the effects of bilateral erector spinae plane block (ESPB) and 
serratus anterior plane block (SAPB) on postoperative analgesia in patients 
undergoing breast reduction surgery.
METHODS: Seventy female patients undergoing bilateral breast reduction surgery 
were randomly allocated into two groups: ESPB (Group ESPB, n = 35) and SAPB

included intravenous paracetamol, ibuprofen, and intravenous tramadol

group. Bradycardia occurred in one ESPB group patient (p = 1).

tramadol consumption and a longer time to first PCA demand than SAPB, while pain 
scores were comparable.

PURPOSE: Esophageal variceal (EV) bleeding is a lethal complication in patients 
with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Current risk stratification relies on 
invasive endoscopy or systemic surrogates of liver cirrhosis. This study aimed 
to develop a machine learning model utilizing EV-specific CT radiomics to 
identify high-risk esophageal varices, as defined by endoscopic criteria, in 
patients with HCC.
METHODS: 151 HCC patients were enrolled and divided into a training cohort 
(n = 101; 75 high-risk; January 2017 - December 2022) and an independent 
temporal validation cohort (n = 50; 29 high-risk; January 2023 - December 2024). 
Endoscopic stigmata were used as an endpoint, including active bleeding or 
varices with high-risk features. Radiomic features were extracted from 
contrast-enhanced CT images acquired within six months prior to endoscopy. Model 
performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) of receiver 
operating characteristic (ROC), Brier score, calibration curves, and decision 
curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: In the training cohort, the varix-specific radiomics signature 
developed via the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) 
demonstrated excellent discriminative power (cross-validated AUC: 0.956; 95% CI 
0.872-1.000). In the temporal validation cohort, this model maintained high 
generalizability, yielding an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI 0.846-0.984, sensitivity: 
93.1%, specificity: 71.4%) as well as a Brier score of 0.1186 and good 
calibration (intercept = -0.157, slope = 1.354). Surface-to-Volume Ratio (SVR) 
and NGTDM Coarseness are feasible radiomics.
CONCLUSION: The varix-specific radiomics model provides highly sensitive and 
mathematically stable non-invasive risk stratification for EV bleeding in 
patients with HCC.

PURPOSE: To develop and validate a risk prediction model for postpartum urinary 
retention (PUR) among parturients receiving epidural analgesia (EA) during

reduces PUR incidence remains to be established in prospective interventional 
studies.

PURPOSE: This study examined whether the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) at 
intensive care unit (ICU) admission is associated with major postoperative 
complications after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass and whether this 
association differs from that of absolute ICU admission glucose.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 731 surgical episodes

Recent advances in MXene, MOF, and COF based NH(3) gas sensors for environmental 
monitoring: sensing mechanisms, analytical performance, and future perspectives.

Ahmad K(1), Rajkumar C(2), Oh TH(2), Shabbir M(3).

Author information:
(1)School of Chemical Engineering, Yeungnam University, 280 Daehak-Ro, 
Gyeongsan, 38541, Republic of Korea. khursheed.energy@gmail.com.
(2)School of Chemical Engineering, Yeungnam University, 280 Daehak-Ro, 
Gyeongsan, 38541, Republic of Korea.
(3)Department of Applied Sciences, School of Engineering and Technology, CGC 
University, Mohali, Punjab, 140307, India.

The increasing use of ammonia (NH3) in agriculture, refrigeration, chemical 
processing, and energy applications has increased concerns over its toxicity and 
corrosiveness. This suggest the need for sensitive NH3 monitoring under 
practical conditions. This review critically evaluates recent advances in MXene, 
metal-organic framework (MOF), and covalent organic framework (COF) based NH3 
sensors. MXenes are promising for room-temperature sensing because of their high 
conductivity and efficient charge transport, but oxidation, restacking, and 
humidity interference continue to hinder stable and reproducible performance. In 
contrast, MOFs provide molecular-sieving capability, high porosity, and 
Lewis-acidic adsorption sites, but their poor conductivity and limited stability 
necessitate integrating it with semiconductors, polymers, or carbon-based 
materials. Similarly, COFs exhibit tunable pore structures, ordered transport 
pathways, and good chemical stability. Despite these advantages, their 
application in NH3 sensing remains relatively limited. The analytical 
performance of MXene, MOF, and COF based NH3 sensors has been critically 
discussed with the underlying sensing mechanisms. The key challenges, future 
perspectives, and emerging research directions are also discussed. Unlike 
earlier reviews that discuss these materials separately, this review compares 
MXene, MOF, and COF based NH3 sensors using the same performance criteria, 
providing a clearer view of their strengths and remaining limitations. We 
believe that this review will provide a useful overview for researchers 
developing MXene, MOF, and COF based NH3 sensors.

Vibrational dynamics of TODD-graphene nanosheets via molecular dynamics 
simulations and machine-learning surrogate models: implications for adaptive 
nanomechanical devices.

Ke Y(1), Wei B(2).

Author information:
(1)School of Teacher Education, Nanchong Vocational and Technical College, 
Nanchong, Sichuan, 637131, China. keyaobin1982@163.com.
(2)China Railway Corporation, Wuhan Railway Bureau Hankou Railway Station, 
Wuhan, 430023, China. weibowen1984@gmail.com.

CONTEXT: TODD-Graphene (TODD-G), a porous two-dimensional carbon allotrope 
composed of interconnected 3-8-10-12 carbon rings, has recently emerged as a 
promising candidate for nanoelectromechanical and adaptive nanodevice 
applications due to its metallic conductivity, mechanical compliance, and 
topologically engineered phonon structure. In this work, the vibrational 
dynamics of TODD-G nanosheets were systematically investigated to establish 
structure-property relationships governing resonant behavior under varying 
geometric, thermal, mechanical, and defect conditions. Fundamental frequencies 
were found to span 2.93-13.28 THz and follow the classical f ∝ L-2 scaling 
relation. Increasing temperature from 1 to 1000 K reduced resonance frequencies 
by up to 22% because of thermal expansion and anharmonic phonon interactions, 
while tensile strain up to 10% enhanced frequencies by more than 50%, yielding 
gauge factors of 5.3-5.7 that exceed those of graphene. Vacancy defects 
significantly degraded quality factors and resonance stability, whereas 
multilayer stacking improved energy retention despite modest frequency 
reduction. Boundary conditions strongly altered modal spectra, with 
clamped-clamped configurations producing the highest frequencies and quality 
factors. Phonon density-of-states analysis revealed distinct acoustic, mixed, 
and optical vibrational regimes with a maximum phonon cutoff frequency of 56.5 
THz. To accelerate device-level optimization, machine-learning surrogate models 
were developed for predicting resonance frequency and quality factor across the 
multidimensional design space. Gradient-boosting models achieved excellent 
predictive accuracy ( R2 = 0.98 for frequency and R2 = 0.972 for quality 
factor), demonstrating that thermal activation and vacancy concentration 
dominate vibrational dissipation mechanisms. The combined molecular dynamics and 
machine-learning framework establishes TODD-G as a promising platform for 
tunable nanoresonators, strain sensors, RF filters, vibration energy harvesters, 
and cryogenic nanomechanical systems.
METHODS: Atomic-scale simulations were performed using classical molecular 
dynamics within the large-scale atomic/molecular massively parallel simulator 
(LAMMPS) package. Interatomic interactions were described using the adaptive 
intermolecular reactive empirical bond order (AIREBO) potential with activated 
Lennard-Jones and torsional terms, while multilayer van der Waals interactions 
employed a 12-6 Lennard-Jones potential. Structural relaxation was conducted 
using conjugate-gradient energy minimization. Thermal equilibration employed the 
Nosé-Hoover thermostat within the canonical (NVT) ensemble, followed by 
microcanonical (NVE) simulations for vibrational analysis using a timestep of 
0.5 fs. Vibrational properties were extracted using impulse-response analysis, 
velocity autocorrelation functions, harmonic forcing, fast Fourier transform 
(FFT) spectral analysis, and phonon density-of-states calculations. Simulations 
systematically examined the effects of nanosheet size, temperature (1-1000 K), 
tensile strain (0-10%), vacancy-defect concentration (0.5-5%), multilayer 
stacking (1-5 layers), and boundary conditions (free-free, clamped-free, simply 
supported, and clamped-clamped). Machine-learning surrogate models including 
linear regression, support-vector regression with radial-basis-function kernels, 
random forest regression, and gradient-boosting regression were trained using an 
80/20 train-test split and five-fold cross-validation to predict resonance 
frequency and quality factor across the multidimensional parameter space.

Li Y(1)(2), Wang Y(3), Lei R(4)(5), Zhou Q(6), Li Q(7)(8), Chen

(13)Institute of Global Health, University of Geneva, Geneva, Switzerland.

The "evidence gap" in pediatrics often requires healthcare professionals to use 
evidence that is not fully direct for the target population, intervention, or 
context. Despite its critical clinical relevance, the conceptual understanding 
and practice patterns surrounding indirect evidence among healthcare 
professionals remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the 
awareness, attitudes, practice patterns, and unmet needs regarding the use of 
indirect evidence among pediatric healthcare professionals in China. A 
cross-sectional survey was conducted among clinicians, pharmacists, technicians, 
researchers, and other professionals working in the field of pediatrics in 
China. This survey assessed four domains: self-reported awareness, attitudes, 
practice behaviors, and perceived barriers or support needs. Multivariable 
proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression was the main analysis of four 
single-item ordinal outcomes; linear regression was a sensitivity analysis. 
Multi-item matrix sections were examined using internal-consistency coefficients 
and exploratory factor analysis. A total of 571 valid responses were included in 
the final analysis. After reading a brief definition of indirect evidence, 57 
participants (10.0%) rated themselves as extremely familiar with the concept. 
Respondents reported greater confidence in evidence from similar diseases (41.0% 
reporting high or extremely high confidence) than in adult data (25.0%) or 
animal studies (20.0%). In a separate item, 295 participants (51.7%) reported 
being required to base decisions on indirect evidence in their professional 
routine at least several times per week, and 55.7% reported often or always 
consulting peers or experts when assessing applicability. In adjusted ordinal 
models, tertiary-hospital affiliation was associated with a higher category of 
reported frequency of needing to base decisions on indirect evidence (adjusted 
OR 1.95, 95% CI 1.25 to 3.03), whereas master's or doctoral education was 
associated with a lower category than bachelor's degree or below (adjusted OR 
0.58, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.89). The most frequently reported barrier was the absence 
of unified, standardized evaluation processes or tools.
CONCLUSION:  Our findings suggest a substantial perceived need for structured 
guidance and tools to support the appraisal and application of indirect evidence 
in pediatric practice. Pediatric healthcare professionals in China reported 
awareness of the evidence gap and willingness to consider indirect evidence, but 
also reported low confidence, limited use of standardized methods, and 
substantial reliance on informal, experience-based approaches. These findings 
identify perceived needs that may inform the development and evaluation of 
user-friendly frameworks, targeted training programs, and supportive 
institutional policies.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Pediatric evidence gaps often require professionals to consider 
indirect evidence, yet limited data exist on how they perceive such evidence or 
how often they report encountering decisions that require it.
WHAT IS NEW: • After reading a brief definition of indirect evidence, 10.0% of 
respondents rated themselves as extremely familiar with the concept. In a 
separate item, 51.7% reported being required to base professional decisions on 
indirect evidence at least several times per week; 55.7% often or always 
consulted peers or experts, while frequent use of formal assessment methods was 
uncommon.

Neurosurgical manifestations and management of mucopolysaccharidoses: A 
systematic review.

Lu VM(#)(1), Sanikommu S(#)(2), Vazquez S(2), Roach CS(2), Shah KH(2), Oh T(3), 
Ibrahim GM(4), Samdani AF(5), Hwang SW(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Neurological Surgery, University of Miami Miller School of 
Medicine, 1095 NW 14th Terrace, Miami, FL, 33136, USA. victor.lu@jhsmiami.org.
(2)Department of Neurological Surgery, University of Miami Miller School of 
Medicine, 1095 NW 14th Terrace, Miami, FL, 33136, USA.
(3)Department of Neurological Surgery, Columbia University Irving Medical 
Center, New York, NY, USA.
(4)Division of Neurosurgery, The Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto, ON, 
Canada.
(5)Department of Orthopedic Surgery and Neurosurgery, Shriners Children's 
Philadelphia, Philadelphia, PA, USA.
(#)Contributed equally

Mucopolysaccharidoses (MPS) represent a group of rare inherited lysosomal 
storage disorders, of which neurosurgical issues arise during childhood and 
adolescence. The literature however remains fragmented in terms of these 
specific outcomes. Correspondingly, we sought to synthesize a primer for 
neurosurgeons in regard to MPS, summarizing the neurosurgical manifestations and 
management reported in the contemporary literature. A systematic interrogation 
of the literature was performed according to PRISMA guidelines. Electronic 
databases were searched from inception through June 2026. Studies reporting 
hydrocephalus, craniovertebral junction (CVJ) abnormalities, spinal cord 
compression, myelopathy, spinal deformity, neurosurgical interventions, or 
related outcomes in patients with any MPS subtype were included and their 
findings aggregated. Seventy-eight studies comprising 983 patients with 37.8% 
females and mean age of 12.4 years were included. MPS I (34%), MPS II (31%), and 
MPS IV (26%) represented the majority of reported subtypes. A total of 819 
patients (83%) exhibited neurosurgical manifestations. Spinal deformity (29%) 
and hydrocephalus (28%) were the most frequently reported manifestations, 
followed by spinal cord compression/myelopathy (22%) and CVJ pathology (20%). 
Distinct subtype-specific patterns were observed: spinal deformity predominated 
in MPS I (24%), hydrocephalus in MPS II (20%), and CVJ instability/compression 
in MPS IV (12%). Overall, hydrocephalus was surgically treated in 74% of 
instances, whereas CVJ and spinal cord pathology were surgically treated in 41% 
and 23% of instances respectively. Patients in studies who were not treated by 
any prior systemic therapy reported higher rates of surgical intervention 
compared to those who had received treatment. Neurosurgical manifestations occur 
in over four-fifths of MPS patients and are clinically significant across all 
types of MPS. Hydrocephalus, CVJ instability, spinal cord compression, and 
progressive spinal deformity represent the major surgical morbidities. Early 
recognition, structured imaging surveillance, and timely neurosurgical 
intervention are essential components of MPS management.
