Biochar mitigates microplastic- and nanoplastic-induced soil degradation and 
plant stress: a global meta-analysis.

Putra B(1)(2), Gopar RA(3), Surachman M(3), Darmawan IWA(3), Fanindi A(3), 
Akhadiarto S(3), Husni A(3), H TZP(3), Sutedi E(3), Sirait J(3), Herdiawan I(3), 
Nulik J(3), Hau DK(3), Simanihuruk K(3), Koten BB(4), Wea R(4).

Author information:
(1)Study Program of Nutrition and Feed Technology, Graduate School of IPB 
University, Bogor, 16680, Indonesia. belaputramsc@gmail.com.
(2)Universitas Muara Bungo, Jl. Pendidikan, Muara Bungo, Bungo, Jambi, 37215, 
Indonesia. belaputramsc@gmail.com.
(3)Research Center for Animal Husbandry, The National Research and Innovation 
Agency (BRIN), Jakarta Pusat, Indonesia.
(4)State Agricultural Polytechnic of Kupang, Kupang, Indonesia.

Microplastic (MP) and nanoplastic (NP) contamination threatens soil functioning 
and plant performance, yet the effectiveness of biochar in mitigating these 
impacts varies substantially among experimental conditions. We conducted a 
meta-analysis of 59 peer-reviewed studies comprising 1418 effect-size estimates 
to quantify biochar-mediated responses across the soil-plant continuum. Effect 
sizes were calculated as the natural logarithm of the response ratio (lnRR) and 
analyzed using multilevel random-effects models. Subgroup analyses examined the 
effects of growth medium, plant functional group, plastic type, biochar 
feedstock, application rate, treatment duration, pyrolysis temperature, and 
experimental system, while meta-regression identified continuous moderators of 
response magnitude. Biochar produced positive pooled responses in soil 
properties (lnRR = 0.130), soil biological properties (0.186), biomass yield 
(0.218), photosynthetic performance (0.326), and plant nutrient content (0.599). 
Oxidative-damage indicators declined, including malondialdehyde (lnRR = - 0.154) 
and H2O2 (- 0.150), while plant microplastic accumulation showed a pronounced 
negative response (lnRR = - 0.811). The magnitude of these responses varied 
significantly among environmental and management contexts. Biochar application 
rate was the only significant continuous moderator, whereas pyrolysis 
temperature and treatment duration were not significant linear predictors of 
overall effect magnitude. Stronger responses in controlled systems than in more 
environmentally complex systems further indicated a potential gap between 
experimental efficacy and field-scale performance. Overall, the available 
evidence indicates that biochar is associated with improvements across multiple 
soil and plant response domains under MP/NP stress, although the magnitude of 
these responses is strongly context dependent. These findings provide a 
quantitative basis for developing context-specific biochar strategies while 
highlighting the need for geographically broader and long-term field validation.

Crosstalk through cholinergic and aryl hydrocarbon receptor pathways in the 
anti-inflammatory actions of microbial metabolites.

Sonmez G(1), Sari S(2), Bodur E(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Medical Biochemistry, Faculty of Medicine, Hacettepe 
University, Ankara, Turkey.
(2)Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Faculty of Pharmacy, Hacettepe 
University, Ankara, Turkey.
(3)Department of Medical Biochemistry, Faculty of Medicine, Hacettepe 
University, Ankara, Turkey. ebodur@hacettepe.edu.tr.

The intestinal epithelium maintains immune and metabolic homeostasis at the 
host-microbiota interface, and its disruption contributes to inflammatory bowel 
disease (IBD). Microbial metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and 
indole derivatives are known to regulate epithelial and immune functions, but 
their roles in cholinergic signaling and aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) 
pathways remain incompletely understood. Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cells were 
stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 10 µg/mL) and co-treated with SCFAs 
(acetate, propionate, butyrate) or indole derivatives (IAA, IPA, IBA; 1000 µM). 
The AhR antagonist CH223191 was used to assess receptor involvement. 
Inflammatory markers (TNF-α, IL-6, COX-2), barrier integrity (FITC-dextran 
permeability, ZO-1 and occludin), cholinergic components (CHAT, ACHE, BCHE, 
α7nAChR, mAChR1, mAChR3), and AhR activation (nuclear localization, CYP1A1 
expression) were analyzed using qPCR, ELISA, immunostaining, and enzymatic 
assays. Molecular docking was performed to predict metabolite-protein 
interactions. LPS induced inflammatory cytokine expression and barrier 
disruption, whereas SCFAs and indole derivatives significantly reduced 
inflammation, restored tight-junction organization, and decreased permeability. 
These metabolites enhanced CHAT and muscarinic receptor expression while 
suppressing ACHE upregulation, indicating restoration of cholinergic balance. 
Both groups reactivated AhR signaling, and AhR inhibition disrupted cholinergic 
regulation, supporting an AhR-dependent mechanism. Butyrate and indole-3-butyric 
acid exhibited the strongest protective effects. These findings identify a novel 
AhR-cholinergic axis in intestinal epithelial regulation and highlight microbial 
metabolites as promising therapeutic candidates for IBD.

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a major 
hepatic consequence of metabolic dysfunction, yet evidence-based pharmacologic 
options remain limited. Repurposing widely available agents with metabolic and 
anti-inflammatory actions may offer a clinically meaningful benefit. To compare 
the effects of aspirin and dapagliflozin on hepatic steatosis, fibrosis, liver 
enzymes, and lipid profile in patients with MASLD. In this prospective 
randomized interventional study, 80 adults with confirmed MASLD were allocated 
(1:1) to aspirin 100 mg once daily or dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily for 6 
months (n = 40 per group). Baseline and 6-month measurements included alanine 
aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alkaline phosphatase 
(ALP), triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), total 
cholesterol, and FibroScan-derived parameters, including controlled attenuation 
parameter (CAP; dB/m), which quantifies hepatic steatosis, and liver stiffness 
measurement (LSM; kPa), a surrogate marker of liver fibrosis. The primary 
endpoints included the between-group differences in changes in LSM, CAP, liver 
enzymes, and lipid profile from baseline to 6 months. Ethics approval was 
obtained (FMBSUREC/04032025). The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov 
(NCT07338331) on 20 Dec 2025. Dapagliflozin significantly improved hepatic 
steatosis, reflected by lower CAP values compared to aspirin (260.35 ± 20.78 vs 
271.48 ± 12.58 dB/m; p = 0.005), and reduced total cholesterol levels 
(138.87 ± 54.70 vs 192.48 ± 79.46 mg/dL; p = 0.003). In contrast, aspirin 
demonstrated a greater reduction in liver stiffness (LSM) (6.15 ± 2.55 vs 
8.58 ± 4.13 kPa; p = 0.002) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) percentage change 
(- 44.54% vs - 17.84%; p = 0.025). Other biochemical parameters showed no 
statistically significant between-group differences (all p > 0.05). Aspirin and 
dapagliflozin exert distinct and potentially complementary effects in MASLD, 
with dapagliflozin preferentially improving hepatic steatosis and aspirin 
showing a greater impact on fibrosis-related parameters. These findings support 
a dual-pathway therapeutic model targeting steatosis and fibrosis and underscore 
the need for larger trials evaluating combined strategies and histological 
outcomes.

Systematic qualitative analysis of the designation of medicinal products in the 
Rote Liste® (Red List).

Frank MK(1), Schirmer B(2), Seifert R(1).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Pharmacology, Hannover Medical School, Carl-Neuberg-Str. 1, 
30625, Hannover, Germany.
(2)Institute of Pharmacology, Hannover Medical School, Carl-Neuberg-Str. 1, 
30625, Hannover, Germany. schirmer.bastian@mh-hannover.de.

Medication errors are a serious problem in medicine and can lead to patient harm 
and entail high costs. To investigate the quality of brand names which we 
suggest can favor medication errors, this study looks at the designation of 
drugs (brand name). It analyses whether they are potentially a risk for 
medication errors by presenting a false image of the drug. The Rote Liste® (Red 
List) is one of the best-known drug directories in Germany; this drug directory 
was used for the categorization of medicinal products. The entries included in 
the Rote Liste ® dataset from 2020 were analyzed by their semantic appearance. 
By creating a new methodology, the entries were examined for an association 
between the designation of the medicinal product and their attributes, such as 
the RL-group, the active ingredients and the marketing authorization holder, and 
were divided into three main categories. Subsequently, correlations between the 
results of the analysis and the attributes were performed. To verify the quality 
of this method, the inter- and intra-rater-reliability was determined by using 
Cohen's cappa. One thousand six hundred thirty-seven (22.36%) of the entries had 
a strictly generic designation. Three main categories were established, of which 
most entries (5454; 74.49%) were assigned to the category "coherent". The other 
two categories are "incoherent" (1625; 22.19%) and "potentially confusing" (243; 
3.32%). By looking at the distribution of the three main categories among the 
RL-groups, a few RL-groups condition for the most entries in the category 
"potentially confusing". The inter- and intra-rater-reliability for this newly 
established analysis shows a moderate to substantial agreement. The results show 
that there are heterogenous linguistic forms of designation of medicinal 
products. A more transparent and uniform designation of medicinal products could 
lead to a reduction in medical errors. In this paper, we have provided specific 
suggestions on how drug naming could be improved.

Panax ginseng suppresses endothelin-1-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy through

Numata T(1), Tagashira H(2)(3), Sato-Numata K(2), Takayama R(4), Aoyama A(4), 
Sakai A(2), Tran HN(2)(5), Watanabe H(6).

Author information:
(1)Department of Integrative Physiology, Graduate School of Medicine, Akita 
University, 1-1-1 Hondo, Akita, 010-8543, Japan. numata@med.akita-u.ac.jp.
(2)Department of Integrative Physiology, Graduate School of Medicine, Akita 
University, 1-1-1 Hondo, Akita, 010-8543, Japan.
(3)Second Department of Pharmacology, School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Kyushu 
University of Medical Science, 1714-1 Yoshino-cho, Nobeoka, Miyazaki, 882-8508,

(4)School of Medicine, Akita University, 1-1-1 Hondo, Akita, 010-8543, Japan.
(5)Faculty of Fisheries, Hue University of Agriculture and Forestry, Hue

(6)Department of Cardiovascular Medicine, Graduate School of Medicine, Akita 
University, 1-1-1 Hondo, Akita, 010-8543, Japan.

Panax ginseng (PG) is a traditional herbal medicine widely used for the 
treatment of cardiovascular disorders in East Asia. Although PG has been 
reported to attenuate cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, the molecular mechanisms 
underlying its cardioprotective effects remain incompletely understood. In this 
study, we investigated whether modulation of the endothelin-1 (ET-1)-angiotensin 
II (AngII) signaling axis contributes to the anti-hypertrophic action of PG. 
Neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs) were used to evaluate ET-1-induced 
hypertrophy, and pharmacological experiments using receptor antagonists were 
performed to examine the signaling pathways involved. Extracellular AngII levels 
were quantified by ELISA, intracellular Ca2+ accumulation was assessed in 
AT1AR-overexpressing NRVMs, and whole-cell patch-clamp recordings were performed 
in HEK293T cells co-expressing AT1AR and TRPC6. PG significantly attenuated 
ET-1-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy without altering ETAR or ETBR expression. 
Pharmacological experiments with the ETAR antagonist BQ-123 suggested that the 
anti-hypertrophic effect of PG could not be explained solely by direct 
inhibition of ETAR signaling. PG markedly suppressed ET-1-induced extracellular 
AngII production, and interaction studies with losartan further implicated the 
AngII-AT1AR pathway in the anti-hypertrophic action of PG. Moreover, PG 
inhibited AngII-induced intracellular Ca2+ accumulation in AT1AR-overexpressing 
NRVMs and attenuated AngII-evoked TRPC6-mediated membrane currents without 
affecting basal channel activity. These findings demonstrate that PG suppresses 
ET-1-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy by inhibiting both ET-1-induced AngII 
production and downstream AT1AR-dependent signaling, identifying suppression of 
the AngII-AT1AR signaling axis as a key mechanism underlying its 
cardioprotective effects.

Aydın E(1), Uzun S(2), Karakaş S(3), Günay D(4), Büyükçerçi NN(1).

Author information:
(1)Faculty of Health Sciences, Department of Nursing, Gümüşhane University,

PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to examine the experiences of individuals 
living with cancer across biopsychosocial dimensions and to understand the 
meanings they attributed to spirituality and their forms of spiritual coping 
within the illness process.
METHODS: This qualitative study was conducted using a phenomenological design. 
Thirteen patients with cancer were recruited from a public hospital using 
criterion sampling, a purposive sampling strategy. Data were collected through 
individual, face-to-face, semi-structured in-depth interviews and analyzed using 
Colaizzi's seven-step phenomenological analysis method. The sample size was 
determined based on data saturation.
RESULTS: As a result of data analysis, three themes (perception of cancer and 
reactions to the process, biopsychosocial effects of the disease, and coping

coping methods, and perception of coping) were identified.

physical, psychological, and social difficulties. Spirituality emerged as a

differences in participants' perceptions of coping indicated that the use of 
spiritual resources was not always accompanied by a strong perception of coping. 
These findings highlight the importance of addressing the changing 
biopsychosocial needs and personal coping resources of individuals living with 
cancer through an individualized and holistic approach.

Clinical characteristics and prognosis of central nervous system Klebsiella 
pneumoniae infection: a focus on hypervirulent and classical strains.

You L(1), Bai J(1), Meng F(1), Yin X(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Neurology, The First Hospital of Jilin University, No. 1 Xinmin

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical characteristics, diagnosis, treatment, 
and prognosis of 20 cases of central nervous system (CNS) Klebsiella pneumoniae 
infection diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), and to 
compare the differences between classical Klebsiella pneumoniae (cKP) and 
hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKP) in central nervous system infections.
METHODS: Retrospective single-center study of 20 mNGS-diagnosed CNS K. 
pneumoniae infections (January 2022 - March 2026). Univariate analysis compared 
hvKP and cKP groups.
RESULTS: Among 20 patients, 19 were diagnosed by CSF mNGS and 1 by abscess fluid 
mNGS. The cKP group had a higher proportion of tumor history (P = 0.029) and a 
marginally higher rate of neurosurgery history (P = 0.082). Type 2 diabetes was 
common in both groups (66.7% vs. 62.5%). The hvKP group had higher rates of 
focal neurological deficits (77.8% vs. 12.5%, P = 0.015) and bacteremia/sepsis 
(66.7% vs. 37.5%, P = 0.009), while the cKP group had more delirium (62.5% vs. 
11.1%, P = 0.050). CSF mNGS positivity (95%) surpassed culture (23.5%, 
P < 0.001). Radiologically, hvKP showed more brain abscesses (P = 0.015). hvKP 
had worse modified Rankin Scale scores (P = 0.002) and higher mortality (44.4% 
vs. 0%, P = 0.002). No cKP deaths occurred.
CONCLUSION: hvKP and cKP CNS infections differ significantly. hvKP is associated 
with community-onset severe disease (multiple brain abscesses, pyoventricle, 
focal deficits) and high mortality, while cKP links to nosocomial factors and 
better outcomes. mNGS is key for diagnosis, offering high CSF positivity and 
concurrent virulence/resistance profiling. Potential prognostic factors 
identified include high CSF mNGS reads, resistance genes, early liver abscess 
drainage, timely intravitreal injection, and combination therapy.

resistance-associated loci for Septoria tritici blotch in synthetic hexaploid 
wheat.

Blower A(1)(2), Horsnell R(3), Howell PM(3), Wright TIC(3), Ray R(4), Rawsthorne 
S(5), Leigh FJ(3), Kanyuka K(6).

Author information:
(1)University of Nottingham, Plant Sciences Building, Sutton Bonnington Campus, 
Nottingham, LE12 5RD, UK. Anisa.Blower@nottingham.ac.uk.
(2), Park Farm Campus, Villa Road, Niab, Histon, Cambridge, CB24 9AT, UK. 
Anisa.Blower@nottingham.ac.uk.
(3), Park Farm Campus, Villa Road, Niab, Histon, Cambridge, CB24 9AT, UK.
(4)University of Nottingham, Plant Sciences Building, Sutton Bonnington Campus, 
Nottingham, LE12 5RD, UK.
(5)Morley Business Centre, The Morley Agricultural Foundation, Deopham Road, 
Morley St Botolph, Wymondham, NR18 9DF, UK.
(6), Park Farm Campus, Villa Road, Niab, Histon, Cambridge, CB24 9AT, UK. 
kostya.kanyuka@niab.com.

Synthetic hexaploid wheat harbours STB resistance-associated loci with 
multi-isolate and isolate-specific effects, with partly independent genetic 
control of pycnidia suppression and necrosis. Septoria tritici blotch (STB), 
caused by Zymoseptoria tritici, is a major constraint on wheat production. 
Erosion of host resistance and declining fungicide efficacy highlight the need 
to exploit new resistance sources, including synthetic hexaploid wheat (SHW). We 
used a three-family nested association mapping (NAM) population derived from 
Niab SHW donors (SHW.035, SHW.054, and SHW.075) crossed with the UK variety 
Robigus to dissect the genetic basis of STB resistance under controlled 
conditions. Seedlings were challenged with five UK Z. tritici isolates differing 
in virulence, and disease progress was quantified separately as necrosis 
(AUDPC_N) and pycnidia coverage (AUDPC_P). Many SHW-derived lines showed strong 
suppression of pycnidia despite visible necrosis, consistent with partial 
genetic decoupling of pathogen reproduction and host tissue damage. GWAS 
identified a major multi-isolate association on chromosome 3D (qSTB-3D.1), 
contributed by SHW.035 and detected in response to four of the five isolates, 
defining a 23.7 Mb candidate resistance-associated interval. This interval 
encompasses the Stb16q region but also contains other plausible resistance 
candidates, including a WAK close to the strongest association at 609.21 Mb; the 
causal basis therefore remains unresolved. Additional isolate-specific 
resistance-associated intervals were detected on chromosomes 1B, 2D, 3A, and 6D. 
In a BC2F2 population derived from a resistant SHW.035-derived NAM line, 
pycnidia suppression segregated in a 3:1 ratio consistent with a single dominant 
factor, whereas necrosis showed more complex inheritance. These findings show 
that Niab SHWs are a valuable source of STB resistance and highlight the 
potential to select for reduced pathogen reproduction independently of visible 
leaf damage.

BACKGROUND: Diverting loop ileostomy is commonly used to mitigate the 
consequences of anastomotic leakage after rectal cancer surgery. However, some 
patients do not undergo stoma closure, resulting in a permanent stoma that may 
impair quality of life. This study evaluated the closure rate, reasons for 
non-closure, and associated preoperative factors using multicenter prospective 
data.
METHODS: This study was a subanalysis of a multicenter prospective study 
conducted at 24 institutions. Patients with rectal adenocarcinoma who underwent 
laparoscopic or robotic low anterior resection or intersphincteric resection 
with planned diverting loop ileostomy between July 2015 and April 2021 were 
included. Stomas not closed within 1 year were classified as non-closed. 
Preoperative characteristics were compared between the stoma closure and 
non-closure groups using univariable analyses.
RESULTS: Among 320 patients, 298 (93.1%) underwent stoma closure, whereas 22 
(6.9%) did not. Reasons for non-closure were postoperative complications (n = 
9), cancer recurrence (n = 6), patient preference (n = 5), and death (n = 2). In 
univariable comparisons, patients with stoma non-closure more frequently had 
ASA-PS ≥2 (86.4% vs. 63.8%, P = 0.036), stage III-IV disease (68.2% vs. 38.9%, P 
= 0.012), and serum albumin <3.5 g/dL (31.8% vs. 7.4%, P = 0.002) than those who 
underwent stoma closure.
CONCLUSIONS: Although most diverting loop ileostomies were successfully closed, 
6.9% were not reversed. Patients with stoma non-closure more frequently had 
ASA-PS ≥2, advanced clinical stage, and low serum albumin levels than those who 
underwent stoma closure. These findings may be useful for preoperative 
counseling.

Map-based cloning of the susceptibility locus conditioning bs6 resistance in 
pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) encoding mutant alleles of pseudokinase proteins.

Toth Z(#)(1), Toth ZG(#)(1), Kalo P(1)(2), Kiss GB(1)(3), Szabo Z(4).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Genetics and Biotechnology, Hungarian University of Agriculture 
and Life Sciences, Szent-Györgyi A. u. 4., Gödöllő, 2100, Hungary.
(2)Institute of Plant Biology, HUN-REN Biological Research Centre, Szeged, 
Hungary.
(3)AMBIS Biotechnology Research and Development Ltd., Budapest, Hungary.
(4)Institute of Genetics and Biotechnology, Hungarian University of Agriculture 
and Life Sciences, Szent-Györgyi A. u. 4., Gödöllő, 2100, Hungary. 
szabo.zoltan.gen@uni-mate.hu.
(#)Contributed equally

The bs6 resistance gene against bacterial spot was identified by map-based 
cloning in pepper (C. annuum L.). The recessive bs661 locus of pepper Capsicum 
annuum L. var. 61R (Ca61R) conditions a non-hypersensitive resistance trait, 
characterized by a slightly swollen, pale green, photosynthetically active leaf 
tissue, following Xanthomonas euvesicatoria Race 6 (XeR6) infection. In 
contrast, C. annuum cv. Feherozon (CaFo) is susceptible to XeR6. Map-based 
cloning of the bs661 locus revealed that the bs661 locus encodes three predicted 
proteins, pbs661npk, pbs661n, pbs661pk in Ca61R which are the counterpart of the 
three wild type predicted proteins, pBs6FoNPK, pBs6FoN and pBs6FoPK in CaFo, 
respectively. Sequence analysis revealed that the pBs6FoNPK protein showed 35% 
identity and 53% similarity to the ZRK4 pseudokinase (pAtZRK4) identified in 
Arabidopsis thaliana, which possesses N-terminal and C-terminal (pseudokinase) 
domains. The pBs6FoN and pBs6FoPK proteins resemble the N-terminal and 
C-terminal domains of the pBs6FoNPK protein, respectively, thus, they also 
contain pseudokinase domains/sequences. In Ca61R, pbs661npk and pbs661n are 
truncated counterparts of pBs6FoNPK and pBs6FoN, respectively, as a consequence 
of a single-nucleotide insertion that causes frameshifts and premature stop 
codons, whereas pbs661pk differs from pBs6FoPK by a single amino acid, a serine 
to alanine substitution at position 133. These three proteins are considered 
functionless. The ORF of pBs6FoN, pBs6FoPK and pbs661n, pbs661pk, respectively, 
are encoded by a single transcript in both parental plants. For this reason the 
translation of pBs6FoPK was ambiguous, however, the expression of pBs6FoN-dsRed 
fusion protein demonstrated that pBs6FoPK in fact can be translated. The three 
wild type proteins (pBs6FoNPK, pBs6FoN and pBs6FoPK) were independently 
responsible for ETS (effector-triggered susceptibility), because all three genes 
had to be in mutant configuration to manifest the resistant phenotype, in 
addition, any one of the three was able to reverse the resistant phenotype to 
susceptibility. Functional analysis using virus-induced gene silencing and 
transient genetic complementation demonstrated that the three CaFo proteins 
contribute redundantly to XeR6 susceptibility. Silencing either Bs6FoNPK, Bs6FoN 
and Bs6FoPK alone did not alter susceptibility, whereas simultaneous silencing 
of these genes conferred resistance. Conversely, the individual expression of 
pBs6FoNPK, pBs6FoN, and pBs6FoPK, in the resistant Ca61R background each 
restored susceptibility. These results demonstrate that the three Bs6 proteins 
act redundantly to promote XeR6 susceptibility and that loss of function of all 
three corresponding proteins was required for the recessive resistance phenotype 
conferred by bs661.

imide), shows promise due to the stability, cost, and visible light absorption 
of these materials. However, their low light absorbance and high recombination 
(low charge transfer) pose key challenges that limit their application and 
require further development. One way to address these limitations is through 
dual functionalization, which is tailored to increase absorbance and charge 
transfer. In this context, we characterize dually modified poly(triazine imide) 
(PTI) systems in which one fragment contains a nitrogen site functionalized with 
a hydrogen atom (herein referred to as NH functionalization), while another 
fragment contains a nitrogen atom replaced by a BH group (herein referred to as 
BH substitution). In particular, we investigate how the spatial distance between 
these modified sites modulates the electronic properties of the PTI systems. The 
results reveal a clear exponential dependence of these properties on 
substitution distance, reflecting the short-range nature of electronic 
interactions in π-conjugated systems. Furthermore, a detailed thermodynamic 
analysis indicates that only structures with short substitution distances 
satisfy the rigorous potential requirements for driving both hydrogen and oxygen 
evolution reactions. These findings provide critical microscopic insights for 
the rational design and structural optimization of PTI-based materials for 
enhanced photocatalytic performance.
METHODS: Geometry optimizations and vibrational frequency analyses were 
performed using DFT with the ωB97X-D functional, which should effectively 
describe local and charge- transfer excitations in conjugated organic 
structures, combined with the def2-SV(P) basis set. Vertical excitations were 
calculated using TD-DFT with the same methodology. We evaluated ionization 
energy, charge-transfer character, electrophilicity (Δω±), and the ε3 stability 
index. Regression models were used to evaluate the relationship between 
substitution distance and the electronic properties of the studied structures.

Microbial consortia-driven bioconversion of low-rank coal to methane presents a 
potential strategy for extracting energy from recalcitrant carbon reservoirs. 
Current systems achieve a theoretical conversion efficiency of 40-60%; however, 
hydrolysis poses a significant bottleneck due to its rate limitations. To 
investigate methane production during serial enrichment, we developed a 
six-cycle serial-batch enrichment protocol conducted under anaerobic conditions 
(35 °C, pH 7.2) using lignite-amended activated sludge as microbial seedings. 
High-throughput 16S rRNA gene sequencing revealed an overall decline in 
microbial alpha diversity and shifts in community composition across serial 
passages. The archaeal community was consistently dominated by Methanosarcina, 
with a mean relative abundance of 81.08% across P1-P6, indicating the 
establishment of a methanogenic consortium. XPS analysis showed changes in the 
relative contributions of surface carbon components, whereas SEM observations 
revealed local differences in coal surface morphology after incubation. Across 
six serial passages, the activated sludge enrichment consortia retained 
methane-producing capacity, with faster methane accumulation in later passages 
but no significant directional increase in day-28 methane yield.

METHODS: Infants with BA who underwent Kasai portoenterostomy were identified 
from the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (2008-2019).

episodes and LT was analyzed using exploratory logistic regression analysis.

assessed as a secondary outcome.
RESULTS: This study included 334 infants. Acute cholangitis occurred in 76.3% of

The efficacy of single-modal chemodynamic therapy (CDT) is often restricted by 
the antioxidant scavenging of overexpressed glutathione (GSH) within the tumor 
microenvironment (TME) and insufficient catalytic kinetics. Meanwhile, 
traditional photothermal therapy (PTT) also faces bottlenecks of a single 
therapeutic mechanism and low photothermal conversion efficiency, leading to 
unsatisfactory overall anti-tumor outcomes. To address these challenges, we 
constructed a smart-responsive, core-shell multifunctional nanotheranostic 
platform for near-infrared-II (NIR-II) photoacoustic (PA) imaging-guided 
synergistic PTT/CDT. This platform utilizes copper sulfide nanoparticles (CuS) 
as the photothermal core, conformally coated in situ with an Fe-tannic acid (TF) 
metal-phenolic network (MPN) shell (CuS@TF). In the mildly acidic TME, the TF 
shell dissociates to expose Fe/Cu bimetallic catalytic centers possessing 
excellent intrinsic peroxidase-like and catalase-like activities. Driven by the 
synergistic reduction of endogenous GSH and tannic acid, CuS@TF not only 
effectively depletes antioxidant GSH but also efficiently modulates H2O2 
metabolism, triggering a cascade burst of highly toxic hydroxyl radicals (·OH). 
Furthermore, under 1064 nm laser irradiation, the highly efficient localized 
hyperthermia generated by the CuS core not only directly ablates the tumor but 
also thermodynamically boosts the catalytic kinetics of the nanozymes, achieving 
profound PTT-sensitized CDT. Systematic in vitro and in vivo evaluations 
demonstrate that, under the precise navigation of PA imaging, CuS@TF exhibits 
remarkable tumor eradication efficacy (with a tumor inhibition rate of ~ 96.2%) 
and excellent in vivo biosafety. This work provides a novel design paradigm for 
the development of precise synergistic tumor theranostics based on 
multifunctional nanozymes.

Effectiveness of prenatal predictors for congenital diaphragmatic hernia on 
survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation requirement: a 
retrospective cohort study.

Rogers E(1), Le Vance J(2)(3), Naidu S(3)(4), Singh A(3), Jester I(3), Gurney 
L(5), Pachl M(3)(6).

Author information:
(1)Birmingham Medical School, College of Medicine and Health, University of 
Birmingham, Birmingham, B15 2TT, UK.
(2)Department of Applied Health Sciences, University of Birmingham, Birmingham, 
B15 2TT, UK.
(3)Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust, Birmingham, B15 2TG, 
UK.
(4)Hospital Tuanku Jaafar Seremban, Jalan Rasah, 70300, Seremban, Negri 
Sembilan, Malaysia.
(5)Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust, Birmingham, B15 2TG, 
UK. leo.gurney1@nhs.net.
(6)Institute of Cancer and Genomic Sciences, College of Medicine and Health, 
University of Birmingham, Birmingham, B15 2TT, UK.

INTRODUCTION: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) is associated with high 
mortality and morbidity. Antenatal counselling enables parents to prepare for 
the postnatal outcomes and relies on effective prognostic tools. Ultrasound 
(USS) predictors including observed/expected lung head ratio (o/e LHR) and liver 
position, are used independently, or combined into severity classifications. The 
aim was to evaluate the association between USS predictors, and severity 
classifications with survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane 
oxygenation (ECMO) requirement in prenatally diagnosed CDH at Birmingham Women's 
and Children's Hospital (BWC).
METHODS: CDH patients from BWC with dates of birth between 1st December 2013-1st 
December 2023 were retrospectively collected. Study inclusion required o/e LHR 
measurement between 22- and 32-weeks gestational age (GA.) Comparisons between 
groups was assessed by Fisher exact test and Mann-Whitney U test. Logistic 
regression was performed to determine prognostic ability, with area under curve 
(AUC) calculated.
RESULTS: 91 eligible patients were identified, which included 82 left-sided, and 
9 right-sided CDH. Overall, 55% survived to discharge and 13% required ECMO. In 
the left CDH cohort, 57% of infants survived to discharge, and 15% required 
ECMO. O/e LHR, liver position and the combined predictive model including o/e 
LHR and liver position were predictive of survival to discharge with good 
prognostic ability (AUC 0.769, AUC 0.703, and AUC 0.823, respectively). O/e LHR, 
liver position, and the combined predictive model were not predictive of ECMO 
requirement. In the right CDH patients, 33% survived to discharge, O/e LHR and 
liver position were not predictive of survival to discharge.
CONCLUSION: O/e LHR, liver position and the combination of these predictors, 
predicted survival to discharge in prenatally diagnosed left CDH with the 
combined model, the most predictive particularly in the isolated left CDH 
sub-group. Further analysis into effective predictors for ECMO requirement, and 
for right and complex left CDH is required.

[Nonpharmacological interventions in perioperative pain management].

[Article in German; Abstract available in German from the publisher]

Zugaj MR(1), Erlenwein J(2)(3), Meißner W(4), Keßler J(5).

Author information:
(1)Universität Heidelberg, Medizinische Fakultät Heidelberg, Klinik für

Nonpharmacological interventions can substantially improve the effectiveness of 
perioperative pain management. Positive, realistic information and goal setting, 
together with the deliberate use of communication strategies and placebo 
effects, can positively influence the experience of pain. Maladaptive cognition 
and an unnecessary focus on pain can intensify pain perception. Physiotherapy, 
transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) and acupuncture can be used 
as adjunctive treatment for selected indications. Music, quiet, appropriate 
lighting, a pleasant environment and personal belongings are easily implemented 
environmental factors with potential benefits. Nonpharmacological interventions 
are not a substitute for established postoperative pharmacological analgesia; 
however, as low-risk, patient-centered components they should form an integral 
part of multimodal treatment strategies. Clear responsibilities, appropriate 
training, interprofessional coordination and realistic patient selection are 
prerequisites for successful implementation. This article provides a practical 
overview of the targeted use of these techniques and strategies.

Publisher: Nichtmedikamentöse Verfahren können die Effektivität der 
perioperativen Schmerztherapie deutlich verbessern. Positive, realistische 
Informationen und Zielsetzungen sowie der bewusste Einsatz von 
Kommunikationsstrategien und Placeboeffekten haben einen positiven Einfluss auf 
das Schmerzerleben. Maladaptive Kognitionen sowie eine unnötige Fokussierung auf 
Schmerzen wirken verstärkend auf das Schmerzerleben. Physiotherapeutische 
Maßnahmen, transkutane elektrische Nervenstimulation (TENS) und Akupunktur 
können bei ausgewählten Indikationen ergänzend eingesetzt werden. Musik, Ruhe, 
Licht, angenehme Umgebung und persönliche Gegenstände sind niedrigschwellige 
Umgebungsfaktoren mit potenziellem Nutzen. Nichtmedikamentöse Verfahren ersetzen 
postoperativ keine etablierte medikamentöse Analgesie, sollten als risikoarme, 
patientenzentrierte Maßnahmen jedoch fester Bestandteil multimodaler 
Analgesiekonzepte sein. Voraussetzung für eine erfolgreiche Umsetzung sind klare 
Zuständigkeiten, Schulung, interprofessionelle Abstimmung und eine realistische 
Indikationsstellung. Dieser Beitrag gibt einen praxisorientierten Überblick über 
den gezielten Einsatz entsprechender Techniken und Strategien.

Treatment of pyogenic granuloma with a 577-nm diode laser in dark-skinned 
patients: A prospective case series.

Mohamed E(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Dermatology, Al-Azhar University, Asyut, Egypt. 
dessam73@azhar.edu.eg.

INTRODUCTION: Pyogenic granulomas are common benign vascular lesions found on 
exposed skin in children. Treatment in darker skin types can be challenging 
because of increased epidermal melanin absorption and the associated risk of 
collateral thermal injury.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a 577-nm diode laser for the 
treatment of pyogenic granuloma in patients with dark skin types.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Nine patients with pyogenic granuloma and skin types IV-V 
were enrolled in this prospective case series. They were treated every two weeks 
with a 577 nm diode laser using a 1 mm spot size, with fluence ranging from 
19-23 J/cm2 depending on lesion size until bleeding stopped. Sessions were 
repeated every two weeks until complete clearance. Patients were followed 
clinically and photographically every two weeks, and then one month after the 
final session.
RESULTS: This prospective case series included 9 patients clinically diagnosed 
with pyogenic granuloma. The mean age was 18.0 ± 14.6 years (range, 6-40 years), 
and the mean duration of pyogenic granuloma was 9.1 ± 3.94 months. Lesions were 
present on the lips of 4 patients (44.4%), the cheeks in 2 patients (22.2%), 
hands (2 patients, 22.2%), and neck (1 patient, 11.1%). All patients were 
treated with a 577 nm diode laser session every 2 weeks until complete 
clearance. Complete clearance was achieved in 3 patients after the first 
session, 4 patients after the second session, 1 patient after third session, and 
only one patient required four treatment sessions. Atrophic scarring was the 
only reported side effect, occurring in one case.
CONCLUSION: Treatment with a 577-nm diode laser appears to be a safe and 
effective option for pyogenic granuloma in patients with darker skin types.

Impacts of farming practices on pig gut microbiota and their interactions with 
soil microbial communities in tropical agroecosystems.

Desvennes C(1), Loranger-Merciris G(2), Gourdine JL(3), Montout L(2), Moreau 
F(4), Thouin J(4), Pruneau L(2).

Author information:
(1)ECOTERCA - ÉCOlogie TERrestre CAribéenne, Faculté des Sciences Exactes et 
Naturelles, Campus de Fouillole, Université des Antilles, BP 592, 97159, 
Pointe-à-Pitre Cedex, Guadeloupe, France. 
coraline.desvennes@etu.univ-antilles.fr.
(2)ECOTERCA - ÉCOlogie TERrestre CAribéenne, Faculté des Sciences Exactes et 
Naturelles, Campus de Fouillole, Université des Antilles, BP 592, 97159, 
Pointe-à-Pitre Cedex, Guadeloupe, France.
(3)UR-ASSET, INRAE Centre Antilles-Guyane, 97170, Petit-Bourg, Guadeloupe, 
France.
(4)ADNid, Qualtech, 830 Av. du Campus Agropolis, 34980, Montferrier-sur-Lez, 
France.

Livestock farming systems are associated with differences microbial communities 
in both animals and soils, yet the ecological mechanisms linking these 
compartments remain poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of 
contrasting farming systems (intensive vs. agroecological) on the gut microbiota 
of Creole pigs and associated soil microbial communities in farms located in 
Guadeloupe (French West Indies). Fecal and soil samples were analyzed using 16S 
and 18S Ribosomal Ribonucleic Acid (rRNA) genes metabarcoding to characterize 
bacterial, archaeal and fungal diversity. Pig gut microbiota was dominated by 
Bacillota (63.44% and 67.55% for intensive and agroecological raised pigs 
respectively) and Bacteroidota (24.70% and 18.56% for intensive and 
agroecological raised pigs respectively), whereas soils were mainly dominated by 
Acidobacteriota (14.61% and 17.48% for plowed and unplowed soil respectively), 
Actinomycetota (7.61% and 9.05% for plowed and unplowed soil respectively), and 
Bacillota (6.62% and 9.87% for plowed and unplowed soil respectively), 
indicating limited taxonomic overlap. Agroecological management was associated 
with higher relative abundances of Bacillota and Euryarchaeota in pigs and 
greater fungal diversity in soils. A total of 234 operational taxonomic units 
(OTUs) were common to all four groups (pig gut-agroecological, pig 
gut-intensive, plowed soil and unplowed soil), representing the microbial taxa 
shared between gut and soil environments; however, these taxa were generally 
abundant in the gut and rare in soils. These results suggest an ecological link 
between pigs and soil microbial communities that may be mediated by 
environmental processes. This underscores the interconnectedness of animal and 
environmental health within a One Health framework.

Vibostolimab Coformulated with Pembrolizumab Plus Chemotherapy as First-Line 
Therapy for Extensive-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer.

Sands J(1), Lu S(2), Aerts JG(3), Reck M(4), Navarro A(5), Shentzer Kutiel T(6), 
Peled N(7), Casarini I(8), Kerr SJ(9), Takahashi T(10), Bilici A(11), Cheng 
Y(12), Wang M(13), Lee SY(14), Łowczak A(15), Mazieres J(16), Hu H(17), Wu 
J(18), Aggarwal H(19), El-Osta H(19), Paz-Ares L(20).

Author information:
(1)Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Harvard

(16)Pulmonology Department, Toulouse University Hospital and Centre de Recherche 
Cancérologie Toulouse CRCT, INSERM, Toulouse, France.
(17)MSD (China) Co., Ltd., Beijing, China.
(18)Merck & Co., Inc., Upper Gwynedd, PA, USA.
(19)Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ, USA.
(20)Department of Medical Oncology, Hospital Universitario 12 de Octubre, 
Madrid, Spain.

BACKGROUND: Vibostolimab, an anti-T-cell immunoreceptor with immunoglobulin and 
ITIM domains (TIGIT) antibody, showed antitumor activity with pembrolizumab in 
non-small-cell lung cancer.
OBJECTIVE: The KEYVIBE-008 study evaluated vibostolimab coformulated with 
pembrolizumab (vibostolimab/pembrolizumab) plus etoposide and platinum-based 
chemotherapy (EP) versus atezolizumab plus EP as first-line therapy for 
extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer.
METHODS: Participants aged ≥18 years with untreated extensive-stage small-cell 
lung cancer were randomized 1:1 to vibostolimab/pembrolizumab (200 mg each) or 
atezolizumab (1200 mg) every 3 weeks, with EP and cisplatin/carboplatin for the 
first four cycles. The primary endpoint was overall survival. The prespecified 
interim analysis included a non-binding futility analysis of overall survival 
(futility threshold for actual number of events, P = 0.4816).
RESULTS: Four hundred and sixty participants were randomized (both arms, n = 
230). Median time from randomization to data cutoff (4 June, 2024) was 16.6 
(range 11.3‒26.1) months. The prespecified futility criterion for overall 
survival was met (hazard ratio 1.26; 95% confidence interval 1.00‒1.59; P = 
0.9762). There was no difference in progression-free survival (hazard ratio 
1.01; 95% confidence interval 0.82‒1.23) or objective response rates (71.7% with 
vibostolimab/pembrolizumab vs 74.8% with atezolizumab). Grade ≥3 
treatment-related adverse events occurred in 66.8% of participants treated with 
vibostolimab/pembrolizumab and 57.2% treated with atezolizumab. Immune-mediated 
adverse events and infusion reactions occurred in 39.3% and 29.7% of 
participants, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: In this interim analysis of vibostolimab/pembrolizumab plus EP 
versus atezolizumab plus EP as first-line therapy for extensive-stage small-cell 
lung cancer, the prespecified futility criterion for overall survival was met. 
Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events and immune-mediated adverse events 
were more frequent with vibostolimab/pembrolizumab versus atezolizumab. Given 
the overall benefit/risk profile, treatment with vibostolimab/pembrolizumab was 
discontinued.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov, NCT05224141.

Roles and Biological Effects of Polysaccharides in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A 
Narrative Review.

Ding N(1), Sun C(1), Wang H(1), Lv Y(1), Han Y(2), Kuang H(3).

Author information:
(1)Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine, Harbin, Heilongjiang, China.
(2)The First Affiliated Hospital of Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine, 
Harbin, Heilongjiang, China.
(3)The First Affiliated Hospital of Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine, 
Harbin, Heilongjiang, China. 949304685@qq.com.

Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) represents a prevalent and clinically 
significant reproductive-endocrine disorder among women of childbearing age. 
While dietary interventions, regular physical activity, and targeted lifestyle 
modifications have been validated to confer therapeutic benefits for PCOS 
management, polysaccharides key bioactive components of higher plants with 
extensive distribution throughout the plant and animal kingdoms exhibit distinct 
pleiotropic bioactivities, including anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, 
hypoglycemic, lipid-lowering, and anti-obesogenic properties. In the context of 
PCOS treatment, these natural macromolecules hold considerable promise for 
alleviating clinical manifestations, ameliorating insulin resistance and 
obesity, attenuating inflammatory responses, and restoring sex hormone 
homeostasis. Cumulative evidence from preclinical and clinical studies has 
demonstrated that polysaccharides can improve menstrual irregularities, reduce 
body weight, lower blood glucose and serum testosterone levels, and suppress 
aberrant inflammation. The present review systematically summarizes the 
multifaceted effects of diverse polysaccharide compounds on PCOS, aiming to 
provide insights into their potential as complementary therapeutic agents for 
this complex disorder.

Strengthening Signal Detection by Proactive Adverse Event Case Identification in 
Electronic Health Records Using a Text-Mining Tool.

von Kreijfelt G(1)(2), Zwaveling J(3), van Lint JA(4), Visser LE(5)(6), Kant 
AC(4)(3).

Author information:
(1)The Netherlands Pharmacovigilance Centre Lareb, 's-Hertogenbosch, The 
Netherlands. g.j.von_kreijfelt@lumc.nl.
(2)Department of Clinical Pharmacology and Toxicology, Leiden University Medical 
Centre, Albinusdreef 2, 2333 ZA, Leiden, The Netherlands. 
g.j.von_kreijfelt@lumc.nl.
(3)Department of Clinical Pharmacology and Toxicology, Leiden University Medical 
Centre, Albinusdreef 2, 2333 ZA, Leiden, The Netherlands.
(4)The Netherlands Pharmacovigilance Centre Lareb, 's-Hertogenbosch, The 
Netherlands.
(5)Department of Pharmacy, Haga Teaching Hospital, The Hague, The Netherlands.
(6)Hospital Pharmacy, Erasmus Medical Centre, Rotterdam, The Netherlands.

BACKGROUND: The spontaneous reporting system is the cornerstone of 
pharmacovigilance but is limited by substantial underreporting, which may delay 
safety signal detection.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the electronic health 
record-adverse event search method for identifying and reporting additional 
potential adverse drug reactions in electronic health records to strengthen 
routine signal detection.
METHODS: Between August 2022 and August 2025, targeted searches for adverse drug 
reactions were conducted in approximately 2,750,000 electronic health records 
from two Dutch hospitals using a data collection text-mining tool. Search 
criteria were derived from information in spontaneous reports of specific 
drug-adverse event associations. Structured (e.g. laboratory results, medication 
prescriptions) and unstructured (e.g. clinical notes, hospital discharge 
letters) data were used to identify potential adverse drug reactions. Identified 
cases were manually verified and, when relevant, reported to the Netherlands 
Pharmacovigilance Centre Lareb and analysed alongside spontaneous reports for 
signal detection.
RESULTS: A total of 147 electronic health record-derived cases were reported for 
41 drug-adverse event associations. These contributed to 34 signal detection 
analyses, supporting the assessment of seven safety signals. In 75% of the 
cases, a suspected causal relationship was documented by healthcare 
professionals in clinical notes. Electronic health record-derived cases 
accounted for up to 73% of the reports included in the seven detected signals.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that electronic health records can be used 
as an additional source of individual case safety reports in routine 
pharmacovigilance practice, supporting the further assessment of selected 
potential safety signals. Despite limitations related to efficiency, this 
proactive approach has potential to address underreporting and complement the 
spontaneous reporting system, strengthening signal detection.

Shear-wave elastography combined with ultrasound BI-RADS improves diagnostic 
accuracy in breast lesion characterization: a prospective cross-sectional study.

Bhutia RO(1), Lachungpa T(2), Sherpa M(3), Sharma BK(2), Gupta S(4), Nepal B(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Radiology, Sir Thutop Namgyal Memorial Hospital, Government of 
Sikkim, Gangtok, 737101, Sikkim, India.
(2)Department of Radiology, Sikkim Manipal Institute of Medical Sciences, 
Gangtok, 737101, Sikkim, India.
(3)Department of Pathology, Sikkim Manipal Institute of Medical Sciences, 
Gangtok, 737101, Sikkim, India.
(4)Department of Medical Radiology, Imaging and Therapeutic Technology, Parul 
Institute of Allied and Healthcare Sciences, Faculty of Medicine, Parul 
University, Vadodara, 391760, Gujarat, India. 
Shubham.gupta19175@paruluniversity.ac.in.

BACKGROUND: To compare BI-RADS and shear-wave elastography (SWE) for 
differentiating benign from malignant breast lesions and assess whether adding 
maximum elasticity (Emax) improves discrimination and biopsy decisions.
METHODS: In this diagnostic accuracy study (May 2023-August 2024), 87 adults 
with 93 breast lesions underwent B-mode BI-RADS and SWE (Emax, Emean, Emin). ROC 
analysis and logistic regression incorporating BI-RADS and Emax were performed. 
Patient-level bootstrap resampling with 2,000 iterations provided optimism 
correction.
RESULTS: Eleven lesions (11.8%) were malignant. Median Emax and Emean were 
higher in malignant lesions (200.1 vs 105.7 kPa, P = 0.003; 103.1 vs 70.7 kPa, 
P = 0.004). AUCs were 0.766 for BI-RADS, 0.774 for Emax, 0.767 for Emean, and 
0.697 for Emin; pairwise differences were nonsignificant (all P ≥ 0.153). The 
model had an AUC of 0.853 (95% CI, 0.754-0.951) and optimism-corrected AUC of 
0.844. AUC gain was 0.087 (0.016-0.158; P = 0.017), with corrected gain of 
0.077. At a 2% risk threshold, sensitivity was 100%, but biopsy recommendations 
increased from 41 to 55. The BE1 rule reduced biopsy recommendations by six, 
avoiding five benign biopsies but missing one carcinoma.
CONCLUSION: Adding Emax to BI-RADS improved discrimination, with the gain 
persisting after validation. However, only 11 lesions were malignant, yielding 
imprecise estimates. No operating point reduced biopsy recommendations without 
sacrificing sensitivity. The model and SWE cut-offs require external validation.
IMPLICATION OF PRACTICE: SWE may be used as an adjunct to BI-RADS for 
characterization, but Emax thresholds and the combined model should not yet 
guide biopsy downgrading. Larger prospective studies with external validation 
are needed before implementation.

Venous wash-out at contrast-enhanced ultrasound for the identification of 
hematologic splenic lesions: an exploratory real-world substudy.

Tirotta D(1), Lena C(2), Fabbri E(3), Muratori P(4)(2).

Author information:
(1)Internal Medicine, AUSL Forli', Morgagni Pierantoni Hospital, Forlì, Italy. 
danitirotta@libero.it.
(2)Internal Medicine Bologna, S Orsola University, Bologna, Italy.
(3)Research Office, AUSL Romagna, Rimini, Italy.
(4)Internal Medicine, AUSL Forli', Morgagni Pierantoni Hospital, Forlì, Italy.

PURPOSE: Splenic lesions are a relatively rare but clinically relevant finding 
in internal medicine practice, particularly when hematologic or 
lymphoproliferative disorders are suspected. The aim of this exploratory 
subanalysis was to evaluate the role of CEUS perfusion patterns, with particular 
attention to venous wash-out and its timing, in discriminating between 
hematologic and non-hematologic disease in a real-world Internal Medicine 
cohort.
METHODS: An exploratory retrospective subanalysis was conducted on patients 
included in the intervention arm of a multicenter Quality Improvement study 
evaluating a structured contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS)-based diagnostic 
pathway in newly identified splenic lesions. Consecutive adult patients with 
newly detected splenic lesions identified on B-mode ultrasound who underwent 
CEUS as part of the initial diagnostic evaluation were included. CEUS perfusion 
patterns were qualitatively classified according to arterial wash-in, venous 
wash-out, and wash-out timing. The diagnostic reference standard consisted of 
histologic and/or cytologic examination when available, or integration of 
clinical, laboratory, and imaging follow-up data within 90 days. In patients 
without histologic confirmation, non-hematologic classification required 
clinical and laboratory stability or improvement, stability or resolution of the 
splenic lesion on follow-up imaging, identification of an alternative 
non-hematologic diagnosis when present, and absence of a hematologic diagnosis 
during the 90-day follow-up. In line with the parent study, one patient in the 
intervention-arm cohort did not receive a definitive lesion-specific etiologic 
diagnosis within 90 days; however, no patient remained indeterminate for the 
prespecified binary endpoint because classification as hematologic versus 
non-hematologic was possible in all cases. The study endpoint was binary 
diagnostic classification (hematologic vs non-hematologic).
RESULTS: Fifty patients were included, of whom 11 (22%) had a hematologic 
diagnosis and 39 (78%) had a non-hematologic diagnosis. In univariable analysis, 
multiple lesions, systemic symptoms, and especially venous wash-out were 
associated with hematologic diagnosis. Venous wash-out was present in 10/11 
hematologic cases and in 3/39 non-hematologic cases. In hematologic cases, 
wash-out was almost always early (< 60 s), whereas in the few non-hematologic 
cases with wash-out it was late. In the exploratory multivariable model, venous 
wash-out was the only variable independently associated with hematologic 
diagnosis. Because of the small number of hematologic events, this association 
should be interpreted as statistically unstable and hypothesis-generating. 
Venous wash-out showed a sensitivity of 90.9%, specificity of 92.3%, positive 
predictive value of 76.9%, negative predictive value of 97.3%, and accuracy of 
92.0%.
CONCLUSION: In patients with newly identified splenic lesions, venous wash-out 
at CEUS, particularly if early, was the pattern most strongly associated with 
hematologic diagnosis in this cohort. The absence of wash-out was associated 
with a low probability of hematologic disease, suggesting a possible utility of 
CEUS in diagnostic rule-out in real-world Internal Medicine settings. However, 
diagnostic performance estimates, particularly negative predictive value, should 
be interpreted cautiously in view of the low prevalence of hematologic disease 
and the exploratory sample size. These findings require confirmation in larger 
cohorts.

BACKGROUND: To evaluate whether baseline multi-parametric MRI radiomics models, 
integrating multiple regions of interest (ROIs), can predict pathological 
complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT) in locally 
advanced rectal cancer (LARC), and to validate performance externally.
METHODS: In this multicenter, retrospective cohort study, 510 patients with LARC 
treated with NCRT followed by total mesorectal excision were enrolled (330 for 
training, 83 for internal validation, and 97 for external validation). Radiomic 
features were extracted from three ROIs (primary tumor, mesorectal region, and 
lateral lymph node regions). After redundancy reduction and clustering, the top 
30 features were selected using gradient boosting decision trees via 
cross-validation. Four classifiers, logistic regression, random forest, support 
vector machine, and extra trees, were evaluated, with SMOTE applied to address 
class imbalance. Model performance was compared across ROI combinations, MRI 
sequences, and algorithms using the area under the receiver operating 
characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: Overall, 98 of 510 patients (19.2%) achieved pCR. The multi-ROI, 
multi-parametric model based on extra trees achieved an AUC of 0.717 in the 
external validation set. Among single-ROI models, tumor ROI yielded the highest 
AUC (0.630). Among MRI sequences, the ADC-based model performed best (AUC 
0.629).
CONCLUSION: Baseline multi-parametric MRI radiomics models integrating multiple 
ROIs showed modest predictive performance for pCR in LARC and demonstrated 
similar predictive utility in an independent external cohort. This approach may 
provide pre-treatment risk stratification and support future research on 
individualized treatment strategies and organ preservation.

Post-stroke depression (PSD) is a serious complication that significantly 
hinders stroke patients' recovery and quality of life. Uncovering the molecular 
changes that drive PSD is vital for understanding how depression develops 
following a stroke. In this study, we established a reproducible PSD model using 
minimally invasive photochemical-induced focal cortical lesion. Transcriptomic 
sequencing demonstrated that dysregulation of circadian entrainment genes is a 
central pathway in the development of post-stroke depressive-like behaviors. 
Protein-protein interaction network analysis of these circadian rhythm-related 
genes identified six hub genes. Four of these, including Pomc and Bmp4, 
exhibited expression patterns consistent with experimental validation. 
Integrated single-cell transcriptomic analysis further pinpointed 
cell-type-specific expression abnormalities of Pomc in endothelial cells and 
Bmp4 in oligodendrocytes. Subsequently, in silico perturbation analysis further 
indicated that their shared underlying regulatory mechanisms involve cell 
adhesion and extracellular matrix interaction. Collectively, using 
transcriptomic and single-cell sequencing in a PSD model, this study revealed 
altered expression patterns of circadian rhythm-related genes, providing 
potential targets for further investigation into the pathogenesis of PSD.

Angiogenesis is the physiological process by which blood vessels form to provide 
oxygen and nutrients to cells. While angiogenesis can contribute to the therapy 
of certain ailments, it can also be involved in the pathology of diseases such 
as cancer. Angiogenesis is performed by endothelial cells (ECs), the innermost 
layer of blood vessels and the process is dependent on the expression of 
pro-angiogenic growth factors, cell adhesion proteins, and signaling pathways. 
Several pathways influence and regulate different stages of blood vessel 
formation, including EC proliferation, differentiation, migration, polarity, and 
survival. In tumors, these pathways are dysfunctional, leading to uncontrolled 
cellular attributes, including deregulated angiogenesis. Specifically, 
Wnt-β-catenin signaling, a vital cell proliferation pathway, anomalously 
enhances the expression of pro-angiogenic genes such as vascular endothelial 
growth factor VEGF, fibronectin and other factors. This review elucidates the 
role of angiogenic factors and highlights the interplay among VEGF, β-catenin, 
VE-cadherin, and integrin, all of which are associated with the Wnt-β-catenin 
pathway. Secreted frizzled related protein 4 (SFRP4) is a well-established Wnt 
antagonist proven to have anti-tumorigenic, anti-angiogenic, and pro-apoptotic 
roles. This review proposes a novel role of interaction between SFRP4 and 
integrin which could disrupt Wnt signaling and inhibit angiogenesis by SFRP4 
mediated inhibition of integrin signaling.

Exploring shared genetic architecture in psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis: a 
multi-method approach.

Zhou Z(1), Zhan DD(1), Gan L(1), Fan LL(1), Wang Y(1), Yang J(1), Li M(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Dermatology, The General Hospital of Western Theater Command, 
270#, Rongdu Avenue, Jinniu District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province, China.
(2)Department of Dermatology, The General Hospital of Western Theater Command, 
270#, Rongdu Avenue, Jinniu District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province, China. 
limin0214@126.com.

Psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) are immune-mediated diseases that 
co-occur clinically, but their shared genetic architecture and the direction of 
shared effects remain debated. We integrated genome-wide association study 
(GWAS) summary statistics from FinnGen and UK Biobank using linkage 
disequilibrium score regression (LDSC), high-definition likelihood (HDL), 
ρ-HESS, MTAG, CPASSOC, colocalization, and MAGMA. The primary cross-population 
analysis showed a negative global genetic correlation (LDSC unconstrained: 
rg = - 0.3004, P = 6.70 × 10⁻³; constrained: rg = - 0.2251, P = 3.00 × 10⁻⁴; 
HDL: rg = - 0.3307, P = 1.14 × 10⁻³). Ancestry-matched sensitivity analyses 
produced positive but heterogeneous estimates (FinnGen: rg = 0.2422 to 0.6334; 
UK Biobank: rg = 0.1294 to 0.3777) that were not uniformly significant. 
Cross-trait analyses identified 95 independent SNPs and 10 additional shared 
loci. After allele harmonization, all 10 loci showed opposite MTAG effect 
directions for psoriasis and RA (two-sided exact binomial P = 1.95 × 10⁻³), 
indicating directional heterogeneity and possible antagonistic pleiotropy. 
Colocalization provided evidence for a shared causal signal at two TYK2 
variants, rs11085727 and rs144309607 (PP.H4 > 0.8; r² = 0.0805 and D' = 1.0), 
although these results should be interpreted cautiously because they may reflect 
distinct correlated variants. MAGMA identified immune-related tissue enrichment 
for psoriasis but not RA. Collectively, these findings indicate that psoriasis 
and RA share genetic loci, but the global direction of genetic correlation is 
ancestry- and data-source-dependent and that locus-level effects include 
opposing directions. TYK2 remains a plausible shared target, but its therapeutic 
implications require direction-aware fine-mapping and functional validation.

Automated virtual reduction of pseudo-fractured mandibles using sex-specific 
statistical shape models: a proof-of-concept study.

Morita D(1), Nemoto H(2), Otake Y(3), Tsunoda Y(2), Hanai U(2), Kono T(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, Tokai University School of 
Medicine, 143 Shimokasuya, Isehara, Kanagawa, 259-1193, Japan. 
d-morita@tokai.ac.jp.
(2)Department of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, Tokai University School of 
Medicine, 143 Shimokasuya, Isehara, Kanagawa, 259-1193, Japan.
(3)Division of Information Science, Nara Institute of Science and Technology, 
Nara, 630-0192, Japan.

PURPOSE: This proof-of-concept study developed an automated virtual mandibular 
fracture reduction framework using statistical shape models (SSMs), evaluated it 
in ten controlled pseudo-fracture cases, and compared sex-specific and 
combined-sex SSMs.
METHODS: Male, female, and combined-sex SSMs were constructed from CT-derived 
mandibular meshes using the same correspondence estimation, atlas updating, and 
principal component analysis pipeline. Ten independent mandibles (five male and 
five female) were divided into three fragments and displaced. Reduction jointly 
optimized SSM coefficients and fragment transformations using the covariance 
matrix adaptation evolution strategy. Paired results were compared using exact 
two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
RESULTS: The male, female, and combined-sex SSMs required 28, 32, and 29 
principal components, respectively, to reach 95% cumulative explained variance. 
Using the sex-specific SSMs, the mean symmetric chamfer distance and symmetric 
root-mean-square error were 0.712 ± 0.210 mm and 0.855 ± 0.231 mm, respectively, 
compared with 0.778 ± 0.309 mm and 0.937 ± 0.358 mm using the combined-sex SSM. 
Although the sex-specific SSMs yielded numerically lower mean errors, the 
differences were not statistically significant (p = 0.232 and p = 0.193, 
respectively). Computation time was approximately 23 min per reduction run.
CONCLUSION: The framework achieved near-millimetric accuracy, supporting the 
technical feasibility of automated virtual mandibular reduction under controlled 
conditions. Sex-specific SSMs yielded numerically lower errors than the 
combined-sex SSM, without a statistically significant advantage. Larger 
validation cohorts and real-fracture studies are required before clinical 
application.

He X(#)(1), Zhang H(#)(2), Zhang Y(2), Wu J(2), Wang T(2), Liu Y(2), Jin K(2), 
Tang W(2), Ye Q(2), Wang Q(3).

Author information:

MG53/TRIM72 is a member of the tripartite motif family of E3 ubiquitin ligases 
that regulates metabolic homeostasis and tumor-associated signaling; however, 
its role in bladder cancer remains undefined. We investigated the expression, 
function, and molecular mechanism of MG53 in bladder cancer. MG53 expression was 
analyzed in bladder cancer tissues and cell lines. Functional assays including 
proliferation, invasion, glycolytic metabolism, intracellular reactive oxygen 
species (ROS) accumulation, and apoptosis were performed. The interaction 
between MG53 and AMPKα was examined using co-immunoprecipitation and 
ubiquitination assays. In vivo tumor growth was assessed in xenograft models. 
MG53 was significantly downregulated in bladder cancer tissues compared to 
adjacent normal tissues, and its expression was inversely correlated with AMPKα 
levels. Overexpression of MG53 suppressed cell proliferation, invasion, and 
glycolytic metabolism, and was also accompanied by increased intracellular ROS 
accumulation and a higher apoptotic rate, together with elevated cleaved 
caspase-3 and an increased Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, in bladder cancer cells. 
Mechanistically, MG53 promoted the ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of 
AMPKα. In vivo experiments demonstrated that MG53 overexpression inhibited tumor 
growth in xenograft models. Our findings reveal that MG53 functions as a tumor 
suppressor in bladder cancer by promoting AMPKα degradation through its E3 
ubiquitin ligase activity, thereby attenuating the Warburg effect; MG53 
overexpression was also associated with intracellular ROS accumulation and 
apoptosis in bladder cancer cells. MG53 represents a candidate therapeutic 
target for bladder cancer treatment, whose translational value remains to be 
established in future preclinical and clinical studies.

Robotic surgical platforms are diversifying, and clinical outcomes are 
increasingly comparable across systems, yet the console surgeon's subjective 
experience remains poorly characterized. We developed a surgeon-reported 
questionnaire on robotic surgical systems and performed a preliminary 
psychometric evaluation in robotic radical prostatectomy. The Surgeons' 
Perception Questionnaire on Robotics (SPQR) includes 31 five-point items in six 
domains: technical and operational aspects, key surgical tasks, ergonomics and 
physical comfort, communication and workflow integration, learning curve, and 
overall evaluation. In a cross-sectional web-based survey, surgeons rated the 
platform they primarily used for robotic radical prostatectomy. Internal 
consistency was assessed with polychoric-based Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's 
omega; exploratory (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) were performed 
in the same sample. Fifty-nine surgeons participated (response rate 42%); 81% 
evaluated the da Vinci Xi. Overall internal consistency was high (alpha 0.96; 
omega 0.97). Alpha and omega were ≥ 0.84 in five domains but below 0.70 for 
ergonomics and physical comfort (0.64 and 0.67). EFA suggested three factors 
(system performance and satisfaction; learning curve and training; ergonomics). 
CFA showed high incremental fit (comparative fit index 0.985) but inadequate 
absolute fit (root mean square error of approximation 0.097; standardized root 
mean square residual 0.135), and the ergonomics factor was weakly defined. The 
SPQR showed high internal consistency in most domains and a provisional 
multidimensional structure. Because the sample was small, highly experienced, 
predominantly male, and dominated by one platform, these findings require 
confirmation in larger independent cohorts before the SPQR is used for platform 
comparisons.

Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) and 6,388 from the National Health and Nutrition 
Examination Survey (NHANES). Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline 
analyses were used to assess associations of triglyceride-glucose (TyG), 
TyG-body mass index (TyG-BMI), TyG-waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR), metabolic 
score for IR (METS-IR), and estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) with 
diabetes. Subgroup analyses and receiver operating characteristic curves were 
employed to evaluate robustness and discrimination.
RESULTS: Over 7 years, diabetes developed in 736 CHARLS participants (11.67%) 
and 1,451 NHANES participants (22.71%). Five IR-related markers were 
significantly associated with the risk of diabetes and demonstrated good 
predictive performance. Elevated levels of TyG, TyG-BMI, TyG-WHtR, and METS-IR, 
as well as lower levels of eGDR, were associated with increased diabetes risk 
(all P < 0.001). Most associations remained robust across subgroup analyses. 
Among the five markers, eGDR demonstrated the highest predictive performance in 
the NHANES cohort (AUC: 0.789; 95% CI: 0.776-0.802) and showed favorable 
predictive ability in the CHARLS cohort.
CONCLUSION: IR-related markers are significantly associated with the risk of 
diabetes in individuals with CKM syndrome and serve as reliable predictors of 
new-onset diabetes. Among these indicators, eGDR and TyG-WHtR were relatively 
reliable predictors, highlighting their potential as valuable tools for early 
diabetes screening.

Dental students' intention to treat people living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA): an

Goldstein A(1), Emodi-Perlman A(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Oral Rehabilitation, Maurice and Gabriela Goldschleger School

Limited evidence exists regarding dental students' intentions to treat People 
Living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA). This study aimed to examine the factors associated 
with intentions to treat PLWHA among students at the Tel Aviv University School

He Q(1), Liang J(2), Ganotice F(3).

Author information:
(1)Bau Institute of Medical and Health Sciences Education, Li Ka Shing, Faculty

We respond to Chen's commentary on our recent article, "Personality and 
emotional intelligence among health professions students: the roles of perceived 
group cohesion, perceived team emotional intelligence, and attitudes toward 
interprofessional education." We address methodological and interpretive 
questions concerning covariate coding, variable centering, the Group Cohesion 
(GC) × Attitudes Toward Interprofessional Education (ATIPE) interaction, and the 
perceived team emotional intelligence (TEI)-only indirect pathway. Sensitivity 
analyses supported the main findings of the original article, including the 
serial mediation effects, the negative GC × ATIPE interaction, and the moderated 
mediation effects. We further clarify that the interaction reflects attenuation 
rather than amplification, and that the TEI-only pathway attenuated after 
attitudes toward interprofessional education were included as a predictor. 
Overall, this reply reinforces the robustness of the original findings while 
refining their interpretation.

A gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene score for subtyping and predicting the 
treatment response in rheumatoid arthritis: integrative analysis with in silico 
knockout validation.

Sun XF(1), Yang YJ(1), Li CL(1), Huang T(1), Wang Q(2), Yu Q(3).

Author information:
(1)School of Management, Shanxi Medical University, Taiyuan, China.
(2)School of Management, Shanxi Medical University, Taiyuan, China. 
dr_wangqi_2020@163.com.
(3)School of Management, Shanxi Medical University, Taiyuan, China. 
yuqi@sxmu.edu.cn.

BACKGROUND: The pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves a complex 
interplay between immune dysregulation and metabolic disturbance, with the gut 
microbiota and its metabolites playing pivotal roles. However, integrated 
biomarkers based on the "gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene" regulatory axis 
that can quantify its impact on RA stratification and therapeutic response are 
lacking.
METHODS: We integrated multiple RA transcriptomic datasets to screen for host 
genes explicitly associated with the gut microbiota and metabolites using the 
gutMGene database. A gut microbiota-metabolite-host score (GMS) was constructed 
via principal component analysis (PCA). Immune infiltration patterns were 
evaluated using CIBERSORT. Furthermore, scRNA-seq was employed to map the 
cellular origins of key genes, and in silico knockout analysis using 
scTenifoldKnk was performed to simulate the functional ablation of core host 
genes within this regulatory axis. Additionally, molecular docking was conducted 
to validate the binding affinities between the key host proteins and the optimal 
small molecule.
RESULTS: We identified seven microbiota-metabolite-host hub genes (FOS, JUN, 
IDO1, PEMT, EGFR, ABCC4, and FADS3) and constructed the GMS. The GMS stratified 
patients with RA into two distinct functional subtypes: an adaptive immune 
activation subtype and an inflammatory-metabolic composite subtype. Notably, the 
GMS demonstrated superior performance in predicting responses to anti-TNF and 
rituximab therapies. The scRNA-seq analysis revealed high expression of FOS and 
JUN in T cells and NK cells. In silico knockout analysis further revealed the 
central transcription factors FOS and JUN as key executors of this axis, as 
their ablation significantly affected osteoclast differentiation and the 
enrichment of TNF/MAPK inflammatory pathways. These computational findings 
support the core mechanism by which gut microbiota-metabolite signalling drives 
RA joint pathology via FOS/JUN. Molecular docking results confirmed strong 
binding interactions between the identified active molecules and their 
respective target proteins.
CONCLUSION: This study establishes a GMS based on the gut 
microbiota-metabolite-host gene regulatory axis as a robust tool for molecular 
subtyping and predicting biological therapy responses in patients with RA. 
Crucially, through integrated computational modelling, including in silico 
knockout and molecular docking validation, we identified FOS/JUN as critical 
executor genes linking the gut microenvironment to RA bone destruction, 
providing novel targets for therapeutic strategies aimed at the gut-joint axis.

Dental status, dietary intake, and frailty are closely interrelated among older 
adults. Nevertheless, the association between posterior occlusal support and 
frailty, and whether diet-related indicators can statistically account for part 
of this association, remain insufficiently elucidated. To primarily investigate

interactions between FTUs and frailty (P-interaction > 0.05). Among older adults 
in the United States, higher FTUs are associated with lower odds of frailty.

and frailty in older adults and cannot establish causal relationships.

Cellular senescence and the SASP in the oral-metabolic axis: a putative link 
between periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Wu Y(1), Li B(1), Yang Z(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Stomatology, Wenjiang District People's Hospital, Chengdu, 
611135, Sichuan, P. R. China.
(2)Department of Stomatology, Wenjiang District People's Hospital, Chengdu, 
611135, Sichuan, P. R. China. 19938485871@163.com.

Periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are chronic inflammatory 
disorders with a bidirectional clinical association. Although microbial, immune, 
and metabolic mechanisms contribute to this relationship, they do not fully 
explain the persistence of inflammation and defective tissue repair. Cellular 
senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) may provide 
an additional framework for understanding this interaction. Within periodontal 
tissues, sustained microbial and metabolic stress may promote 
senescence-associated changes that disturb local immune regulation, tissue 
regeneration and bone homeostasis. These processes could interact with microbial 
dysbiosis and systemic inflammation as part of the oral-metabolic axis. However, 
the available evidence remains uneven. Diabetes-related stress can promote 
senescence-like changes in periodontal tissues, whereas direct evidence that 
periodontal senescence impairs distant metabolic organs is limited. This review 
examines the evidence linking cellular senescence to periodontal inflammation 
and T2DM, and discusses the emerging preclinical evidence for targeting 
senescent cells and the SASP.

Influence of final irrigation with EDTA and chitosan on apical microleakage of

Ünal Z(1), Küçükekenci FF(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Endodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, Ordu University, Ordu,

(2)Department of Endodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, Ordu University, Ordu,
