Autism: epidemiology, genetics, molecular mechanisms, clinical features, 
diagnosis, and management.

Fan R(1), Wang Y(2), Miao T(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Human Anatomy, School of Basic Medicine, China Medical 
University, Shenyang, 110122, China.
(2)Department of Human Anatomy, School of Basic Medicine, China Medical 
University, Shenyang, 110122, China. 20242252@cmu.edu.cn.
(3)Department of Human Anatomy, School of Basic Medicine, China Medical 
University, Shenyang, 110122, China. 20222222@cmu.edu.cn.

Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition 
characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and restricted, 
repetitive behaviors. Global prevalence has risen steadily, yet reported rates 
vary markedly across regions and populations. These discrepancies reflect 
inequities in diagnostic access and screening capacity rather than true 
differences in incidence. This review integrates recent advances across the full 
ASD research spectrum. We first examine global epidemiological patterns and 
demographic disparities. We then dissect the genetic architecture of ASD, 
including rare and common variants, copy number variations, and gene-environment 
interactions that disrupt prenatal and early postnatal brain development. At the 
molecular level, diverse risk factors converge on shared neurodevelopmental 
mechanisms. These include synaptic dysfunction, dysregulated signaling through 
mTOR, Ras-ERK-MAPK, Wnt and Notch pathways, impaired neurogenesis, chronic 
neuroimmune inflammation, and excitatory-inhibitory imbalance. We also discuss 
how these mechanisms manifest in core clinical features, including social 
deficits, repetitive behaviors, and sensory abnormalities. We summarize current 
diagnostic standards and their limitations. Cross-species animal models, from 
Drosophila to non-human primates, are evaluated for their essential roles in 
mechanistic validation and therapeutic screening. Finally, we assess clinical 
management strategies, ranging from behavioral and educational interventions to 
pharmacological and supportive services. By tracing a continuous path from risk 
factors at the population level through molecular pathophysiology to 
interventions guided by mechanism, this review offers an integrative synthesis 
that connects basic discovery to clinical translation. We further discuss how 
multi-omics and artificial intelligence may advance precise diagnosis rooted in 
mechanism and personalized treatment.

PARADOX: pharmacological analysis of relation anomalies and drug contradictions 
extraction.

Fata A(1), Rahmani H(2).

Author information:
(1)School of Computer Engineering, Iran University of Science and Technology, 
Tehran, Iran.
(2)School of Computer Engineering, Iran University of Science and Technology, 
Tehran, Iran. h_rahmani@iust.ac.ir.

The rapid expansion of biomedical literature has led to a growing number of 
contradictory pharmacological reports, where the same drug interactions are 
described with opposing outcomes across studies. Critically, many such reports 
are only apparent contradictions arising from mismatched experimental conditions 
such as dosage, strain, endpoint, or population, rather than logically 
incompatible claims under comparable settings. These inconsistencies complicate 
drug safety evaluation and hinder the reliability of automated biomedical 
knowledge systems. In this paper, we introduce PARADOX, a framework for the 
detection and analysis of pharmacological contradictions in scientific text. The 
system integrates BioBERT-based embeddings, a Siamese similarity model, and an 
iterative refinement using a snowball process to progressively extract and 
refine conflicting relational statements. Each candidate contradiction is 
semantically verified using GPT-4o-mini, producing a structured contradiction 
graph derived from validated outputs. Beyond detection, we introduce a 
three-stage decision-tree protocol to distinguish real contradictions from 
apparent ones and outline a conditional biological modulation map that 
summarizes how identical pharmacological inputs may yield divergent outcomes 
under different conditions. On more than 18,000 evaluated pairs, the model 
recovered 39 validated contradiction candidates with only three misses. 
Qualitative analysis shows both genuine logical conflicts and opposing 
statements better explained by contextual differences or missing metadata. The 
results highlight the potential of contradiction-aware mining to strengthen 
pharmacovigilance, enhance literature consistency checking, and support more 
robust biomedical reasoning.

Amphora coffeaeformis supplementation attenuates cypermethrin-triggered

Elbahnaswy S(1), Elshopakey GE(2), Eldessouki EAA(3), Shukry M(4), Ibrahim I(5),

Cypermethrin (CYP), a neurotoxic pesticide, is released into the environment 
uncontrollably, posing a particular threat to aquatic species. Amphora 
coffeaeformis was demonstrated to have a protective effect against hazardous CYP 
exposure by markedly reducing neurotoxicity in Oreochromis niloticus. A total of 
240 O. niloticus were divided equally into four groups in triplicate as follows: 
Control, AMP (5% A. coffeaeformis/kg diet), CYP (1.25 µg/L), and AMP + CYP (5% 
A. coffeaeformis/kg diet + 1.25 µg/L). Our data showed that CYP exposure for 30 
days induced a significant decrease in γ-aminobutyric acid, 
acetylcholinesterase, reduced glutathione, superoxide dismutase, and catalase 
activities, and total antioxidant capacity in brain tissue, as well as in serum 
levels of lysozyme, total immunoglobulin, and nitric oxide. There was also a 
notable increase in brain malondialdehyde and serum cortisol and glucose levels. 
The qPCR analysis demonstrated a significant up-regulation of IL1β, TNFα, HSP70, 
and Cas3 mRNA expression in brain tissue. Importantly, A. coffeaeformis 
significantly shielded against CYP-induced brain impairments, including neuronal 
degeneration, spongiosis, perivascular edema, and inflammation. These 
alterations were markedly reduced following dietary exposure to A. 
coffeaeformis, as confirmed by IHC data. Our data examined the neuroprotective 
effects of A. coffeaeformis in CYP-exposed fish, supporting its potential as an 
anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and neuroprotective agent.

Integrative computational analysis of glycan and ROS-linker effects on 
Pertuzumab-HER2 stability for multimodal ADC architectures.

Noriega HA(1), Wang XS(2).

Author information:
(1)Artificial Intelligence and Drug Discovery (AIDD) Core Laboratory for 
District of Columbia Center for AIDS Research (DC CFAR), Department of 
Pharmaceutical Sciences, College of Pharmacy, Howard University, Washington, DC, 
USA.
(2)Artificial Intelligence and Drug Discovery (AIDD) Core Laboratory for 
District of Columbia Center for AIDS Research (DC CFAR), Department of

ADCs rely on linker chemistry to balance systemic stability with conditional 
activation. Glycoengineering provides additional design opportunities by 
incorporating terminal sialylated glycans that support multimeric interactions 
and PEG conjugation. Here, we applied an integrated computational workflow 
combining structural prediction with AlphaFold3, glycan construction with 
GLYCAM, docking with DiffDock, and all-atom free-energy perturbation (FEP) 
simulations in GROMACS using a double-decoupling framework to evaluate the 
effects of three Fc-linked glycan architectures: a short sialic acid glycan, a 
branched sialylated glycan with a PEG-accessible branch, and a branched 
sialylated glycan incorporating both ROS-cleavable branch and a PEG-accessible 
branch, on Pertuzumab in complex with HER2. Short glycans conferred modest 
stabilization but limited conformational engagement, while branched variants 
produced the strongest stabilization, linking structural effects with PEG 
accessibility. In branched variants, the ROS-responsive branch exhibited reduced 
stabilization consistent with a conditionally labile architecture, while the 
PEG-accessible branch remained structurally intact. These findings demonstrate 
how glycan branching and linker architecture influence relative Fc stabilization 
and structural behavior within modeled systems and support the use of an 
integrated computational workflow combining structural modeling, docking, and 
free-energy calculations to prioritize complex linker chemistries for further 
experimental validation.

Lyme Disease and Other Tick-Borne Infections.

Halperin JJ(1)(2), Wormser GP(3).

Author information:

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The neurologic manifestations of selected tick-transmitted 
infections in North America and Eurasia were reviewed.
RECENT FINDINGS: Both Powassan virus in North America, and Tick-Borne 
Encephalitis (TBE) virus in Eurasia can cause encephalitis, often with 
significant neurologic morbidity. Lyme disease, Ehrlichia chaffeensis (the cause 
of human monocytic ehrlichiosis [HME]), and Borrelia miyamotoi infections can 
cause meningitis (the third primarily in immunocompromised individuals). 
Patients with Lyme disease may also develop cranial neuropathy, and/or 
radiculoneuropathy. Tick-borne infections are being increasingly recognized in 
North America and Eurasia. While many tick-borne infections can cause headaches, 
lethargy or other non-specific symptoms, these are generally not evidence of 
nervous system infection - i.e., neuroinvasive disease. The latter is less 
common but may occur in infections due to Powassan and TBE viruses, in HME and 
in Lyme disease. Patients with symptomatic nervous system infection due to 
Powassan or TBE virus are at high risk of developing significant neurologic 
impairment and sequelae.

Lactobacillus brevis cell-free supernatant attenuates inflammation-associated 
gene expression and differentially modulates host defense-associated genes in 
DSS-stimulated HT-29 cells.

Moghanlou A(#)(1), Rasouli S(#)(2), Asadi Lanjavani S(3), Falsafi S(1), Behrouzi 
A(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Microbiology, TeMS.C, Islamic Azad University, Tehran, Iran.
(2)Department of Immunology & Microbiology, TeMS.C, Islamic Azad University, 
Tehran, Iran.
(3)Islamic Azad University, Central Tehran Branch, Tehran, Iran.
(4)Department of Microbiology, TeMS.C, Islamic Azad University, Tehran, Iran. 
avabehrouzi696463@iau.ac.ir.
(#)Contributed equally

BACKGROUND: Dysregulated Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling in intestinal 
epithelial cells contributes to persistent mucosal inflammation in inflammatory 
bowel disease (IBD). Although Lactobacillus brevis has demonstrated 
anti-inflammatory potential, the transcriptional effects of its secreted 
metabolites on inflammatory and host defense-associated components of epithelial 
innate immune signaling remain insufficiently characterized. This study 
investigated the effects of L. brevis cell-free supernatant (CFS) on 
TLR-associated gene expression in DSS-stimulated HT-29 cells.
METHODS: 1% DSS stimulated HT-29 human intestinal epithelial cells (inflammatory 
epithelial model) were treated with 50% L. brevis CFS (48 h) following viability 
assessment using MTT assay. Transcriptional profiling of 84 key genes involved 
in the TLR signaling pathway was performed using the RT² Profiler™ PCR Array. 
Differential gene expression was analyzed using the ΔΔCt method, followed by 
pathway-level mapping of the MyD88- and TRIF-dependent branches. Raw p-values 
were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg FDR 
procedure.
RESULTS: Treatment with L. brevis CFS was associated with significant 
downregulation of multiple inflammation-associated genes, including TLR2, TLR4, 
MYD88, TIRAP, IRAK1, IRAK4, MAP3K7, NFKB1, IL1A, IL1B, IL6, IL12A, CCL2, and 
PTGS2. Host defense-associated genes exhibited a non-uniform transcriptional 
response. Components of the TRIF-dependent antiviral axis, including TLR3, 
TICAM1, TBK1, IRF3, and CXCL10, were downregulated, whereas TLR1, TLR10, TICAM2, 
and BTK were upregulated, and several other immune-response genes showed no 
significant change. These findings indicate differential modulation of 
TLR-associated transcription rather than uniform suppression of all examined 
immune-related genes.
CONCLUSIONS: L. brevis CFS attenuated the expression of multiple 
inflammation-associated genes and differentially modulated host 
defense-associated genes in DSS-stimulated HT-29 cells. This non-uniform 
transcriptional pattern indicates selective modulation of the TLR-associated 
gene network rather than indiscriminate suppression of all examined 
immune-related genes.

This study investigated the therapeutic effects of acupuncture on post-stroke

(1)PG and Research Department of Zoology, Kongunadu Arts and Science College

(2)DHR- Multi-Disciplinary Research Unit (MRU), Government Mohan Kumaramangalam

In traditional medicine, natural plant-based treatments have played a key role 
in preventing and addressing different ailments. They are also considered an 
important source of bioactive compounds with potential pharmacological 
applications. The leaves of the widely known medicinal plant Piper betle are 
widely utilized in traditional medicine due to their biological qualities. The 
bioactive compounds found in the essential oil extracted from Piper betle leaves 
are especially abundant and are thought to have a major role in the plant's 
medicinal potential. In the current study, the antioxidant and anticancer 
properties of essential oil extracted from Piper betle leaves were objectively 
evaluated using in vitro experimental methods. To thoroughly investigate the 
essential oil's capacity to reduce oxidative stress, its antioxidant activity 
was evaluated using a variety of free radical scavenging assays, such as the 
DPPH, Hydrogen Peroxide, Superoxide Dismutase, and ABTS assays. The anticancer 
activity was investigated against human oral carcinoma (KB) cell lines by 
assessing cytotoxicity and membrane damage. The MTT assay was performed to 
assess cell viability at doses between 6.25 and 100 µg/mL, with an IC50 value 
determined to be 22.8 µg/mL, the essential oil demonstrated considerable 
antiproliferative activity and significant, concentration-dependent cytotoxicity 
against KB cells. In addition, the essential oil demonstrated pronounced 
antioxidant activity across all tested assays. The presence of many bioactive 
components with functional groups known to be important in scavenging free 
radicals and inhibiting cancer cells may be responsible for the reported 
biological activity. Overall, these findings highlight the potential of Piper 
betle leaf essential oil as a dual-action agent with notable anticancer and 
antioxidant capabilities.

Mercury dynamics in surface-active soil invertebrates from an ecological reserve 
in the Brazilian savanna.

Fernandes IO(1), Monteiro LC(2), de Miranda VL(3), de Souza JPR(4), Rodrigues 
YOS(5), de Castro Paes É(6), Júnior WFA(7), Bernardi JVE(5).

Author information:
(1)Graduate Program in Environmental Sciences, Faculty UnB Planaltina, 
University of Brasília, Brasília, Distrito Federal, 73345-010, Brazil. 
iara158@gmail.com.
(2)Graduate Program in Ecology, Institute of Biological Sciences, University of

(3)Graduate Program in Zoology, Institute of Biological Sciences, University of

(4)Graduate Program in Chemistry, Institute of Chemistry University of Brasília,

(5)Graduate Program in Environmental Sciences, Faculty UnB Planaltina,

(6)Graduate Program in Soils and Plant Nutrition, Federal University of Viçosa,

(7)Behavioral Ecology Laboratory (LABECO), Natural Resources Study Center

This study evaluated total mercury (THg) distribution and accumulation in soil, 
litter, and surface-active soil invertebrates at the Águas Emendadas Ecological 
Station (ESECAE), a savanna reserve in central Brazil. We assessed whether THg 
differed between soil and litter; whether soil pH and organic matter influenced 
soil THg, the degree of THg accumulation in invertebrates relative to soil and 
litter; whether feeding habits structured epigeic soil fauna according to THg 
concentrations; and whether biomagnification could be inferred within the local 
trophic network. THg concentrations were significantly higher in litter 
(51.7 ± 5.6 ng g⁻1) than in soil (34.9 ± 13.5 ng g⁻1; t = 4.402, df = 7, 
p = 0.0032). Soil organic matter was positively associated with soil THg 
(R2 = 0.455, p = 0.039), whereas pH showed no significant relationship. 
Invertebrate THg concentrations ranged from 0.095 to 970.70 ng g⁻1, reaching 
values approximately 15 times higher than those in soil or litter. Overall, 
83.75% of samples showed bioaccumulation potential, and macroaccumulation 
predominated relative to both soil (80.38%) and litter (68.53%). Grouping by 
feeding habits revealed consistent accumulation patterns, indicating 
trophic-level biomagnification. Predator frequency increased from 9.1% in the 
lowest THg group to 45.5% in the highest, while phytophagous organisms decreased 
from 26.1% to 2.3%. Our results underscore the complexity of mercury cycling in 
terrestrial food webs and highlight the role of ecological traits and 
environmental parameters in modulating mercury bioavailability and transfer.

Comparative perioperative and oncological outcomes of the da Vinci Xi versus Si 
robotic surgical systems in rectal cancer surgery: a systematic review and 
meta-analysis.

Magalhães IMG(1), de Oliveira Paixão FA(1), Tamura G(2), Averbach P(3)(4).

Author information:
(1)Faculdade de Medicina, Universidade Federal de Juiz de Fora, Avenida 
Presidente Itamar Franco, Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais, Brazil.
(2)Hospital Governador Celso Ramos, Florianópolis, Santa Catarina, Brazil.
(3)Hospital Sírio-Libanês, São Paulo, Brazil. pedro.averbach@gmail.com.
(4)Discipline of Surgical Technique and Experimental Surgery, Faculdade de

pedro.averbach@gmail.com.

The da Vinci Xi replaced the Si with a boom-mounted architecture intended to 
remove the re-docking and multiquadrant limits on pelvic access. Whether it 
changes outcomes in rectal cancer surgery is unresolved: existing syntheses 
pooled rectal with colonic resection. Five databases, Google Scholar and 
citation graphs were searched to August 2026, without language or design 
restriction, for comparative studies reporting outcomes separately by platform 
in rectal cancer resection. Screening, extraction and risk-of-bias assessment 
were done in duplicate. Random-effects models with a Hartung-Knapp adjustment 
were used; certainty was rated with GRADE. Eight non-randomised cohorts (843 
patients; 380 Xi, 463 Si) were included. Pooling all five cohorts reporting 
operative time, the mean difference was - 27.7 min (95% confidence 
interval - 80.4 to + 25.0; I² 95%); restricted to the four reporting means with 
standard deviations, thus conditional on excluding the largest cohort, it was 
- 50.6 min (- 69.4 to - 31.7). Docking time was shorter with the Xi in all three 
reporting cohorts, which defined it differently or not at all. The evidence is 
very uncertain about the effect of platform on anastomotic leak (risk ratio 
0.53, 0.24 to 1.14), complications, conversion, reoperation, margin involvement 
and specimen quality; certainty was very low throughout. The evidence is very 
uncertain about the effect of the da Vinci Xi compared with the Si on 
perioperative and oncological outcomes in rectal cancer, and functional outcomes 
have not been compared. Because the platforms were compared across periods, 
centres and levels of experience, no estimate isolates the platform.PROSPERO 
registration CRD420261480007, registered 18 August 2026, before data extraction.

Circadian regulation of the S1PR1-P2X7 signalling axis in obesity-associated 
metabolic inflammation: molecular crosstalk and therapeutic perspectives.

Patel A(1), Jain P(2), Sahu H(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Pharmacy, Rungta College of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Research, 
Rungta International Skills University, Bhilai, Chhattisgarh, India, 490024.
(2)School of Pharmacy, Rungta College of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Research, 
Rungta International Skills University, Bhilai, Chhattisgarh, India, 490024. 
paragjain1510@gmail.com.

Obesity is a chronic, low-grade inflammatory condition expressed by inflammation 
and immune damage that mediates component(s) of insulin resistance and 
cardiometabolic syndrome in the presence of disruption of circadian rhythms. 
Primary research data indicate that the interplay between biological timing and 
immunological signalling occurs in a synchronised manner to govern metabolic 
homeostasis, thereby leading us to coin the term Circadian regulation of 
metabolic inflammation. These signalling pathways directly affect immune cell 
trafficking and endothelial integrity in sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 
(S1PR1) or purinergic P2X7 receptor (P2X7)-mediated regulation, and inflammasome 
activation. This review highlights a new molecular link establishing the 
S1PR1-P2X7 axis between circadian rhythm and obesity-linked immunometabolic 
disorders. We discuss the interplay of lipid and purinergic signalling, focusing 
on their convergence at nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), phosphoinositide 
3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt), signal transducer and activator of 
transcription 3 (STAT3), reactive oxygen species (ROS), and NOD-, LRR-, and 
pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) activation pathways that act in 
concert to exacerbate both fatty tissue inflammation and systemic insulin 
metabolic resistance. Altogether, we summarise the latest advances in 
receptor-based pharmacotherapy, chronotherapy, and nanomedicine-guided drug 
delivery aimed at restoring circadian homeostasis and metabolic balance. 
Understanding the circadian regulation of the S1PR1-P2X7 axis may inform new 
precision treatment strategies for obesity-linked metabolic diseases.

Updated cancer risks in lynch syndrome.

Drogan CM(1), Kupfer SS(2).

Author information:
(1)Center for Clinical Genetics and Genomics, University of Chicago, IL, 
Chicago, United States of America.
(2)Department of Medicine, Section of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and 
Nutrition, University of Chicago, Chicago, IL, USA. skupfer@bsd.uchicago.edu.

Lynch syndrome, one of the most common hereditary cancer predisposition 
syndromes, is caused by pathogenic variants in the mismatch repair genes (MLH1, 
MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) and the EPCAM gene. Individuals who inherit pathogenic 
variants in Lynch-associated genes experience increased lifetime risk of 
colorectal, endometrial, and several other cancer types. Risks of 
Lynch-associated cancers vary by the affected gene and within each gene, 
especially for lower penetrance genes. This poses challenges for clinicians to 
provide patients and families with accurate cancer risk estimates and determine 
individualized surveillance protocols. Compounding this challenge is that study 
designs and potential biases could yield different risk estimates. In this 
review, we present up-to-date Lynch syndrome cancer risk estimates and discuss 
how study design could impact these risk estimates.

METTL14-mediated FDX1 m6A methylation inhibited the proliferation of clear cell 
renal cell carcinoma.

Bai Z(#)(1), Wang C(#)(2), Shen J(#)(2), Yang Y(3), Liu Q(4), Shang Z(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Urology, Tianjin First Central Hospital, Tianjin Medical 
University, Tianjin, China.
(2)Tianjin Institute of Urology, The Second Hospital of Tianjin Medical 
University, Tianjin Medical University, Tianjin, China.
(3)Shunde Hospital of Southern Medical University, Guangdong, China.
(4)Department of Urology, Tianjin First Central Hospital, Tianjin Medical 
University, Tianjin, China. Simonlq@163.com.
(5)Tianjin Institute of Urology, The Second Hospital of Tianjin Medical 
University, Tianjin Medical University, Tianjin, China. Zhiqun_shang@tmu.edu.cn.
(#)Contributed equally

FDX1 exerts a significant influence in the process of cuproptosis by 
facilitating the lipoacylation of proteins and reducing copper ions to 
monovalent copper ions. The methyltransferase METTL14 is an enzyme that 
modulates the m6A methylation of RNA, which can impact the stability, 
translation efficiency, and degradation rate of RNA. Nevertheless, the 
regulatory association between METTL14 and FDX1 in kidney cancer requires 
further investigation. The differential expression of METTL14 and FDX1 between 
normal tissues and renal cancer tissues was analyzed via the GEO public 
database. The association between these factors and patient survival was 
analyzed by utilizing the TCGA public database. A correlation analysis between 
METTL14 and FDX1 was performed based on the TCGA database. The findings were 
validated through RT - qPCR, Western blot, and immunohistochemistry assays. By 
using SRAMP tools and m6A correlation experiments, the study elucidated the 
reason for the decreased expression of FDX1 in renal cancer cells. In vivo and 
in vitro experiments were conducted to verify the regulatory effect of METTL14 
on FDX1. In clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), METTL14 and FDX1 exhibit 
downregulation and are correlated with a poor prognosis among ccRCC patients. 
METTL14 augments the expression of FDX1 by enhancing the stability of the FDX1 
messenger RNA. METTL14 upregulates FDX1 expression and consequently enhances 
cuproptosis in ccRCC cells. Methyltransferase METTL14 preserves the stability of 
FDX1 messenger RNA via m6A modification of FDX1 messenger RNA and acts as a

PURPOSE: Early identification of surgical necrotizing enterocolitis (S-NEC) 
before clinical deterioration remains challenging in extremely low-birth-weight 
infants (ELBWIs). We evaluated whether coagulation and fibrinolysis markers at 
birth could predict subsequent S-NEC.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 250 ELBWIs (< 1000 g) treated from 2013 to 
2022; 22 developed S-NEC. Eleven coagulation and fibrinolysis markers were 
measured within 24 h of birth. Multivariable logistic regression models and a 
simple birth-time risk score were developed.
RESULTS: Relative to controls, S-NEC infants had higher D-dimer (11.7 vs. 
5.5 µg/mL, p = 0.003) and PT-INR (1.71 vs. 1.42, p = 0.023), prolonged PT (62.2 
vs. 52.7 s, p = 0.022), and lower fibrinogen (107.3 vs. 160.7 mg/dL, p = 0.037).

0.710, 0.763). A four-item risk score (D-dimer > 5 µg/mL, PT-INR > 1.5, 
fibrinogen < 100 mg/dL, and birth weight < 700 g) achieved an AUC of 0.702, with 
85.0% sensitivity and 96.3% negative predictive value (NPV). S-NEC incidence 
increased across risk categories (3.7%, 14.5%, and 19.6%; p for trend = 0.013).
CONCLUSIONS: Hemostatic abnormalities at birth were associated with subsequent 
S-NEC in ELBWIs, suggesting perinatal or intrauterine origins. The risk score 
showed a high NPV and may serve as a practical rule-out tool for early neonatal 
intensive care unit stratification.

Benchmarking wall models for confined active Brownian particles near planar and 
channel walls.

Escalante-Velázquez CA(1).

Author information:
(1)SECIHTI-Centro de Ingeniería y desarrollo industrial, 76125, Querétaro, 
México. carlos.escalante@cidesi.edu.mx.

Different microscopic wall models are frequently used in simulations of confined 
active Brownian particles (ABPs), but their practical equivalence for standard 
steady-state observables is rarely assessed against an analytical benchmark with 
explicit and reproducible criteria. In this work, we present a reproducible 
benchmark for three common wall models in confined ABPs simulations-stochastic 
hard, specular hard, and exponential soft-using the analytical hard-wall theory 
of Duzgun and Selinger as reference. After validating the soft wall against the 
Boltzmann limit at Pe = 0 , we compare density and polarization profiles across 
Pe ∈ {1, …, 10} using local and integrated error metrics. The stochastic wall 
consistently matches the analytical reference best, the specular rule fails 
sharply in polarization, and the exponential wall's fidelity depends strongly on 
both activity and observable; reducing its range improves local but not 
integrated agreement. A compact two-wall channel test confirms this ranking 
survives finite confinement. The results provide an explicit, 
observable-dependent criterion for selecting wall models in ABP simulations.

severe lower urinary tract dysfunction, but recurrent urinary tract infection, 
urolithiasis and mucus-related complications remain incompletely understood.

bladder augmentation and assessed transferable insights from adult bowel-derived

Targeting pyroptosis in intestinal and systemic inflammatory diseases: 
mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.

Li J(1), Chen Y(1)(2), Yu Q(1), Fu X(1), Sun J(1), Zhu L(3).

Author information:
(1)Division of Gastroenterology, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, 
Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, 430022, China.
(2)Department of Endoscopy and Digestive System, Guizhou Provincial People's 
Hospital, Guiyang, 550000, China.
(3)Division of Gastroenterology, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, 
Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, 430022, China. 
zhuliangru@hust.edu.cn.

Pyroptosis is a lytic form of programmed cell death driven by gasdermin cleavage 
and subsequent plasma membrane pore formation, which triggers cell swelling, 
lysis, and the release of inflammatory cytokines that amplify tissue injury. 
Once viewed as an innate antimicrobial defense mechanism, pyroptosis is now 
recognized as a central pathogenic pathway in both acute and chronic 
inflammatory diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Its execution 
proceeds through a cascade of druggable events-inflammasome assembly, caspase 
activation, and gasdermin pore formation-and it operates within an 
interconnected cell death network, engaging apoptosis, necroptosis, and 
ferroptosis under the emerging PANoptosis framework. In the intestine, this 
network displays striking cell type- and context-dependent duality: 
gasdermin-mediated death can disrupt the epithelial barrier and exacerbate 
mucosal inflammation, yet the same effectors support barrier integrity, 
epithelial repair, and controlled cytokine release. This duality may explain why 
pyroptosis inhibition, although robustly protective in preclinical colitis 
models, has so far shown limited clinical efficacy. In this review, we summarize 
the molecular mechanisms of pyroptotic signaling, its crosstalk with other death 
pathways, and its roles in intestinal and systemic inflammatory diseases. We 
then critically evaluate the therapeutic landscape, covering NLRP3 inflammasome 
inhibitors, regulators of gasdermin post-translational modifications, natural 
compounds, and nanotechnology-based delivery systems, with emphasis on 
multi-indication clinical progress and the lessons from recent trial failures. 
Finally, we highlight priorities for translation-human disease models, 
tissue-restricted delivery, and biomarker-guided patient stratification-that may 
convert mechanistic insight into clinical benefit for patients with IBD and 
related inflammatory disorders.

Wang H(1), Wang X(1), Ai Q(1), Pei D(2).

Author information:

Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) comprise a spectrum of cognitive 
disturbances after anesthesia and surgery, affecting learning, memory, and 
executive function. Although systemic inflammation, surgical trauma, anesthetic 
exposure, and patient vulnerability have been implicated in PND, the mechanisms 
linking perioperative stress to persistent cognitive changes remain incompletely 
understood. Microglia, as resident immune cells of the central nervous system, 
are important regulators of neuroimmune interactions and may contribute to PND 
through alterations in inflammatory signaling, synaptic regulation, vascular 
function, metabolism, and epigenetic programs. In this Overview, we summarize 
current evidence regarding microglial involvement in PND across five 
interconnected domains: neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, 
microglia-neuron communication, mitochondrial and metabolic regulation, and 
epigenetic remodeling. We further discuss emerging single-cell transcriptomic 
and multi-omic studies indicating that microglial responses are heterogeneous, 
dynamic, and context dependent rather than adequately described by the 
traditional M1/M2 framework. We propose that PND involves complex interactions 
among peripheral immune activation, neurovascular dysfunction, microglial state 
transitions, and neuronal vulnerability. Finally, we highlight current 
challenges in translating microglial mechanisms into clinical applications and 
discuss future directions for identifying biomarkers and developing 
context-specific perioperative neuroprotective strategies.

Therapeutic potential of varenicline in neuropsychiatric disorders: insights

Talebi Taheri A(1)(2), Aschner M(3), Rahmati-Dehkordi F(4), Tamtaji OR(5).

Author information:

Neuropsychiatric disorders pose significant health challenges. Current drug 
therapies are often inadequate, highlighting the urgent need for new and 
effective treatments. The α4β2 nicotinic receptor has been implicated in the 
pathophysiology of various neuropsychiatric disorders. In this context, 
varenicline, its selective agonist, has garnered increasing attention for its 
potential therapeutic effects across a range of neuropsychiatric conditions. 
Emerging preclinical evidence suggests that varenicline may exert 
neuroprotective effects through modulation of pathways that include synaptic 
plasticity and synaptic proteins, neuroinflammation, microglial activation, 
apoptosis, and autophagy. However, direct target engagement for many of these 
pathways has not yet been established. In this review, we provide a 
comprehensive review of the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which 
varenicline might be expected to exert therapeutic effects in a range of 
neuropsychiatric disorders. Most previous reviews of varenicline have 
concentrated on its use as a smoking cessation aid or on its potential to treat 
individual diseases. The current review takes a different approach, focusing at 
the molecular level on the various pathways that are affected in different 
diseases, and discussing within each section the evidence that currently exists 
in relation to each of these in studies conducted in rodent models and in 
clinical trials. The review seeks to provide insight into the potential benefits 
and drawbacks of using a single compound to treat a variety of disorders, and to 
highlight areas for future research.

Evolutionary Entropy Shapes Lifespan of the Greenland Shark.

Buescu J(1)(2), Elaydi SN(3)(4), Oliveira HM(5)(6).

Author information:
(1)Departamento de Ciências Matemáticas, Faculdade de Ciências, Universidade de 
Lisboa, Lisbon, Portugal.
(2)Centro de Estudos Matemáticos de Ciências - ULisboa (CEMS.UL), Lisbon, 
Portugal.
(3)Department of Mathematics, Trinity University, San Antonio, Texas, USA.
(4)Fellow of the Center for Mathematical Analysis, Geometry and Dynamical 
Systems (CAMGSD), University of Lisbon, Lisbon, Portugal.
(5)Departamento de Matemática, Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de 
Lisboa, Lisbon, Portugal. henrique.m.oliveira@tecnico.ulisboa.pt.
(6)Centro de Análise Matemática, Geometria e Sistemas Dinâmicos (CAMGSD), 
Universidade de Lisboa, Lisbon, Portugal. 
henrique.m.oliveira@tecnico.ulisboa.pt.

The Greenland shark (Somniosus microcephalus) is among the longest-lived 
vertebrates known, with female maturity estimated at about 156 years and maximum 
ages approaching four centuries. We use the entropic theory of life histories 
and an open-group Leslie model to determine which reproductive windows are 
compatible with this extreme demographic profile. The model yields generation 
times, reproductive quantiles and entropy-maximizing reproductive endpoints. A 
critical value of reproductive persistence, qc ≈ 0.9763 , separates two regimes: 
below it, evolutionary entropy increases towards an asymptote; above it, entropy 
is maximized at a finite reproductive endpoint. Longevity-calibrated scenarios 
lie on both sides of this threshold and imply generation times near or above two 
centuries, with reproductive contributions extending into the third, fourth and 
fifth centuries of life. As an independent benchmark, an empirically 
parametrized Leslie model for the bowhead whale yields comparable entropy-based 
demographic quantities while allowing the reproductive and survivorship 
parameters to be calculated directly. The method provides quantitative 
constraints on reproductive organisation in exceptionally long-lived species for 
which detailed demographic data are unavailable.

PRKAR2A/RIIα as a candidate spatial cAMP-PKA signal router in triple-negative 
breast cancer metastasis: evidence boundaries, competing models and decisive 
experiments.

Muzaffar T(1), Saha B(2).

Author information:
(1)School of Biosciences, Engineering and Technology, VIT Bhopal University, 
Kothrikalan, Sehore, Madhya Pradesh, 466114, India.
(2)School of Biosciences, Engineering and Technology, VIT Bhopal University, 
Kothrikalan, Sehore, Madhya Pradesh, 466114, India. 
biswajitsaha@vitbhopal.ac.in.

Metastatic relapse remains the principal lethal event in triple-negative breast 
cancer (TNBC), yet the contribution of PRKAR2A, which encodes the type IIα 
regulatory subunit (RIIα) of protein kinase A (PKA), remains unresolved. RIIα 
creates a mechanistic duality: it restrains catalytic PKA within the holoenzyme 
while recruiting type II PKA to A-kinase anchoring protein (AKAP) microdomains. 
A targeted critical narrative search identified no eligible published study in 
the searched sources that causally linked PRKAR2A to a TNBC metastasis endpoint. 
Direct evidence is limited to four association or detection contexts: PRKAR2A 
mRNA differed at the adjusted-significance boundary between pathological 
complete response and residual disease but was not retained in the final 
consensus predictor; its transcript was induced in a lipid-adapted TNBC 
heterospheroid state without gene-specific perturbation; RIIα was detected in 
mitochondria-endoplasmic-reticulum contact fractions whose local PKA activity 
controlled calcium transfer and apoptosis without isolating RIIα; and PRKAR2A 
entered a multigene prognostic signature without independent or cell-resolved 
validation. AKAP2 depletion altered focal-adhesion signalling, invasion, 
primary-tumour growth and lung signal, but neither the operative PKA regulatory 
subunit nor a burden-independent metastatic effect was established. These 
boundaries support four competing interpretations: PRKAR2A may be a driver, 
compensatory brake, localisation determinant or passenger state marker. Decisive 
tests require inducible depletion, near-endogenous domain-resolved rescue, 
compartment-targeted PKA reporters, endogenous complex mapping and 
stage-resolved metastasis assays. Until then, RIIα is best treated as a 
candidate spatial signal router rather than a validated biomarker or therapeutic 
target.

Diet and physical activity in multiple sclerosis: associations with quality of 
life and disability by disease duration.

Nag N(1), Yu M(2), Román CAF(3)(4), Vaglio-Garro A(5)(6), Schmidt H(7).

Author information:
(1)Neuroepidemiology Unit, Centre of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, Melbourne 
School of Population and Global Health, The University of Melbourne, Melbourne, 
VIC, Australia. nnag@unimelb.edu.au.
(2)Neuroepidemiology Unit, Centre of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, Melbourne 
School of Population and Global Health, The University of Melbourne, Melbourne, 
VIC, Australia.
(3)Keck School of Medicine, University of Southern California, Los Angeles, CA, 
USA.
(4)Kessler Foundation, West Orange, NJ, USA.
(5)Ludwig Boltzmann Institute for Traumatology, The Research Center in 
Cooperation with AUVA, Vienna, Austria.
(6)Austrian Cluster for Tissue Regeneration, Vienna, Austria.
(7)Accelerated Cure Project for Multiple Sclerosis, Waltham, MA, USA.

BACKGROUND: Healthy lifestyle factors are associated with higher quality of life 
(QoL) and reduced disability in people with multiple sclerosis (pwMS). Whether 
these associations differ according to MS duration is unclear. We examined 
associations between diet, supplement use, wellness activities, and physical 
activity with QoL and ambulatory disability, and whether these associations 
differed between pwMS diagnosed within ≤ 5 years versus > 5 years.
METHODS: Cross-sectional self-reported survey data from 1,083 pwMS were 
analysed. Diet, supplement use, and wellness activities were queried via 
tick-box options and recategorised. Physical activity was assessed using the 
Godin-Shephard Leisure-Time Physical Activity Questionnaire. QoL was measured 
using Neuro-QoL, and ambulatory disability using the Patient Determined Disease 
Steps. Multivariable linear and moderation analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: Associations differed by MS duration: a low-saturated fat diet and 
"other" diets were associated with lower QoL in the > 5-years group, whereas 
omega-3 supplement use was associated with higher physical QoL in the ≤ 5-years 
group. Physical activity was associated with higher QoL in both groups, with 
mostly stronger associations within ≤ 5-years. Very active physical activity was 
associated with lower ambulatory disability across both groups. Mind-based 
wellness activities were associated with lower QoL in the > 5-years group, with 
no group differences. Vitamin D supplement use was not associated with outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Physical activity is associated with higher QoL and lower 
disability irrespective of MS duration and should be integrated across the 
disease course. MS duration may modify associations between other lifestyle 
factors and QoL, supporting consideration of disease stage when tailoring 
lifestyle recommendations.

Rahman I(1), Khan BM(2)(3), Hossen I(4)(5), Rahman Z(6).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Environmental Radioactivity, Fukushima University, 1 Kanayagawa, 
Fukushima-shi, Fukushima, 960-1296, Japan. immrahman@ipc.fukushima-u.ac.jp.
(2)Institute of Environmental Radioactivity, Fukushima University, 1 Kanayagawa, 
Fukushima-shi, Fukushima, 960-1296, Japan.
(3)Faculty of Science, Institute of Forestry and Environmental Sciences, 
University of Chittagong, Chattogram, 4331, Bangladesh.
(4)Graduate School of Symbiotic Systems Science and Technology, Fukushima 
University, 1 Kanayagawa, Fukushima-shi, Fukushima, 960-1296, Japan.
(5)Department of Chemistry, Faculty of Science, University of Chittagong,

(6)Forest Biomass Chemical Innovation Unit, Fukushima Institute for Research,

Radiocesium (r-Cs: 137Cs) from the Fukushima Daiichi accident and earlier 
nuclear fallout remains a long-term contaminant in agricultural soils. It poses 
an ongoing threat to global food safety because crops readily absorb it as a 
potassium analog. This review synthesizes a decade of mechanistic, agronomic, 
and ecological advances in suppressing r-Cs uptake and root-to-shoot 
translocation. First, the impact of soil mineralogy, particularly clay fixation, 
on initial r-Cs bioavailability is examined. At the molecular level, r-Cs influx 
is governed by a shared calcium-signaling hub linked to potassium status. 
Consequently, optimizing potassium fertilization can transcriptionally silence 
the principal uptake genes. Furthermore, controlling xylem loading and managing 
internal sodium interactions directly restrict r-Cs translocation, protecting 
edible plant parts. Supplementary countermeasures, including plant-microbe 
symbioses, porous soil amendments, and targeted genetic exclusions, are also 
evaluated. To ensure long-term agricultural resilience, multi-site field trials 
and the molecular dissection of translocation pathways must be prioritized in 
future research. Ultimately, sustainable crop production requires integrating 
biological and agronomic strategies rather than relying solely on intensive 
potassium fertilization.

The precise quantification of amylases activities in complex environments is 
crucial in actual manufacturing. We synthesized a self-cascading nanozyme

amylases during food manufacturing with advanced self-cascading and 
self-activating nanozymes.

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review critically evaluates evidence on sleep spindles 
(SP), slow oscillations (SOs), and their coordination in mild-to-moderate 
Alzheimer's disease (AD), focusing on their relationships with cognition, AD 
biomarkers, and their therapeutic potential.
RECENT FINDINGS: Longitudinal studies associate greater SP and/or SO activity 
with better cognition and favourable amyloid and tau profiles after clinical 
onset. Spindle and SO coupling may index network integrity. Preserved NREM sleep 
oscillations are associated with lower orexin concentrations and weaker adverse 
relationships between orexin and cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes.

coupling, although cognitive and biomarker benefits remain uncertain. Spindle-SO 
activity, including their temporal coupling, are associated with cognition and 
AD biomarkers across the disease continuum. Closed-loop acoustic and electrical 
stimulation can modify these oscillations, but biomarker-characterized trials in 
MCI and AD are needed to determine whether treatment produces durable cognitive 
and biomarker benefits.

Volumetric stone size assessment did not demonstrate improved prediction of 
treatment success compared with cumulative stone diameter.

Padovani PZ(1), Palasi S(1), Thoman M(1), Neff D(1), Duchene D(1), Sardiu ME(2), 
Molina WR(1), Whiles BB(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Urology, The University of Kansas Health System, 3901 Rainbow 
Blvd Mailstop #3016, Kansas City, KS, 66160, USA.
(2)Department of Biostatistics, University of Kansas Medical Center, Kansas

(3)Department of Urology, The University of Kansas Health System, 3901 Rainbow

PURPOSE: To evaluate whether volumetric assessment of stone burden improves 
prediction of treatment success compared with cumulative stone diameter (CSD) 
and whether performance varies by surgical modality or stone size.
METHODS: We analyzed a prospectively maintained cohort undergoing PCNL or 
ureteroscopy (URS) from October 2020 to September 2024. Stone burden was 
assessed by CSD, ellipsoid volume, and software-derived three-dimensional 
volume. Treatment success was defined as no residual fragment ≥ 2 mm on 
postoperative CT. ROC analyses and three parallel multivariable logistic 
regression models, each containing one stone-burden metric plus stone 
multiplicity, HU, and surgical modality, were performed. Calibration was 
assessed using 500 bootstrap resamples, and modality interactions were tested.
RESULTS: Among 150 patients (81 PCNL, 69 URS), 91 (61%) achieved treatment 
success. Univariable AUCs were 0.632 (95% CI 0.540-0.724) for CSD, 0.602 
(0.511-0.693) for ellipsoid volume, and 0.595 (0.504-0.687) for software-derived 
volume. Adjusted-model AUCs were 0.703 (0.615-0.791), 0.690 (0.602-0.779), and 
0.687 (0.599-0.776), respectively, with no significant pairwise differences. 
Stone multiplicity was associated with lower odds of success in both 
volume-based models. No metric-by-modality interaction was significant. 
Exploratory PCNL analyses by a 2-cm CSD threshold had wide confidence intervals.
CONCLUSIONS: Volumetric assessment did not demonstrate improved prediction of 
treatment success compared with CSD. The three metrics showed similar, modest 
discrimination in parallel adjusted models. Stone multiplicity may capture 
clinically relevant complexity not represented by stone size alone.

Ciliated hepatic foregut cyst in children and adolescents: a systematic review 
of clinical presentation, diagnosis, management, and outcomes.

Kumar B(1), Ahmad MF(2), Jain V(1), Goel P(1), Yadav DK(1), Agarwala S(1), Dhua 
AK(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pediatric Surgery, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New 
Delhi, India.
(2)Department of Pediatric Surgery, Central Armed Police Forces Institute of 
Medical Sciences, New Delhi, India.
(3)Department of Pediatric Surgery, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New 
Delhi, India. dhuaanjan@gmail.com.

Ciliated hepatic foregut cyst (CHFC) is a rare congenital cystic liver lesion 
described predominantly in adults, in whom malignant transformation to squamous 
cell carcinoma has been reported. Pediatric experience is scattered across case 
reports and small series, and no systematic synthesis has been published. We 
conducted a systematic review per PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Scopus, and Embase 
(Elsevier) were searched on 3 August 2026 without language or date restrictions, 
supplemented by citation searching and grey-literature screening (JMIR 
Preprints, bioRxiv, medRxiv). We included case reports and case series of 
patients aged ≤ 19 years with histopathologically confirmed CHFC. Screening 
(Rayyan) and extraction were performed in independent duplicate. Risk of bias 
was assessed with the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklists. 
Findings were synthesised descriptively per SWiM; no meta-analysis was 
performed. Sixteen studies contributed 23 unique pediatric patients 
(female-to-male ratio 1.3:1; median age 4.0 years, range 5 months-19 years). 
Antenatal detection occurred in 5 (21.7%) of 23. Symptomatic presentation was 
reported in 14 (60.9%) of 23. Median cyst size was 6.0 cm (range 0.6-19.3), and 
4 patients (17.4%) had giant cysts (≥ 10 cm). Segment IV was involved in 11 of 
19 patients with location reported (57.9%). Biliary communication was documented 
in 5 of 14 evaluable cases (35.7%; 5/23 overall); 4 of these patients underwent 
Roux-en-Y biliary reconstruction. Squamous metaplasia was reported in 4 of 7 
evaluable cases (57.1%; 4/23 overall). No dysplasia (0/7 evaluable) and no 
malignant transformation (0/22 evaluable) were reported. Postoperative 
complications occurred in 2 (8.7%) of 23. No recurrence (0/11 evaluable) or 
mortality (0/23) was reported over a median 19-month follow-up (reported for 8 
patients). Pediatric CHFC appears to present more often with symptomatic, larger 
and biliary-communicating lesions than the classical adult phenotype. Complete 
excision was associated with favorable reported short-term outcomes, but the 
evidence is of very low certainty, and limited follow-up and substantial 
non-reporting preclude conclusions about long-term recurrence or malignant 
transformation.

Bidirectional Regulatory Mechanisms of T cell-microglia Interactions in Cerebral 
Ischemic Disease: Molecular Crosstalk, Experimental Techniques and Therapeutic 
Implications.

Zheng Y(#)(1), Cheng J(#)(1), Li F(#)(2), Ren Z(1), Chen C(3), Zhang Z(1), Lan 
X(1), Zhang C(1), Zhao Y(1), Han J(1), Li J(1), Cheng F(1), Wang Q(4), Li C(5), 
Wang X(6).

Author information:
(1)School of Traditional Chinese Medicine Department, Beijing University of 
Chinese Medicine, 11 Beisanhuandong Road, Chao yang District, Beijing, 100029, 
China.
(2)Dongzhimen Hospital of Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, Beijing, 
100050, China.
(3)Beijing Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine Affiliated to Capital 
Medical University, Beijing, 100010, China.
(4)School of Traditional Chinese Medicine Department, Beijing University of 
Chinese Medicine, 11 Beisanhuandong Road, Chao yang District, Beijing, 100029, 
China. wangqg8558@sina.com.
(5)School of Traditional Chinese Medicine Department, Beijing University of 
Chinese Medicine, 11 Beisanhuandong Road, Chao yang District, Beijing, 100029, 
China. changxiang1202@163.com.
(6)School of Traditional Chinese Medicine Department, Beijing University of 
Chinese Medicine, 11 Beisanhuandong Road, Chao yang District, Beijing, 100029, 
China. wxqbucm@126.com.
(#)Contributed equally

Cerebral ischemic diseases, such as ischemic stroke (IS) and vascular dementia 
(VaD), are major causes of neurological disability and mortality. 
Neuroinflammation acts as a pivotal driver of secondary brain injury, mediated 
by intricate bidirectional interactions between peripheral T cells and central 
nervous system (CNS)-resident microglia. This review delineates the molecular 
mechanisms underlying T cell-microglia crosstalk in cerebral ischemia, 
emphasizing their dual roles in exacerbating neurotoxicity and promoting repair. 
Direct interactions involve antigen presentation via MHC-TCR engagement and 
co-stimulatory checkpoints (e.g., CD80/CD86-CD28, PD-L1-PD-1), which regulate T 
cell activation and microglial polarization. Direct signaling through cytokines 
(IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-17, IL-10) further modulates microglial phenotypes: Th1/Th17 
cells drive pro-inflammatory M1 polarization via STAT1/NF-κB pathways, while 
Tregs/Th2 cells induce anti-inflammatory M2 states through STAT6/SMAD signaling. 
Spatial transcriptomics and single-cell omics reveal spatiotemporal dynamics of 
these interactions, identifying STAT1/STAT6 imbalance as a critical determinant 
of neuroinflammatory outcomes. Advanced methodologies, including two-photon 
intravital microscopy and microfluidic blood-brain barrier (BBB) models, enable 
real-time visualization of immune cell trafficking and synaptic communication. 
Therapeutically, targeting immune checkpoints (CTLA-4, PD-1) or cytokine 
pathways (e.g., IL-4 mimetics) shows promise in recalibrating neuroimmune 
responses. However, challenges such as blood-brain barrier impermeability to 
biologics and interspecies immune heterogeneity necessitate innovative delivery 
strategies. This review integrates molecular, cellular, and technological 
insights to propose a framework for precision immunomodulation. By elucidating 
context-dependent signaling nodes and leveraging emerging tools, the study 
underscores the potential of harnessing T cell-microglia crosstalk to mitigate 
neuroinflammation and enhance neural repair, offering transformative avenues for 
stroke and dementia therapy.

Preparation of artificial tears with in-situ gelling properties for the 
management of dry eye disease: efficient droplet administration by a 3D-printed 
device.

Yousaf S(1), Zafar S(1), Bashir MM(1), Rana SJ(2), Mudassir J(1), Hussain A(3), 
Abbas N(3), Al-Ani E(4), Arshad MS(1), Ahmad Z(4).

Author information:
(1)Faculty of Pharmacy, Bahauddin Zakariya University, Multan, Pakistan.
(2)Department of Pharmacy, The Next Institute of Science and Technology, Multan, 
Pakistan.
(3)University College of Pharmacy, University of the Punjab, Lahore, Pakistan.
(4)Division of Pharmacy and Optometry, School of Health Sciences, University of 
Manchester, Manchester, UK.

AIMS: The present study was aimed at developing in-situ gelling artificial tear 
formulations and a three-dimensional (3D) printed administration aid.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In-situ gelling formulations were prepared using gellan 
gum and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC). Administration aid was developed 
by fused deposition modeling approach. Formulations were evaluated for 
physicochemical properties, sterility, in-vitro erythrocyte morphology 
assessment, disintegration, in-silico analysis, ex-vivo ocular surface 
retention, in-vivo ocular irritation and efficacy in dry eye disease model in 
rabbits. 3D printed device was evaluated for volume of dispensed droplets, 
usability, instillation success rate and acceptance by human participants.
RESULTS: Prepared formulations exhibited acceptable physicochemical properties, 
sterility and did not irritate the rabbit eye. In-silico analysis suggested 
interactions between gellan gum, HPMC and ocular proteins (mucin, 
p-glycoprotein, OATP2A1). Formulations showed an ocular retention time of 
~20-24 hours and disintegrated within the same timeframe. A two-fold increase 
was recorded in the Schirmer 1 test score of formulations treated rabbit eye 
than the untreated counterpart. A ~ 21% increase in the droplet volume was 
observed in the presence of administration aid. 3D printed aid facilitated 
instillation of formulations.
CONCLUSIONS: Schirmer 1 test scores increased following treatment with prepared 
formulations as compared to untreated counterparts. An administration aid was 
successfully engineered for dispensing prepared formulations.

Plain Language Summary: Currently used artificial tear preparations for the 
treatment of dry eyes are removed quickly from the eyes through regular tear 
drainage. Recently, in-situ gelling artificial tear formulations (capable of 
converting into a gel after application) are under investigation. Such 
preparations may stay on the surface of eyes for a longer period and work more 
efficiently. In the 1stpart of present work, in-situ gelling formulations were 
prepared using gellan gum and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC). The prepared 
formulations were crystal clear and converted into a gel within 20–30 minutes 
upon contact with a tear-like fluid. The formulations were able to stay in 
contact with the surface of rabbit eyes for almost 20–24 hours and did not cause 
any irritation. Eyes treated with the formulation showed twice the eye-surface 
moisture levels than the untreated eyes. In the 2nd part of this study, an eye 
drop administration aid was developed to help provide a consistent dose of 
prepared eye formulations than administering by hand alone. In the presence of 
administration aid, the droplet volume increased by ~21% with low variability. 
In addition, the administration aid made instillation of formulations easier for 
participants. In conclusion, the prepared artificial tears may serve as good 
candidates for the treatment of dry eye disease. Furthermore, the developed 
administration aid may facilitate administration of eye drops.

PURPOSE: Brain metastases (BM) incidence and characteristics remain poorly 
defined due to registry data being often incomplete, recording only primary

incidence rates and characteristics confirmed by MRI in North Savo, Finland.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, North Savo residents with first MRI 
diagnosis of BM between 1 January 2004 and 31 December 2023 were identified 
through the radiology information system, irrespective of primary cancer

patients aged 70-74 years.
CONCLUSIONS: MRI-confirmed BM incidence increased over 20 years, despite age 
standardization. Incidence was highest among older adults. These findings

The peach aphid (Myzus persicae) is a major agricultural pest that causes 
significant yield losses and transmits numerous plant viruses. We profiled 
BtACO8 expression in Balsas teosinte and found that aphid infestation induced 
its transcripts 12.6-fold at 12 h post-infestation relative to non-infested 
controls. We therefore cloned BtACO8, encoding 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate 
oxidase, and investigated its role in aphid resistance by heterologous

and supported over 50% fewer aphids, with reduced nymph hatching and 
reproductive capacity. Although ethylene content did not differ significantly 
between OE and wild-type plants, AtEIN2, a key component of ethylene signaling, 
was significantly upregulated in OE lines after aphid infestation. These results 
suggest that BtACO8 enhances aphid resistance through physical barriers and 
enhanced ethylene signaling, rather than through increased ethylene production. 
BtACO8 from Balsas teosinte is therefore a promising candidate gene for 
improving aphid resistance in crops.

Age- and sex-specific values of regional bone mineral density from opportunistic 
CT of the lower lumbar spine, pelvis, sacrum, and proximal femur.

Matoušová K(1)(2), Morávek A(2), Kuchař M(3), Ondruschka B(4), Šafka J(5), Henyš 
P(6).

Author information:
(1)Faculty of Health Studies, Technical University of Liberec, Studentská 
1402/2, Liberec, 461 17, Czechia.
(2)Department of Anatomy, Faculty of Medicine in Hradec Králové, Charles 
University, Zborovská 2207, Hradec Králové, 500 03, Czechia.
(3)Department of Anatomy, Faculty of Medicine in Hradec Králové, Charles 
University, Zborovská 2207, Hradec Králové, 500 03, Czechia. 
kucharm@lfhk.cuni.cz.
(4)Institute of Legal Medicine, University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf, 
Butenfeld 34, 22529, Hamburg, Germany.
(5)The Institute for Nanomaterials, Advanced Technologies and Innovation, 
Studentská 1402/2, Liberec, 461 17, Czechia.
(6)Institute of New Technologies and Applied Informatics, Faculty of 
Mechatronics, Informatics and Interdisciplinary Studies, Technical University of

OBJECTIVE: Standard osteoporosis assessment using dual-energy X-ray 
absorptiometry (DXA) provides limited 2D measures (BMD, T-score), potentially 
missing localized bone density differences relevant to fracture risk. 
Opportunistic CT allows comprehensive 3D volumetric bone density analysis. This 
study presents a detailed 3D statistical model of CT-derived apparent volumetric 
bone mineral density (CT-vBMD) covering the L4 and L5 vertebrae, pelvic bones, 
sacrum, and proximal femur and examines spatial distributions and associations 
with age and sex.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis included 330 routine abdominal CT 
scans (ages 20-91; approximately balanced by sex). Bones were segmented with a 
semi-automated workflow, internally calibrated, registered to bone-specific 
population templates, and projected onto corresponding tetrahedral meshes. 
Whole-bone averages were compared across age groups and between sexes. For each 
element, we calculated mean vBMD, variability, correlations with age and sex, 
and cluster-defined low-density and age-sensitive subregions.
RESULTS: The global spatial pattern was similar in females and males. The 
highest CT-vBMD values were localized mainly to cortical load-bearing zones, 
whereas the lowest values were concentrated in trabecular spongiosa. Older age 
was associated with lower whole-bone CT-vBMD in all bones and with stronger 
negative associations in trabecular-rich regions, such as the subchondral 
acetabulum, femoral neck, sacral ala, and vertebral bodies. Cortical-dominant 
load-bearing regions showed weaker negative associations with age.
CONCLUSION: This framework maps anatomically localized associations between age 
and CT-vBMD beyond the regions routinely assessed by DXA. Opportunistic CT 
mapping may complement standard osteoporosis assessment by providing spatial 
information for the pelvis, sacrum, lower lumbar spine, and proximal femur.

Analysis of CCR2 gene variants in patients with sarcoidosis using targeted

Yıldız Gülhan P(1), Eröz R(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chest Diseases, Faculty of Medicine, Duzce University, Konuralp 
Campus, 81010, Duzce, Turkey. pinaryildiz@duzce.edu.tr.
(2)Department of Medical Genetics, Faculty of Medicine, Aksaray University, 
Aksaray, Türkiye.

BACKGROUND: Sarcoidosis is a systemic granulomatous disease of unknown etiology. 
Genetic susceptibility and environmental factors are thought to play a role in 
the development of the disease. In this study, we aimed to investigate CCR2 gene 
variants in patients diagnosed with sarcoidosis using next-generation sequencing 
(NGS).
METHODS: A total of 50 individuals were included in the study, consisting of 31 
patients followed with a diagnosis of sarcoidosis in the Department of Chest 
Diseases at Düzce University Faculty of Medicine and 19 controls who presented 
for reasons other than sarcoidosis. DNA was isolated from peripheral blood 
samples obtained from the participants, and CCR2 (NM_001123396.4) gene variants 
were analyzed using targeted next-generation sequencing.
RESULTS: In the study, NM_001123396.4:c.1044G>A (p.Thr348=) (rs3092960), 
NM_001123396.4:c.156G>T (p.Val52=) (rs3918367), NM_001123396.4:c.190G>A 
(p.Val64Ile) (rs1799864), and NM_001123396.4:c.780T>C (p.Asn260=) (rs1799865) 
variants were detected in the CCR2 gene. The statistical significance mainly 
resulted from the higher frequency of the NM_001123396.4:c.780T>C (p.Asn260=) 
(rs1799865) variant in the sarcoidosis group compared with the control group 
(p<0.05). Although the NM_001123396.4:c.156G>T (p.Val52=) (rs3918367) variant 
was detected only in the patient group, a reliable statistical inference could 
not be made due to the small number of cases.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that CCR2 gene variants may be associated 
with genetic susceptibility in the development of sarcoidosis. Further studies 
including larger patient series are needed to better understand the role of CCR2 
polymorphisms in the etiopathogenesis of sarcoidosis.

Application of machine learning to identify risk factors for bloodstream 
infections caused by different antimicrobial resistance phenotypes in 
chemotherapy patients.

Villani Junior A(1), Freire MP(2)(3), De Padua Covas Lage LA(4), Lazar Neto 
F(5), Oliveira MS(6)(7), Abdala E(8)(6), Nunes FLS(1)(7), Levin ASS(6)(7).

Author information:
(1)School of Arts, Sciences and Humanities, University of Sao Paulo, Sao Paulo, 
Brazil.
(2)Infectious Diseases Service, Cancer Institute, University of São Paulo School 
of Medicine, Sao Paulo, Brazil. maristelapf@uol.com.br.
(3)Department of Infectious Diseases, University of São Paulo School of 
Medicine, Dr Eneas de Carvalho Aguiar Street, 255, Sao Paulo, SP, 05403-900, 
Brazil. maristelapf@uol.com.br.
(4)Department of Hematology, Cancer Institute, University of Sao Paulo School of 
Medicine, Sao Paulo, Brazil.
(5)Department of Oncology, Cancer Institute, University of Sao Paulo School of 
Medicine, Sao Paulo, Brazil.
(6)Department of Infectious Diseases, University of São Paulo School of 
Medicine, Dr Eneas de Carvalho Aguiar Street, 255, Sao Paulo, SP, 05403-900, 
Brazil.
(7)CAMO-Net - Centre for Antimicrobial Optimisation Network, London, UK.
(8)Infectious Diseases Service, Cancer Institute, University of São Paulo School 
of Medicine, Sao Paulo, Brazil.

PURPOSE: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) remain a major cause of morbidity and 
mortality in patients undergoing chemotherapy. The rising incidence of 
multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) further challenges the adequacy of 
empirical antimicrobial therapy. Therefore, this study aimed to identify 
features associated with different microbiological profiles of BSIs in 
chemotherapy patients using machine learning models.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1435 confirmed BSI episodes among 1220 
patients treated at a tertiary cancer center from 2017 to 2022. A multi-label 
classification approach was used to model BSIs associated with 
carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacilli (CR-GNB), methicillin-resistant 
staphylococci, third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales 
(3GCRE), fungal pathogens, and non-MDRO/non-fungal. Classifier chain models 
based on logistic regression, random forests, neural networks, and gradient 
boosting were trained and evaluated using cross-validation with an independent 
test set. Model outputs were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations 
(SHAP) to estimate feature contributions.
RESULTS: Most BSIs occurred during the first chemotherapy cycle and were due to 
non-MDROs or fungal agents (1193 episodes; 83.1%), CR-GNB was identified in 109 
(7.6%). Model performance varied across pathogen groups, with the highest 
discrimination observed for CR-GNB (AUC-ROC 83.25%; 95% CI 73.91%-91.64%). Key 
features included hospitalization days, hematologic malignancy, prior MDRO 
infection, monocytopenia, and palliative chemotherapy. Chemotherapy class 
contributed differently across pathogen groups, with alkylating agents 
contributing to candidemia, antitumor antibiotics to CR-GNB, and antimetabolites 
to 3GCRE. Prior CR-GNB infection was the strongest predictor for CR-GNB BSI, 
while palliative chemotherapy correlated with non-MDRO/non-fungal BSI.
CONCLUSION: Multi-label machine learning approaches may help disentangle the 
complex etiologies of BSIs in cancer patients by identifying associations 
between host factors, prior MDRO infection, and chemotherapy class within 
confirmed BSI episodes, informing future hypothesis generation.

The effect of seizure-free period on seizure recurrence following antiseizure 
medication withdrawal: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

Zhou H(1), Zhou W(2), Xu X(3).

Author information:
(1)Chongqing Medical University, Chongqing, China.
(2)Department of Psychiatry, The First Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University 
School of Medicine, Hangzhou, China.
(3)Chongqing Key Laboratory of Neurology, Department of Neurology, The First 
Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, 1 Youyi Road, Chongqing, 
400016, China. xuxin86516@163.com.

BACKGROUND: The seizure-free period before withdrawal is an important factor 
that influences the risk of epilepsy relapse. Our study aimed to evaluate the 
effect of the seizure-free period on the relapse risk after antiseizure 
medication(ASM) withdrawal in epilepsy populations and identify the optimal 
timing of ASM withdrawal.
METHODS: The Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PubMed and Web of 
Science were searched for literature published from inception to November 2, 
2025. The primary outcome was the relapse risk of epilepsy patients after ASM 
withdrawal. Random-effects meta-analysis models were used to estimate the pooled 
recurrence risk based on heterogeneity.
RESULTS: We identified 45 studies with 10,896 patients; 22 studies with 3933 
patients were included in the meta-analysis. According to the analyses of all 
the epilepsy patients, there was a greater risk of recurrence in patients with 
<5 years of seizure freedom (RR (95% CI) 1.49 (1.17-1.88), p=0.001). Our results 
also revealed that patients with ≥10 years of seizure freedom had a higher risk 
of recurrence (RR (95% CI) 0.21 (0.09-0.49), p<0.001); however, it needs further 
validation due to the limited number of participants and the inclusion of 
studies. With respect to the subgroup analyses, paediatric patients who had 
<3 years of seizure freedom, adult patients who had <5 years of seizure freedom, 
European patients who had <2 years of seizure freedom and Middle Eastern 
patients who had <3 years of seizure freedom had a higher relapse risk(RR(95% 
CI) 1.70(1.20-2.39),p=0.003; RR(95% CI) 1.52(1.02-2.26),p=0.04; RR(95% CI) 
2.11(1.48-2.99),p<0.001; RR(95% CI) 1.87 (1.41-2.48),p<0.001; RR(95% CI) 
1.37(1.03-1.83),p=0.03).
SIGNIFICANCE: The seizure-free period may be an important factor that influences 
patients' risk of recurrence after ASM withdrawal. Without strong 
recommendations and evidence regarding the seizure-free period and risk of 
seizure recurrence, this meta-analysis provides evidence of the optimal timing 
of ASM withdrawal in epilepsy subpopulations.

AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Paracrine signalling by hormone-producing endocrine cells 
potentially influences pancreatic development, but this feedback regulation 
remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the roles of gastrin (GAST), 
cholecystokinin (CCK) and their receptor cholecystokinin B receptor (CCKBR) 
during human pancreatic development.
METHODS: Human iPSCs were differentiated stepwise into definitive endoderm and 
then the pancreatic endocrine lineage. To assess CCKBR function, CRISPR/Cas9 was 
used to generate CCKBR-knockout iPSC lines. We profiled transcriptional states 
by bulk and single-cell RNA-seq with computational analyses, and complemented 
these with biochemical assays, flow cytometry (FACS) and confocal microscopy.
RESULTS: CCKBR expression peaked during definitive endoderm formation and 
progressively declined during differentiation, remaining detectable in 
pancreatic progenitors but largely absent from the endocrine lineage. By 
contrast, GAST and CCK were expressed only transiently during pancreatic 
progenitor and endocrine lineage formation. Pharmacological 
activation/inhibition and genetic knockout implicated CCKBR signalling during 
definitive endoderm formation. Consistently, bulk RNA-seq indicated that CCKBR 
deletion triggered ectodermal- and mesodermal-associated transcriptional 
programs and diminished pancreatic lineage specification. During pancreatic 
induction and lineage formation, sustained CCKBR activation with GAST or CCK 
attenuated endocrinogenesis and promoted epithelial structure formation. Further 
analysis revealed the emergence of a pancreatic ductal-like cell formation under 
prolonged CCKBR stimulation.
CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: This study provides mechanistic evidence that the 
GAST/CCK-CCKBR axis is functionally important during human endoderm and pancreas 
development. This pathway is repeatedly required during in vitro pluripotent 
stem cell differentiation, regulating germ-layer formation as well as ductal vs 
endocrine fate decisions. These findings support the optimisation of pancreatic 
differentiation protocols and inform future studies on whether this axis 
contributes to human pancreas development and disease.

Integrated computational and biochemical identification of 
quinoline-8-arylsulfonamides as disruptors of the Skp2-Cks1 protein-protein 
interaction.

Kamel EM(1), Allam AA(2), Rudayni HA(2), Othman SI(3), Alshabrmi FM(4), Alkhayl 
FFA(4), Lamsabhi AM(5).

Author information:
(1)Chemistry Department, Faculty of Science, Beni-Suef University, Beni-Suef, 
62514, Egypt. emad.abdelhameed@science.bsu.edu.eg.
(2)Department of Biology, College of Science, Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic 
University (IMSIU), 11623, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
(3)Department of Biology, College of Science, Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman 
University, P.O. BOX 84428, 11671, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
(4)Department of Medical Laboratories, College of Applied Medical Sciences, 
Qassim University, 51452, Buraydah, Saudi Arabia.
(5)Departamento de Química, Facultad de Ciencias and Institute for Advanced 
Research in Chemical Science (IAdChem), Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, Módulo 
13, 28049, Madrid, Spain.

CONTEXT: The Skp2-Cks1 protein-protein interaction is essential for the 
recognition and ubiquitination of cell-cycle regulators such as p27 and 
represents an attractive target for anticancer drug discovery. This study aimed 
to identify small-molecule disruptors of the Skp2-Cks1 interface from a 
quinoline-8-arylsulfonamide library using an integrated computational and 
experimental approach. Comparative MM/PBSA analysis indicated that C2 and C1 
produced the greatest predicted weakening of the interface, with ΔΔGₚₚᵢ values 
of +13.19 and +9.54 kcal/mol, respectively. Conversely, C3 and C4 yielded 
negative values of -15.21 and -26.47 kcal/mol, consistent with predicted 
interface stabilization. These computational findings were supported by the 
biochemical activity ranking: C2 and C1 exhibited the lowest IC₅₀ values, at 
1.48 ± 0.13 and 1.87 ± 0.13 µM, respectively, compared with 2.62 ± 0.35 µM for 
the reference compound NSC689857. C3 and C4 showed substantially weaker 
activity. These findings identify quinoline-8-arylsulfonamides as a promising 
chemotype for targeting the Skp2-Cks1 interface and prioritize C2 for further 
optimization.
METHODS: A funnel-based virtual screening strategy was applied to 74 compounds, 
incorporating diversity and drug-likeness filtering, molecular docking with 
AutoDock Vina, short molecular dynamics refinement, and MM/PBSA rescoring. 
Prioritized complexes underwent 1000 ns molecular dynamics simulations, 
free-energy landscape analysis, quantitative assessment of protein-protein 
interaction disruption metrics, and in silico ADMET profiling. Comparative 
MM/PBSA calculations evaluated ligand-induced changes in Skp2-Cks1 interaction 
energy relative to the apo complex. Biochemical inhibitory activity was assessed 
using an in vitro homogeneous time-resolved fluorescence (HTRF) assay.

Survival outcomes with Lutetium-177-PSMA-617 in metastatic castration-resistant

PURPOSE: To investigate cancer-control outcomes in metastatic 
castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) patients receiving Lutetium-177 
Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen-617 (Lu-177-PSMA) radioligand therapy 
according to initial baseline tumor characteristics.
METHODS: We relied on the FRAMCAP (FRAnkfurt Metastatic Cancer Database of the 
Prostate) database to assess progression-free survival (PFS) and overall 
survival (OS) in patients receiving Lu-177-PSMA as first to seventh mCRPC 
therapy line, according to initial time of metastasis (synchronous vs. 
metachronous), tumor grading (Gleason score [GS] 6-7 vs. 8-10) and M-stage (M1a 
vs. M1b vs. M1c) at initial metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer 
(mHSPC). Kaplan-Meier curve analyses and multivariable Cox regression models 
were applied; multivariable models are additionally adjusted for ECOG status and 
line of Lu-177-PSMA therapy (1-2 L vs. 3 L vs. 4-7 L).
RESULTS: Of 344 Lu-177-PSMA mCRPC patients, 198 (58%) had synchronous vs. 146 
(42%) metachronous mHSPC, 87 (29%) vs. 107 (62%) GS 6-7 vs. 8-10 and 15 (10%) 
vs. 121 (81%) vs. 13 (9%) M1a vs. M1b vs. M1c mHSPC disease. No significant 
differences were observed in PFS (12.1 vs. 13.0 months) or OS (14.9 vs. 18.3 
months) between synchronous and metachronous patients (both p > = 0.09), or in 
PFS (12.9 vs. 11.8 months) and OS (21.4 vs. 15.1 months) between GS 6-7 and GS 
8-10 (both p > = 0.3). M-stage-stratified analyses showed an OS difference (17.9 
vs. 17.7 vs. 9.0 months for M1a vs. M1b vs. M1c, p = 0.01), but not for PFS 
(11.9 vs. 9.5 vs. 8.2 months, p = 0.08). After multivariable adjustment 
including ECOG status and treatment line, initial timing of metastasis, GS, and 
M-stage were not independently associated with PFS or OS. However, later 
treatment line was independently associated with worse OS (3 L vs. 1-2 L: HR 
2.40, 95% CI 1.14-5.04, p = 0.021; 4-7 L vs. 1-2 L: HR 4.01, 95% CI 1.83-8.80, 
p < 0.001) as well as worse ECOG status (1-2 vs. 0: HR 2,60, 95% CI 1.38-4,91, 
p = 0.003).
CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort of mCRPC patients treated with 
Lu-177-PSMA, initial timing of metastatic disease, Gleason score, and M-stage 
were not independently associated with PFS or OS after multivariable adjustment 
including ECOG status and treatment line. These observational findings should 
not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent treatment efficacy across 
subgroups.
