The ubiquitination/deubiquitination system is a key regulatory mechanism for 
maintaining proteome homeostasis in eukaryotic cells. Deubiquitinating enzymes 
(DUBs), which remove ubiquitin from substrate proteins, regulate plant 
development, stress responses, and other physiological processes. Although DUBs 
have emerged as important regulators of plant growth and stress responses, their 
systematic genomic characterization in white birch (Betula platyphylla) remains 
limited, restricting our understanding of their potential roles in the 
reproduction of woody plants. In this study, 56 BpDUB genes were identified in 
white birch (Betula platyphylla) and classified into six conserved subfamilies 
(UBP, OTU, UCH, MJD, JAMM, and MINDY). Comparative and synteny analyses revealed 
that DUB genes are evolutionarily conserved while exhibiting lineage-specific 
divergence across angiosperms. Promoter analysis showed that BpDUBs harbor 
diverse cis-acting elements associated with growth and development, stress 
responses, hormone signaling, and transcription factor binding. Treatment with 
the broad-spectrum DUB inhibitor PR-619 markedly impaired both pollen 
germination and pollen tube elongation, supporting the involvement of DUB 
activity in pollen development. RNA-seq analysis showed that BpUBP3 exhibited 
stage-specific induction during pollen germination, and AS-ODN-mediated 
downregulation of BpUBP3 reduced pollen germination and pollen tube growth. 
These findings provide preliminary evidence supporting a role for BpUBP3 in 
pollen germination and pollen tube growth and provide a basis for further 
investigation of DUB functions in reproductive development in white birch.

Metabolic scaling in a freshwater predator is robust across wild and 
hatchery-reared populations and experimental designs.

Bihun CJ(1), Faust MD(2), Hintz WD(3), Ritchie EB(4), Brownscombe JW(5), Raby 
GD(4)(6).

Author information:
(1)Environmental and Life Sciences Graduate Program, Trent University, 2089 East 
Bank Dr., ON, K9L 1Z8, Peterborough, Canada. christianj.bihun@gmail.com.
(2)Sandusky Fisheries Research Station, Ohio Department of Natural Resources, 
Sandusky, OH, USA.
(3)Department of Environmental Sciences and Lake Erie Center, University of 
Toledo, Oregon, OH, USA.
(4)Environmental and Life Sciences Graduate Program, Trent University, 2089 East 
Bank Dr., ON, K9L 1Z8, Peterborough, Canada.
(5)Great Lakes Laboratory for Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences, Fisheries and 
Oceans Canada, Burlington, ON, Canada.
(6)Biology Department, Trent University, Peterborough, ON, Canada.

Standard metabolic rate (SMR) and maximum metabolic rate (MMR) define the 
energetic limits of aerobic metabolism in fishes and are increasingly recognized 
as flexible traits linked to life history variation. Yet the factors driving 
intraspecific variation in how SMR and MMR scale with body mass and temperature 
remain unresolved. We assessed mass- and temperature-scaling relationships in 
SMR, MMR and aerobic scope of walleye (Sander vitreus) using data from multiple 
intermittent-flow respirometry experiments conducted from 2020 to 2025. The 
dataset included wild fish from Lake Erie, Lake Ontario, and Rice Lake, and 
hatchery-reared individuals of Lake Ontario origin (n = 207). Additional MMRSwim 
estimates from swim tunnel respirometry (n = 33) were compared with MMRRecovery 
estimates obtained from a chase and air exposure protocol. Together, body mass 
and temperature explained 94.7% of the variation in SMR and 80.2% of variation 
in MMR across the 1-24.5°C range. Sex effects on SMR and MMR were negligible, 
and apparent differences between populations largely reflected differences in 
temperature ranges sampled rather than intrinsic population-level differences. 
Among wild fish (0.36-3.74 kg), SMR scaled hypoallometrically (b = 0.919), 
whereas hatchery fish, which were relatively smaller, were slightly 
hyperallometric (b = 1.081). Mass scaling of MMRRecovery was shallower (b = 
0.664) and consistent with MMRSwim (b = 0.682). Our findings suggest that 
metabolic scaling in walleye is largely conserved across populations in the 
Laurentian Great Lakes, supporting single-population estimates for 
regional-scale bioenergetics models used to predict consumption and growth under 
climate warming.

CD274 Knockout Promotes Bone Formation and Reduces Osteoclast Activity.

El Assaad H(1)(2), Komrakova M(3), Lienenklaus S(4), Decker S(1), Neunaber C(5), 
Bundkirchen K(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Trauma Surgery, Hannover Medical School, Carl-Neuberg-Straße 1, 
30625, Hannover, Germany.
(2)Department of Orthopedics, Trauma Surgery and Plastic Surgery, Leipzig 
University Hospital, Liebigstraße 20, 04103, Leipzig, Germany.
(3)Department of Trauma Surgery, Orthopaedics and Plastic Surgery, Goettingen 
University Medical Center, Robert-Koch-Str. 40, 37075, Goettingen, Germany.
(4)Institute of Laboratory Animal Science, Hannover Medical School, 
Carl-Neuberg-Straße 1, 30625, Hannover, Germany.
(5)Department of Trauma Surgery, Hannover Medical School, Carl-Neuberg-Straße 1, 
30625, Hannover, Germany. neunaber.claudia@mh-hannover.de.

Osteoporosis is a systemic disease characterized by decreased bone density, and 
deterioration in the micro-architectural remodelling of bone tissue, leading to 
an increased susceptibility to bone fractures. One molecule implicated in bone 
metabolism is Programmed Death Ligand 1 (PD-L1), a pharmacologically targetable 
immune-checkpoint molecule encoded by the gene Cd274. The aim of this study was 
to investigate the bone phenotype of Cd274 knockout (KO) mice at 26 weeks of age 
compared to C57BL/6J control wildtype mice on radiological, histological and 
biomechanical level. The cortical wall thickness and cortical volume increased, 
and the trabecular space decreased significantly in both femur and tibia of 
Cd274 KO mice. Moreover, there was a significant increase in BV/TV and 
trabecular volume of lumbar vertebrae of Cd274 KO mice. Yield load, stiffness, 
anorganic amount increased and organic amount decreased significantly in femoral 
bones of Cd274 KO mice. Additionally, there was a significantly higher number of 
osteocytes and lower number of osteoclasts in both humerus and lumbar vertebra 
of Cd274 KO mice. The findings demonstrate that constitutive knockout of Cd274 
was associated with significantly increased bone mass and strength. These 
results-obtained in healthy, skeletally mature constitutive knockout 
mice-indicate an improved bone phenotype in the absence of Cd274 and thus 
contrast with previous studies that associate disruption of the PD-1/PD-L1 axis, 
including immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, with bone loss and increased 
fracture risk. Further studies, particularly in dedicated osteoporosis models, 
are required to elucidate the influence of CD274 on bone metabolism before 
translational conclusions can be drawn.

Effects of first-step constraints on multi-muscle synergies and early postural 
adjustments during step initiation.

Santos-Dias M(1), de Freitas PB(2), Freitas SMSF(3), Latash ML(4).

Author information:
(1)Interdisciplinary Graduate Program in Health Sciences, Universidade Cruzeiro 
do Sul, Rua Galvão Bueno, 868, Bloco B, 12º Andar, Liberdade, São Paulo, SP, 
01506-000, Brazil.
(2)Interdisciplinary Graduate Program in Health Sciences, Universidade Cruzeiro 
do Sul, Rua Galvão Bueno, 868, Bloco B, 12º Andar, Liberdade, São Paulo, SP, 
01506-000, Brazil. deFreitasPB@gmail.com.
(3)Master and Doctoral Program in Physical Therapy, Universidade Cidade de São 
Paulo, São Paulo, SP, Brazil.
(4)Department of Kinesiology, The Pennsylvania State University, University

Step initiation requires the coordinated preparation of posture and movement, 
yet how first step constraints influence multi-muscle synergies stabilizing the 
center of pressure (COP), anticipatory synergy adjustments (ASAs), and early 
postural adjustments (EPAs) remains poorly understood. This study examined the 
effects of stepping surface height and step length on these outcomes in healthy 
young adults. Sixteen participants initiated a step under five conditions: 
level, step-up, step-down, short-step, and long-step. Surface electromyography 
was recorded from 16 leg and trunk muscles bilaterally, and COP coordinates were 
obtained from a force platform. The uncontrolled manifold approach was used to 
quantify multi-muscle synergies and ASAs stabilizing COP in the anteroposterior 
(AP) and mediolateral (ML) directions during steady-steady and around the foot 
lift-off {-25:+25 ms}. Multi-muscle synergies stabilizing COP-AP were present 
across all conditions, and their index did not differ significantly across 
stepping conditions, supporting the view that steady-state synergic organization 
reflects the demands of upright stance rather than anticipation of the upcoming 
step. Synergies stabilizing COP-ML were absent in all conditions. ASAs were not 
detected in any condition or direction, suggesting that step initiation relies 
more on EPA-based rather than synergy-level anticipatory mechanisms. Stepping 
surface height significantly influenced EPA onset timing and COP displacement 
magnitude in both directions, with the step-down condition producing earlier EPA 
onset and smaller displacements than the step-up condition. Step length did not 
significantly affect EPAs. These findings reveal a dissociation between synergic 
muscle organization and COP trajectory control and highlight the asymmetric 
postural demands of descending versus ascending steps during step initiation.

Growth-Controlled Strain-Driven Epitaxial Spalling of Freestanding Oxide 
Membranes.

Guarino A(1), Scuderi M(2)(3), Rubano A(4), Chen Y(5), Di Gennaro E(4)(5), 
Fittipaldi R(1), Konstantinopoulou P(6), Jespersen TS(6)(7), Vecchione A(1), 
Miletto Granozio F(5), Sambri A(5).

Author information:
(1)CNR-SPIN, c/o University of Salerno, Via Giovanni Paolo II 132, Fisciano 
(SA)84084, Italy.
(2)IMM-CNR, Strada VIII n. 5 Zona Industriale, Catania95121, Italy.
(3)INFN-LNS, Via S. Sofia 62, Catania95123, Italy.
(4)University "Federico II" di Napoli, Complesso di Monte S. Angelo, via Cinthia 
, Napoli80126, Italy.
(5)CNR-SPIN, c/o Complesso di Monte S. Angelo, via Cinthia, Napoli80126, Italy.
(6)Department of Energy Conversion and Storage, Technical University of Denmark,

(7)Center For Quantum Devices, Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen,

Freestanding complex-oxide membranes are promising platforms for heterogeneous 
integration, strain engineering, and device architectures on non-native 
substrates. Strain-driven epitaxial spalling offers a sacrificial-layer-free 
route to such membranes, but its use in complex oxides has so far been explored 
mainly under fixed growth conditions. Here we show that the formation of 
freestanding LaAlO3/SrTiO3 micromembranes can be systematically controlled by 
tuning the pulsed-laser-deposition (PLD) conditions of the LaAlO3 stressor 
layer. By mapping the membrane formation yield as a function of laser fluence 
and oxygen background pressure, we identify a process window for reproducible 
high-yield spalling and correlate it with cracking behavior, membrane release, 
and microstructural evolution. We show that efficient spalling requires both 
sufficient elastic-energy accumulation and preservation of a structurally 
coherent early interface. Low oxygen pressure conditions during the first unit 
cells as well as low laser fluence during growth promote premature strain 
relaxation and suppress membrane formation. We also show that, within the 
optimized growth window, additional perovskite layers can be integrated into the 
LaAlO3/SrTiO3 architecture while preserving the spalling process, enabling the 
design of functionalized spalled membranes. We further show that complete 
spalling, with high-yield membrane formation, is achieved for LaAlO3 thicknesses 
down to 53-55 nm, substantially reducing the total membrane thickness compared 
with previous implementations. Finally, we demonstrate that the spalling 
approach can be extended to selected alternative substrates, including Ca-doped 
SrTiO3 and Sr2RuO4. These results establish epitaxial spalling as a 
growth-controlled and interface-sensitive route to structurally complex 
freestanding oxide micro-membranes.

Determining whether a person died from drowning remains a major forensic 
challenge, particularly in cases involving advanced decomposition where only 
skeletal remains are available. Traditional methods, such as diatom analysis and 
macroscopic autopsy findings, often lack sufficient specificity and reliability. 
Although several molecular biomarkers have been investigated, none has yet 
demonstrated sufficient accuracy for routine forensic application. This 
prospective experimental study evaluated a novel dual-biomarker approach using 
Aquaporin 5 (AQP5), a water channel protein, and Cytochrome c (CYCS), an 
apoptosis-related protein, as potential indicators of drowning. Thirty-eight 
adult Wistar rats were randomly assigned to experimental drowning groups or 
non-drowning control groups (exposed to freshwater from Boračko and Jablaničko 
lakes. Lung, femoral bone, and dental tissues were collected postmortem, and 
AQP5 and CYCS concentrations were quantified using commercially available ELISA 
kits. Statistical analyses included the Shapiro-Wilk test and the Mann-Whitney U 
test, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. AQP5 expression in dental 
tissue differed significantly between drowning and control groups in both 
freshwater environments (p = 0.0184 and p = 0.0235), whereas no significant 
differences were observed in lung or bone tissues. CYCS expression did not 
differ significantly between drowning and control groups in any tissue examined. 
These findings suggest that AQP5 expression in dental tissue may represent a 
promising supplementary biomarker for the forensic diagnosis of drowning, 
particularly in cases where only skeletal remains are available. Further 
validation in human tissues and larger experimental cohorts is warranted.

Chen Y(1), He Y(1), Pan X(1), Wen C(1), Wang H(1), Chen H(1), Chen Y(1), Lai 
Y(1), Pan C(1), Zou S(2), Lu Z(3), Chen L(3), Li Z(1), Yu H(1), Li L(1)(4).

Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, endothelial 
dysfunction, impaired angiogenesis, and poor local retention of therapeutic 
agents, all of which hinder effective repair. Here, we combined 
Netrin-1-enriched exosomes (NTN-Exos) from genetically modified adipose-derived

acid methacryloyl/polyvinyl alcohol (HAMA-PBA/PVA) hydrogel to create a diabetic

Nanomaterial Design for Macrophage Reprogramming: Emerging Strategies and 
Mechanistic Insights for Inflammation and Tumor Therapy.

Giri N(1), Chakraborty A(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chemistry, School of Advanced Sciences, Vellore Institute of 
Technology, Vellore632014, Tamil Nadu, India.

Macrophages play a paradoxical role in inflammation and tumor. They can protect 
the host during acute inflammation but act as the main driver for the chronic 
inflammation which is a common characteristic of several diseases including 
rheumatoid arthritis, atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes, inflammatory bowel 
disease, and neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and 
Parkinson's disease. In the tumor microenvironment, macrophages switch their 
phenotype to the immunosuppressive M2 state that promotes tumor growth, 
angiogenesis, and metastasis. Emerging nanomaterial platforms are trying to 
offer transformative solutions by enabling the precise delivery of 
immunomodulatory drugs directly to disease-site macrophages. This review will 
provide comprehensive comparative analysis of these emerging nanomaterial 
designs strategies across two disease paradigms: inflammatory diseases and 
tumor. The discussion will focus on various strategies which include inhibiting 
chemokine axis (CCL2-CCR2 axis), selective elimination of macrophages through 
apoptosis, metabolic reprogramming, biomimetic and apoptotic cell-inspired 
nanoparticles leveraging natural macrophage clearance pathways to promote M2 
polarization in inflammation, and the activation of tumor-associated macrophages 
via TLR and STING agonist. We highlight the role of nanoparticle surface 
chemistry, composition, and targeting ligands in achieving the two opposite 
therapeutic outcomes of these two diseases while maintaining some common design 
principles including EPR-mediated accumulation at the disease sites and 
biomimetic modifications. We also mentioned novel next-generation 
nanoparticle-based platforms that are currently in clinical trials for the 
treatment of tumor and inflammatory diseases. Finally, we discuss the barriers 
that limit the clinical translational potential of broad nanoparticles, with 
particular emphasis on nanoparticle-related immunotoxicity, macrophage 
heterogeneity, and manufacturing reproducibility of the nanoparticles.

Large language model responses to structured textual descriptions of salivary 
gland imaging findings: impact of contextual enrichment on self-reported 
diagnostic confidence and reporting behavior.

Lazzeroni M(1), Capaccio P(2)(3), Estomba CC(4), Buccichini G(5), Firetto MC(5), 
Pignataro L(5), Gaffuri M(5), Carrafiello G(6), Lavalle S(7), Salerno VM(7), 
Lentini M(7)(8), Maniaci A(9)(10).

Author information:
(1)Department of Otorhinolaryngology & Head and Neck Surgery, ASST Grande 
Ospedale Metropolitano Niguarda, Milan, Italy.
(2)Department of Biomedical, Surgical and Dental Sciences, University of Milan, 
Milan, Italy.
(3)Department of Otorhinolaryngology & Head and Neck Surgery, Fatebenefratelli 
Hospital, ASST Fatebenefratelli Sacco, Milan, Italy.
(4)Department of Otolaryngology & Head and Neck Surgery, Donostia University 
Hospital, San Sebastián, Spain.
(5)Department of Otolaryngology and Head and Neck Surgery, Fondazione IRCCS Ca' 
Granda Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico di Milano, Milan, Italy.
(6)Operative Unit of Radiology, Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda Ospedale, Maggiore 
Policlinico Di Milano, Milan, Italy.
(7)Department of Medicine and Surgery, University of Enna "Kore", Enna, 94100, 
Italy.
(8)ASP Ragusa, Hospital Giovanni Paolo II, Ragusa, 97100, Italy.
(9)Department of Medicine and Surgery, University of Enna "Kore", Enna, 94100, 
Italy. antonino.maniaci@unikore.it.
(10)ASP Ragusa, Hospital Giovanni Paolo II, Ragusa, 97100, Italy. 
antonino.maniaci@unikore.it.

PURPOSE: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in clinical 
decision support, yet their behavior when presented with structured textual 
descriptions of imaging findings, particularly in salivary gland disease, 
remains poorly defined. The present study was set out to evaluate how the 
responses of different LLMs change as the textual input is progressively 
enriched. The models did not receive imaging data; all inputs were text.
METHODS: This exploratory, simulation-based observational study assessed 3 LLMs 
(ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) across 10 salivary gland cases. For each case, a 
standardized textual description of the imaging findings was prepared and 
submitted as a text prompt; no image files were uploaded to any platform. Each 
case was evaluated under 3 input conditions of increasing informational content: 
single-plane textual description, multiplanar textual description, and 
multiplanar textual description plus clinical information, generating 90 total 
observations derived from repeated measurement of the same 10 cases. Primary 
outcomes were the model-generated severity score, self-reported diagnostic 
confidence, and the number of additional reported anatomical structures. AI 
outputs were not benchmarked against a verified reference diagnosis. The primary 
analysis was a proportional-odds model with input condition as the fixed effect 
of interest, AI system as a covariate, and cluster-robust standard errors by 
case; non-parametric tests were used as sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Model-generated severity scores did not significantly differ among LLMs 
(χ²=2.31; P = 0.31). Self-reported diagnostic confidence increased significantly 
as the textual input was enriched (Friedman χ²=18.86; P < 0.001; 
proportional-odds model, multiplanar description plus clinical information vs. 
single-plane description, cumulative OR 5.43, 95% CI 3.00-9.81). ChatGPT 
produced stable outputs with no additional reported structures, whereas Claude 
produced substantially more detailed reports (mean additional structures, 5.67 
vs. 0.00). Gemini produced lower severity scores but comparable self-reported 
confidence. Mixed-model analysis revealed a significant effect of AI system on 
reporting verbosity (P < 0.001). Associations between model-reported parenchymal 
changes and self-reported confidence were also observed; because both variables 
were generated by the same model within the same response, these represent 
within-output associations rather than independent diagnostic relationships and 
are reported descriptively.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory pilot study, LLMs produced comparable severity 
ratings, while self-reported diagnostic confidence increased as more information 
was supplied in the prompt. This pattern may reflect the tendency of an LLM to 
express greater certainty when given richer input rather than genuinely improved 
diagnostic reasoning. Substantial variability in reporting behavior exists 
across models, particularly in output detail. These findings suggest that LLMs 
may warrant further investigation as adjunctive tools for text-based tasks in 
salivary gland care. The present design does not evaluate image interpretation 
and does not support use as standalone diagnostic systems.

PURPOSE: Cocaine-induced midline destructive lesions (CIMDL) may cause 
progressive septonasal and palatal destruction, but the optimal timing of 
reconstruction remains undefined. Because relapse is common, particularly within 
the first year, premature surgery may lead to failure and, in advanced cases, 
severe complications. This work synthesizes the available evidence and expert 
opinion to guide surgical timing and practical management.
METHODS: We performed a narrative evidence-based review of studies addressing 
cocaine relapse, abstinence verification, and reconstructive or prosthetic 
management in CIMDL, integrated with multidisciplinary expert consensus. Key 
relapse data were drawn from large longitudinal cohorts, including national 
treatment and follow-up studies and analyses of continuing care and initial 
abstinence.
RESULTS: Relapse risk remains clinically significant throughout the first 12 
months after treatment, with weekly-use relapse rates of approximately 20-24% at 
12 months. Beyond 12 months, increases appear smaller in longitudinal cohorts. 
Early sustained abstinence is protective, with at least 12 weeks of abstinence 
during treatment associated with substantially lower relapse rates. As 
self-report is often unreliable, repeated toxicology testing combined with 
serial endoscopic assessment offers objective monitoring, facilitates shared 
review with patients, and may improve adherence. Reconstructions beyond simple 
septal perforations are usually staged, and relapse during treatment can 
irreversibly compromise outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Based on relapse dynamics and expert consensus, reconstruction in 
CIMDL should be deferred until at least 12 months of toxicology-verified 
abstinence within a multidisciplinary pathway including structured monitoring, 
optimized prosthetic care, staged surgery, and prolonged postoperative 
surveillance.

Does local steroid therapy improve outcomes in acute otitis media with serous 
labyrinthitis? A retrospective analysis.

Fischer HT(1), Keller F(2), Schmit C(3), Theurl F(1), Santer M(1), Hils A(1), 
Stecher L(1), Koller F(1), Schmutzler L(1), Gottfried T(1), Schmutzhard J(1), 
Hofauer B(1), Dejaco D(1).

Author information:
(1)Universitätsklinik Für Hals, Nasen- Und Ohrenheilkunde, Medizinische 
Universität Innsbruck, Anichstraße 35, A-6020, Innsbruck, Österreich.
(2)Univ.-Klinik Für Innere Medizin IV (Nephrologie Und Hypertensiologie), 
Medizinische Universität Innsbruck, Innsbruck, Österreich.
(3)Universitätsklinik Für Hals, Nasen- Und Ohrenheilkunde, Medizinische 
Universität Innsbruck, Anichstraße 35, A-6020, Innsbruck, Österreich. 
Charles.schmit@i-med.ac.at.

PURPOSE: Sensorineural hearing loss represents a rare but clinically relevant 
complication of acute otitis media (AOM). Although intratympanic glucocorticoid 
(GC) therapy is established in other cochleovestibular disorders, its efficacy 
in this context remains insufficiently investigated. The aim of this study was 
to retrospectively assess whether local intratympanic glucocorticoid application 
is associated with improved clinical outcomes in patients with acute otitis 
media-related sensorineural hearing loss.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on patients diagnosed with 
AOM-associated inner ear involvement between January 2014 and November 2024. 
Patients were stratified according to GC treatment regimen: (1) intratympanic 
application of glucocorticoids (IC), (2) no intratympanic application of 
glucocorticoids (NIC). Subgroup analyses were performed according to the 
surgical drainage method and severity of inner ear involvement. Primary endpoint 
was improvement in bone-conduction pure-tone average (BCPTA4).
RESULTS: A total of 137 patients were included (IC: 44, NIC: 93). Sex, affected 
side and subjective improvement did not differ significantly between both groups 
(all p > 0.08). Both groups demonstrated significant hearing improvement 
following treatment (p < 0.001). Although numerical trends favored the NIC group 
across different severity levels, no statistically significant differences in 
BCPTA4 improvement were observed between treatment modalities (p = 0.8); 
however, the non-randomized design and baseline group differences limit 
interpretation. In exploratory analyses, Ventilation Tube Insertion (VT) and 
CO₂-laser myringotomy (LP) were associated with significant hearing recovery 
(p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Both treatment regimens (IC, NIC) led to significant hearing 
improvement in AOM-associated inner ear involvement. In this non-randomized 
comparison, no statistically significant difference in BCPTA4 improvement was 
detected between groups; however, selection bias, baseline imbalances and 
residual confounding may have obscured small treatment effects. These findings 
do not constitute evidence of equivalence.

Riedel thyroiditis mimicking malignancy: a fatal surgical outcome.

Gündoğdu Y(1), Çavlan CE(2), Tereci Oran B(1), Asya O(1), Çeşmecioğlu Karavin 
E(3), Türköz K(3), Yumuşakhuylu AC(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Otorhinolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, Marmara University 
School of Medicine, Istanbul, Turkey.
(2)Department of Otorhinolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, Marmara University 
School of Medicine, Istanbul, Turkey. cavlan0695@gmail.com.
(3)Department of Pathology, Marmara University School of Medicine, Istanbul,

PURPOSE: Riedel thyroiditis (RT) is a rare fibroinflammatory disorder that can 
mimic malignancy clinically and radiologically. We report an unusually 
extensive, ultimately fatal case and highlight its diagnostic and therapeutic 
lessons.
METHODS: Case report of a 40-year-old man, with review of the clinical, imaging, 
histopathological and follow-up data, reported in accordance with the CARE 
guidelines.
RESULTS: The patient presented with a right cervicothoracic mass 
(64 × 45 × 115 mm) circumferentially encasing the common carotid, subclavian and 
innominate vessels with mediastinal extension. Three tissue procedures were 
non-diagnostic and FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake (SUVmax 8.15). Radical en 
bloc resection was undertaken because malignancy could not be excluded. The 
course was complicated by bilateral vocal-cord paralysis, Horner syndrome, 
mediastinitis, osteomyelitis and a tracheo-innominate fistula. Histology showed 
obliterative phlebitis, storiform fibrosis and 74 IgG4-positive plasma cells/HPF 
(IgG4:IgG 44%), confirming RT despite normal serum IgG4. The patient died of a 
recurrent tracheo-innominate fistula approximately 20 months postoperatively.
CONCLUSION: RT can mimic malignancy and, when radical surgery is undertaken for 
diagnostic uncertainty, may prove fatal. Adequate tissue sampling with IgG4 
immunostaining is essential before contemplating radical surgery.

Functional outcomes of conventional air- and bone-conduction hearing aids in 
patients with unilateral sensorineural hearing loss.

Wang R(1), Xie H(1), Zhang Z(1), Li D(1), Jiang D(1), Liu J(1), Zhang Z(1), Luo 
J(1), Wang H(1), Xu L(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, Shandong Provincial ENT 
Hospital, Shandong University, Jinan, 250022, P.R. China.
(2)Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, Shandong Provincial ENT 
Hospital, Shandong University, Jinan, 250022, P.R. China. sdphxl@126.com.

PURPOSE: To explore speech performance in multi-talker environments, subjective 
satisfaction with hearing and spatial ability, and factors influencing outcomes 
in patients with unilateral sensorineural hearing loss (USNHL) fitted with 
conventional hearing aids (HAs).
METHODS: A total of 32 native Mandarin-speaking individuals with USNHL were 
retrospectively enrolled. Patients were fitted with either air-conduction (AC) 
or bone-conduction (BC) HAs based on individual suitability. Real-ear 
measurements (REM) were performed for AC HA fitting according to NAL-NL2 
(adults) or DSL v5 (pediatric) prescriptive targets. At the initial fitting 
session, speech perception in noise was assessed under multi-talker conditions 
across three spatial configurations representing binaural squelch, summation, 
and head shadow effects. The Chinese version of the Speech, Spatial and 
Qualities of Hearing Scale (C-SSQ12) was administered to evaluate subjective 
performance. Follow-up assessments at 6 months included speech perception 
testing, re-administration of the C-SSQ12, and an overall satisfaction survey.
RESULTS: Comparing aided and unaided conditions at the initial HA fitting, no 
significant differences in speech recognition threshold (SRT) were observed 
under S0N0, S0NSSD, or SSSDNNH configurations (p = 0.5983,p = 0.1008, 
p = 0.9375, respectively). At 6-month follow-up (n = 12), no significant 
improvements in speech perception were detected compared to baseline (p > 0.05 
for all configurations). However, regarding C-SSQ12 outcomes (n = 26), scores 
for questions assessing spatial localization (Questions 6 and 7) showed 
significant improvements at 6 months compared to baseline (r=-0.5691, p = 0.004 
and r=-0.6674, p < 0.001, respectively), while the score for music perception 
(Question 10) declined (r=-0.5254, p = 0.007). The effect sizes were all large 
according to Cohen's standards. At initial fitting, a negative correlation was 
observed between hearing loss duration and SRT variation under SSSDNNH 
(r =-0.3549, p = 0.0463), and a negative correlation was found between worse ear 
pure-tone average (PTA) and ∆SRT under S0NSSD (r=-0.4057, p = 0.0212). Pre-aided 
speech was correlated negatively with ΔSRTs under all three conditions (p all 
< 0.05). The worse ear PTA was positively correlated with improvement in total 
C-SSQ12 score at 6 months (r = 0.4743, p = 0.0144).
CONCLUSION: Within a 6-month adaptation period, patients with USNHL fitted with 
conventional HAs demonstrated limited improvements in only two items of 
subjective spatial perception abilities, while the majority of subjective 
domains and all objective measures of binaural speech-in-noise performance 
showed no significant benefit. Hearing loss duration, pre-aided speech, and 
worse ear PTA emerged as factors influencing short-term speech outcomes at 
initial HA fitting. The worse ear PTA also influenced subjective speech, 
spatial, and qualities of hearing performance at 6-month follow-up.

Stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (sTIL) in laryngeal squamous cell 
carcinoma: association with pharyngocutaneous fistula, recurrence, and 
mortality.

Erol S(1), Büyük BB(2), Erol A(3), Bozdoğan N(3), Toprak F(2), Arslan A(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Otorhinolaryngology, University of Health Sciences, Ankara 
Atatürk Sanatoryum Training and Research Hospital, Ankara, Türkiye. 
drselcukerol95@gmail.com.
(2)Department of Otorhinolaryngology, University of Health Sciences, Dr. 
Abdurrahman Yurtaslan Ankara Oncology Training and Research Hospital, Ankara, 
Türkiye.
(3)Department of Pathology, University of Health Sciences, Dr. Abdurrahman 
Yurtaslan Ankara Oncology Training and Research Hospital, Ankara, Türkiye.

PURPOSE: Previous studies suggest a favorable prognostic role for 
tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma, although 
findings vary by immune-cell phenotype, assessment method, tumor compartment, 
and cohort characteristics. This study evaluated associations between sTIL 
percentage and pharyngocutaneous fistula, recurrence, and mortality after 
surgery.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 81 patients who 
underwent primary or salvage total laryngectomy between January 2019 and March 
2024. sTIL was assessed on H&E sections according to International TILs Working 
Group guidelines. Because sTIL was non-normally distributed (Shapiro-Wilk 
W = 0.908; p < 0.001), non-parametric tests were used. Associations were 
assessed using Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, chi-square/Fisher's exact tests, 
and Spearman correlation. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox 
regression.
RESULTS: Median sTIL was 30% (IQR: 10-50%). sTIL was not significantly 
associated with fistula, recurrence, mortality, surgical approach, 
lymphovascular or perineural invasion, T stage, or differentiation grade (all 
p > 0.05). Mortality was associated with older age (68 vs. 60 years; p = 0.004). 
Deceased patients had longer observed follow-up, reflecting time-to-event 
structure rather than a prognostic association. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no 
survival difference by sTIL group (log-rank p = 0.914). In the reduced 
multivariable Cox model, age (HR: 1.05; p = 0.043) and lymphovascular invasion 
(HR: 4.79; p < 0.001) were independently associated with mortality, whereas sTIL 
was not (HR: 1.01; p = 0.600).
CONCLUSIONS: H&E-based sTIL scoring was not significantly associated with 
pharyngocutaneous fistula, recurrence, or overall survival. Given the limited 
number of fistula events, the fistula-related findings should be considered 
exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Age and lymphovascular invasion were 
independently associated with mortality. These non-confirmatory findings require 
validation in larger studies using spatial and phenotypic immune profiling.

Association of beta-blockers use with risk and clinical outcomes of head and 
neck cancer: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.

Zhang LE(1), Aizawa Y(2), Oishi A(2), Kanai S(2), Sumita Y(2), Hirai H(2), 
Tomihara K(2).

Author information:
(1)Division of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Faculty of Dentistry and Graduate 
School of Medicine, Dentistry and Health Sciences, Niigata University, Niigata, 
Japan. chou@dent.niigata-u.ac.jp.
(2)Division of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Faculty of Dentistry and Graduate 
School of Medicine, Dentistry and Health Sciences, Niigata University, Niigata, 
Japan.

PURPOSE: Preclinical evidence suggests beta-blockers (BBs) may inhibit 
stress-induced tumor progression, but clinical data on their association with 
head and neck cancer (HNC) outcomes remain conflicting. This study evaluated the 
association between BB use and the risk and prognosis of HNC.
METHODS: A comprehensive search of five databases was conducted. We performed a 
meta-analysis to assess cancer risk, overall survival (OS), disease-free 
survival (DFS), and disease-specific survival (DSS) between BB users and 
non-users. Heterogeneity was explored by subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Seven studies were included. BB use was significantly associated with a 
reduced risk of HNC (RR = 0.58, 95%CI: 0.45-0.75). But in patients with HNC, BB 
use was linked to poor prognostic outcomes. Users demonstrated significantly 
worse DFS (HR = 1.85, 95%CI: 1.10-3.11) and DSS (HR = 1.82, 95%CI: 1.39-2.39). 
Exploratory subgroup analysis identified that cancer type might be a potential 
source of heterogeneity.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest a potential inverse association between BB 
use and the development of HNC. This estimate should be regarded as exploratory 
because it is derived from only two eligible non-lip head and neck cancer 
cohorts. In diagnosed patients, observational data link BB use to poorer DFS and 
DSS. However, given the statistical fragility of these prognostic estimates and 
potential confounding by indication, these trends must be interpreted with 
caution. Current evidence does not support BBs as adjuvant therapy for HNC. 
Future studies should prioritize adjustment for comorbidities and stratification 
by HPV status and tumor subsite.

Quantitative pathological lymph node parameters in head and neck squamous cell 
carcinoma: a comprehensive analysis of complementary prognostic value in 
clinically relevant subgroups.

Kürten CHL(1), Funk V(2), Theurer S(3), Ingenwerth M(3), Sivakumar V(2), 
Lazzarini E(2), Aksu S(2), Gauler T(4), Guberina M(4), Hartmann S(3), Daser 
A(2), Stähr K(2), Mattheis S(2), Lang S(2), Hussain T(2)(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, University Hospital 
Essen, University of Duisburg-Essen, Hufelandstraße 55, 45147, Essen, Germany. 
cornelius.kuerten@uk-essen.de.
(2)Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, University Hospital 
Essen, University of Duisburg-Essen, Hufelandstraße 55, 45147, Essen, Germany.
(3)Institute of Pathology, University Hospital Essen, University of 
Duisburg-Essen, Hufelandstraße 55, 45147, Essen, Germany.
(4)Department of Radiation Oncology, University Hospital Essen, University of 
Duisburg-Essen, Hufelandstraße 55, 45147, Essen, Germany.
(5)Klinikum rechts der Isar, Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Munich Technical 
University, Ismaninger Straße 22, 81675, München, Germany.

PURPOSE: Quantitative pathological lymph node parameters (qpLNP), i.e. lymph 
node yield (LNY), lymph node ratio (LNR), and weighted lymph node ratio (WLNR), 
are potential prognostic markers in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma 
(HNSCC). Incorporation into post-operative staging may help to direct more 
precise adjuvant treatment regimens. Available data warrant more detailed 
subgroup analyses, we therefore evaluated their prognostic value with particular 
attention to neck dissection laterality, pN0 disease, and patients without 
recommendation for adjuvant therapy.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of 410 surgically treated HNSCC 
patients from a single tertiary center (2010-2020). Data-derived cutoffs were 
determined by recursive partitioning. Overall survival was analyzed using 
Kaplan-Meier estimates, log-rank tests, and multivariable Cox regression. 67 
patients with HPV-associated oropharyngeal carcinoma were analyzed separately.
RESULTS: In 343 patients with HPV-unrelated HNSCC, LNY, LNR, and WLNR were 
independently associated with overall survival on multivariable analysis (LNY: 
HR 1.58, p=0.012; LNR: HR 1.77, p=0.026; WLNR: HR 2.30, p<0.001). Discriminative 
performance increased from LNY (C-index 0.55) to LNR (0.59) to WLNR (0.61). 
Prognostic signal was primarily driven by the ipsilateral and not the 
contralateral neck. LNY (HR 1.92, p=0.044) and WLNR (HR 2.31, p=0.038) showed 
prognostic value in patients without adjuvant therapy, and LNY remained 
independently prognostic in node-negative patients on multivariable analysis (HR 
1.88, p=0.027). Site-specific analyses in patients with HPV-unrelated 
oropharyngeal carcinoma and oral cavity carcinoma treated with bilateral neck 
dissection confirmed independent prognostic value for LNY and WLNR in both 
subgroups. In HPV-associated oropharyngeal carcinoma, qpLNP held no prognostic 
value. Here, extranodal extension was the dominant prognostic factor.
CONCLUSION: LNY, LNR, and WLNR provide complementary prognostic information in 
HPV-unrelated HNSCC. The validity of LNY in node-negative patients emphasizes 
its value as a quality control parameter for surgery while WLNR's performance in 
patients without adjuvant therapy suggests additional value in patient 
stratification for adjuvant treatment.

Efficacy and safety of middle turbinate resection versus preservation during 
endoscopic sinus surgery in patients with chronic rhinosinusitis: a systematic 
review and meta-analysis.

Almaimoni MA(1)(2), Alghazi JH(3)(4), Alagrafy NAH(3)(4), Alharby DF(3)(4), 
Alseraye AS(3)(4), Alsuhaibany KSA(3)(4), Alanazi OI(3)(4)(5), Al-Bahkaly 
S(3)(4)(5).

Author information:
(1)College of Medicine, King Saud bin Abdulaziz University for Health Sciences 
(KSAU-HS), Riyadh, 13611, Saudi Arabia. almaimonimarnd@outlook.com.
(2)Division of Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery, King Abdullah Specialized 
Children's Hospital, King Abdulaziz Medical City, National Guard Health Affairs, 
Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. almaimonimarnd@outlook.com.
(3)College of Medicine, King Saud bin Abdulaziz University for Health Sciences 
(KSAU-HS), Riyadh, 13611, Saudi Arabia.
(4)Division of Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery, King Abdullah Specialized 
Children's Hospital, King Abdulaziz Medical City, National Guard Health Affairs, 
Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
(5)King Abdullah International Medical Research Center (KAIMRC), Riyadh, Saudi 
Arabia.

BACKGROUND: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a common inflammatory disease that 
significantly impairs quality of life. When symptoms persist despite medical 
therapy, endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) is performed. During ESS, whether to 
resect or preserve the middle turbinate remains controversial: resection may 
improve access and reduce postoperative obstruction, while preservation 
maintains anatomy and may support normal healing and airflow. Evidence comparing 
both approaches is limited and inconsistent, so their relative efficacy and 
safety remain unclear.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted across various 
databases until January 2026 to identify relevant studies. The quality was 
assessed using the ROB2 and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) tools and the analysis 
was performed using R software.
RESULTS: The search identified 4,265 records; after screening and full-text 
assessment, 31 studies were included. Compared with preservation, middle 
turbinate resection showed a statistically significant improvement in 
Lund-Kennedy endoscopic score (MD = - 0.58), while symptom improvement measured 
by SNOT showed no significant difference. Resection significantly reduced 
postoperative adhesion/synechiae (RR = 0.35) and sinus ostium restenosis 
(RR = 0.41). For secondary outcomes, olfaction and POSE scores did not differ 
significantly between groups, and crustation and middle meatal antrostomy 
patency were not significantly different. Postoperative bleeding risk was higher 
with resection (RR = 2.24), whereas lateralization (RR = 0.29) and polyp 
recurrence (RR = 0.58) were lower with resection.
CONCLUSION: Middle turbinate resection during ESS for CRS appears to improve 
postoperative endoscopic healing and patency-related outcomes (including reduced 
synechiae and ostial restenosis), but it does not confer a consistent advantage 
in patient-reported symptoms and is associated with a higher risk of 
postoperative bleeding; therefore, MT management should be individualized and 
anatomy-/risk-guided rather than routine.

Outcome of myringoplasty and type 1 tympanoplasty in children: a systematic 
review and meta-analysis.

Yee HH(1), Aziz A(2), Salim R(1), Yaacob NM(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Otorhinolaryngology - Head & Neck Surgery, School of Medical 
Sciences, USM Health Campus Kubang Kerian, Campus Kubang Kerian, 16150, Bharu, 
Kelantan, Malaysia.
(2)Department of Otorhinolaryngology - Head & Neck Surgery, School of Medical 
Sciences, USM Health Campus Kubang Kerian, Campus Kubang Kerian, 16150, Bharu, 
Kelantan, Malaysia. az_aziz@usm.my.
(3)Biostatistics and Research Methodology Unit, School of Medical Sciences, USM 
Health Campus Kubang Kerian, 16150, Bharu, Kelantan, Malaysia.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the anatomical and audiological outcomes of myringoplasty 
and type I tympanoplasty in the pediatric population through systemic review and 
meta-analysis.
METHOD: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane 
Library databases was conducted for studies published between January 2021 until 
September 2025. Studies involving patients ≤ 18 years undergoing myringoplasty 
or type 1 tympanoplasty were included. Random-effects meta-analysis was 
performed to estimate pooled proportions of tympanic membrane closure and 
postoperative complications, as well as pooled mean air-bone gap (ABG) 
improvement. Heterogeneity, publication bias, sensitivity analyses, subgroup 
analyses, and meta-regression were performed. The risk of bias of studies was 
evaluated using JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist and categorizing them into low, 
moderated or high risk of bias according to methodological constraints.
RESULT: Thirty-eight studies comprising 4658 ears were included. The pooled 
tympanic membrane closure rate was 85.8% (95% CI: 83.3 to 88.3), with 
substantial heterogeneity (I² = 81.0%). The pooled rates of postoperative 
infection, keratin pearl formation, and recurrent perforation rates were 11.6%, 
4.0%, and 11.5%, respectively. The pooled mean postoperative air-bone gap (ABG) 
gain was 11.18 dB (95% CI: 9.55 to 12.81). Subgroup analysis demonstrated 
significantly higher success rates in studies with higher risk of bias.
CONCLUSION: Myringoplasty and type 1 tympanoplasty in children demonstrate high 
anatomical success rates and meaningful hearing improvement with relatively low 
complication rates. However, substantial heterogeneity and variability in study 
design warrant cautious interpretation of these findings.

Effects of surgery, radiotherapy or surveillance on the objective vestibular 
function, vestibular symptoms and quality of life in vestibular schwannoma 
patients.

Fuentealba Bassaletti C(1), van Esch BF(2), van Lieshout K(3), Jansen JC(2), 
Koot RW(4), Wiltink LM(5), Bruintjes TD(2), van Benthem PPG(2), Hensen EF(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Otorhinolaryngology / Head and Neck Surgery, Leiden University 
Medical Center, Leiden, The Netherlands. c.a.fuentealba_bassaletti@lumc.nl.
(2)Department of Otorhinolaryngology / Head and Neck Surgery, Leiden University 
Medical Center, Leiden, The Netherlands.
(3)Institute of Education and Child Studies, Leiden University, Leiden, the 
Netherlands.
(4)Department of Neurosurgery, Leiden University Medical Center, Leiden, The 
Netherlands.
(5)Department of Radiotherapy, Leiden University Medical Center, Leiden, The 
Netherlands.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of active surveillance, radiotherapy and 
surgery on the vestibular function, vestibular symptoms, and quality of life in 
unilateral vestibular schwannoma (VS) patients.
METHODS: In this prospective longitudinal study at a tertiary referral center, 
patients underwent caloric and video head impulse (vHIT) testing and completed 
the Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI) and Penn Acoustic Neuroma Quality of Life 
(PANQOL) questionnaires before and after treatment, with treatment-specific 
follow-up: at 6, 12 and 24 months after surveillance start, at 6 weeks, 6 and 12 
months after radiotherapy, and 1, 3, and 12 months after surgery. Longitudinal 
changes were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA.
RESULTS: Compared with baseline, the percentage of abnormal caloric tests 
remained stable in the active surveillance (57%) and surgery groups (93%), but 
increased significantly in the radiotherapy group (from 77% to 92%; p= 0.02) at 
12 months after intervention. All surgical patients showed abnormal vHIT gains 
one month after surgery, whereas abnormalities gradually increased in the active 
surveillance (33%) and radiotherapy (85%) groups. Vestibular symptoms remained 
stable during active surveillance, increased after radiotherapy, and decreased 
after surgery. At 12 months, DHI and PANQOL scores no longer differed 
significantly or clinically between groups.
CONCLUSION: Active surveillance was associated with the most stable objective 
and subjective vestibular function. Surgery caused immediate vestibular 
deterioration, whereas radiotherapy had a delayed comparable effect on mid- to 
long-term vestibular function. Despite baseline differences, vestibular symptoms 
and quality of life did not differ significantly between groups 12 months after 
treatment or initiation of surveillance.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level II.

Mastoid obliteration after cholesteatoma surgery with bone substitute mastoid 
obliteration: A 9-year retrospective experience of 81 cases.

Defaye S(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, CHU Dijon Bourgogne, 
21000, Dijon, France. sdefaye@icloud.com.

INTRODUCTION: The aim of this study was to evaluate disease control and 
functional outcomes of mastoid obliteration using bone substitute material in 
cholesteatoma surgery.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 81 adult patients 
operated on between March 2014 and March 2023. All patients underwent mastoid 
obliteration using bone substitute material either during canal wall down 
cholesteatoma surgery with external auditory canal reconstruction or for 
rehabilitation of a pre-existing mastoid cavity. Follow-up at 18 months, 
including otoscopy, audiometry, CT scan and/or MRI, was available for all 
patients. The STAMCO classification was used to describe disease extension. The 
mean follow-up duration was 34.5 months (median 28 months; range: 18-112 
months).
RESULTS: At the last follow-up visit, 80 patients had a healthy and healed 
tympanic membrane, while one patient had a persistent perforation. There was no 
significant difference in mean air conduction pure-tone average before and after 
surgery (51.8 ± 18.8 dB vs 53.1 ± 21.4 dB, respectively; Wilcoxon test, n=77). 
Mean air and bone conduction thresholds, as well as the air-bone gap, remained 
unchanged after surgery. Audiometric outcomes were not influenced by STAMCO 
classification or by the type of surgery (primary versus revision) in this 
series. One patient presented with residual cholesteatoma, and no cases of 
recurrent cholesteatoma were observed.
CONCLUSION: Mastoid obliteration using bone substitute in cholesteatoma surgery 
achieves favorable anatomical outcomes, a low complication rate, and 
preservation of hearing. In the absence of a control group, these results 
support the technique's safety rather than a demonstrated reduction in 
recurrence, and comparative studies are needed to confirm its benefit on disease 
control.

Following myocardial infarction (MI), splenic humoral immune responses 
contribute to cardiac injury and repair, yet the cardiac signals that govern 
these responses remain poorly defined. Here, we identified ischemic 
cardiomyocytes as a source of interleukin 30 (IL-30; the interleukin 27 p28 
subunit) and investigated its role in heart-spleen communication. In mice, 
cardiomyocyte-specific IL-30 deficiency enhanced splenic germinal center 
responses and signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) 
phosphorylation. This deficiency increased myocardial IgG deposition, TNF-α 
expression in Fc gamma receptor III-positive macrophages, and cardiomyocyte 
apoptosis, while impairing cardiac function and aggravating ventricular 
remodeling. Recombinant IL-30 suppressed splenic germinal center responses and 
STAT1 phosphorylation and improved cardiac function. The effects of recombinant 
IL-30 on germinal center responses and cardiac function were abolished by B 
cell-specific deletion of glycoprotein 130 (gp130). Furthermore, no detectable 
improvement in cardiac function was observed following IL-30 treatment in 
splenectomized mice. In patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction 
(STEMI; n = 75), lower circulating IL-30 levels were associated with higher 
peripheral IgG-positive B cell frequencies. In a separate longitudinal cohort of 
247 patients with STEMI, low circulating IL-30 was independently associated with 
adverse left ventricular remodeling at 6 months (odds ratio, 4.44; 95% 
confidence interval, 2.16-9.80; P< 0.001). Circulating IL-30 discriminated 
patients with and without adverse remodeling with an area under the receiver 
operating characteristic curve of 0.738. These findings identify 
cardiomyocyte-derived IL-30 as an endogenous regulator of heart-spleen 
communication that restrains splenic humoral responses and limits adverse 
cardiac remodeling after MI.

[Physical activity and mental health in childhood and adolescence: a summary of 
the evidence from three national studies].

[Article in German; Abstract available in German from the publisher]

Reiß F(1), Niessner C(2), Kaman A(1), Volk C(2), Behn S(1), Napp AK(1), 
Hanssen-Doose A(3), Woll A(2), Ravens-Sieberer U(4).

Author information:
(1)Zentrum für Psychosoziale Medizin, Klinik für Kinder- und Jugendpsychiatrie, 
-psychotherapie und -psychosomatik, Forschungssektion "Child Public Health", 
Universitätsklinikum Hamburg-Eppendorf, Hamburg, Deutschland.
(2)Institut für Sport und Sportwissenschaft, Karlsruher Institut für 
Technologie, Karlsruhe, Deutschland.
(3)Institut für Bewegungserziehung und Sport, Pädagogische Hochschule Karlsruhe 
, Karlsruhe, Deutschland.
(4)Zentrum für Psychosoziale Medizin, Klinik für Kinder- und Jugendpsychiatrie, 
-psychotherapie und -psychosomatik, Forschungssektion "Child Public Health", 
Universitätsklinikum Hamburg-Eppendorf, Hamburg, Deutschland.

Young people are increasingly burdened by global crises. Physical activity (PA) 
is considered a key factor for mental health; however, for Germany, an 
integrated synthesis of population-based evidence is still lacking. The aim of 
this narrative overview is therefore to consolidate current findings on the 
association between PA and mental health.The analysis draws on three 
population-based studies conducted as module or follow-up studies in cooperation 
with the KiGGS study: the MoMo study (motor performance/physical activity), the 
BELLA and COPSY studies (mental health), and the COMO study (interdisciplinary 
integration). Nationwide representative samples of children and adolescents aged 
4 to 23 years were examined using validated instruments to assess PA and mental 
health. Findings are synthesised narratively and reported by type of activity, 
age, sex and socioeconomic status.Overall, positive associations between PA and 
mental health are observed. Higher levels of PA are associated with fewer 
psychological problems and higher health-related quality of life. There is 
evidence of protective effects, particularly in relation to leisure-time sport, 
both within and outside sports clubs. Self-reported PA shows stronger 
associations with well-being than objectively measured PA. Children from 
socioeconomically disadvantaged families are less likely to be physically active 
and experience more mental health problems. Social integration and sense of 
competence in sport have been identified as further key psychosocial factors. PA 
can therefore be considered an important resource for promoting mental health. 
There is a need to promote low-threshold access to physical activity programmes 
that specifically target disadvantaged groups in order to reduce health 
inequalities.

Understanding Past and Present Surgical Registries for Patients with

INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Registries following patients who undergo surgery 
for uterovaginal pelvic organ prolapse provide real-world postoperative 
evidence. We aimed to identify characteristics of successful registries that 
could be used to develop a sustainable global registry for these patients.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review of the literature to identify existing 
and past registries on the surgical management of primary uterovaginal pelvic 
organ prolapse. Once identified, key characteristics of the registries were 
collected, and consensus statements about future efforts to develop a global 
registry were created. These statements were evaluated through a modified Delphi 
process.
RESULTS: One hundred and eleven articles were identified and reviewed, published 
from 17 registries. Consensus was achieved for the following three statements: 
surgeons treating patients for uterovaginal pelvic organ prolapse should 
standardize baseline, surgical, and postoperative objective and subjective data 
to facilitate the development of a universal registry; urogynecological surgeons 
and researchers should seek to minimize cost and maximize feasibility by 
automating data collection through emerging 
technologies; urogynecological surgeons and researchers should seek the input of 
key stakeholders to iteratively improve the registry and ensure that 
it remains evidence-based and current.
CONCLUSIONS: Understanding past and present surgical registries prepares us for 
the multifaceted efforts that will be required to develop a sustainable, global 
registry for the surgical management of uterovaginal pelvic organ prolapse.

In Situ Tracking of Se Vacancy-Promoted Surface Reconstruction of NiCoSe2 into 
NiCoOOH during Alkaline Oxygen Evolution.

Singha Roy S(1)(2)(3), Muraleedharan A(3)(4), Vishesh V(3)(4), Koka Ruparani 
V(3)(4), C P FD(3)(4), Kundu S(1)(2)(3).

Author information:
(1)Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research (AcSIR) , Ghaziabad201002, 
India.
(2)Electrochemical Process Engineering (EPE) Division, CSIR-Central 
Electrochemical Research Institute (CECRI), Karaikudi, Tamil Nadu630003, India.
(3)Muthayammal College of Arts and Science , Rasipuram, Tamil Nadu637408, India.
(4)Centre for Education (CFE), CSIR-Central Electrochemical Research Institute 
(CECRI), Karaikudi, Tamil Nadu630003, India.

Understanding the dynamic surface reconstruction of precatalyst materials during 
the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is a forefront area of research for 
designing and studying effective electrocatalysts. Here, we report the 
deliberate engineering of Se vacancies in NiCoSe2 via a facile NaBH4 reduction 
strategy and systematically investigate how anion vacancies govern surface 
reconstruction behavior under alkaline OER conditions. The presence of Se 
vacancies is confirmed via EPR spectroscopy and ICP-MS analysis. Cyclic 
voltammetry and in situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy during the 
electrochemical activation process reveal that the vacancy-enriched NiCoSe2-x 
undergoes faster and more extensive structural reconstruction than pristine 
NiCoSe2. Quasi in situ ATR-FTIR and Raman spectroscopy track the dynamic 
evolution of NiCoOOH during anodic polarization, providing direct spectroscopic 
evidence for the Se vacancy-promoted NiCoOOH active phase generation with 
abundant Ni-O-Co synergy. Evaluation of electrochemical surface area and 
turnover frequency establishes that the generation of abundant Ni-O-Co synergy 
in NiCoSe2-x simultaneously increases the density of accessible active sites and 
enhances the intrinsic activity per site. Consequently, the NiCoSe2-x 
precatalyst delivers significantly improved OER performance relative to bare 
NiCoSe2, along with high Faradaic selectivity and long-term stability. 
Post-stability characterizations confirm bulk structural and morphological 
reconstruction driven by Se vacancies and thus highlight the complete 
utilization of the available catalytic sites. This work provides a fundamental 
mechanistic framework linking anion vacancy engineering, surface reconstruction 
kinetics/mechanism tracking, and intrinsic OER activity enhancement in 
bimetallic chalcogenide precatalysts, offering rationalized design principles 
for next-generation earth-abundant OER catalysts.

A tape-based intestinal chip co-culture model for assessing anti-inflammatory 
activity of chitosan oligosaccharides.

Yan J(1), Wu X(2), Gao J(1), Su W(1), Ren X(1), Kong F(1), Song S(1).

Author information:
(1)SKL of Marine Food Processing & Safety Control, National Engineering Research 
Center of Seafood, Collaborative Innovation Center of Seafood Deep Processing, 
National & Local Joint Engineering Laboratory for Marine Bioactive 
Polysaccharide Development and Application, Liaoning Key Laboratory of Food 
Nutrition and Health, School of Food Science and Technology, Dalian Polytechnic 
University, Dalian 116034, China. songs1008@163.com.
(2)College of Pharmacy, Ningxia Medical University, Yinchuan 750004, P.R. China.

Intestinal inflammation is a central pathological process in gastrointestinal 
diseases, yet conventional in vitro models poorly reproduce epithelial-immune 
interactions, and accessible platforms for rapid anti-inflammatory screening 
remain lacking. Here, a low-cost, high-throughput tape-based intestinal chip 
co-culturing Caco-2 epithelial cells and RAW264.7 macrophages under dynamic flow 
was applied to approximate the epithelial-macrophage interface of the intestinal 
wall and to evaluate the anti-inflammatory activity of chitosan oligosaccharides 
(COS). Three COS fractions (COS1, COS2, COS3; 3.6, 2.7, and 0.8 kDa) prepared 
from Antarctic krill shell exhibited molecular weight-dependent transepithelial 
permeability, with COS3 showing the highest permeability. All COS fractions 
significantly suppressed LPS-induced NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation, macrophage 
morphological activation, and the production of NO, IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6, with 
the low-molecular-weight COS3 showing the strongest effects under equal-mass 
dosing. Targeted metabolomics identified four candidate marker metabolites 
(proline, asparagine, GTP, and α-ketoglutaric acid) that were elevated by LPS 
and partially restored by COS treatment, providing a metabolic signature for 
rapid evaluation of anti-inflammatory efficacy. These findings establish the 
integrated tape-based chip-metabolomics strategy as an accessible platform for

Velioglu Tosuner Z(1), Kurudayioglu Ş(2), Aydinlioglu Z(2), Ozturk Urek R(3).

Author information:

Agro-industrial-residues, such as potato peel waste (PPW), constitute a 
substantial portion of the waste stream and offer significant opportunities for 
valorization within circular bioeconomy frameworks. In this study, a 
laboratory-scale solid-state fermentation (SSF) process for biosurfactant 
production using fresh or dried PPW as renewable substrates was optimized with 
Saccharomyces cerevisiae BY4742. A Box-Behnken design was implemented to 
optimize peel amount, initial pH, and incubation time, targeting enhanced 
surface tension reduction. Under optimized conditions (10 g fresh PPW, pH 5.25, 
5th day), the biosurfactant reduced surface tension to 30.12 ± 0.32 mN/m and 
demonstrated a high emulsification index (51.35 ± 0.49%), low critical micelle 
concentration (1.1 ± 0.09 mg/mL), strong oil spreading activity (6.3 ± 0.05 cm), 
and positive drop collapse results. Partial structural characterization by 
FTIR,1H-NMR and TGA/DTG was consistent with a heterogeneous surface-active 
biopolymeric fraction, supporting its robust functional properties. The obtained 
biosurfactant maintained remarkable stability across wide ranges of pH, 
temperature, and salinity, while achieving an oil removal efficiency of 
91.37 ± 0.89%, indicating its strong potential for bioremediation applications. 
Notably, the SSF platform enabled the simultaneous production of a 
surface-active fraction and extracellular amylase activity, highlighting the 
potential of PPW-based SSF as a resource-efficient approach for producing 
value-added bioproducts.

Anabaena, a multicellular model for cyanobacterial cell biology and 
biotechnology.

Flores E(1), Luque I(1), López-Igual R(1).

Author information:
(1)Instituto de Bioquímica Vegetal y Fotosíntesis, CSIC and Universidad de 
Sevilla, Seville, Spain.

Heterocyst-forming cyanobacteria (order Nostocales) are a monophyletic group of 
organisms that grow as filaments usually made of dozens to hundreds of cells 
(termed vegetative cells) that can perform oxygenic photosynthesis. Under 
combined nitrogen deficiency, some cells in the filament differentiate into 
N2-fixing heterocysts, which do not produce oxygen and, indeed, keep a microoxic 
environment appropriate for the expression and functioning of the N2-fixing 
enzyme, nitrogenase. Thus, in the diazotrophic filament, oxygenic photosynthesis 
and N2 fixation are segregated into two different cell types, vegetative cells 
and heterocysts, which require intercellular molecular exchange to feed each 
other with fixed nitrogen and reduced carbon, respectively. The current 
understanding of heterocyst biology, including regulation of heterocyst 
differentiation, which also involves intercellular signaling, is the result of 
studying mainly a few strains of the genus Anabaena. Here, we review the 
classical studies that established Anabaena as a model for the Nostocales and 
clarified the basics of N2 fixation in these organisms. Then, we show how 
molecular genetics came into the scene and how it was complemented by genomic 
analysis. This, together with the introduction of modern cell biology 
approaches, led to a renewed understanding of cellular differentiation and 
unraveled a system for intercellular communication that is unique in the 
biological world. In turn, the new accumulated knowledge on Anabaena physiology 
and genetics makes these organisms an excellent system for the development of 
new synthetic biology tools that will be crucial for their use in biotechnology.

Zonula adherens junctions (zAJs) are spatially proximal to tight junctions 
(TJs), in a superstructure known as the apical junctional complex (AJC). A key 
component of the AJC is a circumferential ring of F-actin, but how actomyosin

The role of cell growth rate on accumulation of the mitotic cyclin Cdc13 in 
fission yeast.

Vandal SE(1), Rezaee S(2), Nieto C(2), Flynn MJ(1), Singh A(2), Moseley JB(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biochemistry and Cell Biology, The Geisel School of Medicine at

Eukaryotic cells control their size by coordinating growth and division. Fission 
yeast divide at a reproducible cell size due to regulated activation of the 
cyclin-dependent kinase Cdk1. The nuclear concentration of mitotic cyclin Cdc13 
increases in a time-dependent manner to promote Cdk1 activation as cells grow. 
Here, we show that interphase Cdc13 is stable against degradation and nuclear 
export but is diluted by cell growth. Low glucose reduced the cell growth rate 
but not the time-dependent accumulation of Cdc13. Uncoupling the rates of cell 
growth and Cdc13 accumulation resulted in higher concentrations of nuclear Cdc13 
despite reduced cell size. This change coincided with reduced activating 
phosphorylation of Cdk1-T167. Mathematical modeling and experiments showed that 
cells maintain size homeostasis under these conditions. In contrast to low 
glucose, poor nitrogen reduced both cell growth rate and Cdc13 accumulation 
rate. Therefore, Cdc13 accumulation is independent of cell growth rate but can 
be altered by nutrient-specific mechanisms.

A transcriptional repressor co-regulatory network integrates iron homeostasis

Mehta K(1)(2), Kajal(1)(2), Goar H(1), Bamniya B(1)(2), Sarkar D(1)(2).

(1)CSIR-Institute of Microbial Technology, Chandigarh, India.

A hallmark of Mycobacterium tuberculosis survival and proliferation within the 
host is attributable to the effective stress response of the pathogen against 
hostile environmental conditions. Although controlled iron (Fe) uptake and 
maintenance of Fe homeostasis are closely associated with intracellular survival 
of mycobacteria, the underlying mechanism that accounts for the interdependence 
of mycobacterial Fe regulation and oxidative stress response remains unknown. In 
this study, we discovered that Fe accumulation connects intra-bacterial redox 
environment via the phoP locus. Gene expression analyses coupled with genetic, 
biochemical, and transcriptomic studies uncover a distinct mechanism that 
utilizes Lsr2 and the virulence regulator PhoP to modulate transcriptional 
control of the major Fe storage protein-encoding gene bfrB. Remarkably, 
regulated expression of bfrB determines bacterial tolerance to oxidative stress 
and its intracellular survival. Although both regulators could independently 
influence bfrB expression, the most fundamental insights are derived from the 
inhibition of Lsr2 binding at the bfrB regulatory region of the phoP-KO mutant 
strain owing to Lsr2-PhoP protein-protein interactions. Building on these 
results, we proposed a model suggesting how Lsr2-PhoP interaction, or lack 
thereof, contributes to stress-specific regulation of bfrB expression.

to oxidative stress response, an essential pathogenic determinant of M. 
tuberculosis.IMPORTANCEWhile the availability of Fe remains essential for 
Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection and replication of the pathogen in human 
macrophages, Fe may be harmful as it catalyzes the generation of toxic reactive 
oxygen species from products of aerobic respiration to induce oxidative stress. 
Although interdependence of mycobacterial Fe regulation and oxidative stress 
response has been reported, the mechanism connecting Fe acquisition and 
oxidative stress response is yet to be fully understood. Results reported in 
this study identify and elaborate on a new mechanism of regulation of expression 
of the major mycobacterial Fe storage protein, which determines bacterial 
tolerance to oxidative stress and impacts intracellular survival of the 
pathogen. We demonstrate that the virulence-associated phoP locus controls Fe 
accumulation and contributes to the intra-bacterial redox environment. The 
results uncover a distinctly different transcriptional control mechanism of the 
major Fe storage protein requiring a co-repressor-dependent regulatory circuit, 
including nucleoid-associated protein Lsr2 and the virulence regulator PhoP. 
Together, these results unveil a unique mechanism of stress-specific gene 
expression, which integrates Fe homeostasis to oxidative stress response, an 
essential pathogenic determinant of M. tuberculosis.

Finerenone: A Non-Steroidal Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist and Its 
Emerging Role in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.

Fischer KG(1), Beavers CJ(2).

Author information:
(1)Ascension Texas; Austin, Texas; Department of Pharmacy.
(2)University of Kentucky College of Pharmacy.

Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents the interconnected 
pathophysiology of metabolic risk factors, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and 
cardiovascular disease, leading to multiorgan dysfunction and elevated adverse 
outcomes. Overactivation of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), via 
aldosterone-dependent and ligand-independent pathways, drives inflammation, 
fibrosis, and oxidative stress and facilitates CKM progression. Finerenone is a 
selective non-steroidal MR antagonist (nsMRA) that exhibits high MR affinity, 
has balanced cardiac and renal distribution, and minimal off-target steroidal 
effects, which make it mechanistically different from steroidal MRAs. Large 
phase 3 trials such as FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD in type 2 diabetes with CKD, 
and FINEARTS-HF in heart failure (HF) with a left ventricular ejection fraction 
(LVEF) > 40%, demonstrated consistent cardiorenal benefits. The prespecified 
FINE-HEART pooled analysis showed finerenone reduced all-cause mortality (HR 
0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.99), HF hospitalizations (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.75-0.92), and 
the kidney composite outcome (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90), with benefits 
consistent across CKM components and background therapies including 
sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors. Recent data from FIND-CKD 
extend utility to non-diabetic CKD. Various guidelines incorporate finerenone as 
an additive therapy for patients with persistent albuminuria on maximal 
renin-angiotensin system inhibition (RASi) + SGLT2i. This review summarizes the 
MR pathophysiology in CKM syndrome, compares the mechanisms of non-steroidal 
versus steroidal MRAs, synthesizes clinical trial evidence, safety, and 
guideline-directed place in therapy, addresses implementation barriers, 
including cost, and outlines future research directions. Finerenone may fill a 
critical gap in multimodal CKM management, enabling comprehensive pillar-based 
therapy to mitigate residual cardiorenal risk.

Elliott G(1)(2), Kowal J(2), Zybenkov A(2)(3), Pinhal-Enfield G(1)(2)(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Neuroscience and Cell Biology, Robert Wood Johnson Medical

(3)Department of Neuroscience and Cell Biology, Anatomical Association, Robert

Team-based learning (TBL) is widely used in health professions education; 
however, its role within integrated curriculum redesigns serving increasingly 
heterogeneous student populations remains less well understood. Grounded in a 
conceptual framework emphasizing preparation, individual accountability, 
collaborative knowledge construction, immediate feedback, and application, this 
study evaluated TBL within a redesigned graduate-level gross anatomy course. 
Four cohorts (2022-2025) were analyzed: Two completed the original lecture-based 
curriculum and two completed a redesigned curriculum incorporating TBL, required 
human donor dissection laboratories, formative assessments, and team-based 
examinations. A standardized Individual Performance Score (IPS) enabled 
comparison across cohorts. Grade distributions, item-level psychometric indices, 
early assessment predictive value, and student perceptions were also evaluated. 
Overall IPS differences were not significant (H = 6.50, p = 0.089); however, the 
redesigned curriculum was associated with a higher proportion of A grades 
(+11.7%, p = 0.012) and differences in performance distribution (U = 16,143.5, 
p = 0.043). TBL-aligned items demonstrated stronger discrimination and 
point-biserial correlations, while early practical performance strongly 
predicted overall outcomes. Student perceptions were favorable, with 90.8% 
endorsing TBL activities and 94.1% reporting that team-based examinations 
supported understanding. Embedding TBL within an integrated graduate anatomy 
curriculum may support high achievement, assessment quality, and collaborative 
learning. However, the historical cohort design, concurrent admissions changes, 
and multifaceted curricular redesign limit causal attribution to TBL alone. 
These findings support positioning TBL as one component of a broader curricular 
framework rather than an isolated intervention.

Psychological needs in individuals with lower limb amputation: a narrative 
review of evidence for clinical practice across the rehabilitation continuum.

Walczak E(1), Dervaux B(1), Dumortier M(1), Bassement J(1).

Author information:
(1)Medical Care and Rehabilitation Department, Hospital Center of Valenciennes,

PURPOSE: To synthesize the psychological needs of individuals undergoing 
lower-limb amputation (LLA) and their association with overall adjustment across 
the rehabilitation continuum, in order to propose clinical recommendations 
spanning the entire continuum of care.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A narrative review was conducted in accordance with the 
SANRA criteria, using MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, and PsycArticles. We identified 
peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and July 2025 that met the 
following criteria: original research; focused on individuals with LLA; examined 
psychological, emotional, or psychosocial dimensions throughout the 
rehabilitation continuum care journey; studies that explored how psychological 
factors influence overall adjustment; written in English.
RESULTS: A total of 28 quantitative and 12 qualitative studies were included. 
Individuals undergoing LLA report significant psychological distress from limb 
threat to long-term rehabilitation care, including anxiety, depression, body 
image disturbance, impairment in social life and sexuality, low balance 
confidence, and cognitive impairment.
CONCLUSIONS: Psychological distress is associated with poorer overall 
adjustment, confirming that mental health plays a key role in adaptation. The 
integration of structured psychological screening and personalized interventions 
targeting psychological and psychosocial needs may be beneficial throughout the 
rehabilitation continuum. Further studies are needed to assess the applicability 
for healthcare providers, and patient benefits of these recommendations.

Plain Language Summary: Lower-limb loss is a life-changing event associated with 
substantial emotional challenges that play a crucial role in overall adjustment 
throughout the rehabilitation continuum, from limb threat to lifelong 
rehabilitation care.During the initial rehabilitation episode, screen for 
anxiety before surgery and implement tailored counseling, emotional support, and 
non-pharmacological anxiety-management interventions.Following surgery, screen 
for depression, strengthen social support, and promote acceptance through 
Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)-based interventions.During prosthetic 
training and ongoing rehabilitation, support psychological adjustment by 
monitoring mood, addressing prosthesis-related fears, and promoting active 
coping through cognitive-behavioral interventions.
