Vertical Jump Performance as a Functional Indicator of Bone Health in Older 
Adults.

Huang H(1), Liu Z(1), Leng B(1), Ge X(2), Tang C(2), He Y(1), Sun J(1), Zhang 
C(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Physical Education and Sports, Central China Normal University, 
Wuhan, China; and.
(2)School of Kinesiology, Beijing Sport University, Beijing, China.

Huang, H, Liu, Z, Leng, B, Ge, X, Tang, C, He, Y, Sun, J, and Zhang, C. Vertical 
jump performance as a functional indicator of bone health in older adults. J 
Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-Mechanical loading generated during 
dynamic lower-limb tasks is believed to be critical for skeletal maintenance, 
but the relative importance of different vertical jump performance metrics for 
bone health has not been established. The purpose of this study was to 
systematically evaluate the relationship between vertical jump performance and 
bone health in community-dwelling older adults. Sixty healthy older adults (17 
men) completed countermovement jump (CMJ) and squat jump (SJ) assessments, from 
which phase-specific power and net impulse metrics normalized to body weight, 
and stretch-shortening cycle utilization were calculated. Bone outcomes 
including intertrochanteric (IT) geometry, strength indices, and hip and spine 
bone mineral density (BMD) were assessed using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. 
Associations were examined using covariate-adjusted linear regression models. 
Higher CMJ propulsive impulse was positively associated with IT cross-sectional 
area (standardized β = 0.219, p = 0.033) and cross-sectional moment of inertia 
(standardized β = 0.194, p = 0.022). Countermovement jump and SJ propulsive 
impulse, SJ and CMJ peak propulsive power all showed positive associations with 
IT section modulus (standardized β range 0.195-0.240, all p < 0.05). No jump 
performance metrics were associated with buckling ratio or hip or spine BMD (all 
p > 0.05). Stretch-shortening cycle utilization was not associated with any bone 
outcomes (all p > 0.05). In conclusion, in older adults, vertical jump 
performance metrics, particularly CMJ propulsive impulse, are associated with 
hip bone geometry and strength. These findings suggest CMJ assessment may serve 
as a practical functional indicator reflecting mechanical loading relevant to 
hip bone strength.

Cyclopalladation to form palladium pincer complexes is typically performed at

Jha SK(1)(2), Srivastava P(1)(2), Krause B(2), Rohini R(1).

Author information:
(1)Indian Institute of Technology Jammu, India. rani.rohini@iitjammu.ac.in.

Single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNT) are efficient materials for

advantageous for flexible thermoelectric applications.

Guo Z(1), Chen W(1)(2), Xie J(1)(2), Pu Y(3), Yang H(3), Mu Q(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Neuromodulation and Neuroimaging, Beijing Anzhen Nanchong

(3)Department of Medical Imaging, Beijing Anzhen Nanchong Hospital of Capital

mild cognitive impairment; however, conventional single-site stimulation

alterations underlying the condition. This study investigated the clinical 
efficacy and neurobiological modulatory mechanisms of multisite versus 
single-site repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation in patients with mild 
cognitive impairment. A total of 101 patients with mild cognitive impairment

modulation of structural integrity, spontaneous neural activity, and functional 
connectivity within core cognitive brain networks. These mechanisms reflect 
repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation-induced synaptic plasticity and 
neurovascular coupling, driving network-level neural repair and providing a

Lau Y(1), Zabihi S(1)(2), Hartmann M(1), Mathlin G(1), Banerjee S(3), Marouf

(3)Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, University of Nottingham,

OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence of diabetes mellitus and its associations 
with hospitalisation and mortality in adults with multiple sclerosis (MS) and 
matched controls.
METHODS: Using English primary care data from the Clinical Practice Research 
Datalink, linked to hospital and mortality records, we matched adults with MS 
with up to 10 controls without MS by age, sex and practice. We excluded 
individuals with pre-existing diabetes mellitus. Outcomes included all-cause 
hospitalisation (number and duration) and mortality. We used Poisson, negative 
binomial, linear and Cox proportional hazards models, adjusting for demographic 
and socioeconomic factors, with interaction terms for ethnicity, deprivation and 
urbanity.

diabetes mellitus (adjusted incidence rate ratio = 1.16, 95% confidence interval 
1.11-1.21). Among people with MS, incident diabetes mellitus was associated with 
higher hospitalisation rates (adjusted incidence rate ratio = 1.52, 1.42-1.64), 
longer hospitalisation duration (median 12 vs. 2 days) and increased mortality 
(adjusted hazard ratio = 1.41, 1.31-1.49). Similar patterns were observed among 
controls. The association between diabetes mellitus and increased 
hospitalisation was stronger in rural areas among those with MS and in White 
groups among controls.
INTERPRETATION: MS was associated with a higher incidence of diabetes mellitus, 
which was in turn associated with greater hospitalisation and mortality. These 
findings may support consideration of equitable screening, prevention and 
management of diabetes mellitus in people living with MS.

Colophony Detection in Military Footwear and Its Implications for the Management 
of Allergic Contact Dermatitis in Soldiers.

Elazar Avital O(1), Berman T(1), Abuhasira S(2), Chechik Y(1).

Author information:
(1)Israel Defense Forces, Medical Corps, Tel Hashomer, Ramat Gan, Israel.
(2)The Dina Recanati School of Medicine, Reichman University, Herzliya, Israel.

INTRODUCTION: Allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) of the feet is an occupational 
problem in military populations and may affect soldiers' ability to meet 
occupational and operational requirements, particularly in roles requiring 
prolonged use of standard military footwear. Colophony (rosin) is a recognized 
contact allergen implicated in shoe dermatitis. In the Israel Defense Forces 
(IDF), standard-issue military boots are considered colophony-free based on 
manufacturer declarations.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This investigation was conducted as a quality-improvement 
initiative combined with policy implementation within the IDF Medical Corps. 
Following a recurring clinical pattern of suspected footwear-related ACD in 
which colophony sensitization was identified during specialist evaluation, 
laboratory analyses were performed in June and August 2025 at an independent 
analytical laboratory. The initial assessment included 2 commonly issued boot 
pairs. The expanded assessment included 9 boot pairs representing footwear types 
issued by the IDF at the time of testing and multiple manufacturers. Four 
samples were obtained from each pair from internal regions selected to 
correspond to the recurring clinical distribution of dermatitis. Samples 
underwent solvent extraction, methylation, and quantitative gas chromatographic 
analysis according to Methods for the Determination of Hazardous Substances 
(MDHS) 83/3. Before formal footwear testing, a preliminary feasibility 
assessment was performed to confirm extraction of colophony from the footwear 
matrix; a full footwear-specific validation was not performed. Individual-level 
clinical data and case counts were not systematically collected.
RESULTS: In the initial laboratory assessment, 8 samples were analyzed from 2 
boot pairs. Five contained quantifiable colophony concentrations above the limit 
of quantification (3.0 µg/g), ranging from 4.73 to 12.94 µg/g. One additional 
sample contained 2.1 µg/g, above the limit of detection but below the limit of 
quantification, and 2 samples were below the limit of detection (<1 µg/g). In 
the expanded assessment, all 36 samples from 9 boot pairs were below the limit 
of detection (<1 µg/g). Clinically, a recurring pattern of dermatitis associated 
with standard military footwear was observed, including improvement during 
footwear exemption and recurrence following return to standard boots. Colophony 
sensitization was identified on patch testing during specialist evaluation. 
These findings contributed to the development of a structured, stepwise footwear 
replacement protocol.
CONCLUSIONS: Colophony was detected in selected military footwear samples, 
although this finding was not reproduced in the expanded assessment. In soldiers 
with suspected footwear-related ACD, laboratory findings should be interpreted 
in conjunction with clinical history and patch test results. A structured, 
stepwise management protocol can provide individualized care while supporting 
continued service in footwear-dependent roles and maintaining operational 
standards.

Physical Health Crises Preceding Suicide from Late Midlife Through Older Age: 
Illnesses, Contexts, and Age-Group Differences.

Choi NG(1), Marti CN(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Social Work, The University of Texas at Austin, Austin, Texas, USA.

OBJECTIVES: To examine how physical health (PH) crises preceding suicide differ 
from late midlife (50-64 years) to older age (≥65 years).
METHODS: Using 2022-2023 National Violent Death Reporting System-Restricted 
Access Data, we analyzed suicide decedents aged ≥ 50 with a PH problem as a

autonomy, dependence, perceived burdensomeness, and care transitions.

illnesses and contexts differed from late midlife through older age.
CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Healthcare professionals should assess suicide risk when 
older adults experience serious or worsening PH problems. Suicide prevention 
approaches should adopt collaborative safety planning including both health

Kilpatrick M(1)(2)(3), Hutchinson A(1)(2)(3)(4), Manias E(5), Bouchoucha 
S(1)(2)(3)(6).

Author information:
(1)School of Nursing and Midwifery, Deakin University, Geelong, VIC, Australia.
(2)Centre for Innovation in Infectious Disease and Immunology Research (CIIDIR), 
Deakin University, Geelong, VIC, Australia.
(3)Centre for Quality & Patient Safety Research, Institute of Health

Parents play an essential role in their child's care, including infection 
prevention and control (IPC), during hospitalisation. Despite this, their role 
in IPC is not clearly defined. This study explored how parents of children 
admitted to an Australian tertiary paediatric hospital understand and 
participate in IPC initiatives. A qualitative descriptive study was conducted in 
oncology/haematology, adolescent, and surgical wards, involving semi-structured 
interviews with 24 parents and 2 mature minors. Data were analysed thematically 
using the Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices model as a deductive framework. 
Three themes were derived, highlighting parents' engagement in IPC. Heightened 
parental vigilance involved maintaining hygiene, monitoring their child's 
condition, educating children, and seeking clarification when clinical 
communication or staff practice was inconsistent. Balancing infection risk with 
daily life involved recognising the ubiquity of infections, managing community 
exposures, and weighing risk against their child's need for a normal life. 
Hospital care was seen as both a risk and a necessity, emphasising reliance on 
treatment and concerns about potential infection exposure. Parents' IPC efforts 
were ongoing and adapted to the realities of home, community exposure, and 
hospital admission. Their role in managing infection risk highlights the 
importance of integrating parents into IPC in paediatric care.

Analytical Strategies for the Identification and Differentiation of Positional 
Isomers of N-(2-Methoxybenzyl)-2-(trimethoxyphenyl)ethanamines by Chromatography 
and Mass Spectrometry.

Kupriyanova OV(1)(2), Shevyrin VA(3).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Fundamental Medicine and Biology, Kazan (Volga Region) Federal 
University, Kazan, Russian Federation.
(2)Kazan State Medical University, Kazan, Russian Federation.
(3)Institute of Chemical Engineering, Ural Federal University, Ekaterinburg, 
Russian Federation.

N-(2-Methoxybenzyl)-2-(trimethoxyphenyl)ethanamines (TMPEA-NBOMe series) 
constitute a relatively new group of synthetic compounds, some of which are 
known as psychotomimetics on the illicit drug market and are subject to legal 
control in many countries (e.g., 
N-(2-methoxybenzyl)-2-(3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl)ethanamine, also known as 
Mescaline-NBOMe). Like their 2,5-dimethoxy analogues (25X-NBOMe series), they 
act as agonists at 5-HT2A receptors and affect behavioral and cognitive 
functions, albeit to a lesser extent. When the relative arrangement of the three 
methoxy groups on the phenylethyl moiety is altered (positional isomers), 
compounds of the TMPEA-NBOMe series may lack psychoactive effects and therefore 
possess a legal status. The present study explores the potential of 
chromatography and mass spectrometry to differentiate positional isomers of the 
TMPEA-NBOMe series that differ in the location of the three methoxy groups on 
the phenylethyl moiety and that have different legal statuses. Differentiation 
of positional isomers by gas chromatography was achieved through the separation 
of their trifluoroacetyl derivatives on an HP-5 type column under isothermal 
conditions (230°C). Retention indices were determined for both the underivatized 
TMPEA-NBOMe isomers and their N-trifluoroacetyl derivatives, providing 
additional criteria for identification in GC analysis. It was found that these 
isomers could be distinguished by electron ionization mass spectrometry only 
when mass spectra were recorded for both the underivatized compounds and their 
N-trifluoroacetyl derivatives, since the spectra of the latter exhibited 
substantial differences depending on the position of the three methoxy groups. 
As an alternative, this study proposes a derivatization-free approach using 
high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.

OBJECTIVE: Minor strokes may be associated with early neurological deterioration 
(END) and disabilities. The objective was to investigate the role of serum glial 
fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) levels in predicting END.
METHODS: Data originated from a multicenter cohort study conducted 
prospectively. ΔGFAP was calculated as the ratio of post-thrombolysis GFAP at 
24 h to baseline GFAP. Univariable and multivariable binary logistic regression 
analyses were performed to assess the association between ∆GFAP and END, and a 
nomogram was established to illustrate its predictive value.
RESULTS: END occurred in 20 (7.35%) of the 272 patients with minor stroke who 
underwent intravenous thrombolysis (IVT). Elevated ∆GFAP was independently 
associated with END (OR, 3.50; 95% CI, 1.67 to 7.31; p < 0.001), even after 
adjusting for confounders (adjusted OR, 4.64; 95% CI, 1.86 to 11.54; p < 0.001). 
Furthermore, a model combining ∆GFAP, age, and National Institutes of Health 
Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score at admission demonstrated a good predictive value for 
END (AUC = 0.77; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.89).
INTERPRETATION: ∆GFAP is a strong, independent predictor of END in patients with 
minor strokes. Integrating ∆GFAP, age, and NIHSS score into a prognostic model 
results in a good discriminative ability for predicting END.

Informal Caregiving in Australian Veteran Families: Economic Costs, Caregiver 
Burden, and Health-Related Quality of Life Spillover Effects.

Dang TTH(1)(2), Hu J(1)(2), Tabinga A(1)(2), Mellor R(1)(3), Tuffaha H(4), 
Guindalini C(1)(2), Nghiem SH(5)(6), Van Hooff M(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Veteran Mental Health Initiative, Gallipoli Medical Research, Greenslopes, 
QLD 4120, Australia.
(2)Greenslopes Clinical Unit, The University of Queensland, Greenslopes, QLD 
4120, Australia.
(3)School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences, The University of Queensland, 
St Lucia, QLD 4072, Australia.
(4)Centre for Business and Economics of Health, The University of Queensland, St 
Lucia, QLD 4072, Australia.
(5)School of Public Health, The University of Queensland, Woolloongabba, QLD

(6)Lac Hong University, Bien Hoa, Vietnam.

INTRODUCTION: Military service can have substantial spillover effects on family 
well-being, particularly in households where informal caregiving is required for 
injured or ill veterans. Despite increasing recognition of the importance of 
incorporating caregiver and family outcomes into economic and health service 
evaluations, there is limited empirical evidence quantifying the economic value 
and impacts of informal caregiving among Australian veteran families. This study 
aimed to estimate the economic value of caregiving and examine the impact of 
informal caregiving for injured or ill veterans on caregiver burden and 
health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in Australian veteran families.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In a national cross-sectional survey, 245 adult veteran 
caregivers reported demographics, caregiving intensity and burden (Self-Reported 
Burden Scale [SRB]), HRQoL (Assessment of Quality of Life 8 Dimension 
[AQoL-8D]), and care recipient health (EQ-5D-5L). Costs of informal care were 
estimated using the replacement cost method, with varying wage-rate loadings and 
intensive caregiving thresholds tested for robustness. HRQoL spillovers were 
assessed as relative (associations between caregiver and care recipient HRQoL 
using regression) and absolute (differences between veteran caregivers and 
matched general population caregivers from the Household, Income, and Labour 
Dynamics in Australia Survey). Sensitivity analyses using different matching 
techniques tested the robustness of absolute spillover estimates.
RESULTS: Caregivers provided a median of 30 hours/week, with a median caregiving 
duration of 10 years; nearly half reported needing additional support. The 
caregiver perceived burden was moderate (mean SRB score 5.7). Median weekly 
replacement costs were AU$1,052, translating to a median total cost of 
AU$544,895 per caregiver over their respective caregiving durations. Caregiver 
HRQoL was positively associated with care recipient HRQoL, caregiver age, and 
caregiver postgraduate education, and negatively associated with caregiver 
perceived burden and caregiver number of chronic conditions. Compared with 
general caregivers, veteran caregivers experienced significant HRQoL losses 
(0.135 QALYs/year; 95% CI: -0.17 to -0.10). Findings were robust in sensitivity 
analyses.
CONCLUSION: Informal caregiving for injured or ill veterans is associated with 
substantial economic, caregiving, and HRQoL burdens on family caregivers. 
Incorporating caregiver outcomes into economic evaluations, service planning, 
and policy is essential for a more accurate estimate of intervention value and 
better inform resource allocation decisions across Defence, Veterans' Affairs, 
and national disability and mental health systems.

Spatial organization underpins efficient multistep catalysis in nature, yet 
recreating such organization on living cell surfaces using mild, 
enzyme-compatible and catalytically functional materials remains challenging. 
Here we report an l-cysteine-triggered silk fibroin/lysozyme ultrathin film 
(SLF) that assembles directly on living microbial cells as a catalytic surface 
layer. SLF forms continuous nanoscale coatings on Saccharomyces cerevisiae, 
Gluconobacter oxydans and Escherichia coli Nissle 1917. Spectroscopic and 
structural analyses show that film formation proceeds through electrostatic 
complexation, restricted conformational rearrangement, increased hydrophobic 
exposure, β-sheet-rich ordering and network formation, rather than simple 
deposition. The coating maintains cell viability, enhances stress tolerance and 
provides size-selective permeability for small-molecule transport. SLF also

stepwise process. This work establishes ultrathin protein films as living 
catalytic interfaces for single-cell biocatalyst design and cascade 
biomanufacturing.

Selective Biexciton Generation under Energy-Time Entangled Quantum Light in 
Quantum Dots.

Peng K(1), Tsao C(1), Utzat H(1)(2), Rabani E(1)(2)(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chemistry, University of California, Berkeley, California94720, 
United States.
(2)Materials Sciences Division, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley,

(3)Fritz Haber Center for Molecular Dynamics, Institute of Chemistry and

Quantum light provides opportunities for controlling multiphoton absorption 
beyond the classical limits. Here, we investigate biexciton generation in 
nanocrystal quantum dots driven by energy-time-entangled photon pairs generated 
via spontaneous parametric downconversion. We show that frequency-time 
correlations between pairs of photons increase the population of biexcitons over 
excitons, thereby lending specificity to the excitation of many-body states. By 
employing a three-level model, we demonstrate that biexciton generation depends 
nontrivially on the photon entanglement time and pump bandwidth. We find that 
maximizing efficiency requires an optimally shaped entangled photon field rather 
than simply scaling parameters for a monotonic improvement. Extending to a 
realistic CdSe/CdS core-shell quantum dot containing many excitonic states 
coupled to the quantum field, we demonstrate that increasing the biphoton 
arrival-time entanglement (closer arrival time) enhances constructive pathway 
interference and expands accessible excitation channels while preserving better 
energy-conservation in excitation than classical light when generating 
biexcitons. Furthermore, tuning the time-correlation properties enables 
selective excitation of closely spaced biexciton states. These results establish 
entangled photons as tools for selective excitation and control of higher-order 
excited states in quantum-confined systems.

In solid tumors, communication between dendritic cells (DCs) and T cells is 
impaired by poor immune infiltration and lack of physical contact, limiting 
current immunotherapies. Here, we develop a bispecific immune-bridging platform 
(NVMB) to address these limitations. NVMB consists of tumor cell 
membrane-derived nanovesicles enriched with damage-associated molecular patterns 
(DAMPs) that activate DCs and support T-cell responses. The vesicle surface is 
further functionalized with two aptamers targeting DCs and CD8+ T cells, 
respectively, thereby enhancing their spatial proximity and facilitating

stability with programmable surface functionalization. Mechanistically, NVMB 
promotes DC-T interactions and enhances activation-associated phenotypes in both 
cell populations. In multiple immunocompetent mouse tumor models, NVMB 
suppresses tumor growth, increases intratumoral accumulation of mature DCs and

toward enhanced antitumor immune responses. Moreover, combination with immune

enhances T-cell-mediated clearance of CTCs. These findings support NVMB as a 
stable and modular nanoplatform that integrates immunogenic signaling with 
immune-cell spatial coordination, providing a promising strategy for 
strengthening antitumor immunity and improving the efficacy of existing 
immunotherapies.

Ubiquitous arsenic (As) nanophases in soils are metastable due to the size

Heterogeneous photocatalysis has emerged as a sustainable paradigm for C-N bond 
construction; however, its application has been predominantly confined to 
C(sp2)-N couplings, typically relying on the modulation of nickel catalytic 
cycles. The efficient construction of C(sp3)-N bonds remains a formidable 
challenge due to the high energy barriers of alkyl-metal oxidative addition and 
the inability of traditional semiconductors to orchestrate radical kinetics. 
Herein, we report a robust and versatile C(sp3)-N cross-coupling system enabled 
by a boron-doped nanomaterial (BDN) in synergy with a copper catalyst. The 
strategic incorporation of boron atoms─characterized by their vacant p-orbitals 
and Lewis acidity─into the heptazine framework transcends the role of simple 
light-harvesting, creating chemically active sites that effectively direct 
charge carrier separation and dictate alkyl radical generation. Extensive 
characterization, including quasi-in situ XPS and EPR, confirms that boron 
centers act as efficient electron acceptors, facilitating spatially directed 
charge transfer. This synergistic BDN/Cu platform accommodates an exceptionally 
broad substrate scope, including various N-nucleophiles (amides, sulfonamides, 
heterocycles) and diverse radical precursors (alkanes, alkyl boronic acids, and 
alkyl iodides). Furthermore, the protocol's synthetic utility is underscored by 
its successful extension to C(sp2)-N arylation and its seamless transition to a 
continuous-flow system, achieving gram-scale production. This work provides a 
general strategy for molecular-level engineering of heterogeneous catalysts to 
unlock challenging bond-forming transformations.

Pyrolysis has been widely employed as a pretreatment strategy to remove organic 
components from spent lithium-ion batteries, which is traditionally considered 
to have minimal influence on subsequent metal recovery. By investigating the 
synergistic pyrolysis behavior of organic composites with spent lithium nickel 
cobalt manganese oxide (NCM) cathode materials, it is found that the 
carbonaceous residues formed during pyrolysis can significantly impact the 
microstructure and interfacial chemistry of the cathode material and 
substantially hinder the lithium migration during subsequent low-temperature 
roasting recovery. It is demonstrated that the functional groups released from 
organic matter selectively adsorb on the cathode surface under thermal 
conditions, altering the thermal decomposition pathways of organic components, 
including poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) and the separator, and impeding their 
complete volatilization. This interfacial interaction between PVDF/separator and 
cathode active materials promotes the activation and release of lattice oxygen, 
which further interacts with the partially decomposed carbonaceous species and 
forms oxygen-rich carbonaceous composites. These migrate into the particle 
interior and form dense, conformal coatings along the grain boundaries, yielding 
a physical barrier that obstructs lithium diffusion. During sulfur-assisted 
roasting for selective lithium extraction from ternary black mass, this 
interfacial architecture significantly suppresses lithium release, reducing 
extraction efficiencies to below 80%. In this case, enhancing the oxygen partial 
pressure facilitates complete oxidation of the carbonaceous species, effectively 
removing interfacial barriers and restoring the lithium leaching efficiency to 
96.88%. This work underscores the critical influence of pyrolytic pretreatment 
on the efficiency of pyrometallurgical recycling and suggests reconsideration of 
its presumed inertness.

Self-driving laboratories or autonomous experimentation are emerging as 
transformative platforms for accelerating scientific discovery. Bayesian 
optimization (BO) is among the most widely used machine learning frameworks in 
self-driving laboratories, but these BO-based frameworks rely on predefined 
scalar descriptors to guide experimentation. This limits their ability to handle 
complex phenomena that are difficult to formalize as scalar descriptors. In many 
situations, the determination of an appropriate scalar descriptor can be 
challenging, and may fail to capture subtle yet scientifically important 
phenomena apparent to experts with interdisciplinary insight. This problem is 
particularly pronounced in nanoscale imaging experiments, where strong local 
heterogeneity, multidimensional observations, and emergent physical behaviors 
often cannot be effectively represented using scalar metrics. To overcome this 
limitation, here we develop deep-kernel pairwise learning (DKPL), an approach 
for autonomous microscopy experiments which incorporates human expertise and 
interdisciplinary scientific knowledge into an active learning loop. Instead of 
relying on explicit scalar objectives, DKPL enables experts to directly evaluate 
which experimental output is more promising using interdisciplinary knowledge. 
DKPL then learns a latent utility function from these expert judgments to guide 
subsequent autonomous microscopy experiments. We demonstrate DKPL's performance 
in learning physically meaningful nanoscale structures in lead titanate thin 
films while effectively prioritizing high-information measurement regions using 
an experimental model dataset with known ground truth. We further apply DKPL to 
analyze the character of ferroelectric domain walls, where we find DKPL capable 
of distinguishing between high and low characteristic domain-wall angles in lead 
zirconium titanate, and able to discover both head-to-head and tail-to-tail 
domain-wall character in erbium manganite. Autonomous experiments in mixed-phase 
bismuth ferrite also demonstrate DKPL's ability to link material structure with 
their properties in on-the-fly measurements. This development demonstrates an 
approach to integrate expert knowledge into autonomous microscopy experiments 
across a variety of material systems, and demonstrates a pathway toward 
expert-guided self-driving laboratories capable of addressing scientific 
problems beyond the limits of scalar-metrics-driven learning.

The ultrafast transport dynamics of photogenerated carriers at buried 
semiconductor heterointerfaces govern the operation of modern optoelectronic 
devices, yet direct real-space visualization of in-plane carrier motion at such 
interfaces has remained an outstanding experimental challenge. Here, using 
scanning ultrafast electron microscopy (SUEM), we directly image, with nanometer 
and picosecond spatiotemporal resolution, the in-plane photocarrier dynamics at 
a shallow-buried cadmium sulfide (CdS)/CdSe heterointerface. Upon focused fs 
laser excitation, we observe that electrons and holes undergo picosecond-scale 
radial separation along the interface plane, orthogonal to the built-in electric 
field, forming a ring-shaped charge distribution that persists for nanoseconds.

that this behavior originates from a heterointerface-mediated lateral 
photo-Dember (LPD) effect, driven by the intrinsic mobility asymmetry between 
separated electrons confined in the upper CdS layer and holes confined in the 
bottom CdSe layer. The analysis yields a pronounced difference (∼241.8 cm2/s) in 
subdiffusive transport coefficients between the two carrier populations, 
providing a quantitative measure of the asymmetric in-plane mobility that 
underpins the ultrafast radial charge separation. Our work provides direct 
real-space imaging evidence of the LPD effect in semiconductor heterostructures, 
which holds implications for optoelectronic devices including on-chip terahertz 
emitters, high-speed photodetectors, and photocatalyst architectures. These 
results also establish SUEM as a powerful tool for visualizing and quantifying 
hidden carrier dynamics at buried interfaces with high spatiotemporal 
resolution.

pressure at the object-gripper interface without strain-induced artifacts from 
gripper deformation. Here, we report an ultrathin pressure-gated ionic-contact

Circular dichroism in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (CD-ARPES) is 
widely used to probe orbital angular momentum (OAM) and Berry-curvature-related 
phenomena in two-dimensional quantum materials. However, in many materials, 
conventional micron-scale measurements often average over domains with opposite 
OAM polarization, canceling intrinsic dichroic signals and leaving spectra 
dominated by extrinsic asymmetries arising from photoelectron final-state 
interference. Here, we combine circularly polarized light with NanoARPES to 
achieve spatially resolved CD-ARPES with sub-800 nm resolution. By isolating 
individual domains, this approach enables direct access to the intrinsic OAM 
texture. As a model system, we investigate the K/K' point valley states of the 
quantum spin Hall insulator indenene─a triangular indium monolayer epitaxially 
grown on SiC(0001)─where substrate-induced terraces host alternating valley 
configurations whose dichroic response is averaged out in conventional 
measurements. Terrace-resolved NanoARPES disentangles these contributions, 
allowing direct visualization of oppositely polarized domains and revealing the 
OAM texture associated with a topological band inversion. Our results establish 
spatially resolved CD-ARPES as a robust approach for isolating intrinsic OAM 
contrast by eliminating domain averaging and correcting for extrinsic 
geometry-dependent contributions. This enables direct access to the Berry 
curvature near the Fermi level, providing a powerful probe of the system's 
intrinsic topological character.

Isomers of semiconductor magic-size clusters (MSCs) share the same molecular 
formula but can exhibit distinct optical and electronic properties. Most of the 
reported MSC isomers have been so far limited to cadmium chalcogenides. Herein, 
we report the reversible transformation between two Ag2S MSC isomers synthesized 
in solution under mild reaction conditions. These MSC isomers, which we denote 
as MSC-356 and MSC-306 according to their characteristic excitonic peaks in 
their absorption spectra (356 and 306 nm, respectively), share the same 
inorganic core and organic ligand shell composition confirmed by matrix-assisted 
laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry, Fourier transform 
infrared spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, differential scanning 
calorimetry, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry, powder 
X-ray diffraction, and Raman spectrometry. Reversible transformation between 
these two isomers is thermally induced. The isomerization from MSC-356 to 
MSC-306 follows the first-order kinetics with an activation energy of 233 kJ 
mol-1. It occurs within a narrow temperature window of 54-66 °C, with lower 
temperatures resulting in significant delays in the transition, while the 
reverse conversion from MSC-306 back to MSC-356 requires a significantly higher 
temperature of 110 °C. These two isomers also display different energy band 
structures and electronic properties, with MSC-306 possessing a slightly smaller 
work function (3.85 eV) than MSC-356 (3.92 eV); the former also shows better 
catalytic performance in the hydrogen evolution reaction. The synthetic strategy 
reported here enables the synthesis of environmentally benign silver 
chalcogenide MSC isomers and provides important insights into their growth 
mechanisms and nanoscale structure-property relationships.

In conventional field-effect transistors (FETs), the gate dielectric primarily 
provides electrostatic control of the channel and is engineered to remain 
chemically and electronically inert to ensure stable operation. Emerging 
studies, however, suggest that functional dielectrics integrated with 
two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors can introduce additional physical mechanisms 
that influence device behavior. Here, we investigate AgInP2S6 (AIPS), a high-κ 
van der Waals thiophosphate, as a functional top-gate dielectric in MoS2

the dielectric yet collectively modulate the channel conductance. Optical 
excitation redistributes charge within the dielectric, gradually reconfiguring 
the ionic landscape and altering the interfacial electrostatic potential. The 
resulting conductance exhibits strong temperature dependence. At low 
temperatures (∼0 °C), reduced phonon activity suppresses Ag+ mobility, leading 
to persistent photoconductivity. At elevated temperatures (∼80 °C), thermally 
activated ion hopping accelerates relaxation of the stored state. This 
temperature-dependent retention behavior enables a thermally tunable fading 
memory response, where the persistence of the optically induced conductance 
state can be controlled through ionic dynamics. These results highlight how 
opto-ionic coupling at 2D/dielectric interfaces can introduce 
stimulus-responsive functionality in transistor architectures, providing a 
platform for devices that combine sensing and memory behavior within the gate 
stack.

Optical sensing in semiconductors is traditionally governed by photoconductive, 
photovoltaic, and photogating effects, in which optical inputs are encoded as 
continuous variations in average current. Here, we demonstrate a fundamentally 
distinct paradigm in which light is encoded in stochastic transport dynamics 
rather than steady-state conductance. Using a monolayer MoS2 field-effect 
transistor with an aggressively scaled gate stack (∼1.3 nm equivalent oxide 
thickness), we access a regime where interfacial defect states dominate 
transport and form gate-tunable potential wells. At low temperature, carrier

to large-amplitude ("giant") random telegraph noise. This enables independent 
control of capture and emission processes through electrostatic gating and

kinetics, confirming the role of photon-assisted detrapping. These results show 
a light-induced nonequilibrium transport regime in which defect-mediated 
fluctuations, conventionally treated as noise, act as a functional signal and 
provide a stochastic sensing framework for ultralow-light detection in nanoscale 
electronic systems.

Transition metal ditellurides exhibit structural and electronic properties 
distinct from their selenide and sulfide counterparts, including the 
stabilization of multiple charge density wave (CDW) phases. Within the niobium 
compound family, notable differences in structure are also observed: bulk NbTe2

based on a phonon instability. These findings motivate the exploration of the 
complex phase behavior and electronic properties of NbTe2 in the 2D limit.

Randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled clinical safety evaluation of a 
facial brightening toner containing niacinamide and β-arbutin used with 4% 
hydroquinone.

Maldonado López AM(1), da Silva Souza ID(1).

Author information:
(1)Good Molecules, LLC, Philadelphia, PA, USA.

BACKGROUND: Hydroquinone (HQ) remains the gold standard for treating facial 
hyperpigmentation, but irritation concerns may limit its use. β-arbutin and 
niacinamide are widely used cosmetic brightening ingredients; however, concerns 
that β-arbutin may release HQ have led to recommendations against combining 
β-arbutin-containing products with HQ. Clinical evidence evaluating the 
tolerability of this combination is limited.
OBJECTIVES: Assess the safety of a Facial Brightening Toner containing 3% 
niacinamide and 2% β-arbutin when combined with 4% HQ.
METHODS: An 18-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study was 
conducted in adult female volunteers with facial hyperpigmentation and/or 
melasma. Volunteers received either a facial Brightening Toner or a Placebo 
Toner for 18 weeks, with 4% HQ through Week 10; they continued toner use through 
Week 18 without HQ. Assessments were performed at Baseline, Week 10, and Week 
18, including facial erythema by a* measurements, VISIA CR red feature analysis, 
and adverse events monitoring.
RESULTS: Forty-seven volunteers completed the study (Brightening Toner n = 23; 
Placebo Toner n = 24). Within-group and between-group analyses showed no 
significant changes in a* values from Baseline to Week 10, Baseline to Week 18, 
or Week 10 to Week 18 in either group, nor differences at any time point. Red 
feature analysis supported these findings. No irritation-related adverse events 
were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: A Facial Brightening Toner containing 3% niacinamide and 2% 
β-arbutin was well tolerated when combined with 4% HQ. These findings offer 
preliminary clinical safety evidence supporting the tolerability of β-arbutin- 
and niacinamide-containing cosmetic products used to support HQ therapy.

INTRODUCTION: The epidemiology of breast cancer among men is poorly 
characterized. As the Veterans Health Administration (VA) serves a 
disproportionally male population, a larger percentage of breast cancer cases 
diagnosed and treated in VA are among male patients. However, whether current 
breast oncology operational infrastructure is prepared to address this need is 
unclear.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The VA Breast and Gynecologic Oncology System of 
Excellence (BGSoE) established a tracking dashboard for all incident breast and 
gynecologic malignancies in VA in 2021. All breast surgery cases within the VA 
performed on male Veterans for an indication of cancer in 2023 were reviewed and 
mapped by the Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN). Operative cases 
performed for gynecomastia were excluded. To determine the total affected 
population, incidence of male breast cancer was calculated using data from the 
Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Breast surgeries, 
reported as a fraction of incident cases, were plotted. The number of active 
surgeons performing breast surgery in 2023 was garnered from the staff surgeon 
identified in the BGSoE dashboard.
RESULTS: Based upon SEER age-adjusted estimates of breast cancer in men 
nationally and current Veteran census data, there were estimated to be 188 
incident cases of breast cancer among male Veterans in 2023. In comparison, 82 
(44%) male Veterans underwent surgery for their breast cancers in VA in 2023. 
The median age of the cohort was 72 years (interquartile range 58-78). 
Geographic variability in surgical volume was noted, with the number of 
surgeries performed in each VISN ranging from 0 to 13 cases. VISNs performed 
between 0% and 112% of the expected number of cancer operations for male 
Veterans. All VISNs had at least 1 surgeon performing breast surgery among this 
population in 2023 (range: 1-15).

male Veterans treated in VA. Whether these geographic differences are reflective 
of differential incidence, discrepancies in access, or availability of breast 
oncology health services is unclear. Although most patients with breast cancer 
do present with resectable disease, the proportion of incident cases among male 
Veterans by our estimates with stage IV disease (not amenable to surgery) cannot 
be ascertained. Future work will be aimed at characterizing availability of 
multidisciplinary breast cancer care in VA.

Fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) exhibits the nexus of transparency, electrical 
conductivity, heat resistivity, and reduced reliance on critical minerals, 
making it vital in solar panels, IR-reflective glass, and optical electronics. 
This work leverages the synergistic combination of two emerging liquid 
metal-based concepts-liquid metal doping and liquid metal bridge solubility-for 
the generation of ultrathin FTO layers, reducing reliance on current 
energy-intensive and hazardous chemical vapour deposition (CVD) processes. Here, 
tin (Sn) and silver fluoride (AgF) are melted together to form a homogeneous 
liquid, from which the surface oxide is transferred onto a solid substrate. 
While Ag plays an essential role in facilitating the incorporation and 
solubility of F in Sn, its presence at the liquid metal surface is restricted 
due to its very low tendency to oxidise at the surface. The technology enables 
the harvesting of multilayer architectures at moderately low temperatures and 
under ambient atmospheric conditions. The harvested FTO nanosheets exhibited a 
thickness of up to 10 nm, enhanced conductivity, and a transparency of 80% in 
the visible region. Tin oxide (SnO2), obtained from a similar liquid metal-based 
deposition process, was also used as a reference for comparison. This work 
validates the feasibility of liquid metal-based technology for the efficient 
synthesis of ultrathin doped oxides as a potential alternative to complex and 
energy-intensive state-of-the-art sputtering and CVD techniques.

Homochiral Evolution from Self-Assembly of Chiral Block Copolymers.

Shao SW(1), Ho RM(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chemical Engineering, National Tsing Hua University, No. 101,

A block copolymer containing a chiral block is referred to as a chiral block 
copolymer, which can form a helical phase (H*) in diblock copolymers and an 
alternating gyroid phase (GA) in triblock terpolymers with controlled chirality 
from self-assembly, as evidenced by electron tomography. Polylactide-containing 
chiral block copolymers can be used as a representative system for the 
investigation of homochiral evolution from molecular chirality examined by 
electronic circular dichroism (ECD) to conformational chirality examined by C═O 
vibrational circular dichroism (VCD), and finally to phase chirality 
characterized by electron tomography, with C-O-C VCD providing insight into 
interchain chiral interactions. The intra- and interchain contributions should 
be evaluated in the context of the specific molecular structure and sample 
conditions. By taking advantage of noncovalent chirality induction, it is 
feasible to introduce a chiral bias by associating a chiral dopant with an 
achiral block, giving H* with controlled chirality from an achiral block 
copolymer. This Viewpoint highlights the fundamental principles, providing 
perspectives on the design of chiral soft materials for device applications.

Positional isomerism, a universal structural regulation strategy in nature, 
achieves precise control over biological functions through minute variations in 
substituent positions on a molecular backbone. Despite its extensive application 
in small-molecule chemistry, the systematic introduction of positional isomerism 
as the sole structural variable into polymer main chains remains unexplored. 
Herein, inspired by biological systems, we employ three isomeric aromatic diols, 
1,2-, 1,3-, and 1,4-benzenedimethanol (o-, m-, and p-BDM) as chain extenders to 
synthesize three thermoplastic polyurethanes with identical chemical 
composition, differing only in the substitution pattern on the aromatic ring. 
The para-substituted polyurethane (p-PU) exhibits a tensile strength of 13.1 
MPa, an elongation at break of 2016%, and a toughness of 151.8 MJ/m3, 
representing a 7.7-fold increase in tensile strength and a 19.2-fold increase in 
toughness over its ortho-substituted counterpart (o-PU, with a tensile strength 
of 1.7 MPa, an elongation at break of 604%, and a toughness of 7.9 MJ/m3), while 
the meta-substituted polyurethane (m-PU) shows intermediate values (tensile 
strength: 7.4 MPa; elongation at break: 1271%; toughness: 47.0 MJ/m3). Combined 
characterization using small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), density functional 
theory (DFT) calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations reveals that the 
para isomer, with minimal steric hindrance, promotes ordered hydrogen bonding 
and π-π stacking within hard segments, inducing the most well-defined 
microphase-separated morphology among the three isomers. This work demonstrates 
the feasibility of positional isomerism as an independent dimension for tuning 
polymer properties and offers a molecular design strategy for precisely 
modulating mechanical performance without altering chemical composition.

Absence of Ionomer Peaks in X-ray Scattering Does Not Imply Absence of Nanophase

Frischknecht AL(1).

Author information:
(1)Center for Integrated Nanotechnologies, Sandia National Laboratories, 
Albuquerque, New Mexico87185, United States.

A peak at low wavevectors in the X-ray scattering of hydrated, ionic polymers is 
typically indicative of nanophase separation between the hydrophobic and 
hydrophilic domains. Here we use atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to 
show that low intensity or absent ionomer peaks in the X-ray scattering from 
hydrocarbon-based ion exchange membranes do not necessarily indicate a lack of 
nanophase separation. Instead, there is often a lack of contrast between the 
hydrophobic and hydrophilic domains in these systems, due to the similar X-ray 
atomic form factors of carbon and oxygen. We show that when the backbone 
hydrogen atoms in three simulated ionic polymers scatter like fluorine instead 
of like hydrogen, large ionomer peaks are observed. Similarly, when we assume 
the water in these membranes is fully deuterated, calculations of the expected 
small angle neutron scattering also show clear ionomer peaks. The correlation 
lengths calculated from neutron scattering agree with those from the water 
partial X-ray structure factors and follow expected trends with increasing water 
content.

Author information:
(1)Department of Macromolecular Science and Engineering, Case Western Reserve 
University, 10900 Euclid Avenue, Cleveland, Ohio44106, United States.

Polymer grafting affects chain relaxation dynamics in ways that can strongly 
influence the physical properties of polymer nanocomposites and surface layers. 
Here, we performed energy-conserving dissipative particle dynamics (eDPD) 
simulations with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) to investigate the 
dominant relaxation modes of planar polymer brushes. While the dynamics parallel 
to the substrate remain largely consistent with classical Rouse behavior, the 
perpendicular dynamics collapse into a single persistent, surface-localized mode 
that remains remarkably robust across polymer chain lengths and grafting 
densities. We show that this mode can be represented by a localized exponential 
contribution together with a small number of low-order Rouse modes. While the 
spatial extent of the localized contribution increases with grafting density, 
the local strength of the graft-induced perturbation becomes approximately 
independent of grafting density once a brush is formed. Further analysis of the 
contour-resolved dynamical memory confirms that grafting produces increasingly 
anisotropic dynamics that extend farther along the polymer contour with 
increasing grafting density. These results provide a mechanistic framework for 
understanding how grafting reorganizes polymer dynamics and identify a 
surface-localized dynamical mode that may underlie the suppression of 
long-wavelength Rouse modes observed in neutron scattering experiments.

that affords rapid healing with negligible scarring, but its clinical efficacy 
is severely limited by tumor hypoxia and aggregation-induced quenching of 
photosensitizers. Perfluorocarbons possess excellent oxygen dissolution and 
transport capacities and have been widely employed to construct oxygen-enriched 
microenvironments. In addition, the heavy-atom effect enhances intersystem 
crossing by promoting spin-orbit coupling, thereby increasing singlet oxygen 
generation. Herein, we synthesized a series of amphiphilic bottlebrush polymers 
(BBPs) covalently grafted with porphyrin photosensitizers, featuring tunable 
fluorine-containing side chains and iodine functionalization. Distinct from 
conventional polymeric PDT systems that primarily serve as photosensitizer 
carriers, the BBP architecture provides a confined multifunctional 
microenvironment that simultaneously regulates photosensitizer aggregation, 
oxygen availability, and intersystem crossing. The strong steric repulsion 
between neighboring side chains prevents undesired photosensitizer aggregation 
and preserves their photoactivity, while the fluorine-rich domains and iodine 
substituents cooperatively promote singlet oxygen generation through oxygen 
enrichment and external heavy-atom effects, respectively. Consequently, polymer 
vesicles assembled from these fluorinated and iodinated BBPs exhibit 
significantly enhanced PDT efficacy. This work establishes a cooperative 
molecular-design strategy that integrates aggregation suppression, oxygen 
regulation, and heavy-atom-enhanced intersystem crossing within a single 
bottlebrush polymer platform for improved PDT.

Two-Step Self-Assembly Mechanisms and Crystal-Quasicrystal Transition Kinetics

Sun YW(1), Xia XY(1), Li ZW(1).

Author information:
(1)College of Chemistry, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou450001, China.

Quasicrystals are materials that exhibit long-range bond-orientational order 
without translational periodicity. Although various crystals and quasicrystals 
have been assembled from DNA nanomotifs, the self-assembly mechanisms of 
quasicrystals and the transition kinetics between crystals and quasicrystals 
remain poorly understood. Here, we introduce a coarse-grained 
patchy-particle-chain model for branched DNA nanomotifs to reveal the formation 
and transition kinetics of two-dimensional dodecagonal quasicrystals. The 
simulations capture the self-assembly of bridged 5- and 6-point-star DNA motifs 
into dodecagonal quasicrystals at appropriate stoichiometric ratios, consistent 
with experiments. The formation proceeds via a non-classical two-step 
self-assembly pathway, involving network-like intermediates, followed by 
nucleation and assimilation growth into ordered quasicrystals. By tuning DNA 
motif rigidity, the transition from hexagonal crystals to dodecagonal 
quasicrystals occurs through nucleation and growth at defect sites, whereas the 
reverse transition preferentially proceeds via destabilization of square-like 
arrangements, with both transitions driven by binding-energy differences. 
Rational design of 3- and 4-point-star DNA motifs further enables the assembly 
of decagonal quasicrystal approximants. These findings clarify the formation 
mechanisms of quasicrystals and crystal-quasicrystal transition kinetics, 
providing insights into symmetry breaking and structural reorganization in 
complex self-assembly systems.

Polymer capsules capable of adopting distinct shell nanostructures in response 
to external stimuli are attractive microcompartments for encapsulation, 
separation, and triggered release. Realizing such capsules requires orthogonal 
control, in which distinct stimuli independently define the structural outcome.

Črešnar KP(1)(2), Slatinek T(1), Zemljič LF(1), Schlögl S(3)(4).

Author information:
(1)Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Maribor, SI-2000Maribor,

Poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL)-based dynamic polymers are promising adaptive 
biomaterials due to their biocompatibility, biodegradability, and high chain 
mobility; however, the onset temperature for bond-exchange reactions, often 
referred to as topology-freezing temperature, Tv, remains difficult to control 
and is typically treated as a bulk property governed by catalyst selection and 
network structure. Consequently, many reported dynamic polymers operate at 
temperatures well above the biomedical operating window, limiting their 
biomedical applicability. Here, we propose an interfacial kinetic engineering 
strategy in which nanoparticle-polymer interfaces act as localized kinetic 
regulators of dynamic covalent bond exchange. By tailoring nanoparticle (NP) 
surface chemistry, including functional group density, polarity, and catalytic 
activity, the activation energy (Ea) can be modulated at the nanoscale, enabling 
programmable control of Tv. Exchange kinetics in PCL-based dynamic polymers are 
expected to be highly sensitive to the local chemical environment, indicating 
that interfacial effects can decouple dynamic behavior from bulk composition. 
This perspective establishes NP-dynamic polymer interfaces as a programmable 
kinetic design parameter for controlling bond-exchange reactions in dynamic 
polymer networks, opening a pathway toward spatially defined covalent adaptable 
materials with application-specific and programmable dynamic behavior.

Evidence suggests that increased local temperatures are associated with higher 
prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in environmental bacteria. This 
observational cohort study investigates associations between local climate and 
the proportion of antimicrobial-resistant Escherichia coli isolated from 2,766 
farm environment samples from 53 English dairy farms. A non-linear Bayesian 
model that accounts for decreased test sensitivity at low E. coli abundance was 
used to estimate the proportion of antimicrobial-resistant E. coli from colony 
count data. A 20°C increase in local temperature was associated with a 5.0-fold 
increase in the proportion of streptomycin-resistant E. coli (95% credible 
interval [CI]: 1.03-33.0; absolute increase: 0.2%, 95% CI: 2.3 × 10-3%-1.2%). 
Weaker evidence suggested that increased temperatures were associated with 
increased proportions of tetracycline-resistant E. coli. Increasing relative 
humidity was associated with an increase in the proportion of amoxicillin-, 
streptomycin-, and tetracycline-resistant E. coli. A 32% increase in relative 
humidity (from 60% to 92%) was associated with a 4.7-fold increase in the 
proportion of amoxicillin-resistant E. coli (median; 95% CI: 1.4-15.7; absolute 
increase: 1.3%, 95% CI: 0.2%-3.5%). For amoxicillin and streptomycin, a 
synergistic effect where increasing both temperature and humidity was associated 
with increased proportions of antimicrobial-resistant E. coli was observed, with 
weak evidence of this effect observed for tetracycline. These findings highlight 
the importance of considering weather conditions, sample characteristics, and 
seasonality in livestock AMR surveillance. Associations between local weather 
conditions and the proportion of livestock E. coli exhibiting AMR suggest that 
climate change may influence the burden of One Health 
AMR.IMPORTANCEUnderstanding how environmental conditions are associated with 
variability in antimicrobial resistance (AMR) prevalence is critical for 
developing robust livestock AMR surveillance and anticipating the potential 
effects of climate change. The non-linear Bayesian modeling approach developed 
here adjusts for Escherichia coli abundance-associated variability in test 
sensitivity, enabling the influence of risk factors associated with the 
proportion of antimicrobial-resistant E. coli within samples to be more 
accurately estimated. Applying this approach to 2,766 fecal samples from 53 
dairy farms in Southwest England indicated that the proportion of 
antimicrobial-resistant E. coli generally increased under warmer and wetter 
conditions. These findings suggest that environmental conditions can influence 
the prevalence of antimicrobial-resistant E. coli in dairy farm environments and 
demonstrate the importance of accounting for weather-related variability in 
livestock AMR surveillance. Adjusting for these associations in livestock AMR 
surveillance could improve the accuracy of modeling AMR trends and strengthen 
the assessment of climate-associated AMR risks.

Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic 
Leptospira.

Ozuru R(1)(2), Yoshimura M(1), Powers DA(2), Sonoda T(1), Papin JA(2), Obata

Author information:
(1)Department of Microbiology and Immunology, Faculty of Medicine, Fukuoka

(2)Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Virginia, 
Charlottesville, Virginia, USA.
(3)Division of Bacteriology, Department of Microbiology and Immunology, Faculty

Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian 
hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although 
Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids 
for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like 
temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, 
we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine 
temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. Models 
contextualized with transcriptomic data from cultures at 37°C predicted 
increased flux through glucose transport, glucose phosphorylation, and 
downstream glucose-associated reactions than it did at 29-30°C. Similar 
temperature-dependent predictions were obtained for another pathogenic 
Leptospira species under in vitro conditions. Consistent with these findings, 
analysis of leptospires cultivated intraperitoneally in dialysis membrane 
chambers also predicted enhanced glucose uptake and metabolism under 
host-temperature conditions. In vitro validation experiments showed increased 
bacterial uptake or accumulation of a fluorescent glucose analog, elevated 
expression of candidate glucose transporter genes, and glucose-dependent 
enhancement of bacterial growth at 37°C. Treatment with a glucose degradation 
pathway inhibitor, 2-deoxy-d-glucose, further supported a contribution of 
glucose-associated processes to proliferation at 37°C. Together, these findings 
indicate that pathogenic Leptospira displays condition-dependent glucose uptake 
and glucose-associated metabolic activity that become apparent at host-like 
temperature, as opposed to being glucose-incompetent at environmental-like 
temperature. This prediction-driven framework refines the conventional view of 
Leptospira carbon metabolism and provides a basis for future studies of 
glucose-associated metabolic capacity during mammalian infection.
IMPORTANCE: Environmental reservoirs play a central role in the transmission of 
many bacterial pathogens, yet the metabolic mechanisms that enable adaptation to 
both environmental and host-associated niches remain largely unknown. Using a 
prediction-driven framework that combines contextualized genome-scale metabolic 
modeling with multi-omics analyses and experimental validation, we discovered 
that pathogenic Leptospira activates glucose uptake and metabolism only under 
host-like conditions. This finding resolves a long-standing misconception 
arising from studies performed under conventional laboratory conditions and 
fundamentally revises our understanding of Leptospira physiology. More 
importantly, our study establishes an integrative systems biology strategy for 
uncovering condition-dependent metabolic traits that would be difficult to 
identify experimentally alone, with broad applicability to diverse 
environmentally transmitted pathogens.

Growth mechanisms of body-centered cubic and quasi-crystalline Ta.

Huang C(1), Chen L(1), Zhang W(1), Liu LH(1).

Author information:
(1)National Engineering Research Center of Near-Net-Shape Forming for Metallic 
Materials, Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory for Processing and Forming of 
Advanced Metallic Materials, South China University of Technology, Guangzhou 
510640, China.

Compared with the growth of periodic crystals, the growth of aperiodic 
quasi-crystals remains elusive in many respects, particularly regarding their 
underlying growth mechanisms. Here, we perform molecular dynamics simulations to 
investigate the growth behavior of the body-centered cubic phase and the 
quasi-crystalline metastable phase in tantalum (Ta). The results show that both 
phases can be described by a diffusion-limited growth model, yet they exhibit 
fundamentally distinct atomistic mechanisms. The crystalline phase grows via a 
continuous mechanism, in which atoms can simultaneously propagate across 
multiple unit cells on a rough interface. In contrast, the quasi-crystalline 
metastable phase grows through a screw dislocation-mediated mechanism on a 
smooth interface, where atomic attachment is restricted to approximately a 
single unit cell. As a result, the growth rate of quasi-crystals is several 
times slower than that of crystals under comparable conditions. The distinct 
growth mechanisms of crystals and quasi-crystals are closely related to the type 
and characteristics of the locally ordered atomic species at their respective 
interfaces. These findings offer new physical insights into the correlation 
between crystal and quasi-crystal growth mechanisms and provide a fresh 
perspective on the underlying origin of the remarkable glass-forming ability of 
elemental Ta.

The std2 package: A computationally efficient program to calculate molecular 
response properties and excited states using simplified quantum chemistry 
methods.

Beaujean P(1), Liger A(2), Satisha A(2), Maraldi MG(2), Bannwarth C(3), de 
Wergifosse M(2).

Author information:
(1)Theoretical Chemistry Laboratory, Unit of Theoretical and Structural Physical 
Chemistry, Namur Institute of Structured Matter (NISM), University of Namur, Rue 
de Bruxelles, 61, B-5000 Namur, Belgium.
(2)Theoretical Chemistry Group, Molecular Chemistry, Materials and Catalysis 
Division (MOST), Institute of Condensed Matter and Nanosciences, Université 
Catholique de Louvain, Louvain-la-Neuve B-1348, Belgium.
(3)Institute of Physical Chemistry, RWTH Aachen University, Melatener Str. 20, 
Aachen D-52074, Germany.

The std2 modular program package is dedicated to the computation of excited 
states and molecular response properties using simplified quantum chemistry 
approaches. The framework involves several variants of the simplified 
time-dependent density functional theory, including sTDA, sTD-DFT, SF-sTD-DFT, 
XsTDA, XsTD-DFT, and SF-XsTD-DFT methods. Combining controlled approximations 
with efficient implementations, the std2 program enables routine calculations on 
systems containing thousands of atoms while retaining a favorable balance 
between computational cost and predictive accuracy. Therefore, the framework 
supports all-atom quantum mechanics (AQM) methodologies for the treatment of 
surrounding and dynamical structural effects considering realistic systems. In 
this contribution, the capabilities of the std2 package are illustrated for 
spectroscopic observables, such as one- and two-photon absorption, electronic 
circular dichroism, optical rotation, second-harmonic generation, and 
excited-state absorption. Among results, benchmark calculations show that the 
recent XsTD-DFT scheme improves the description of excited states relative to 
sTD-DFT especially, for charge-transfer excitations while preserving a speedup 
of two to three orders of magnitude compared to standard TD-DFT. Applications of 
AQM methodologies to explicitly solvated systems and ultra-large systems are 
also highlighted, showing the adequacy of the std2 program to treat such 
systems. Overall, std2 provides an efficient platform for large-scale 
excited-state and spectroscopic simulations, especially in AQM protocols.

Defect organization in coexisting hexagonal and square lattices on ellipsoids.

Liu W(1), Xie H(2)(3), Li B(1), Chen JZY(2), Li Y(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Physics and Key Laboratory of Functional Polymer Materials of 
Ministry of Education, Nankai University, and Collaborative Innovation Center of 
Chemical Science and Engineering, Tianjin 300071, China.
(2)Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of Waterloo, Waterloo, 
Ontario N2L 3G1, Canada.
(3)Department of Physics, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, 
Clear Water Bay, Kowloon, Hong Kong, China.

Curvature and topology jointly organize defects in two-dimensional crystals, but 
their combined role remains unresolved when competing lattice symmetries coexist 
with spatially varying curvature. We use simulated-annealing Langevin dynamics 
to study Hertzian particles forming coexisting hexagonal (Hex) and square (Sq) 
lattices on prolate and oblate ellipsoids. Mapping reduced density and aspect 
ratio reveals a broad sequence of scar- and domain-based morphologies in both 
Hex-dominant and Sq-dominant backgrounds. Latitude-resolved comparisons show 
that Gaussian curvature biases defects toward its maxima under weak deformation. 
Strong prolateness, however, confines high curvature to small polar caps that 
cannot independently accommodate all defect motifs. Defects then spread toward 
lower-curvature latitudes to relieve defect crowding and elastic repulsion. In 
the Hex-dominant regime, this competition drives vertex-contacted domains with 
neutralized corner contacts, and compensating positive defects locate away from 
the poles. The Sq-dominant regime features Hex-rich triangular domains, bridged 
states, and linear or open scars similarly reorganized by curvature anisotropy. 
On oblate ellipsoids, the extended equatorial high-curvature belt allows defects 
to separate azimuthally while remaining curvature-localized. This work 
elucidates that nonuniform curvature can engineer rich defect patterns by 
selecting the spatial distribution of topological charge and the connectivity of 
finite defect motifs.

runner 2.0: A software suite for high-dimensional neural network potentials.

Knoll ALM(1)(2), Schäfer MR(1)(2), Lausch KN(1)(2), Gubler M(3)(4), Wang 
H(1)(2), Springborn R(1)(2), El Haouari R(1)(2), Liebetrau AM(1)(2), Finkler 
JA(3), Kocer E(1)(2), Eckhoff M(5), Goedecker S(3), Schmitz G(1)(2), Behler 
J(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Lehrstuhl für Theoretische Chemie II, Ruhr-Universität Bochum, 44780 Bochum, 
Germany.
(2)Research Center Chemical Sciences and Sustainability, Research Alliance Ruhr, 
44780 Bochum, Germany.
(3)University of Basel, Department of Physics, Klingelbergstrasse 82, CH-4056 
Basel, Switzerland.
(4)PSI Center for Scientific Computing, Theory and Data, Paul Scherrer 
Institute, 5232 Villigen PSI, Switzerland.
(5)ETH Zurich, Department of Chemistry and Applied Biosciences,

We present runner 2.0, the "Ruhr University Neural Network energy 
representation," a highly optimized software suite for training and evaluating 
high-dimensional neural network potentials (HDNNPs) of the second, third, and 
fourth generations. Long-range electrostatics and charge equilibration (QEq) for 
the description of non-local charge transfer in fourth-generation (4G) HDNNPs 
are accelerated by quasi-linear-scaling plane wave methods, reducing QEq 
computational complexity from O(N3) to O(N⁡log2⁡N) such that linear or 
quasi-linear scaling is achieved across all HDNNP generations. An optimized 
memory management strategy eliminates the training overhead traditionally 
associated with long-range interactions, allowing 4G-HDNNPs to be trained with 
the same efficiency as their local counterparts. Developed in modern Fortran 
(2003/2008 standards), combined with a hybrid Message Passing Interface 
(MPI)/Open Multi-Processing (OpenMP) parallelization scheme, runner 2.0 has been 
designed to run efficiently in any central processing unit (CPU) environment, 
from cost-effective local workstations to massive high-performance computing 
(HPC) clusters. Its modular library architecture facilitates straightforward 
binding to external simulation software; native interfaces to the Large-scale 
Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS) and the atomic simulation 
environment (ASE) provide full access to all its features, including built-in 
committee-based uncertainty quantification. The high efficiency and scalability 
of the runner 2.0 ecosystem are demonstrated through detailed benchmarks.

Investigation of surface and subsurface defects of Cu(111) surface by scanning 
tunneling microscopy.

Walshe K(1), Walls B(1), Aladyshkin AY(2)(3)(4), Matveev VN(5), Zhussupbekov 
K(1), Ionov AM(6), Shvets IV(1), Bozhko SI(6).

Author information:
(1)School of Physics and Centre for Research on Adaptive Nanostructures and 
Nanodevices (CRANN), Trinity College Dublin, Dublin 2, Ireland.
(2)Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology, Dolgoprudny, 141700 Moscow, 
Russia.
(3)Institute for Physics of Microstructures Russian Academy of Sciences, 
GSP-105, Nizhny Novgorod 603950, Russia.
(4)Lobachevsky State University of Nizhny Novgorod, Gagarin Avenue 23, Nizhny 
Novgorod 603022, Russia.
(5)Institute of Microelectronics Technology and High-Purity Materials, Russian

(6)Institute of Solid State Physics, Russian Academy of Sciences, Chernogolovka 
142432, Russia.

Various types of surface defects are observed using scanning tunneling 
microscopy (STM) on a clean Cu(111) surface. Detailed STM images of defects show 
an asymmetric structure comprised of a bright protrusion inside a hexagonal 
depression. Protrusions are consistently aligned in the same direction, Cu[001], 
on the surface. The defects are observed to interact with one another, as each 
defect is separated by an integer multiple of half the Fermi wavelength, evident 
from the quasiparticle interference oscillations resulting from the defects. 
This interaction is also suspected to dictate the orientation of the defects, 
resulting in their uniform alignment. Ab initio density functional theory 
methods are used to investigate Cu(111) surface defects and adatoms. Simulated 
STM images using the Tersoff-Hamann scheme are compared to STM images. Results 
are also discussed in the context of existing literature on similar structures.

Hidradenitis suppurativa skin microbiome: In-depth analysis and modulation by 
systemic therapies.

Amar Y(1), Baumann D(1), Niedermeier S(1), Silva RL(1), Walch S(2), Schloter 
M(2), Köberle M(1), Biedermann T(1), Volz T(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Dermatology and Allergology, Technical University of Munich, 
School of Medicine, Munich, Germany.
(2)Research Unit Comparative Microbiome Analysis, Helmholtz Zentrum München, 
Deutsches Forschungszentrum für Gesundheit Und Umwelt (GmbH), Neuherberg, 
Germany.

BACKGROUND: Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease 
with a multifactorial pathogenesis involving genetic, lifestyle and microbial 
factors. While cutaneous microbiome shifts have been reported for this disease, 
the impact of systemic immunomodulators and antibiotics on HS microbiome remains 
poorly defined.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize species-level cutaneous dysbiosis in HS and evaluate 
the effects of three standard-of-care systemic therapies, clindamycin/rifampicin 
(ATB), adalimumab (ADA) and secukinumab (SEC) on skin microbial composition.
METHODS: We performed 16S rRNA sequencing on 251 skin swabs from lesional and 
non-lesional sites of 52 HS patients and 31 healthy matched controls. In a 
sub-cohort of 28 patients, microbial shifts were evaluated following 12 weeks of 
therapy with ATB (n = 8), ADA (n = 12) and SEC (n = 8).
RESULTS: HS skin exhibited profound dysbiosis defined by the depletion of 
homeostatic commensals (Cutibacterium acnes, Staphylococcus hominis, S. 
epidermidis) and a synergistic expansion of anaerobic pathogens, primarily 
Gram-positive anaerobic cocci (GPAC; Finegoldia magna, Peptoniphilus grossensis 
and Fenollaria massiliensis), Lawsonella clevelandensis and Campylobacter 
ureolyticus. A 13-taxa microbial signature accurately discriminated the HS 
phenotype (AUC = 0.92). Following 12 weeks of treatment, ATB markedly attenuated 
dysbiosis by reducing pathogen loads and significantly increasing microbial 
richness. In contrast, ADA and SEC did not alter pathogen abundance and were 
associated with a slight decline in protective commensals.
CONCLUSIONS: Systemic antibiotics partially restore cutaneous microbiome 
homeostasis in HS by targeting anaerobic pathogens while preserving beneficial 
commensals, an effect not observed with the tested biologics. These findings 
highlight the need for microbiome-directed adjuvant therapies to complement 
immunomodulation in HS management.

Plain Language Summary: WHAT IS THE DISEASE?: Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a 
painful, long‐lasting inflammatory skin condition that mainly affects the 
armpits and genital areas. The frequency of the disease ranges from 0.05% in 
Europe to about 4.1% in the USA, and it affects three times more females than 
males.
LOCATION OF THE STUDY: This study was conducted in Germany at the Technical 
University of Munich.
AIM OF THE STUDY: While imbalances in HS skin microorganisms (dysbiosis) are 
documented, how treatments affect these bacteria remains unclear. This study 
evaluates the impact of systemic antibiotics (clindamycin/rifampicin) and 
anti‐inflammatory biologics (adalimumab, secukinumab) on HS skin bacteria.
METHODOLOGY: We analysed 251 skin swabs from 52 patients with HS (both affected 
and unaffected skin) and compared them to samples from 31 healthy individuals. 
We then tracked a smaller group of 28 HS patients over 12 weeks to see how their 
skin bacteria (microbiome) changed while taking one of the three standard 
therapies.
KEY FINDINGS: HS skin showed profound dysbiosis, characterized by a loss of 
beneficial bacteria (like Cutibacterium acnes) and an expansion of harmful 
pathogens. After 12 weeks, oral antibiotics successfully restored microbial 
balance by reducing pathogens and increasing bacterial diversity. Surprisingly, 
even though the anti‐inflammatory biologic treatments helped heal visible HS 
skin inflammation, they were unable to clear the harmful pathogens or bring back 
the healthy bacteria.
CONCLUSIONS AND PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: Visible skin healing from 
anti‐inflammatory treatments is not sufficient to correct the microbial 
imbalance observed in HS patients. Because biologics leave harmful bacteria 
completely untouched, future HS care should combine targeted anti‐inflammatory 
biologic treatments alongside microbiome‐targeted therapies that actively 
restore a balanced skin microbiome.
