Marine-Derived Injectable Hydroxybutyl Chitosan with Tunable Thermoresponsive 
Properties and Potential Anti-aging Applications.

Du S(1)(2), Navarrete-Segado P(1), Sevostianova V(1), Patterson J(1).

Author information:
(1)IMDEA Materials Institute , Getafe, Madrid28906, Spain.
(2)Universidad Politécnica de Madrid , Madrid, Madrid28040, Spain.

Skin aging, largely driven by oxidative stress, leads to fibroblast senescence, 
deterioration of the extracellular matrix, and impaired regenerative capacity; 
however, effective biomaterial-based interventions remain limited. While 
marine-derived chitosan offers sustainable antioxidative potential, its poor 
solubility limits clinical use. In this study, we developed an injectable, 
thermoresponsive hydroxybutyl chitosan (HBC) hydrogel that combines intrinsic 
radical-scavenging activity with thermoresponsive modulation of the local 
hydrated microenvironment. HBC (degree of substitution: 1.88; Mw: 188 ± 34 kDa) 
demonstrated robust radical scavenging, reaching 80% for hydroxyl radicals at a 
concentration of 1.6 mg/mL. At 37 °C, HBC exhibited rapid, 
concentration-dependent gelation (40-60 s), forming hydrogels that exhibited 
time- and concentration-dependent increases in modulus and a characteristic 40% 
diameter shrinkage. HBC hydrogel extracts were not cytotoxic, maintaining 
metabolic activity levels near the positive controls for both L929 fibroblasts 
and human dermal fibroblasts (HDFs). In a hydrogen peroxide-induced senescence 
model using HDFs, the 5% HBC hydrogel led to a significant decrease in 
senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity (>50%) and mitigated 
intracellular reactive oxygen species activity. Furthermore, HBC treatment 
effectively sustained collagen I synthesis. These findings support 
marine-derived HBC as a multifunctional, thermoresponsive biomaterial with 
potential for skin-regenerative and anti-aging applications involving oxidative 
stress modulation.

Searchfield AK(1), Milne B(2), Waldie KE(3), Slykerman RF(4), Murphy R(5),

AIM: Small for gestational age (SGA) has been linked to lower school achievement 
in childhood. However, this association has only been shown consistently in 
preterm-SGA cohorts. This paper aims to determine whether being born SGA at term 
is associated with school performance at 7, 11 and 16 years of age.
METHODS: n = 871 children born at term (n = 433 small-for-gestational-age [SGA] 
and n = 438 appropriate for gestational age [AGA]) had education outcomes 
analysed at age 7 (n = 265 SGA, n = 304 AGA), 11 (n = 200 SGA, n = 218 AGA) and 
16 (n = 152 SGA, n = 185 AGA). The outcomes studied were the risk of

1.71, CI 1.04-2.80) and oral comprehension at 11 (OR 2.10, CI 1.22-3.62). These 
associations were not statistically significant once adjusted for confounders

1.79, CI 0.99-3.25). There was no statistically significant difference in 
secondary school achievement (OR 0.80, 95% CI 0.45-1.42) between SGA and AGA 
children.
CONCLUSIONS: Our results show that being born SGA at term does not independently 
increase the risk of below-average performance at ages 7, 11 or 16 after 
adjusting for known social and environmental confounders. However, clinicians 
should maintain active surveillance for term SGA infants, particularly when 
co-occurring environmental or maternal risk factors are present.

Association between thyroid feedback quantile-based index and the risk of 
in-hospital amputation in patients with diabetic foot ulcer.

Wang J(1)(2), Huang Y(1), Wang F(1)(2), Lao M(1)(2), Lan L(1), Liang P(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)The Eighth Clinical Medical College of Guangzhou University of Chinese 
Medicine, Foshan, Guangdong, China.
(2)Foshan Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Foshan, Guangdong, China.

AIMS: To investigate the relationship between the thyroid feedback 
quantile-based index (TFQI) and the risk of amputation during hospitalization in 
patients with diabetic foot ulcers (DFU).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 381 hospitalized 
patients with DFU and normal thyroid function. Logistic regression assessed 
continuous TFQI and quartiles. Model 1 was unadjusted; Model 2 adjusted for age, 
sex, BMI, and smoking; Model 3 additionally adjusted for diabetes duration, 
HbA1c, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, 
hypertension, CRP, and dyslipidemia. RCS assessed dose-response patterns; Firth 
regression was used for sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Fifty-six patients underwent amputation. In Model 3, each 1-SD increase 
in TFQI (equivalent to a 1-unit increase in pre-scaled TFQI) was associated with 
higher odds of amputation (OR 2.27, 95% CI 1.63-3.15; P < 0.001). Compared with 
Q1, ORs were 2.94 (0.98-8.83; P = 0.055), 5.60 (1.88-16.67; P = 0.002), and 
14.79 (5.22-41.89; P < 0.001) for Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively. RCS showed an 
overall association (P = 0.002) and nonlinearity (P = 0.046) in Model 3. Firth 
estimates were broadly consistent with conventional regression.
CONCLUSION: Among hospitalized DFU patients with normal thyroid function, higher 
TFQI levels are associated with an increased risk of amputation during 
hospitalization. Nevertheless, the clinical utility of TFQI requires further 
validation in prospective studies.

Genome-scale evidence for host-associated lineage divergence in the parasitoid, 
Microctonus aethiopoides.

Hussain M(1), Parvizi E(1), McNeill MR(2), McGaughran A(1).

Author information:
(1)Te Aka Mātuatua - School of Science, University of Waikato, Hamilton, New 
Zealand.
(2)Bioeconomy Science Institute, Tuhiraki, Christchurch, New Zealand.

Parasitoids closely rely on their hosts for successful reproduction and 
development. This dependence, combined with exposure to different environmental 
conditions, can lead to ecological specialisation and divergent selection. The 
parasitoid Microctonus aethiopoides serves as a valuable model for investigating 
such processes, as its use as a biocontrol agent against weevils of the genera 
Hypera and Sitona has revealed clear intraspecific divergence largely driven by 
different host pressures. This study examined M. aethiopoides strains from three 
different host species (Hypera postica, Sitona discoideus, Sitona obsoletus) and

H. postica-associated strain from those associated with Sitona species. This 
separation was accompanied by distinct heterozygosity patterns, with the H. 
postica strain showing the highest heterozygosity, followed by S. discoideus and 
S. obsoletus-associated strains, and the lowest heterozygosity observed in the 
S. obsoletus-associated Irish strain, most likely due to its asexual 
reproductive mode. Further comparisons indicated that most gene families were 
conserved across strains, with rapid evolution of transposable element-related 
genes suggesting ongoing genomic diversification among strains. Chemosensory 
gene family classification showed broad conservation of these genes across 
strains, with modest variation in odourant receptor copy numbers. Overall, our 
study suggests that host associations may be key drivers of genomic divergence 
within M. aethiopoides strains, with this primarily driven by genome-level 
variation and limited evidence for major changes at the gene family level.

Planned Biologic Discontinuation in Severe Asthma: A Systematic Review and

Srivali N(1), De Giacomi F(2).

Author information:
(1)Division of Pulmonary, Allergy, and Critical Care Medicine, Duke University 
School of Medicine, DUMC 102356, Durham, NC 27710, USA.
(2)Respiratory Unit, Cremona Hospital, Viale Concordia 1, 26100 Cremona, Italy.

OBJECTIVE: Biologic agents targeting IgE, IL-5/IL-5Rα, IL-4Rα, and TSLP have 
transformed severe asthma outcomes. Whether planned discontinuation of biologics 
after achieving sustained asthma control is safe and feasible remains 
unresolved.
DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane (inception to June 2026); reference 
lists were hand-searched.
STUDY SELECTION: RCTs and observational cohort studies enrolling patients (≥12 
years) with severe asthma who achieved sustained control on an approved biologic 
(≥12 months) before planned discontinuation/tapering; non-response-driven 
discontinuation and studies with ≤10 participants were excluded. Primary 
outcome: uncontrolled asthma or exacerbation within 12 months; secondary 
outcomes included symptom scores, lung function, biomarker rebound, and 
resumption rate of biologics.
RESULTS: Twenty-three studies were included (3 RCTs [n = 897], 2 non-randomized 
comparator cohorts [n = 77], 17 single-arm cohorts, 1 mixed-biologic registry 
[n = 118]). Two randomized withdrawal trials, XPORT (omalizumab; risk ratio [RR] 
1.59; 95% CI, 1.11-2.27) and COMET (mepolizumab; RR 1.29; 95% CI, 1.03-1.61), 
yielded a pooled RR of 1.36 (95% CI, 1.13-1.65; I2=0%; moderate certainty). An 
exploratory pool adding DESTINATION (tezepelumab; RR 1.22; 95% CI, 0.88-1.68; 
non-equivalent comparator) yielded RR 1.32 (95% CI, 1.13-1.56). No eligible 
dupilumab or reslizumab study was identified. Biomarker rebound followed 
class-specific kinetics; baseline eosinophilia ≥300 cells/μL and exacerbation 
burden predicted relapse, with no withdrawal syndrome.
CONCLUSION: Biologic discontinuation in severe asthma carries a 
moderate-certainty increased exacerbation risk. Because universal de-escalation 
criteria cannot yet be defined, decisions should be individualized, guided by 
eosinophil count, exacerbation history, remission duration, and biomarker 
trajectory, until prospective trial data become available.

OBJECTIVE: Mobile health tools offer scalable strategies for asthma 
self-management, but relationships between usability, engagement, and clinical 
outcomes remain unclear. We evaluated whether usability of ASTHMAXcel PRO, a 
mobile asthma education and self-management application, promotes educational 
engagement and whether early engagement predicts asthma outcomes.

mucosa. OMLs can be a localized disease due to trauma or infections, a 
manifestation of systemic or dermatological disease, or a sign of neoplasia. The 
aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of OMLs among Finnish adults.
METHODS: Dentist-nurse teams performed clinical oral health examinations among a 
nationally representative sample of Finnish adults. Sociodemographic 
characteristics recorded included age and sex.

were clinically examined (51.6% participation rate) in 2023. The prevalence 
estimate of OMLs in the Finnish population was 33.2% (95% CI: 26.8, 40.3) and

procedures in high-risk patients with limited options and resulted in healthy 
neonates without apparent comorbidities.

Quantification of Intact MDa Poly(A)-Tailed and Non-Tailed mRNA Fractions with 
Charge Detection Mass Spectrometry.

Robles J(1), Miller ZM(1), Roe AM(2), Thibert SM(2), Gardner MR(2), Magaling 
JTM(2), Torpey JW(2), Castañeda AF(2), Williams ER(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chemistry, University of California, Berkeley,

(2)Scribe Therapeutics , Alameda, California94501, United States.

The clinical success of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) therapeutics has 
driven the need for robust analytical techniques capable of characterizing 
mixtures of megadalton (MDa) constructs. A critical attribute of these 
therapeutics is the presence and length of the 3' poly(A) tail, which governs 
mRNA stability and translational efficiency. Charge detection mass spectrometry 
(CDMS) was used to distinguish and quantify intact MDa mRNA variants differing 
only by the poly(A) content. Initial analysis under native-like conditions was 
limited by salt adduction, but a 75% methanol solution resulted in nearly a 
five-fold increase in charge (from ∼60e to ∼280e) and substantially less 
adduction. Measured masses of the intact mRNA were 1.054 MDa and 1.027 MDa for 
the tailed and non-tailed mRNA constructs, respectively, consistent with the 
theoretical 26.6 kDa mass difference. Mixtures of various compositions resulted 
in broad, unresolved peaks at intermediate mass owing to residual salt 
adduction. A constrained Gaussian deconvolution of these data enabled accurate 
quantification across seven different mole fractions (R2 = 0.978). Notably, an 
analysis of a subpopulation of the highest charge-state ions revealed separation 
into two distinct peaks, demonstrating that mass resolution for MDa mRNA 
analysis is limited by adduction rather than instrumental factors, motivating 
additional studies on methods to increase charging for more accurate 
quantification. These results establish CDMS as a powerful, top-down method for 
precise monitoring of mRNA heterogeneity and degradation in high molecular 
weight therapeutics.

Multiway Modeling of 2D NMR Spectra for Enhanced Chemical Characterization of 
Complex Mixtures.

Mayer PS(1), Engelsen SB(1), Hinrich JL(2), Mørup M(2), Khakimov B(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Food Science, University of Copenhagen, Rolighedsvej 26, 
Frederiksberg1958, Denmark.
(2)Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science, Technical University 
of Denmark, Richard Petersens Plads 321, Kgs. Lyngby2800, Denmark.

One-dimensional (1D) proton nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is 
widely used for complex mixture analysis because of its high reproducibility, 
minimal sample preparation, and inherent quantitative capabilities. However, 1D 
NMR remains constrained by three interrelated limitations: signal overlap among 
compounds, chemical-shift variability of the same compounds across samples, and 
masking of low signal-to-noise features by neighboring high-intensity 
resonances. Two-dimensional (2D) NMR spectroscopy can reduce these limitations 
by dispersing spectral information over a second dimension and providing 
additional structural information. Yet its broader implementation in large-scale 
studies remains limited by a major data-processing bottleneck: the analysis of 
multisample, high-dimensional 2D NMR data sets. When acquired across multiple 
samples, 2D NMR spectra form three-way tensors that contain richer chemical 
information than conventional 1D data sets but are not readily handled by 
standard NMR data analysis workflows. In this paper, we discuss how localized 2D 
spectral alignment combined with tensor decomposition and shift-tolerant 
multilinear modeling, including PARAFAC, PARAFAC2, and shift-invariant 
approaches, can recover overlapped, shifted, and low-intensity signals from 
complex 2D NMR spectra. These workflows hold considerable promise for advancing 
NMR-based complex mixture analysis by expanding metabolite coverage, improving 
deconvolution of elusive signals, and enabling more reliable quantification of 
low-abundance biomarkers in large-scale studies.

Atmospheric aerosol viscosity governs diffusion time scales of reactive gases 
into aerosols, thereby influencing gas uptake, heterogeneous chemistry, and 
atmospheric aging. However, direct viscosity measurements of individual 
semisolid aerosols have been restricted to a relatively high viscosity range and 
submicrometer size. Herein, a new atomic force microscopy-based nanorheological

Li MH(1), Zhang X(1), Su XC(1).

Author information:
(1)State Key Laboratory of Elemento-organic Chemistry, College of Chemistry,

Lanthanoid are indispensable for modern technologies including high-performance 
magnets, electronics, renewable energy, and medical imaging. However, their 
similar ionic radii and chemical properties make it inherently challenging for 
existing chemical, biochemical, and optical probes to distinguish individual 
Ln3+ ions in mixtures. It is even more difficult to simultaneously quantify 
multiple Ln3+ ions in solution. Due to their distinct magnetic anisotropy, Ln3+ 
ions and their complexes exhibit a wide range of magnetic anisotropies (except 
for La3+, Gd3+, and Lu3+) and exert differential effects on the NMR signals of 
nuclear spins surrounding the metal center. Designing high-performance probes 
for Ln3+ ion binding and discrimination is a great challenge because of their 
high coordination numbers and their tendency to form multiple conformations. 
Here, we designed and synthesized two chemical-magnetic probes (CF3-TDA and 
F-TDA), each containing a 19F reporter and metal chelating moiety, for 
simultaneous discrimination and quantification of Ln3+ ions in solution thanks 
to the distinct magnetic anisotropy of Ln3+ ions. These probes form stable 
lanthanoid complexes, generating well-resolved 19F NMR chemical shifts induced 
by the distinct magnetic anisotropy of Ln3+. This strategy enables the 
simultaneous identification and quantification of individual Ln3+ in mixtures, 
even in the presence of competing common metal ions. This approach combines the 
metal-chelating property and distinct magnetic anisotropy for lanthanoid ion 
quantification by NMR. It provides a conceptually innovative and broadly 
applicable platform for precise lanthanoid assays, facilitating the monitoring 
of critical elements in industrial and strategic contexts.

Controlling interfacial charge without compromising mass transport remains a 
challenge in charge-selective electrochemical sensing. Here, we use phosphate 
adsorption on indium tin oxide (ITO) as a model system to investigate how 
specifically adsorbed anions regulate the apparent electron-transfer kinetics 
and enable charge-selective electrochemical sensing. Using three ferrocene 
derivatives with distinct charge states, we show that phosphate adsorption 
enhances the voltammetric response of cationic species while suppressing that of 
anionic species, in a manner strongly dependent on pH and phosphate speciation. 
To elucidate the underlying mechanism, we directly quantify shifts in the 
potential of zero charge using scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) 
and correlate these measurements with the observed kinetic trends. Comparison of 
orthophosphate, pyrophosphate, and tripolyphosphate demonstrates that

electrostatic modulation. Leveraging this effect, we achieve charge-selective 
electro-oxidation of dopamine in the presence of ascorbic acid and uric acid, 
with oligophosphate adsorption further enhancing the discrimination of dopamine 
and yielding detection limits of 0.15 and 0.11 μM for pyrophosphate and 
tripolyphosphate, respectively. The reversibility of phosphate adsorption under 
mild alkaline treatment further establishes this approach as a simple and 
regenerable alternative to conventional film-based interface engineering.

p-Type Dopant-Mediated Electron-Hole Recombineering to Tune the 
Electrochemiluminescence of Metal-Organic Frameworks.

Li G(1), Luo S(1), Zhang S(1), Li M(1), Liu H(2), Ju H(1).

Author information:
(1)State Key Laboratory of Analytical Chemistry for Life Science, School of 
Chemistry, Nanjing University, Nanjing210023, China.
(2)College of Smart Materials and Future Energy, Fudan University, 
Shanghai200438, China.

Constructing high-performance electrochemiluminescence (ECL) emitters through 
rational structural engineering is pivotal to overcoming the intrinsic 
limitations of conventional systems and advancing their practical applications. 
This work reports an electron-hole recombination engineering strategy to enhance 
the ECL emission of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) by p-type doping of metal 
single-atom sites. Using Zr-TBAPy as a model, the experimental data and 
theoretical calculations demonstrate that the doping of single-atom Au induces 
notable defect energy levels, thereby providing additional recombination 
channels for conduction-band (CB) electrons and valence-band (VB) holes. The 
defect level ultimately increases the electron-hole recombination efficiency. 
Compared to Zr-TBAPy, single-atom Au-doped Zr-TBAPy (Au@Zr-TBAPy) exhibits a 
4-fold enhancement in cathodic ECL intensity with an ECL efficiency of up to 
50.56%. An ECL immunoassay was used to demonstrate the ECL application of 
Au@Zr-TBAPy. This work not only proposes a rational metal single-atom doping 
strategy for engineering ECL emitters to achieve high performance but also 
provides fundamental insights into the dependence of ECL emission on metal 
single-atom sites, opening new avenues for advanced applications of MOFs in 
sensitive ECL biosensing.

Electrochemical Dual-Sensing Platform for HLA-B*13:01 Detection to Prevent 
Severe Cutaneous Adverse Reactions (SCARs) Induced by Dapsone and Cotrimoxazole.

Attapong J(1)(2), Kaset C(1)(2), Nakkam N(3), Tassaneeyakul W(3), Kamsong W(4), 
Karuwan C(4), Sukasem C(5), Chomean S(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Medical Technology, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, 
Thammasat University, Pathum Thani12120, Thailand.
(2)Thammasat University Research Unit in Medical Technology and Precision 
Medicine Innovation, Pathum Thani12120, Thailand.
(3)Department of Pharmacology, Faculty of Medicine, Khon Kaen University, Khon 
Kaen40002, Thailand.
(4)National Nanotechnology Center (NANOTEC), National Science and Technology 
Development Agency (NSTDA), Pathum Thani12120, Thailand.
(5)Division of Pharmacogenomics and Personalized Medicine, Department of 
Pathology, Faculty of Medicine, Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok10400, Thailand.

The HLA-B*13:01 allele is a critical biomarker for dapsone- and 
cotrimoxazole-induced severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs). Overcoming the 
limitations of centralized laboratory screening, we developed a portable 
electrochemical dual-sensing platform (EDP) for the simultaneous, ultrasensitive 
detection of HLA-B*13:01 alongside a TIMP-1 internal control. On screen-printed 
carbon electrodes (SPCEs), TIMP-1 is captured through robust biotin-streptavidin 
interactions, while HLA-B*13:01 relies on sequence-specific ssDNA hybridization. 
Crucially, the system utilizes methylene blue (MB) to precisely modulate both 
electrostatic repulsion and physical steric hindrance, enhancing signal 
discrimination. The platform demonstrates exceptional limits of detection, 
reaching 0.992 pg and 65.5 fg when evaluated by electrochemical impedance 
spectroscopy (EIS) and cyclic voltammetry (CV), respectively. Notably, 
accounting for genomic copy number, this corresponds to a practical detection 
limit of ∼3 HLA-B gene copies (1 × 10-2 ng genomic DNA), several orders of 
magnitude below conventional gel electrophoresis. Validated against 100 blinded 
clinical samples, the EDP achieved 100% sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy 
using ROC-derived cut-offs. By delivering a highly scalable, portable post-PCR 
screening tool, this work provides a high-performance alternative to standard 
methods, effectively mitigating SCAR risks and advancing the global 
accessibility of precision medicine.

Monitoring of Doxorubicin-Mediated Mitochondria-Lysosome Crosstalk by In Situ 
Raman Spectroscopy: The Molecular Mechanism during Apoptosis and Implications 
for Cardiotoxicity.

Song L(1)(2), Wang Z(1), Chen Y(1), Li W(2), Zhu J(2), Cai L(1), Han XX(2).

Author information:
(1)National Engineering Laboratory for AIDS Vaccine, School of Life Sciences, 
Jilin University, Changchun130012, P. R. China.
(2)State Key Laboratory of Supramolecular Structure and Materials, College of 
Chemistry, Jilin University, Changchun130012, P. R. China.

Doxorubicin is among the most commonly used chemotherapeutic agents for a wide 
range of cancers. Despite its effectiveness, it poses long-term cardiotoxic 
risks that elevate mortality among cancer patients. In this study, 
doxorubicin-mediated mitochondria-lysosome crosstalk in apoptosis and the 
underlying molecular mechanism are explored. The interactions between 
organelle-specific phospholipids and doxorubicin, and their structural basis, 
are investigated using comprehensive spectroscopy and molecular dynamics 
simulations. Our results by in situ Raman spectroscopy reveal that doxorubicin 
can directly trigger mitochondrial and lysosomal permeabilization, facilitating 
the release of key apoptotic modulators. Besides phospholipids, doxorubicin is 
found to interact with cytochrome c and boost its proapoptotic effect. Further 
study indicates that protecting cardiolipin is sufficient to inhibit 
doxorubicin-induced disruption of CL conformation. Accordingly, the molecular 
mechanism underlying doxorubicin-mediated mitochondria-lysosome crosstalk in 
apoptosis is proposed, paving the way for the rational design of 
cardioprotective agents targeting mitochondria and lysosomes for cancer 
patients.

Task-Dependent Synergy between FTIR and Raman Spectroscopy for Sperm Quality 
Prediction.

Campanella B(1), Birindelli L(1), Legnaioli S(1), Lorenzetti G(1), Consani C(2), 
Ales V(2), Benedetti E(3), Bertozzi MA(2), Bramanti E(1).

Author information:
(1)Istituto di Chimica dei Composti Organometallici - Consiglio Nazionale delle 
Ricerche (ICCOM-CNR) , via Giuseppe Moruzzi 1, Pisa56124, Italy.
(2)Unità di Andrologia, Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria Pisana, via Roma 67, 
Pisa56124, Italy.
(3)Unità di Ematologia, Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria Pisana, via Roma 67, 
Pisa56124, Italy.

Male infertility affects approximately 15% of couples worldwide, contributing to 
40-50% of infertility cases in Western countries. Standard semen analysis 
remains the cornerstone of fertility assessment, yet conventional parameters 
(concentration, motility, morphology) have limited predictive value for 
fertilization success. Vibrational spectroscopy, particularly Fourier transform 
infrared (FTIR) and Raman spectroscopy, offers rapid, nondestructive chemical 
fingerprinting of biological samples. However, optimal strategies for 
integrating multimodal spectroscopic data remain unclear, and the value of 
fusion may depend on the biological end point. This study systematically 
compares FTIR and Raman spectroscopy, both independently and through multiple 
fusion strategies, for predicting rectilinear progressive sperm motility (binary 
classification) and normal morphology (continuous regression) in human seminal 
plasma. We determine whether complementary information exists, when fusion 
provides value, and which strategy optimally leverages multimodal data. Building 
on Raman-derived Multivariate Curve Resolution-Alternating Least Squares 
(MCR-ALS) concentration profiles, we further develop a clinical classifier based 
on four seminal plasma biomarkers (human serum albumin, glutathione 
S-transferase, transferrin, lysophosphatidylcholine), validated by 
leave-one-patient-out cross-validation and Firth's penalized logistic regression 
to address near-complete separation in this small-sample setting (n = 30). Our 
findings reveal technique-specific advantages: Raman spectroscopy substantially 
outperforms FTIR for binary motility classification, with feature-level fusion 
matching but not exceeding Raman's performance, indicating limited 
complementarity. Conversely, FTIR alone achieves superior predictive accuracy 
for continuous morphological outcomes. The clinical classifier based on 
MCR-ALS-derived biomarkers achieved AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) = 0.855, 
accuracy = 86.7%, and BER (Balanced Error Rate) = 0.136, with model significance 
confirmed by permutation testing. Elevated human serum albumin and 
lysophosphatidylcholine emerged as the strongest negative predictors of high 
motility, consistent with seminal tract inflammation and sperm-cytotoxic 
phospholipid accumulation, while transferrin showed a positive association in 
line with its role in iron availability for sperm function. These results 
demonstrate that optimal spectroscopic approaches depend on the biological end 
point, with Raman's structural sensitivity favoring motility assessment and 
FTIR's compositional profiling better capturing morphological variation. The 
biomarker-based classifier is easier to interpret and complements whole-spectrum 
models by bridging chemometric analysis and biological interpretation.

Antimony-Doped Violet Phosphorus Nanosheets: Band Gap Engineering for Enhanced 
Photodynamic Effect and Efficient Antibacterial Activity.

Gao Y(1), Wu X(1), Wang H(1), Li J(1), Kang J(1), Jian W(2), Zhang J(3), Dong 
A(1).

Author information:
(1)College of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Engineering Research Center of 
Dairy, Quality and Safety Control Technology, Ministry of Education, Inner 
Mongolia University, 235 University West Street, Hohhot010021, People's Republic 
of China.
(2)Inner Mongolia Key Laboratory of Green Catalysis, College of Chemistry and 
Environmental Science, Inner Mongolia Normal University, Hohhot010022, People's 
Republic of China.
(3)State Key Laboratory of Electrical Insulation and Power Equipment, Center of 
Nanomaterials for Renewable Energy (CNRE), School of Electrical Engineering, 
Xi'an Jiaotong University, Xi'an710049, People's Republic of China.

Bacterial infections pose a severe threat to public health worldwide, and 
overuse of traditional antibiotics induces bacterial resistance, limiting the 
efficacy of conventional therapies. Two-dimensional violet phosphorus nanosheets 
(VPNS) have emerged as promising photodynamic antibacterial materials owing to 
their unique layered structure and light-responsive capability. However, the 
inherent wide band gap of VPNS restricts photogenerated electron transition and 
reactive oxygen species production, resulting in unsatisfactory photodynamic 
therapy efficiency, which severely hinders their biomedical applications. To 
address these limitations, a facile antimony (Sb) doping strategy is developed 
to modulate the electronic band structure of VPNS for significantly boosted 
photodynamic antibacterial performance. As a congener of phosphorus, Sb 
possesses excellent optical and electrical properties, which can effectively 
optimize the photoelectric characteristics of VPNS. Results confirm that Sb 
doping narrows the band gap of VPNS from 1.91 to 1.42 eV and boosts reactive 
oxygen species (ROS) generation by 2.3-fold. In mouse skin wound infection 
models, Sb-doped VPNS (VPSb) achieves remarkable therapeutic efficacy against 
Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) infection and accelerates wound healing at a 
low concentration of 0.1 mg/mL. The optimized VPSb, with its excellent 
therapeutic performance, demonstrates great application prospects for clinical 
bacterial wound infection therapy.

Acceptability and Experience of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Adult ADHD: A 
Systematic Review With Narrative Synthesis.

Sobolak R(1), Aho B(1), Hunter MS(1), Foster JLH(1), Dommett EJ(1).

Author information:
(1)King's College London, UK.

OBJECTIVES: Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) is a first-line psychosocial 
treatment for adults with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). While 
its clinical efficacy has been the focus of considerable research, the 
acceptability of CBT for ADHD remains under-studied. This is a critical gap, as 
core ADHD deficits may impact on acceptability and, therefore, utility. This 
review evaluates CBT acceptability for adults with ADHD using the Theoretical 
Framework of Acceptability (TFA).
METHOD: Five databases (Scopus, PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science and PsycINFO) 
were systematically searched in February 2026. Twenty-one studies including 
randomised controlled trials, pilot, feasibility, qualitative and mixed-methods 
studies, were included. Data were integrated and mapped to the seven TFA 
domains.
RESULTS: Across studies, CBT acceptability in adults with ADHD most strongly 
explored the domains of affective attitude, intervention coherence, perceived 
effectiveness and self-efficacy. Acceptability was driven by skills training, 
psychoeducation, therapeutic support, accountability strategies, 
individualisation and diverse materials. Burden was linked to homework, 
cognitive load and treatment intensity, while opportunity costs and ethicality 
were rarely reported. Group and digital formats were generally acceptable but 
dependent on facilitation quality, accessibility and therapeutic presence. CBT 
for adult ADHD is most acceptable when it enhances affective response, 
understanding, perceived effectiveness and self-efficacy while minimising 
burden.
CONCLUSIONS: Acceptability is optimised through structured, flexible 
interventions with therapeutic support, accountability, individualisation and 
engaging delivery. Rather than being determined by intervention format alone, 
acceptability reflects the combined influence of intervention content, delivery 
approach and treatment intensity. Future research should use standardised, 
prospective measures of acceptability and further explore ethicality, burden and 
opportunity costs. (J. of Att. Dis. XXXX; XX(X) XX-XX).

METTL3 destabilizes RFX7 to ameliorate PDGF-BB-induced airway smooth muscle cell 
dysfunction and inflammation in an in vitro model of childhood asthma.

Chenxia D(1), Shao Z(1), Zhan L(1), Shen D(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pediatrics, Hangzhou Red Cross Hospital, Hangzhou, 310003, 
Zhejiang, China.

BACKGROUND: Childhood asthma represents a significant global health burden, 
characterized by chronic airway inflammation and remodeling. Regulatory factor 
X7 (RFX7) has emerged as a potential key player in asthma pathogenesis. However, 
its specific role in modulating airway smooth muscle cell (ASMC) dysfunction-a 
hallmark of asthma pathology-remains poorly understood.
METHODS: An in vitro asthma model was established by stimulating airway smooth 
muscle cells (ASMCs) with platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB). 
Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and Western blotting were employed to 
measure the mRNA and protein expression levels of RFX7 and METTL3, respectively. 
Functional assays, including 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine incorporation, Transwell, 
and wound-healing assays, were utilized to evaluate ASMC proliferation, 
invasion, and migration. Inflammatory responses were assessed by enzyme-linked 
immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) targeting interleukin-6 (IL-6).
RESULTS: RFX7 expression levels were significantly elevated in the serum of 
pediatric asthma patients and in PDGF-BB-induced ASMCs, whereas METTL3 
expression was downregulated. PDGF-BB stimulation enhanced ASMC proliferation, 
invasion, and migration, all of which were markedly attenuated by RFX7 
knockdown. Furthermore, RFX7 deficiency reduced PDGF-BB-induced production of 
IL-6, TNF-α, ROS, and MDA, as well as the proportion of CD86-positive 
macrophages. Notably, METTL3 exhibited a negative correlation with RFX7 in 
patient sera and destabilized RFX7 transcripts in a YTHDF2-dependent manner. 
Consequently, overexpression of METTL3 alleviated PDGF-BB-induced ASMC 
dysfunction by downregulating RFX7.
CONCLUSION: METTL3-mediated destabilization of RFX7 ameliorated PDGF-BB-induced 
ASMC proliferation, migration, and invasion, while simultaneously suppressing 
inflammation, oxidative stress, and macrophage polarization. Targeting this 
METTL3-RFX7 axis may offer a novel therapeutic strategy to mitigate airway 
remodeling and inflammation in childhood asthma.

Dual-Enzyme-Driven Thermosensitive Hydrogel Triggers Disulfidptosis and 
Alleviates Hypoxia for Enhanced Osteosarcoma Radiosensitization.

Zhu T(1), Liu Y(1), Hu W(2), Tang J(3), Song S(4), Li K(5), Zhan Y(6), Liu C(3), 
Feng Y(3)(7), Zhou Y(2), Zhan W(3)(7).

Author information:
(1)The First Clinical Medical College, Ningxia Medical University, Yinchuan, 
Ningxia750004, China.
(2)College of Clinical Medicine, Xi'an Medical University, Xi'an, Shaanxi710021, 
China.
(3)Department of Radiation Oncology, General Hospital of Ningxia Medical 
University, Yinchuan, Ningxia750004, China.
(4)School of Life Sciences, Jishou University, Jishou, Hunan416000, China.
(5)Xi'an Key Laboratory for Prevention and Treatment of Common Aging Diseases, 
Translational and Research Centre for Prevention and Therapy of Chronic Disease, 
Institute of Basic and Translational Medicine, Xi'an Medical University, Xi'an, 
Shaanxi710021, China.
(6)School of Life Science and Technology, Xidian University and Engineering 
Research Center of Molecular and Neuro Imaging, Ministry of Education, Xi'an,

(7)State Key Laboratory of Pathogenesis, Prevention and Treatment of High

Osteosarcoma shows poor responsiveness to radiotherapy (RT), largely due to the 
efficient DNA damage repair capacity of tumor cells and the hypoxic tumor 
microenvironment. In addition, achieving adequate safe surgical margins after 
resection remains difficult, contributing to low long-term patient survival. 
Current clinical radiosensitization strategies are limited by insufficient tumor 
specificity and considerable systemic toxicity. In this study, we loaded glucose 
oxidase (GOx) and catalase (CAT) into a thermosensitive hydrogel to construct a 
local cascade catalytic system, termed FS-GC. The SLC7A11-mediated conversion of 
cystine to cysteine is highly dependent on glucose availability. GOx consumes 
glucose and depletes NADPH, increasing the NADP+/NADPH ratio and promoting 
cystine accumulation. This triggers filamentous actin contraction and 
downregulation of filamin A, thereby inhibiting DNA repair proteins and inducing 
disulfidptosis. Meanwhile, CAT converts H2O2 generated by GOx into oxygen to 
alleviate local hypoxia. FS-GC exhibits favorable biosafety, structural 
stability, and sustained enzyme release and degrades almost completely within 14 
days. In vitro and in vivo results confirm that FS-GC suppresses DNA repair and 
relieves hypoxia through disulfidptosis and the dual catalytic activity of GOx 
and CAT, leading to significantly enhanced RT efficacy and inhibition of 
osteosarcoma progression.

Mediation and Moderation Effects in a Blended Physical Activity Intervention for 
Office Employees.

Sun Y(1)(2), Gao Y(2), Wang X(2), Ou AYT(2), Tao D(2), Xie Y(3), Zhang D(3), 
Baker JS(4).

Author information:
(1)The Chinese University of Hong Kong, China.
(2)Hong Kong Baptist University, China.
(3)The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, China.
(4)Ningbo Second Hospital, China.

Physical inactivity is a critical global health challenge, especially for 
sedentary office employees. Blended interventions show promise for improving 
moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), but their mechanisms remain 
understudied. This study investigated the mediation effects of theoretical 
determinants and the moderation effects of sociodemographic characteristics on 
MVPA changes. Data were drawn from a 24-week randomized controlled trial 
(N = 141) comprising a blended intervention, a web-based intervention, and a 
control group. The intervention, developed using Intervention Mapping and 
informed by dual-process perspectives on behavior change, incorporated 
motivational, self-regulatory, and habit-formation strategies to promote MVPA. 
The blended intervention combined web-based modules with live e-workshops to 
enhance engagement and support behavior change. Mediation analyses identified 
self-efficacy as the only significant mediator, specifically for the effect of 
the blended intervention versus control on MVPA change from baseline to 
follow-up 12 weeks after the intervention, suggesting its potential role in 
short-term maintenance of behavior change. Moderation analyses indicated that 
the relative effects of the blended intervention varied across sociodemographic 
subgroups, with stronger effects observed among males, participants aged 29 
years or older, participants with lower education levels, and non-single 
participants in specific group comparisons and time points. These findings 
provide insights for optimizing MVPA interventions by strengthening 
self-efficacy and tailoring strategies to sociodemographic subgroups. Future 
research with larger, adequately powered samples, extended follow-up periods, 
and more diverse populations is needed to confirm these mediation and moderation 
pathways and further refine theoretical models underlying blended interventions.

Selective recovery effects of short-term beetroot juice supplementation after 
exercise-induced muscle damage in trained female volleyball players.

Zhang S(1)(2), Yang X(3), Xu H(1), Liu Q(4), Quan H(1).

Author information:
(1)Exercise Capacity Assessment and Promotion Research Center, School of 
Physical Education, Northeast Normal University, Changchun, Jilin, People's 
Republic of China.
(2)China Volleyball College, Beijing Sport University, Beijing, People's 
Republic of China.
(3)Department of Sport Science, Chungnam National University, Daejeon, South 
Korea.
(4)Jilin Green Food Engineering Research Institute, Changchun, Jilin, People's 
Republic of China.

BACKGROUND: Beetroot juice (BRJ) has been proposed as a nutritional aid for 
recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), but evidence in female 
team-sport athletes is limited. It also remains unclear whether any benefit 
extends across functional, pain-related, swelling, and strength outcomes.
METHODS: Seventeen female university volleyball players entered a randomized, 
double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Four did not complete the 
second period, so outcomes were analyzed with linear mixed models. After 
baseline testing, participants performed 200 loaded vertical jumps and consumed 
BRJ or placebo at 24, 48, and 72 h post-EIMD. Recovery outcomes were 
countermovement jump (CMJ) height, volleyball-specific agility time, pressure 
pain threshold, thigh circumference, visual analog scale soreness, and knee 
isokinetic measures. Holm-adjusted planned contrasts were used.
RESULTS: CMJ height was the clearest BRJ-related functional finding. The 
treatment × time interaction showed a trend toward statistical significance 
(P = 0.062), and CMJ height was higher under BRJ than PLA at 72 h post-EIMD 
(P = 0.033, d = 1.01). Calf pressure pain threshold also favored BRJ at 72 h, 
accompanied by a significant treatment × time interaction (P < 0.001). In 
contrast, agility time and soreness changed over time without clear 
between-condition differences, while thigh pressure pain threshold, thigh 
circumference, and low-velocity knee isokinetic outcomes showed no consistent 
BRJ-related advantage.
CONCLUSIONS: Short-term BRJ supplementation was associated with selective rather 
than generalized recovery benefits after EIMD in trained female volleyball 
players. The clearest findings were higher CMJ height and calf PPT under BRJ 
than PLA at 72 h, whereas the remaining outcomes showed no consistent 
treatment-related differences.

Correlation of Neuron-Specific Enolase and S100ß Protein Levels, Inflammatory 
Cytokines, and Neurological Injury in Children Undergoing Cardiopulmonary 
Bypass.

Twite M(1), Sophocles A(1), Pan Z(1), Friesen R(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Anesthesiology, Children's Hospital Colorado, University of 
Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, Aurora, Colorado, USA.

BACKGROUND: The systemic inflammatory response syndrome to cardiopulmonary 
bypass (CPB) affects all organ systems including the brain. Perioperative brain 
injury in children with congenital heart disease is often clinically silent in 
the acute perioperative period and may not be detected until patients are older. 
The plasma biomarkers neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and S100ß protein show 
potential for detecting neurological injury in the perioperative period.
OBJECTIVES: The three objectives of this study were to examine the correlation 
of NSE and S100ß protein levels with inflammatory cytokines, parameters of CPB, 
and the development of neurological injury in the intensive care unit following 
cardiac surgery in children.
METHODS: 50 children undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB had blood samples drawn 
at three time points: after induction of anesthesia, 30 min post-CPB, and 24 h 
post-CPB. Blood samples were analyzed for NSE, S100ß, and the inflammatory 
cytokines IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10. Data were collected on CPB durations and 
neurological injury diagnosed in the postoperative period.
RESULTS: NSE and S100ß increased significantly following bypass and correlated 
with increases of IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10. There was a significant positive 
correlation of NSE and S100ß with duration of CPB, and of S100ß with duration of 
aortic cross clamp. Three patients suffered neurological insult. These patients 
had greater levels of NSE during the post-CPB period (p = 0.02) and S100ß at 
24 h post-CPB (p = 0.02) than patients without neurological deficits.
CONCLUSION: The positive correlation between NSE, S100ß, inflammatory cytokines, 
and neurological deficits suggests that the systemic inflammatory response to 
CPB may contribute to neurological injury and that NSE and S100ß may be useful 
tools to detect neurological injury following CPB.

Computer-assisted voice training for bilateral vocal fold paralysis following

Fang G(1), Zhou Q(1), Wang C(1), Zhuang R(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Rehabilitation Medicine, Changzhou Dean Hospital, Changzhou,

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term efficacy of computer-assisted voice 
training in a patient with bilateral vocal fold paralysis (BVFP) following 
traumatic brain injury (TBI), a condition for which no standardized non-surgical 
protocol exists and long-term objective outcome data are entirely absent.
METHODS: A 27-year-old female with severe TBI who developed BVFP after 
tracheostomy decannulation underwent 3 months of computer-assisted voice 
training (five sessions per week, 20 min per session) targeting maximum 
phonation time and vocal intensity via visual biofeedback. Voice outcomes were 
assessed using the Dysphonia Severity Index (DSI), maximum phonation time (MPT), 
jitter, shimmer, and the Voice Handicap Index-10 (VHI-10), with follow-ups at 6 
and 26 months. Fiberoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES) was also 
performed.
RESULTS: DSI improved dramatically from -22.28 at baseline to +0.73 at 26 months 
(a 23.01-point gain). MPT increased by 191% (from 8.60 s to 25.02 s, exceeding 
normative values), jitter normalized to 0.43%, and VHI-10 improved by 64.7% 
(from 34 to 12). FEES demonstrated improved vocal fold adduction with 
Penetration-Aspiration Scale improvement from 6 to 1.

produce significant and sustained improvements in post-TBI BVFP, offering a 
viable non-surgical rehabilitation option for this rare complication. The

population.

DENV-NS1 drives novel microRNAs to disrupt cerebral endothelial barrier 
functions.

Apoorva(1), Singh SK(1)(2)(3).

Author information:
(1)Molecular Biology Unit, Faculty of Medicine, Institute of Medical Sciences, 
Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi, India.
(2)Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Center for Biomedical Research (ACBR), University of Delhi, 
New Delhi, India.
(3)Delhi School of Public Health (DSPH), University of Delhi, New Delhi, India.

Dengue virus non-structural protein 1 (DENV-NS1) plays a key role in the 
vascular leakage associated with severe dengue; however, the molecular 
mechanisms by which NS1 induces endothelial dysfunction remain poorly 
understood. This study aimed to identify a new aspect of the pathogenic 
strategy: the post-transcriptional reprogramming of host endothelial cells via 
microRNAs (miRNAs) in NS1-induced DENV pathogenesis. Small RNA sequencing and 
subsequent bioinformatic analysis identified novel miRNA-gene regulatory 
networks responsive to DENV-NS1 in human brain microvascular endothelial cells.

critical antiviral components (STAT1, SOCS1-6, OAS1), suggesting suppressed 
interferon signaling. Downregulation of identified novel miRNAs targeting IL-6,

stability, characterized by cytoskeletal remodeling and compromised tight 
junction integrity as a bystander effect of DENV-NS1. The downregulation of

involvement of novel miRNAs in apoptosis regulation and TGF-β/SMAD-mediated 
endothelial cell signaling. Our findings suggest that DENV-NS1 alters 
endothelial miRNA networks, leading to reduced antiviral immunity, increased 
inflammation, and compromised vascular integrity. This study identifies novel 
miRNA-mediated regulatory nodes that could function as therapeutic targets to 
prevent or mitigate dengue-associated vascular leakage.

A Weight-Inclusive Approach in High School Nutrition Education: An Exploratory 
Mixed-Methods Study.

Gamble J(1), Levinson JA(1), Garnett BR(1), Hinchey D(1), Pope L(1).

Author information:
(1)University of Vermont, Burlington, USA.

Nutrition education in schools is a key health promotion strategy that has the 
potential to influence lifelong relationships with food, bodies, and health. 
However, many programs in U.S. schools are taught from a weight-centric approach 
that positions body weight as a primary indicator of health despite evidence of 
associated stigma and harm. Weight-inclusive nutrition (WIN) offers an 
alternative framework that emphasizes non-weight-based indicators of health, 
rejects diet culture, and acknowledges the social determinants of health; yet 
little is known about student outcomes when nutrition is taught from this 
paradigm. This study examined the implementation and preliminary outcomes of a 
newly developed eight-lesson WIN curriculum in high school health education 
classrooms. Pre- and post-intervention surveys were administered to students in 
Grades 7-12 across 17 classrooms in eight schools in the Northeast United States 
(N pre = 292; N post = 263) during fall 2024. Quantitative results showed 
positive shifts across all items, with statistically significant improvements in 
students' endorsement of weight-inclusive beliefs, including reduced 
moralization of food, decreased reliance on appearance-based health judgments, 
and increased recognition that health is socially shaped. Qualitative findings 
revealed emerging critical nutrition literacy-particularly students' ability to 
identify and critique diet culture-alongside continued difficulty disentangling 
weight from health. These findings suggest that, while WIN curricula can 
initiate meaningful shifts in how students conceptualize food, bodies, and 
health, continued efforts are needed to support appropriate educator training 
and strengthen alignment with school-wide policies to sustain long-term change.

Load transfer and energy routing mechanisms in the vibration friction of 
metallic coatings on a compliant substrate.

Huang G(1), Cheng Q(1), Wang Y(1), Yang T(2), Ma C(1)(3), Ren K(1), Wang G(1).

Author information:
(1)College of Mechanical and Electronic Engineering, Nanjing Forestry 
University, Nanjing, 210037, China. wangguoqing@njfu.edu.cn.
(2)State Key Laboratory of Mechanics and Control for Aerospace Structures, 
Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Nanjing 210016, China.
(3)College of Mechanical Engineering, Nanjing University of Industry Technology, 
Nanjing 210023, China.

Normal vibration is widely used to regulate nanoscale friction, but whether the 
resulting reduction in tangential resistance can also suppress the subsurface 
disturbance and protect a compliant Al substrate remains unclear. In this study, 
molecular dynamics simulations were used to investigate vibration friction in 
Ni-, Ti-, and Nb-coated systems supported by the same compliant Al substrate. 
The results reveal that normal vibration redistributes mechanical input between 
the tangential frictional work and mechanical work exchange associated with 
normal vibration. This indicates that a reduction in tangential frictional work 
does not necessarily correspond to enhanced substrate protection, because 
vibration can redirect energy into subsurface deformation. These findings 
establish energy routing as the mechanistic link between vibration input, 
coating load-bearing behavior, and subsurface deformation, providing a 
mechanics-based design principle for nanoscale coated contacts under dynamic 
loading.

A robust Hf(0.5)Zr(0.5)O(2) ferroelectric memory with high remanent polarization 
at 1 V and excellent stability up to 250 °C.

Wu H(1), Ding Y(2), Zhang G(1), Lu X(3), Yan Z(4), Liu JM(4), Yuan G(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Materials Science and Engineering, Nanjing University of Science 
and Technology, Nanjing 210094, China. yuanguoliang@njust.edu.cn.
(2)School of Integrated Circuits, Nanjing University, Suzhou, Jiangsu 215163, 
China. yechengding@nju.edu.cn.
(3)Institute for Advanced Materials, South China Academy of Advanced 
Optoelectronics, South China Normal University, Guangzhou 510006, China.
(4)Laboratory of Solid State Microstructures and School of Physics, Nanjing 
University, Nanjing 210093, China.

The 5.5 nm Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) ferroelectric films exhibit a stable orthorhombic 
(o-) phase and outstanding memory performance near room temperature, achieving a 
remanent polarization (Pr) of 20.5 μC cm-2 under a low operating voltage (Vrw) 
of 1 V. However, upon heating to 250-400 °C, most of the o-phase transforms into 
an antiferroelectric tetragonal (t-) phase. Conversely, a unidirectional 
voltage-pulse "wake-up" process can potentially promote the recovery of the 
t-phase back to the o-phase under high-temperature conditions; as a result, at 
250 °C, Pr reaches 19.3 μC cm-2 at Vrw = 1 V and 25.3 μC cm-2 at Vrw = 1.5 V, 
with the corresponding endurance exceeding 1010 and 109 cycles, respectively. 
Remarkably, most of the restored ferroelectric polarization can be well 
maintained even at elevated temperatures up to 350 °C. Notably, Pr remains ≥24.0 
μC cm-2 at Vrw = 1.5 V across the broad temperature range of 25-250 °C, even 
after ten complete thermal cycling steps (25 °C → 250 °C → 25 °C). This work 
establishes a robust materials foundation for high-density ferroelectric 
memories that simultaneously achieve high-temperature operational stability, low 
write voltage, superior endurance, and excellent retention.

Scientists: A Systematic Review.

Boudilmi M(1), Landais L(1), Guenoun T(2), Smaniotto B(3), Urgese S(2), Ravit 
M(2), Mitsopoulou L(2), Wathelet M(4), Essadek A(5)(6)(7).

Author information:
(1)Université de Lorraine, Nancy, France.
(2)Université Lyon 2, Bron, France.
(3)Université Sorbonne Paris Nord, Villetaneuse, France.
(4)Agence Régionale de Santé, Hauts de France, Lille, France.
(5)Université Paris-Cité, Paris, France.
(6)Hopitaux de Saint-Maurice, France.

This systematic review aims to explore the mental health of police officers and 
digital forensic analysts exposed to cases involving minors who are victims of 
sexual violence. This review places a particular emphasis on secondary traumatic 
stress experienced by these professionals. For this study, seven databases were 
consulted: PubMed, PsycINFO/PsycARTICLE, Web of Science, Cairn, Cochrane, 
Embase, and Biomed, up until February 2025. After preselecting the studies, one 
reviewer extracted the data and assessed the quality of the studies, followed by 
a double-check performed by a second reviewer. Twenty-six articles were included 
in the systematic review. To be included in this review, the articles had to 
focus on the mental health of police officers working with children who are 
victims of sexual violence. The analysis revealed that there is a negative 
impact on police officers, who may develop a form of secondary traumatic stress. 
This stress affects both their professional and personal lives. Additionally, 
the lack of support from their superiors, high workload, and insufficient 
resources in the care systems available contribute to the negative impact on law 
enforcement. This review sheds light on these factors and underscores the need 
to focus more on the needs of these professionals by implementing appropriate 
care measures to preserve psychological well-being and effectiveness.

Study on the Active Pharmaceutical Substances and Potential Quality Markers of 
Yueju Wan Antidepressant Based on Metabolomics.

Sun S(1), Ren H(1), Dong Q(1), Liu L(1), Wang D(1), Zhu Y(1), Zou X(2), Qu Z(1), 
Wu S(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Pharmacy, Harbin University of Commerce, Harbin, China.
(2)Engineering Research Center on Natural Antineoplastic Drugs, Ministry of 
Education, Harbin University of Commerce, Harbin, China.

AIM OF THE STUDY: Integrating metabolomics, network pharmacology, and zebrafish 
depression models, this study explored the pharmacodynamic material basis and 
potential quality markers (Q-markers) of Yueju Wan (YJW) against depression.
METHODS: Chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) was adopted to establish a rat 
depression model for evaluating the antidepressant efficacy of YJW. 
UPLC-QTOF-MS/MS was utilized to characterize the chemical constituents of YJW, 
and relevant databases were employed to predict its potential therapeutic 
targets. Metabolomics analysis was performed to screen differential metabolites 
in serum and urine, followed by pathway enrichment analysis. A 
compound-target-metabolite-pathway interaction network was constructed to screen 
core therapeutic targets and candidate pharmacodynamic substances, and RT-qPCR, 
Western blot, and zebrafish depression models were applied to validate the

detection method for the candidate quality markers was established.

depression-associated differential metabolites. Further integrated analysis

through modulation of arachidonic acid metabolism, microglial polarization, and 
neuroinflammatory responses. Seventeen compounds including α-cyperone, 
geniposide, ferulic acid, and atractylodin were verified to exert antidepressant 
activities via molecular docking and zebrafish models. Ferulic acid, α-cyperone, 
geniposide, and atractylodin show satisfactory detectability and are proposed as 
potential Q-markers.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides new evidence for the candidate antidepressant 
pharmacodynamic substances and potential quality markers of YJW and provides a 
scientific basis for the new drug development and quality control of YJW.

Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Associated With Severe Medetomidine Withdrawal: A Case 
Report.

Krishna D(1), Bennett B(2), Lin A(2), Spadaro A(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Emergency Medicine, Penn Medicine, Philadelphia, PA, USA.
(2)Department of Internal Medicine, Penn Medicine, Philadelphia, PA, USA.

BACKGROUND: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TCM) is a transient syndrome of cardiac 
dysfunction with no occlusive coronary arterial disease, which may mimic an 
ischemic cardiac event. The pathogenesis of TCM is thought to be primarily 
driven by the effects of a temporary catecholamine surge on cardiac and vascular 
tissue. Medetomidine (an a2 agonist commonly found in the Philadelphia fentanyl 
supply) withdrawal is characterized by agitation and sympathetic hyperactivity 
that can precipitate a catecholamine surge. Though withdrawal from other Central 
Nervous System (CNS)-depressing substances such as opioids and clonidine have 
been found to be associated with TCM, there is little documentation of this 
phenomenon occurring from medetomidine withdrawal.
CASE: A 51-year-old woman with no reported medical history other than opioid use 
disorder presented to the emergency department due to concern for withdrawal 
from fentanyl and medetomidine. Her opioid withdrawal was well controlled with 
methadone and oxycodone. Shortly after coming off her dexmedetomidine infusion 
(started for medetomidine withdrawal), she developed acute ST-segment changes on 
electrocardiogram, elevated troponin levels on bloodwork, and regional 
wall-motion abnormalities on transthoracic echocardiogram. Her coronary 
angiography showed no occlusion and repeat cardiac laboratory workup days later 
had normalized with improvement in ejection fraction on cardiac echocardiography 
and magnetic resonance imaging. This signifies a temporary stress 
cardiomyopathy, likely from a2 agonist withdrawal.
DISCUSSION: This case describes TCM in a patient experiencing medetomidine 
withdrawal. This patient's cardiac dysfunction was transient, temporally 
correlating with the cessation of her dexmedetomidine infusion. This suggests an 
a2 agonist mediated withdrawal leading to sympathetic hyperactivity which can 
precipitate TCM.

Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in patients with systemic lupus 
erythematosus and lupus nephritis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

Suruagy-Motta RFO(1), Canuto AMG(1), Ferreira BMV(1), Carvalho BCP(1), Nogueira 
CFSC(1), Firmino MMR(1), Souza-Carvalho JA(2), Martinez D(3), Costa AFP(1)(2), 
Figueroa MLCO(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Medicine, Cesmac University Center, Maceió, AL, Brazil.
(2)Department of Medicine, Federal University of Alagoas, Maceió, AL, Brazil.
(3)Department of Psychiatry, Martinez Institute of Mental Health, São Paulo, SP, 
Brazil.

IntroductionSystemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and lupus nephritis (LN) carry 
substantial cardiorenal risks. Conventional immunosuppressive therapies 
primarily target inflammation but leave a burden of residual renal and metabolic 
damage. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide clear 
cardiorenal protection in general populations, but data specific to SLE remains 
limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and 
safety of SGLT2i in patients with SLE and LN.MethodsComprehensive searches 
across five electronic databases (PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, 
Embase, and Scopus) were conducted up to April 2026 to identify randomized 
controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies assessing SGLT2i in adult 
SLE/LN patients. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to synthesize 
cardiorenal and safety outcomes using R Software.ResultsSix studies published 
between 2024 and 2025 were included. Pooled data demonstrated that SGLT2i use 
was associated with a significant improvement in estimated glomerular filtration 
rate (eGFR) compared to controls (MD: 4.02; 95% CI: 1.39-6.65; I2 = 60.1%). 
SGLT2i significantly reduced the risks of progression to end-stage kidney 
disease (RR: 0.37; 95% CI: 0.25-0.56; I2 = 11.0%), heart failure development 
(RR: 0.65; 95% CI: 0.56-0.75; I2 = 0.0%), incident lupus nephritis (RR: 0.58; 
95% CI: 0.44-0.76; I2 = 0.0%), and re-hospitalizations (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 
0.57-0.79; I2 = 0.0%). Furthermore, a significant reduction in all-cause 
mortality was observed (RR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.36-0.86; I2 = 76.2%). SGLT2i 
treatment demonstrated an acceptable safety profile across the included cohorts. 
The certainty of evidence for these findings was rated as low to very low, and 
results remain vulnerable to residual confounding from variables such as disease 
activity, corticosteroid burden, and immunosuppressive 
regimen.ConclusionPreliminary exploratory evidence suggests potential 
associations between SGLT2 inhibitors and cardiorenal outcomes in lupus 
nephritis. Given the low certainty of evidence and vulnerability to residual 
confounding from disease-specific variables, these hypothesis-generating 
findings require confirmation in well-designed randomized controlled trials.

Cytology and hrHPV Testing in HPV-Vaccinated Women Entering Cervical Screening: 
A Prospective Observational Study.

Cruickshank ME(1), Pan J(2), Cuschieri K(3), Liptrot S(4), Cotton SC(1), Ghosh 
S(1), Kavanagh K(5), Cubie H(6), Robertson C(5)(7).

Author information:
(1)Aberdeen Centre for Women's Health Research, University of Aberdeen, 
Aberdeen, UK.
(2)Cancer Team, Greater Glasgow and Clyde Health Board, Glasgow, UK.
(3)Scottish Human Papillomavirus Reference Laboratory, NHS Lothian and Centre 
for Reproductive Health, University of Edinburgh, Edinburgh, UK.
(4)Department of Pathology, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow, UK.
(5)Department of Mathematics and Statistics, University of Strathclyde, Glasgow, 
UK.
(6)Global Health Academy, Usher Institute, School of Population Health Sciences, 
Usher Building, The University of Edinburgh, Edinburgh, UK.
(7)Clinical and Protecting Health, Public Health Scotland, Glasgow, UK.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the predictive performance of cytology and high-risk HPV 
(hrHPV) testing in young HPV-vaccinated women participating in the cervical 
screening programme in Scotland.
DESIGN: Prospective observational study.
SETTING: Routine cervical screening services in three Scottish Health Boards 
between 2011 and 2015.
POPULATION: Women born between 1991 and 1995 attending routine cervical 
screening who were eligible for HPV immunisation, including catch-up vaccination 
cohorts.
METHODS: Residual liquid-based cytology samples were tested for hrHPV using 
Hybrid Capture 2. Women with high-grade cytology, hrHPV-positive and BNA/mild 
dyskaryosis, and a subset of hrHPV-positive women with negative cytology from 
one participating region were invited for colposcopy. Colposcopy and histology 
outcomes were obtained from the National Colposcopy Clinical Information Audit 
System (NCCIAS). Positive and negative predictive values (PPV, NPV) for CIN2+ 
were estimated within the study referral framework, and hrHPV persistence across 
repeat testing was examined.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: PPV and NPV for CIN2+ within the colposcopy referral 
pathway and patterns of hrHPV persistence in a selected group who attended for 
colposcopy.
RESULTS: From 10 000 co-tested residual samples, hrHPV positivity was 86% in 
borderline/mild cytology and 27% in cytology-negative samples. Among 1352 women 
who attended for colposcopy, 184 CIN2+ cases were identified. Within the 
selective referral framework, hrHPV testing demonstrated a PPV for CIN2+ of 
14.3% (95% CI: 12.5-16.4) and an NPV of 98.9% (95% CI: 94.0-99.9), while 
high-grade cytology demonstrated a PPV of 71.7% (95% CI: 59.2-81.5) and an NPV 
of 89.2% (95% CI: 87.4-90.8). Among 1007 women with repeat testing, hrHPV 
persistence declined with increasing inter-test intervals, with greater 
clearance observed over longer follow-up periods.
CONCLUSIONS: In this early HPV-vaccinated cohort screened within the historical 
Scottish programme from age 20 years, hrHPV testing retained a high negative 
predictive value but a low positive predictive value for CIN2+, reflecting the 
low prevalence of disease in vaccinated populations. These estimates reflect 
outcomes within a selective colposcopy referral framework and should not be 
interpreted as population-level screening accuracy measures. The findings 
support the role of cytology triage alongside hrHPV testing while highlighting 
the need for further evaluation of screening strategies in highly vaccinated 
populations.

Sleep Duration and Mental Well-Being Among Older Chinese Adults: A Four-Wave 
Fixed-Effects Analysis Using CHARLS.

Chen Z(1), Wang JJ(2), Chen C(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Graduate Studies, Lingnan University, Tuen Mun, Hong Kong SAR, 
China.
(2)Department of Elderly Healthcare, Shenzhen Polytechnic University, Shenzhen, 
China.

OBJECTIVES: To examine within-person associations between nighttime sleep 
duration and mental well-being among older Chinese adults.
METHODS: We analyzed four waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal 
Study (CHARLS; 2011-2018) using individual fixed-effects linear regressions with 
wave fixed effects and individual-clustered standard errors. Outcomes were 
CES-D-10 depressive symptoms and reverse-coded life satisfaction. Sleep was 
modeled continuously and categorically, with main categories of ≤6 h, >6 to 
<9 h, and ≥9 h; sensitivity models used ≤ 5 h, >5 to <9 h, and ≥9 h.
RESULTS: Among observations with valid CES-D-10 data, 36.74% met the ≥10 
screening threshold. Each additional hour of sleep was associated with lower 
CES-D-10 scores (β =  -0.305) and higher life satisfaction (β = 0.015). Compared 
with the main reference range, short sleep was associated with higher CES-D-10 
scores (β = 0.846) and lower life satisfaction (β =  -0.046). Long-sleep 
estimates varied by specification and outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: Shorter nighttime sleep duration, particularly sleep in the 
operational short-sleep category, was associated with poorer mental well-being 
within individuals over time.
CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Usual sleep duration can inform mood and sleep assessment 
but should not substitute for evaluation of sleep quality or sleep disorders.

Asymmetric metaphyseal cones versus medial modular block augment with central 
cone for medial tibial defects : a biomechanical comparison in varying bone 
quality.

Ren Y(1), Scott CEH(2)(3), Clement ND(2), Xie S(4)(5), Pankaj P(1).

Author information:
(1)Institute for Bioengineering, School of Engineering, The University of 
Edinburgh, Edinburgh, UK.
(2)Edinburgh Orthopaedics, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, Edinburgh, UK.
(3)Department of Mechanical Engineering, Imperial College London, London, UK.
(4)Department of Bioengineering, Imperial College London, London, UK.
(5)Smart Surgical Solutions, London, UK.

AIMS: Managing large medial tibial bone defects during total knee arthroplasty 
(TKA) remains technically demanding, particularly in elderly patients. This 
study quantitatively compares two reconstructive strategies: 'bridging' the 
defect using an asymmetric metaphyseal cone versus 'anatomical reconstruction' 
employing a symmetrical cone with a metallic block augment, and assesses their 
sensitivity to osteoporotic bone quality.
METHODS: A finite element model of a tibia with a standardized medial defect 
(Anderson Orthopaedic Research Institute (AORI) Type 2a) was adapted to simulate 
both configurations under physiological loading cycles in healthy and severe 
osteoporotic bone. Cumulative interface micromotion was quantified using a 
coordinate-based post-processing algorithm that decouples normal separation from 
tangential shear. A parametric sweep of the tangential contact clearance 
evaluated near-surface biological interaction zones without additional 
simulations.
RESULTS: In healthy bone, both strategies demonstrated adequate stability with 
micromotions predominantly below 50 μm. In osteoporotic bone, the asymmetric 
cone exhibited a loss of stability, characterized by intermittent lift-off 
during walking and excessive tangential shear during stair descending. This 
instability induced a toggle effect at the distal stem. The augmented 
symmetrical cone maintained stable fixation regardless of bone quality. 
Expanding the tangential contact clearance revealed considerable unrecognized 
shear risk surrounding the asymmetric cone, while the augmented construct 
remained insensitive to this parameter in the high-risk range (> 100 μm).
CONCLUSION: Asymmetric cones are viable in good bone stock but exhibit 
instability in osteoporosis due to the cantilever effect. Anatomical 
reconstruction with a modular augment and central cone provides a predictable, 
load-sharing structural column, making it the preferred strategy for large 
medial defects in osteoporotic patients.

Tumour Antigen-Specific Antibody Signatures as Diagnostic Biomarkers for 
Melanoma.

Vico-Alonso C(1)(2), De Carvalho Gil T(3), Sashindranath M(4), Mar V(5), Da Gama 
Duarte J(3)(6).

Author information:
(1)Dermatology Department, Fundación Instituto de Investigación Hospital 12 de 
Octubre [i+12], Universidad de Alcalá, Escuela de Doctorado, Madrid, Spain.
(2)Monash School of Public Health and Preventive Medicine, Monash University, 
Melbourne, Australia.
(3)Olivia Newton-John Cancer Research Institute, and La Trobe School of Cancer 
Medicine, La Trobe University, Heidelberg, Victoria, Australia.
(4)Australian Centre for Blood Diseases, Central Clinical School, Monash 
University, Alfred Hospital, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.
(5)Victorian Melanoma Service, Alfred Hospital, School of Public Health and 
Preventive Medicine, Monash University, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.
(6)Department of Cancer Medicine, School of Translational Medicine, Monash 
University, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.

Early detection of melanoma remains challenging, and minimally invasive 
diagnostic tools are needed to complement imaging and histopathology. 
Circulating tumour antigen-specific antibodies (Abs) are promising biomarkers, 
but their diagnostic value across melanoma stages is not fully established. 
Circulating IgG and IgM Abs were profiled in plasma from two independent 
melanoma cohorts, early-stage (n = 65) and advanced-stage (n = 77), alongside 
healthy controls (n = 86) and individuals with prior cancer in remission 
(n = 37). A protein microarray containing 263 tumour antigens, predominantly 
cancer-testis (CT) antigens, was used to measure plasma antibody (Ab) 
reactivity. Univariate and multivariate ROC analyses identified candidate 
diagnostic biomarker signatures. Early-stage melanoma was best distinguished by 
an IgM signature comprising AURKA, BAGE3, BAGE4, CDK7, CEP290, MYBL2, PIAS2, 
RAD51 and SPANXB1 (AUC = 0.939). An IgG signature including ANKRD45, BCL2L14, 
CDK2, MAGEA4v3, MAPK3 and RBM46 achieved AUC = 0.827. Advanced-stage melanoma 
exhibited broader Ab repertoires, including an IgG signature (CTAG1A, DKKL1, 
PIWIL2, SPANXN1, TSGA10, TSPY1; AUC = 0.865) and an IgM signature (CPXCR1, 
CSAG2, FMR1NB, FOXR2, LIPI, MAGEA5, TSGA10; AUC = 0.889). Individuals in cancer 
remission displayed persistent Ab signatures distinct from early melanoma and 
healthy controls. Overlap between IgG and IgM repertoires was minimal, 
highlighting complementary discriminatory value. Circulating IgG and IgM Abs 
against tumour antigens reveal stage-specific signatures that distinguish 
melanoma from healthy individuals and those in cancer remission, identifying 
candidate discovery-stage diagnostic biomarker signatures warranting independent 
validation in larger prospective cohorts to determine clinical utility.
