The CBI-M framework for characterization of traumatic brain injury: Evaluation 
of performance using data from the CENTER-TBI and TRACK-TBI prospective cohort 
studies.

Pisică D(1)(2), Mikolić A(1), Yue JK(3)(4), McCrea MA(5), Dams-O'Connor K(6)(7), 
De Keyser V(8), Jain S(9), Markowitz AJ(3)(4), Menon DK(10), Newcombe V(10), 
Steyerberg EW(11), Sun X(9), Lingsma HF(1), Manley GT(3)(4), Maas AIR(8)(12); 
CENTER-TBI and TRACK-TBI Investigators.

Author information:
(1)Department of Public Health, Erasmus MC - University Medical Center 
Rotterdam, Rotterdam, The Netherlands.
(2)Department of Neurosurgery, Erasmus MC - University Medical Center Rotterdam, 
Rotterdam, The Netherlands.
(3)Department of Neurological Surgery, University of California, San Francisco, 
California, United States of America.
(4)Brain and Spinal Injury Center, Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, 
San Francisco, California, United States of America.
(5)Department of Neurosurgery, Medical College of Wisconsin, Milwaukee, 
Wisconsin, United States of America.
(6)Department of Rehabilitation and Human Performance, Icahn School of Medicine 
at Mount Sinai, New York, New York, United States of America.
(7)Departments of Neuroscience and Neurology, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount 
Sinai, New York, New York, United States of America.
(8)Department of Neurosurgery, Antwerp University Hospital, Edegem, Belgium.
(9)Biostatistics Research Center, Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and 
Longevity Science, University of California, San Diego, California, United 
States of America.
(10)Department of Medicine, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, United Kingdom.
(11)Julius Center for Health Sciences and Primary Care, University Medical 
Center Utrecht, Utrecht, The Netherlands.
(12)Department of Translational Neuroscience, Faculty of Medicine and Health 
Science, University of Antwerp, Antwerp, Belgium.

BACKGROUND: The CBI-M Framework, incorporating Clinical, Biomarker, Imaging, and 
Modifier pillars, was recently proposed to provide a comprehensive 
characterization of patients with acute traumatic brain injury (TBI). Such 
detailed characterization reflects the clinical and biological heterogeneity of 
TBI, and is considered essential to inform appropriate clinical management. 
Still unclear is the extent to which CBI-M captures clinically relevant 
heterogeneity in relation to diagnosis, clinical care pathways, and longer-term 
outcome. Prior to broad implementation into clinical practice and research, its 
diagnostic and prognostic performance needs to be ascertained. In this study, we 
aim to explore how CBI-M and its constituent pillars relate to diagnosis, 
clinical care pathways, and outcome in two large contemporary TBI cohorts.
METHODS AND FINDINGS: We analyzed data of patients with acute TBI enrolled in 
the European-based CENTER-TBI (N = 4,509) and US-based TRACK-TBI (N = 2,552) 
prospective observational studies. We assessed associations of the CBI-M 
Framework, its pillars, and pillar components with key clinical endpoints: 
diagnosis (traumatic intracranial injury on computed tomography); care pathways 
(hospital admission, intensive care admission, intracranial pressure monitoring, 
and major cranial surgery); and outcomes at 6 months post-injury (mortality, 
Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOSE), and health-related quality of life 
(HRQoL)). Discriminatory performance was calculated using the AUC and explained 
variability expressed with Nagelkerke's pseudo-R2. Prognostic performance was 
compared to the established IMPACT-Lab and CRASH-CT prediction models in their 
respective target populations. For diagnostic and care path endpoints full CBI-M 
models achieved excellent discrimination (AUC CENTER-TBI: from 0.83 to 0.95; 
TRACK-TBI: from 0.88 to 0.98), and high proportions of explained variability 
(pseudo-R2 CENTER-TBI: from 0.41 to 0.72; TRACK-TBI: from 0.55 to 0.80). 
Contributions of individual pillars varied by endpoint, with the Biomarker 
pillar contributing most for CT-defined abnormalities and the Imaging pillar to 
major cranial surgery. For mortality and unfavorable outcome (GOSE ≤ 4) 
similarly strong performance was observed: CENTER-TBI: AUC 0.89 (95% Confidence 
intervals (CI) [0.88,0.90]) and 0.92 (95% CI [0.91,0.94]) respectively; 
pseudo-R2 0.53 (95% CI [0.50,0.57]) and 0.55 (95% CI [0.51,0.59]) respectively; 
TRACK-TBI: AUC 0.91 (95% CI [0.89,0.93]) and 0.95 (95% CI [0.93,0.97]) 
respectively; pseudo-R2 0.57 (95% CI [0.52,0.62] and 0.57 (95% CI [0.50, 0.64] 
respectively), whereas performance for HRQoL was modest. Compared to the 
IMPACT-Lab and CRASH-CT models in their respective target populations, pseudo-R2 
values suggest that the full CBI-M model was more strongly associated with 
6-month mortality and unfavorable outcomes. Methodological limitations include 
the restriction to analysis of data from high-income settings, limiting 
generalizability, the absence of three elements of the modifier pillar in the 
datasets accessed, and risk of possible reverse causality in some analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: CBI-M provides a robust multimodal characterization of acute TBI 
that aligns closely with clinical decision-making and outcomes. Further 
prospective validation and optimization are justified and needed to inform 
implementation of the CBI-M Framework in clinical practice and research.

Impact of Opt-Out Versus Opt-In Recruitment on Engagement of FDNY WTC-Exposed 
Responders in a Tobacco Cessation Intervention.

Moline T(1)(2), Mueller AK(1)(2), Prezant DJ(1)(2)(3), Bars MP(1), Zeig-Owens

BACKGROUND: World Trade Center (WTC)-exposed Fire Department of the City of New 
York (FDNY) rescue/recovery workers have an elevated risk of smoking-related 
morbidity. Despite access to free tobacco cessation treatment, some individuals 
in this population continue to smoke. In other settings, opt-out treatment 
approaches increase treatment initiation, but effectiveness in occupational 
health programs is unclear. Accordingly, we (1) assessed whether an opt-out 
strategy increases engagement with a Tobacco Cessation Program and (2) 
identified factors associated with engagement.

Medical Service (EMS) who self-reported smoking and were eligible for the WTC 
Health Program Lung Cancer Screening Program. 1:1 randomization occurred prior 
to contact for opt-out recruitment with Enhanced Care treatment 
(Opt-Out/Enhanced) or opt-in recruitment with Standard Care treatment 
(Opt-In/Standard). Opt-Out/Enhanced included proactive outreach and tailored 
biofeedback during counseling; Opt-In/Standard included participant-initiated 
engagement and standard counseling. Both groups were offered identical no-cost 
pharmacotherapy (varenicline). Engagement was defined as: consented enrollment 
(expressed interest and provided informed consent) and treatment initiation 
(attendance at ≥1 counseling session). Engagement differences were evaluated

characterized descriptively without formal testing due to small numbers.

(n = 23; OR = 3.05; 95% CI = 1.11-9.72) and treatment initiation (n = 18;

Opt-In/Standard. Treatment initiators had a median age of 60.5 (vs 65.0 years 
among non-initiators); 38.9% were EMS (vs 18.0%), 22.2% were female (vs 6.9%), 
77.8% had a prior cessation attempt (vs 23.5%), and 55.6% had abnormal lung 
function (vs 32.9%). Participants were too few to analyze cessation outcomes in 
depth.

engagement with tobacco cessation treatment. This supports other work that has 
found opt-out treatment to be encouraged for hard-to-reach populations.

A Molecular-Sieving Pitch Shell Decouples Surface Passivation from Sodium 
Storage in Hard-Carbon Anodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries.

Sun L(1), Zi Y(1), Li X(1), Yan S(1), Li Z(1), Zhang L(1), Mao J(2)(3), Dai 
K(1).

Author information:
(1)Academy of Interdisciplinary Studies on Intelligent Molecules, Tianjin Key 
Laboratory of Structure and Performance for Functional Molecules, College of 
Chemistry, Tianjin Normal University, Tianjin300387, China.
(2)State Key Laboratory of Critical Metals Beneficiation, Metallurgy and 
Purification, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou450001, China.
(3)School of Materials Science and Engineering, State Centre for International 
Cooperation on Designer Low-Carbon and Environmental Materials, Zhengzhou 
University, Zhengzhou, Henan450001, China.

Pitch carbon coating is a practical route to reconcile the capacity-kinetics 
trade-off of biomass-derived hard-carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet 
the role of the coating sequence has not been isolated. Here, an identical, 
industrially realistic 2 wt % pitch loading was applied to a lychee-wood hard 
carbon either before carbonization (co-carbonization, HC-PB) or after it 
(thin-shell carbonization at 800 °C, HC-PA25), and both were benchmarked 
head-to-head against the pitch-free baseline. Neither route alters the 
turbostratic bulk, the 324-328 mAh g-1 first-sodiation capacity, or its 
plateau/slope partition. Dual-probe (N2/CO2) adsorption shows that the two 
sequences engineer the pores oppositely. The post-coated shell seals the open 
surface porosity (N2-accessible area 115 → 3.6 m2 g-1) while retaining the 
internal ultramicropores, including the whole sub-0.45 nm population (0.068 vs 
0.064 cm3 g-1), a molecular-sieving gate, whereas co-carbonization erases that 
population entirely (its pore-size distribution starts at 0.48 nm) and 
kinetically gates the rest (40% lower CO2 uptake, pronounced trapping 
hysteresis). The sieving shell raises the initial Coulombic efficiency to 91.3%, 
stabilizes an organic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and delivers the 
best long-term cycling stability (237.7 mAh g-1 after 1000 cycles at 5C/2C) 
while maintaining a high rate capability (259.0 mAh g-1 at 10C desodiation, 
88.3% retention). Although co-carbonization gives HC-PB the highest apparent Na+ 
diffusivity, the decisive advantage of the pitch-after route lies at the 
interface, and in Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 full cells it translates into 89.6% capacity 
retention after 200 cycles vs 81.2% for the baseline and only 65.1% for the 
co-carbonized HC-PB.

patterns in Nepal from 2016 to 2023 and explore monotonic and linear temporal

Hydrogel Microneedle-Enabled In Situ Monitoring of Leaf Nitric Oxide for 
Evaluating NO Nanoprodrug-Mediated Salt Stress Alleviation in Maize.

Wang Y(1), Wulan J(2), Huang Q(1), Zhao P(1), Cao C(1), Lin Y(2), Cao L(1).

Author information:
(1)State Key Laboratory for Biology of Plant Diseases and Insect Pests, 
Institute of Plant Protection, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences,

(2)Department of Chemistry, Capital Normal University, Beijing100048, China.

Chemical signals in living plants are spatially confined, rapidly consumed, and 
strongly dependent on the delivery history of exogenous regulators, creating a 
need for bioelectronic interfaces that can interrogate molecular dynamics 
directly within intact tissues. Here, we integrate a nitric oxide (NO) 
nanoprodrug with a conductive hydrogel microneedle platform to connect 
controlled molecular delivery, in planta electrochemical readout, and downstream 
biological responses in living maize. The working electrode comprises a 
poly(vinyl alcohol)/aramid nanofiber (PVA/ANF) hydrogel containing FeMo-N/C and 
an MXene conductive network. The hydrated microneedle architecture provides 
tissue-conformal contact and analyte transport, FeMo-N/C enhances the 
NO-associated electrochemical response, and MXene improves interfacial charge 
transfer. The resulting platform responds to NO from 1 nM to 100 μM with a 
detection limit of 0.3 nM and discriminates NO from representative electroactive 
plant interferents. Chitosan nanoparticles containing S-nitroso-mercaptosuccinic 
acid were used to moderate NO release, and the microneedle interface resolved 
treatment-dependent leaf signals over 7 days under salt stress. Signal 
attenuation by the NO scavenger cPTIO supported the NO-related origin of the

growth, reduced lipid peroxidation, changes in osmotic and antioxidant 
responses, and altered expression of stress-responsive genes. This 
delivery-bioelectronics-analysis framework provides a materials-based strategy 
for evaluating reactive nanoprodrugs and interrogating transient chemical 
signaling in living plants.

Multiplexed CRISPRi reveals a transcriptional switch between KLF activators and 
repressors in the maturing neocortex.

Kirk RW(1), Sun L(1), Xiao R(1), Clark EA(1), Nelson SB(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biology, Brandeis University, Waltham, United States.

Update of
    doi: 10.1101/2025.02.07.636951.
    doi: 10.7554/eLife.106510.1.
    doi: 10.7554/eLife.106510.2.

A critical phase of mammalian brain development takes place after birth. Neurons 
of the mouse neocortex undergo dramatic changes in their morphology, physiology, 
and synaptic connections during the first postnatal month, while properties of 
immature neurons, such as the capacity for robust axon outgrowth, are lost. The 
genetic and epigenetic programs controlling prenatal development are well 
studied, but our understanding of the transcriptional mechanisms that regulate 
postnatal neuronal maturation is comparatively lacking. By integrating chromatin 
accessibility and gene expression data from two subtypes of neocortical 
pyramidal neurons in the neonatal and maturing brain, we predicted a role for 
the Krüppel-like factor (KLF) family of transcription factors in the 
developmental regulation of neonatally expressed genes. Using a multiplexed 
CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) knockdown strategy, we found that a shift in 
expression from KLF activators (Klf6, Klf7) to repressors (Klf9, Klf13) during 
early postnatal development functions as a transcriptional 'switch' to first 
activate, then repress a set of shared targets with cytoskeletal functions 
including Tubb2b and Dpysl3. We demonstrate that this switch is buffered by 
redundancy between KLF paralogs, which our multiplexed CRISPRi strategy is 
equipped to overcome and study. Our results indicate that competition between 
activators and repressors within the KLF family regulates a conserved component 
of the postnatal maturation program that may underlie the loss of intrinsic axon 
growth in maturing neurons. This could facilitate the transition from axon 
growth to synaptic refinement required to stabilize mature circuits.

continue to use cannabis and physicians must be prepared to counsel them.

BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Relapses, need for further treatment lines and 
significant treatment attrition are typical for multiple myeloma (MM). This 
retrospective study investigates attrition and outcomes among MM patients in 
Finland. Patient, material and methods: Study included all adult MM patients (n 
= 1733) diagnosed and treated in four hospital districts in Finland in 
2013-2022. Data were collected from hospital data lakes, Statistics Finland and 
Social Insurance Institution. Treatment attrition was defined as death before 
next treatment line.
RESULTS: By the end of follow-up 31% of patients without stem cell 
transplantation (non-SCT) had died before initiation of second line treatment 
(2L), compared with 5% of stem-cell transplant (SCT) patients. The factors 
associating with this early attrition in the non-SCT cohort were older age (over 
75 years), higher comorbidity burden, International Staging System (ISS), and 
(R)-ISS scores (p < 0.001). Furthermore, non-SCT patients were more likely 
administered less intensive therapy during 1L (p < 0.001). During the first 6 
months post diagnosis in the non-SCT cohort, the most common immediate cause of 
death was MM. Also, during later stages MM was responsible for 54% of deaths in 
the non-SCT and 68% in the SCT cohorts whereas infections were linked 
principally with early deaths before 2L treatment.
INTERPRETATION: This study highlights significant treatment attrition across 
disease course and also early mortality especially in the non-SCT cohort 
resulting primarily from progressive MM or infections. The findings underscore 
the need for more tolerable and effective anti-myeloma treatments in earlier 
course of the disease to enhance patient survival.

PURPOSE: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the effects 
of meeting physical activity guidelines for people with multiple sclerosis 
(PAG-MS) on cognition in people with multiple sclerosis (MS). Meeting PAG-MS has 
shown to elicit numerous health benefits in people with MS; minimal work has 
examined the influence of PAG-MS on cognition.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, EMBASE, Web 
of Science, SPORTDiscuss, Scopus, and PsycINFO. Two independent reviewers 
assessed included studies for eligibility, extracted data, and evaluated risk of 
bias. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) including physical activity that met 
PAG-MS and assessed cognition were included.
RESULTS: Twelve randomized controlled trials met the inclusion criteria with 462 
total participants. Eleven studies showed improvement in at least one aspect of 
cognition. Meta-analyses indicated meeting PAG-MS significantly improved 
processing speed (SMD = 0.29; 95% CI 0.08-0.51; p = 0.008), visuospatial memory 
(SMD = 0.47; 95% CI 0.14-0.80; p = 0.005), and verbal memory (SMD = 0.75; 95% CI 
0.27-1.23; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: Meta-analyses indicated meeting PAG-MS significantly improved 
processing speed and memory. The findings were based on a limited number of 
studies with a high risk of bias and more RCTs that meet PAG-MS and examine 
cognition are needed.

intensity necessary to elicit significant cognitive changesExercise regimens 
that meet the physical activity guidelines in people with MS (PAG-MS) may 
improve processing speed and memory compared to non-PAG-MS controls.

Race-neutral GLI-2022 interpretation in GOLD-positive COPD: reclassification in

Al-Qerem W(1), Jarab A(2), Al Oweidat K(3), Eberhardt J(4), AlKouri O(5), 
Al-Hashaki DK(1), Sawaftah L(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pharmacy, Faculty of Pharmacy, Al-Zaytoonah University of

(5)Faculty of Nursing, Yarmouk University, Irbid, Jordan.

BACKGROUND: Diagnostic interpretation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease 
(COPD) depends on the reference equation used to define airflow obstruction. 
This study examined how often race-neutral Global Lung Initiative (GLI-2022) 
lower-limit-of-normal (LLN) interpretation reclassified clinically confirmed 
COPD patients meeting Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease 
(GOLD) criteria as non-obstructed. GLI-2012 Caucasian, GLI-2012 Other/Mixed, and 
local Jordanian equations were secondary comparators.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 845 patients aged ≥40 years with 
newly diagnosed, clinically confirmed COPD attending Jordan University Hospital, 
Amman, between August 2025 and March 2026. Diagnosis incorporated compatible 
symptoms, clinical history, post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC <0.70, and additional 
investigations when clinically indicated. Patients with asthma or suspected 
asthma-COPD overlap were excluded. Predicted values, LLNs, and z scores were 
computed for each reference equation. Reclassification was examined across 
FEV1/FVC bands and using an adjusted bias-reduced logistic model.
RESULTS: Of 845 clinically confirmed COPD patients, 224 (26.5%) did not meet the 
GLI-2022 LLN criterion for airflow obstruction, compared with 262 (31.0%) using 
GLI-2012 Caucasian, 174 (20.6%) using GLI-2012 Other/Mixed, and 13 (1.5%) using 
the Jordanian equation. GLI-2022 classified 621 patients as obstructed (73.5%; 
95% CI 70.4-76.4), and all three paired comparisons with GLI-2022 were 
statistically significant (exact McNemar p < 0.001). GLI-2022 reclassification 
increased from 2.8% at ages 40-49 years to 46.0% at ≥80 years and was 
concentrated in the post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.65-0.699 band.
CONCLUSION: Over a quarter of patients with clinically confirmed COPD in this 
cohort did not meet the GLI-2022 LLN criterion for airflow obstruction. GLI-2022 
LLN-negative status should not be used in isolation to negate a COPD diagnosis 
established through guideline-based clinical assessment.

Plain Language Summary: Using the GLI-2022 LLN criterion, 26.5% of GOLD-positive 
patients with clinically confirmed COPD were classified as non-obstructed, while 
73.5% remained classified as obstructed.GLI-2022 LLN-negative status should not 
be used in isolation to negate a COPD diagnosis established through 
guideline-based clinical assessment.The local Jordanian equation showed closer 
concordance with clinically confirmed COPD, identifying airflow obstruction in 
98.5% of patients compared with 73.5% using GLI-2022.

Embodied Grief in the Shadow of Violence: An Integrative Conceptual Review of 
Widowhood, Trauma, and Social Constraint.

Khalifa G(1).

Author information:
(1)Al-Qasemi Academic College of Education, Baqa al-Gharbiyye, Israel.

Violent widowhood remains among the least theorized forms of bereavement. While 
dominant Western psychological models have advanced grief theory, they do not 
adequately explain grief following intentional spousal loss amid violence, 
ongoing threat, and gendered social regulation. This integrative conceptual 
review synthesizes interdisciplinary and cross-cultural scholarship on violent 
widowhood, traumatic bereavement, embodiment, structural violence, and social 
constraint to develop a context-sensitive framework for grief after intentional 
spousal loss. Four interrelated dimensions are identified: traumatic 
bereavement, embodied grief, gendered and culturally situated mourning, and 
structural violence under enduring threat. These conditions are argued to 
fundamentally shape grief in violent widowhood. Rather than following a linear 
recovery trajectory, grief is conceptualized as an ongoing process of 
negotiating identity, embodiment, and social belonging. The proposed framework 
positions adaptation as relational, context-dependent, and constrained by 
persistent social and structural conditions, thereby extending contemporary 
bereavement theory beyond individualistic psychological models.

Rho-related GTPases of plants (ROPs) are evolutionarily conserved molecular 
switches that typically maintain PIN-formed proteins at the plasma membrane 
(PM), yet their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal 
that a single amino-acid substitution at residue 194 acts as a core determinant, 
driving the evolutionary split between Brassicaceae and Malvaceae ROP6 
orthologs: glycine enforces PM stabilization, whereas alanine licenses endocytic 
function. In cotton, the Malvaceae-predominant alanine mutated GhROP6 displays 
an auxin-independent manner. The distinct activity is attributed to the

and promote F-actin assembly and bundling. The resulting actin reorganization 
facilitates GhPIN3a internalization and proteolysis, consequently enhancing 
cotton fiber elongation. Our findings demonstrate that a single amino-acid 
change can reprogram ROP signaling and uncover a molecular switch underlying the 
functional evolution of ROP6 in regulating plant development.

Dark septate endophytes (DSE) are widespread root-colonising fungi with poorly 
understood lifestyle and ecological functions. We investigated their genomic 
traits, sexual reproduction signatures, carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) and 
secondary metabolites profiles, and tested whether genomic features distinguish 
DSEs and other endophytes from fungi with other lifestyles. We also 
reconstructed ancestral states to clarify the evolutionary origins of DSEs. We 
analysed 107 Ascomycota genomes representing diverse lifestyles, including nine 
newly sequenced DSE genomes. The dataset allowed us to test whether secreted 
enzyme profiles differ between fungi colonising roots vs shoots and those 
associated with grass vs nongrass hosts. DSEs evolved through multiple 
independent trajectories and diverse lifestyles and show remarkable metabolic 
diversity. They possess extensive degradative capacities and some of the largest 
biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) richness among fungi. Despite sharing BGC 
richness with other endophytes, DSEs form a distinct subgroup with fewer 
cellulose- and more hemicellulose-targeting enzymes. Genomes also revealed 
genomic signatures associated with fungi colonising grass vs nongrass hosts and 
root- vs shoot-associated niches. Our comparative genomics approach highlights 
how genome-level data can deepen our understanding of endophytic lifestyle and 
the biology of the enigmatic DSE fungi.

Ting Z(1), Spear L(1), Smith J(2), Porter C(1), Krivda SJ(3), Solus JF(3),

Mechanical stress on the pilosebaceous unit can contribute to mechanical 
alopecia (MA) as seen with traction alopecia (TA) and trichotillomania (TTM). 
While some histological features that point to TA and TTM have been described, 
these may be absent in biopsies obtained at earlier stages of disease. 
Additional anomalies of the pilosebaceous unit have been observed that may 
assist in the histopathological detection of MA. A blinded, retrospective, 
qualitative, and semiquantitative study was performed comparing horizontally 
processed scalp biopsy sections of clinicopathologically confirmed TA (n = 16) 
and TTM (n = 9) to nearly matched controls (n = 15). Translocation of sebocytes 
into the follicular canal was seen in both TA and TTM, supporting a shared 
underlying mechanism. Vectorially warped sebaceous lobules were observed 
predominately in TA (p = 0.0002), while collapse of the inner root sheath of the 
lower follicular isthmus and surface lichenification were primarily seen in TTM 
(p < 0.0002). Lateral impingement of the follicular canal was seen in both TA 
and TTM (p < 0.0001), although more commonly in TA. These alterations were 
observed in the absence of other previously described features. Further 
validation studies in larger cohorts are warranted to assess their diagnostic 
utility in the recognition of MA.

Carbon dioxide (CO2) emission remains one of the most pressing concerns for 
society to achieve net-zero emissions. The functionalized nanocrystals have 
recently exhibited their potential to capture CO2. We synthesized ZnO and 
Zn1-xAgxO nanocrystals by chemical co-precipitation to fulfil the aim of CO2 
capture. The X-ray diffraction spectra of ZnO nanocrystals depict their 
hexagonal wurtzite structure; however, Ag doping shifts the (100), (002), and 
(101) reflection peaks toward higher 2θ values, indicating lattice distortion 
and reduced crystallite size. Besides, the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy 
analysis shows that Zn1-xAgxO nanocrystals contain around 0.5 at% Ag in the ZnO 
lattice. Henceforth, the nanocrystals have been functionalized with N-annulated 
perylene tetraester (PT) to enhance their reactivity. The ability of these 
nanocrystals to capture CO2 and its relevance for sustainable climate 
initiatives have been examined by CO2-temperature programmed desorption 
(CO2-TPD) studies. This study reveals that the CO2 molecules are effectively 
adsorbed on the PT-functionalized Zn1-xAgxO nanocrystals and do not detach until 
400 °C, which has been explained using the Polanyi-Wigner relation. This 
investigation demonstrates a compelling aspect of maintaining an environmentally 
sustainable and pollution-free ecosystem.

OBJECTIVE: This process evaluation assessed the implementation of electrical 
stimulation (ES) for pressure ulcers (PUs) prevention in individuals with spinal 
cord injury alongside a randomized controlled trial and identified facilitators 
and barriers for the implementation in home environment and rehabilitation care.
METHOD: A mixed-methods evaluation was structured according to the RE-AIM 
framework. Semi-structured interviews were thematically analyzed using the 
Fleuren framework; questionnaire and fieldnote data were supplementary sources.
RESULTS: Of 70 SCI PREVOLT participants, 13 and 13 healthcare professionals were 
interviewed. Recruitment via rehabilitation centers was most effective; PUs 
prevention was the main motivation for participation. Participants reported both 
positive and negative effects of ES, although most perceived the intervention as 
beneficial overall. Adoption depended on prior experience, staff involvement, 
and motivation. Adherence was hindered by limited time, need for assistance, and 
user-friendliness. Barriers included limited evidence, unclear responsibilities, 
and lack of reimbursement. Successful maintenance requires flexibility, clear 
guidance, support, and additional training for professionals.
CONCLUSION: ES is a promising but demanding intervention for PUs prevention. 
Limited evidence, usability issues, and organizational barriers hinder 
implementation. Improved usability, clear roles, and strong support are 
essential for future use.

Huynh TM, Ong T, Le QD, Le NQ, Le HM, Quach DT.

INTRODUCTION: Accurate optical characterization of small colorectal polyps 
relies on narrow-band imaging (NBI) or artificial intelligence, both of which 
are unavailable in resource-limited settings.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to develop and validate a web-based nomogram using 
white-light endoscopy (WLE) and routine clinical variables to predict neoplastic 
polyp histology.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This prospective single-center study (Vietnam, September 
2020-April 2021) included 301 patients with 451 small colorectal polyps (≤10 
mm). Polyps were assessed in real time using WLE and NBI before histological 
confirmation. Data were split at the patient level into training (254 patients, 
383 polyps) and validation (47 patients, 68 polyps) cohorts. L1-penalized 
generalized linear mixed-effects models were used for feature selection and

exposure in this population is limited.
OBJECTIVES: We examined whether long-term O3 exposure was associated with 
adverse cerebrovascular and cardiovascular outcomes.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed the population-based ARS-PARTICLES cohort of 
20757 adults with prevalent AF residing in Podlaskie Voivodeship, northeastern 
Poland, in 2014, with follow-up through December 31, 2019. O3, nitrogen dioxide

and assigned by residential municipality. The primary endpoint was a composite 
of ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack or ischemic stroke-related death;

area-level socioeconomic status, co-pollutants and outdoor artificial light at 
night.
RESULTS: The mean (SD) age was 72.6 (11.5) years, and 52.9% were women. The 
median follow-up was 5.6 years (interquartile range [IQR], 2.8-6), during which 
3,139 primary composite events and 5,400 cardiovascular deaths occurred. The 
median annual O₃ concentration was 43.48 μg/m³ (IQR, 42.6-46.63). Each IQR

risks of the primary composite endpoint (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR],

were directionally consistent across adjustment strategies and sensitivity 
analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Long-term O3 exposure was associated with higher cerebrovascular 
and cardiovascular risks in patients with AF. O3 may contribute to residual risk 
in this clinically vulnerable population and warrants evaluation in other 
high-risk cardiovascular cohorts.

Mapping policy instruments and challenges in health innovation development: 
implications for the role of early HTA - an umbrella review.

Hong M(1), Mou L(1), Har CE(1), Wang Y(1).

Author information:
(1)Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health, National University of Singapore, 
Singapore.

OBJECTIVES: Health innovation encounters challenges across the innovation 
lifecycle. Although various policy instruments aim to support innovation, their 
alignment with stage-specific challenges remains unclear. This study synthesizes 
evidence to examine how innovation challenges and policy responses are 
distributed across the health innovation lifecycle, with particular attention to 
the role of early Health Technology Assessment (early HTA).
METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review of review-level studies that examined 
health innovation challenges and related policy instruments. A comprehensive 
literature search was performed across five databases, including PubMed, Web of 
Science, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL. Twenty-four eligible studies were included 
and synthesized using a well-established analytical framework. Innovation 
challenges and policy instruments were mapped across stages of the development 
pathway and linked to the contributions of early HTA.
RESULTS: Innovation challenges were most pronounced in product design and 
clinical trial stages. Institutional barriers, including lengthy approval 
processes, became more prominent during regulatory approval and market access. 
Eighty policy responses were identified and clustered into economic, regulatory, 
and informational instruments. Economic measures were concentrated in product 
design and clinical trial stages, while regulatory instruments focused on 
regulatory approval and market access. Early HTA emerged as a complementary 
decision-support approach that may help address product design and clinical 
trial stages challenges.
CONCLUSIONS: There is a clear misalignment between where innovation challenges 
arise and where policy responses are applied. Integrating early HTA more 
systematically into innovation policy frameworks could help address challenges 
in product design and clinical trial stages and improve the likelihood of 
successful innovation adoption.

Contact-Induced Grammaticalization in Turkish Sign Language: From Mouthings to 
Grammatical Markers.

Makaroğlu B(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Linguistics, Faculty of Languages and History-Geography, Ankara 
University, Türkiye.

This study investigates the contact-induced grammaticalization of the Turkish 
existential mouthing /var/ ("there is") in Turkish Sign Language, proposing a 
novel Cross-Modal Contact Route for grammaticalization. Based on 1,024 attested 
existential/possessive constructions identified within a corpus of 101,908 
tokens from 58 signers, we analyze the distribution of variants along a 
unidirectional reduction cline (/var/ > /va/ > biting lips, bl). Generalized 
estimating equations and multinomial logistic regression analyses reveal a 
robust apparent time effect: while older signers retain the full spoken 
mouthing, younger signers predominantly use the biting lips-a visual remnant of 
the initial labiodental fricative [v]-indicating a change from below.

118 tokens-produced exclusively by signers aged 45 or younger (16-45)-where the 
bl marker attaches to non-existential hosts (e.g., group, pocket) and pronominal 
signs, functioning as an independent clitic for existence and possession. These 
findings problematize the rigid theoretical distinction between mouthings and 
mouth gestures, demonstrating that spoken lexical items can be scavenged, 
eroded, and nativized into the visual grammar of a sign language, effectively 
expanding current models of grammaticalization.

Striated duct adenoma (SDA) is a rare benign salivary gland neoplasm with 
limited cytologic characterization. We report a case of SDA with cytologic, 
histologic, immunohistochemical, and molecular correlation to further define its 
morphologic spectrum and diagnostic considerations. The patient was a 
62-year-old male with a submandibular gland mass. Cytologically, the specimen 
demonstrated loose clusters of monomorphic epithelial cells ranging from 
cuboidal to rare elongated or slightly spindled morphology, with moderate

cytologic and histologic features of SDA overlap with other salivary gland 
neoplasms, especially those with oncocytic/oncocytoid features. Definitive 
classification relies on histopathologic correlation and, when available, 
supportive molecular evidence of an IDH2 mutation.

and glucose catabolism, yet catabolic processes like these can also coordinate 
with lysosome-dependent degradation. However, the impact of cAMP signaling on 
lysosomal dynamics remains unclear. Transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master 
regulator of lysosomal biogenesis, is regulated by stimulus-dependent 
nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling through a variety of phosphorylation events. Here, 
we find that elevating intracellular cAMP with forskolin and IBMX induces rapid 
nuclear import of TFEB-GFP within 30 minutes and coincides with a transient 
upregulation of TFEB target lysosome genes. By 8 hours, TFEB returns to the 
cytoplasm, accompanied by transcriptional downregulation. Inhibition of 
cAMP-dependent protein kinase A (PKA) using H89 did not block nuclear import but 
unexpectedly caused sustained nuclear accumulation, indicating that PKA promotes 
TFEB nuclear export. Consistent with this, phosphoproteomic profiling revealed 
increased phosphorylation of a PKA-consensus motif (RRxS) during the export 
phase. These findings suggest that cAMP-PKA signaling plays a novel role in 
temporally "tuning" lysosomal gene expression by regulating TFEB 
nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling.

Promoting the use of osteopathic manipulative treatment with a student-led 
program: a retrospective review of 713 patient visits' characteristics and 
outcomes.

Hruby RJ(1), Martinez ES(1), Necas C(2), Tong C(2), Takebayashi C(2), Inouye 
K(1), Dew A(1), Luba J(1), Barrios A(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Neuromusculoskeletal Medicine/Osteopathic Manipulative 
Medicine, College of Osteopathic Medicine of the Pacific at Western University 
of Health Sciences, Pomona, CA, USA.
(2)College of Osteopathic Medicine of the Pacific at Western University of 
Health Sciences, Pomona, CA, USA.

CONTEXT: Early clinical exposure (ECE), especially within osteopathic medicine, 
helps bridge the gap between medical theory and practical skills by giving 
students the chance to apply osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) early in 
their training. This enhances their competency and builds a stronger connection 
to osteopathic principles. Current literature highlights that the early use of 
OMT in osteopathic institutions motivates students to continue utilizing their 
skill set, yet few programs offer real-world, hands-on experience outside of 
lectures and practicals. This paper describes and evaluates one of these 
programs, a student-led, faculty-supervised clinic focused on enhancing early 
OMT skills and confidence.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to describe this student-run, faculty-supervised 
clinic and to document the most common somatic dysfunctions and the OMT 
utilized, and to compare pre-and posttreatment pain scores for participants.
METHODS: This study was a retrospective chart review of 713 volunteer patient 
visits over a 3-year period, from the Fall semester of 2022 to the Spring 
semester of 2025. Data collected included volunteer demographics such as age, 
date of birth, gender identifier, status (faculty, staff, or student), chief 
complaint, body regions with somatic dysfunction, OMT modalities, and pre-and 
posttreatment Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) scores. Descriptive statistics 
were utilized to summarize the demographic frequencies to characterize the 
clinic's operational impact. NPRS scores were compared before and after 
treatment, utilizing a Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed-rank test for nonparametric 
data to assess the effect of OMT on volunteer-reported pain levels.
RESULTS: Of the 713 volunteer patient visits at the clinic, 533 (74.8 %) were 
students, 149 (20.9 %) were staff, and 14 (2.0 %) were faculty. Volunteers' ages 
ranged from 21 to 78 years, with a median age of 25.3 years. The most treated 
body regions were the cervical and thoracic regions, whereas the abdomen was the 
least treated region. On average, four body regions were treated per volunteer. 
The most utilized OMT modalities were the muscle energy technique and myofascial 
release, with lymphatic and visceral techniques being the least frequently 
utilized. An average of four modalities were utilized per volunteer. 
Posttreatment NPRS levels were consistently lower than the pretreatment scores 
(p<0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: The data from this study provide insight into the most encountered 
diagnoses in a more real-world clinical setting for our students and the 
corresponding treatments most frequently applied. Although not explicitly 
investigated in this retrospective chart review, this student-run, 
faculty-supervised clinic allowed students to treat patients over 700 times in 
3 years, presumably preparing them better to utilize OMT in their future 
clinical practice. Additionally, consistently improved patient-reported pain 
scale scores suggest the clinical effectiveness of the students' OMT 
interventions.

Porous, Interface-Rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 Nanocatalyst for Chemical Upcycling of PET 
Plastic Waste.

Pallavi K(1), Kumar MA(1), Sudarsanam P(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chemistry, Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad, Kandi, 
Telangana502284, India.

Interface engineering is a pivotal strategy for achieving superior 
thermochemical stability and distinct acid-base and redox active sites in 
heterogeneous nanocatalysts. We report a morphology-controlled, porous 
MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst with well-defined interfaces for efficient chemical 
upcycling of PET waste bottles into a high-value monomer, bis-(hydroxy 
neopentyl) terephthalate (BHNT), using neopentyl glycol. Electron microscopy 
analysis confirmed the high dispersion of MnOx nanoparticles (90 ± 10 nm) on 
porous α-Al2O3 nanosheets (length: 2800-5050 nm and width: 780-970 nm). This 
unique heterostructure combination provided intimate interfaces between MnOx and 
α-Al2O3, facilitating stronger acid sites (especially Lewis acidity) and 
Mn2+/Mn4+ active sites. The interface-rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst 
demonstrated excellent activity in PET upcycling, yielding 90% isolated BHNT 
monomer. The MnOx/α-Al2O3 catalyst exhibited good reusability up to 4 cycles, 
with only an 8% decrease in BHNT yield. The crystal structure, morphology, 
porosity, and interfaces remain unchanged during the reaction, as confirmed by 
the spent catalyst's analysis. The potential of the BHNT monomer was 
demonstrated by polyurethane synthesis, offering a truly circular plastic 
economy. The versatile properties and remarkable efficiency of the MnOx/α-Al2O3 
nanocatalyst, along with sustainable green chemistry metrics, underscore the 
vital role of interface engineering in heterogeneous catalysts for the plastic 
recycling industry.

Children's Surgery: The Missing Link in the Global Child Survival Agenda.

De Costa A(1), Wallis L(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Sexual, Reproductive, Maternal, Child, Adolescent Health and 
Ageing, World Health Organization, Geneva, Switzerland.
(2)Performance, Financing and Delivery Department, World Health Organization, 
Geneva, Switzerland.

Global child health is at an inflection point. Under-five mortality has fallen 
substantially over recent decades, yet progress is slowing and preventable 
deaths and disability remain concentrated in low- and middle-income countries. 
As mortality from vaccine-preventable diseases and other infections declines, 
birth defects and other surgically treatable conditions account for an 
increasing share of the residual burden. For many children, access to timely, 
safe and affordable surgical, anesthesia and perioperative care is the 
difference between survival, disability and death. Yet these services remain 
insufficiently embedded in child health policy, service delivery and universal 
health coverage. Children's surgery should therefore be understood not as a 
peripheral specialty, but as an essential component of integrated services to 
improve child health outcomes. Congenital anomalies make this case clear. 
Outcomes for surgically treatable conditions differ starkly by setting, 
reflecting inequities in early recognition, safe referral, anesthesia, operative 
and postoperative care, infection prevention, and follow-up. The same services 
are also required for injuries, burns, surgical infections, complications of 
sickle cell disease and acute abdominal emergencies. Strengthening them would 
extend well beyond specialist surgery; it would build the capacity of health 
systems to respond to some of the most time-sensitive and disabling conditions 
affecting children. Recent World Health Assembly resolutions on operative care, 
universal health coverage and newborn screening provide a clear mandate for 
action. The next phase of the global child survival agenda must recognize 
children's surgical care as an essential service to be planned, adequately 
financed and routinely monitored. Integrating surgical, anesthesia, 
perioperative and rehabilitation care into child health programmes is critical 
to avert preventable deaths, reduce lifelong disability, protect families from 
catastrophic costs and ensure that children everywhere have the opportunity not 
only to survive but also to thrive.

Cretaceous Chikuniidae fam. nov. (Diptera: Brachycera) illuminates the evolution 
of blood-feeding in lower brachyceran flies.

Feng Q(1)(2)(3), Wang J(4), Zhou C(2), Yang D(5), Engel MS(6), Ren D(2), Wang 
Y(3).

Author information:
(1)College of Plant Protection, Shanxi Agricultural University, Jinzhong, China.
(2)College of Life Sciences, Capital Normal University, Beijing, China.
(3)Guangdong Key Laboratory of Animal Conservation and Resource Utilization, 
Guangdong Public Laboratory of Wild Animal Conservation and Utilization, 
Institute of Zoology, Guangdong Academy of Sciences, Guangzhou, China.
(4)Key Laboratory of Animal Biodiversity Conservation and Integrated Pest 
Management, Institute of Zoology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China.
(5)Department of Entomology, China Agricultural University, Beijing, China.
(6)Division of Invertebrate Zoology, American Museum of Natural History, New

With over 80 000 extant species, brachycerans are among the most diverse insect 
lineages, exhibiting a wide range of feeding strategies and ecological 
adaptations. Originating in the Early Jurassic, this megadiverse clade then 
underwent rapid speciation and morphological diversification during the 
Mesozoic, profoundly shaping its modern diversity. However, the early 
evolutionary history of many lineages remains poorly known due to a sparse 
fossil record. Here, we describe a new brachyceran family, †Chikuniidae Feng, 
Yang, Engel, Ren et Wang fam. nov., from mid-Cretaceous Kachin amber. 
Phylogenetic analyses place it as the earliest-diverging lineage of the 
Asiloidea + Eremoneura clade within Muscomorpha, providing a critical fossil 
calibration for estimating the crown age of Brachycera and refining the early 
diversification scenario. Exceptional preservation allows functional 
reconstruction of the mouthparts, corroborating specialized haematophagy in both 
sexes. This discovery reveals previously unknown ecological diversity among 
Mesozoic brachyceran flies and provides direct fossil evidence for multiple 
independent origins of haematophagy within Brachycera. Furthermore, evolutionary 
analyses of haematophagous brachycerans and their potential hosts indicate that 
Mesozoic blood-feeding lineages likely exploited different host resources from 
their modern descendants, suggesting a major host transition during the 
replacement of Mesozoic and modern ecosystems.

Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with blood pressure (BP) instability 
and increased cerebrovascular risk, but how CKD alters cerebral pressure-flow 
relationship remains unclear. Seventeen adults with moderate to severe CKD and 
17 controls completed a multimetric protocol including resting supine recordings 
to assess spontaneous BP-middle cerebral artery mean blood velocity (MCAv) 
interactions using wavelet phase synchrony index and Granger based conditional 
joint transfer entropy, acute BP increases via 3 min isometric handgrip at 30% 
maximal voluntary contraction, acute BP decreases using sit to stand, and forced 
ABP oscillations using repeated squat-stands at 0.05 Hz and 0.10 Hz. Mean 
arterial pressure, MCAv, and end-tidal carbon dioxide partial pressure (PETCO2) 
were continuously recorded. Transfer function metrics and MCAv responses to 
transient mean arterial pressure increases and decreases were comparable between 
groups. Directional sensitivity was present in both groups at 0.05 Hz only. 
Wavelet phase synchrony index was elevated in ultra low frequency bands 
(0.030-0.035 Hz and 0.035-0.040 Hz), and Granger based conditional joint 
transfer entropy increased by 55% in forward MAP→MCAv information transfer in 
CKD persisting after PETCO2 correction. No between-group differences were 
detected using the linear assessments employed in this study, whereas nonlinear 
analyses identified differences during spontaneous resting conditions.

The Job Demands-Resources model: a framework for fostering trainee engagement on 
the inpatient wards.

Ratelle JT(1), Goldszmidt M(2)(3)(4), Knees M(5).

Author information:
(1)Division of Hospital Internal Medicine, Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota, 
United States.
(2)Centre for Education Research and Innovation (CERI), Western University, 
London, Ontario, Canada.
(3)Division of General Internal Medicine, Department of Medicine, Western 
University, London, Ontario, Canada.
(4)London Health Sciences Centre, London, Ontario, Canada.
(5)Division of Hospital Medicine, University of Colorado Anschutz School of 
Medicine, Aurora, Colorado, United States.

The inpatient ward is a cornerstone of medical training but is increasingly 
strained by high levels of trainee burnout and withering educational engagement. 
The Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model offers a useful framework for 
understanding these challenges. The model categorizes aspects of work as either 
demands or resources and describes how mismatches between the two can lead to 
exhaustion and impaired performance, while the right balance (high demands with 
commensurate resources) promotes work engagement and professional growth. 
Although widely used in other work settings, the JD-R model has seen limited 
application in medical education. This perspective describes the JD-R model and 
illustrates how it can be applied to evaluate educational practices on the 
inpatient wards. These practices can function either as demands or as resources 
depending on how they are implemented. A day-in-the-life vignette illustrates 
the application of the JD-R model, highlighting opportunities for attending 
physicians and program leaders to shape the work environment in ways that 
promote demand-resource balance and foster trainee engagement and learning on 
the inpatient wards.

Firmonertinib 160mg in EGFR-Mutated NSCLC with Brain Metastases After EGFR-TKI 
Resistance (iFORCE): Clinical Outcomes and Mechanistic Insights.

You M(1), Xie T(2), Wu L(1), Liu J(3), Li Y(1), Wang Q(4), Zhang J(4), Wang 
Z(1), Gao R(1), Hao X(1), Li J(1), Xing P(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Medical Oncology, National Cancer Center/National Clinical 
Research Center for Cancer/Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences 
and Peking Union Medical College, Beijing, China.
(2)Department of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Beijing Hospital, 
National Centre of Gerontology, Institute of Geriatric Medicine, Chinese Academy 
of Medical Sciences, Beijing, China.
(3)Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, Beijing Institute of 
Respiratory Medicine and Beijing Chao-Yang Hospital, Capital Medical University, 
Beijing, China.
(4)Department of Medical Oncology, Beijing Chaoyang District Sanhuan Cancer 
Hospital, Beijing, China.

BACKGROUND: Brain metastases (BM) are frequent in EGFR-mutated (EGFRm) non-small 
cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and remain challenging after prior EGFR tyrosine kinase 
inhibitor (TKI) therapy. This exploratory study evaluated high-dose 
fimmonertinib and explored subtype-specific spatial biology.
METHODS: iFORCE was a prospective, single-center, single-arm study. Eligible 
patients had advanced NSCLC harboring EGFR mutations with previously treated BM 
following EGFR-TKI therapy, or intracranial disease progression. Patients 
received 160 mg firmonertinib once daily. The primary endpoint was intracranial 
progression-free survival (iPFS). Archival paired primary tumors and BM 
specimens from an independent retrospective cohort underwent exploratory digital 
spatial profiling (DSP).
RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 19.7 
months (95% CI, 14.5-25.3), median iPFS was 14.6 months (95% CI, 4.2-not 
estimable [NE]), with 12- and 18-month iPFS rates of 53.8% and 46.1%, 
respectively. Based on the best intracranial overall response, intracranial 
objective response and disease control rates were 34.8% (95% CI, 16.4-57.3) and 
91.3% (95% CI, 72.0-98.9). Median systemic PFS was 10.7 months (95% CI, 3.9-NE). 
Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 13 (56.5%) patients, mostly grade 
1; one patient (4.3%) developed grade 3 stomatitis. No treatment 
discontinuations or treatment-related deaths were observed. DSP revealed 
distinct EGFR subtype-specific BM ecosystems: exon 19 deletion tumors retained 
immune-enriched inflammatory programs, whereas L858R-mutated tumors showed 
tumor-intrinsic cell-cycle, DNA-repair, RNA-splicing, apoptosis-resistance, and 
immune-evasion features.
CONCLUSIONS: Fimonertinib 160 mg showed promising intracranial activity with a 
manageable safety profile in EGFR-TKI-treated EGFRm NSCLC with BM. L858R BM 
displayed tumor-intrinsic, microenvironment-independent biology, suggesting 
preferential sensitivity to high-dose firmonertinib.

Plain Language Summary: Brain metastases are a serious complication of 
EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer, particularly when the cancer progresses 
in the brain after previous EGFR-targeted therapy. This study evaluated a higher 
dose of firmonertinib, 160 mg once daily, in patients whose cancer had 
progressed in the brain after prior EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor treatment. 
The treatment showed encouraging control of brain metastases and was generally 
well tolerated. The study also analyzed tumor samples from the lung and brain, 
suggesting that brain metastases with the L858R mutation may rely more on cancer 
cell–intrinsic growth and survival programs, which could make them more 
sensitive to intensified EGFR inhibition. These findings support further 
clinical studies of high-dose firmonertinib for patients with EGFR-mutated lung 
cancer and intracranial progression after prior EGFR-targeted therapy.

Lifetime family caregiving for older U.S. adults by men and women, 2011 and 
2023.

Freedman VA(1), Ng YT(1).

Author information:
(1)Institute for Social Research, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, Michigan, 
USA.

OBJECTIVES: Prior research finds that women spend more years than men caring for 
older relatives and friends ("lifetime family caregiving") in the United States. 
This study examines whether these amounts have changed in recent years (2023 vs. 
2011) and how recent estimates differ for men and women by relationship to the 
care recipient and type of care provided.
METHODS: We update and expand previously published estimates, drawing upon the 
National Study of Caregiving (n=1,972 in 2011; n=6,500 in 2021-2023) and the 
Current Population Survey. We use a demographic technique to calculate years of 
remaining life men and women ages 20+ would provide family caregiving to an 
older adult if current age-specific rates held.
RESULTS: In 2023, lifetime family caregiving for an older adult was nearly three 
years longer for women relative to men: 7.1 (95%CI: 6.2,8.0) vs. 4.2 (95%CI: 
3.7,4.7) (p<.001). For women, estimates for lifetime family caregiving were a 
year higher in 2023 than in 2011 (p=.03); for men, estimates were nearly 
identical in both years. In 2023, lifetime family caregiving for an older spouse 
or partner was similar for women and men but was higher for women than for men 
for caring for a parent, grandparent, and other relationship and for personal, 
household, transportation, and medical tasks.
DISCUSSION: Our results indicate lifetime family caregiving has increased for 
women. Gaps in lifetime family caregiving for men and women may grow further as 
late-life care needs increase and the percentage of older adults without close 
kin continues to rise.

Effects of private health insurance coverage gains on colorectal cancer 
outcomes: a modeling study.

van den Puttelaar R(1), Shi KS(2), Zhao J(2), Doria-Rose VP(3), Harlass M(1), 
Hahn AI(4), Zauber AG(4), Yabroff KR(2), Lansdorp-Vogelaar I(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Public Health, Erasmus University Medical Center, Rotterdam, 
The Netherlands.
(2)Surveillance, Prevention, and Health Services Research Department, American

(3)Healthcare Delivery Research Program, National Cancer Institute, Bethesda,

(4)Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer

BACKGROUND: Lack of health insurance limits access to health care, leading to 
potentially preventable inequities in health outcomes. This modelling study 
estimates the impact of providing insurance to currently uninsured individuals 
on colorectal cancer (CRC) outcomes in the US.
METHODS: The MISCAN-Colon model was adapted to an uninsured population aged 
40-100 during 2025-2055, using age-specific estimates from national data sources 
for screening, stage distribution, survival and all-cause mortality by insurance 
status (ages 40-64: privately insured vs. uninsured; ages 65-100: Medicare and 
private coverage vs. Medicare only). The effects of this uninsured population 
gaining health insurance coverage in 2025 were compared with the same population 
remaining uninsured for CRC incidence, mortality, and costs. Both groups were 
assumed age-eligible for Medicare coverage at 65 years.
RESULTS: In an uninsured population, the model predicted 170 CRC cases and 73 
deaths per 100,000 in 2055. If this population gained private insurance, up to 
15 (8.9%) cases and 22 (30.7%) deaths per 100,000 could be averted by 2055.

100,000 (-4.8%) through prevention and earlier diagnoses, total CRC-related 
costs would increase by $1.29 million per 100,000 (+3.7%) due to increased 
screening costs ($2.66 million per 100,000, +41.7%).
CONCLUSION: If the previously uninsured population gained health insurance, CRC 
incidence and CRC mortality could be reduced substantially because of improved 
access to care. Assuming analogous improvements for other cancers, this case 
study provides an example for the potential benefits of gaining health insurance 
on mitigating health disparities.

MOTIVATION: Although large scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have 
identified many risk variants for psychiatric traits their functional 
implication remain largely unknown. One potential mechanism for their risk is 
through cellular context-dependent epigenetics such as methylation. Previous 
methodologies have focused on integrating GWAS with single cell transcriptomics, 
which allowed identification of within-cell-type heterogeneity in disease risk 
association. We extended this framework to provide a method called met-scDRS 
that integrates GWAS with single cell epigenomics and investigates how 
psychiatric disease risk can manifest through methylomics at single cell 
resolution.
RESULTS: We propose an approach that integrates single cell methylomes with 
disease associated genes identified from GWAS at single-cell resolution. We 
found our method to be well calibrated and powered in different scenarios. We 
then analyzed a publicly available single cell methylome dataset of the human 
brain for 75 different traits and generated disease relevance scores for each 
cell for each trait. We find high brain specificity with major cell type 
enrichments congruent with known findings. We identify within-cell-type 
heterogeneity for psychiatric disease risk along the brain spatial axis as well 
as subpopulations that are differentially associated with diseases. Finally, we 
showed that genes with high correlation between methylation levels and disease 
relevance scores to be highly enriched in specific functional pathways such as 
synaptic formation and transmission.

MIT license: https://github.com/bogdanlab/met-scDRS. Source code is also 
available from Zenodo with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21841506. All dataset used in 
this work are publicly available.

An Updated Review of the Opportunities and Challenges in Insects as Food and 
Feed.

Robertson KD(1), Vale-Hagan W(1), Stratakos AC(2), Doran O(2), Drinkwater E(3),

The global demand for sustainable protein sources is increasing in response to 
population growth, climate change and food insecurity. Edible insects are a 
promising alternative, offering nutritional, environmental and socio-economic 
advantages. Currently consumed by approximately two billion people worldwide, 
insects are rich in protein, essential amino acids, unsaturated fatty acids, 
vitamins and minerals, usually making them nutritionally comparable to or 
potentially superior to conventional protein sources. Their farming systems 
require minimal land, water and feed inputs while generating substantially lower 
greenhouse gas emissions. Despite these advantages, several challenges hinder 
mainstream adoption. Consumer acceptance in Western markets remains low due to 
cultural neophobia, while regulatory frameworks, safety standards and welfare 
guidelines remain underdeveloped. Technical barriers, including variable 
nutritional composition, contamination risks and the great influence of rearing 
substrates, also limit scalability, while ethical debates on insect sentience 
and welfare further complicate industry development. This review provides an 
updated, stand-alone review to that of Doberman et al. This review highlights 
the current opportunities and challenges in insects as food and feed by 
evaluating key factors which support and hinder its wider integration.

RATIONALE: Early mobilization of mechanically ventilated patients within 
72 hours of intubation is underutilized despite its known clinical benefits. The 
most cited barrier to implementation is physiologic instability.
OBJECTIVES: To quantify eligibility for early mobilization across established 
physiologic criteria in a multicenter cohort of mechanically ventilated adults 
and estimate the relative impact of structural and process implementation 
barriers.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort of adults receiving invasive mechanical 
ventilation for ≥4 hours across nine CLIF Consortium health systems (2018-2024) 
and MIMIC-IV (2008-2022). Four physiologic eligibility criteria, from clinical 
trials (Chicago, TEAM) and consensus guidelines (Green, Yellow), were applied 
between 8am and 5pm within 72 hours of intubation. Random-effects meta-analysis 
compared eligibility across criteria and quantified the relative effect of two 
implementation barriers: weekday-only availability (structural) and 4-hour 
continuous eligibility (process).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 223,281 hospitalizations, 86.9-95.6% met 
eligibility for mobilization within 72 hours of intubation across all 4 
criteria. Compared with Chicago trials criteria, eligibility was reduced under 
TEAM (SHR 0.782, 95% CI 0.746-0.820) and Green (SHR 0.631, 0.611-0.651) but not 
Yellow (SHR 0.990, 0.976-1.005). Restricting eligibility to weekdays 
(structural) or requiring continuous eligibility (process) each reduced 
eligibility by 26-39% across all four criteria (SHR range 0.61-0.74); imposing 
both barriers together reduced eligibility by 45-56% (SHR range 0.44-0.55).
CONCLUSIONS: Most mechanically ventilated adults met physiologic eligibility 
criteria for early mobilization within 72 hours of intubation. Structural and 
process barriers, such as staff availability on weekends and sustained 
eligibility for care coordination, reduced opportunity more potently than 
physiologic instability alone.

Alveolar epithelial regeneration is critical for normal lung function and 
disrupted in disease. Precise identification of alveolar epithelial cell 
populations, particularly type I (AT1) cells, remains a barrier to understanding 
alveolar homeostasis and repair. We previously identified GRAM domain-containing 
2 (GRAMD2) as enriched in distal alveolar epithelium, with predominant 
expression in type I (AT1) cells. However, recent single-cell datasets reveal 
low level Gramd2 transcripts in other lung epithelial populations raising 
questions about specificity. To address this, we performed immunofluorescence of 
whole lung and cytospins of GFPhigh cells from Gramd2CreERT2;mTmG mice. 
Cre-induced lineage labeling predominantly marked cells expressing established 
AT1 markers, with minimal labeling of AT2 or club cells. GFPhigh cells were 
enriched for AT1 cells and formed organoids in culture that over time showed 
expression of AT2 and airway markers, suggesting plasticity. Despite apparent 
purity of the GFPhigh population by immunostaining, single-cell RNAseq 
identified AT2 cells and a small number of club cells in the labeled population, 
revealing discordance between GRAMD2 transcript and protein expression. 
Gramd2CreERT2;mTmG mice enable enrichment of AT1 cells but have limitations for 
definitive lineage tracing.

OBJECTIVE: Juvenile systemic sclerosis (JSSc) often presents with overlapping 
features, making phenotypic classification and disease progression difficult to 
define. This study investigated whether JSSc comprises latent disease severity 
subgroups with distinct longitudinal trajectories and examined baseline 
predictors of class membership.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected data from 45 
patients with JSSc between January 2005 and December 2024. Demographic, 
clinical, laboratory, and disease severity data were collected. The primary 
outcome was progression-free survival (PFS), defined as percentage change in the 
Juvenile Systemic Sclerosis Severity score (J4S) over time. A Growth Mixture 
Model identified latent disease severity classes with distinct longitudinal 
trajectories and their baseline predictors.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight JSSc patients (66% females), followed for ≥48 months, 
entered the study. PFS remained high in the fibrotic and limited cutaneous JSSc 
subtypes (80-100%) over the observation period, whereas the diffuse and sine 
scleroderma subtypes showed marked deterioration, with PFS decreasing to 54% and 
25%, respectively. We identified two latent classes of disease severity: Class 1

outcome were J4S >7.5, treatment initiation >9 months from disease onset, and 
>1.5 organs involved. Latent trajectory classes showed good concordance with 
JSSc clinical subtypes (κ = 0.660).
CONCLUSION: We identified two latent classes of disease severity in JSSc with 
clear prognostic significance. High baseline J4S, delayed treatment, and greater 
organ involvement predicted a more severe disease course, paving the way for 
precision health strategies and optimized.

EXPRESS: Increases in Intraluminal Viscosity Disrupt Microvascular Flow 
Dynamics.

Franco C(1), Gonzales A(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Physiology and Cell Biology University of Nevada School of 
Medicine Reno, NV, 89557-0318, USA.

BACKGROUND: Autoregulation of blood flow relies on a balance between 
pressure-induced constriction and shear stress-mediated dilation. While these 
mechanisms are well characterized in arterioles, far less is known about how 
blood enters and is distributed within capillary networks, the site of oxygen 
and nutrient exchange. Because neuronal function requires rapid, on-demand 
perfusion, local mechanisms must regulate both capillary inflow and flow 
distribution. Capillary endothelial cells and pericytes, contractile cells that 
envelop capillaries, are emerging contributors to these processes, yet 
capillary-level autoregulation remains poorly defined.
METHODS: Using an ex vivo pressurized retinal preparation that preserves the 
arteriole-to-capillary continuum, we examined how intraluminal viscosity, and 
thus shear stress, regulates endothelial and mural cell signaling during 
pressure-driven flow.
RESULTS: Increased viscosity delayed capillary filling and enhanced endothelial 
calcium activity in transitional and capillary segments. In contrast, viscosity 
suppressed pressure-induced calcium signaling in smooth muscle cells and 
ensheathing pericytes via nitric oxide-dependent inhibition. Chronic elevation 
of intraluminal viscosity induced arteriolar remodeling and increased tone but 
impaired endothelial shear sensing and reduced capillary perfusion.
CONCLUSION: These findings reveal fundamental differences in autoregulatory 
mechanisms between arterioles and capillaries and identify viscosity-driven 
endothelial signaling as a key determinant of capillary perfusion and flow 
distribution.

(2)Service of Clinical Pharmacology, University Hospital of Lausanne and

BACKGROUND: Despite growing availability of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), 
many potential users turn to online forums for advice and information 
collection. These forums provide a window into real-world questions, concerns 
and misinformation. They serve as a tool for users to query for sensitive 
information without revealing their identities. These platforms could therefore 
be a potential source of understanding of the unmet needs of users. This study 
systematically analyses the social media posts referring to the four drugs 
mentioned in the study to identify common questions and thematic concerns among 
the community and uses this insight to inform the design of an AI-driven, 
privacy-preserving chatbot for PrEP education based on evidence.
METHODS: Between May 2011 to October 2025, we found 1168 relevant Reddit posts 
mentioning one of the four names for PrEP therapies, by either brand or generic 
name: Truvada (Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate + emtricitabine (TDF/FTC)), Descovy 
(Tenofovir alafenamide + emtricitabine (TAF/FTC)), Apretude (long-acting 
cabotegravir), Yeztugo (lenacapavir) using a systematic search. We used Natural 
Language processing (NLP) techniques to understand user needs.
RESULTS: Seven distinct discussion themes were identified within PrEP social 
media discourse, with side effects emerging as the most frequently discussed 
primary topic among 1076 posts. Across all medications, weight changes were the 
most frequently mentioned side effect. Truvada was the most frequently discussed 
PrEP medication. 96.7% of the dataset comprised questions, showing that Reddit 
serves as a primary information-seeking platform. Early period discussions were 
emphasized basic access and effectiveness questions, with more recent 
discussions (2022-2025) displaying increased attention to injectable and 
long-term safety considerations.
CONCLUSIONS: Reddit users demonstrate persistent uncertainty about PrEP side 
effects, drug interactions and medication switching. Drug interactions 
represented the most frequently identified information gap (26.5% of posts). 
These empirically derived information needs will inform the design of a 
privacy-preserving PrEP chatbot trained on authoritative UK sources 
(hiv-druginteractions.org, BHIVA guidelines, NHS resources).

Androgen signalling plays a central role in the development and function of the 
male urogenital system, including the adrenal gland, prostate, and testis. 
Disruption of the androgen axis underlies diseases ranging from infertility to 
castration-resistant prostate cancer, yet current models fail to fully display 
its multi-organ and hormone-driven complexity. Organoid systems provide a 
promising platform to model androgen-responsive tissues while preserving

systemic integration. Future efforts toward multi-organ platforms and engineered 
microenvironments may enable the elucidation of the role of androgen signalling 
in physiological conditions and disease development.

BACKGROUND: Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors have improved outcomes in hormone 
receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) 
early breast cancer (eBC) in the NATALEE and monarchE trials. However, 
real‑world evidence on the proportion of candidates for adjuvant CDK4/6

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, population‑based cohort

BackgroundFollowing successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic 
stroke, tissue with abnormal perfusion may have impaired oxygen extraction and 
metabolism. MRI model-based oxygen extraction fraction (OEFmax) and cerebral 
metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2) were characterized in hypoperfusion and 
hyperemia regions 24 hours post-EVT.MethodsEighty-four patients were included

MRI at 24 hours post-EVT. Time-to-maximum (Tmax) and cerebral blood flow (CBF)

A case of STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy highlighting the 
pathogenetic role of interferon regulatory factor 5.

Kamiyama Y(1), Ban T(2), Sato GR(2), Kikuchi M(1), Nozawa T(1), Hattori S(1), 
Nishimura K(1), Tamura T(2), Ito S(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pediatrics, Yokohama City University Graduate School of 
Medicine, Yokohama, Japan.
(2)Department of Immunology, Yokohama City University Graduate School of 
Medicine, Yokohama, Japan.

OBJECTIVES: To elucidate the pathophysiology of stimulator of interferon genes 
(STING)-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy (SAVI), we evaluated 
interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) expression and nuclear translocation of 
interferon regulatory factors 3 and 5 (IRF3 and IRF5) in patient-derived cells 
before and after Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor treatment.
METHODS: A 3-year-old girl presenting with refractory eczema, polyarthritis, and 
interstitial lung disease (ILD) was confirmed to have SAVI. Baricitinib, a 
JAK1/2 inhibitor, was initiated for refractory ILD, and peripheral blood samples 
were analysed before and 4 months after baricitinib initiation. Expression of 
representative ISGs (IFI27, MX1, and OAS1) was quantified by 
reverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Nuclear 
localization of IRF3 and IRF5 was examined in sorted monocytes and B cells using 
confocal microscopy after intracellular staining. Activation was quantified by 
the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic mean fluorescence intensity ratio.
RESULTS: ISG expression was markedly elevated at baseline and decreased to 
levels comparable to those in a healthy control subject after 4 months of 
treatment. IRF3 localization remained unchanged, whereas IRF5 showed pronounced 
nuclear enrichment in monocytes at baseline, an effect that diminished after 
treatment. This reduction paralleled clinical improvement, including resolution 
of lung involvement and rash, and seroreversion of autoantibodies.
CONCLUSION: IRF5 activation may sustain chronic inflammation in SAVI 
independently of IRF3. The observed reduction in IRF5 nuclear translocation 
paralleled the improvement in disease activity, suggesting that targeting IRF5 
may help suppress inflammatory processes not adequately controlled by existing 
treatments.

An Attending-Directed Intervention to Enhance Interprofessional Teaching on ICU 
Rounds.

Petri CR(1), Punnamaraju A(2), Beltran CP(3), Sullivan AM(1)(4), Cohen AP(5), 
FitzGerald J(6), Anandaiah AM(1).

Author information:
(1)Division of Pulmonary and Critical Care, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical 
Center, Boston, MA, USA.
(2)Touro College of Osteopathic Medicine, Middletown, NY, USA.
(3)New York University Grossman School of Medicine, New York, NY, USA.
(4)Shapiro Institute for Education and Research, Harvard Medical School and Beth 
Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston, MA, USA.
(5)Department of Health Policy and Management, Harvard T.H. Chan School of 
Public Health, Boston, MA, USA.
(6)Department of Nursing, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston, MA, USA.

INTRODUCTION: Interprofessional teaching (IPT) during rounds may enhance 
teamwork and collaborative patient care, but previous studies have shown low 
rates of IPT during intensive care unit (ICU) rounds. We designed a study to 
explore contributions by interprofessional providers (IPPs) during ICU rounds 
and an attending-targeted intervention to promote IPT.
METHODS: Using a novel observation tool, we collected details regarding 
contributions made by IPPs during rounds in two ICUs at an academic medical 
center. A study team member conducted observations for six weeks before and 
after implementation of an attending-directed intervention. Comparisons were 
made between pre- and post-intervention data.
RESULTS: Before the intervention, six attendings were observed for 59 
patient-rounds with 309 contributions recorded, and after, eleven attendings 
were observed for 94 patient-rounds with 512 contributions recorded. The 
majority of contributions from IPPs were classified as "reporting" (pre/post: 
42.7% vs. 43.6%) and "observing" (pre/post: 29.1% vs. 29.7%). "Teaching" 
contributions were rare, but increased from 3.9% (12/309) to 4.7% (24/512) of 
all contributions (p > 0.05). The mean number of contributions per patient did 
not change after the intervention (5.24 vs. 5.45), and the types of 
contributions were similar across different attendings. When an IPP 
spontaneously provided a recommendation (pre: 33, post: 55), the contribution 
often changed the care plan (pre/post: 97.0% (32/33), 83.6% (46/55)).
CONCLUSIONS: IPPs predominantly contribute to rounds by reporting data and 
providing observations. An intervention to improve attending facilitation of IPT 
did not affect rates of teaching. However, recommendations made by IPPs 
consistently impacted the patient care plan.

PURPOSE: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI) is a highly prevalent, yet 
modifiable determinant of treatment tolerance in pancreatic cancer (PC). Despite 
its clinical significance, management remains inconsistent due to a lack of 
oncology-specific guidelines. This project aimed to establish the first U.S. 
multidisciplinary consensus to standardize pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy 
(PERT) dosing, education, and longitudinal management in pancreatic oncology.

framework to reduce provider inertia and practice variability. Broad 
implementation of these standards offers a vital opportunity to stabilize 
nutritional status, improve quality of life, and optimize treatment continuity
