Celiac Disease: Waiting to Explode in Asia.

Agarwal S(1), Ooi CJ(2), Anderson RP(3), Ahuja V(1), Makharia GK(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Gastroenterology and Human Nutrition, All India Institute of

(2)Duke-NUS Medical School, Singapore.
(3)Mackay Base Hospital, Mackay, Queensland, Australia.

Celiac disease (CeD) is an acquired immune enteropathy for which the presence of 
two factors, i.e., predisposing HLA genes (HLA DQ2/DQ8) and gluten in diet are 
essential for induction of the pathogenic immune response. Acute symptoms/gut 
injury specifically depend on the amount of gluten ingested. The incidence and 
prevalence of medically diagnosed CeD is expected to rise in the coming decades, 
and most of these people are expected to be from Asia. Through publicly 
available datasets, we mapped the estimated proportion of population harboring 
HLA DQ2/DQ8 in different regions of Asia and the per-capita gluten consumption 
for each country. We estimated each Asian's country's celiac risk based on these 
two factors and compared it with the published literature on population-based 
serological studies from these countries. The expected trajectory of CeD and the 
challenges in making different countries in Asia "celiac ready" is discussed.

Seeing inside the black box: Effects of algorithmic knowledge on system 
trustworthiness in aviation.

Hamann A(1), Heise A(1), Lenz H(1), Gampe A(1).

Author information:
(1)German Aerospace Center, Institute of Flight Guidance, Braunschweig, Germany.

Automation has shaped aircraft design for the past seven decades, moving from 
fully manual control to highly automated systems. Despite this, pilots retain 
final authority for safety-critical decisions, which requires continuous trust 
calibration. This study investigated how algorithmic transparency influences 
pilots' learned trust in an AI-based cockpit assistant. Twenty-one commercial 
pilots were randomly assigned to an early transparency condition (detailed 
explanations of the AI's algorithms and performance provided before the 
tutorial) or a late transparency condition (the same information delivered after 
the experiment). Each pilot used the assistant during a tutorial and a realistic 
simulated flight. Mixed-effects ordinal models showed higher trust ratings for 
the early compared to the late transparency group during both tutorial and 
flight, and a larger trust increase between phases. In conclusion, providing 
pilots with timely, clear information about AI processes modestly improves trust 
and supports calibrated reliance.

Plain Language Summary: Investigated whether giving pilots early algorithmic 
explanations of an AI cockpit assistant increases trust. Used a mixed-design 
experiment with 21 Airbus pilots, comparing early vs. late transparency across 
tutorial and flight phases. Found early transparency raised both initial and 
dynamic trust, especially ease-of-use.

How Serious Is "Serious"? Rethinking the Label of "Serious Suicide Attempt".

Baltzis S(1)(2), Lindström S(1)(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Clinical Sciences, Psychiatry, Lund University, Lund, Sweden.
(2)Department of Psychiatry, Skåne University Hospital, Helsingborg, Sweden.
(3)Department of Psychiatry, Skåne University Hospital, Lund, Sweden.

Background: The term serious suicide attempt is widely used in both clinical and 
research contexts yet lacks a consistent operational definition. It is variably 
applied to denote medical lethality, suicidal intent, method choice, or clinical 
outcome, dimensions that are empirically separable and theoretically distinct. 
Aims: We examine the conceptual assumptions and contemporary use of the term and 
evaluate its compatibility with contemporary models of suicidal behavior. 
Method: Drawing on developments in suicide theory, nomenclature, and 
epidemiological practice, we analyze how the term is used and what assumptions 
it entails. Results: We argue that serious suicide attempt functions as a global 
severity label that often combines distinct dimensions into a broad severity 
construct. This conflation risks inferring intent from outcome and introducing 
implicit hierarchies of legitimacy. A review of the literature demonstrates 
substantial heterogeneity in how the term is operationalized, with definitions 
variably based on medical severity, method lethality, or contextual indicators. 
Different frameworks tend to integrate these dimensions into composite 
constructs, which may contribute to conceptual ambiguity. Contemporary models of 
suicidal behavior and emerging precision-oriented approaches emphasize 
stratified risk, raising questions regarding the continued use of broad global 
severity terminology. Conclusions: We propose replacing global severity labels 
with explicit descriptive terminology specifying medical severity, suicidal 
intent, method lethality, and contextual factors. Aligning terminology with 
current models may improve conceptual clarity, clinical reasoning, and the 
validity of suicide research.

PURPOSE: Little is known on critical care services globally. This study aimed to 
describe ICU resources and organization across countries and assess variability

Persistent wait times in Specialized Geriatric Services increase risks for older 
adults living with frailty and place additional pressure on primary care. While 
workforce shortages contribute to delays, variation across programs suggests 
that access is also influenced by how referral, triage, assessment, follow-up, 
and care integration are organized. The Regional Geriatric Program of Toronto 
conducted a multi-phase engagement initiative including a targeted literature 
scan, stakeholder interviews and surveys, and a regional summit to identify 
system-level barriers and prioritize opportunities for improvement. Findings

geriatric assessment design, follow-up and discharge, and integration with 
primary and community care. Stakeholders prioritized clinically guided triage, 
tailored assessment pathways, clearer follow-up accountability, strengthened 
shared care models, and enhanced data infrastructure. These findings identify 
opportunities to strengthen access through coordinated system planning, 
operational improvements, and regional leadership within existing resource 
constraints.

Inotuzumab ozogamicin (InO) is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration 
(FDA) for relapsed/refractory (R/R) B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia 
(B-ALL), with a standard schedule of 1.8 mg/m2 fractionated into three doses for 
cycle 1. Alternative dosing with fewer doses or lower cumulative doses may be 
considered to minimize toxicity or expedite transition to consolidative therapy, 
though data on the efficacy and toxicity of this approach are limited. We 
conducted a multi-institutional retrospective analysis of 72 paediatric, 
adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients receiving at least one InO dose; 41 
with standard dosing and 31 with alternative dosing. Between the two approaches, 
standard dosing was associated with improved composite complete response (CRc); 
however, there was no difference in ability to proceed to consolidative cellular 
therapy, nor differences in 2-year event-free or overall survival. Ten per cent 
of patients experienced sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS), all following 
haematopoietic stem cell transplant. Most cases occurred in patients receiving 
standard InO dosing; however, given the overall few cases, it is unclear if this 
is due to a difference in dosing regimen. In conclusion, this large real-world 
study of InO use in the paediatric/AYA R/R B-ALL population suggests using 
alternate InO dosing strategies can successfully bridge patients to 
consolidative therapy with no difference in outcomes compared with standard 
dosing.

Hepatitis-Associated Aplastic Anemia in Children and Adolescents: A 
Comprehensive Review.

Liao E(1), Subedi S(2)(3), Kasper V(2)(3), Fassel H(2)(4).

Author information:
(1)Division of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Department of Pediatrics, 
Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, Massachusetts, USA.
(2)Department of Pediatrics, The Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown 
University, Providence, Rhode Island, USA.
(3)Division of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Department of Pediatrics, Hasbro 
Children's, Providence, Rhode Island, USA.
(4)Division of Pediatric Hematology-Oncology, Department of Pediatrics, Hasbro 
Children's, Providence, Rhode Island, USA.

Hepatitis-associated aplastic anemia (HAAA) is a rare but life-threatening 
subtype of acquired aplastic anemia (AA) that predominantly affects children and 
adolescents, characterized by bone marrow failure developing weeks to months 
following acute hepatitis. Although HAAA accounts for a small proportion of AA 
cases, it presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges and remains 
poorly understood. Most cases are seronegative, with no identifiable viral 
pathogen, supporting an immune-mediated pathophysiology. Emerging evidence 
implicates dysregulated cytotoxic T-cell activation, reduced regulatory T-cell 
function, and a shared immune target within hepatic and hematopoietic tissues. 
HAAA follows a variable course of hepatitis and pancytopenia, which necessitates 
a high index of suspicion and thorough evaluation to exclude inherited and 
secondary causes of bone marrow failure. Management strategies are largely 
extrapolated from severe AA and include supportive care, immunosuppressive 
therapy with antithymocyte globulin and cyclosporine, and hematopoietic stem 
cell transplantation. While outcomes have improved with modern therapy, relapse, 
treatment failure, and clonal evolution remain challenges. This review 
synthesizes current knowledge on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical 
features, diagnostic approach, treatment options, and outcomes of pediatric 
HAAA, highlighting critical gaps in evidence and the need for prospective 
studies to guide risk stratification and therapy optimization.

Hybrid lesions of hepatocellular adenoma and focal nodular hyperplasia: a 
clinicopathological and molecular study of two cases.

Zen Y(1), Schirmacher P(2).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Liver Studies, King's College Hospital, King's College London, 
London, UK.
(2)Institute of Pathology, University Hospital, Heidelberg, Germany.

AIMS: Hybrid lesions containing distinct components of hepatocellular adenoma 
(HCA) and focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) within a single nodule are 
exceptionally rare. This study aimed to investigate the biological nature of 
these unusual lesions.
METHODS AND RESULTS: The two cases identified to date were examined by 
histopathological, immunohistochemical and targeted next-generation sequencing 
analyses. In case 1, the hybrid tumour (6.0 cm) consisted of approximately equal 
proportions of HNF1α-inactivated HCA and FNH, which were intimately admixed but 
remained histologically distinct. In case 2, the tumour (9.5 cm) consisted 
predominantly of HNF1α-inactivated HCA but contained a small peripheral nodule 
of FNH, resulting in a nodule-in-nodule appearance. The HCA components in both 
cases showed loss of FABP1 expression, whereas the FNH components retained FABP1 
expression and showed a map-like pattern of glutamine synthetase expression. 
Next-generation sequencing in case 1 demonstrated that the mutations were not 
shared between the HCA and FNH components, with HNF1A and FLT1 mutations 
identified only in the HCA component. In case 2, the same HNF1A splice-site 
mutation was identified in both the HCA and FNH components, but was also present 
in the non-neoplastic gallbladder, confirming its germline origin. The HCA 
component, but not the FNH component, additionally harboured somatic mutations 
in ATM and FAT4.
CONCLUSION: HCA, particularly the HNF1α-inactivated subtype, rarely coexists 
with FNH. The distinct molecular and immunohistochemical profiles of the two 
components support a collision mechanism, indicating that the FNH component 
represents a separate non-neoplastic lesion and arguing against one component 
arising from the other.

Concomitant Centralization Procedure With Medial Meniscus Posterior Root Repair 
May Have Zone-Specific Effects on the Medial Femoral Condyle and Enhance Repair 
Healing Compared With Isolated Root Repair: An In Vivo Experimental Study in 
Rabbit Knees.

Dzidzishvili L(1), Nelson B(2), Santangelo K(2), Sikes KJ(2), Burton L(2), Del 
Águila López-Pintor Ó(3), Fernández-Valle ME(3), Goodrich L(2), Cole BJ(4), 
LaPrade RF(5), Chahla J(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Knee Surgery and Arthroscopy Unit, 
Hospital Universitari Germans Trias i Pujol, Universidad Autónoma de Badalona, 
Barcelona, Spain.
(2)Preclinical Surgical Research Laboratory, Orthopaedic Research Center, C. 
Wayne McIlwraith Translational Medicine Institute, College of Veterinary 
Medicine and Biomedical Sciences, Colorado State University, Fort Collins, 
Colorado, USA.
(3)ICTS Complutense Bioimaging (BioImac), Complutense University of Madrid, 
Madrid, Spain.
(4)Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Rush University Medical Center, Midwest 
Orthopaedics at Rush, Chicago, Illinois, USA.
(5)Twin Cities Orthopedics, Edina, Minneapolis, USA.

BACKGROUND: Short-term clinical outcomes of meniscal centralization are 
promising, but questions remain whether it can protect articular cartilage and 
delay osteoarthritis progression.
PURPOSE: To assess cartilage status and healing potential after isolated medial 
meniscus posterior root (MMPR) repair (RR) versus MMPR repair augmented with a 
centralization procedure (RR-CP) in a rabbit stifle model.
STUDY DESIGN: Controlled laboratory study.
METHODS: MMPR tears were surgically induced in 16 New Zealand White rabbits. 
Eight underwent RR and 8 underwent RR-CP using interlocking knotless anchors; 
contralateral limbs served as controls. After 4 months, animals were euthanized 
and articular cartilage was harvested for macro- and microscopic evaluation, 
including repair tissue assessment for healing potential. Microscopic assessment 
was performed using the Osteoarthritis Research Society International (OARSI) 
scoring system. Cartilage thickness and meniscal extrusion (ME) were assessed 
using high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at 9.4 T. The medial 
femoral condyle was divided into 3 regions of interest (anterior, central, and 
posterior), and zone-specific changes were evaluated.
RESULTS: The mean ± standard deviation gross pathology joint degeneration score 
was significantly higher in the RR group compared with the RR-CP group (12.3 ± 
2.2 vs 9.1 ± 2.0; P = .01). The mean OARSI score was significantly lower in the 
RR-CP group compared with the RR group (3.1 ± 1.6 vs 4.2 ± 1.5; P = .04). 
Nonhealed root repairs were more frequent in the RR group, and repair healing 
scores favored the RR-CP group (1.75 ± 0.5 vs 2.5 ± 0.7; P = .041). MRI 
demonstrated significantly reduced central and posterior cartilage thickness in 
the RR group compared with the RR-CP and control knees (P ≤ .02), with no 
difference anteriorly (P = .23). ME did not differ between the RR and RR-CP 
goups (P = .12). Both experimental groups showed greater chondral damage 
compared with contralateral controls (P < .001).
CONCLUSION: RR-CP was associated with reduced total joint cartilage damage and 
improved repair healing compared with isolated RR. MRI showed greater loss of 
central and posterior cartilage thickness after RR, while no difference in 
postoperative ME was detected. Both treatment groups demonstrated increased 
chondral damage compared with control knees.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study provides important biological insights into a 
clinically relevant question and establishes a foundation for future clinical 
investigations aimed at defining patient selection criteria and surgical 
indications for a concomitant meniscal centralization procedure.

Malpractice Payments and State Medical Board Discipline: National Evidence From 
the National Practitioner Data Bank.

Patel S(1), Tran Q, Bettis T, Glosser L, Maegawa F.

Author information:
(1)Department of Surgery, Division of General and GI Surgery, Emory University, 
Atlanta, GA.

BACKGROUND: Malpractice payments and state medical board discipline are often 
assumed to identify the same physicians, yet that assumption has never been 
tested nationally.
METHODS: National retrospective cohort study using the National Practitioner 
Data Bank Public Use Data File (March 31, 2026 release). A total of 76 353 
allopathic and osteopathic physicians without prior state licensure actions were 
followed from their first observed paid malpractice report (2004-2018) through 
March 2026. The primary outcome was any substantive new state licensure action; 
secondary outcomes classified actions as quality-of-care-related, nonclinical, 
or severe. All outcomes describe the first subsequent action in a 
time-to-first-event design.
RESULTS: Overall, 71 372 physicians (93.5%) had no subsequent state licensure 
action during observed follow-up; a severe first action occurred in 2.1% within 
15 years, including license revocation in 0.2%. Among the 4981 physicians (6.5%) 
with a subsequent action, the first action occurred a median of 5 years after 
the index report, and 43.7% involved exclusively nonclinical conduct. The 
15-year cumulative incidence was 2.54% for quality-of-care actions and 2.94% for 
nonclinical actions. Severe injury or death in the index report was not 
associated with subsequent quality-of-care discipline (adjusted hazard ratio, 
1.01; 95% CI, 0.90-1.12).
CONCLUSIONS: Board discipline following a paid malpractice report was uncommon, 
delayed, and frequently unrelated to clinical care. These accountability systems 
appear to serve complementary rather than interchangeable roles in assessing 
physician quality.

Standardization of the Monocyte Monolayer Assay: Lessons Learned From Laboratory 
Optimization and Literature Review.

Shastry S(1), Babu K(1), Chenna D(1), Mohan G(1), Iyer K(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Immunohematology and Blood Transfusion, Kasturba Medical 
College, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Manipal, India.

OBJECTIVES: Several variables influence the outcome of cellular assays. We 
conducted a comprehensive literature review to identify the factors affecting 
the Monocyte Monolayer Assay (MMA) and subsequently standardized the assay 
through systematic in-house laboratory trials.
METHODS: The study was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 involved a literature 
review using PubMed and Scopus databases to identify factors influencing the 
assay. Phase 2 included experimental trials to evaluate the effects of these 
factors. Monocytes were isolated from buffy coat bags, and assay parameters, 
such as centrifugation speed, monocyte adherence conditions, RBC sensitization, 
incubation time, and staining, were systematically standardized. A blinded 
evaluation was employed for slide reading to assess the influence of procedural 
factors on assay reliability.
RESULTS: A literature review using the PubMed and Scopus databases identified 
key variables influencing MMA performance. Twelve sequential trials were 
conducted to identify the effects of these variables on assay outcome. Optimal 
centrifugation speed and time was 600 × g for 15 min, and the use of four buffy 
coat bags improved monocyte yield to 8.3 × 106/mL. Dilution with Phosphate 
buffer saline (PBS, pH 7.2) and use of Histopaque provided consistent cell 
recovery. A 1-h incubation yielded optimal monocyte adherence with minimal 
lysis. The final protocol demonstrated high reproducibility and improved 
visualization of phagocytosis.
CONCLUSION: This study emphasizes the importance of standardizing the MMA 
procedure before implementation. Optimizing the parameters to ensure enhanced 
monocyte yield, reduced cell lysis, and reliable interpretation for assessing 
the clinical significance of red cell alloantibodies is essential.

Drug repurposing in fibrosis: From molecular networks to antifibrotic 
therapeutics-A narrative review.

A RN(1), Sathiamoorthy K(1), Karthick Rajan P(1), Rajendran P(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pharmacology, Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical 
Education and Research (JIPMER), Puducherry, India.

Fibrosis is a common pathological endpoint of chronic diseases affecting 
multiple organs and remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. 
Despite advances in understanding fibrogenesis, current antifibrotic therapies 
primarily slow rather than reverse disease progression, underscoring the need 
for more effective treatments. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy by 
leveraging the established safety and pharmacokinetic profiles of approved drugs 
while reducing development time and cost. This review provides a mechanism-based 
synthesis of repurposed agents targeting the interconnected pathways driving 
fibrosis, including transforming growth factor-β signalling, chronic 
inflammation, oxidative stress and emerging regulatory networks such as 
mechanotransduction and cellular senescence. Evidence from mechanistic studies, 
preclinical models, randomized trials and meta-analyses is critically appraised, 
highlighting promising candidates and translational challenges arising from the 
distinct cellular mechanisms and variable reversibility of fibrosis across 
organs. By integrating molecular insights with clinical evidence, this review 
advocates a pathway-guided, biomarker-driven approach to drug repurposing as a 
rational strategy for accelerating development of personalized, multi-target 
antifibrotic therapies.

Real-world effectiveness of first-line chemoimmunotherapy versus chemotherapy in 
older adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer: an inverse probability 
treatment weighted analysis.

Cui S(1)(2)(3), Zhao K(1)(2)(3), Wang N(1)(2)(3), Meng Y(1)(2)(3), Wang 
X(1)(2)(3), Wang C(1)(2)(3), Kong F(1)(2)(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Oncology, First Teaching Hospital of Tianjin University of 
Traditional Chinese Medicine, Tianjin, China.
(2)National Clinical Research Center for Chinese Medicine, Tianjin, China.
(3)Tianjin Cancer Institute of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Tianjin, China.

AIMS: First-line chemoimmunotherapy (ICI-chemo) has become the standard of care 
for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC). However, older adults are 
underrepresented in pivotal trials due to strict inclusion criteria that limit 
participation to highly selected, fit patients. Given the limited real-world 
comparative data, this study aimed to determine whether older adults with 
ES-SCLC derive greater benefit from ICI-chemo compared with chemotherapy (chemo) 
alone.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study 
including ES-SCLC patients aged 65 years or older who started first-line 
ICI-chemo or chemo between January 2020 and July 2024. Inverse probability of 
treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to adjust for baseline confounding. The main 
outcome was overall survival (OS) in the IPTW population.
RESULTS: In the IPTW population, median OS was significantly longer in the 
ICI-chemo group (14.95 months; 95% CI, 12.94-19.91) compared with chemo 
(10.28 months; 95% CI, 8.11-13.17; HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.48-0.91; p = 0.011). 
Multivariable analysis confirmed that ICI-chemo exposure was independently 
associated with improved OS (HR, 0.608; 95% CI, 0.440-0.841; p = 0.003).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings provide comparative evidence of improved survival in 
association with ICI-chemo compared with chemo in older adults with ES-SCLC.

Plain Language Summary: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer is a fast-growing 
disease. Recently, doctors started adding a specific type of immunotherapy to 
standard chemotherapy. This treatment works by releasing the brake on the immune 
system, thereby unleashing our immune cells to attack tumors. However, most of 
the evidence for this combined treatment comes from large clinical trials that 
mostly included younger, very fit patients. We need to know more about how this 
treatment affects older adults in everyday medical practice, because they often 
have other health problems. To explore this, we reviewed the medical records of 
171 patients aged 65 or older treated at our hospital. We compared the results 
of patients who received both immunotherapy and chemotherapy with those who 
received only chemotherapy. We found older patients who received the combined 
treatment lived significantly longer. They lived for an average of about 
15 months, compared to about 10 months for those who received only chemotherapy. 
While a single hospital study cannot provide definitive proof, our findings 
suggest that adding immunotherapy might offer a meaningful survival benefit for 
older adults in routine clinical care. This provides helpful real-world 
information that complements the results of large clinical trials.

BACKGROUND: Clinic workflow efficiency influences patient and employee 
satisfaction, impacting effective delivery of care. Utilizing lean methodology, 
we aim to increase the percentage of patients seen within 15 minutes of 
scheduled appointment to 75% and reduce nonvalue-added time (NVT) per visit by 
half within 6 months.
METHODS: Frontline stakeholders observed workflow inefficiencies in an 
outpatient general surgery clinic, leading to long wait times and generalized 
dissatisfaction. From August to September 2023, patient and staff flow was 
captured and appointment component time intervals observed. Only 35.8% of

reduced median NVT from 74% to 55.9%. Late in PDSA 2 in December, when the 
clinic was short-staffed, both median AST and NVT increased. PDSA 3 resulted in 
reduced median AST of 5.00 minutes, with 82.9% of patients seen within 15 
minutes of appointment and reduced median NVT to 51.5%, with improved 
performance stability particularly with respect to AST.
CONCLUSIONS: Utilization of lean methodology with multiple targeted workflow and 
scheduling interventions resulted in improved efficiency in an outpatient 
general surgery clinic.

Mouse Tail Models for Surgical Lymphedema Induction-A Comprehensive Systematic 
Review and Quality Assessment.

Bahtiri L(1), Bucan A(1)(2), Frendø M(3)(4), Remvig C(1), Hölmich LR(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Plastic Surgery, University of Copenhagen, Herlev and Gentofte 
Hospital, Copenhagen, Denmark.
(2)Department of Clinical Medicine, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, 
Denmark.
(3)Department of Plastic and Breast Surgery, Zealand University Hospital, 
Roskilde, Denmark.
(4)Copenhagen Academy for Medical Education and Simulation (CAMES), Center for 
HR & Education, Copenhagen, Denmark.

Lymphedema remains a significant clinical and research challenge, requiring 
reliable experimental models to investigate its underlying mechanisms and 
evaluate potential therapies. Among available options, the surgical mouse tail 
model is widely used due to its simplicity, reproducibility, and low cost. While 
prior reviews have examined surgical lymphedema models across species, this is 
the first systematic review dedicated exclusively to the mouse tail model, 
providing a comprehensive evaluation of its application in practice and a formal 
assessment of its methodological reporting quality. We conducted a systematic 
review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and 
Meta-Analyses guidelines, searching four databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of 
Science, and Scopus) from inception to January 2025. Studies claiming to 
surgically induce lymphedema in the mouse tail were included. We defined 
lymphedema as a significant volume difference. Reporting quality was assessed 
using the Animals in Research Reporting In Vivo Experiments (ARRIVE 2.0) 
guidelines. The review was conducted and reported in accordance with the 
Synthesis Without Meta-analysis and Statistical Analyses and Methods in the 
Published Literature guidelines. One hundred five studies were included; 65% 
(68/105) successfully induced lymphedema. Four main models were identified. The 
median follow-up period was 35 days, and the median peak of swelling was 14 
days. Adverse events such as tail ischemia were reported in 15 studies. Notably, 
51% of studies (54/105) lacked controls. The mean reporting quality coefficient 
was 0.61, corresponding to "average" quality. The surgical mouse tail model is 
valuable for studying lymphatic pathophysiology but limited by inconsistent 
methods and reporting. Drawing on 105 studies and a formal multiframework 
quality assessment, this review identifies six key areas for improvement: (1) 
standardized induction protocols, (2) validated and consistently reported 
outcome measures, (3) control-group design, (4) defined minimum follow-up 
durations, (5) transparent adverse event reporting, and (6) mandatory adherence 
to ARRIVE 2.0 guidelines.

Blinking membrane patterns induced by protein binding/unbinding.

Noguchi H(1).

Author information:
(1)Institute for Solid State Physics, University of Tokyo, Kashiwa, Chiba 
277-8581, Japan. noguchi@issp.u-tokyo.ac.jp.

Nonequilibrium membrane pattern formation is studied using meshless membrane 
simulation. Bound proteins are considered to have two states that generate 
different membrane spontaneous curvatures. Protein binding and unbinding occur 
cyclically owing to chemical potential differences, as an off-lattice active 
Potts model. It is found that this cyclic binding/unbinding can induce blinking 
domains, with oscillating size: convex domains of the proteins with a higher 
spontaneous curvature grow, and subsequently, the proteins change to the other 
state with a lower spontaneous curvature, resulting in domain shrinkage. These 
processes repeat. In thermal equilibrium, hexagonal convex domains are formed by 
the competition between bending and surface tension energies, so that they are 
stably formed only under positive surface tension. However, blinking domains can 
form even in tensionless membranes.

Nilutamide (NLM) and flutamide (FLU) are important non-steroidal antiandrogen

recoveries in spiked samples. Finally, challenges, limitations, and future 
directions are discussed, including improved interface design, mechanistic 
understanding, standardized testing, and portable sensing systems for efficient

BACKGROUND: Recent advances in artificial intelligence enable fully automated 
3-dimensional computed tomography (CT)-based body composition quantification. We 
investigated whether automated CT-derived thoraco-abdominopelvic body 
composition measures are associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic 
valve replacement.
METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, consecutive patients 
undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with preprocedural CT imaging 
were included between 2014 and 2023. A deep learning-based pipeline performed 
automated 3-dimensional segmentation of thoraco-abdominopelvic noncontrast CT 
scans to quantify volumes (L/m2) and attenuations (Hounsfield units) of 
subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, muscular adipose tissue, 
and lean skeletal muscle, indexed to body surface area. Associations with 
mortality were evaluated using Cox models and Harrell C statistics, adjusting 
for demographics (age, sex, body mass index) and cardiometabolic risk factors 
(hypertension, diabetes, chronic renal failure).
RESULTS: Among 915 patients (median age, 84 years [interquartile range, 77-90]; 
58% men), 160 (17.5%) died over a median follow-up of 22 months (interquartile 
range, 14-36). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated that lower 
subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation were 
associated with increased mortality, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and 
attenuation were associated with improved survival. Addition of body composition 
measures provided incremental discriminatory value beyond demographics and 
cardiometabolic risk factors (Harrell C, 0.66 versus 0.71; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Automated 3-dimensional CT-derived body composition measures 
provide independent prognostic information and improve risk stratification for 
mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Low subcutaneous adipose 
tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation identify patients at 
increased risk, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation are 
associated with lower mortality.

BACKGROUND: Variants in the ion channel gene KCNQ1 are the leading cause of 
congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS), a disorder characterized by QT prolongation 
and risk of fatal arrhythmias. The expanding use of genetic testing has led to 
the identification of numerous variants of uncertain significance, complicating 
clinical interpretation and risk stratification. Functional characterization of 
KCNQ1 variants is essential to define their role in long QT syndrome and advance 
precision medicine in cardiovascular care.
METHODS: We generated a nearly comprehensive variant library of 13 403 
protein-coding variants in KCNQ1. Using 4 pooled assays followed by 
high-throughput sequencing, we characterized the variants' effects on cell 
surface abundance and channel function in both the variant-only and heterozygous 
states. Case-control analyses and data from large-scale biobanks were used to 
assess the clinical impact of loss-of-function variants on QT prolongation and 
long QT syndrome. Heterozygous assay results were used to determine 
dominant-negative effects, which were also evaluated for association with 
arrhythmia risk. Protein structural clustering of distinct classes of 
deleterious variants was analyzed.
RESULTS: Across the 4 assays, we generated 49 305 functional measurements of 
KCNQ1 variants. Of the 13 403 KCNQ1 studied variants, 1757 demonstrated strong 
pathogenic evidence, and 6660 showed moderate benign evidence. Loss-of-function 
variants were significantly associated with QT prolongation and long QT syndrome 
in case-control and biobank analyses. Deleterious variants clustered within 
distinct structural domains based on their functional classification. A majority 
of pathogenic variants exhibited dominant-negative effects; these variants were 
linked to a higher risk of arrhythmia diagnoses than were haploinsufficient 
variants.
CONCLUSIONS: This comprehensive KCNQ1 functional atlas provides novel functional 
evidence for most KCNQ1 variants of uncertain significance. It also reveals 
mechanistic principles linking genetic variation to ion channel biology and 
arrhythmia susceptibility, advancing cardiovascular precision medicine.

BACKGROUND: Although Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) domains 
independently quantify patients' symptoms, physical and social functioning, and 
quality of life, the interrelationships between domains (eg, symptoms impacting 
physical limitations) have not been described, nor whether these vary by age or 
sex.
METHODS: Cross-sectional data from adult outpatients with heart failure and 
reduced ejection fraction from 2 multicenter US registries, the Change the 
Management of Patients With Heart Failure Registry (2015-2017) and 
Cardiovascular Outcomes Research Consortium (2001-2002), were used to fit 
recursive path analysis models relating age, sex, and KCCQ domain scores. The 
interrelationships of these factors were quantified using unstandardized and 
standardized effect estimates. Unstandardized effects denote the linear effect 
of the independent variable on the dependent variable in units specific to both 
variables. Standardized effects are unitless and are obtained by multiplying the 
unstandardized effect by the ratio of the standard deviations of the dependent 
and independent variables.
RESULTS: The analytic cohorts included 4839 patients from the Change the 
Management of Patients With Heart Failure Registry (mean age, 66.1±12.5 years, 
29.3% women) and 547 patients from the Cardiovascular Outcomes Research 
Consortium (mean age, 66±12 years, 23.8% women). Standardized effect estimates 
revealed moderate to strong interrelationships among the KCCQ domains (effect 
size range, 0.34-0.70). Symptoms were strongly associated with all other domains 
(range, 0.61-0.70). Quality of life was most associated with symptoms and social 
limitations (range: 0.48-0.60), and less so with physical limitations (effect 
size=0.34). By comparison, the associations of age and sex with KCCQ domains 
were much smaller (effect sizes <0.2), and no interactions by age and sex were 
found.
CONCLUSIONS: KCCQ domains were strongly interrelated, and these relationships 
did not differ appreciably by age or sex. These data enhance the interpretation 
of KCCQ domain scores in research and clinical practice; in particular, symptoms 
and social limitations may be key drivers of impaired quality of life in heart 
failure. Targeted interventions prioritizing these domains may most effectively 
improve patients' overall health status.

Whisky H(1), Shahrestani M(1), Amalina I(2), Ullah N(3), Fernandez GV(4), Drake

Author information:
(1)Department of Medical Sciences, Faculty of Health and Social Care, University

Cubic iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) are commonly synthesized via thermal 
decomposition in organic solvents, yielding well-defined particles but requiring 
complex phase-transfer steps that hinder scalability. In contrast, aqueous 
co-precipitation offers a simple, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly 
alternative, although it typically produces spherical nanoparticles with limited 
control over size and morphology. In this study, sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) 
was introduced as an additive during the aqueous co-precipitation of iron 
chlorides, enabling the direct synthesis of cubic IONPs. Particle size was 
precisely tuned from 15 to 38 nm by varying the reaction pH between 11.6 and 
13.2, as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy. Electron diffraction 
revealed that the nanoparticles consisted predominantly of magnetite with minor 
hematite impurities, while Raman spectroscopy showed enhanced magnetite 
formation at higher pH values through increased intensity of the characteristic 
668 cm-1 peak. Magnetic hyperthermia measurements performed at 93 kHz and 7.9 kA 
m-1 produced specific absorption rate (SAR) values of 2.0-3.4 W g-1 [Fe], with 
SAR increasing with particle size. Notably, 38 nm cubic IONPs exhibited a 
3.8-fold higher SAR than comparable particles synthesized via organic-solvent 
routes, demonstrating a scalable aqueous strategy for producing high-performance 
cubic IONPs for biomedical applications.

Label-free fluorescent detection of miRNA-21 via EXPAR-triggered rolling circle 
amplification coupled with a dimeric/tandem G-quadruplex-thioflavin T reporter.

Zhang H(1), Yuan Y(1), Ren Y(2), Zhao Y(2), Qi Y(2), Feng F(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)School of Medical Technology, Shaanxi University of Chinese Medicine, 
Xianyang, Shaanxi, China.
(2)Department of Clinical Laboratory, Affiliated Hospital of Shaanxi University 
of Chinese Medicine, Xianyang, Shaanxi, China. feixue0422@126.com.

MicroRNA-21 is a well recognized oncogenic microRNA and is involved in the 
initiation and development of many cancers, making it an important candidate 
marker for diagnosis. In this work, a label-free fluorescent assay was designed 
for highly sensitive miRNA-21 detection by coupling exponential amplification 
reaction (EXPAR), rolling circle amplification (RCA), and dimeric 
G-quadruplex/thioflavin T (ThT) signal reporting. The designed asymmetric 
hairpin probe specifically recognizes the target and initiates the EXPAR, 
generating abundant trigger strands that subsequently activate RCA. The RCA 
products contain repeated G-rich segments encoding tandem/dimeric G4-forming 
motifs, which form multiple G-quadruplex units in the presence of K+. After ThT 
binds to these structures, a clear fluorescence output is generated. Benefiting 
from the effectively suppressed background leakage by the hairpin design and the 
significantly enhanced signal generation enabled by the EXPAR-RCA cascade, the 
assay exhibits excellent analytical performance. The fluorescence response shows 
a good linear correlation over the range of 10 fM to 10 nM, with a limit of 
detection (LOD) of 1.58 fM. The method also demonstrates high selectivity toward 
miRNA-21, capable of discriminating single-base mismatched sequences. 
Furthermore, analysis of diluted serum and cellular RNA samples demonstrated the 
preliminary applicability of the proposed strategy in biological matrices. The 
method provides a convenient, low-cost, and highly sensitive analytical platform 
for miRNA detection and bioanalytical research.

Polyurethane (PU) is a ubiquitous polymer in modern life across the world yet 
its inherent flammability and the severe toxicological impacts of traditional 
halogenated flame retardants (FRs) present critical safety and environmental 
challenges. This review comprehensively examines the framework shift from 
petrochemical-based, additive-reliant PUs toward inherently flame-retardant, 
bio-based polyurethanes and non-isocyanate polyurethanes (NIPUs). Herein we 
introduce an integrative "Structure-Property-Sustainability" framework that 
systematically connects molecular design, flame-retardant performance, material 
properties, industrial applicability, and lifecycle sustainability. We 
thoroughly analyze the molecular engineering of renewable feedstocks, such as 
lignin, chitosan, proteins, phytic acid and tannins, to promote robust 
condensed-phase charring and thermal shielding. We further explore advanced 
composite architectures, including layer-by-layer (LbL) nanocoatings and 
microencapsulation, designed to decouple fire performance from mechanical 
degradation. Furthermore, this review broadens its scope beyond conventional 
combustion performance to evaluate lifecycle impacts and techno-economic

Speciation and thermodynamic properties of the cobalt(II)

Derison F(1), Lommelen R(1), Raiguel S(1), Binnemans K(1).

Author information:
(1)KU Leuven, Department of Chemistry, Solvomet Group, Celestijnenlaan 200F, Box

research has motivated further study of methanesulfonate systems. Cobalt, like 
nickel, is an essential component of the cathode active materials used in 
lithium-ion batteries, yet its solution chemistry in MSA media remains 
insufficiently characterized. In this work, the Co(CH3SO3)2-MSA-H2O system was 
investigated with an emphasis on solid-liquid equilibria. The liquid phase was 
characterized via solubility, density, and water activity measurements over a

investigated through thermogravimetric analysis and single-crystal X-ray 
diffraction. Three different hydrates were identified: Co(CH3SO3)2·6H2O,

independent experimental methods, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) and the 
isothermal solubility method, with good agreement between both approaches. The 
solubility data reveal that cobalt(II) methanesulfonate solubility decreases 
with increasing MSA concentration but remains higher than that in sulfuric acid 
media, while temperature effects are limited within the studied range. The 
experimental dataset was used to develop a thermodynamic model with the 
Mixed-Solvent Electrolyte (OLI-MSE) framework of OLI Systems. Thermodynamic 
properties of the hydrates and interaction parameters for the aqueous phase were 
optimized to achieve an accurate calculation of the system.

Dietary strategies to combat arterial stiffness in cardiometabolic disease: a 
network meta-analysis.

Norouzzadeh M(1)(2)(3), HasanRashedi M(4), Afrashteh S(5)(1), Emamat H(5)(1).

Author information:
(1)The Persian Gulf Tropical Medicine Research Center, The Persian Gulf 
Biomedical Sciences Research Institute, Bushehr University of Medical Sciences, 
Bushehr, Iran. mononutrition77@gmail.com.
(2)Department of Clinical Nutrition, School of Nutritional Sciences and 
Dietetics, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran.
(3)Students' Scientific Research Center (SSRC), Tehran University of Medical 
Sciences, Tehran, Iran.
(4)Department of Nutrition, School of Public Health, Iran University of Medical 
Sciences, Tehran, Iran. minoohrs98@gmail.com.
(5)Addiction and Lifestyle Research Center, Bushehr University of Medical 
Sciences, Bushehr, Iran. Hadiemamat@yahoo.com.

Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and hypertension (HTN) are leading causes of 
global morbidity and mortality. Arterial stiffness, assessed via augmentation 
index (AIx) and pulse wave velocity (PWV), serves as an independent prognostic 
marker of vascular damage; however, the comparative efficacy of dietary 
interventions on these parameters remains poorly characterized. This network 
meta-analysis (NMA) aimed to compare and rank the efficacy of dietary 
interventions, including supplements, nutraceuticals, and dietary patterns, on 
AIx and PWV in individuals with CVD or HTN. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and 
the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for eligible randomized 
controlled trials (RCTs) published up to January 2025. Two independent reviewers 
screened and extracted data following PRISMA-NMA guidelines. A total of 48 RCTs 
comprising 2719 participants and 31 dietary interventions were included. Study 
quality and certainty of evidence (CoE) were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of 
Bias tool and GRADE approach, respectively. A random-effects NMA within a 
frequentist framework estimated mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence 
intervals (CIs). For PWV, grape seed extract (MD: -1.70; 95%CI: -3.36 to -0.04; 
CoE: Moderate) and vitamin B9 (MD: -1.46; 95%CI: -2.61 to -0.31; CoE: Moderate) 
reduced arterial stiffness versus placebo. No intervention reached significance 
for AIx, though alpha-linolenic acid, dietary nitrate, and wine extract showed 
the greatest numerical improvements. Sensitivity analyses yielded results 
consistent with the primary analyses, with no publication bias detected. The 
grape seed extract and folic acid show potential to reduce arterial stiffness. 
Future population-specific, dose-optimized RCTs are warranted to establish 
definitive therapeutic recommendations.

Substitution, addition or stepping-stone? Exploring the temporal associations 
between the consumption of alcoholic and alcohol-free beverages among Dutch 
university students.

van Hooijdonk KJM(1), Dams LJJ(1), van Noorden THJ(1), Vink JM(1).

Author information:
(1)Behavioural Science Institute, Radboud University, Nijmegen, The Netherlands.

BACKGROUND AND AIM: Stimulating the use of alcohol-free beverages is portrayed 
as one strategy to reduce excessive alcohol use and alcohol-related harm among 
students in higher education. This strategy relies on the assumption that 
students drink alcohol-free to substitute alcohol (i.e. 'substitution effect'), 
while other possibilities like drinking alcohol-free in addition to alcohol 
(i.e. 'addition effect') or alcohol-free acting as a step-up to consume (more) 
alcohol (i.e. 'stepping-stone' effect) have largely been neglected. 
Consequently, this pre-registered study aimed to examine bi-directional temporal 
associations between the quantity of alcohol and alcohol-free use among 
university students (aim 1). Next, these bi-directional temporal associations 
were examined in subgroups: females vs. males (aim 2) and members vs. 
non-members of student associations (aim 3).
DESIGN: Observational study, utilizing wave 2, wave 3 and wave 4 of Radboud 
University's Healthy Student Life study. Data were collected May-July 2022, 2023 
and 2024.
SETTING: The Netherlands.
PARTICIPANTS: 9951 university students, of which 6790 students had only 
cross-sectional data, while 2383 and 778 students participated in 2 and 3 
surveys, respectively. At wave 2, participants' mean age was 23 (standard 
deviation = 4.0). 70% were female, 17% were members of a student association, 
13% were international students and 57% were enrolled in a bachelor programme.
MEASUREMENTS: At all waves, participants self-reported the frequency and 
quantity of alcohol and alcohol-free beverage consumption, using two (adapted) 
items of the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test - Consumption (AUDIT-C). 
Additionally, participants self-reported on: gender, student association 
membership, living situation, relationship status and other substance use. Last, 
information on biological sex, age, educational programme and (inter)national 
status was received from the university administrative records. Random Intercept 
Cross-Lagged Panel Models were used to study reciprocal effects between the 
quantity of alcohol and alcohol-free use, by decomposing observed scores in 
between-person differences and within-person dynamics.
RESULTS: None of the analyses, in the total sample (aim 1; b between 0.02 and 
0.03, p between 0.414 and 0.779) or in subgroups (aims 2-3; b between -0.001 and 
0.12, p between 0.192 and 0.988), provided support for within-person 
cross-lagged effects between the quantity of alcohol and alcohol-free use.
SUMMARY: Among Dutch university students, no evidence was found for substitution 
or stepping-stone effects of alcohol-free beverages, which (indirectly) suggests 
that students generally drink alcohol-free as an additive to alcohol, rather 
than as a substitute or stepping-stone.

A New Protocol for Evaluating Maximum Respiratory Pressures in Individuals With

Fabero-Garrido R(1), Aguilar-Zafra S, Del Corral T, López-de-Uralde-Villanueva 
I.

Author information:
(1)Department of Physiotherapy, Faculty of Nursing, Physiotherapy and Podiatry, 
Complutense University of Madrid, Madrid, Spain (R.F.-G.); Departamento de 
Fisioterapia, Facultad de Ciencias de la Salud, Motion in Brains Research Group, 
Centro Superior de Estudios Universitarios La Salle, Universidad Autónoma de 
Madrid, Spain (S.A.-Z.); Téxum S.L. Physiotherapy Center, Coslada, Spain 
(S.A.-Z.); and Department of Physiotherapy, Faculty of Nursing, Physiotherapy 
and Podiatry, Universidad Complutense de Madrid; IdISSC, Madrid, Spain (T.d.-C.

BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: There is a need for new and inexpensive methods for the 
maximum inspiratory and expiratory pressures (MIP/MEP) test. The one-repetition 
maximum (1RM) test is an easy and cost-effective method to measure maximal 
strength. The purpose of this study was to validate a MIP/MEP test protocol 
based on the 1RM test, its test-retest reliability, and minimal detectable 
change (MDC) in individuals with multiple sclerosis.
METHODS: Fifty-two individuals (53.6 ± 10 years; 5.7 ± 1.8 points on Expanded 
Disability Status Scale) (46% relapsing-remitting; 23% primary progressive; 31% 
secondary progressive) attended two appointments 7 to 10 days apart. MIP/MEP 
tests were performed using a threshold valve device (1RM-based protocol) and a 
digital manometer (reference test). The 1RM-based protocol included an 
incremental phase (load increase [30 cmH2O] to achieve task failure) and a 
halving phase (load halfway between the lowest failed attempt and the last valid 
attempt was prescribed).
RESULTS: The concurrent validity of the 1RM-based protocol was good to excellent 
with respect to the reference test (MIP: day 1, n = 49, intraclass correlation 
coefficient [ICC (95% confidence intervals)] = 0.87 (0.78-0.93); day 2, n = 48, 
ICC = 0.91 (0.82-0.95); MEP: day 1, n = 49, ICC = 0.82 (0.60-0.91); day 2, n = 
49, ICC = 0.88 (0.64-0.95)). The test-retest reliability was good for MIP [n = 
46, ICC = 0.88 (0.79-0.93)] and excellent for MEP [n = 48, ICC = 0.90 
(0.83-0.94)]. The MDC(90-95) for MIP ranged from 23.7 to 28.2 cmH2O, and for MEP 
ranged from 19 to 22.5 cmH2O.
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: This study validated a new 1RM-based protocol for the 
MIP/MEP tests using a respiratory muscle training threshold valve device in 
individuals with multiple sclerosis, showing good to excellent concurrent 
validity compared with the reference test, as well as good to excellent 
test-retest reliability. The MDC reported can be interpreted and applied in the 
clinical setting.

Modeling intraframe dynamics in STEM imaging and their impact on 
three-dimensional nanoparticle reconstruction: when time blurs space.

Stoops T(1)(2), Luyckx K(1)(2), De Backer A(1)(2), Van Aert S(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)EMAT, University of Antwerp, Groenenborgerlaan 171, 2020 Antwerp, Belgium. 
Sandra.VanAert@uantwerpen.be.
(2)NANOlight Center of Excellence, University of Antwerp, Groenenborgerlaan 171, 
2020 Antwerp, Belgium.

The unique properties of nanoparticles arise from their specific structures and 
sizes. In particular, the dynamics of atoms on the surface of a nanoparticle are 
of great interest as they may influence properties such as optical response, 
electronic structure, magnetic behavior, and catalytic activity. Annular dark 
field scanning transmission electron microscopy (ADF-STEM) combined with atom 
counting enables the 3D reconstruction of nanoparticles at the atomic scale from 
a single projection. This approach implicitly assumes that the nanoparticle 
remains static during the acquisition of a single image. While surface dynamics 
have been investigated through time series of images, the intraframe dynamics 
that occur during the acquisition of a single image have been ignored so far. 
Since single pixel dwell times are typically of the order of microseconds, 
significant atomic dynamics may occur during the acquisition of an entire image. 
In this study, we use a controlled simulation framework to investigate the 
effect of intraframe dynamics on the quantitative interpretation of ADF-STEM 
images by explicitly modeling atomic motion during image acquisition and 
analyzing its impact on atom counting and the 3D reconstruction. Our results 
provide a physics-based interpretation of single frame ADF-STEM images of 
simulated dynamic nanoparticles and show that 3D reconstructions closely 
approximate the nanoparticle's median occupancy structure, suppressing low 
occupancy positions corresponding to mobile surface features.

BACKGROUND: As weight-loss therapies are increasingly incorporated into clinical 
practice for MASLD, assessing body composition has become increasingly 
important. Body muscle-to-fat ratio (BMFR) may provide an intuitive and 
integrated measure of body composition balance, but its association with 
long-term prognosis in MASLD remains unclear.
METHODS: We studied 83 006 UK Biobank participants with MASLD. BMFR was 
calculated as whole-body muscle mass divided by whole-body fat mass using 
bioelectrical impedance analysis. Restricted cubic spline, threshold-effect and 
two-piecewise Cox models assessed associations with liver-related events (LREs), 
cardiovascular events (CVEs), cardiovascular mortality and all-cause mortality, 
adjusting for BMI and other confounders.

Sex-specific inflection points were identified for each outcome. For LREs, the 
thresholds were 2.82 in men and 1.45 in women; below these thresholds, each 1-SD 
increase in BMFR was associated with a lower risk of LREs (men: HR = 0.86, 95%

HR = 1.33, 95% CI: 1.11-1.59). For CVEs, the thresholds were 2.03 in men and 
1.48 in women; below these thresholds, each 1-SD increase in BMFR was associated 
with a lower risk in both sexes (men: HR = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.70-0.85; women: 
HR = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.81-0.89), whereas above them the association was not 
significant in men but was associated with a higher risk in women (HR = 1.19, 
95% CI: 1.09-1.30). Cardiovascular mortality and all-cause mortality showed 
sex-specific non-linear patterns similar to those observed for CVEs.

outcomes. Associations were generally U-shaped in women; in men, they were 
U-shaped for LREs and closer to L-shaped for cardiovascular outcomes and 
mortality. BMFR may provide complementary information on body composition beyond 
BMI. Further studies are needed to validate these exploratory findings.

Ibuprofen (IBU), a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agent, faces restricted 
application mainly due to its intrinsically poor aqueous solubility and 
resultant low membrane permeability. With the continuous advancement of gel 
research, small-molecule hydrogels have garnered increasing attention in the

personal experiences). There were no restrictions on language, location, or year

increase in suicide bereavement/postvention publications annually. 95% of 
publications were by first authors from high-income countries, while 1.3% of 
first authors were from lower-middle-income and low-income countries. Most 
studies were empirical and followed a quantitative or qualitative design, 
primarily cross-sectional, increasing over the years, while nonempirical 
publications declined. We identified few longitudinal or interventional studies. 
Populations sampled most frequently were working-age adults, with few studies 
focused on older adults. Limitations: The results provide little information 
about the methodological quality of the included studies. Some full texts could 
not be found and were unavailable for data extraction. Conclusion: The research 
gaps identified suggest that future studies should focus on underrepresented 
populations as well as on high-quality intervention studies to address adverse 
outcomes among suicide loss survivors.

Health misinformation and disinformation: Old narratives, new technologies.

Rzymski P(1), Czech-Szczapa B(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Environmental Medicine, Poznan University of Medical Sciences, 
Poland.
(2)Department of Preventive Medicine, Epidemiology Unit, Poznan University of 
Medical Sciences, Poland.

This editorial discusses how health misinformation and disinformation combine 
long-established narratives with new technologies that substantially increase 
the speed, reach, personalization, and apparent credibility of misleading 
content. The novelty of the contemporary information environment lies less in 
entirely new false narratives than in digital infrastructures that allow 
misleading content to be created, tailored, disseminated, and monetized at 
unprecedented scale. Online social media platforms and generative artificial 
intelligence (AI) have transformed these conditions, enabling misleading health 
information to be created and disseminated at previously impossible scale and 
speed. Health misinformation and disinformation can influence behavior, 
undermine trust in scientific and public health institutions, delay appropriate 
care, promote ineffective or harmful interventions, and weaken responses to 
disease outbreaks. Their effects may be particularly pronounced among 
populations with limited access to reliable information, healthcare, and trusted 
institutions. This editorial also examines how engagement-driven platform 
design, commercial and political incentives, synthetic media, and inconsistent 
safeguards amplify the problem. It argues that fact-checking and individual 
media literacy, while necessary, are insufficient on their own. A more effective 
response requires timely, transparent public health communication; institutional 
support for healthcare professionals; greater platform accountability; 
systematic safety evaluation of generative AI; independent access to relevant 
data; and policies that address the incentives sustaining the production and 
circulation of false and misleading health information.

Generation Sequencing. Dysgeneses of the AS are still controversial in their 
nosology and etiology; most are discussed on the basis of brain imaging findings 
alone. In this series, complete fetal and neuropathological examination allowed 
detection of key clinical and histopathological clues, allowing the orientation 
of molecular screenings and the identification of cellular mechanisms involved

Jiang G(1), Xue X(1), Tao F(1), Imran T(1), Wang Q(2), Nazeeruddin MK(1)(3), Gao

Author information:
(1)Institute of Perovskite Photovoltaics and Integrated Optoelectronics (IPO),

2D/3D perovskite heterointerfaces are widely used to improve the operational 
stability of perovskite solar cells, but their molecular role is often described 
mainly in terms of surface passivation. Bulky spacer cations coordinate 
under-coordinated surface sites, form hydrogen-bonding networks, and suppress 
ion migration. Simultaneously, poorly coupled organic tails may increase 
tunnelling distance and weaken charge extraction. This review discusses bulky 
cations as dual-directional chemical bridges rather than simple insulating 
barriers. The polar headgroup anchors the inorganic lattice through 
coordination, hydrogen bonding, and conformational restriction, whereas the 
exposed organic segment may tune interfacial energetics through dipolar effects, 
orbital overlap, and intermolecular π-π coupling. We compare the chemical 
mechanisms governing downward lattice stabilization and upward electronic 
communication, and highlight surface-sensitive tools required to probe molecular 
orientation, local potential shifts, and buried interfacial interactions. 
Together, these considerations support a design framework in which spacer-cation 
arrays are treated as organized interfacial ensembles. In such ensembles, 
geometric matching and multiple non-covalent interactions may help connect 
lattice stabilization with charge extraction, providing a chemical basis for 
mitigating the efficiency-stability trade-off.

vulnerable populations, and the lack of standardized clinical protocols. Current 
evidence suggests that probiotics may represent a useful adjunct to existing AMR 
management strategies. However, their broader clinical application requires

ptau217 results. Diagnostic reclassification was assessed using binary (ptau217 
> 0.18) and higher threshold (ptau217 > 0.325) classification schemes. McNemar 
tests evaluated reclassification patterns, with subgroup analyses by 
apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 carrier status.
RESULTS: Diagnosis reclassification occurred in 37.8% and 46.9% of patients 
using the lower and higher threshold, respectively (both P<0.001). With the 
higher threshold (ptau217 > 0.325), reclassification among APOE ε4 carriers was 
balanced (42% from AD to non-AD vs. 43% from non-AD to AD, P=0.096). In 
contrast, APOE ε4 noncarriers showed significantly greater reclassification from 
AD to non-AD than from non-AD to AD (66% vs.14%, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Plasma ptau217 meaningfully influences diagnostic decisions in 
memory clinic practice and may be particularly valuable for refining diagnoses 
among APOE ε4 noncarriers.

BACKGROUND: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an autosomal recessive disease caused by 
mutations in cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene. 
CFTR modulators are drugs developed to target the defective protein. All over 
the world, there are patients considered non-eligible for this therapy according 
to local regulatory policies.
METHODS: To characterise the Portuguese CF patients defined as non-eligible

clinical trials exploring alternative therapeutic approaches.

Prone positioning in acute respiratory distress syndrome: A critical review of 
clinical evidence and practical challenges.

Park KJ(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Ajou University School of 
Medicine, Suwon, South Korea.

BACKGROUND: Early randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of prone positioning (PP) 
in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) failed to demonstrate a survival 
benefit despite consistent improvements in oxygenation. Subsequent meta-analyses 
suggested a survival advantage in patients with severe hypoxaemia, culminating 
in the landmark Proning Severe ARDS Patients (PROSEVA) trial, which reported a 
28-day mortality rate of 16.0% in patients with a PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio <150 mmHg. 
However, the optimal criteria for repeating and discontinuing PP sessions remain 
uncertain.
METHODS: A structured search of PubMed, Embase.com, and the Cochrane Central 
Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) was conducted to identify RCTs 
evaluating PP in adults with ARDS with mortality as a prespecified principal 
outcome. Relevant clinical studies, meta-analyses, and review articles were also 
evaluated to provide context for the narrative review.
RESULTS: Six RCTs were included in the main comparative analysis. Previous RCTs 
conducted before the PROSEVA trial used diverse protocols and treatment settings 
and did not demonstrate a survival benefit. Therefore, comparative assessments 
of these trials may provide valuable insights for optimising clinical practice. 
Based on a detailed comparison of the RCTs, the currently proposed benefits of 
early implementation of PP with prolonged duration may not fully explain the 
differences in outcomes observed across trials. Other potentially influential 
factors, including patient selection, timing, ventilatory management, centre 
experience, treatment delivery, and criteria for repeating and discontinuing PP 
sessions, warrant further evaluation in practical implementation studies. The 
development of automated equipment for PP may further improve procedural 
efficiency. This review critically examines both the positive and negative 
evidence regarding PP, highlighting methodological limitations and practical 
challenges to greater utilisation of PP.
CONCLUSION: PP has established clinical value in severe ARDS, but important 
uncertainties remain regarding its optimal implementation. Concerted efforts are 
required to establish standardised protocols and to optimise implementation of 
PP in ARDS management.

Understanding the change in calcium ion-binding, protein dynamics, and hydration

Pooja(1), Bandyopadhyay P(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Computational and Integrative Sciences, Jawaharlal Nehru 
University, New Delhi, India.

The protein Troponin-C is an important player in muscle contraction, and 
mutations in Cardiac Troponin-C (cTnC) have been associated with inherited 
cardiomyopathies. Till now, eight mutants of the N-domain of cTnC have been 
listed in the ClinVar database as pathogenic or likely pathogenic. Understanding 
the molecular mechanisms of these mutations is crucial for mitigating their 
effects. Previous work studied mutations A8V, A31S, and I4M and found that 
changes in the conformational landscape are a key feature of these mutations. In 
the current work, our focus is on two mutations, D3V and G34R, the only ones out 
of the eight mentioned that undergo a change of charge on mutation. We have 
performed molecular dynamics simulation and network analysis to calculate 
binding affinity between Ca2+ and mutants vis-à-vis the wild type, the change of 
Ca2+ coordination shell, the effect of water, protein dynamics, and the 
communication path from the mutation site to the binding site. Our findings show 
that both electrostatics and the location of the mutation are the key factors 
for the difference between WT and the two mutants. D3V, in a disordered region, 
disrupts long-range allostery through electrostatic and hydration changes, 
whereas G34R, near the binding site, induces local electrostatic and structural 
perturbations. The changed conformational landscape, as found for the previously 
studied mutants, is a general feature for these two mutations also; however, 
specific effects found here illustrate the diversity present in different 
mutants.

Molecular charge modulation offers a promising strategy for controlling the 
excited-state properties and aggregation behavior of organic luminophores. 
Nevertheless, the consequences of cationization strongly depend on the molecular 
structure. Herein, we investigate a twisted π-extended pyridine-dimethylacridan 
derivative (PyAcr) and its cationic pyridinium analogue (PyAcr+) to elucidate 
how neutral-to-cationic transformation affects their photophysical properties.

insight into the relationship between molecular structure, charge distribution, 
excited-state character, and emission behavior. PyAcr exhibits 
aggregation-induced delayed fluorescence (AIDF), accompanied by a moderate 
photoluminescence quantum yield of 45% and strong two-photon-excited 
fluorescence (TPEF) under near-infrared excitation. In contrast, conversion of

weakened emission, likely reflecting the combined effects of cation formation

exhibit high thermal stability, with onset temperatures of thermal degradation 
above 360 °C, good electrochemical stability, and small singlet-triplet energy 
gaps of 0.07-0.13 eV. Overall, the results demonstrate that cationization alone 
does not necessarily enhance luminescence and that the interplay between 
molecular charge, electronic coupling, and aggregation is critical for 
controlling excited-state dynamics. These structure-property relationships 
provide useful guidelines for the rational design of environment-responsive 
luminophores, while PyAcr shows promise as a two-photon-excited probe for 
bioimaging.

O-containing coordination spheres, even when conventional X-ray absorption or 
diffraction techniques provide limited contrast. This combined 
experimental-computational framework demonstrates that Zr Kβ VtC XES can resolve 
subtle ligand-dependent coordination changes in Zr-based materials, offering a

compatibility, bioaccessibility, safety assessment, quality specifications, and

Flavored e-cigarette use and its association with subsequent short-term 
e-cigarette abstinence among youth, young adults and adults: Findings from the 
United States longitudinal population assessment of tobacco use and health, 2016 
to 2023.

Streck JM(1)(2), Hyatt AS(2)(3), Schuster RM(1)(2), Gilman J(1)(2), Levy 
S(2)(4), Winickoff JP(2)(5), Evins AE(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Center for Addiction Medicine, Department of Psychiatry, Massachusetts 
General Hospital, Boston, MA, USA.
(2)Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA.
(3)Health Evaluation Research Lab, Department of Psychiatry, Cambridge Health 
Alliance, Cambridge, MA, USA.
(4)Division of Addiction Medicine, Boston Children's Hospital, Boston, MA, USA.
(5)Department of Pediatrics, Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, MA, USA.

AIMS: This study examined e-cigarette flavor use and its prospective association 
with short-term e-cigarette abstinence among youth (12-17 years old), young 
adults (18-24 years old) and adults (25+ years old) using United States 
(US)-representative data.
DESIGN: Observational study using longitudinal data obtained from the Population 
Assessment of Tobacco and Health (PATH) study, waves 4-7 (2016-2023). A lagged 
design assessed three wave-pairings per participant.
SETTING: Household computer-assisted self-interviews of US youth and adults from 
2016 to 2023.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of n = 8418 non-institutionalized youth and adults in the 
US.
MEASUREMENTS: The primary exposure was past 30-day e-cigarette flavor use at the 
previous wave using the following mutually exclusive flavor groupings: exclusive 
tobacco flavor or flavorless e-cigarette use, exclusive menthol/mint flavor, 
exclusive sweet flavors (e.g. candy, fruit, chocolate, clove/spice) or use of 
multiple e-cigarette flavors (defined as individuals vaping multiple flavor 
combinations from: tobacco/flavorless, menthol/mint and sweet flavors); the 
primary outcome was past 30-day e-cigarette abstinence at the subsequent wave 
(yes/no). Generalized estimating equation (GEE) models examined prospective 
association between e-cigarette flavor type and covariates [e.g. demographics, 
e-cigarette dependence (time to first e-cigarette: ≤ 30 minutes of waking vs. > 
30 minutes), dual cigarette and e-cigarette use (yes/no)], on e-cigarette 
abstinence (primary outcome). We ran an overall GEE model adjusting for age 
group and three individual GEE models stratified by age group. All estimates 
were weighted.
RESULTS: Exclusive sweet flavors were the most common e-cigarette flavor used 
among youth (46%), young adults (44%) and adults (41%). In the adjusted model, 
young adults [adjusted odds ratio (AOR) = 3.63, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 
3.0-4.3, P < 0.001] and adults (AOR = 4.58, 95% CI = 3.8-5.6, P < 0.001) who 
vaped in the past 30 days had higher odds of subsequent e-cigarette abstinence 
compared with youth who vaped in the past 30 days. Across ages, among past 
30-day vapers, exclusive tobacco/flavorless e-cigarette use was prospectively 
associated with increased e-cigarette abstinence (AOR = 2.2, 95% CI = 1.9-2.5, 
P < 0.001), multiple-flavor-use was associated with decreased e-cigarette 
abstinence (AOR = 0.61, 95% CI = 0.53-0.71, P < 0.001), compared with exclusive 
menthol or sweet-flavored e-cigarette use. Dual e-cigarette and cigarette use 
was prospectively associated with reduced e-cigarette abstinence in young adults 
(AOR = 0.60, 95% CI = 0.50-0.80, P < 0.001), yet increased e-cigarette 
abstinence in adults (AOR = 1.4, 95% CI = 1.1-1.6, P < 0.001).

When do starch-polyphenol complexes qualify as type 5 resistant starch? A 
critical evidence framework from molecular assembly to colonic utilization.

Su K(1), Xiao W(1), Han S(1), Yang X(1), Zheng Z(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Food and Biological Engineering, Key Laboratory for Agricultural 
Products Processing of Anhui Province, Hefei University of Technology, Hefei, 
China.

Starch-polyphenol complexes are increasingly explored for modulating starch 
digestibility, developing low-glycemic-index foods, and improving polyphenol 
stability and delivery. Some systems have been described as type 5 resistant 
starch (RS5) or RS5-like based on V-type crystalline signals, increased 
resistant starch content, or reduced glucose release. However, these outcomes 
alone are insufficient for RS5 assignment because they may also arise from 
surface adsorption, non-inclusion networks, substrate shielding, enzyme 
inhibition by free or released polyphenols, or food-matrix effects. This review 
critically assesses the evidence required to describe starch-polyphenol systems 
as V-type starch-polyphenol complexes with demonstrated enzymatic resistance and 
examines their relationship to the proposed non-lipid extension of RS5. Evidence 
from molecular assembly, structural characterization, processing-induced 
rearrangement, resistance to enzymatic digestion, polyphenol release, colonic 
fermentation, and physiological relevance is integrated. V-type or V-type-like 
inclusion provides the strongest structural basis for identifying a V-type 
starch-polyphenol complex, whereas surface-bound complexes, non-inclusion 
networks and covalent derivatives require different mechanistic descriptions. 
Mechanistic attribution should include removal and quantification of unbound 
polyphenols, physical-mixture and washed-complex controls, and enzyme-inhibition 
kinetics. A tiered evidence framework is proposed to classify these systems as 
putative RS5, RS5-like complexes, polyphenol-bound resistant starch candidates, 
enzyme-inhibition-dominated systems, or non-RS mixtures.

Dual-Interface Engineering of Cs2CuBiBr6-Based Memristive Synaptic Devices for 
Neuromorphic Computing.

Kim CE(1), Cho S(2), Choi YS(1), Lee JY(3), Lee D(4), Kim J(5), Kang DW(6), Ha 
TJ(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Electronic Materials Engineering, Kwangwoon University, 
Seoul01897, Republic of Korea.
(2)Department of Smart Cities, Chung-Ang University, 84 Heukseok-ro, Dongjak-gu, 
Seoul06974, Republic of Korea.
(3)Young Investigator Group, Robotized Material and Photovoltaic Engineering, 
Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie GmbH, Hahn-Meitner-Platz 1, 
Berlin14109, Germany.
(4)School of Semiconductor Systems Engineering, Kwangwoon University, 
Seoul01897, Republic of Korea.
(5)School of Engineering, Macquarie University , Sydney, NSW2109, Australia.
(6)Department of Energy Systems Engineering, Chung-Ang University, 84 
Heukseok-ro, Dongjak-gu, Seoul06974, Republic of Korea.

Pb-free double perovskite Cs2CuBiBr6 (CCBB)-based resistive random-access memory 
(ReRAM) synaptic devices are developed using a dual-interface engineering 
approach to achieve stable resistive switching and neuromorphic functionality. 
High-quality CCBB thin films are obtained via optimized antisolvent-assisted 
crystallization, enabling enhanced crystallinity and reduced defect-induced 
energetic disorder. Modification of the bottom interface with a 
poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) interlayer 
improves CCBB film continuity and provides a more favorable environment for 
homogeneous charge injection. The introduction of an ultrathin bathocuproine 
(BCP) interlayer at the top interface regulates the spatial redistribution of 
Ag-related species. The cooperative regulation of charge injection and 
Ag-related electro-ionic processes promotes more reproducible formation and 
rupture of localized conductive pathways, resulting in improved switching 
stability and device-to-device reproducibility. The CCBB-based ReRAM exhibits 
reliable bipolar resistive switching over 600 cycles, an on/off current ratio of 
approximately 103, and stable data retention up to 104 s. Gradual and repeatable 
conductance modulation under electrical pulse stimulation further demonstrates 
synaptic potentiation and depression behaviors. MNIST-based neural network 
simulations reveal excellent neuromorphic performance, with up to 90% 
recognition accuracy. This work highlights cooperative dual-interface regulation 
of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes as an effective 
design strategy for achieving reliable Pb-free perovskite ReRAM and neuromorphic 
synaptic operation.
