Hydrogen-bonded conjugated small molecules in organic electronics.

Más-Montoya M(1), Curiel D(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Organic Chemistry - Faculty of Chemistry, University of Murcia, 
Murcia 30100, Spain. miriammas@um.es.

Organic semiconductors have become highly important for next-generation 
electronic devices. However, further research is needed to enhance their 
charge-transport properties and long-term stability. These challenges largely 
originate from their solid-state structure, as organic semiconductors are 
molecular solids whose organisation is governed by very weak non-covalent 
interactions. Accordingly, the weakness of intermolecular interactions increases 
the chances of having structural disorder and generating defects, which 
detrimentally affect the performance of organic semiconductors. Therefore, 
controlling molecular organisation is a key objective. Hydrogen bonding is 
particularly effective for promoting solid-state self-assembly and gaining 
certain control over molecular organisation. The strength of hydrogen bonds, 
their directionality, and the broad range of functional groups and structures 
that can act as hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors have encouraged their 
rational incorporation into the molecular design of organic semiconductors. This 
Feature Article presents a review of the structural approaches developed to 
enhance the performance of materials based on small molecules through the 
integration of hydrogen-bond donor and acceptor sites within the conjugated 
framework. It also discusses the implementation of these materials in different 
types of electronic devices.

Recent declines in Finnish students' reading performance highlight the need for 
efficient assessment tools that identify specific processes underlying reading 
comprehension. This study aimed to adapt and validate the deep cloze test for 
Finnish sixth graders. The test is designed to measure the ability to draw 
global coherence inferences for reading comprehension and has previously been

the surgical treatment of mild-to-moderate aponeurotic blepharoptosis with a 
positive 2.5% phenylephrine test, but the mechanisms by which it achieves 
adequate eyelid elevation remain incompletely understood. The aim of this study 
was to quantify the proportion of Müller's muscle present in surgical specimens, 
to evaluate the degree of chronic inflammation in the resected tissue, and to 
correlate these histological findings with postoperative clinical outcomes

AIM: To examine how artificial intelligence literacy, self-efficacy and 
perceptions and attitudes relate to artificial intelligence acceptance among 
nutrition and dietetics students, practising dietitians and academics in 
Türkiye.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was administered to 317 participants

A host-virus arms race over FAM134B in African swine fever virus infection.

Wang T(1), Luo R(1), Huang R(1), Sun Y(1), Qiu HJ(1).

Author information:
(1)State Key Laboratory of Animal Disease Control and Prevention, Harbin 
Veterinary Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Harbin,

Although reticulophagy, the selective autophagy of the endoplasmic reticulum 
(ER), restricts several RNA viruses, whether this pathway constrains DNA virus 
infection remains unknown. Recently, we found that FAM134B (family with sequence 
similarity 134 member B), an ER-resident cargo receptor that mediates 
reticulophagy, restricts African swine fever virus (ASFV), a large cytoplasmic 
DNA virus, by targeting the major capsid proteins p72 and pA137R for lysosomal 
degradation, thereby blocking capsid assembly at perinuclear viral factories. 
ASFV counters this restriction through the virulence factor pMGF300-2 R encoded 
by the MGF300-2 R gene of ASFV, which binds to FAM134B, recruits LC3B 
(microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta), an ATG8 
(autophagy-related protein 8) family member, via the C-terminal LC3-interacting 
region (LIR) motif, and directs FAM134B into autophagic degradation. Deletion of 
the MGF300-2 R gene in the ASFV genome restores FAM134B abundance, reduces viral 
replication, and attenuates virulence in pigs. These findings establish 
reticulophagy as a previously unrecognized antiviral barrier against a large DNA 
virus and reveal a host-virus arms race centered on the reticulophagy receptor.

transition remains poorly characterised.

METHODS: We analysed the Afghanistan Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2022-23.

depth and facility-based delivery, with substantial uncertainty around several 
median-based classifications.Global health impact for policy and action:

Lee BH(1), Green MC(1), Tenzek KE(1), Paravati E(1).

AIM: ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter proteins play pivotal roles in 
antimicrobial resistance and bacterial virulence. However, their 
characterisation across major endodontic pathogens remains limited. This study 
aimed to characterise ABC transporter proteins in silico across five endodontic 
pathogens and to investigate their implications for antimicrobial resistance and 
virulence.
METHODOLOGY: Reference genome-predicted proteomes of Enterococcus faecalis, 
Porphyromonas gingivalis, Fusobacterium nucleatum, Actinomyces naeslundii and

InterProScan and HMMER and assigned to five functional categories based on Pfam 
domain signatures. Physicochemical parameters were computed and analysed by

independence. Domain architecture and phylogenetic analyses were performed using 
MAFFT, FastTree and Interactive Tree of Life.

per species), with A. naeslundii exhibiting the highest transporter density 
(55.3 per Mb). Putative multidrug resistance pumps were dominant (78.7%) and 
were highest in F. nucleatum (87.1%) and E. faecalis (82.2%). Functional 
category distribution differed significantly between species (χ2 = 22.043, 
df = 8, p = 0.005). Significant inter-species differences were identified in 
Grand Average of Hydropathy (GRAVY) score, aromaticity, isoelectric point and 
instability index (all p < 0.001). BLASTP confirmed the efrAB efflux operon in 
E. faecalis (EfrA: 99.65%; EfrB: 100.00%) alongside 13 homologue proteins.

sequence-confirmed efrAB proteins and 13 homologues in E. faecalis, provides a

Pre-sleep milk-derived proteins do not impair sleep or recovery in elite female

Paterson KGP(1)(2), Griest TD(1)(2), Angeles E(2), Fenner SP(1)(2), Eberhardt 
HK(1)(2), McKay CR(1)(2), Helms KLW(1), Calderon A(1), Vukovich MD(3), Ormsbee 
MJ(1)(2)(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Health, Nutrition, and Food Sciences, Florida State University, 
Tallahassee, FL, USA.
(2)Institute of Sports Sciences & Medicine, Florida State University, 
Tallahassee, FL, USA.
(3)College of Education and Human Sciences, South Dakota State University, 
Brookings, SD, USA.
(4)School of Health Sciences, Discipline of Biokinetics, Exercise and Leisure 
Sciences, University of KwaZulu-Natal, Durban, South Africa.

BACKGROUND: Sleep is essential for athlete recovery and performance, yet 
athletes frequently experience restricted or poor-quality sleep. Pre-sleep 
feeding (PSF) has emerged as a strategy to support recovery, but randomized, 
double-blinded, crossover trials comparing PSF macronutrient options on 
objective and subjective sleep outcomes in elite female athletes remain limited.
METHODS: Twenty-five National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I 
female athletes (18-25 years old) were recruited; 21 completed the trial. In a 
randomized, double-blinded, placebo controlled, crossover design conducted over 
4-8 weeks, participants consumed four treatments for three consecutive nights 
each: 40 g casein protein (CAS; 160 kcal), 40 g α-lactalbumin protein (ALA; 
160 kcal), 40 g carbohydrate (CHO; 160 kcal), and 40g of a placebo (PLA; 
5 kcal), with a minimum three-day washout between conditions. Supplements were 
consumed ~2 h after the final meal and ~30 min before bedtime as the last 
caloric intake of the day. Objective outcomes were obtained from the WHOOP 4.0 
device (total sleep time (TST), sleep onset latency (SOL), sleep efficiency 
(SE), resting heart rate (RHR), and heart rate variability (HRV)). Subjective

Nocturnal interstitial glucose was assessed via blinded continuous glucose 
monitoring (CGM) in a subset (n = 6). Sleep and recovery variables were analyzed 
using one-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) to evaluate 
treatment effects across the four supplementation conditions. For CGM data, a 
two-way repeated-measures ANOVA was used to evaluate main effects of treatment 
and time, as well as the treatment × time interaction. Tukey's post hoc testing 
was used with significance set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: No significant treatment effects were observed for TST, SOL, SE, RHR, 
or HRV (p > 0.05). TST ranged from 7.47-7.62 h, SE from 91.5-92.0%, RHR from 
53.5-54.1 bpm, and HRV from 98.2-103.9 ms across conditions. No significant 
treatment effects were detected for SSQ, SSOL, or SREC (p > 0.05); SSQ ranged 
from 69-75%, SSOL from 16-20 min, and SREC from 61-66%. In the CGM sub-analysis, 
a main effect of time was observed for nocturnal glucose (p = 0.008), but no 
differences among treatments (p = 0.187) or a time × treatment interaction 
(p = 0.550) were detected.
CONCLUSIONS: In NCAA Division I female athletes, three consecutive nights of 
pre-sleep ingestion of CAS, ALA, or CHO did not impair objective or subjective 
measures of sleep or recovery compared with PLA. These findings demonstrate that 
pre-sleep feeding, regardless of macronutrient type, can be incorporated without 
negatively affecting sleep quality or recovery metrics.

child or young person’s mealtime quality of life.Allied health professionals

Altermagnetism has emerged as a third fundamental magnetic phase, uniquely 
combining the zero net magnetization and ultrafast dynamics of antiferromagnets 
with spin splitting typically reserved for ferromagnets(FMs). This review 
provides a systematic overview of the burgeoning field of altermagnets(AMs) and

and opportunities for this new paradigm of energy-efficient spintronics.

Precision Thyroid Oncology Using Genetic-Based Therapies: A Narrative Review.

Marotta V(1), Xing M(2), Vitale M(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Medicine, Surgery and Dentistry, "Scuola Medica Salernitana", 
University of Salerno, Baronissi, Italy.
(2)School of Medicine, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, 
Guangdong, China.

BACKGROUND: Most thyroid malignancies harbor a limited set of well-characterized 
mutations driving tumor initiation and determining phenotype. This relatively 
direct genotype-phenotype association, bringing insights into molecular 
mechanisms of progression and drug resistance, makes advanced thyroid cancers 
suitable for genetic-based therapies. Personalized cancer treatment by targeting 
actionable tumor mutations represents one of the most innovative frontiers in 
oncology.
SUMMARY: The present narrative review focuses on actionable mutations occurring 
in thyroid cancers and provides a state-of-the-art overview of genetic-based 
treatments that have received regulatory approval worldwide. These include two 
selective RET inhibitors (sRET-Is) (selpercatinib and pralsetinib), three NTRK 
inhibitors (NTRK-Is) (larotrectinib, entrectinib, and repotrectinib), and two 
dual BRAF/MEK inhibitor regimens (dabrafenib plus trametinib and encorafenib 
plus binimetinib). The most significant impact has been observed in the 
management of RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer. Selpercatinib, available in 
many countries, demonstrated superiority over standard multikinase inhibitors 
(MKIs) in a head-to-head comparison. It currently represents the best first-line 
treatment option. In BRAFV600E-positive anaplastic thyroid cancer, both 
dabrafenib plus trametinib and encorafenib plus binimetinib showed efficacy that 
appeared to exceed that historically observed with standard approaches. However, 
their approval is currently limited to a few countries. In 
radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), sRET-Is and NTRK-Is 
are effective in molecularly selected patients and are approved in many 
countries. However, their applicability is limited by the low prevalence of the 
corresponding actionable alterations. In BRAFV600E-positive 
radioiodine-refractory DTC, dabrafenib plus trametinib has emerged as a useful 
option after MKI failure, although a tumor-specific approval has been granted 
only in Europe.
CONCLUSIONS: Precision oncology is increasingly being integrated into the 
management of advanced thyroid cancer. However, its impact varies widely across 
different tumor settings, and its real-world use is strongly influenced by 
country-specific drug regulations.

BACKGROUND: A body of research has shown that deceptively administering a 
placebo described as caffeine can significantly improve sport performance. We 
aimed to synthesize and estimate the effect size of the deceptive administration 
of a placebo described as caffeine on sport performance outcomes (e.g. bench 
press, cycling time-trial, repeated sprint).
METHODS: We searched for studies sampling healthy adults from database creation 
to July 2026. The standardized mean difference (d) between placebo caffeine and 
baseline was calculated and Cochrane's risk of bias assessment was used.
RESULTS: Seventeen studies were included. Nine studies were judged to be of 
high-risk of bias and eight unclear. Random-effect models revealed a 
small-to-moderate effect of placebo caffeine benefiting performance (d = 0.49, 
95% CI = 0.28 to 0.69) and meta-regressions indicated that pooled effects were 
more likely to be greater when researchers were blinded (b = 0.52 ± 0.24, 95% 
CI = 0.01 to 0.99) and in studies sampling more males (b = -0.93 ± 0.38, 95% 
CI = -1.68 to -0.19).
DISCUSSION: Data highlight that placebo effects of caffeine can significantly 
affect sport performance with a pooled effect estimate suggesting a 
small-to-moderate effect. However, as per the GRADE assessment, the overall 
quality of evidence was low. As such, given the high risk of bias across all 
studies and the variation in confidence interval, stronger research designs are 
needed to examine placebo effects of caffeine, whereby researchers are blinded 
to treatment administration and allocation concealment. No funding was received 
for the review and the protocol can be found here: doi: 10.17605/OSF.IO/W8KY6.

Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) is a prototypical transition metal dichalcogenide 
semiconductor with excellent optical and electrical properties. In this study, 
the irradiation behavior of monolayer and multilayer MoS2was compared under 
irradiation with 2 MeV protons at 300 K, at fluences of 1 × 1014,1 × 1015, and 5

provide insights into the irradiation behavior of MoS2and its layer-dependent 
property modifications.

Borophene is a compelling 2D material known for its considerable structural 
diversity, and its lack of a band gap can be overcome by synthesis of 
hydrogenated borophene, also known as borophane. However, with the realization 
of semiconductor borophane polymorphs, understanding the mechanisms controlling 
their band gaps is fundamental, particularly in vertically stacked 
architectures, where the role of interlayer coupling must be fully elucidated.

material. These findings establish a fundamental framework for band gap 
engineering in borophene-based architectures, paving the way for their 
integration into next-generation nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices.

typically guided by pharmacodynamic responses rather than direct measurement of 
concentrations. This limitation largely arises from traditional monitoring 
procedures that rely on repeated venous sampling followed by laboratory analyses 
using cumbersome and costly instrumentation, often returning results hours or 
days later. Access to a bedside platform capable of real-time drug monitoring 
would represent a major advance toward personalized dosing, particularly for 
drugs exhibiting rapid pharmacokinetics (t1/2 < 4 h). Here, we present 
PK-Tracker, a bedside device that enables real-time point-of-care monitoring of 
therapeutic drugs. We demonstrate its in vivo applicability for monitoring the 
curare rocuronium, a nondepolarizing neuromuscular blocker widely used for 
surgical procedures. Using a newly developed aptamer sensor, PK-Tracker provides 
time-resolved measurements every 10 s, allowing high-precision pharmacokinetic 
profiling. We also demonstrate PK-Tracker's versatility through the continuous 
in vivo monitoring of the antibiotic vancomycin, highlighting the platform's 
generalizability across clinically relevant pharmacological classes for broad 
therapeutic drug monitoring. Together, these results establish PK-Tracker as a 
promising bedside technology for real-time drug monitoring of short half-life 
drugs, enabling precision dosing toward improved perioperative patient care.

Clinical and Research Trends in Adult Acupressure Randomized Controlled Trials: 
A Scoping and Bibliometric Review.

Wilandika A(1), Sari DNI(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Nursing, Universitas 'Aisyiyah Bandung, Bandung, Indonesia.
(2)Department of Public Health, Universitas 'Aisyiyah Bandung, Bandung, 
Indonesia.

INTRODUCTION: Acupressure has gained increasing attention as a noninvasive, 
low-risk, and cost-effective complementary intervention to address persistent 
symptoms such as pain, anxiety, fatigue, and sleep disturbances among adults. 
Although the volume of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating 
acupressure has grown substantially, an integrated synthesis that combines 
clinical evidence mapping with bibliometric characterization remains limited. 
This study aimed to conduct an integrated scoping review and bibliometric 
analysis of RCTs on acupressure interventions among adults in order to map the 
scope of clinical evidence and identify publication trends, thematic 
concentrations, and research collaboration patterns.
METHOD: This integrated scoping review was reported in accordance with the 
Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 
Extension for Scoping Reviews reporting guideline. RCTs published between 2020 
and 2025 were retrieved from the Scopus database using 
Population-Concept-Context (PCC) eligibility criteria. The included studies 
involved adults aged 18 years or older who received acupressure interventions in 
clinical or health care settings. Data extraction captured both clinical 
characteristics and bibliometric indicators. Descriptive synthesis was 
integrated with bibliometric analyses of annual publication trends, subject 
areas, geographic distribution, author productivity, collaboration networks, and 
keyword co-occurrence.
RESULTS: A total of 303 RCTs were included. Publication output increased 
steadily, with a notable surge after 2022. Most studies were indexed within 
Medicine and Nursing. China, Iran, and the United States were the most 
productive countries, while international collaboration remained limited. 
Thematic analysis revealed that pain and musculoskeletal conditions were the 
dominant focuses, closely linked to quality-of-life outcomes. Psychological 
symptoms and sleep disturbances formed a strongly interconnected cluster, 
alongside emerging applications in women's health and chronic disease 
management.
CONCLUSION: The evidence base for adult acupressure has expanded rapidly and 
demonstrates increasing thematic coherence. Future research should prioritize 
broader collaboration, diversified clinical applications, and 
implementation-oriented studies to enhance the translation of findings into 
practice.

Boosting Male Participation in Research: Exploring Motivation, Engagement, and 
Retention Efforts.

Papajorgji-Taylor D(1), Muessig KR(1), Francisco M(1), Schmidt MA(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Kaiser Permanente Center for Health Research, Portland, OR, USA.
(2)Kaiser Permanente Bernard J Tyson School of Medicine, Pasadena, CA, USA.

INTRODUCTION: Males are persistently underrepresented in longitudinal health 
research, yet effective strategies to improve their recruitment and retention 
remain limited. This study examined motivational factors, engagement strategies, 
and retention approaches among males in the context of the Connect for Cancer 
Prevention Study (Connect), a large National Cancer Institute-sponsored 
longitudinal observational study.
METHODS: The authors conducted a qualitative study using individual and group 
interviews with 2 cohorts of Kaiser Permanente Northwest male members: enrolled 
Connect participants (n = 22) and Connect-eligible members who had not enrolled 
(n = 13). Interviews explored motivations for participation, barriers to 
engagement, and retention strategies. Transcripts were analyzed using thematic 
analysis with NVivo software.
RESULTS: Distinct motivational profiles emerged across cohorts. Enrolled 
participants were primarily driven by altruism, family cancer history, and civic 
responsibility, while Connect-eligible participants approached participation 
transactionally, prioritizing financial incentives, convenience, and minimal 
disruption to daily routines. Across both groups, key facilitators included 
institutional trust, practitioner endorsement, and low-burden participation 
mechanisms. Retention was linked to consistent communication, visible study 
progress, and a sense of community.
DISCUSSION: Recruitment and retention require distinct but complementary 
strategies. Initial enrollment is best supported by addressing practical 
barriers and communicating tangible benefits, while long-term retention depends 
on fostering connection and demonstrating impact. These findings offer 
actionable, gender-sensitive guidance for improving participation among males in 
longitudinal health research.
CONCLUSION: Gender-sensitive, equity-informed approaches are essential for 
engaging males, particularly those from underrepresented groups, in longitudinal 
research. Strategies addressing masculinity norms, socioeconomic context, and 
institutional trust will strengthen the diversity and generalizability of 
observational study findings.

PURPOSE: Healthcare planning and resource allocation require accurate estimates 
of the burden of motor neuron diseases (MNDs). This study evaluated the global 
impact of MNDs from 1990 to 2021 as part of the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 
Study 2021.
METHODS: GBD 2021 data were used to assess the global burden of MNDs from 1990 
to 2021 in terms of prevalence, incidence, disability-adjusted life years 
(DALYs), and deaths. The relationship between MND burden and the 
Socio-demographic Index (SDI) was also examined.
RESULTS: Globally, MNDs accounted for 272,732 prevalent cases (95% uncertainty 
interval [UI], 236,195-313,676), 64,178 incident cases (95% UI, 58,506-70,270),

35,757-42,433) in 2021. The corresponding age-standardized rates per 100,000

numbers of prevalent and incident cases increased, but their age-standardized

age-standardized mortality rate increased by 19.84%. MND burden was generally 
higher in regions with a high SDI, although rates in high-income Asia Pacific 
were relatively low compared with those in regions with similar SDI values.

age-standardized prevalence and incidence rates declined slightly, and 
mortality-related burden increased. These trends underscore the need for 
evidence-based national and global healthcare planning. Geographic variation in 
MND burden may reflect regional differences in the roles of sociodemographic and 
genetic factors.

Psoas-lumbar vertebral index and short-term pain relief after pulsed 
radiofrequency treatment of the dorsal root ganglion in postherpetic neuralgia 
in Korea: a retrospective pilot study.

Yoo SH(#)(1), Cho E(#)(1), Kim WJ(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine, Ewha Womans University 
Mokdong Hospital, Ewha Womans University College of Medicine, Seoul, Korea.
(2)Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine, Ewha Womans University 
Mokdong Hospital, Ewha Womans University College of Medicine, Seoul, Korea. 
ickypoo@ewha.ac.kr.
(#)Contributed equally

PURPOSE: The psoas-lumbar vertebral index (PLVI), a marker of central sarcopenia 
measured using computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), has 
been linked to the development of postherpetic neuralgia (PHN). Whether PLVI 
predicts short-term pain relief after pulsed radiofrequency (pRF) treatment of 
the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) in established PHN remains unknown. This pilot

scale (NRS) pain scores 1 month after pRF.

reduction.

reduction rate of 29.3%±34.0%. PLVI was not significantly correlated with the

group comparison was not significant (Welch P=0.051) and 15 variables were 
tested without correction for multiple comparisons.
CONCLUSION: This pilot cohort showed no detectable association between PLVI and 
short-term pain relief after pRF; its small size precludes establishing the 
absence of an association. The exploratory sex difference warrants investigation

TAOK1 Protects against Renal Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Aged Mice through 
the STK3/BNIP3 Mitophagy Pathway.

Li Z(1), Chen H(1), Xia C(1), Hu S(1), Ye L(1), Fu L(1), Ye Q(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Nephrology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang Chinese 
Medical University (Zhejiang Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine), Hangzhou, 
China.

The elderly suffer from a higher incidence and greater severity of acute kidney 
injury (AKI), yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. 
This study dissects the possible role of thousand and one amino acid protein 
kinase 1 (TAOK1) in age-related AKI, specifically examining its regulation of 
mitophagy. Aged (23~24 months) C57BL/6 mice were subjected to renal 
ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and TAOK1 was overexpressed in these mice.

(NET) formation, and fibrosis were assessed. The involvement of the STK3/BNIP3

by increased expressions of key mitophagy-related proteins. Conversely, Taok1 
knockdown in aged mouse renal tubular cells exacerbated H/R-induced cell injury 
and apoptosis, and suppressed the STK3/BNIP3 pathway and mitophagy. Our findings 
demonstrate that TAOK1 protects against renal IRI in aged mice by promoting 
mitophagy through the STK3/BNIP3 axis. The age-related decline in TAOK1 may 
contribute to the heightened susceptibility to AKI, positioning TAOK1 as a 
potential therapeutic target for mitigating AKI in the aging population.

Development and temporal validation of a simple CT-based body surface landmark

Kida T(1), Sumitomo M.

Author information:
(1)From the Departments of Anaestheesiology, Yokosuka Kyosai Hospital, Yokosuka,

BACKGROUND: Accurate positioning of central venous catheter (CVC) tips is 
essential to avoid complications, yet consistent appropriate placement within 
the superior vena cava remains challenging without a simple method for depth 
adjustment.
OBJECTIVES: To develop and temporally validate a simple computed 
tomography-based (CT-based) body surface landmark approach for estimating 
optimal insertion depth (OID) and to assess its impact on appropriate catheter 
tip positioning.
DESIGN: Single-centre prospective observational cohort study.
SETTING: Tertiary care hospital in Japan; February 2017 to June 2019.
PATIENTS: Adult patients undergoing surgery requiring CVC placement via the 
right internal jugular vein with preoperative chest CT. After exclusions, 86 
patients were included in the derivation cohort and 100 in the validation 
cohort.
INTERVENTION: In the derivation cohort, insertion depth was determined by the 
attending anaesthesiologist; in the validation cohort, it was determined using a 
model derived from the derivation cohort.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: The primary outcome was the proportion of appropriately 
placed catheter tips.
RESULTS: The final model retained the insertion point-to-body surface landmark 
distance (ILD), defined using a body surface landmark corresponding to the

associated with increased likelihood of appropriate positioning (adjusted odds 
ratio 4.68 (95% CI, 1.97 to 12.27)). Model performance showed good calibration 
and moderate explanatory ability (R2 approximately 50%) in both cohorts.
CONSLUSIONS: A CT-based body surface landmark approach was associated with 
improved consistency of appropriate CVC tip placement and enables 
patient-specific estimation of insertion depth.

Artificial intelligence in personalized internal dosimetry for 
radiopharmaceutical therapy: a narrative mini-review.

Jowhari MA(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Radiological Sciences, College of Applied Medical Sciences.
(2)Health Research Center, Najran University, Najran, Saudi Arabia.

Personalized internal radiation dosimetry supports individualized 
radiopharmaceutical therapy but remains difficult to implement because workflows 
require repeated quantitative imaging, segmentation, registration, kinetic 
modeling, and absorbed-dose calculation. This mini-review summarizes current 
evidence on artificial intelligence across the personalized dosimetry workflow 
and considers clinical readiness. A narrative PubMed search was completed in 
early 2026 and covered peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to early 2026. 
Studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning 
in quantitative image reconstruction, segmentation, registration, time-activity 
curve estimation, absorbed-dose calculation, or clinical decision support were 
considered. Studies reporting quantitative performance or validation results 
were prioritized. Deep learning reduced yttrium-90 single-photon emission 
computed tomography reconstruction error from 149.5% ± 31.2% to 9.2% ± 1.7%; 
lesion dose-rate error was 8.6% ± 5.7% in virtual-patient testing. 
Learning-based registration reduced computation time from about 50 s to under 
6 s. Single-time-point approaches can simplify imaging, and recent machine 
learning work has explored prediction of organ effective half-life. Automated 
segmentation methods show improving reproducibility, whereas evidence for 
artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support remains mainly 
retrospective and single-center. Artificial intelligence applications in 
reconstruction and segmentation appear closer to clinical readiness, while 
decision-support applications still require prospective, multicenter validation.

BACKGROUND The use of ex vivo liver resection and autologous liver

Interfacial Regulation via Organic-Inorganic Interpenetrating Networks for 
Enhanced Protection in Waterborne Polyurethane Nanocomposites.

Wang S(1)(2), Ji M(1)(2), Zhang Y(1)(2), Song X(1)(2), Li J(1)(2), Li J(1)(2), 
Man J(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Key Laboratory of High Efficiency and Clean Mechanical Manufacture (Ministry 
of Education), School of Mechanical Engineering, Shandong University, Jinan, 
Shandong250061, China.
(2)National Demonstration Center for Experimental Mechanical Engineering 
Education, Shandong University, Jinan250061, China.

The abundance of hydrophilic groups and the linear polymer chain structure in 
waterborne polyurethane (WPU) lead to insufficient water resistance and 
corrosion protection. These inherent characteristics make it challenging for WPU 
to be applied in the marine protection field, where high comprehensive 
performance of coatings is demanded. Herein, a WPU nanocomposite was designed 
incorporating hydroxyl-terminated polydimethylsiloxane and bifunctionalized 
nano-silica (modified with 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane and 
propyltrimethoxysilane) during prepolymerization. This strategy established an 
organic-inorganic interpenetrating cross-linked network through covalent bonding 
and intermolecular interactions. The silica nanoparticles act as interfacial 
bridges between polymer segments, mitigating phase separation and agglomeration 
caused by polarity mismatch, thereby enhancing coating compactness and improving 
stress transfer. Performance tests demonstrate that the properties of the 
coating have been comprehensively enhanced. The coating exhibits an elongation 
at break of 254.64% while maintaining a tensile strength of 21.17 MPa. 
Additionally, the water absorption rate of the coating decreases to 
approximately 5%, the electrochemical protection efficiency reaches 99.9920%, 
and no obvious corrosion phenomenon is observed after a 7 day salt spray 
corrosion test. Additionally, the coating shows excellent drag-reduction 
performance, with a drag-reduction rate of 6.56% under turbulent flow. By 
integrating interfacial design with nanocomposite architecture, this work 
develops a robust WPU coating system suitable for marine engineering 
applications, and employs molecular dynamics simulations to reveal the 
microscopic mechanism by which amino and n-propyl silane dual modification 
inhibits the aggregation of silica nanoparticles as well as the interfacial 
interaction mechanism, thereby highlighting the role of colloidal and 
nanomaterial strategies in advancing functional protective coatings.

BACKGROUND/AIMS: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography with stone 
extraction is the standard treatment for common bile duct (CBD) stones. However,

pilot trial to explore the potential effect of a terpene preparation in this 
setting.
METHODS: Thirty patients who had undergone endoscopic management of CBD stones

be drawn. The primary contribution is to inform the feasibility and design of a 
confirmatory trial. (cris.nih.go.kr, KCT0002289).

Triangle (PAT) was recorded at arrival. Multivariable logistic regression was 
used to identify factors associated with severe clinical outcomes and mortality. 
Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating 
characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: We included 412 critically ill children; 63 (15.3%) had severe clinical 
outcomes, and 12 (2.9%) died. Abnormal circulation and appearance when 
evaluating the PAT and abnormal systolic blood pressure were independently 
associated with severe clinical outcomes (AUC: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.68-0.82). Prior 
pediatric intensive care unit admission and abnormal appearance and abnormal 
circulation when evaluating the PAT were independently associated with mortality 
(AUC: 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.95).
CONCLUSIONS: Structured bedside assessment at ED presentation may provide 
clinically meaningful prognostic insight, supporting earlier prioritization and 
escalation of care for critically ill children, pending external validation.

Social Isolation and Loneliness Across the Cardiovascular Disease Spectrum: A 
Narrative Review of Evidence, Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications.

Kaushik S(1), Naeem IA(2), Nandyal S(3), Gajjar R(3), Nubla A(3), Tasamma AT(3), 
Imran A(4), Salama B(2), Frishman WH(2), Aronow WS(2).

Author information:
(1)From the Department of Medicine, Jacobi Medical Center/Albert Einstein 
College of Medicine, Bronx, NY.
(2)Departments of Medicine, Westchester Medical Center and New York Medical 
College, Valhalla, NY.
(3)Department of Medicine, John H. Stroger Jr. Hospital of Cook County, Chicago, 
IL.
(4)Department of Medicine, CMH Lahore Medical College & Institute of Dentistry, 
Lahore, Pakistan.

Social isolation is the objective paucity of social ties; loneliness is the 
subjective distress of relationships falling short of what one desires. Both are 
common, affecting roughly a quarter to a third of older adults, and both have 
cardiovascular consequences through several mechanisms, with some estimates 
suggesting an increase of 29% in coronary heart disease risk and 21-23% in heart 
failure hospitalization. We review the evidence for social isolation and 
loneliness' impact on cardiovascular disease separately for ischemic heart 
disease, heart failure, arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death, and stress- and 
substance-related cardiomyopathies. We also highlight plausible mechanisms by 
which social isolation and loneliness are linked to downstream adverse 
cardiovascular events, limitations with existing evidence, societal guidance, 
and policy frameworks currently aimed at addressing them. The evidence is 
densest for ischemic heart disease, though the largest cohort shows a 43% excess 
risk of myocardial infarction attenuating by approximately 84% to 
nonsignificance after full adjustment, and Mendelian randomization estimates a 
far smaller effect. The prognostic signal is more consistent than the etiologic 
one, with low functional social support carrying a pooled hazard ratio of 1.59 
in established coronary disease. In heart failure, objective isolation rather 
than loneliness predicts post-diagnosis mortality, mainly in women, consistent 
with a self-care-dependent behavioral pathway.

Safety.

Grewal P(1), Seidman MB(2), Chasen J(3), Lench D(1), Dickens I(3), Brennan 
EA(4), Rodriguez-Porcel F(1), Kindred J(5), George MS(3)(5), Kautz S(6),

Author information:
(1)Department of Neurology, Medical University of South Carolina, Charleston.
(2)Department of Neurology, University of Colorado, Aurora.
(3)Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences, Medical University of South 
Carolina, Charleston.
(4)Medical University of South Carolina Libraries, Medical University of South 
Carolina, Charleston.
(5)Research Service, Ralph H. Johnson VA Health Care System, Charleston, SC.
(6)College of Health Professions, Medical University of South Carolina, 
Charleston.

OBJECTIVE: Apathy is a neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by impairment of 
goal-directed behavior, cognition, and emotional responsiveness. In this scoping 
review, the authors evaluated the literature on brain stimulation for the 
treatment of patients with apathy across diagnostic categories and provide 
recommendations to guide future research and practice.
METHODS: The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, and PsycInfo for studies involving 
brain stimulation for apathy as a primary or secondary outcome.
RESULTS: From 1,209 records, 52 studies evaluating brain stimulation were 
included; of these, 10 systematic reviews or meta-analyses were synthesized 
separately. Modalities included repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation 
(rTMS; N=26), deep brain stimulation (DBS; N=7), transcranial direct current 
stimulation (tDCS; N=6), electroconvulsive therapy (N=1), transcranial 
alternating current stimulation (N=1), and transcranial pulsating 
electromagnetic field therapy (N=1). Populations included patients with 
schizophrenia (N=477), Parkinson's disease (PD; N=289), depression (N=288), 
Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) (N=210),

stroke (N=14), COVID-19 (N=12), and dementia with Lewy bodies (N=6) (total 
N=1,366). rTMS improved apathy measures, most consistently in AD, with positive 
trends in depression, MCI, stroke, and schizophrenia. tDCS showed variable 
effects, with some benefits for schizophrenia. DBS showed mixed results, varying 
with stimulation location. Observed adverse events were mild and modality 
specific.
CONCLUSIONS: Investigations into brain stimulation as a treatment for apathy 
show some promise. Conclusions were limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous 
study designs, and variable outcome measures. Randomized trials with common 
validated apathy instruments, standardized stimulation parameters, and 
harmonized diagnostic measures may help advance the field.

Shahzad M(1), Siddiqui S, Premji R, Liu JJ, He Y, Mencia Ledo J, Nandan S, Dos

Author information:
(1)Author Affiliations: Rehabilitation Sciences Institute (Shahzad, Tam-Seto, 
and Nowrouzi-Kia), Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto, Toronto,

BACKGROUND: Public safety personnel (PSP) face a heightened risk of traumatic 
brain injury (TBI) and barriers in resuming daily activities and returning to 
work (RTW). Despite these risks, evidence on interventions targeting functional 
recovery and participation in this population is scarce.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize evidence on interventions targeting functional recovery 
and RTW in PSP with TBI.
DESIGN: MEDLINE, CINAHL, EMBASE, PsycINFO, and Scopus on January 23, 2026. 
Eligible studies included PSP with TBI such as armed forces and/or military 
personnel and law enforcement personnel. Randomized controlled trials,

certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.

Individualized Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for 
Acute Coronary Syndrome: Current SAPT Strategies and the Potential Role of 
Indobufen.

Chai J(1), Li X, Liu Q, Li Y, Jian J, Cheng Y.

Author information:
(1)From the Department of Cardiology, Shandong Medical and Pharmaceutical 
University Hospital, Binzhou, China.

Acute coronary syndrome requires effective antiplatelet therapy after 
percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), while contemporary patients often 
present with overlapping ischemic and bleeding risks. This clinical complexity 
has shifted post-PCI management from fixed-duration dual antiplatelet therapy 
(DAPT) toward individualized strategies based on DAPT duration, single 
antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) selection, and aspirin withdrawal. Aspirin is 
traditionally the default maintenance agent after DAPT, although long-term 
aspirin use is limited by gastrointestinal intolerance, mucosal injury, and 
bleeding risk. P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy represents an important aspirin-free 
strategy, with clinical application influenced by drug potency, genetic 
variability, tolerability, cost, and adherence. Indobufen, a reversible 
cyclooxygenase-targeting antiplatelet agent, has reemerged as a potential 
aspirin alternative by suppressing thromboxane A2 generation through a mechanism 
distinct from that of aspirin. Current evidence suggests that indobufen-based 
DAPT may provide comparable ischemic protection with fewer bleeding or 
gastrointestinal adverse events in selected PCI patients, particularly those 
with aspirin intolerance, gastrointestinal vulnerability, or high bleeding risk. 
These patients often present with multiple high-risk features that 
simultaneously elevate both ischemic and bleeding risks, underscoring the need 
for careful risk stratification. Most available studies have evaluated indobufen 
as an aspirin substitute within DAPT rather than as SAPT after DAPT 
discontinuation. From a pharmacoeconomic perspective, indobufen is more 
expensive than aspirin, although this must be weighed against potential benefits 
in bleeding reduction. Future randomized trials are needed to define the optimal 
DAPT-to-SAPT strategy and clarify the clinical position of indobufen in acute 
coronary syndrome-PCI.

Effects, and Implications for Cardiovascular Practice.

Arslan FS(1), Ahmad R, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.

Author information:
(1)From the Department of Medicine, Westchester Medical Center and New York

Obstructive sleep apnea affects approximately one billion adults worldwide and 
is associated with hypertension, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and stroke. 
Obesity is its dominant reversible cause, yet positive airway pressure therapy 
splints the pharyngeal airway without addressing the adiposity that narrows it,

fat. We then review the SURMOUNT-OSA program: two parallel 52-week, 
double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials enrolling 469 adults with 
obesity and an apnea-hypopnea index of at least 15 events per hour, one 
conducted without positive airway pressure and one during established positive 
airway pressure use. Tirzepatide reduced the apnea-hypopnea index by an 
estimated 20.0 and 23.8 events per hour relative to placebo, with concurrent 
reductions in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, systolic blood 
pressure, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein.

Traumatic Brain Injury in First Responders: From Hidden Burden to Occupational 
Health Action.

Caccese JB(1), Williams WH, Smith N.

Author information:
(1)Author Affiliations: School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences, College of 
Medicine, The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, Columbus, Ohio 
(Caccese); and School of Psychology, Faculty of Health and Life Sciences, Exeter 
University, United Kingdom (Smith and Williams).

Traumatic brain injury (TBI), including concussion, is an important but often 
underrecognized occupational injury among first responders. Despite frequent 
exposure to circumstances that increase the risk of TBI, law enforcement 
officers, firefighters, and emergency medical services personnel often lack 
consistent pathways for injury recognition, reporting, clinical assessment, 
rehabilitation, and safe return to duty. This topical issue of the Journal of 
Head Trauma Rehabilitation brings together emerging evidence on TBI prevalence, 
underrecognition, mental health, functional recovery, and occupational 
reintegration in first responder populations. Collectively, the articles 
demonstrate a substantial burden of TBI, persistent gaps in diagnosis and 
treatment, and the complex relationships among TBI history, psychological 
health, and occupational functioning. They also highlight the limited evidence 
available to guide rehabilitation and determine readiness to resume 
safety-sensitive duties. A multidisciplinary consensus statement included in 
this issue offers 28 recommendations addressing recognition and reporting, early 
assessment, return to duty, mental health, prevention, and organizational 
policies. Although first responder-specific evidence remains limited, these 
recommendations provide a practical framework for improving care while 
identifying priorities for future research. Advancing TBI care in first 
responders will require coordinated efforts among healthcare professionals, 
first responder organizations, researchers, and policymakers to establish 
supportive reporting systems, improve access to appropriate care, and develop 
and evaluate occupation-specific return-to-duty pathways. Addressing TBI in 
first responders requires moving beyond individual injury management toward a 
coordinated occupational health approach that protects first responders and the 
communities they serve.

From Physiological to Potential Cardiovascular Maladaptation in Endurance 
Exercise: Current Evidence, Pathophysiology, and Clinical Implications.

Luvianto J(1), Suastika LOS(2).

Author information:
(1)From the Faculty of Medicine, Udayana University, Denpasar, Bali, Indonesia.
(2)Department of Cardiology and Vascular Medicine, Faculty of Medicine, Udayana 
University, Denpasar, Bali, Indonesia.

Emerging evidence suggests that the cardiovascular benefits of exercise may not 
increase indefinitely with training volume and intensity. As participation in 
ultraendurance sports continues to rise, concerns have been raised regarding the 
potential adverse cardiovascular effects of exposure to extreme or 
ultraendurance exercise. In this Review, we synthesize the current evidence and 
the pathophysiology regarding the structural, functional, and electrical 
cardiovascular maladaptations to endurance exercise and highlight the clinical 
implications of these changes. Several evidences demonstrate that extreme 
exertion can induce transient cardiac dysfunction; when sustained over years, it 
may contribute to myocardial fibrosis and associated arrhythmic events. 
Endurance athletes frequently exhibit a higher prevalence of coronary artery 
calcification, atherosclerotic plaque burden, and increased arterial stiffness. 
The alteration driven by long-term endurance training is also strongly 
implicated in the higher incidence of atrial fibrillation. Although definitive 
long-term outcomes remain debated, the assumption that limitless exercise yields 
exclusively protective cardiovascular effects might no longer seem prudent. 
While regular exercise is unequivocally cardioprotective, extreme endurance 
training may cross a threshold from physiological adaptation to potential 
maladaptation. Understanding the pathophysiological mechanisms of 
exercise-induced cardiac remodeling is critical to optimize the benefit of 
exercise and the potential risk associated with exercise.

OBJECTIVE: Examine the association between neighborhood characteristics and 
parent-reported lifetime concussion history.
SETTING: National Survey of Children's Health, a nationally representative 
survey of parents of children ages 0-17 years in the United States.
PARTICIPANTS: Parent/guardian(s) (hereafter: parents) with children ages 0-17 
years.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional.
MAIN MEASURES: Neighborhood disorder was assessed via items asking whether the 
child's neighborhood had (1) sidewalks or walking paths, (2) a park or

library or bookmobile, (5) litter or garbage on the streets or sidewalks, (6)

response to a single question.

Cell-Based Inflammatory Indices for Risk Stratification in Acute Myocardial 
Infarction: Current Evidence and Future Perspectives.

Payami B(1), Mousaeinejad N(2), Borghei A(3), Baharvand F(4), Borghei Y(4).

Author information:
(1)From the Faculty of Medicine, Cardiology Department, Ahvaz Jundishapur 
University of Medical Sciences, Ahvaz, Iran.
(2)Emergency Medicine Management Research Center, Health Management Research 
Institute, Iran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran.
(3)Medical School, Kurdistan University of Medical Sciences, Sanandaj, Iran.
(4)Cardiovascular Diseases Research Center, Department of Cardiology, Heshmat 
Hospital, School of Medicine, Guilan University of Medical Sciences, Rasht, 
Iran.

Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains a leading cause of cardiovascular 
morbidity and mortality worldwide, despite substantial advances in reperfusion 
strategies and guideline-directed therapies. Increasing evidence highlights the 
pivotal role of inflammation. Therefore, identifying reliable and accessible 
inflammatory biomarkers may provide valuable prognostic information for patients 
with AMI. Cell-based inflammatory indices derived from routine complete blood 
count parameters have emerged as promising biomarkers due to their simplicity, 
low cost, and widespread availability. Unlike single inflammatory markers, these 
indices reflect the complex interactions among different immune cell populations 
involved in cardiovascular inflammation. Recent studies have demonstrated 
associations between elevated cell-based inflammatory indices and adverse 
outcomes following AMI. Inflammation represents a central mechanism linking 
coronary plaque instability, myocardial injury, and adverse outcomes after AMI. 
Cell-based inflammatory indices provide a practical and cost-effective approach 
for evaluating systemic inflammatory activity and may improve prognostic 
assessment in patients with AMI. Further prospective studies are required to 
determine their optimal clinical application, standardized cutoff values, and 
integration into routine cardiovascular risk models.

The promotion of brain health has generally been undertaken at the level of 
individuals, for instance, in the quest for precision treatments for persons 
with, or at high risk of, neurological disorders. But the growing global burden 
of neurological conditions and the increasing understanding of the brain's 
central role in all facets of human life have spurred interest in public health 
approaches to the brain that emphasise population-level strategies benefitting 
everyone as part of a "brain health for all" vision of society. This article 
defines the emerging concept of public brain health as intersectoral action to 
establish brain health priorities, empower communities, and reduce health 
inequities, with the ultimate goal of improving brain health at the population 
level across the lifetime. We propose a framework to promote and safeguard 
population brain health with the following key elements: co-defining priorities 
with communities, balancing prevention strategies, and reducing global gaps in 
brain health through ambitious policy-making. Public brain health calls for 
collective responsibility to maximise brain health equity across the life 
course.

Undertreatment of Wernicke encephalopathy in alcohol-related clinical contexts: 
a scoping review of diagnosis, thiamine regimens, and clinical management.

Goldani AAS(1)(2), Feitosa G(3), Colchete EV(4), Falleiro CF(4), Pedro CW(4), 
Kessler FHP(4)(5), Fidalgo TM(3), von Diemen L(4)(5).

Author information:
(1)Centro de Pesquisa em Álcool e Drogas (CPAD), Hospital de Clínicas de Porto 
Alegre (HCPA), Av. Protásio Alves, 211 - Bloco C - Santa Cecília, Porto 
Alegre-RS, 90035-903, Brazil. agoldani@hcpa.edu.br.
(2)Departamento de Psiquiatria e Medicina Legal, Universidade Federal do Rio 
Grande do Sul, Porto Alegre, Brazil. agoldani@hcpa.edu.br.
(3)Departamento de Psiquiatria, Universidade Federal de São Paulo (UNIFESP), São 
Paulo, Brazil.
(4)Centro de Pesquisa em Álcool e Drogas (CPAD), Hospital de Clínicas de Porto 
Alegre (HCPA), Av. Protásio Alves, 211 - Bloco C - Santa Cecília, Porto 
Alegre-RS, 90035-903, Brazil.
(5)Departamento de Psiquiatria e Medicina Legal, Universidade Federal do Rio 
Grande do Sul, Porto Alegre, Brazil.

BACKGROUND: Wernicke encephalopathy (WE) is a potentially reversible 
neurological emergency that remains frequently missed and undertreated in 
patients with alcohol use disorder (AUD). Although thiamine is widely accepted 
as the cornerstone of prevention and treatment, diagnostic uncertainty, limited 
comparative evidence, and heterogeneous clinical recommendations contribute to 
substantial variability in real-world management. This scoping review aimed to 
map the available evidence on the diagnosis and clinical management of WE in 
patients with AUD or clinically significant alcohol use, with particular 
attention to practice variability, undertreatment, and clinically actionable 
gaps in care.
METHODS: We conducted a scoping review in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidance. 
Electronic databases and trial registries were searched for studies addressing 
the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of WE in populations with AUD or 
clinically significant alcohol use. Eligible sources included randomized 
controlled trials, observational studies, clinical audits, and 
implementation-focused reports. Data were charted and synthesized thematically.
RESULTS: A total of 26 studies were included. The evidence base was limited and 
heterogeneous. Only two randomized controlled trials evaluated thiamine 
regimens, and no consensus emerged regarding optimal dosing. Diagnostic criteria 
for WE varied widely across studies, with inconsistent use of formal criteria 
such as the Caine criteria. Across observational studies and prescribing audits, 
undertreatment was consistently reported, including delayed initiation of 
therapy and frequent use of oral thiamine in high-risk scenarios. Studies 
describing more protocolized and guideline-concordant care more often reported 
earlier treatment initiation and use of parenteral thiamine in suspected or 
confirmed cases.
CONCLUSIONS: WE remains underrecognized and undertreated in AUD and clinically 
significant alcohol use. The mapped evidence suggests that diagnostic 
uncertainty, limited trial data, and inconsistent implementation of 
recommendations are associated with persistent variability in care. Although the 
optimal thiamine regimen remains unresolved, early recognition and appropriate 
parenteral treatment in high-risk or suspected cases represent actionable 
opportunities to reduce preventable neurological morbidity.

From simulation to stimulation: a predictive synergy-based control strategy for 
functional electrical stimulation cycling in a person with spinal cord injury.

Peres AB(#)(1), Carmona GG(#)(1), de Sousa ACC(#)(2)(3), Baptista RS(#)(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Electrical Engineering, Universidade de Brasília, Brasília, 
Brazil.
(2)Department of Industrial Engineering, Institut Químic de Sarrià, Universitat 
Ramon Llull, Barcelona, Spain.
(3)Institute for Research and Innovation in Health, Universitat Politècnica de 
Catalunya - Barcelona Tech, Barcelona, Spain.
(4)Department of Electrical Engineering, Universidade de Brasília, Brasília, 
Brazil. baptista@ieee.org.
(#)Contributed equally

BACKGROUND: Functional electrical stimulation (FES) cycling stimulation 
strategies are often derived from heuristics, or able-bodied kinematics and 
electromyography, which may be unsafe and non-representative for people with 
complete spinal cord injury. Optimally controlled predictive musculoskeletal 
simulations with synergy implementation offer a way to generate individualized, 
physiologically plausible muscle trajectories without prior experimental data. 
Building on a previous proof of concept, this study developed and experimentally 
validated a simulation-derived stimulation strategy for FES cycling.
METHODS: A two-stage musculoskeletal predictive simulation framework was 
implemented using OpenSim Moco. First, a speed-tracking optimal control problem 
optimized the model's kinematics and individual muscle trajectories. Second, 
muscle excitations were decomposed into functional synergies using non-negative 
matrix factorization, producing coordinated activation patterns for quadriceps 
and hamstrings muscle groups. Subject-specific constraints were incorporated 
into the model. The resulting activation profile was then processed and 
converted to a crank-angle lookup table for real-time control. Experimental 
validation was conducted in one subject with complete spinal cord injury (SCI), 
comparing the simulation-derived control signal (CS) with a refined empirical 
bang-bang (BB) protocol used in the Cybathlon 2024 edition.
RESULTS: Simulations generated stable synergy-based muscle trajectories aligned 
with expected cycling dynamics. Experimentally, performance varied with trial 
order, with both CS and BB enabling unassisted FES cycling. BB produced higher 
average power and cadence, while CS delivered more symmetrical left-right 
balance and showed partial recovery in performance in higher stimulation 
intensities.
DISCUSSION: Although BB outperformed CS in power and cadence, the CS approach 
proved to be feasible and has methodological advantages. The consistent and 
physiologically structured behavior of the CS signal demonstrates that 
predictive simulation can provide a safe, reproducible baseline for 
individualized FES cycling control, particularly for new users or research 
groups.
CONCLUSION: This was the first implementation in cycling of optimal 
control-driven FES combined with muscle synergies, generating feasible, 
physiologically grounded stimulation profiles for FES cycling in an individual 
with complete SCI. While not surpassing a highly refined empirical strategy, the 
simulation-derived signal performed reliably and represents a promising 
foundation for model-based personalization of FES control.

Obstructive sleep apnea is frequent in patients with Long COVID fatigue but is 
not significantly associated with alterations of quality of life and cognition.

Bawa AP(1), Lopez M(2), Miller J(2), Sala MA(3), Maas MB(2), Liotta EM(2), 
Koralnik IJ(4).

Author information:
(1)Davee Department of Neurology, Northwestern Medicine, Chicago, IL, USA.
(2)Davee Department of Neurology, Northwestern University Feinberg School of 
Medicine, Chicago, IL, USA.
(3)Division of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Department of Medicine, 
Feinberg School of Medicine, Northwestern University, Chicago, IL, USA.
(4)Davee Department of Neurology, Northwestern University Feinberg School of 
Medicine, Chicago, IL, USA. igor.koralnik@northwestern.edu.

Neurologic manifestations of Long COVID, also called post-acute sequelae of 
SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), include fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, sleep 
disturbances, and headaches, which can be debilitating. Since these symptoms 
overlap with those of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), we sought to determine the 
prevalence of OSA in the population of a Neuro-COVID-19 clinic. We performed 
home sleep testing in 100 consecutive patients with Long COVID and no prior 
history of OSA who reported fatigue after an episode of COVID-19 not requiring 
hospitalization. The average age was 46.4 years and 70% of patients were female. 
OSA was present in 53% of patients, including 33% with mild OSA (apnea-hypopnea 
index (AHI) 5-14.9) and 20% with moderate to severe OSA (AHI ≥ 15). Male sex, 
higher age, and body mass index were significantly associated with OSA. However, 
there were no significant differences in other comorbidities, Long COVID symptom 
burden, quality of life measures (QoL), and objective cognitive function test 
results between groups. Additionally, multiple linear regression models 
demonstrated that neither AHI nor mean desaturation nadir were significant 
predictors of QoL or cognitive function. Although OSA is nearly twice as 
prevalent among our study participants compared to the general adult population 
of the US, it was not significantly associated with Long COVID symptoms, 
alteration of QoL, or objective cognitive dysfunction. However, 20% of patients 
were diagnosed with moderate to severe OSA, a clinically significant finding 
that warrants intervention to prevent irreversible cardiopulmonary 
complications.

Translating Evidence: The Curious History of the Word that Transformed Medicine.

Altschuler S(1), Lachenal G(2)(3).

Author information:
(1)Northeastern University, Boston, United States. 
s.altschuler@northeastern.edu.
(2)Sciences Po, Paris, France. Guillaume.lachenal@sciencespo.fr.
(3)Institut Universitaire de France, Paris, France. 
Guillaume.lachenal@sciencespo.fr.

Evidence-Based Medicine (EBM) is arguably the dominant paradigm in medicine 
today. Most doctors across the globe will be familiar with the term, and many 
would consider it the bedrock of good clinical care. Yet, EBM has met with 
unexpected difficulties translating its aspirations globally. We focus on the 
word evidence as a key to understanding this problem. Following the trajectory 
of the word evidence in French and Spanish medicine as a case of 
untranslatability (Barbara Cassin), we argue that the troubles inherent in 
translating evidence across languages and cultures point back to the complexity 
and nonobviousness of the word in English. This complexity haunts EBM, and it 
should be centered, not obscured, in discussions about how to translate clinical 
research into medical practice. We conclude by encouraging medicine, first, to 
embrace these linguistic difficulties as a key to offering better care; second, 
to view the issues we raise not as solvable with the right word but as an 
intrinsic part of the languages themselves; and, finally, to use the difficulty 
and underacknowledged pluralism within the language of medicine as a provocation 
for thinking more broadly about how medical knowledge is made, understood, and 
circulated.

Development of efficient betaine-based natural deep eutectic solvents for metal

Oke EA(1), Potgieter JH(2).

The rapid growth of electronic waste has intensified the need for sustainable 
approaches for metal recovery from waste printed circuit boards (WPCBs). In this 
study, betaine-based natural deep eutectic solvents (NADES) were developed as 
lixiviants for metal extraction from WPCBs. Betaine (BET) was used as the 
hydrogen bond acceptor, while ethane-1,2-diol (ETD), propane-1,2-diol (PPD), and 
butane-1,2-diol (BTD) served as hydrogen bond donors (HBDs) to investigate the 
influence of HBD structure on the physicochemical properties and leaching 
performance of the resulting NADES. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy 
(FTIR) indicated intermolecular interactions between BET and the diol-based 
HBDs, while thermogravimetric analysis/derivative thermogravimetry (TGA/DTG) 
showed pronounced mass-loss-rate maxima above 240 °C for all three NADES. 
Rheological measurements revealed Newtonian flow behaviour, with viscosity 
increasing with increasing diol chain length; BET:ETD exhibited the lowest 
viscosity (50.1 mPa·s) at 20 °C. Under the experimental conditions of 75 °C, 
6 h, 1.0 M H2O2, 500 rpm, and a solid-to-liquid ratio of 1:20, BET:ETD achieved 
leaching efficiencies of 99.3% for Cu, 99.5% for Pb, 97.8% for Fe, 95.4% for Al, 
90.5% for Sn, and 73.9% for Ti. Kinetic analysis based on the shrinking core 
model and activation energy evaluation indicated a mixed-control mechanism 
involving interfacial reaction and diffusion processes. SEM, XRD, and FTIR 
analyses further indicated substantial dissolution of metallic phases while the 
polymeric and glass-fibre matrix was largely preserved. Overall, the results 
demonstrate that betaine-based NADES, most especially BET:ETD, offer tunable 
physicochemical properties and effective metal-leaching performance for WPCB 
recycling.

Carbapenem resistance and mortality in pediatric Acinetobacter bloodstream 
infections: determinants from a 12-year tertiary-care cohort study.

Karauzum SE(1), Erci E(1), Koc G(2), Yazici Ozkaya P(2), Kiran Tasci E(3), 
Karakoyun M(3), Ozek G(4), Ataseven E(4), Terek D(5), Yasar Duman M(6), Cilli 
FF(6), Sahbudak Bal Z(1), Avcu G(7).

Author information:
(1)Division of Pediatric Infectious Diseases, Department of Pediatrics, Faculty 
of Medicine, Ege University, Izmir, Turkey.
(2)Division of Pediatric Intensive Care, Department of Pediatrics, Faculty of 
Medicine, Ege University, Izmir, Turkey.
(3)Division of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Department of Pediatrics, Faculty of

(4)Division of Pediatric Oncology, Department of Pediatrics, Faculty of

Carbapenem-resistant (CR) Acinetobacter spp. bloodstream infections (BSIs) are 
difficult to treat in children, yet pediatric data on factors associated with 
resistance and mortality remain limited. We aimed to identify factors associated 
with carbapenem resistance and 30-day mortality in pediatric Acinetobacter BSIs. 
We retrospectively analyzed children with monomicrobial Acinetobacter BSIs at a 
tertiary-care university hospital between January 2014 and September 2025. 
Factors associated with carbapenem resistance were assessed using co-primary 
logistic regression analyses in the full cohort and within A. baumannii; 30-day 
mortality was assessed using Cox regression. Among 128 episodes, median age was 
2.0 years (IQR 0.76-8.01), 60.2% (77/128) were male and 90.6% (116/128) had 
comorbidities. Carbapenem resistance was identified in 54/128 episodes (42.2%), 
all caused by A. baumannii (54/87, 62.1%). Increasing age, longer 
hospitalization before BSI onset, mechanical ventilation (MV), and prior 
meropenem exposure were associated with resistance in both co-primary models. 
Adjusted ORs for MV were 23.77 (95% CI, 7.54-74.92) in the full cohort and 23.20 
(95% CI, 5.39-99.95) within A. baumannii. Overall 30-day mortality was 13.3% 
(17/128) and was higher in CR than carbapenem-susceptible episodes (22.2% versus 
6.8%; p = 0.011). Exploratory comparisons across CR A. baumannii treatment 
categories were inconclusive (exact p = 0.256). Thrombocytopenia (aHR, 6.12; 95% 
CI, 2.13-17.61) and carbapenem resistance (aHR, 3.01; 95% CI, 1.04-8.71) were 
associated with mortality in the primary Cox model.
CONCLUSION:  Thrombocytopenia and carbapenem resistance were associated with 
30-day all-cause mortality in the primary adjusted analysis; the resistance 
association was not statistically significant in A. baumannii-restricted and 
first-episode-only sensitivity analyses.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Acinetobacter BSIs mainly affect medically complex hospitalized 
children. • Pediatric evidence on factors associated with carbapenem resistance 
and mortality remains scarce.
WHAT IS NEW: • Increasing age, longer hospitalization before BSI onset, 
mechanical ventilation, and prior meropenem exposure were associated with 
carbapenem resistance in both the full Acinetobacter cohort and within A. 
baumannii. • Carbapenem resistance was associated with 30-day mortality in the 
primary model, but this finding was not consistently supported in sensitivity 
analyses; thrombocytopenia remained associated with mortality.

Low-dose histrelin for ovulation induction in mares: a partially randomized 
crossover pilot study.

de Barros Fogagnoli L(1), Jose KCA(2), Weckl R(2), Mota CMO(2), Fernandes MO(2), 
Machado RC(2), Camargo CE(2), Michelotto PV(3)(4).

Author information:
(1)Graduate Program in Animal Science, School of Medicine and Life Sciences, 
Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Paraná, Rua Imaculada Conceição 1155, Prado 
Velho, Curitiba, Paraná, 80215-901, Brazil.
(2)Veterinary Program, School of Medicine and Life Sciences, Pontifícia 
Universidade Católica do Paraná, Rua Imaculada Conceição 1155, Prado Velho, 
Curitiba, Paraná, 80215-901, Brazil.
(3)Graduate Program in Animal Science, School of Medicine and Life Sciences, 
Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Paraná, Rua Imaculada Conceição 1155, Prado 
Velho, Curitiba, Paraná, 80215-901, Brazil. p.michelotto@pucpr.br.
(4)Veterinary Program, School of Medicine and Life Sciences, Pontifícia

This partially randomized crossover pilot study evaluated reduced doses of 
histrelin for ovulation induction in mares and compared intramuscular (IM) 
administration with pharmacopuncture at the Bai-hui and Yan-chi acupoints. 
Eleven mares were enrolled, of which nine completed all eight protocols and were 
included in the analyses. The protocols comprised 250 µg histrelin IM (standard 
dose), 75 µg IM, 25 µg IM, no intervention, saline at Bai-hui, saline at 
Yan-chi, 25 µg histrelin at Bai-hui, and 25 µg histrelin at Yan-chi. Ovulation 
was assessed by transrectal ultrasonography at scheduled examinations until 
detected, with ovulation within 48 h as the primary outcome. Ovulations first 
detected at 24 h were excluded from the primary analysis. Ovulation within 48 h 
occurred in 88.9% (8/9) of observations with 250 µg IM, 87.5% (7/8) with 75 µg 
IM, 87.5% (7/8) with 25 µg IM, 37.5% (3/8) with no intervention, 50.0% (3/6) 
with saline at Bai-hui, 100% (9/9) with 25 µg histrelin at Bai-hui, 12.5% (1/8) 
with saline at Yan-chi, and 87.5% (7/8) with 25 µg histrelin at Yan-chi. Exact 
95% confidence intervals were wide, reflecting the small sample size. 
Exploratory pairwise comparisons with the no-intervention protocol were 
performed without adjustment for multiple comparisons and should be interpreted 
cautiously. The findings provide preliminary evidence that reduced histrelin 
doses, including 25 µg, may induce ovulation within 48 h in mares. However, this 
study did not demonstrate an advantage of pharmacopuncture over IM 
administration of the same reduced dose. Larger, fully randomized studies are 
required to confirm the efficacy of reduced-dose histrelin and determine whether 
administration at specific acupoints provides any additional effect.

Impact of (131)I-MIBG dose escalation (12 vs. 18 mCi/kg) during conditioning for 
autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in pediatric neuroblastoma: a 
retrospective cohort study.

Kalantari A(1), Behfar M(1)(2), Karimizadeh Z(1), Karimzadeh A(1), Paymani Z(3), 
Farzanehfar S(4), Abbasi M(4), Tajalli A(1), Ansari S(1), Ashkevari P(1), 
Mohseni R(1), Karami N(1), Hamidieh AA(5).

Author information:
(1)Pediatric Cell and Gene Therapy Research Center, Gene, Cell & Tissue Research 
Institute, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran.
(2)Children's Medical Center, Pediatric Center of Excellence, Tehran University 
of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran.
(3)Nuclear Medicine Department, Children's Medical Center, Tehran University of 
Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran.
(4)Department of Nuclear Medicine, Vali-Asr Hospital, Tehran University of

(5)Pediatric Cell and Gene Therapy Research Center, Gene, Cell & Tissue Research 
Institute, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran. 
aahamidieh@tums.ac.ir.

This study aimed to evaluate whether dose escalation of 
131I-meta-iodobenzylguanidine (131I-MIBG) from 12 to 18 mCi/kg improves 
survival, engraftment, or toxicity profiles in children with high-risk 
neuroblastoma undergoing autologous HSCT. We retrospectively analyzed 56 
pediatric patients under 18 years of age with high-risk, MIBG-avid neuroblastoma 
who underwent autologous HSCT between 2016 and 2025. Patients received either 
12 mCi/kg (n = 17) or 18 mCi/kg (n = 39) of 131I-MIBG as part of a myeloablative 
chemotherapy conditioning regimen. Outcomes included engraftment, overall 
survival (OS), and event-free survival (EFS). Twenty-one deaths had occurred 
(8/17 [47.1%] in the 12 mCi/kg group; 13/39 [33.3%] in the 18 mCi/kg group). OS 
at 1 and 5 years was 76.5% and 59.5% for the 12 mCi/kg group, compared with 
76.6% and 58.2% for the 18 mCi/kg group (log-rank p = 0.786). EFS at 1 and 
5 years was 45.3% and 38.8% for the 12 mCi/kg group, compared with 69.1% and 
36.2% for the 18 mCi/kg group (log-rank p = 0.656). Furthermore, at 1-year 
post-HSCT, the 18 mCi/kg group demonstrated a significantly higher rate of 
normal MIBG scans (83.3% vs. 46.2%, p = 0.024). Neutrophil engraftment was 
faster in the 18 mCi/kg group (median 10 vs 12 days; p = 0.001). Platelet 
engraftment was also more frequent in the 18 mCi/kg group (92.3% vs 70.6%; 
p = 0.047), with similar time to engraftment (16 vs 16.5 days).
CONCLUSION:  In this retrospective cohort, escalation from 12 to 18 mCi/kg was 
associated with faster neutrophil engraftment and a higher rate of normal MIBG 
scans at 1 year, without a significant difference in OS or EFS. The study was 
underpowered, and did not demonstrate a significant benefit of either the lower 
or the higher dose; the optimal dose remains undetermined and requires 
prospective evaluation.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • 131I-MIBG is incorporated into conditioning regimens prior to 
autologous HSCT for high-risk pediatric neuroblastoma, with doses up to 
18 mCi/kg being tolerable, but the optimal dose and its impact on long-term 
survival remain unclear.
WHAT IS NEW: • In this direct retrospective comparison (12 vs. 18 mCi/kg), the 
higher dose was associated with faster neutrophil engraftment and a higher 
platelet engraftment rate and a higher rate of normal MIBG scans at year, but 
without a significant difference in OS or EFS, and with a non-significant trend 
toward more renal and thyroid toxicity. The study was underpowered and did not 
demonstrate a significant benefit of either dose; the optimal MIBG dose remains 
undetermined.

Community-based behavioral change interventions to reduce the burden of 
inherited genetic disorders in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs): a 
scoping review.

Lasi S(1), Asim M(2), Tariq J(3), Zainab S(2), Liaquat S(2), Uddin A(4), Haider 
S(2), Waqar K(4), Khan AZ(4), Brown N(5), Kirmani S(4).

Author information:
(1)Human Development Programme, Aga Khan University, Karachi, Pakistan. 
seema.laasi@aku.edu.
(2)Community Health Sciences, Aga Khan University, Karachi, Pakistan.
(3)Medical College, Aga Khan University, Karachi, Pakistan.
(4)Human Development Programme, Aga Khan University, Karachi, Pakistan.
(5)Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden.

BACKGROUND: Genetic and congenital disorders related to consanguineous marriage 
are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in regions where cousin marriages 
are common. Their burden may be reduced through community education and 
awareness, but evidence for a consistently effective means of implementing is 
sparse. Our aim is to review the published literature and to describe behavioral 
change approaches that have been used to reduce the burden of inherited genetic 
disorder in highly consanguineous communities.
METHODS: A scoping review based on PRISMA guidance, utilizing methodological 
framework outlined by Arksey and O'Malley was conducted. A systematic search was 
done across multiple electronic databases for literature published between 2000 
and 2024. Studies related to community-level intervention targeting behavior, 
knowledge and attitudes related to continuity and genetic disease prevention in 
relevant LMIC settings were included.
RESULTS: We found nine papers fulfilling our priori search criteria, 6 from 
South and Southeast Asia and one each from the Middle East, West Africa and 
North Africa. Overall, the methodological quality of the included studies ranged 
from low to high, with MMAT scores spanning 40% to 100%. All involved short-term 
education and counselling sessions aimed at young couples, high school-age 
adolescents and community members. The majority were haemoglobinopathy targeted. 
Overall, the included studies reported positive effects of educational, 
counseling, and integrated behavioral interventions on increasing knowledge 
about genetic screening, testing, and genetic diseases.
CONCLUSION: Community-based interventions show promise in improving awareness of 
consanguinity-related genetic risks in LMIC settings, particularly when 
culturally adapted and embedded within trusted community platforms. However, 
evidence remains limited regarding their effectiveness in achieving sustained 
behavioral change.
