Spatiotemporal controls of soil Pb distribution and ecological risk in the 
Qorveh mining region, Western Iran.

Saedpanah M(1), Souri B(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Environmental Sciences, Faculty of Natural Resources, 
University of Kurdistan, P.O. Box 416, Sanandaj, Iran.
(2)Department of Environmental Sciences, Faculty of Natural Resources, 
University of Kurdistan, P.O. Box 416, Sanandaj, Iran. bsouri@uok.ac.ir.

To investigate the spatiotemporal variability of lead (Pb) in mining 
environments, 100 topsoil samples were collected from different locations across 
a semi-arid mining district in western Iran over a 4-month monitoring period, 
with sampling conducted at different sites in each month. Key explanatory 
variables, namely, pH, electrical conductivity (EC), soil organic carbon (SOC), 
zirconium (Zr), and elevation and slope as topographic attributes alongside 
normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), were integrated into the 
Geographic and Temporal Weighted Regression (GTWR) framework. Pb was selected 
because of its strong association with mining activities, high environmental 
persistence, and ecological significance. The effectiveness of the GTWR model 
was evaluated and compared with Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Geographically 
Weighted Regression (GWR) and Temporally Weighted Regression (TWR) using 
multiple statistical evaluation metrics and model-fitting criteria. In addition, 
the ecological implications of Pb contamination were assessed using the risk 
quotient (RQ) index. The evaluation metrics demonstrated the superiority of GTWR 
(R2 = 0.79) over the other models. The results indicate that Pb distribution was 
influenced by geological, geochemical, and biological factors, with Zr showing a 
predominantly spatially positive association, EC exhibiting spatially variable 
effects, and NDVI and pH showing relatively stable temporal associations with 
Pb. Furthermore, RQ values exceeded the ecological threshold throughout the 
study area, indicating widespread potential ecological risk. Integrating GTWR 
with ecological risk assessment provides a useful framework for characterizing 
heterogeneous Pb patterns and supporting the identification of priority areas 
for environmental monitoring and risk management in mining-affected landscapes.

Ground-level ozone (O3) has become a major challenge for air quality improvement 
in China, but its short-term variability is controlled by complex interactions 
among pollutant persistence, precursor conditions, and meteorological factors. 
In this study, hourly air quality observations and ERA5 reanalysis 
meteorological data for an urban monitoring site in Wuhan during 2019-2025 were 
integrated to evaluate O3 temporal variability and interpretable machine 
learning prediction. Three models, namely, deep neural network (DNN), random 
forest (RF), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), were compared using 
baseline and lag-enhanced feature sets, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) 
were used to interpret predictive contributions. O3 remained at relatively high 
levels during 2019-2025, with exceedances of the national grade II standard in 
2019, 2023, and 2024, while most primary pollutants generally declined. O3 
exhibited a unimodal diurnal cycle with afternoon peaks at 14:00-16:00 and a 
seasonal pattern of summer > spring > autumn > winter. The enhanced XGBoost 
model achieved the best short-term prediction performance, with R2 = 0.9756 and 
RMSE = 6.35 μg m-3 on the test set. SHAP analysis showed that the 1-h lagged O3 
concentration was the dominant predictor, indicating strong short-term 
persistence rather than independent chemical forcing. NO2 and lagged NO2 showed 
negative predictive contributions, consistent with the expected role of NO 
titration under high-NOₓ conditions, whereas temperature and radiation-related 
variables showed positive contributions. These results suggest that 
interpretable machine learning can help identify the statistical conditions 
associated with O3 variability, but the absence of direct VOC observations means 
that O3 sensitivity and VOC-related control implications should be further 
verified using VOC measurements or chemical transport/observation-based 
modeling.

Comparison of raw-signal, feature-based and hybrid representations for 
machine-learning classification of retinal diseases from pattern 
electroretinography.

Aygün AB(1), Açıkgöz R(2), Coşkun M(3), Erden MA(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biomedical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering and Natural 
Sciences, Karabük University, Karabük, Türkiye. abilalaygun@karabuk.edu.tr.
(2)Department of Biomedical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering and Natural 
Sciences, Karabük University, Karabük, Türkiye.
(3)Department of Ophthalmology, Faculty of Medicine, Karabük University, 
Karabük, Türkiye.

Pattern electroretinography (PERG) is a non-invasive test of macular and retinal 
ganglion cell function, but its low amplitude and inter-subject variability 
limit its diagnostic use. This study compares three representations of the 
transient PERG waveform for the detection of six retinal and optic nerve 
conditions - Birdshot chorioretinopathy, cone-rod dystrophy, hereditary optic 
atrophy, macular dystrophy, retinitis pigmentosa and Stargardt disease - against 
healthy controls, using the publicly available PERG-IOBA dataset. A total of 672 
recordings from 336 examinations of 304 participants were preprocessed in six 
stages, and three representations were evaluated under one identical protocol: 
the raw 255-point amplitude-preserving waveform; 60 engineered clinical, 
spectral, wavelet and complexity descriptors; and a hybrid representation of 343 
variables combining both, with multi-wavelet features from db4, sym2 and coif3. 
Performance was estimated by 10 × 5-fold participant-grouped cross-validation, 
in which both eyes and all repeat visits of an individual were kept in the same 
partition, with nested hyperparameter selection and all data-derived 
preprocessing fitted inside each training fold. Under the pre-specified primary 
classifier, the raw waveform gave the highest pooled out-of-fold AUC in four of 
the six classes (0.906 in cone-rod dystrophy, 0.842 in retinitis pigmentosa, 
0.755 in macular dystrophy, 0.673 in hereditary optic atrophy) and the 
engineered descriptors in the remaining two (0.803 in Stargardt disease, 0.657 
in Birdshot chorioretinopathy). The hybrid representation was highest in none, 
falling below the raw waveform in five of six classes by 0.002 to 0.018, and no 
non-linear classifier showed a hybrid advantage above 0.006 in mean AUC. A 
sensitivity analysis identified what does matter: removing the absolute 
amplitude scale by per-signal z-scoring cost the raw representation 0.055 AUC on 
average but the engineered descriptors only 0.023, and reversed the ordering of 
the three representations. Engineered descriptors did not improve on the 
waveform, but they made the problem tractable for linear models, which gained 
0.128 in mean AUC from the reduction in dimensionality. These internally 
validated findings indicate that absolute PERG amplitude should be preserved 
rather than normalised away; participant-independent, multi-centre validation is 
required before clinical application.

Visual estimation of guidewire contact forces by integrating multi-scale 
features and region mask.

Guo J(1), Yang D(1), Xiao N(2), Li J(1), Zheng Q(1), Wei W(3).

Author information:
(1)The School of Electronic and Information Engineering, Suzhou University of 
Science and Technology, Suzhou, 215009, China.
(2)School of Medical Technology, No.5 Zhongguancun South Street, Haidian 
District, Beijing, 100081, China.
(3)The School of Electronic and Information Engineering, Suzhou University of 
Science and Technology, Suzhou, 215009, China. weiwei0728@usts.edu.cn.

During percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), the contact force between the 
guidewire and the vessel wall is a key mechanical factor in vessel injury, yet 
it cannot be measured directly with conventional imaging. Although sensor-based 
methods measure the contact force directly, they increase both the complexity 
and the cost of the instrumentation. A sensorless guidewire contact force 
estimation method is therefore proposed, in which multi-scale feature extraction 
is combined with region mask mean pooling to learn an end-to-end mapping from 
conventional planar images to the contact force in each of the four predefined 
contact regions. The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of 343 samples 
acquired on a 3D-printed vessel phantom, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) 
of 0.861 g and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.036 g. Ablation experiments 
show that the region mask reduces the MAE by 79% relative to the identical 
architecture without the region mask. Requiring neither additional sensing 
hardware nor complex physical modeling, the method estimates the contact force 
from visual information alone. These results support the feasibility of 
vision-based sensorless contact force estimation and suggest a possible route 
toward force feedback in interventional procedures.

Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow: from diagnosis to rehabilitation.

Donati D(1)(2), Morselli M(3), Ricci V(4), D'Auria L(2), Boccolari P(2), 
Tedeschi R(5), Vita F(6), Amoruso V(7), Tarallo L(3).

Author information:
(1)Physical Therapy and Rehabilitation Unit, Policlinico di Modena, 41125, 
Modena, Italy.
(2)Clinical and Experimental Medicine PhD Program, University of Modena and 
Reggio Emilia, 41121, Modena, Italy.
(3)Orthopedic and Traumatology Department of Modena, University of Modena and 
Reggio Emilia, Modena, Italy.
(4)Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine Unit, Luigi Sacco University Hospital, 
ASST Fatebenefratelli-Sacco, 20157, Milan, Italy.
(5)Independent Researcher, Bologna, Italy. roberto.tedeschi82@gmail.com.
(6)IRCCS Istituto Ortopedico Rizzoli, Bologna, Italy.
(7)Rehabilitation Unit Santa Corona Hospital, 17027, Pietra Ligure, Italy.

BACKGROUND: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (UNE) is the second most common 
entrapment neuropathy of the upper limb, involving physical medicine and 
rehabilitation, neurology, orthopedics, and plastic surgery. It results from 
static or dynamic ulnar nerve instability, cubital tunnel syndrome, or 
space-occupying lesions. Accurate diagnosis requires thorough history, clinical 
examination, and selection of appropriate diagnostic tests.
SEARCH STRATEGY: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched 
(January 2000-August 2026) using combinations of "ulnar neuropathy", "cubital 
tunnel syndrome", "elbow", "ultrasound", "electrodiagnosis", "conservative 
treatment", "rehabilitation" and "surgery". English-language original studies, 
systematic reviews and meta-analyses were eligible; case reports were included 
only where no higher-level evidence existed. Approximately 220 records were 
screened; 58 were retained, following SANRA recommendations for narrative 
reviews.
DISCUSSION: High-resolution ultrasound provides dynamic, non-invasive, 
cost-effective evaluation of the ulnar nerve and real-time assessment of 
compression or instability, and guides minimally invasive procedures such as 
perineural injections, although the only randomized placebo-controlled trial did 
not show superiority of corticosteroid injection over placebo. Conservative 
treatment is usually first-line, although surgery may be required in advanced or 
refractory cases; comparative evidence shows no clear superiority among surgical 
techniques, while endoscopic decompression carries a higher complication rate 
than open approaches.
CONCLUSIONS: This narrative review summarizes current evidence on diagnostic 
pathways and therapeutic options for UNE, highlighting the role of ultrasound as 
both a diagnostic and interventional tool, and outlines gaps in the literature 
regarding standardized conservative and surgical protocols.

Comparison of robotic and laparoscopic gastrectomy using textbook oncologic 
outcome: a matched cohort study.

Kim EY(1), Seo JW(2), Park KB(2), Lim ST(3), Jun KH(4), Chin HM(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Surgery, Uijeongbu St. Mary's Hospital, College of Medicine, 
The Catholic University of Korea, Seoul, Republic of Korea.
(2)Department of Surgery, St. Vincent's Hospital, College of Medicine, The 
Catholic University of Korea, 93, Jungbudaero, Paldal-gu, Seoul, Suwon, 
Gyeonggi-do, 16247, Republic Of Korea.
(3)Department of Surgery, St. Vincent's Hospital, College of Medicine, The 
Catholic University of Korea, 93, Jungbudaero, Paldal-gu, Seoul, Suwon, 
Gyeonggi-do, 16247, Republic Of Korea. in-somnia@hanmail.net.
(4)Department of Surgery, St. Vincent's Hospital, College of Medicine, The

By evaluating whether a patient simultaneously satisfies multiple desirable 
goals, textbook oncologic outcome (TOO) offers a composite assessment of 
cancer-surgery quality. This study investigated whether TOO attainment after 
curative gastric cancer surgery differed according to the operative approach. We 
retrospectively reviewed 945 patients with gastric adenocarcinoma who received 
curative-intent robotic gastrectomy (RG; n = 161) or laparoscopic gastrectomy 
(LG; n = 784) between 2017 and 2025. Propensity score matching yielded 147 
patients in each group. When each of the following was recorded, a TOO was 
attained: margin-negative resection, assessment of at least 15 lymph nodes, 
survival beyond 30 postoperative days, hospital discharge no later than 
postoperative day 7, and guideline-appropriate adjuvant chemotherapy. We 
compared operative characteristics, postoperative recovery, complications, and 
survival between the approaches. Among matched patients, the complete TOO was 
attained after 66.0% of RG procedures and 43.5% of LG procedures (P < 0.001). 
Although RG had a longer operating time, it was linked to quicker 
gastrointestinal healing and discharge as well as decreased blood loss. The 
between-group difference in the composite measure was driven chiefly by 
discharge within 7 days. Overall and major complication rates did not differ 
significantly. Multivariable analysis identified RG (odds ratio [OR], 2.48; 95% 
confidence interval [CI], 1.52-4.07; P < 0.001) and distal gastrectomy (OR, 
3.32; 95% CI, 1.46-7.56; P = 0.004) as positive correlates of TOO attainment, 
whereas estimated blood loss of at least 50 mL was a negative correlate (OR, 
0.37; 95% CI, 0.21-0.67; P = 0.001). The approaches showed no significant 
difference in estimated 5-year overall or disease-free survival. Patients 
undergoing RG met all five TOO criteria more frequently, largely because they 
were more likely to leave the hospital by postoperative day 7 rather than 
because of differences in oncologic radicality. RG was also associated with 
lower blood loss and faster early recovery, while morbidity and survival were 
comparable between approaches. These findings should be interpreted as 
reflecting an advantage of RG in postoperative recovery and length of stay 
rather than demonstrable superiority in overall oncologic or surgical quality.

Raj ASWW(1), Babu JYM(1), Sabanayagam R(2)(3), Muthusami S(2)(3), Manoharan

Author information:
(1)Department of Biochemistry, Guindy Campus, University of Madras, Chennai,

Colorectal cancer (CRC) cells undergo significant alterations in glucose and 
glutamine metabolism to support rapid growth and migration. However, the 
molecular mechanisms underlying these metabolic changes remain incompletely 
understood. Although NUAK1 and NUAK2, members of the NUAK kinase family have 
been implicated in CRC tumorigenesis, their specific roles in metabolic 
reprogramming that drives CRC progression and metastasis have not been 
elucidated. In this study, we demonstrate that NUAK1 and NUAK2 are overexpressed 
in human CRC tissues and that their expression is associated with increased 
tumor metastasis and poorer patient survival. NUAK1/2 promotes CRC cell 
proliferation and migration, whereas their depletion markedly reduces cell 
growth and migratory capacity. Furthermore, knockout of NUAK1/2 disrupts key 
metabolic pathways, including aerobic glycolysis, pentose phosphate pathway 
(PPP), and glutamine metabolism. Mechanistically, NUAK1/2 facilitates

suppressing AMPK activity. Depletion of NUAK1/2 impairs metabolic function, 
cellular growth, and migration potential in CRC cells, effects that are further 
enhanced by pharmacological activation of AMPK with AICAR and inhibition of mTOR 
using Rapamycin. In conclusion, these findings identify NUAK1/2 as critical 
regulators of CRC progression and migration through AMPK/mTOR-mediated metabolic 
reprogramming, highlighting their potential as therapeutic targets in colorectal 
cancer.

Neuroimaging studies have reported that chronic pain may be associated with 
brain functional changes and related molecular mechanisms. However, there are 
few studies in anterior shoulder pain (ASP). Thus, we aimed to assess the 
possible brain functional changes and their associations with neurotransmitter 
receptor maps in ASP patients. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance 
imaging data were obtained from 27 ASP patients and 20 healthy controls (HCs). 
Regional homogeneity (ReHo) and fractional amplitude of low-frequency 
fluctuation (fALFF) methods were used to examine altered brain functions. 
JuSpace toolbox was employed for evaluating the spatial correlations between

accuracy in the middle temporal gyrus, precentral gyrus and putamen. Our study 
investigated abnormal brain function and associated neurotransmitter receptor 
maps in ASP patients, which may contribute to improving our understanding of the 
pathophysiological mechanisms in ASP.

Clinical whole exome sequencing in childhood epilepsy: a tertiary center 
retrospective study from Saudi Arabia.

Abumansour IS(1), Daghistani RO(2), Muthaffar OY(3), Alyazidi AS(4)(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Medical Genetics, Faculty of Medicine, Umm Al-Qura University, 
Makkah, Saudi Arabia.
(2)Pediatric Neurology Section, Department of Pediatrics, King Faisal Specialist 
Hospital and Research Center, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
(3)Pediatric Neurology Section, Department of Pediatrics, Faculty of Medicine,

(4)Department of Paediatric Neurology, Royal London Hospital, Barts Health NHS

(5)Pediatric Neurology Division, Pediatric Department, King Saud University

Childhood epilepsy, particularly when drug-resistant, often has an underlying 
genetic etiology. Populations with high consanguinity rates, such as Saudi 
Arabia, are expected to have a higher burden of autosomal recessive disorders. 
However, the diagnostic yield and clinical utility of whole-exome sequencing 
(WES) in this context require further characterization. We conducted a 
retrospective cross-sectional study at King Faisal Specialist Hospital and 
Research Centre-Jeddah (KFSHRC-J) between May 2017 and November 2021. We 
reviewed charts of all patients with clinical WES results (n = 561) and included 
108 pediatric patients (< 14 years) for whom epilepsy was the primary indication 
for testing. Data on demographics, clinical presentation, radiological findings, 
and WES results were extracted from electronic medical records. Variants were 
classified according to ACMG guidelines. Among 108 patients (53 males, 49%; 55 
females, 51%), the mean age at epilepsy onset was 2.6 years, and 77% (83/108) 
reported consanguinity. WES identified reportable genetic findings in 98 cases 
(90.7%), classified as pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants (n = 32) or 
variants of unknown significance (VUS) (n = 66). In the remaining 10 cases 
(9.3%), no variant considered sufficient to explain the clinical phenotype was 
identified. The definitive diagnostic yield, defined as pathogenic or likely 
pathogenic variants explaining the clinical phenotype, was 30% (32/108; 95% CI: 
22-39%). Autosomal recessive inheritance accounted for 72% (23/32) of diagnosed 
cases. When including VUS with strong phenotype correlation, the potential 
diagnostic yield increased to 60% (65/108). WES results directly influenced 
clinical management in 5% (5/108) of patients, including targeted metabolic 
therapy, medication optimization, and avoidance of contraindicated 
therapies. WES demonstrates significant diagnostic utility in childhood 
epilepsy, particularly in consanguineous populations with a high burden of 
autosomal recessive disorders. Integration of WES into the diagnostic workflow 
enables precision medicine approaches and supports early genetic counseling.

Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are evolutionarily conserved regulators of innate 
immunity and extensively characterized in mammals and Drosophila melanogaster; 
however, their functional roles in other insects remain incompletely defined. In 
this study, we investigated the immunological function of TmToll-6 in Tenebrio 
molitor larvae under systemic pathogenic bacterial and fungal challenge. 
Transcriptional analyses revealed that its expression was strongly induced in 
the fat body, gut, Malpighian tubules, and hemolymph following exposure to 
Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Candida albicans. The RNA 
interference-mediated silencing of TmToll-6 significantly increased larval 
mortality after E. coli and S. aureus infection, highlighting its essential role 
in antibacterial defense. Mechanistic evaluation further demonstrated that 
TmToll-6 knockdown markedly suppressed the antimicrobial peptide (AMP) gene 
expression, particularly in the fat body and gut, which are the main effector 
tissues of insect humoral immunity. Although TmToll-6 was strongly induced 
following C. albicans infection, its silencing produced comparatively limited 
effects on AMP expression, indicating that antifungal AMP regulation is less 
dependent on TmToll-6 and may involve partially redundant immune pathways.

through Toll pathway-dependent AMP regulation in a tissue- and pathogen-specific 
manner. This study highlighted the evolutionary diversification of Toll 
receptors in coleopteran immunity.

No effective treatments currently exist for tauopathies. Given emerging evidence 
that moderate-dose ionizing radiation (IR) may exert neuroreparative effects in 
neurodegeneration, we investigated the impact of combined IR exposure on disease 
progression in the Tau P301S mouse model. Tau P301S mice received combined 
gamma-ray (0.24 Gy) and carbon-12 nuclei (0.18 Gy, 400 MeV/n) irradiation at the 
presymptomatic stage. Following longitudinal behavioral testing until the 
terminal stage, post-mortem brains were analyzed via RT-qPCR, ELISA, and HPLC to 
assess gene expression, protein levels, and monoamine quantification. At the 
symptomatic stage, Tau+R mice showed normalized endurance, fear-dependent 
memory, and disinhibition-like behavior, reaching wild-type levels. At the 
terminal stage, Tau+R mice demonstrated significantly superior balance, 
coordination, and grip strength compared to untreated Tau P301S mice. These 
benefits correlated with restored striatal serotonin and a 76% reduction in 
cerebellar tau protein (transcription-independent). Furthermore, IR normalized 
Gsk3b expression in the hippocampus and cerebellum, and Trem2 in the cerebellum, 
to WT levels. Notably, IR up-regulated cerebellar Iba1 by 31% and 86% compared 
to WT and Tau mice, respectively. Combined radiotherapy not only alleviates 
behavioral symptoms but also modulates key neurochemical parameters. These 
findings demonstrate robust symptomatic improvements and suggest a potential 
neuroprotective capacity of combined radiotherapy in a mouse model of severe 
tauopathy.

Computerized fine motor assessment in Parkinson's Disease: Task-specific 
measures provide complementary clinical information.

Menteşe B(1), Savran FN(2), Batum M(3), Kutlu N(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Physiology, Faculty of Medicine, Manisa Celal Bayar University, 
Manisa, Türkiye. bestementese@gmail.com.
(2)Department of Physiology, Faculty of Medicine, Manisa Celal Bayar University, 
Manisa, Türkiye.
(3)Department of Neurology, Faculty of Medicine, Manisa Celal Bayar University, 
Manisa, Türkiye.

BACKGROUND: Fine motor impairment is a common feature of Parkinson's disease 
(PD) and contributes substantially to functional disability. Although the 
Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS 
Part III) remains the standard clinical tool for motor evaluation, quantitative 
computerized assessments may provide complementary task-specific information.
OBJECTIVES: This cross-sectional case-control study compared fine motor 
performance measured using the Motorische Leistungs-Serie (MLS) between 19 
patients with idiopathic PD and 20 healthy controls and examined associations 
between MLS-derived parameters and clinical motor severity.
METHODS: Motor performance was evaluated using five MLS subtests covering aiming 
behavior, hand steadiness, precision arm-hand coordination, speed arm-hand, and 
speed wrist-finger tasks.
RESULTS: After adjustment for age, sex, and educational level, patients with PD 
showed significantly poorer overall fine motor performance, as reflected by the 
Composite Motor Performance Score, together with significant impairments in 
selected task-specific measures of aiming performance and visuomotor tracking. 
Several MLS-derived parameters, particularly aiming duration and hand 
steadiness, were significantly associated with MDS-UPDRS Part III scores.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that MLS-derived task-specific measures 
provide objective quantitative information that complements conventional 
clinical motor assessment in Parkinson's disease. Analysis of individual 
task-specific parameters may provide complementary clinically relevant 
information beyond a single global composite score. However, larger prospective 
studies are required to determine the clinical utility of task-specific 
computerized fine motor assessment for monitoring disease progression and 
treatment response.

ASIC1a as an integrating node in ischemic neurotoxicity: crosstalk with NMDAR 
and TRPM signaling.

Lai K(1), Wang LY(2)(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital, Shanghai 
Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Shanghai, 200032, China.

Ischemic stroke triggers acidosis, glutamate excitotoxicity and oxidative 
stress, which converge to disturb ionic homeostasis through several cation 
channels, including acid-sensing ion channel 1a (ASIC1a), N-methyl-D-aspartate 
receptors (NMDARs) and transient receptor potential melastatin (TRPM) channels. 
Emerging evidence suggests that ASIC1a functions as a context-dependent 
integrating node: protons directly gate ASIC1a, glutamate and 
bilirubin-associated signaling can modulate ASIC1a-dependent injury pathways. 
ASIC1a directly couples with NMDAR-dependent signaling and indirectly engages 
TRPM-associated pathways. Here, we discuss the mechanistic basis, therapeutic 
potential and unresolved questions regarding ASIC1a-associated signaling in 
ischemic brain injury.

Children's Cognitive Abilities Moderate Parent/Teacher Agreement on 
Internalizing and Externalizing Psychopathology.

All K(1), Carter CJ(2), Kemanian Leites M(2), Wikander R(2), He C(2), 
Huang-Pollock CL(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Psychology, The Pennsylvania State University, 140 Moore 
Building, 138 Fischer Road, University Park, Pennsylvania, PA, 16802, USA. 
kea5471@psu.edu.
(2)Department of Psychology, The Pennsylvania State University, 140 Moore 
Building, 138 Fischer Road, University Park, Pennsylvania, PA, 16802, USA.

Multi-informant assessment (typically parents and teachers) is a gold-standard 
process used to inform diagnosis and tailor treatment in children, but 
multi-informant agreement is notoriously low. Children's cognitive abilities 
might partially account for reporter discrepancies, particularly in situations 
when a child's abilities are insufficient to meet context-specific demands 
(i.e., increased academic difficulties resulting in increased symptomatology at 
school compared to the home). Existing work examining this possibility has been 
limited to subjective reports of cognitive ability and/or neglected 
internalizing symptoms. The current study investigated whether objectively 
measured cognitive abilities moderate parent/teacher agreement on both 
externalizing and internalizing psychopathology in children. Parents and 
teachers of 853 school-age children (ages 8-12) rated children's internalizing 
and externalizing symptoms, and children completed tasks assessing intellectual, 
academic, and executive functioning. Structural equation modeling was used to 
evaluate the latent interaction between parent-reported psychopathology and 
cognitive abilities when predicting teacher-reported psychopathology, thus 
testing whether cognitive abilities moderate parent/teacher agreement. 
Parent/teacher agreement on internalizing and externalizing symptoms was 
moderated by intellectual functioning and reading achievement, but not math 
skills or executive functioning. Stronger skills were associated with higher 
agreement, and post-hoc analyses indicated that lower cognitive abilities were 
associated with higher parent versus teacher concerns. Cognitive abilities 
moderate parent/teacher agreement, which may reflect the strength of the 
reporter's knowledge of the child or reporter perceptions rather than 
context-based behavioral differences. Findings point to the importance of 
comprehensive assessment that gathers information from multiple informants and 
multiple domains to form a full-picture understanding of children's functioning.

BACKGROUND: Although Patient and Public Involvement (PPI) workshops with 
families affected by hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes can benefit both 
affected individuals and their support networks, PPI workshops are rarely being 
organized. This article presents the planning and implementation of a one-day 
PPI workshop for families affected by Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer 
(HBOC) or Lynch Syndrome (LS) in Switzerland.
WORKSHOP DESIGN & IMPLEMENTATION: The event was funded by the Swiss National 
Science Foundation and planned over a 12-month period. The program included 
expert sessions presented by clinicians and researchers; moderated, small-group 
participatory exchanges exploring patients' and families' unmet health, 
psychosocial and educational needs; and interactions with patient advocates. 
Participant satisfaction surveys were analyzed using descriptive statistics.
RESULTS: One hundred and five adults attended the workshop in Bern in May 2025, 
with representation from the three major linguistic regions of Switzerland. 
Almost 75% of participants reported a personal genetic predisposition to cancer. 
Most respondents were very satisfied or satisfied with the workshop (92%), and 
nearly all (96%) found the presentations engaging, with the topic of 
immunotherapy as an emerging treatment rated highest. The participatory exchange 
sessions were the most valued component of the workshop overall (97% positive 
feedback).
CONCLUSIONS: We provide proof of concept for the feasibility and positive impact 
of organizing a national workshop for families affected by HBOC and LS. The 
participatory nature of the workshop allowed affected individuals and their 
support networks to communicate unmet needs related to their personal 
experiences and suggest future avenues for research.

Kwon M(1), Yildirim O(1), Peck KK(2)(3), Starc M(1), Arevalo-Perez J(1), Lis

Author information:
(1)Department of Radiology, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, 1275 York

(2)Department of Radiology, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, 1275 York

OBJECTIVE: Spinal osteosarcoma is rare and highly aggressive malignancy 
associated with poor clinical outcomes. To our knowledge, the perfusion MRI 
features of spinal osteosarcoma using T1-weighted DCE MRI, including plasma 
volume, permeability, and time-intensity analysis, have not previously been 
studied. In addition, changes in these features following radiation treatment 
have not yet been evaluated. We hypothesize that highly malignant spinal 
osteosarcoma demonstrates hypervascularity based on its pharmacokinetic 
perfusion parameters.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed 27 patients (mean age 44.5, SD 21.8) of 
untreated metastatic Spinal osteosarcoma who underwent DCE-MRI. Perfusion 
parameters, including Ktrans and plasma volume (Vp) as an indicator of 
permeability and tumor vascularity respectively, were measured using the 
extended Tofts model. A subset of 12 patients underwent preradiation therapy 
(RT), 18F-FDG PET, and 7 patients had post-RT DCE-MRI for assessment of 
treatment effects. Additionally, time intensity curve analysis was conducted to 
evaluate post-treatment changes.
RESULTS: Thirty-five lesions in 27 patients were evaluated. Perfusion 
characteristics including mean Ktrans and Vp were 0.323 and 3.54, respectively, 
indicating that metastatic Spinal osteosarcoma is hypervascular. In the 7 
patients with post-RT DCE-MRI, the mean post-RT Vp decreased to 1.77 from a 
pre-RT mean of 3.28, reflecting a 46.04% decrease to radiation therapy.
CONCLUSION: DCE-MRI evaluation of metastatic Spinal osteosarcoma demonstrates a 
rich blood supply, consistent with hypervascular metastatic disease. Changes in 
the time intensity curve analysis may serve as non-invasive marker of radiation 
treatment response.

BACKGROUND: Coexistent chronic heart failure and iron deficiency is frequently 
encountered in clinical practice and affects prognosis. We investigated factors 
associated with serum growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15, iron deficiency 
and lower hemoglobin levels in patients with heart failure and healthy elderly 
individuals.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Blood tests were performed on 90 patients with heart 
failure (aged 75.0 ± 10.7 years) and 73 healthy elderly individuals (aged 
76.3 ± 6.4 years). Serum GDF-15, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) α, N-terminal 
pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and hepcidin concentrations were 
measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Left atrial volume index 
(LAVI) was measured by echocardiography. Hemoglobin (Hb) in healthy elderly 
individuals correlated with serum iron and hepcidin. In contrast, Hb in patients 
with heart failure correlated with serum iron and GDF-15. Serum GDF-15 
concentration in healthy elderly subjects correlated with estimated glomerular 
filtration rate, serum iron, and hepcidin. In contrast, in patients with heart 
failure, it correlated with NT-proBNP and TNFα. In patients with heart failure, 
serum iron correlated with LAVI.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower hemoglobin levels in patients with heart failure might be 
associated with elevated serum GDF-15 due to higher serum NT-proBNP and 
inflammation, as well as iron deficiency. In contrast, lower hemoglobin levels 
in healthy elderly individuals might involve lower serum iron and hepcidin 
levels. Lower serum iron concentration was suggested to be involved in left 
atrial remodeling in patients with heart failure.

Among patients with cardiogenic shock receiving Impella-based mechanical 
circulatory support, pulmonary vascular load and right ventricular dysfunction 
may affect left ventricular preload and device flow. Prospective data on the 
acute hemodynamic effects of inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) in this setting are 
limited. We evaluated short-term hemodynamic changes after iNO initiation in 
patients receiving Impella or Impella combined with veno-arterial extracorporeal 
membrane oxygenation (ECPELLA) support. We conducted a prospective single-center 
pilot study of adult patients receiving Impella or ECPELLA support who were 
treated with iNO. iNO was initiated at 20 ppm after initial circulatory 
resuscitation once pulmonary artery pulse pressure could be reliably assessed. 
Hemodynamic variables were recorded immediately before iNO initiation (T0) and 
30 min (T1) and 24 h (T2) after initiation. The primary endpoint was the change 
in mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) from T0 to T1. We enrolled 11 patients, 
and 10 were analyzed. mPAP decreased from 19.0 (14.8-20.3) mmHg at T0 to 16.5 
(12.8-19.3) mmHg at T1 (P = 0.004). The T0-T2 difference was not significant. 
Lactate levels decreased, but this temporal change could not be attributed 
directly to iNO without a control group. Methemoglobin levels increased slightly 
at T2 without clinical methemoglobinemia. iNO was temporally associated with an 
early reduction in mPAP in patients receiving Impella-based support, without 
clear improvement in systemic hemodynamic indices. These hypothesis-generating 
findings require confirmation in larger controlled studies.

Metabolic hallmarks of regulated cell death.

Kang R(1), Chen X(2)(3), Kroemer G(4)(5)(6)(7), Tang D(8).

Regulated cell death (RCD) is characterized by distinct molecular execution 
mechanisms, but its initiation, progression, and biological consequences are 
increasingly recognized as being shaped by cellular metabolism. Bioenergetic 
state, redox homeostasis, nutrient availability, metal ion metabolism, 
inflammatory metabolism, and organelle function collectively determine cellular 
susceptibility to death and influence the activation and execution of diverse 
RCD programs. In this review, we synthesize the metabolic hallmarks of 
established, independently validated, and recently proposed forms of RCD, 
highlighting both their mechanistic diversity and their extensive metabolic 
convergence. We then examine the endogenous mechanisms that maintain metabolic 
homeostasis and discuss how their disruption reshapes cell death responses in 
human disease and therapeutic contexts. Together, these insights provide a guide 
to  the metabolic landscape of RCD and reveal metabolism not only as a modifier 
of cell death, but as a fundamental determinant of when, how, and with what 
consequences cells die. We conclude by discussing key conceptual and mechanistic 
challenges and emerging opportunities for therapeutically exploiting the 
metabolic control of RCD.

Impact of fire extinguishing agents on DNA quantity and integrity.

Konrad H(1), Fertyk S(2), Firl K(2), Hartung B(2), Poetsch M(2).

Author information:
(1)Institute of Legal Medicine, University Hospital Essen, Hufelandstr. 55, 
D-45122, Essen, Germany. helen.konrad@uk-essen.de.
(2)Institute of Legal Medicine, University Hospital Essen, Hufelandstr. 55, 
D-45122, Essen, Germany.

In routine forensic genetics, samples from crime scenes after use of a fire 
extinguisher are often examined. These are usually vehicle or house fires in 
which the fire extinguisher was used to fight the fire. The vehicles include 
cars that have been stolen or used for criminal activities, or both, and then 
set on fire to destroy evidence. In addition, there are vehicles that have been 
involved in hit-and-run accidents and caught fire. Furthermore, fire 
extinguishers are sometimes used without a fire in order to deliberately destroy 
evidence at the scene of the crime. Either way, it can lead to an unsuccessful 
STR analysis and prevent the identification of the individuals involved. To 
investigate the hypothesis that the use of fire extinguisher or the chemicals 
they contain could be responsible for the failure, three different fire 
extinguishers were selected (powder, foam, and CO2 extinguishers), which are 
commonly used to extinguish small fires. Various surfaces were selected, 
including a laboratory table and typical vehicle surfaces. We created 620 
artificial samples of blood, saliva, and epithelial cells on these surfaces, 
allowed them to dry, and then sprayed them with one type of extinguisher each. 
As a control, one cohort was not sprayed and used as reference. In summary, the 
use of the various extinguishers after a short incubation period (one hour) had 
no effect on DNA concentration and in STR analysis. However, with increasing 
incubation time (25 h) prior to sampling, the foam extinguisher cohort showed a 
reduction in DNA concentration, but there was no reduction of complete STR 
profiles for blood and saliva in any of the cohorts. Only the 
quality/completeness of the STR profiles based on epithelial cells decreased in 
the powder and foam extinguisher cohorts. The proportion of full profiles fell 
by 6% and 15% respectively, and the proportion of no evidence profiles rose by 
17% and 13% respectively. However, the study did not reflect the impact of a 
real-world fire scenario. It could be assumed that completely charred surfaces 
or areas exposed to intense heat would yield poorer results in subsequent DNA 
analysis. Similarly, longer incubation times of fire extinguisher chemicals can 
have a greater impact and thus lead to a more reduction in the number of 
successfully typed samples.

High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to 
compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are 
limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron-hole polarization. 
Although widely described by a phenomenological coherence time, the microscopic 
origin of this dephasing has remained unresolved. Here, we combine 
wavelength-dependent HHG measurements in monolayer and bulk semiconductors with 
ab initio many-body calculations of electron-phonon scattering and strong-field 
simulations. We show that the measured wavelength scaling of the HHG yield is 
quantitatively reproduced only when semiconductor Bloch equations incorporate 
momentum-dependent dephasing derived from first principles scattering rates. The 
calculations reveal that strong-field-driven carriers rapidly enter regions of 
the Brillouin zone with enhanced electron-phonon scattering, giving rise to 
effective few-femtosecond dephasing. Our results establish a microscopic 
foundation for dephasing in solid-state HHG and provide a framework for 
engineering coherence in strongly driven solids for quantum photonic 
applications.

Dysregulated splicing factors play critical roles in tumor progression. Here, we 
identify family with sequence similarity 50 member A (FAM50A) as a pivotal 
oncogenic splicing factor involved in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). 
Multi-omics and multi-cohort analyses revealed that FAM50A is upregulated in 
ESCC and correlates with a poor prognosis. Functional studies demonstrated that 
FAM50A promotes ESCC proliferation and migration both in vitro and in vivo, 
primarily through the activation of mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs) 
and focal adhesion kinase (FAK). We further characterized the FAM50A-binding RNA

identified a novel FAM50A-dependent backsplicing event that generates circSDK1, 
which originates from exons 2-4 of the sidekick cell adhesion molecule 1 (SDK1) 
pre-mRNA. Mechanistically, circSDK1 binds to dual-specificity phosphatase 22 
(DUSP22) and occupies its phosphatase domain, inhibiting the DUSP22-mediated 
dephosphorylation of MAPKs and FAK and thereby sustaining their activation. 
Furthermore, the transcription factor TFAP2C increased FAM50A expression. 
Finally, we identified rifabutin as a small-molecule inhibitor of FAM50A and 
confirmed its anti-tumor efficacy in cell-derived xenograft, patient-derived 
organoid, and patient-derived xenograft models. In summary, FAM50A promotes ESCC 
progression via the FAM50A/circSDK1/DUSP22 axis, leading to MAPKs and FAK 
activation. Genetic or pharmacological targeting of FAM50A with rifabutin 
represents a promising therapeutic strategy for ESCC.

Eukaryotic cells contain various membrane- and non-membrane-bound organelles, 
whose spatial and functional organization underpins intracellular homeostasis. 
Organelle coordination is governed by complex signaling and metabolic networks, 
often facilitated by direct physical contacts and molecular exchange. 
Mitochondria, as central hubs of bioenergetic and metabolic activity, are 
essential to functional coordination among cellular organelles. They engage in 
diverse cellular processes, encompassing ATP production, biosynthesis of key 
metabolites, calcium ion buffering, redox balance, and cellular turnover. To 
preserve their integrity and functionality, dysfunctional mitochondria undergo 
selective elimination via mitophagy, a specialized form of macroautophagy. 
Mitophagy plays dual roles in maintaining mitochondrial fidelity and actively 
shapes interorganelle communication. Through bidirectional signaling, mitophagy 
influences the activity of multiple organelles, including the endoplasmic 
reticulum, nucleus, lysosomes, peroxisomes, and lipid droplets. This 
interorganelle crosstalk is essential for adapting to metabolic stress, 
maintaining redox balance, and coordinating cell fate decisions. In this review, 
we explore the intricate signaling networks connecting mitophagy with various 
organelles and discuss how these interactions influence organ function and 
overall cellular health. We also highlight emerging small-molecule modulators of 
mitophagy, providing insight into potential therapeutic strategies aimed at 
restoring or enhancing organelle communication in pathological conditions.

The addition of entinostat, a histone deacetylase inhibitor, to exemestane has 
demonstrated improved progression-free survival (PFS) in hormone 
receptor-positive (HR + ), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative 
(HER2-) advanced breast cancer (ABC) following endocrine therapy failure in the 
EOC103A3101 randomized trial (NCT03538171). This study reports long-term overall 
survival (OS) results. In this study, 354 patients with HR + /HER2- ABC that had 
recurred or progressed after endocrine therapy were randomized (2:1) to receive 
entinostat plus exemestane (n = 235) or placebo plus exemestane (n = 119). After 
a median follow-up of 31.8 months, the median OS was 38.6 months (95% confidence 
interval [CI]: 29.6-44.0) in the entinostat-exemestane group versus 29.2 months 
(95% CI: 22.5-41.6) in the placebo-exemestane group (hazard ratio [HR] 0.83, 95% 
CI: 0.62-1.10, P = 0.184). The entinostat-exemestane group demonstrated more 
pronounced OS benefits when adjusting subsequent antitumor therapies such as 
cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors, or the combination of endocrine 
therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and chemotherapy. The sensitivity analysis based on 
the per-protocol set showed more significant OS benefits. The median time to 
post-discontinuation chemotherapy and chemotherapy-free survival in the 
entinostat-exemestane group were 11.7 and 9.3 months, respectively, compared to 
6.8 and 5.6 months in the placebo-exemestane group (both P < 0.05). Grade ≥3 
treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 65.5% of patients in the 
entinostat-exemestane group, without new safety signals observed. In conclusion, 
among patients with HR + /HER2- ABC after endocrine therapy failure, entinostat 
plus exemestane was associated with a numerically longer OS, with an acceptable 
safety profile.

Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease face 
persistent risks despite standard care. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide lacks 
real-world renoprotective evidence in high-risk Chinese populations relative to 
non-incretin-based standard care. This multicenter, ambispective cohort study 
enrolled 3305 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, renal impairment, and 
elevated cardiovascular risk at six Chinese tertiary institutions (median 
follow-up 36.4 months; trial registration: ChiCTR2300073001). Data were 
extracted via an artificial intelligence-enhanced pipeline. Co-primary analyzes 
comprised multivariable-adjusted Cox regression and 1:1 propensity score 
matching (332 per group); pre-specified landmark analyzes at 6 and 12 months 
addressed immortal time bias. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide was associated with 
a reduced risk of the primary kidney composite outcome in the original cohort 
(hazard ratio [HR], 0.49; 95% CI, 0.25-0.95; P = 0.035), which was corroborated 
in the propensity score matched cohort (HR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.20-0.97; P = 0.043) 
and progressive across 6-month (HR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.19-0.84) and 12-month (HR, 
0.33; 95% CI, 0.14-0.75) landmarks. While a reduction in 3-point major adverse 
cardiovascular events was observed in the unmatched cohort (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 
0.43-0.85; P = 0.004), this association was not sustained in the matched 
analysis (HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.57-1.48; P = 0.735). In conclusion, long-term 
therapy was associated with an attenuated risk of major renal events. Given the 
null findings in the matched cohort, the cardiovascular observations are 
exploratory and require randomized confirmation.

The lack of tumor-specific targeting by oncolytic viruses (OVs) restricts their 
therapeutic potential. Here, we report a "cap-linker" strategy to modify the 
vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) glycoprotein (G protein, VSV-GIN). The modified

regulatory T cells, and potent CD8+ T cell activation and clonal expansion in 
tumors. This preclinical work demonstrates a new tumor-specific targeting 
strategy of VSV for enhanced immunotherapy safety with superior efficacy.

Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit remarkable functional 
heterogeneity, with conserved subtypes observed across diverse malignancies. 
However, their shared roles in shaping the tumor microenvironment (TME) and 
their dynamic plasticity remain incompletely understood. In this study, through 
integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling across four cancer 
types, we identified two distinct immunomodulatory CAF states, termed 
antigen-presenting CAFs (apCAFs) and matrix-producing CAFs (mCAFs). Across 
multiple solid tumors, apCAFs were associated with enhanced anti-tumor immune 
features and favorable prognosis, whereas mCAFs were associated with 
immunosuppressive characteristics and poorer clinical outcomes. Spatial analyses 
revealed distinct localization patterns of apCAFs and mCAFs within the TME. 
Functionally, patient-derived apCAFs promoted T-cell migration, proliferation, 
and activation, whereas mCAFs suppressed these responses in vitro. Pan-cancer 
analyses further revealed a strong inverse correlation between apCAF and mCAF 
abundance across tumor tissues. Mechanistically, IFN-γ and TGF-β-associated 
signaling contexts were linked to distinct CAF transcriptional programs, with 
IFN-γ promoting apCAF-associated features and TGF-β favoring mCAF-associated 
features, suggesting a potential role of cytokine context in shaping CAF state 
heterogeneity. Clinically, apCAFs correlated with favorable immunotherapy 
response, whereas mCAFs predicted poor therapeutic outcomes. Collectively, these 
findings identify conserved immunomodulatory CAF subtypes across cancers, reveal 
distinct cytokine-associated CAF programs, and support stromal reprogramming as 
a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

BACKGROUND: Bipolar (BP) electrocautery has been introduced as an alternative to 
monopolar (MP) electrocautery in arthroplasty, with proposed advantages 
including reduced blood loss and improved haemostasis. This study aimed to 
compare peri-operative blood loss and haemoglobin levels associated with bipolar 
versus monopolar electrocautery in PrimaryTHA and TKA.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials 
(RCTs) was performed in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. MEDLINE, EMBASE, and 
Cochrane databases were searched by two independent reviewers. Studies comparing 
BP and MP electrocautery in primary THA or TKA were included. Meta-analysis was 
performed using fixed-effect models.
RESULTS:  Eight RCTs comprising 971 patients (476 bipolar, 495 monopolar) were 
included; six were suitable for meta-analysis. Pooled THA and TKA analyses 
showed no significant differences in haemoglobin drop (MD 0.21 g/dL; p = 0.07), 
total blood loss (MD 5.06 mL; p = 0.57), or length of stay (MD 0.12 days; 
p = 0.26). Subgroup analysis in TKA showed reduced haemoglobin drop (MD 
0.32 g/dL; p = 0.002) and blood loss (MD 89.67 mL; p = 0.03) with BP 
electrocautery; this was not observed in THA.
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis found no clinically meaningful advantage of BP 
over MP electrocautery in primary THA and TKA. Reductions in blood loss and 
haemoglobin drop in TKA are likely multi-factorial and not clearly attributable 
to electrocautery type. Routine use of BP electrocautery in primary arthroplasty 
is not supported.

Sociodemographic correlates of daytime napping in Canadian preschoolers.

Acheampong E(1), Lang JJ(2), Reid GJ(3), Chaput JP(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Health Sciences, Carleton University, Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.
(2)Centre for Surveillance and Applied Research, Public Health Agency of Canada, 
Ottawa, Ontario, Canada; Healthy Active Living and Obesity Research Group, 
Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario Research Institute, Ottawa, Ontario, 
Canada; Alliance for Research in Exercise, Nutrition and Activity (ARENA), 
School of Allied Health and Human Performance, Adelaide University, Adelaide, 
SA, Australia.
(3)Children's Health Research Institute, London, Ontario, Canada; Departments of 
Psychology, Family Medicine & Paediatrics, The University of Western Ontario, 
London, Ontario, Canada; Lawson Health Research Institute, London, Ontario,

(4)Healthy Active Living and Obesity Research Group, Children's Hospital of

Electronic address: jpchaput@cheo.on.ca.

OBJECTIVES: To examine the sociodemographic and sleep-related characteristics of 
Canadian children aged 3 to 4 years who napped compared with those who did not.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the 2023 Canadian Health 
Survey on Children and Youth (CHSCY), a nationally representative survey. 
Parents of children aged 3 to 4 years (n=6291) reported napping status, nap 
duration, nighttime sleep characteristics, and sociodemographic factors. 
Weighted proportions and chi-square tests compared nappers and non-nappers. 
Multivariable logistic regression identified sociodemographic characteristics 
independently associated with daytime napping.
RESULTS: Napping prevalence was lower among 4-year-olds than 3-year-olds (27.6% 
vs. 48.7%, P<.001). Children who napped were more likely to be from non-White 
ethnoracial backgrounds, live in lower-income households, and have landed 
immigrant status, whereas non-nappers were more often White, from higher-income 
households, and Canadian-born. After multivariable adjustment, Black and 
Arab/West Asian children had higher odds of daytime napping, whereas Indigenous 
children had lower odds than White children. Immigration status was no longer 
independently associated with daytime napping. No significant differences were 
observed by gender, parental education, or perceived general or mental health. 
Non-nappers were more likely to obtain at least 10 hours of nighttime sleep (3 
years: 95.4% vs. 79.4%, P<.001; 4 years: 90.1% vs. 76.7%, P<.001) and, at age 3, 
to fall asleep within 10 minutes at night (55.3% vs. 39.7%, P<.001). Among 
4-year-olds, nappers were more likely to report no or almost never experiencing 
nighttime awakenings (57.3% vs. 44.3%, P<.001). Mean nap duration remained 
stable at approximately 2.4 to 2.5 hours.
CONCLUSIONS: Daytime napping in Canadian preschoolers varies by developmental 
stage and sociodemographic characteristics, supporting previous evidence that 
sleep patterns during the preschool years reflect both developmental variability 
and contextual influences.

Genetic evidence for the causal effects of malocclusion and dental attrition on 
temporomandibular disorders: A multivariable Mendelian randomization study.

Sivakumar S(1), Sathish S(2), Ramalingam B(3), Sundramoorthy AK(4), Sivakumar 
G(5).

Author information:
(1)Doctoral student, Department of Public Health Dentistry, Saveetha Dental 
College and Hospitals, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, 
Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India; and Project Research Scientist, Division of 
Discovery Research, Indian Council of Medical Research, New Delhi, India.
(2)Professor, Department of Oral Medicine and Radiology, Teerthanker Mahaveer 
Dental College and Research Centre, Teerthanker Mahaveer University, Moradabad,

(3)Professor, Department of Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery, Sree Balaji Dental

(4)Professor, Department of Prosthodontics, Saveetha Dental College and

(5)Postgraduate student, Department of Prosthodontics and Crown & Bridge, Ragas

STATEMENT OF PROBLEM: The causal role of occlusal factors, particularly 
malocclusion and dental attrition, in temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) remains 
unclear because of inconsistent observational evidence and confounding 
influences, limiting definitive conclusions regarding their independent 
etiological contributions.
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to investigate the independent causal 
effects of malocclusion and dental attrition on TMDs using multivariable 
Mendelian randomization (MVMR).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A 2-sample MR framework used genome-wide association study 
(GWAS) summary data from European cohorts. Pairwise Mendelian randomization (MR) 
analyses and linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC) estimated genetic 
correlations. MVMR then assessed independent causal effects, accounting for 
shared genetic architecture, utilizing the inverse variance weighted (IVW) 
method as the primary estimator. Instrument strength was verified via 
conditional F-statistics. Sensitivity analyses evaluated instrument 
heterogeneity (Cochran Q) and directional horizontal pleiotropy (MR-Egger 
intercepts).
RESULTS: Genetic liability to malocclusion demonstrated a strong association 
with TMD risk (IVW β=1.059, P<.001), remaining robust in MVMR (β=1.013, P≤.001). 
Conversely, dental attrition showed no causal effect (MVMR β=-.018, P=.078). 
LDSC revealed moderate genetic correlation (rg=.580). Sensitivity diagnostics 
confirmed the absence of heterogeneity and pleiotropy (P>.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Genetic liability to malocclusion was found to be an independent 
risk factor for TMDs, whereas attrition was found to be a secondary marker of 
occlusal instability, lacking an independent direct effect.

Neurovascular Coupling and Subclinical White Matter Alterations in Young Adults 
with Migraine without Aura: A Multimodal MRI and Machine Learning Study.

Chen Y(1), Kong Y(1), Zhang J(1), Wang H(1), Zhan S(1), Wang B(2), Tan W(1), Xu 
J(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Radiology, Shuguang Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University 
of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China (Y.C., Y.K., J.Z, H.W., S.Z., 
and W.T.).
(2)Department of Acupuncture, Shuguang Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai 
University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China (B.W.).
(3)Department of Pharmacy, Shanghai Municipal Hospital of Traditional Chinese 
Medicine, Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China 
(J.X.). Electronic address: 13636489796@163.com.

RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Young adults with migraine without aura (MwoA) may 
exhibit subtle white matter abnormalities, but their relationships with 
neurovascular measures, neurotransmitter distributions, and clinical burden 
remain unclear. We investigated these multimodal imaging associations in MwoA.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 130 patients with MwoA and 110 healthy 
controls (HCs) were enrolled. Multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was 
used to quantify white matter hyperintensity volume, free water (FW) fraction, 
peak width of skeletonized mean diffusivity (PSMD), and global neurovascular 
coupling (NVC); the regional measure was the cerebral blood flow 
(CBF)/fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (fALFF) ratio. Regional 
CBF/fALFF ratio alterations were spatially correlated with canonical 
neurotransmitter maps. Correlation, chain mediation, and machine-learning 
analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Relative to HCs, patients with MwoA showed increased global FW fraction 
and PSMD and reduced global NVC. Decreased regional CBF/fALFF ratios involved 
sensorimotor, striatal, and cingulate regions. The spatial pattern of NVC 
abnormalities was positively associated with 5-HT1A, D1, DAT, and GABAergic 
maps, and negatively associated with D2 and noradrenaline transporter maps. FW 
fraction, PSMD, and regional CBF/fALFF ratio alterations were associated with 
migraine-related clinical indices. Random forest yielded the numerically highest 
area under the curve (0.866). Exploratory mediation analysis indicated that FW 
and PSMD statistically accounted for part of the association between regional 
CBF/fALFF ratios and clinical severity.
CONCLUSION: Young adults with MwoA exhibited subtle white matter microstructural 
abnormalities, reduced global NVC, and altered regional CBF/fALFF ratios. These 
cross-sectional findings suggest a potentially clinically relevant multimodal 
imaging pattern but require longitudinal and independent validation.

A Dual pH‑Responsive Hydrogel with Site‑Specific Therapeutic Functions for 
Differential Pathological Microenvironment Remodeling and Accelerated Repair of 
Infected Diabetic Wounds.

Dong M(1), Lu S(2), Zhang H(1), Liu M(1), Ma Q(1), Guo Z(1), Liu B(1), Yuan 
Y(1), Zhang Y(1), Shi C(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Orthopedic Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou 
University, Zhengzhou450052, China.
(2)Department of Pharmacy, The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou 
University, Zhengzhou450052, China.

Diabetic skin wounds have disrupted local acid-base balance, prone to bacterial 
adhesion and sustained chronic inflammation that hinders tissue repair. 
Benefiting from the unique properties of oxidized sodium alginate, we prepared a 
dual pH-responsive Schiff base crosslinked hydrogel loaded with herbal 
nanoparticles to remodel the defective wound microenvironment and speed up 
regeneration. Dynamic covalent crosslinking endows the hydrogel with favorable 
flexibility and shape adaptability to fit irregular wound surfaces. It exhibits 
obvious dual pH sensitivity: strong antibacterial activity in bacteria-rich 
acidic niches and slow hydrolysis under diabetic wound alkalinity, achieving 
stable drug release without burst leakage. The encapsulated nanoparticles 
exhibit multiple complementary functions. Zn2+ acts as an efficient bactericide 
to eliminate pathogens. L-Arginine facilitates nitric oxide (NO) generation to 
promote angiogenesis and M2 macrophage polarization. The glycyrrhetinic 
acid-2-hydroxyacetophenone conjugate (GA-HAP) suppresses proinflammatory 
cytokines to relieve local inflammation. In vitro and in vivo experiments verify 
that this composite hydrogel balances wound pH, eradicates bacterial infection, 
and mitigates persistent inflammation, remarkably accelerating diabetic wound 
healing. This pH-sensitive herbal hydrogel holds great potential for 
microenvironment regulation and clinical therapy of intractable diabetic wounds.

Recent Advances in Graphene-Based Aerogels for Electromagnetic Wave Absorption: 
A Comprehensive Review.

Gong X(1), Wang H(2), Zhang X(1), Yang L(1), Dong B(3), Zhang Y(1)(4)(5).

Author information:
(1)College of Materials Science and Engineering, Chongqing University, 
Chongqing400044, China.
(2)School of Automation, Chongqing University, Chongqing400030, China.
(3)College of Civil and Transportation Engineering, Shenzhen University, 
Shenzhen518060, China.
(4)State Key Laboratory of Safety and Resilience of Civil Engineering in 
Mountain Area , Chongqing400045, China.
(5)Mingyue Lake Laboratory , Chongqing401100, China.

With the rapid development of high-frequency communications, smart electronic 
devices and aerospace, the problem of electromagnetic interference has become 
increasingly severe, creating an urgent need for electromagnetic waves (EMWs) 
absorbing materials that combine high absorption efficiency, broadband response, 
light weight, and environmental stability. Graphene-based aerogels (GAs) show 
great promise for EMWs absorption due to their three-dimensional (3D) porous 
structure, tunable conductivity and surface chemistry, and lightweight 
high-strength properties. However, existing reviews on EMWs absorbing materials 
based on GAs have not systematically summarized the synergistic mechanisms 
between GAs and other materials, nor have they provided an in-depth discussion 
of optimization strategies for the coordinated regulation of composition and 
structure. This review comprehensively summarizes the latest research advances 
in GAs-based EMWs absorbing, explores the fundamental principles of EMWs 
absorption, and highlights the properties, structural characteristics, and 
preparation methods of graphene and GAs. In addition, the study examined the 
effects of defect engineering, multicomponent composites, and structural design 
(core-shell and heterostructures) on the regulation of EMWs absorption 
properties. These strategies synergistically yield broad bandwidth and strong 
attenuation. The review also analyzes the application of GAs in EMWs absorption 
under special conditions, and discusses the potential use of artificial 
intelligence (AI) and machine learning in EMWs absorbing materials. Finally, 
this review discusses the current challenges and future directions for GA-based 
EMWs absorbing materials, with the aim of establishing relationships between 
synthesis, structure, and function, filling gaps in existing reviews, and 
providing guidance for the future development of EMWs absorbing materials.

Cumulative Exposure to High Systemic Inflammation and Incident Metabolic 
Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Longitudinal Cohort Study.

Liu L(1), Wang C(2), Hu Z(3), Chen K(1), Wang Y(1).

Author information:
(1)Health Management Medical Center, The Third Xiangya Hospital, Central South 
University, Changsha, China.
(2)General Surgery Department, The Third Xiangya Hospital, Central South 
University, Changsha, China.
(3)Department of Neurology, The Third Xiangya Hospital, Central South 
University, Changsha, China.

BACKGROUND: This study aimed to examine the association between cumulative 
exposure to systemic inflammation and incident metabolic dysfunction-associated 
steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and related liver fibrosis in mainland China.
METHODS: This study used data from an ongoing longitudinal physical examination 
cohort. We enrolled 9,725 participants (aged ≥18 years) who completed three 
consecutive biennial health examinations between 2018 and 2022, with complete 
follow-up in 2024. Systemic inflammation was quantified using three established 
biomarkers: neutrophil count (NC), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and 
systemic immune-inflammation index (SII). Cumulative exposure was calculated 
from baseline to the third examination by multiplying biomarker values by the 
time (years) between consecutive examinations. The primary outcome was MASLD 
development at the fourth examination, and advanced liver fibrosis among 
incident MASLD cases was further evaluated using the fibrosis-4 index (≥2.67). 
Multivariable logistic regression models were used to explore the associations 
between cumulative exposure to inflammation and MASLD incidence and fibrosis 
severity.
RESULTS: At the fourth examination, 939 incident MASLD cases (9.66%) were 
identified. In fully adjusted models, participants in the highest quartile of 
cumulative NC exposure had 2.20-fold higher odds of MASLD (95% confidence 
interval [CI], 1.81 to 2.69; P for trend <0.001) than those in the lowest 
quartile. Similarly, the highest quartile of cumulative SII exposure had 
1.32-fold higher odds (95% CI, 1.09 to 1.59; P for trend=0.003). Conversely, 
cumulative NLR exposure showed no significant association with MASLD incidence. 
The addition of cumulative NC or SII to the basic model comprising traditional 
risk factors improved the ability to predict MASLD. Furthermore, among 
participants who developed MASLD, the highest quartile of cumulative NC (odds 
ratio [OR], 4.74; 95% CI, 1.76 to 12.75; P for trend <0.001) and cumulative SII 
(OR, 3.74; 95% CI, 1.48 to 9.45; P for trend=0.006), but not cumulative NLR, 
were significantly associated with an elevated risk of advanced liver fibrosis.
CONCLUSION: Greater NC exposure and excessive SII exposure were each 
independently associated with incident MASLD and related advanced liver 
fibrosis. Whether reducing inflammation can help prevent MASLD requires further 
investigation.

Venous sinus of Kelch: a cadaveric study with embryological insights and 
clinical implications.

D'Silva MH(1), Swer RT(2), Shanthini S(3), Hnamte L(4).

Author information:
(1)Department of Anatomy, NEIGRIHMS, Shillong, India.
(2)Department of Anatomy, Shillong Medical College, Shillong, India.
(3)Department of Anatomy, Pondicherry Institute of Medical Sciences, Puducherry, 
India.
(4)Department of Anatomy, Zoram Medical College and Hospital, Aizawl, India.

The venous sinus of Kelch (VSK) represents a rare but clinically significant 
venous variant of the middle cranial fossa, with very limited documentation in 
the existing literature. This study aimed to understand the morphology, course, 
and morphometry of VSK along with associated variations in the drainage pattern 
of the superficial middle cerebral vein (SMCV) and middle meningeal sinus (MMS). 
This study was conducted over the period from 2022 to 2025 at Zoram Medical 
College and Hospital, Aizawl, Mizoram. In the present study, VSK was observed in 
9.26% of the 54 middle cranial fossae examined from 27 cadavers. Moreover, SMCV 
and MMS, which normally drain into either the spheno-parietal sinus or cavernous 
sinus, drained into VSK. From an embryological perspective, VSK can be 
understood as a persistent primitive tentorial sinus (PTS). The variable course 
and termination of PTS may also result in other reported venous variants like 
Spheno-basal sinus, Spheno-petrosal sinus and Petro-basal sinus, which 
underscore the complexity of venous adaptations influenced by hemodynamic 
factors. Clinically, awareness of such variants is crucial for accurate 
radiological interpretation and for minimising the risk of iatrogenic injury 
during surgical and endovascular procedures involving the middle cranial fossa. 
Importantly, recognition of these alternative venous pathways may have future 
implications in facilitating novel endovascular approaches for neuromodulation, 
targeted therapy, and minimally invasive access to the temporal lobe and 
trigeminal nerve.

Cherqaoui B(1)(2), Jaume L(3)(4), Schleiermacher G(4)(5), Lesage F(4)(6),

We report the challenging diagnosis of an 11-year-old boy, presenting with 
subacute erythroblastopenia, followed by a multisystemic immune-mediated 
syndrome characterized by polymorphic mucocutaneous manifestations, associated 
with severe myositis related to a dermatomyositis-like phenotype and mild

Prehospital Pediatric Ventilation Quality Following Use of a Feedback Device: A 
Randomized Study.

Finney JD(1)(2), Siegler J(2), Wang J(3), John K(1), Robinson D(1), Grawey T(4), 
McClain B(5), Hoon Lee S(5), Riney LC(5), Babcock L(5), Browne LR(6)(7), Ahmad 
FA(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pediatrics, Washington University School of Medicine in Saint 
Louis, St. Louis, Missouri.
(2)Department of Emergency Medicine, Washington University School of Medicine in 
Saint Louis, St. Louis, Missouri.
(3)Center for Biostatistics and Data Science, Washington University School of 
Medicine in Saint Louis, St. Louis, Missouri.
(4)Department of Emergency Medicine, Medical College of Wisconsin, Milwaukee, 
Wisconsin.
(5)Department of Pediatrics, Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center, 
University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, Ohio.
(6)Department of Pediatrics, Children's Wisconsin and Medical College of 
Wisconsin, Milwaukee, Wisconsin.
(7)Department of Emergency Medicine, Children's Wisconsin and Medical College of 
Wisconsin, Milwaukee, Wisconsin.

OBJECTIVE: Manual ventilation is a lifesaving intervention for children in 
respiratory arrest, yet the quality of pediatric ventilation delivered by 
emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians across geographically distinct sites 
is poorly characterized. We evaluated baseline EMS ventilation performance and 
whether a ventilation feedback device (VFD) improves adherence to national and 
international ventilation guidelines for ventilation rate, tidal volume, and 
mask seal.
METHODS: We conducted a single-anonymized, randomized, crossover study of EMS 
clinicians from 5 EMS agencies across 3 metropolitan sites in the United States. 
Using a simulated 3-year-old toddler manikin, participants completed 2 
sequential 2-minute respiratory arrest scenarios separated by a 10-minute 
washout period. Participants performed ventilation with and without real-time 
VFD feedback in randomized order. The EOLifeX VFD recorded ventilation rate, 
tidal volume, and mask leak with each breath. Adherence to age-based guidelines 
was analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models with participants 
nested within sites.
RESULTS: We enrolled 123 participants across 5 agencies. With VFD feedback, 
guideline-recommended tidal volumes were achieved in 87% of breaths compared 
with 16.2% without feedback. Ventilation rate adherence improved from 65% to 
88.6%. Mask leak of less than 30% occurred in 88.4% of ventilations with 
feedback vs 80% without feedback.
CONCLUSION: In our simulation study, EMS clinicians rarely met manual 
ventilation guidelines for pediatric patients in respiratory arrest. The use of 
a VFD substantially improved guideline adherence, suggesting broad potential to 
improve ventilation performance.

Driving Legislative Change for Access to Medications.

Aldabbas A(1), Giefer MJ(1)(2), Carlson JC(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Ochsner Health System, New Orleans, Louisiana.
(2)Xavier Ochsner College of Medicine, New Orleans, Louisiana.

An insurance company denied coverage for an inflammatory bowel disease 
medication, stating that the lack of a pediatric Food and Drug Administration 
indication made that treatment experimental. This was legally permissible. The 
patient's pediatric gastroenterologist partnered with others to create a new 
state law that mandated insurance coverage for medications in children when the 
treatment was covered for adult patients and there were data to support 
pediatric efficacy and safety. Coalition building included support from a 
hospital system, community petitions, and interactions with legislators. Family 
and physician testimony supported passage of the law, in effect since 2023. The 
patient was able to obtain the necessary treatment, and the law has been used to 
help other children gain access to prescribed treatments. This process can serve 
as a model for similar advocacy in other states.

Effects of Protein Intake on Gut Microbiota in Physically Active Individuals: A 
Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

Bao Z(1), Jiao M(1), Zhao M(1), Huang FY(1), Liu Y(1)(2), Wang S(1).

Author information:
(1)School of Physical Education, Huaibei Normal University, Huaibei, China.
(2)Department of Sport and Health, Shinhan University, Uijeongbu-si, Republic of 
Korea.

CONTEXT: Protein (PRO) intake supports exercise adaptation and recovery, but its 
effects on gut microbiota (GM) in physically active individuals remain 
inconsistent across doses, PRO sources, and exercise conditions.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate and meta-analyze the effects of PRO intake 
on GM in physically active individuals.
DATA SOURCES: The PubMed, EBSCOhost, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science 
databases were searched through June 2026. Reference lists of relevant studies 
and reviews were also examined.
DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted 
study, participant, intervention, and outcome data. Eligible studies quantified 
PRO intake, included an exercise or physical-activity component, and reported 
extractable GM outcomes. Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed using 
the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool and Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, 
Development and Evaluation approach, respectively.
DATA ANALYSIS: Random-effects meta-analyses using Hedges' g, subgroup analyses, 
and meta-regression were performed. Eighteen studies (n = 819 participants) were 
included. Protein intake significantly increased the Shannon and Chao1 indices 
but not the Simpson index or observed operational taxonomic units (OTUs). A 
significant U-shaped association was observed between PRO dose and the 
α-diversity effect size, with the fitted curve reaching its lowest point at 
1.5-2.0 g kg-1 d-1. Protein intake significantly decreased populations of 
Actinobacteria, Bifidobacterium, and Firmicutes, and the Firmicutes to 
Bacteroidetes ratio, and increased Bacteroidetes numbers. Subgroup findings 
suggested that age, body mass index, intervention duration, PRO dose, and 
exercise modality and intensity moderated the effects on Shannon diversity and 
Bifidobacterium abundance.
CONCLUSIONS: Protein intake appears to improve gut microbial diversity in 
physically active individuals but may also induce notable shifts in beneficial 
taxa, particularly reductions in Bifidobacterium. Future studies should 
prioritize individualized microbiome-informed strategies, evaluate long-term 
safety, and clarify the ecological impact of different PRO sources to optimize 
exercise nutrition interventions.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. CRD420261288197.
