Key considerations in the design, conduct, analysis, and interpretation of 
observational studies in dialysis.

Quinn RR(1), Lam NN.

Author information:
(1)Departments of Medicine & Community Health Sciences, Cumming School of 
Medicine, University of Calgary, Canada.

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: In this review, key considerations in the design, conduct, 
and analysis of observational studies in dialysis research are explored in a 
unique patient population for which interventional trials are challenging and 
limited.
RECENT FINDINGS: The use of target trial emulation is increasing and provides a 
conceptual framework for the design of observational studies. A target trial is 
a hypothetical trial that would be conducted to answer a research question. It 
requires investigators to ask a clinically relevant question and then specify 
eligibility criteria, the treatment strategies that will be compared, the 
follow-up period, outcomes of interest, and the causal contrast 
(intention-to-treat vs. per-protocol analysis). The protocol for an 
observational study is then created to mirror the target trial. In doing so, the 
question is clear, bias is reduced, and underlying assumptions are made 
transparent. Illustrative examples are used to highlight common pitfalls in 
dialysis research.
SUMMARY: In conclusion, randomized controlled trials are not always feasible or 
even the ideal approach for answering certain questions. However, observational 
studies are challenging and require careful planning and execution to ensure 
robust, unbiased results. Target trial emulation provides a blueprint to improve 
the quality of observational study design.

Appropriateness of antiphospholipid antibody testing and its impact on 
diagnostic yield and clinical outcomes: a multicentre cohort study.

Natarajan R(1), Shrestha P(2), Elliott K(2), Partha Sarathy P(2).

Author information:
(1)Queen's Hospital, Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS 
Trust, Romford.
(2)William Harvey Hospital, East Kent Hospitals NHS Trust, Ashford, UK.

Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an uncommon but important cause of thrombosis 
and pregnancy morbidity. Despite guidelines, antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) 
testing is frequently performed outside specialist settings, potentially 
reducing diagnostic yield and leading to unnecessary downstream investigations. 
We evaluated real-world aPL testing practices, diagnostic yield, and clinical 
outcomes. We conducted a retrospective cohort study across three acute 
hospitals, two satellite sites and 63 general practices between February and 
June 2024. Adults undergoing aPL testing (anticardiolipin, β2-glycoprotein-I or 
lupus anticoagulant) were identified from electronic pathology records. 
Appropriateness, completeness, results and downstream clinical outcomes were 
assessed against BSH/EULAR guidance and the documented clinical context. Among 
691 patients tested (mean age 51.3 years; 67% women), only 34% requests were 
considered appropriate, and complete panels were requested in 26%. APS was 
confirmed in 14 patients (2%). Appropriate requests were associated with higher 
rates of positive results [risk ratio (RR) 2.39], APS diagnosis (RR 27.0) and 
management changes (RR 21.4) (all P < 0.001). Haematology, Obstetrics and 
Rheumatology demonstrated the highest rates of appropriate testing. aPL testing 
is frequently performed outside recommended clinical indications, resulting in 
low overall diagnostic yield. Appropriate testing is associated with improved 
diagnostic accuracy and clinically meaningful changes in patient management, 
supporting the implementation of targeted diagnostic stewardship interventions.

Autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in a patient with relapsed 
diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and type 3 von Willebrand disease: a case report.

Anžej Doma S(1)(2), Rozman M(1), Fink M(1), Preložnik Zupan I(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Hematology, University Medical Centre Ljubljana.
(2)Faculty of Medicine, University of Ljubljana, Ljubljana, Slovenia.

Autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (auto-HSCT) is standard 
therapy for eligible patients with relapsed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma 
(DLBCL). Type 3 von Willebrand disease (VWD) poses additional haemostatic 
challenges during postconditioning aplasia. We report a 65-year-old man with 
DLBCL in second complete remission and type 3 VWD who underwent auto-HSCT. 
During bone marrow aplasia, complicated by mucositis and melena, intensified 
VWF/FVIII replacement and transfusion support were required. Following a switch 
to a concentrate with a higher VWF-to-FVIII ratio, improved haemostatic control 
was achieved. Poor platelet increments were associated with anti-HLA class I 
antibodies, indicating immune-mediated platelet refractoriness. Bleeding was 
controlled with twice-daily platelet transfusions, full-dose antifibrinolytic 
therapy, and VWF/FVIII replacement maintaining trough levels above 0.50 IU/ml. 
To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of auto-HSCT in a patient with 
a severe congenital bleeding disorder, highlighting the importance of 
individualized VWF/FVIII replacement and optimized transfusion support.

TMPRSS2-coagulation nexus: a novel molecular link revealed by pairwise 
correlation analysis following AstraZeneca (ChAdOx1 nCoV-19) vaccination in a 
Nigerian cohort.

Ekprikpo ES(1), Jeremiah ZA, Ken-Ezihuo SU, Echonwere-Uwikor BE.

Author information:
(1)Department of Haematology and Transfusion Science, Faculty of Medical 
Laboratory Science, Rivers State University, Nkpolu-Oroworukwo, Port Harcourt, 
Nigeria.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the pairwise molecular-haematological and coagulation 
correlations, specifically evaluating the relationship between TMPRSS2 gene 
expression and coagulation profiles, following AstraZeneca (ChAdOx1 nCoV-19) 
vaccination within an African population.
METHODS: In this case-control study, 102 adults (51 vaccinated with AstraZeneca 
≥6 months prior, 51 unvaccinated controls) aged 18-65 years in Port Harcourt, 
Nigeria, were evaluated. Full blood count (Sysmex XN-1000), PT/aPTT (Erba 
Mannheim), RNA concentration, and qRT-PCR for ACE2/TMPRSS2 (normalized to GAPDH) 
were performed. Pearson correlations and t-tests were conducted (SPSS v26, P < 
0.05).
RESULTS: The AstraZeneca-vaccinated group demonstrated a statistically 
significant prolongation of mean aPTT compared to unvaccinated controls (34.233 
± 0.653 s vs. 28.196 ± 0.657 s, P < 0.0001), with both group means falling 
within the laboratory reference interval (20-40 s). A statistically significant 
inverse correlation was observed between TMPRSS2 cycle threshold (CT) values and 
activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) among vaccinated participants (r = 
-0.325, P = 0.0202), whereas no corresponding association was detected in 
unvaccinated controls. Because CT values are inversely proportional to 
transcript abundance, this indicates that higher relative expression of TMPRSS2 
(lower CT values) correlates with a progressively longer aPTT baseline. No 
participant reported severe thrombotic or haemorrhagic complications.
CONCLUSION: This secondary analysis identified a statistically significant 
inverse correlation between TMPRSS2 CT values and aPTT among 
AstraZeneca-vaccinated individuals. The baseline parameters confirm that this 
variation occurs within physiological normal boundaries at least 6 months 
postvaccination, suggesting a potential long-term molecular-haemostatic 
homeostatic adaptation rather than a transient acute-phase prothrombotic 
response.

Genetic evaluation in living liver donors: beyond individual risk to system 
responsibility.

Kasahara M(1), Sakamoto S.

Author information:
(1)Organ Transplantation Center, National Center for Child Health and 
Development, Tokyo, Japan.

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) increasingly 
depends on biologically related donors, particularly in Asia and the Middle 
East, where deceased donation remains limited. This review evaluates genetic 
risks in living donors and proposes a system-based approach to donor selection.
RECENT FINDINGS: Heterozygous carriers exhibit variable functional capacity 
determined by enzyme thresholds and epigenetic mechanisms such as X-chromosome 
lyonization. In ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency (OTCD), maternal donors 
may have insufficient enzymatic activity, resulting in donor risk and incomplete 
metabolic correction. Conversely, certain autosomal recessive disorders permit 
safe use of heterozygous donors within defined functional limits. In regions 
with high consanguinity, especially in parts of the Middle East, hereditary 
liver diseases are more prevalent, increasing the likelihood that potential 
donors share pathogenic variants. Additionally, reports of acute liver failure 
following gene therapy in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) highlight systemic 
vulnerability in genetically affected individuals.
SUMMARY: Donor evaluation must extend beyond anatomical suitability to include 
disease-specific genetic risk assessment. A system-based, globally informed 
framework integrating genomics, functional assessment, and multidisciplinary 
oversight is essential to ensure donor safety and optimize outcomes.

Management of seizures in patients with brain tumors.

Koh HY(1), Tobochnik S(2)(3).

Author information:
(1)Division of Neurology and Developmental Neuroscience, Department of 
Pediatrics, Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, Texas.
(2)Center for Neuro-Oncology, Department of Medical Oncology, Dana-Farber Cancer 
Institute.
(3)Department of Neurology, Harvard Medical School, Boston, Massachusetts, USA.

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Discoveries relating to the cancer neuroscience of gliomas 
have reframed brain tumor-related epilepsy (BTRE) as the product of reciprocal 
interactions at the neural-tumor interface. This framework provides the 
rationale for targeted strategies to optimize both seizure control and brain 
tumor survival outcomes.
RECENT FINDINGS: Feedforward dynamics involving hyperexcitability and cellular 
proliferation in glioma-infiltrated cortex drive synaptic remodeling of neural 
circuits that correlate with shorter survival. Seizure assessment metrics 
demonstrate that worsening seizure control may precede or align with progressive 
disease. In this context, early evidence indicates a potential role for targeted 
tumor-directed therapy in addition to antiseizure medications (ASMs) for 
optimizing seizure control. Noncontrolled studies evaluating ASM tapering 
strategies in BTRE suggest that tumor stability is more important for seizure 
control than the duration of seizure freedom.
SUMMARY: BTRE involves dynamic and fluctuating seizure risk driven by tumor 
biology, tumor-directed therapy, and treatment response. Hyperexcitability at 
the cellular level and clinical seizure activity are increasingly understood as 
a reflection of tumor biology and a potentially modifiable target to improve 
outcomes. The addition of seizure assessments as secondary endpoints in brain 
tumor clinical trials may lead to a refined individualized and disease-specific 
approach to ASM management.

The electrical life of cancer: cancer neuroscience from circuits to patient 
care.

Pittarello M(1), Dada A(1), Hervey-Jumper SL(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Neurological Surgery.
(2)Weill Institute for Neurosciences, University of California San Francisco,

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Cancer neuroscience has evolved from a predominantly 
preclinical, mechanistic discipline into a clinically relevant framework for 
understanding and treating patients with brain malignancies. This review 
synthesizes recent advances across glioblastoma (GBM), diffuse midline glioma 
(DMG), and brain metastases, with particular emphasis on identifying 
circuit-level, neurotransmitter-mediated, electrophysiologic, and network 
properties that are emerging as clinically actionable biomarkers and therapeutic

RECENT FINDINGS: Human connectomics and retrograde tracing studies demonstrate 
that GBM integrates into distributed, brain-wide neural circuits. In DMG, 
neuron-tumor signaling has expanded beyond glutamatergic mechanisms to include 
GABAergic and cholinergic neurotransmission, while patterns of neural 
connectivity have been associated with regional immunosuppression and patient 
survival. Patch-seq and electrophysiologic profiling have identified distinct 
functional states of malignant cells, and spatial transcriptomic analyses have 
linked malignant cell plasticity to neuron-rich invasive niches. Although these 
discoveries are driving the development of neurophysiologic biomarkers and 
circuit-directed therapeutic strategies, they have not yet translated into 
clinical practice. Emerging cellular atlases and mechanistic studies of small 
cell lung cancer and brain metastases further suggest that neural circuit 
integration is a broader feature of cancer biology rather than a phenomenon 
restricted to gliomas.
SUMMARY: The field's critical next step is to integrate cancer 
neuroscience-directed therapeutic strategies with prospectively validated, 
multimodal biomarkers that account for age and disease-specific neurobiology and 
reliably distinguish tumor associated states from physiologic aging and adaptive 
changes within the peritumoral microenvironment.

factors, associated with polyarteritis nodosa (PAN) could not be shown. However,

DADA2, that manifests as early-onset strokes. In Kawasaki disease, a complex 
polygenic model exists involving HLA-DRB1*15:01 for susceptibility and 
HLA-DRB1*14:01 for coronary lesions. ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) better 
correlates with autoantibody status rather than with clinical phenotypes. 
PR3-ANCA exhibits a strong association with HLA-DPB1*0401 and SERPINA1 variants, 
predicting chronic relapses. MPO-ANCA is linked to HLA-DQ loci, predisposing 
patients to rapidly progressing glomerulonephritis. Association of certain HLA 
susceptibility markers with different subgroups of AAV was also reported. 
Finally, Behçet's syndrome exhibits strong epistatic interactions with HLA-B*51 
and ERAP1.
SUMMARY: Genomic mapping reveals not only associations of specific genetic 
variations with different vasculitis but also their effects to determine 
clinical subgroups, ischemic risk, and clinical outcomes.

Palliative Care in Surgery: Updated Research Priorities from the Surgical 
Palliative Care Research Expert Consensus Conference.

Wong BO(1)(2)(3), Hoffman DI(1)(2)(3), Williams K(1)(4), Morton C(1)(5),

BACKGROUND: Surgical palliative care (SPC) research has advanced since the 2017 
research agenda, but persistent gaps in patient selection, intervention 
delivery, and outcome measurement limit implementation across evolving surgical 
care settings.
STUDY DESIGN: In November 2025, a national consensus conference convened 28 SPC 
experts and researchers. Through iterative discussion and consensus-building 
during the meeting and subsequent months, participants updated research 
priorities across the surgical continuum and health system context. Full 
methodology and participant attributes were described in Supplemental Materials 
https://links.lww.com/JACS/A821.
RESULTS: The updated agenda identified 11 research gaps across 3 priority areas: 
patient selection; interventions, care processes, and competencies; and outcome 
measurement. Priorities were mapped at 2 levels: surgical episodes, encompassing 
patient-, family-, and provider-level factors, and health systems, encompassing 
organizational and structural factors affecting SPC delivery. The agenda 
prioritizes identifying which patients benefit from SPC and when; broadening SPC 
beyond traditional populations; defining primary SPC competencies and the role 
of specialty consultation; improving communication of surgical intent, 
trade-offs, and preference-sensitive decisions; integrating and sustaining SPC 
across heterogeneous systems and care transitions; transforming clinical 
cultures; and developing patient-centered, context-specific surgical and 
systems-level outcomes. Emerging electronic health record, natural language 
processing, and large language model approaches may support scalable patient 
identification, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement, while requiring 
attention to bias and task-dependent performance.
CONCLUSIONS: SPC research should move beyond narrow proof-of-concept settings 
toward pragmatic, scalable approaches that define who should receive SPC, what 
should be delivered, and how success should be measured across diverse surgical 
environments.

Eligibility and prescribing of low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia prevention 
under two international guidelines: a retrospective cohort study.

Geçici NA(1), Demir FN(1), Sabır YA(2), Karaağaç H(2), Öztürk S(1), Kayıkçı 
U(3).

Author information:
(1)Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Kastamonu Training and Research 
Hospital, Ministry of Health, Kastamonu, Türkiye.
(2)Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Kastamonu University Faculty of 
Medicine, Kastamonu, Türkiye.
(3)Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Division of Maternal and Fetal 
Medicine, Kastamonu Training and Research Hospital, Ministry of Health, 
Kastamonu, Türkiye.

OBJECTIVES: The primary objective was to compare eligibility for low-dose 
aspirin prophylaxis according to the American College of Obstetricians and 
Gynecologists (ACOG) and the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence 
(NICE) recommendations. Secondary objectives were to evaluate aspirin 
prescribing among eligible women and preeclampsia outcomes according to 
guideline eligibility.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1,064 pregnant women with 
complete clinical data from a tertiary referral hospital in Türkiye. Eligibility

were also evaluated.
RESULTS: According to the ACOG criteria, 311 women (29.23 %, 95 % CI,

7.72-19.06 %) according to NICE criteria.
CONCLUSIONS: Although the ACOG guideline identified substantially more women as

Biochemical and anthropometric assessment of nutritional status at discharge in 
very-low-birth-weight infants: a retrospective cohort study.

Yaprak D(1), Saygılı Karagöl B(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Pediatrics, Division of Neonatology, University of Health 
Sciences, Gülhane Training and Research Hospital, Ankara, Türkiye.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate nutritional status at discharge in VLBW infants using 
biochemical and composite nutritional indices, and to examine their relationship 
with extrauterine growth restriction (EUGR; also termed "growth faltering" in 
more recent literature).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 124 very low birth weight 
infants (≤32 weeks, ≤1,500 g) admitted to a tertiary NICU (2021-2025). 
Anthropometric, nutritional, and biochemical parameters were recorded from birth 
to discharge. Four composite biochemical deficiency outcomes were constructed: 
protein (CPDO), nutritional (CNDO), mineral-protein (CMPDO), and 
protein-nitrogen (CPNDO). Multivariable Firth logistic regression and ROC 
analyses were performed. EUGR was defined cross-sectionally (discharge weight 
<10th percentile) and longitudinally (weight-for-age Z-score decline >1).
RESULTS: EUGR occurred in 43.5 % (cross-sectional) and 38.7 % (longitudinal) of 
infants. Hypouremia (18.0 %) and hypocreatininemia (12.0 %) were the most 
frequent abnormalities. Composite outcomes were associated with lower 
gestational age and small-for-gestational-age status. Cross-sectional EUGR was 
nominally associated with CNDO (aOR 3.72, p=0.023) and CMPDO (aOR 3.96, p=0.031) 
but not CPDO; given testing across four correlated composite outcomes without 
formal correction for multiple comparisons, these associations should be 
regarded as nominal. AUCs for the four composites ranged narrowly from 0.761 to 
0.794 and were not formally compared. Anthropometric differences were not 
significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Subclinical biochemical deficiency was common at discharge despite 
non-significant anthropometric differences. Composite biochemical indices showed 
similar, moderate discriminative performance across definitions; findings are 
hypothesis-generating and require external, prospective validation before any 
composite can be considered superior or used clinically.

INTRODUCTION: Pharmaceutical development of dry‑powder inhaler (DPI) products 
has traditionally relied on aerodynamic performance metrics. However, these 
parameters do not capture the post-deposition fate of inhaled particles, where 
dissolution impacts mucociliary clearance, macrophage uptake, retention, and 
systemic absorption, particularly for poorly soluble drugs. Consequently, there 
is increasing interest in understanding the dissolution behavior of orally 
inhaled drug products.
AREAS COVERED: This review critically examines the unique physiological 
environment of the lungs and the interactions of inhaled drugs with surfactants 
and mucins, highlighting why the respiratory tract cannot be regarded as a

between dissolution and pulmonary clearance, alongside key methodological 
challenges in dissolution testing, including sample collection, apparatus

and 2026 was identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and 
Web of Science databases.
EXPERT OPINION: Widespread implementation of dissolution testing is hindered by 
the lack of standardized methodologies on aerosol collection, dissolution 
apparatuses, hydrodynamic conditions, and physiologically relevant dissolution 
media that can accurately replicate the lung environment. Future progress will 
require harmonized regulatory guidance, validated testing platforms for routine 
quality control, and advanced biorelevant airway models for in vitro-in vivo

BACKGROUND: Millions of people worldwide lack resources to manage menstruation 
in a safe and dignified way. Period poverty in high-income countries affects 
vulnerable populations, including young people experiencing homelessness. This 
leads to poor menstrual health and negatively affects physical, psychological, 
and social wellbeing. This review examines the available evidence on menstrual 
health among people experiencing homelessness to inform understanding of the 
menstrual health challenges faced by young people experiencing homelessness.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR 
methodology. Three online databases (CINAHL, Medline, and Web of Science) were

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Midurethral sling (MUS) surgery is the standard procedure for 
stress urinary incontinence, offering favorable long-term outcomes. Despite its 
success, postoperative voiding dysfunction - manifesting as urinary retention, 
elevated post-void residuals (PVRs), slow or weak stream, hesitancy, or the need 
for prolonged catheterization - remains a clinically significant complication 
that is difficult to predict using traditional risk stratification. Conventional 
methods, including history, physical examination, PVR measurement, and selective 
urodynamics, provide limited individualized predictive power and fail to 
integrate the complex interplay of patient, anatomical, and surgical factors.
RECENT FINDINGS: Artificial intelligence and machine learning offer a promising 
approach to addressing this gap by analyzing multidimensional datasets to 
forecast individualized risk and guide perioperative management. While 
artificial intelligence applications in pelvic floor surgery have demonstrated 
utility in predicting general surgical outcomes, validated models specifically 
targeting post-MUS voiding dysfunction are lacking. Development of such 
predictive tools will require high-quality multicenter datasets, careful 
algorithm selection, and validation.
SUMMARY: Integrating artificial intelligence into clinical practice has the 
potential to enhance preoperative counseling, support shared decision-making, 
optimize surgical planning, and ultimately improve patient outcomes. This 
perspective highlights the unmet need for predictive modeling of voiding 
dysfunction after MUS, outlines the promise of artificial intelligence, and 
emphasizes the importance of responsible implementation.

5.46-13.30% in G3 (≥65 years). Among all HPV-positive women, HPV-16 accounted

Regarding PAP results, 95.63% of adequate tests were classified as negative for 
intraepithelial lesion or malignancy, while low-grade squamous intraepithelial 
lesion (LSIL) (NIE I) was found in 0.77%, high-grade squamous intraepithelial 
lesion (HSIL) (NIE II) in 0.33%, and severe HSIL (NIE III) in 0.26% of cases. 
This nationwide registry-based study establishes the first comprehensive 
baseline of HR-HPV positivity and cervical cytology in Chile. The predominance 
of non-16/18 h-HPV infections reinforces the importance of broad-spectrum 
extended HPV genotyping surveillance and provides a benchmark for evaluating the 
long-term impact of HPV vaccination and implementation of primary HPV screening.

Use of vaginal estrogens in urogynecology: current evidence, controversies and 
clinical applications.

Singh P(1), Pancholy J, Pancholy A.

Author information:
(1)Department of Obstetrics, Gynecology, and Reproductive Sciences, University 
of Texas Houston, Houston, Texas, USA.

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a prevalent yet 
underrecognized condition in postmenopausal women, characterized by progressive 
vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract symptoms from estrogen deficiency. Vaginal 
estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as 
new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special 
populations continues to evolve. This review summarizes current evidence on 
vaginal estrogen formulations, clinical effectiveness, safety, and therapeutic 
applications.
RECENT FINDINGS: Recent randomized controlled trials confirm that low-dose 
vaginal estrogen significantly improves GSM symptoms - including vaginal 
dryness, dyspareunia, and irritation - while restoring epithelial integrity and 
normalizing pH. Evidence also supports its role in reducing recurrent urinary 
tract infections by restoring lactobacilli-dominant flora, reinforced by a 2025 
multisociety clinical guideline recommending topical, but not systemic, estrogen 
for this indication. Comparative studies show similar efficacy across creams, 
tablets, inserts, and rings, differing primarily in convenience and absorption 
rather than effectiveness. Large cohort studies indicate no increased risk of 
cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or malignancy. Use in breast 
cancer survivors remains controversial, but emerging data suggest minimal 
systemic absorption and no clear increase in recurrence risk, supporting shared 
decision-making. In addition, long-term outcomes show that adjunctive vaginal 
estrogen does not improve anatomic surgical success after native tissue apical 
prolapse repair. Nonhormonal therapies and agents like ospemifene or prasterone 
offer alternative options, though they demonstrate lower or more variable 
efficacy than vaginal estrogen.
SUMMARY: Vaginal estrogen therapy is the most effective, evidence-based 
treatment for GSM and helps prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in 
postmenopausal women. Its favorable safety profile and multiple formulations 
enable individualized care. Recent evidence clarifies that while overall safety 
is reassuring, caution is necessary for breast cancer survivors using aromatase 
inhibitors. Additionally, longer-term perioperative trial data temper 
expectations regarding surgical-recurrence benefits, while confirming its value 
for local tissue optimization. Ongoing research should focus on long-term safety 
in high-risk groups and the effectiveness of emerging non-estrogen alternatives.

Truncal blocks in ambulatory surgery: what is the evidence?

Steinfeldt T(1), Marx A(1), Heinen R(2).

Author information:
(1)Klinik für Anästhesiologie, Intensivmedizin und Schmerzmedizin, BG 
Unfallklinik Frankfurt am Main, Frankfurt am Main.
(2)Klinik für Anästhesiologie und Intensivmedizin, Universitätsklinikum Köln, 
Köln, Germany.

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Truncal blocks are increasingly used in ambulatory pathways, 
although evidence predominantly concerns short-term inpatient outcomes. This 
review evaluates clinically important, procedure-specific benefits over 
realistic multimodal comparators.
RECENT FINDINGS: Benefits are small and comparator-dependent. Trials comparing 
laparoscopic transversus abdominis plane and rectus sheath blocks with wound 
infiltration were neutral; quadratus lumborum block showed no clinically 
important superiority. Erector spinae plane block provides early analgesic 
signals, but heterogeneity and negative multicentre evidence limit 
generalizability. Evidence for pectoral and serratus plane blocks remains 
heterogeneous. Paravertebral block is more consistently effective but requires 
expertise, additional time, antithrombotic precautions, and observation. Only 
two randomized trials prespecified day-case or discharge endpoints.
SUMMARY: Truncal blocks supplement multimodal analgesia rather than replace 
general anesthesia, except for selected small, superficial abdominal wall 
procedures. Transversus abdominis plane block has the largest, heterogeneous 
evidence base, but benefits over optimized infiltration are often small or 
absent. Evidence on discharge, recovery at home, and rebound pain remains 
insufficient. Despite efficacy in major breast surgery, paravertebral block is 
less suitable for routine day-case pathways because of procedural and monitoring 
requirements. Current evidence does not support recommending routine truncal 
blocks for intraoperative and postoperative analgesia in ambulatory surgery.

Liver-targeted DGAT2 siRNA ameliorates steatosis and fibrosis in a high-fat 
diet-induced MASH mouse model.

Zhang E(1)(2), Zheng W(3), Li Y(2)(4), Cheng Z(3), Cai Y(2)(5), Cheng Y(3), 
Zhang X(3), Hou Q(3), Liu Y(3), Meng B(3), Hou M(3), Wang C(3), Hu T(3), Tian 
G(3), Shen J(1)(2)(4)(5).

Author information:
(1)School of Chinese Materia Medica, Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine, 
Nanjing, China.
(2)State Key Laboratory of Drug Research, Shanghai Institute of Materia Medica, 
Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai, China.
(3)Vigonvita Shanghai Co., Ltd, Shanghai, China.
(4)College of Pharmacy, Xinjiang Medical University, Urumqi, China.
(5)University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China.

Diacylglycerol O-acyltransferase 2 (DGAT2), a key enzyme in hepatic triglyceride 
(TG) synthesis, is considered a promising therapeutic target for metabolic 
dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) 
targeting conserved regions of human and mouse DGAT2 mRNA were designed, 
synthesised and screened in vitro leading to the identification of a 
GalNAc-conjugated siRNA, VX093L, which mediates potent DGAT2 mRNA knockdown in 
both human and mouse hepatocytes and exhibits sustained hepatic DGAT2 silencing 
in healthy mice. In a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced MASH mouse model, the effects 
of VX093L (1 or 3 mg/kg, biweekly) were evaluated in comparison with the 
approved drug resmetirom (10 mg/kg, daily). Eight weeks of treatment with VX093L 
potently silenced hepatic DGAT2 (>80%, p < 0.0001), thereby inhibiting hepatic 
TG synthesis and significantly ameliorating hepatic steatosis. Notably, VX093L 
treatment also effectively attenuated fibrosis, with 1 mg/kg VX093L exhibiting 
greater anti-fibrotic efficacy than resmetirom, without an increase in 
inflammation. In conclusion, VX093L represents a promising siRNA-based 
therapeutic for the treatment of MASH.

Modified Suzuki Frame Fixation for the Treatment of Dorsal Proximal 
Interphalangeal Joint Fracture-Dislocation.

Jerome JTJ(1), Malshikare V(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Orthopedics, Hand and Reconstructive Microsurgery, Olympia 
Hospital & Research Centre, Tamilnadu, India.
(2)18.52 North Hospital & Research Centre, Pune, India.

BACKGROUND: The proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint is critical for hand 
function, contributing substantially to grasping and overall dexterity1-3. 
Injuries to this joint, often caused by axial loading, can lead to various 
fracture patterns and dislocations, resulting in long-term complications such as 
pain, stiffness, reduced range of motion, arthritis, and instability1,2. 
Traditional surgical approaches for unstable dorsal PIP joint 
fracture-dislocation include dorsal block pinning, open reduction and internal 
fixation (ORIF), hemi-hamate or hemi-capitate arthroplasty, and external 
fixation1-3. Although these methods can be effective, they may have limitations 
in certain situations. The Suzuki frame, a pins-and-rubber-band traction system, 
offers a dynamic external fixation option that allows for early controlled 
motion while maintaining fracture reduction. This technique has several 
advantages, including ligamentotaxis (the traction force helps to reduce 
fracture fragments and restore joint alignment), early mobilization (the dynamic 
nature of the frame allows for early active motion, minimizing joint stiffness), 
and simplicity (the technique is relatively straightforward and can be performed 
with readily available materials).
DESCRIPTION: The modified Suzuki frame procedure for dorsal PIP joint 
fracture-dislocation involves administering local anesthesia and establishing a 
sterile field. Under fluoroscopic guidance, three 1.0-mm Kirschner wires are 
inserted: 1 through the center of rotation of the proximal phalangeal head, 1 
through the center of rotation of the middle phalangeal head, and 1 (the 
"translation pin") in the middle phalanx distal to the fracture. The wires are 
then bent to create a frame with hooks, and the translation pin is secured to 
the proximal wire. Rubber bands are applied between the hooks to provide 
traction and maintain reduction. PIP joint congruency is confirmed through a 
full range of motion under fluoroscopy. Dressings and a splint are applied, 
allowing for limited immediate postoperative motion. Formal hand therapy begins 
1 week postoperatively.
ALTERNATIVES: Although nonsurgical treatment may be considered for stable, 
minimally displaced dorsal PIP joint fracture-dislocations, unstable injuries 
often necessitate operative intervention to restore joint congruity and 
stability. Several surgical techniques are available to treat these injuries, 
each with its own advantages and limitations. These techniques include dorsal 
block pinning, ORIF, hemi-hamate or hemi-capitate arthroplasty, and the use of 
modified external fixators with various external fixation constructs and pins to 
provide stability and allow for early controlled motion.
RATIONALE: The modified Suzuki frame is a dynamic external fixator that 
addresses the limitations of other treatment options for dorsal PIP joint 
fracture-dislocation. The modified Suzuki frame provides distraction, 
ligamentotaxis, and a volar-directed force while allowing early range of motion, 
preventing stiffness, and promoting cartilage healing1,2. This technique 
dynamically adjusts traction, unlike the use of static fixation, and is less 
invasive than ORIF, preserving joint anatomy that is crucial for younger 
patients. Use of the modified Suzuki frame is also simpler than that of 
traditional external fixators, making it ideal for complex fractures, 
soft-tissue injuries, and early mobilization1-3.
EXPECTED OUTCOMES: The modified Suzuki frame is designed to stabilize finger 
fractures while permitting early mobilization during the healing process. This 
approach helps reduce stiffness and increases the likelihood of regaining full 
finger function. Dynamic external fixation of this type has been shown to be 
highly effective for complex PIP joint injuries. Suzuki et al. reported that 
patients achieved an average range of motion of 80° at the PIP joint1. Ellis et 
al. demonstrated comparable outcomes, with patients achieving an average range 
of motion from 1° to 89°2. With appropriate care and diligent rehabilitation, 
patients can generally expect to regain satisfactory motion and function of the 
injured finger. Continuous monitoring and structured exercise programs are 
recommended to support optimal recovery outcomes.
IMPORTANT TIPS: This technique is best suited for unstable dorsal PIP joint 
fracture-dislocations that are reducible with traction or translation.Accurate 
pin placement is crucial for optimal results. Utilize fluoroscopy to confirm pin 
position and avoid injury to the surrounding structures.Ensure adequate traction 
with the rubber bands to maintain fracture reduction and joint alignment.Utilize 
sharp, double-ended Kirschner wires of approximately 15 cm (6 in) and 23 cm (9 
in).Bend the wires carefully to create secure hooks and avoid sharp edges that 
could irritate the skin.Maintain approximately 2.5 cm (1 in) between the 
proximal and distal hooks to ensure adequate stability.Pin-site infection is a 
potential complication. Emphasize proper pin care to patients.Kirschner wire 
migration or breakage can occur. Monitor pin sites regularly and address any 
issues promptly.Excessive traction can lead to distraction of the fracture or 
joint. Adjust the rubber bands as needed to maintain appropriate 
tension.Achieving and maintaining adequate reduction in complex fracture 
patterns can be challenging.Balancing stability and motion requires careful 
adjustment of the frame and rubber band tension.Patient compliance with pin care 
and rehabilitation protocols is essential for optimal outcomes.
ACRONYMS AND ABBREVIATIONS: K-wire = Kirschner wire.

Vertebral Body Tethering of Double Major Curvature via Mini-Open, 
Thoracoscopically-Assisted Thoracic and Thoracoabdominal Approaches.

Lonner BS(1), Kurapatti M(1), Dolgopolov S(2), Youssef G(2), Mucollari O(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Orthopedic Surgery, Mount Sinai Hospital, Icahn School of 
Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY.
(2)Department of Surgery, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY.

BACKGROUND: We describe key pearls and principles of a mini-open, 
thoracoscopically-assisted vertebral body tethering case for double-major 
scoliosis with 2 distinct anterior approaches: thoracic and thoracoabdominal.
DESCRIPTION: The thoracic curve is addressed through a mini-thoracotomy combined 
with thoracoscopic portals utilizing single-lung ventilation to provide clear 
visualization. Key steps include precise fluoroscopic marking of vertebral 
levels, muscle-sparing entry between the ribs, controlled pleural entry and 
mobilization, and careful management of segmental vessels. Vertebral body screws 
are placed under direct and fluoroscopic guidance with strict adherence to 
orthogonal trajectories and avoidance of disc violation. Tether placement 
proceeds segment-by-segment, maximizing correction at the apex while maintaining 
appropriate laxity distally to prevent overcorrection. Major tethering 
principles include maintaining colinear screw alignment to prevent tether 
kinking and utilizing bicortical fixation when anatomy permits. These principles 
ensure uniform force transmission and minimize stress concentrations within the 
tether construct, optimizing tether durability. The lumbar curve is accessed 
through a thoracoabdominal exposure that includes mobilization of the diaphragm 
with cuffed detachment and blunt retroperitoneal dissection to safely identify 
the iliopsoas muscle and sympathetic chain. Double-screw constructs are used at 
most accessible lumbar levels, with priority given to the apical region to 
enhance durability under higher mechanical loads. Screws are positioned 
posteriorly within the vertebral body to help maintain lumbar lordosis and are 
inserted with a controlled trajectory to achieve bicortical fixation while 
avoiding a posterior cortical breach and maintaining a safe distance from the 
spinal canal. Two tethers are applied (first posterior, then anterior) to 
distribute corrective forces and reduce peak tether strain, balancing correction 
with load-sharing. Adherence to these principles optimizes lordosis 
preservation, construct longevity, and safe modulation during growth.
ALTERNATIVES: The primary alternative treatment is posterior spinal fusion 
(PSF), the current standard surgical treatment for adolescent idiopathic 
scoliosis1. PSF generally provides greater and more predictable curve 
correction, particularly for thoracic-major curves, but sacrifices motion across 
the fused spinal segments.
RATIONALE: This surgical technique is appropriately applied in skeletally 
immature patients with flexible double-major adolescent idiopathic scoliosis who 
are undergoing vertebral body tethering through combined thoracic and 
thoracoabdominal anterior approaches1-7. A representative scenario is a patient 
with a right thoracic and a left lumbar curve demonstrating ≥50% correction of 
both curves on preoperative bending radiographs, indicating sufficient 
flexibility for growth modulation. Ideal candidates typically have Cobb angles 
between 40° and 65° and are skeletally immature (Risser 0 to 2, Sanders 3 to 4). 
The principles demonstrated are particularly relevant when treating double-curve 
deformities that require 2 distinct anterior exposures, wherein precise screw 
alignment, safe vessel and soft-tissue management, and differential tether 
tensioning are critical to predictable growth modulation. In the thoracic spine, 
this technique is useful when placing vertebral body screws through a 
mini-thoracotomy with thoracoscopic assistance, wherein colinear screw alignment 
and segmental tensioning are necessary to avoid tether kinking and maintain 
physiologic thoracic kyphosis. In the lumbar spine, thoracoabdominal exposure 
requires diaphragm mobilization and screws are posteriorly positioned; 
dual-screw constructs and staged posterior-then-anterior tethering help preserve 
lumbar lordosis and improve construct durability. These use cases emphasize 
scenarios in which precise fluoroscopic planning, harmonious screw trajectories, 
and controlled tether laxity are essential to avoid overcorrection, minimize 
mechanical stress on the tether, and achieve durable correction through guided 
spinal growth.
EXPECTED OUTCOMES: In appropriately selected adolescents with double-curve 
adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, bilateral vertebral body tethering can provide 
meaningful correction of both curves while preserving spinal motion1-3. Outcomes 
appear more favorable for thoracolumbar-major curves than thoracic-major curves, 
but patients should be counseled regarding risks of tether breakage, 
overcorrection, loss of correction, and potential revision or fusion. Long-term 
durability remains uncertain.
IMPORTANT TIPS: Maintain optimal orthogonal fluoroscopic views throughout screw 
placement.Align screw tulips colinearly to avoid tether shear forces.Leave 
controlled laxity distally in patients with substantial remaining growth.Use 
bicortical fixation posteriorly in the lumbar spine for reliable fixation.Avoid 
placing screws too anteriorly or posteriorly, which increases the risk of a 
visceral or canal breach.Avoid overtensioning end segments, which increases the 
risk of overcorrection.Avoid grasping or damaging the tether with 
instruments.Avoid insufficient thoracotomy and/or portal placement, which can 
lead to poor exposure and suboptimal screw trajectory.
ACRONYMS AND ABBREVIATIONS: VBT = vertebral body tethering.

Proximal Scaphoid Pole Reconstruction Utilizing Ipsilateral Proximal Hamate 
Autograft.

Jerome JTJ(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Orthopedics, Hand and Reconstructive Microsurgery, Olympia 
Hospital & Research Centre, Tamilnadu, India.

BACKGROUND: Proximal pole scaphoid fractures complicated by nonunion and 
osteonecrosis present a challenging scenario with few good reconstructive 
options, especially when the proximal fragment is small or fragmented1-4. The 
use of an ipsilateral proximal hamate osteochondral autograft has emerged as a 
promising technique for reconstructing the proximal scaphoid pole, with the 
potential to restore carpal mechanics while avoiding the morbidity associated 
with free vascularized bone grafts or distant autograft sites.
DESCRIPTION: The procedure involves replacing the diseased proximal scaphoid 
with a structurally matched osteochondral graft from the ipsilateral proximal 
hamate. After excising the necrotic or fragmented scaphoid pole, a size-matched 
graft-harvested with its attached volar capitohamate ligament-is rotated 180° on 
its longitudinal axis to replicate normal scaphoid anatomy. The defect is 
measured in 3 planes using the scapholunate joint (proximal) and viable distal 
scaphoid surface as boundaries. On the hamate, an osteotomy is marked 8 to 10 mm 
distal to its proximal tip, parallel to the articular surface. The volar 
capitohamate ligament is preserved to guide graft orientation and maintain 
stability. These measurements align with recent anatomic and biomechanical 
studies that have confirmed 6 to 10-mm grafts accurately reproduce scaphoid 
morphology without compromising carpal kinematics. The graft is then inserted 
into the defect and secured with rigid internal fixation (headless compression 
screws or Kirschner wires). Residual gaps may be filled with cancellous bone 
graft. Scapholunate interosseous ligament (SLIL) reconstruction is typically 
performed by suturing the hamate's volar capitohamate ligament to the dorsal 
SLIL remnant on the lunate with a 2-0 nonabsorbable suture. In patients with a 
partially intact SLIL, such as after failed fixation, the hamate graft alone may 
provide adequate stability, making formal reconstruction unnecessary. If 
intraoperative findings reveal dorsal scapholunate instability or an attenuated 
SLIL, reconstruction is indicated. Healthy, tensionable ligament remnants are 
repaired directly or reinforced with suture anchors. When dorsal fibers are 
deficient but volar remnants remain, the attached volar capitohamate ligament is 
used for reinforcement. For small defects, a micro-interference screw may be 
employed for fixation. Postoperatively, the wrist is immobilized in a cast. When 
radiographic evidence of union is observed, the cast is removed and the patient 
begins a structured hand therapy program.
ALTERNATIVES: Alternatives include vascularized and nonvascularized bone grafts 
(e.g., iliac crest), a vascularized medial femoral trochlear osteochondral flap, 
costochondral rib graft, proximal row carpectomy, and wrist arthrodesis1,2. 
These may be limited by donor-site morbidity, complexity, or suboptimal 
restoration of wrist biomechanics.
RATIONALE: The articular surface of the proximal hamate closely matches the 
curvature and size of the proximal pole of the scaphoid, making it an ideal 
structural substitute. The use of an articular autograft from the same wrist 
avoids the need for distant donor sites and microsurgical anastomoses, reducing 
overall morbidity. Additionally, because the graft is harvested with its volar 
ligament attached, it enables a simultaneous SLIL reconstruction, addressing 
carpal instability in a way that standard bone grafts cannot. This technique is 
relatively straightforward and reproducible, and it is especially beneficial in 
young, active patients with an irreparable proximal scaphoid, offering a chance 
to heal the nonunion and preserve near-normal wrist function without resorting 
to salvage procedures.
EXPECTED OUTCOMES: Radiographic union is expected in the majority of cases 
within 8 to 12 weeks. Published series have demonstrated union rates of >90%, 
improved pain, restoration of near-normal wrist kinematics, and substantial 
improvements in range of motion and grip strength, although not always to the 
level of the contralateral wrist. Complications are rare but include nonunion, 
donor-site pain, and persistent stiffness.
IMPORTANT TIPS: Limit proximal hamate resection to approximately 10 mm distal to 
its tip in order to replicate the scaphoid defect size while maintaining carpal 
stability.Ensure preservation of the triquetrohamate and volar capitohamate 
ligaments, as their integrity prevents instability.Rotate the graft 180° on its 
longitudinal axis in order to correctly orient the articular surfaces.Fixation 
should be rigid but not violate adjacent cartilage.Supplement with a distal 
radial bone graft if a distal scaphoid defect is present.Early controlled motion 
prevents stiffness.
ACRONYMS AND ABBREVIATIONS: ON = osteonecrosisVAS = visual analog scaleROM = 
range of motionQuickDASH = abbreviated version of the Disabilities of the Arm, 
Shoulder and HandCT = computed tomographyMRI = magnetic resonance imagingECRL = 
extensor carpi radialis longusEPL = extensor pollicis longusK-wire = Kirschner 
wireAP = anteroposteriorDISI = dorsal intercalated segment instabilityNA = not 
applicable.

PMID: 42890928

2275. JBJS Essent Surg Tech. 2026 Oct 20;16(4):e26.00003. doi:

All-Suture Fixation for Acute Turf Toe Injuries.

Pappa NK(1), Haritos C(1), Ardavanis KS(2), Eckel T(1), Martin KD(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, The Ohio State University Wexner Medical 
Center, Columbus, Ohio.
(2)Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Irwin Army Community Hospital, Fort Riley, 
Kansas.

BACKGROUND: Turf toe is a hallux metatarsophalangeal joint (MTPJ) injury caused 
by hyperextension of the great toe with axial loading1,2. High-grade injuries 
may threaten return to sport and require surgery3,4. Here, we describe a 
capsular reconstruction of the great toe MTPJ with all-knotless suture anchors 
and suture tape augmentation for turf toe injuries, in isolation or in 
combination with a traumatic bunion, designed to reduce suture burden, minimize 
soft-tissue irritation, and facilitate recovery.
DESCRIPTION: The procedure begins with the patient supine. A direct medial 
approach to the hallux MTPJ is performed. Both the medial base of the proximal 
phalanx and the medial eminence of the metatarsal head are drilled at isometric 
points, and augmentation with suture tape is then performed. Isometric drill 
holes are placed in the medial proximal phalanx base and metatarsal head for 
suture tape augmentation. A knotless suture anchor is placed approximately 3 mm 
proximal to the articular margin of the metatarsal head, repairing the medial 
capsule in a horizontal mattress fashion. An additional knotless anchor is 
placed at the plantar plate insertion, and the suture is passed through the 
tibial sesamoid sling and tensioned with the toe in 20° of plantar flexion. 
Suture tape is secured into the proximal phalanx with an interference screw, 
then passed through the deep capsule into the metatarsal head, followed by the 
placement of an additional interference screw into the metatarsal head. The 
anchor is inserted into the plantar-medial proximal phalanx at the flexor 
hallucis brevis insertion. The toe is flexed during tensioning, then adjusted 
per clinical examination and the sesamoid location beneath the metatarsal head. 
Knotless fixation permits incremental tensioning with intraoperative assessment 
of motion. Final tensioning is performed with the toe in neutral to correct 
deformity without overconstraint, preserving range of motion.
ALTERNATIVES: Nonoperative alternatives include rest, ice, compression and 
elevation; anti-inflammatory drugs; activity modification; and brief 
immobilization5,6. Operative alternatives include primary capsuloligamentous 
complex repair with nonabsorbable sutures, plantar plate advancement with bone 
tunnels or suture anchors if primary repair is not feasible, and concomitant 
procedures such as sesamoidectomy and bunionectomy based on the injury 
pattern2,7,8.
RATIONALE: This technique is intended for high-grade turf toe injuries with 
capsuloligamentous disruption, sesamoid complex insufficiency, and MTPJ 
instability. Nonoperative treatment may be appropriate in cases of low-grade 
injury; however, persistent pain, instability, or loss of push-off strength 
following nonoperative treatment would indicate a higher-grade injury. Compared 
with isolated repair or plantar plate advancement alone, this technique restores 
both static and dynamic stabilizers of the hallux MTPJ while addressing 
associated angular deformity. Suture tape augmentation resists recurrent 
hyperextension and valgus forces while allowing controlled physiologic motion. 
Knotless, low-profile suture anchors minimize bulk and hardware prominence in a 
region with limited soft-tissue coverage and bone stock. This construct offers a 
robust reconstruction option for athletes requiring predictable restoration of 
stability and reliable return to sport.
EXPECTED OUTCOMES: Operative treatment of high-grade turf toe injuries has been 
shown to result in reliable pain relief, restored stability, and high rates of 
return to sport8. Previous studies have suggested improved function and earlier 
return to play compared with prolonged nonoperative treatment in appropriate 
patients6,7. Knotless suture anchors reduce implant prominence and eliminate 
knot-related irritation, while the small insertional diameter of the suture 
anchors preserves bone stock in the metatarsal head and proximal phalanx. This 
construct provides immediate stability while allowing controlled motion, 
facilitating rehabilitation, and reducing postoperative stiffness. Athletes 
typically return to unrestricted activity within 6 to 9 months, aided by the 
suture tape augmentation allowing earlier movement through the range of motion. 
This augmentation reduces the need for long-term spica splinting and bracing and 
reduces the risk of recurrence.
IMPORTANT TIPS: The small anchor diameter and use of suture tape allow easy 
access without hardware burden.○ Suture choice depends on surgeon preference 
regarding construct stiffness and on the tissue quality and risk of irritation. 
We believe that suture tape lays flatter and, if required, knots are 
smaller.Avoid suture twisting or kinking, which can prematurely lock anchors, 
compromising fixation.○ After the anchor is placed, we keep the suture tape 
secured out of the field as we prepare the capsule with absorbable suture. As we 
load the second anchor, we maintain tension on the tape to prevent 
twisting.Overtightening the MTPJ capsule may lead to altered biomechanics.

INTRODUCTION: Progression following CDK4/6 inhibition remains a therapeutic 
challenge in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer. 
Gedatolisib, an FDA-approved pan-class I PI3K/mTORC1/2 inhibitor, introduces a 
treatment strategy for disease without a detected PIK3CA mutation.
AREAS COVERED: This review critically evaluates gedatolisib pharmacology,

Controlled functionalization of cellulose nanocrystals directs polymer-specific 
protein coronas and immune cell interactions.

Fuku R(#)(1), Giuliana P(#)(2), Liu Y(1), Kumar B(3), Malhotra K(3), Jiang V(2), 
Sedighi A(3), Gunning PT(3), Edgar LJ(1)(2)(4), Winnik MA(1)(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Chemistry, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON M5S 3H6, Canada.
(2)Department of Pharmacology and Toxicology, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON 
M5S 1A8, Canada.
(3)Department of Chemical and Physical Sciences, University of Toronto 
Mississauga, Mississauga, ON L5L 1C6, Canada.
(4)Department of Immunology, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON M5S 1A8, Canada.
(5)Department of Chemical Engineering and Applied Chemistry, University of

Polymer coatings are widely used to suppress nonspecific protein adsorption and 
modulate nanoparticle-cell interactions. However, the biological outcomes of 
polymer-functionalized nanoparticles remain difficult to predict in complex 
biological environments because protein corona formation rapidly alters 
nanoparticle identity. This challenge is particularly pronounced when 
hydrophobic moieties are incorporated for imaging or therapeutic applications, 
as they can promote nonspecific interactions at the nano-bio interface. Herein, 
we establish a modular grafting-to platform based on cellulose nanocrystals 
(CNCs) that enables systematic comparison of polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based, 
zwitterionic, and acrylamide-based polymers with controlled grafting density and 
chain conformation on a common porphyrin-modified surface. We demonstrate that 
dense polymer brushes reduce nonspecific protein adsorption in single-protein 
assays. By contrast, all CNC surfaces form dynamic coronas upon exposure to 
serum proteins, while specific polymer coatings selectively enrich or suppress 
distinct protein populations. We further demonstrate that polymer-dependent 
immune cell interactions are substantially reduced following protein corona 
formation, although differences among polymer chemistries persist. Zwitterionic 
coatings broadly suppress immune cell interactions, whereas PEG-based coatings 
preferentially promote interactions with antigen-presenting cells. These 
findings establish design principles for polymer-functionalized nanoparticles 
with specific immune cell interaction profiles.

Thermal imbalance drives avian performance and responses to climate warming.

Porter CK(1)(2), Adams DR(3), Levy O(4), Urinovsky N(4), Riddell EA(1)(5).

Author information:
(1)Department of Ecology, Evolution, and Organismal Biology, Iowa State 
University, Ames, IA 50010.
(2)Biology Department, Hope College, Holland, MI 49423.
(3)Biology Department, University of Central Arkansas, Conway, AK 72035.
(4)School of Zoology, Tel Aviv University, Tel Aviv 6997801, Israel.
(5)Biology Department, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Chapel Hill,

Thermal performance curves are widely used to predict ectothermic responses to 
climate warming but are less effective for predicting endotherm performance 
across environmental conditions because thermoregulation often decouples body 
temperature from ambient temperature. We develop theory and provide empirical 
evidence for performance curves in endotherms structured by net sensible heat 
flux (Q), an integrative index of thermoregulatory imbalance. Using biophysical 
simulations in tree swallows, we show that performance varies predictably with Q 
(which we term "QPCs"), thereby explaining variation in nestling provisioning 
performance, reproductive fitness, and geographic limits, while also forecasting 
responses to climate change. We also demonstrate that thermal imbalance helps 
shape breeding ranges of birds across North America. Our findings introduce Q as 
a broadly relevant ecophysiological dimension that constrains performance in 
endotherms and provides a framework for predicting endotherm responses to 
climate warming.

Dynamic partitioning shapes the in vivo organization of the Escherichia coli RNA 
degradosome.

Troyer L(#)(1), Wang YH(#)(1), Wu K(1), Kim S(1), Kim S(1)(2).

Author information:
(1)Department of Physics, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Urbana, IL 
61801.
(2)Center for Biophysics and Quantitative Biology, University of Illinois 
Urbana-Champaign, Urbana, IL 61801.
(#)Contributed equally

The bacterial RNA degradosome is a central mediator of RNA turnover, yet how its 
components are organized and regulated in living cells remains unclear. Using 
live-cell single-molecule imaging, we quantified the spatial distribution and 
dynamics of the four major Escherichia coli degradosome components: RNase E, 
RhlB, PNPase, and enolase. These proteins occupied distinct membrane-associated 
and cytoplasmic pools whose relative abundance varied among proteins and changed 
with physiological state. In particular, PNPase underwent pronounced 
redistribution between membrane-associated and cytoplasmic states in response to 
altered RNA availability and growth conditions, whereas RNase E and RhlB 
remained largely membrane associated. To determine the functional consequences 
of this organization, we examined the degradation of lacZ reporter transcripts 
with different translation initiation strengths. PNPase and RhlB preferentially 
promoted degradation of weakly translated transcripts, whereas strongly 
translated transcripts were largely insensitive to their loss. Together, these 
results reveal that the bacterial RNA degradosome is not a static, uniformly 
assembled molecular machine. Instead, RNA decay is organized through dynamic 
intracellular partitioning of degradosome components, linking physiological 
state and translation status to transcript degradation.

Husk leaves are the closest photosynthetic organs to the ear, which contribute 
directly to grain filling and have potential for yield improvement in maize. 
Teosinte has a long husk extended leaf blade, whereas maize exhibits a reduced 
or even no husk leaf blade. However, the genetic basis of this transition in the

Physical origins of speed control in swimming fishes.

Seo JH(1), Zhou J(#)(1), Peterson AN(#)(2), McHenry MJ(2), Di Santo V(3), Mittal 
R(1).

Author information:
(1)Mechanical Engineering, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD 21218.
(2)Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, University of California at Irvine, Irvine, 
CA 92697.
(3)Scripps Institution of Oceanography, Marine Biology, University of 
California, San Diego, CA 92093.
(#)Contributed equally

The linear relationship between tail-beat frequency and swimming speed in fish, 
first described by Bainbridge in 1958, has since been confirmed in species as 
disparate as eels and tuna. Dimensional scaling has explained why linearity 
should emerge at high Reynolds numbers, but the frequency-speed relationship 
itself has remained empirical, with no physical framework describing its 
behavior across swimming regimes, and no account of what sets the two quantities 
that define it: the distance covered per tail beat and the frequency below which 
forward motion supposedly ceases. Here, we derive a relationship from a balance 
of fin thrust, generated by a leading-edge vortex, and drag due to the boundary 
layer on the body. This framework yields an explicit expression for speed in 
terms of midline kinematics and body morphology. This formulation shows that the 
maximum stride length is set by the undulatory wavelength and the tail-beat 
phase offset, rather than by the conventional scaling metric of body length, and 
that no minimum frequency is required for forward motion. The model reproduces 
kinematic measurements from freely swimming glass catfish, published 
simulations, and Bainbridge's original data. Without recalibration, it predicts 
the results of independent simulations spanning wide variations in wavelength, 
phase offset, and morphology to within ten percent. Linear scaling is thus one 
asymptotic limit of a more general propulsive relationship linking morphology 
and body-wave kinematics to swimming speed in fishes and bioinspired vehicles, 
where the body waveform, rather than the actuation frequency, emerges as the 
variable that sets performance.

Insights from coproduced scenarios toward urban sustainability transformations.

Iwaniec DM(1), Grimm NB(2), Berbés Blázquez M(3), Cook EM(4)(5), Muñoz-Erickson 
TA(6); UREx City Scenarios Team.

Author information:
(1)Urban Studies Institute, Andrew Young School of Policy Studies, Georgia State 
University, Atlanta, GA 30313.
(2)School of Life Sciences, Global Institute of Sustainability and Innovation, 
and Global Futures Lab, Arizona State University, Tempe, AZ 85287.
(3)School of Environment, Resources, and Sustainability, University of Waterloo, 
Waterloo, ON N2L 3G1, Canada.
(4)Cary Institute of Ecosystem Studies, Millbrook, NY 12545.
(5)Environmental Science Department, Barnard College, New York, NY 10027.

Urban sustainability transformations call for fundamental shifts in how cities 
are organized, developed, and governed. Yet we need a better understanding of 
the diversity of visions and pathways that can enable transformative change. We 
address this gap through an analysis of 60 coproduced positive scenario visions 
and pathways developed using the Sustainable Future Scenario process, across 
nine US and Latin American cities participating in the Urban Resilience to 
Extremes Sustainability Research Network. We engaged diverse urban 
stakeholders-including government, nonprofit, and private decision-makers, 
community leaders, residents, and academic collaborators-in more than 20 
coproduction workshops to explore alternative urban futures of sustainability 
and resilience. We examined how the coproduced scenarios represent five domains 
of transformative change (nature-human relationships, economic transformation, 
governance, social and environmental justice, and infrastructure futures) and 
four theories of transformative change (structural/institutional, agency/power, 
goals of the system, and worldviews/values). Most pathways combined multiple 
theories of change operating across multiple domains, revealing urban 
transformations as entangled rather than singular interventions. Some strategies 
were common across cities-car-free regions, decentralized infrastructure, 
community-based governance, expanded fundamental rights-yet were pursued with 
different transformative aims, demonstrating how a strategy's transformative 
intent depends on the theories of change behind it. These findings position 
coproduced scenarios as more than a normative or planning tool and offer an 
analytical approach for surfacing the possibility space of urban transformation.

Poly(phenolic) deposition is a prerequisite to poly(aliphatic) deposition for 
functional potato suberin.

Esfandiari M(1), Alabi I(1), Dhaubhadel S(1)(2), Bernards MA(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Biology, University of Western Ontario, London, ON N6A 5B7, 
Canada.
(2)London Research and Development Centre, Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, 
London, ON N5V 4T3, Canada.

Suberin deposition in specialized cells is a critical aspect of plant 
protection, providing both water retention and pathogen protection functions. 
Tissue specific suberization during plant development is mirrored by its wound 
induction in cells that do not normally suberize and provides a robust 
experimental system to investigate the process. Suberized cells are 
characterized by a cell wall-associated lignin-like poly(phenolic) domain, and 
an ester-linked poly(aliphatic) domain, with the latter often laid down in 
distinct lamellar bands between the cell wall and plasma membrane. Previous work 
provides evidence that poly(phenolic) deposition precedes, and is necessary for, 
poly(aliphatic) deposition. To test this further, we generated RNAi knockdown 
lines of three wound-induced peroxidase genes, PRX19, PRX55, and PRX105, in 
potato (Solanum tuberosum), the tubers of which produce an abundance of suberin 
upon wounding. Peroxidases catalyze the oxidative free radical coupling of 
phenolic monomers to form the suberin poly(phenolic) domain. The wound-induced 
suberin of PRX19-RNAi tubers had severely reduced poly(phenolics), reduced 
poly(aliphatics), and no apparent lamella. Functionally, wound-induced 
PRX19-RNAi tubers were more permeable to water loss and susceptible to bacterial 
soft rot. Overall, our data support the hypothesis that poly(phenolic) domain 
assembly is a strict requirement for subsequent deposition of aliphatic lamella 
within wound-induced suberin.

The iridescent colors of birds originate in nanoscale feather structures that 
interact with light. Although the physical principles governing avian 
iridescence are well established, the molecular mechanisms assembling these 
nanostructures into photonic materials remain unknown. Here, we integrated 
genomic, cellular, and optical approaches to investigate the molecular basis of 
iridescent color formation in birds. We leveraged mutations that arose in the 
domesticated Indian peafowl and natural color variation in wild birds. In 
peafowl, we identified eight genes underlying gains, losses, and shifts of 
iridescence, whereas in two wild species, we used single-cell transcriptomics to 
profile asymmetric feathers in which iridescent and noniridescent barbules 
develop on opposite sides of the same feather. We found that all peafowl 
mutations mapped to melanogenesis genes, showing that variation in this pathway 
can modify diverse geometric features of feather photonic nanostructures. 
Mutations altering melanin composition collapsed multilayered photonic systems 
and yielded noniridescent tissues, whereas changes in melanosome abundance, 
elongation, or deposition timing generated multilayer architectures with 
variable periodicity and color. We further show in peafowl that transitions from 
noniridescent to iridescent plumage were associated with single-nucleotide 
mutations in a melanogenesis gene, suggesting that, in species already capable 
of forming multilayered nanostructures, iridescence can be gained by relatively 
small genetic changes. Single-cell transcriptomes from wild species also 
supported extensive melanocyte-centered regulatory rewiring associated with 
iridescence, including changes in melanosome maturation, trafficking, and 
intercellular signaling. Together, these results show that the nanoscale order 
underlying iridescence is developmentally plastic and highly responsive to the 
melanogenic environment.

The acquisition of paired appendages was a key innovation in vertebrate 
evolution. Although HoxA/D paralog groups (PGs) 9-13 play central roles in 
patterning paired fins and limbs, the evolutionary origin of this paired

Human immunoglobulin (Ig) A (IgA) protects ≈400 m2 of mucosae from microbes. 
Bacterial IgA-peptidases subvert this defense by cleaving the Fab-Fc hinge of 
subclass IgA1 while sparing the hinge-divergent, colon-dominant IgA2 subclass. 
The exception is IgAse, a ≈140-kDa, seven-domain, membrane-bound 
metallopeptidase from the colonic commensal Thomasclavelia ramosa that targets 
both subclasses but no other protein. We previously narrowed the minimal 
functional assembly down to the IgAse catalytic and wrapping domains (CD and WD) 
plus the IgA1/2 Fab', i.e., the hinge and a Fab of light and heavy chains (LC, 
HC), each with a variable and a constant Ig domain (VL + CL, VH + CH1). The 
transient interaction culminates in cleavage of a proline-valine bond within the 
first two hinge residues, downstream of a conserved C-terminal CH1 disulfide 
(SS2). Here, single-particle cryoelectron microscopy of a disulfide-stabilized 
minimal IgAse:IgA2 Fab' complex yielded high-quality density strongly supporting 
two states along the cleavage reaction coordinate, a "recognition complex" and a 
subsequent "precatalytic complex," in which Fab' binds frontally to the IgAse CD 
via a CH1 β-sheet and overhang loop LβEβF. This loop binds like a knob to a 
preformed hole in the active-site cleft. Binding rearranges the knob and rotates 
SS2 ≈ 180°, enabling access of the hinge into the cleft of the otherwise 
unaffected precatalytic complex. Together, this work defines a unique, 
CH1-mediated hinge-delivering "gate" mechanism, validated by a crystal structure 
of unbound IgA2 Fab, point mutations disrupting the CH1:CD interface, and 
molecular dynamics calculations, which provide the structural framework for 
subclass-independent IgA cleavage.

Quiescence to proliferation transition regulates asynchronous mitochondrial DNA 
replication dynamics.

Miyagawa K(1), Hosoya N(1).

Author information:
(1)Laboratory of Molecular Radiology, Center for Disease Biology and Integrative 
Medicine, Graduate School of Medicine, The University of Tokyo, Tokyo 113-8655,

Each human cell contains hundreds to thousands of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) 
copies, only a small fraction of which replicates independently of the cell 
cycle. An asynchronous replication of the leading and lagging strands has been 
proposed to represent a major replication mode in mitochondria, complicating the 
investigation of mechanisms that regulate mtDNA replication. Using 
single-DNA-molecule analysis that distinguishes the origins and timing of 
replication of each strand, we show that the mitochondrial DNA replication 
machinery responds to the transition from quiescence to proliferation by 
dynamically dissociating strand-specific replication rates and modulating the 
physiological requirements for factors involved in replication and 
transcription. During this response, the requirement for mitochondrial RNA 
polymerase (POLRMT) in replication initiation increases, whereas that for 
primase-polymerase (PrimPol), which is thought to function in DNA repriming at 
DNA lesions, eventually decreases. Thus, precise quantification of mtDNA 
replication rates at the single-strand level reveals the temporally dynamic 
nature of the mtDNA replication machinery during the transition from quiescence 
to proliferation.

layers. Overall, our framework opens further avenues for developing efficient, 
highly scalable fine-tuning algorithms for industry-scale LLMs.

Understanding how complex systems respond to perturbations, such as whether they 
will remain stable or what their most sensitive patterns are, is a fundamental 
challenge across science and engineering. Traditional stability and receptivity 
(resolvent) analyses are powerful but rely on known equations and linearization,

nonlinear representation of system dynamics while additionally retrieving 
intricate dynamical patterns that were previously difficult to resolve. This 
equation-free methodology establishes a broadly applicable tool for analyzing 
complex, high-dimensional datasets, with potential relevance to grand challenges 
in fields such as climate science, neuroscience, and fluid engineering.

PCS-UQ: Uncertainty quantification via the 
Predictability-Computability-Stability framework.

Agarwal A(#)(1), Xiao F(#)(1), Barter R(#)(2), Ronen O(1), Fan B(1), Yu B(1)(3).

Author information:

As machine learning (ML) enters high-stakes domains, trustworthy uncertainty 
quantification (UQ) is essential for safety. In this paper we introduce PCS-UQ, 
a framework based on the predictability, computability, and stability (PCS) 
principles for veridical data science. Starting with a candidate set of models 
or algorithms, PCS-UQ integrates a rigorous prediction-check to screen out 
unsuitable models in the set and utilizes bootstrap samples in order to capture 
both inter-sample variability and algorithmic instability for the 
prediction-checked algorithms. We then introduce a multiplicative calibration 
scheme to enhance local adaptivity, which can be viewed as a score function in 
conformal prediction. Moreover, we produce a compilation of 17 real-world 
regression datasets with manually constructed subgroups. On this benchmark, 
PCS-UQ maintains the target coverage while outperforming or matching conformal 
methods equipped with oracle-selected algorithms in interval width. PCS-UQ 
achieves consistent subgroup coverage, outperforming these oracle-selected 
conformal methods. Notably, PCS-UQ stands out in achieving both competitive 
interval widths and consistent subgroup coverage. Across six classification 
datasets, PCS-UQ reduces prediction set sizes by 20%. To scale the framework for 
deep learning, we propose computationally efficient variants that bypass 
expensive retraining. On three computer vision benchmarks, these variants reduce 
prediction set sizes by 20% over conformal baselines. Finally, we provide a 
theoretical proof that a modified PCS-UQ algorithm preserves valid coverage 
under exchangeability as a form of split conformal inference.

Nuclear BbAtg8 interacts with BbMac1 as a transcriptional modulator to sustain 
nuclear copper homeostasis during conidial germination.

Ding J(1), Qi G(1), Ye D(1), Li B(1), Lu M(1), Feng M(2), Cai Q(3), Ying S(2).

Author information:
(1)Key Laboratory of Biocatalysis and Enzyme Engineering, School of Life

(2)Institute of Microbiology, College of Life Sciences, Zhejiang University,

Pathogenic fungi endure host impose copper starvation by tightly coordinating 
trace metal homeostasis. However, how pathogens synchronize endogenous metal 
recycling with exogenous copper uptake to promote infection remains enigmatic. 
Using the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana, we uncovered a synergistic 
regulatory network that prioritizes nuclear copper enrichment during conidial 
germination. Under copper deprivation, the fungus deploys a highly coordinated 
dual-track survival strategy. In the cytoplasm, the core autophagy protein

virulence. Together, these findings reveal how pathogens synchronize

fundamentally expanding the role of autophagy proteins BbAtg8 into direct

AI can persuade people to take political actions.

Hackenburg K(#)(1)(2), Hewitt L(#)(2)(3), Wagner C(2), Summerfield C(1)(2), 
Tappin BM(4).

Author information:
(1)Oxford Internet Institute, University of Oxford, Oxford OX2 6GG, United

(2)UK AI Security Institute, London SW1A 2AS, United Kingdom.
